He tells Gon that he used up all his money on the trip fare and that they will need to make more inside the tower. The two plan to register for the tournament to earn money while training at the same time. Gon is surprised by the long line, and Killua explains that unlike the Hunter Exam, Heavens Arena doesn't have any conditions to participate besides defeating one's opponent. After registering, the two enter a crowded arena and wait until their numbers are called. Killua says that it's been a while and that the place hasn't changed. Gon asks him if he's been there before, and Killua replies that he competed when he was only six after his father left him there with no money and told him to reach the 200th floor before returning home. He reveals that it took him two years to do so, and Gon is surprised that it took him so long even though he was only six. Killua then tells Gon that if he wants to fight opponents of Hisoka's level, he will need to reach the higher floors of the tower. Gon's number is called, and he nervously prepares to fight, with Killua assuring him that it will be easy for him since he was able to open the Testing Gate. Gon enters the ring and looks across at his enormous opponent as the referee explains the rules and begins the match. The large man promises to end things with a single punch, but Gon easily dodges the attack and uses a simple palm strike just as Killua instructed him, sending the man flying into the wall behind him. As Gon looks at his hand and wonders when he became so strong, the referee gives him a ticket and tells him that he can make his way to the 50th floor. After easily defeating his opponent as well, Killua is told that he can go to the 180th floor since he has reached the 200th floor before, but he politely declines and decides to start at the 50th floor with Gon. Beside Killua, another young boy easily wins his match and also prepares to make his way to the 50th floor. As the three make their way to the 50th floor, an elevator attendant explains how moving up the tower works, and the boy adds that he has heard they will get their own room if they make it to the 100th floor, introducing himself as Zushi. Gon and Killua also gives their names as they reach the 50th floor. Zushi tells Killua how impressed he was by his match, but Killua points out that he made it there in one fight as well. Zushi humbly replies that he has a long way to go, asking the two which discipline of martial arts they use and revealing that he uses the Shingen-ryu fighting technique. The two reply that they don't belong to any school, and Zushi can't believe how strong they are with no training. Zushi's master suddenly appears and praises his student for following his teachings. After Zushi introduces Gon and Killua, Zushi's master introduces himself as Wing and tells them that he didn't expect to see other children, wondering why they are there. Killua tells him that they hope to get stronger and make money. Wing realizes that while they must be skilled to reach the 50th floor, they should pay close attention to their opponents. The three boys then head to a nearby kiosk and receive their prize money of 152. Killua immediately buys a canned drink with the money and reveals that a win in the 50s has a reward of 50,000. He then adds that wins in the 100s are worth 1 million, leaving Gon and Zushi stunned. Killua continues by saying that any wins past the 150th floor are worth 10 million each, with Gon remembering that Killua made it to the 200th floor when he was younger and wondering how much he made. Killua replies that while he quit once he reached it, he had around 200 million in the 190s and spent it all on snacks in four years, with Gon and Zushi left speechless. The three then make their way to a crowded waiting room to prepare for their next match, with Killua assuring them that they will easily win. It's suddenly announced that Killua and Zushi will fight each other on the 57th floor. Killua bluntly tells Gon that he will wait for him above, already confident that he will easily win the match. The announcer introduces the two fighters and shows highlights from their previous matches, asking the crowd to place their bets on who will win. The odds are in Zushi's favor, and Killua is left frustrated by the result. The referee then explains the rules and begins the match. Although impressed by Zushi's fighting stance, Killua calmly walks toward him and avoids his punch before swiftly striking the back of his neck. Killua earns two points for the strike as the referee checks on Zushi, who suddenly rises to his feet and leaves Killua surprised. Zushi unleashes a barrage of punches, but Killua easily dodges them all and again strikes the back of his neck. Zushi recovers again and decides to resort to a new stance that leaves Killua terrified and causes him to quickly leap back. Watching among the crowd, Wing suddenly screams Zushi's name and causes the spectators around him to put their hands over their ears. He sits down with a stern expression on his face, and Zushi appears visibly shaken before the announcer restarts the match. Killua eventually meets up with Gon, who reveals that he won 60,000 before wondering what took him so long. Killua tells him that while Zushi wasn't strong, he has potential and will keep improving. He then reveals that while he was able to knock him around with ease, he couldn't defeat him, admitting that he had to win by TKO from points. He then reveals that Zushi's aura during his new stance reminded him of his brother's, oblivious to what it was but confident that it's dangerous. He guesses that it's a technique and tells Gon that Wing called it Ren. In a flashback, Killua sees Zushi on his hands and knees apologizing to Wing, who reminds him that he wasn't supposed to use Ren yet. Zushi says that he couldn't resist against such a strong opponent, and Wing tells him that while wanting to win is good, he needs to remember his true goal of reaching the top floor. He then adds that focusing on a single win will reduce his potential and that he needs to be willing to lose a thousand times. Back in the present, Gon wonders if Zushi isn't supposed to use Ren until reaching the top floor, and Killua reveals that he now plans to reach the top floor as well, with Gon happily agreeing and telling himself that it was his original goal anyway. Gon and Killua continue to easily defeat all their opponents over the next few days, with both reaching the 100s. They each receive a private room, and while Gon is happy that they don't have to worry about finding a place, Killua points out that if they drop below the 100s, they have to check out. He then warns Gon that the competition will become more difficult since every opponent wants to keep their spot. However, the two continue to easily win and receive more prize money, with both noting that Zushi is still in the 50s. Gon again wonders about the technique called Ren, and while Killua thinks about encountering it with opponents on the higher floors, Gon suggests simply asking Zushi about it. The two do just that, and Zushi explains that it's one of the four major principles for training one's mind and body. He adds that one must know Ten, learn Zetsu, achieve Ren, and reach Hatsu, which are all part of Nen training. As Killua angrily points out that he didn't understand any of what he said, Wing suddenly appears and wonders if Zushi should be teaching them. Killua tells him that he is eager to know what it is since it's connected to the secret of his brother's power. Wing asks if his brother is able to use Nen, but Killua points out that he doesn't even know what Nen and Ren mean, agreeing to go through the complete learning process. Wing tells the two to join him and Zushi at his house as they prepare to learn about the secret technique of Nen.

Episode 28 (1999) Chatting × Excuses × Endurance (おしゃべり×ヘリクツ×根くらべ, "Oshayberi × Herikutsu × Konkurabe") is the 28th episode of the original Hunter × Hunter anime. It first aired on May 20th, 2000. Overview. "The next fight is between Hanzo and Gon. Gon tries his hardest against Hanzo, though he is no match for the ninja. Hanzo severely injures Gon by breaking his arm, but Gon will not admit defeat. Gon feels that if he is to ever find his father, he must pass the Hunter Exam now." Synopsis. Menchi questions the match between Gon and Hanzo, it's noted that Hanzo has an unfair advantage towards Gon relating to their grades and in terms of power and skill set. However, Satotz states that Gon's overall impression made Netero ranked him higher. After a brief conversation between Hanzo and Masta the referee of the match, Gon confidently believes in his skills and has set his plan to fight his opponent. Using his speed Gon runs around the area, but Hanzo is keeping up with him with ease, then Hanzo landed a chop at the back of Gon's neck putting down Gon. Hanzo then helps Gon to stand up for him to stay awake. Gon unsteady from the attack was asked by Hanzo to just quit, refusing to quit Hanzo then slaps Gon behind his back. Hanzo then repeatedly tries to talk Gon into quitting upon refusing again Hanzo slams his head to the ground. Leorio, being worried shouts at Gon encouraging him to quit, but Kurapika who's in the same situation not long ago, tells Leorio that they would do the same if they are in Gon's situation. The examiners, Menchi in particular continue to questions Chairman Netero's method showing their concern towards Gon. Refusing to quit, Gon stands up only to suffer the effects of Hanzo's previous attacked losing his sight for a short period, relying on his sense of hearing he tries to attack Hanzo, Hanzo then counters and proceeds to crush his right ear. With one ear working, Hanzo then continues to encourage Gon to quit but Gon decides to stand up, relying only on his left ear then Killua throws a bottle of water to Gon to get refreshed. In a span of three hours, Gon continues to take damage from Hanzo. Other examinees aren't able to watch the match considering the beatings Gon is taking. Hanzo then tells Gon that he underestimates him for not using his Fishing Rod against him believing he is not worth using a weapon on. Gon then tells him he doesn't underestimate any opponent, then proceeds to tell Hanzo the reason why he did not use the Fishing Rod, as he wants to win the final phase without using the Fishing Rod of his father who had helped all through his journey before the current event. Not convinced with Gon's reasoning Hanzo then continues to attack Gon who is helpless while on the ground. Leorio who can't handle the scene shouts at Hanzo then tells Hanzo to fight him instead, the referees then intervene and warn Leorio that if he interferes with the match then Gon will be disqualified. Upon hearing Leorio, Gon thanked him, struggling to get up he tells Leorio that there is nothing he cannot handle that he will keep on fighting. Pissed at Gon, Hanzo pins Gon then warns him that if he doesn't he will break his arm, Hanzo proceeds in breaking his arm as Gon refuses to quit. As the audiences continue to watch and hear Gon screaming in pain, Leorio whose at his limits tries to tell Kurapika to not stop him if Hanzo lays one more hand on Gon, Kurapika replies that he isn't planning to stop him, as he won't be able to control himself. Then Hanzo suddenly starts talking about his past and took his time talking about it, Gon who gets enough strength due to Hanzo's continuous mumbling, took his chance and lands a kick towards Hanzo's face which brought Hanzo to the ground. Suddenly the atmosphere surrounding the area change. Hanzo back in his feet suddenly pulls out his weapon under his sleeve then warns Gon yet again asking him to surrender otherwise he will cut his legs, Gon in all seriousness tells Hanzo that he doesn't want his leg to get cut, but neither wants to lose then tells Hanzo to settle the matter in another way. In disbelief, Hanzo ludicrously tells Gon that he is not in a position to negotiate, watching the scene unfold examiners and other examinees were surprise and laughs at the situation. Hanzo who is stress out continues to tell Gon about his situation then Gon tells the referee that if Hanzo cuts his legs then he will die resulting in blood loss then Hanzo will be disqualified, Gon then proceeds to convince Hanzo to settle their fight in another way as Hanzo is speechless. Satotz finally sees why Gon ranks higher based on his overall impression, as Gon has a very rare quality bringing people closer to him, Judges, who were supposed to be in the neutral side suddenly routes for Gon as well as the examinees. Hanzo instantly went serious then points his weapons toward Gon's forehead then tells Gon that killing him won't be a problem as he can try to repeat the exam next time, Hanzo losing his patience and questions Gon on being stubborn, refusing to quit, risking his life when he can still have another chance to try again. Gon responds and said that the reason he doesn't want to quit is because of his father he wants to find him and if he gives up now then he won't be able to find him. Hanzo went on to tell Gon that he is finished, pulling up his weapon in a striking position as a drop of blood falls to the ground.

Episode 28 (2011) Nen × And × Nen (ネン×ト×ネン, "Nen × To × Nen") is the 28th episode of the Hunter × Hunter 2011 series. It first aired on April 22nd, 2012. Overview. "Gon and Killua are taught by Wing about the four principles of Nen. After graduating to the 200s, Gon and Killua run into Hisoka." Summary. Wing teaches Gon, Killua and Zushi in his room. He explains the 4 main principles: Ten, Zetsu, Ren and Hatsu, or Focus, Express, Temper, and Act, respectively. Wing tells Killua he'll think about killing him. He demonstrates Ten by focusing his body; Zetsu by saying the words "I'll kill you"; and Ren by giving off a strong aura of an intent to kill. Because of the strong pressure, Killua jumps back, hanging on the ceiling corner of the room. Wing advises them to train with Zushi and start mastering Ten, but Killua suggests that they should leave. Killua reveals to Gon that Wing lied to them. He admits that Wing's explanation made perfect sense and that his strength is clearly real, but it can't explain how Zushi was able to withstand his last attack with sheer willpower. Back in the room, Wing notices Zushi's Ten is unstable. Zushi then asks why Wing lied to Gon and Killua. Wing tells Zushi that the "Nen" he explained is, in fact, important for learning the real Nen, and adds that he also cannot teach the real Nen to those that are not his students. Wing rips out a page in a book, uses Nen to sharpen it, and easily slices a soda can from across the room in half. As Zushi stands in shock, Wing tells him that anyone can use Nen with enough work, so one must use caution before teaching someone how to use it. After clearing the 190th floor, Gon and Killua advance to the 200th floor. They are stopped by a strong aura of a murderous intent which prevents them from moving forward. They barely get through it as the receptionist appears, stating that they need to register before midnight. Hisoka appears out of nowhere, in front of the two behind the receptionist, and warns them that they are not ready yet. He prevents Gon and Killua from progressing with powerful Nen. Wing appears behind them to stop them from hurting themselves and offers to teach them the real Nen. Before they leave, the receptionist informs Killua that if he isn't able to register at the given time, he will never be able to register again since he failed to register once before when he was younger. In Wing's room, Gon and Killua are finally taught the real Nen. Wing tells Gon and Killua that they must learn Nen to protect themselves from other Nen users, explaining that they must use Ten for defense. To demonstrate how destructive Nen can be to the human body, he puts his hand against one of the room's walls and suddenly damages it, leaving Gon and Killua stunned.

Episode 29 (1999) Pass! × Fail? × Exam Over (合格！×失格？×試験終了, "Gōkaku! × Shikkaku? × Shiken Shūryō") is the 29th episode of the original Hunter × Hunter anime. It first aired on May 27th, 2000. Overview. "Hanzo decides to forfeit his match against Gon. Gon stubbornly argues with Hanzo as he cannot accept the way he won and keeps on telling Hanzo to settle the match in another way, but Hanzo knocks Gon unconscious. Gon awakes and is accompanied by Satotz, both of them went to discuss various things about being a Hunter. Gon finally accepts his Hunter License and now is officially a Hunter. Satotz then proceeds to details the results of the tournament, as Killua finds out that his opponent is his own brother, Illumi disguised as Gittarackur." Synopsis. Hanzo gives up and sheaths his weapon and decided to try to win his next match, Gon refuses to accept Hanzo's decision as he insists on the idea of settling the match in another way, As the two argue, Hanzo hit's Gon with a single punch knocking him out. Gon wins the match and became the next examinee to pass the Hunter Exam. Chairman Netero confirms that even if Gon refuses to accept the results, he won't be able to do anything as he's now a Hunter and it will stay that way once his decision is made. The unconscious Gon is being escorted out of the room. Satotz then gives Hanzo his word that he will take care of Gon once he awakes. Killua then approaches Hanzo asking him why did he decided to lose on purpose as there are plenty of ways to make Gon surrender without killing him, upon saying that all other examinees look at Hanzo having the same thought as Killua then Hanzo state that he never felt any hatred towards Gon even after torturing him, he couldn't be able to fight him anymore that is why he gave up. The next fight begins between Hisoka and Bodoro, Hisoka mocks Bodoro, then Bodoro charges towards him. Gon finally awakes, besides him is Satotz. Then the two talks to each other as Satotz extends his hand to congratulate Gon after giving some advice. Gon refuses to shake Satotz hand as he didn't want to win that way. Then Satotz tries to motivate him, Gon who is still having trouble with how weak he is and continues to feel sorry for himself. Able to grasp Gon's situation, Satotz tells Gon that no matter what he's thinks he cannot change the fact that he is already a Hunter then further explains the reason why he was able to go this far, then he explains about the Hunter License and states that he can do whatever he wants with it such as keeping, throwing, or even selling the license, then further explains the importance and worth of the Hunters License as he can never be able to obtain another one once he passed the Hunters Exam. Upon hearing Satotz, Gon states that he needs to decide on what kind of Hunter he wanted to be, Satotz then gives Gon another motivational speech and tells him the importance of friendship. Gon asks Satotz what kind of work he did at the beginning after he became a Hunter. Satotz reveals that his field is restoration and protection of ancient ruins, then tells Gon about the man who inspired him to be better at his field and wanted to meet him to thank him then he asks Gon if he is familiar with the Ruins of Lurka. Upon hearing this Gon realizes that Satotz inspiration is his father, Ging Freecss. Satotz presents Gon's Hunter License to which he accepted and finally shakes Satotz handshake, then states that he will use his License once he repaid all of his friends who help him become a Hunter. It was revealed that Gon slept for a day and that the Tournament is finally over, then Gon asks Satotz who fails the exam, in a brief moment of silence Gon's heart throb's as he sees a glimpse of Killua in his imagination. Satotz then informs Gon about the matches. Hisoka and Bodoro's match is completely one-sided in favor of Hisoka as he just toys with Bodoro, despite Bodoro's courage he did not stand a chance against Hisoka as he surrenders when Hisoka whispers something in his ear. Pokkle immediately surrenders his match after Hanzo warns him that he will do the same method as he did with Gon, Leorio pleads with the committee to postpone his match with Bodoro so that his opponent can be able to recover from the injuries he took from Hisoka and Netero granted his wish. Killua being arrogant purposely surrenders the match against Pokkle without even fighting him. By forfeiting that match, Killua made a terrible miscalculation, Gittarackur being the opponent of Killua remove the pins in his face and finally reveals his true identity, Killua immediately recognizes his brother Illumi.

Episode 29 (2011) Awakening × And × Potential (カクセイ×ト×カノウセイ, "Kakusei × To × Kanōsei") is the 29th episode of the Hunter × Hunter 2011 series. It first aired on April 29th, 2012. Overview. "After having their Nen released and learning Ten, Gon and Killua are able to pass Hisoka's aura and sign up for a fight. Right after they register, three of the 200th floor fighters are eager to challenge them." Summary. Wing's lesson continues into the night, and it's stated that Gon and Killua must learn Nen before midnight. Wing reveals that while the power of Nen dwells within every person, only a few are capable of using it and are considered geniuses, psychics, superhumans, etc. He explains that there are two ways to awaken the power: deliberately or aggressively (with Zushi having used the former). He adds that Zushi learned quickly and trained hard, allowing him to master Ten in six months. Killua quickly reminds him that they need to learn Ten and pass through Hisoka's barrier before midnight. Wing tells them that they will have to try the aggressive method, and Killua wonders if it will be fast enough. After explaining that the key is learning to contain their aura within their bodies, Wing tells the two that he will now direct his aura toward them, known as Hatsu, the same technique that he used to destroy the wall. With both Gon and Killua left worried, Wing assures them that he will restrain himself so he doesn't destroy their bodies. However, he warns them that the process of forcing open a person's aura nodes is dangerous since it usually takes months for someone to slowly open the nodes on their own. Although he reveals that it took someone as talented as Zushi three months to complete the process, he is confident that it would take Gon and Killua one week at most. He regrets that they have as little time as they do, but Killua points out that the quick method is always better. However, Wing seriously replies that this specific method is dangerous and usually avoided since they could die if the person using it were weak or evil. Gon rightly points out that Wing is neither of the two, and Killua wonders why he suddenly decided to teach them the real four major principles. Wing replies that he didn't want to waste the opportunity since they would stand no chance if they were to compete above the 200th floor since every fighter there knows Nen. He then reveals that the veterans attack new fighters with Nen to awaken them without restraint and don't care if they die as a result, with the survivors sometimes becoming disfigured and maimed. However, he is confident that the method will awaken their power since they both have the necessary potential and ability. He then tells them to put down their belongings, take off their overshirts, and turn their backs toward him. They follow his instructions, and Wing holds his hands near both of their backs, with the two immediately feeling the heat and pressure. As Killua is reminded of Illumi's Nen (although a much weaker version), Wing begins the process and sends his aura through both their bodies, successfully opening all their aura nodes. As a strange substance flows from them both, Wing explains that it's their aura (life energy). Gon likens it to smoke or steam rising out of a kettle, and Killua worries about so much of it leaving their bodies. Wing tells them that they will become tired if enough escapes and eventually collapse from fatigue if they expend all of it. He quickly gets their attention and tells them to concentrate on containing the aura within their bodies, asking them to close their eyes, visualize the aura flowing like blood through them, and picture it hovering around their bodies. The two immediately master the technique, leaving Zushi stunned and Wing in awe as he says to himself that they are incredible for realizing the most effective stance without needing to be told. Wing tells them to slowly open their eyes, and Gon describes the sensation as being surrounded by warm mucus, with Killua saying that he feels like he's wearing weightless clothes. Wing tells them to remember the feeling and that they will eventually be able to use Ten while sleeping. He then suddenly prepares to use hostile Nen against them, explaining that it would have been too painful for them to withstand it before. Killua understands his earlier blizzard analogy, and Wing assures them that if they can withstand the attack, they will be able to make it through Hisoka's barrier, suddenly sending out his aura as Gon and Killua are heard yelling. Back on the 200th floor, Gon and Killua appear before Hisoka, who quickly sends out his Nen toward them. However, with both now using Ten, they confidently walk toward him and easily pass through his barrier. Hisoka dispels his Nen and welcomes them to the 200s, guessing that Gon came to Heavens Arena to train before challenging him. Gon replies that he didn't expect to find Hisoka there and that it saves him time, causing Hisoka to chuckle and tell Gon that he shouldn't become too confident now that he can use Ten. He reveals that they have much more to learn about Nen, holding up two fingers and creating various shapes using his aura. He tells Gon that while he currently has no desire to fight him, he will agree to a match if he is able to win even once in the 200s. After Hisoka walks away, three other fighters watch the two boys and see that they are able to use Nen. A female clerk happily welcomes the two to the 200s and asks them to fill out the necessary forms, wondering if they would also like to register for a match. She assures them that they have 90 days in which to choose a date, warning them that they will be disqualified and their name struck from all records if they don't fight before then. She also reveals that they need ten wins to clear the floor and that if they lose four matches before then, they will also be disqualified. She then excitedly reveals that if they win ten matches, they will have the chance to fight the Floor Masters, the 21 strongest fighters at Heavens Arena who control floors 230 to 250. She adds that they will become the new master of the floor and be able to participate in the Battle Olympia tournament if they defeat its current owner. Gon and Killua are left unimpressed by the explanation, with the latter wondering if the top floor has anything special. The clerk angrily explains that the winner of Battle Olympia gets to live in the penthouse at the top of the tower, but Gon points out that Killua's house is 3,700 meters above ground. Before the official can reveal the amount of prize money, Killua says that he doesn't care about reaching the top floor anymore, with Gon adding that he only wants to fight Hisoka. As the clerk begins to cry and wonders why the two are even there, Killua reminds Gon that he will need to win at least one fight, asking him if he plans to wait first. Gon clenches his fist and reveals that he plans to fight immediately so that he can find out how different the opponents are. As Gon fills out the necessary form, the three fighters approach the two boys and reveal that they are simply waiting to register. Killua realizes that they want to fight on the same day as Gon, who tells the clerk that he is prepared to fight on any day. The three fighters chuckle and remain confident before the clerk gives Gon and Killua their room numbers and promises to let them know on which day they will fight. As the two leave to go to their rooms, Killua glances back at the three fighters and guesses that they must have endured the initiation that Wing mentioned, realizing that they could have ended up like them if they hadn't learned about Nen first. Gon, however, is more focused on how nice his room is, with both happily taking in a view of the city at night. The two suddenly notice a message on the television stating that Gon's fight will take place at 3 p.m. on March 11, and Killua can't believe that it's already been scheduled for the next day. Gon calmly practices using Ten and says that while he probably won't win the fight, he needs to experience a Nen battle and see what he can do with his newfound power. On the day of the match, the announcer introduces Gon first and then his opponent, Gido, who has a 4-1 record. In a flashback, Wing tells Gon and Killua that Ten is used only for defense and reminds the two that they have not worked on their offense at all. He also warns them that a highly skilled Nen user will be able to break through their Ten to deal a possibly lethal strike, asking that they both wait at least two months before their first match and offering to teach them as much as possible during that time. Back in the present, Gon apologizes to Wing and smiles as he tells himself that he's just too eager to fight. As Zushi watches with a smile on his face, Wing is left exasperated by Gon's decision to fight so soon. The referee begins the match, and Gon immediately uses Ten. Gido chuckles in reply and suddenly reveals several spinning tops that move along his walking stick. As the announcer calls them his Dancing Tops, Gido uses his Battle Waltz ability and sends them flying toward Gon. The tops spin all around him and bounce into each other, with one suddenly striking him in the back. Gon quickly recovers, and Gido is given one point for a clean hit. Gido explains that he can use his Nen to allow the tops to spin for hours, revealing that their attack patterns are so complex that even he can't predict their movements. Gon dodges multiple tops and is left worried since each one hits as hard as a hammer, nervously waiting for another to strike.

Episode 2 (1999) Encounter × Hesitation × Departure (出会い×とまどい×出航, "Deai × Tomadoi × Shukkou") is the 2nd episode of the original Hunter × Hunter anime. It aired on October 23rd, 1999. The events of this episode did not occur in the manga. Overview. "Gon arrives at a port town to find a ship that takes passengers to Dolle Harbor. He meets a man named Leorio, who is also intent on taking the exam. With his help, Gon is able to free animals from a cruel exhibition, including a Foxbear cub that was caught by a man claiming to be a Hunter. The man is revealed to be a fake when Leorio takes him down and discovers his fake Hunter license. Afterward, Gon and Leorio manage to board the ship heading to to Dolle." Synopsis. Leorio, hungry and penniless, notices an arm-wrestling event involving someone that claims to be a Hunter. The individuals running the event offer prize money and admission to an animal exhibition at the port to anyone who can defeat the Hunter. Leorio challenges the Hunter to a match, but he loses his strength due to hunger and was unable to win. Gon approaches and offers an apple, as he had heard Leorio's stomach growl during the match. Gon asks for information on how to get to Dolle Harbor, but Leorio ignores him. A man overhears Gon and offers to take him there, and the boy agrees to follow him without suspecting a thing. Leorio notices this and calls the man out for attempted kidnapping. The man tries to stab him, but Leorio is able to block the attack and knocks him down. The man runs off after realizing he stood no chance against him. Gon begins to follow Leorio again. Although Leorio tries to escape him, Gon is able to catch up to him every time. At a restaurant, a waiter approaches Kurapika but backs away when he sees a poisonous spider on his table. Kurapika's eyes briefly flash red and swiftly gets rid of the spider with his fork. Nearby, a man is seen stealing fish and the clerk chases after the thief. Leorio uses this opportunity to steal some fish for himself. While eating, a man steals Leorio's briefcase but Gon uses his fishing rod to retrieve it. Leorio gives up and tells Gon that the Kaijinmaru is the ship that takes passengers to Dolle Harbor. The Kaijinmaru arrives at the port, and Leorio is seen working at the arm-wrestling Hunter's animal exhibition to pay for the ship ride. He sees the Hunter walk by with a caged Foxbear cub. While looking for the Kaijinmaru at the port, a man reels Gon into the animal exhibition. Meanwhile, Leorio serves tea for his employer, who then begins to open up a safe to pay the Hunter for the Foxbear cub. Leorio is dismissed, but continues to eavesdrop on their conversation. At the exhibition, the crowd panics as Gon approaches an agitated adult Foxbear. He is reminded of Konta and reaches out to it, feeling sorry for the caged creature. The Foxbear licks Gon's hand and the surrounding people are impressed by his ability to tame it. The Hunter along with the exhibition owner confronts Gon. The Foxbear sees the Hunter holding its cub in a handheld cage and tries to attack him, but is unable to reach. Gon begins to wonder if this is what Hunters really are. Gon is imprisoned along with the Foxbear, but is able to escape when Leorio brings him the keys. Gon decides to use the keys to free all of the caged animals, and is approached by the exhibition owner and the Hunter. Gon tells them that they are bad people, and that he isn't a Hunter. He prepares to attack Gon when Leorio appears and punches the Hunter in the face, knocking him unconscious. He then shows Gon the guy's fake Hunter License, saying that a real Hunter wouldn't have been taken down from a single punch. The two run towards the Kaijinmaru, but the ship has already embarked and left the shore. Seeing that they are still after the ship, the Captain tells them that they are already too late and that he won't stop the ship for them. Gon tells Leorio to follow him and they get to higher ground. Gon has Leorio grab on to him as he uses his fishing rod to swing them on to the ship. They were successful, and Leorio finally tells Gon his name. As Gon bids Whale Island farewell, the Captain notes that he won't be bored on this year's trip to Dolle.

Episode 2 (2011) Test × Of × Tests (シケン×ノ×シケン, "Shiken × No × Shiken") is the 2nd episode of the Hunter × Hunter 2011 anime. It first aired on October 9th, 2011. Overview. "Gon, Kurapika and Leorio reach Dolle Harbor and are given a tip by the captain to head for the cedar tree on the hilltop behind the city. Moving through a small town, the three are stopped by a group of masked people and an old woman posts a riddle requiring them to choose between two possible answers." Summary. Upon reaching Dolle Harbor, the Captain tells Gon that going to the cedar tree at the top of the hill behind the city will lead them to the exam site. Gon relays the information to Kurapika and Leorio and they consult the map. They learn that the cedar tree is the opposite direction of Zaban City, the Hunter Exam site. Leorio says that there is a bus that directly goes to the city. Kurapika comments that the vague exam notice given to them is another test for the applicants. Gon chooses to go towards the direction of the tree; Kurapika follows suit after telling Leorio that he is curious about what Gon might do. Leorio bids goodbye as well and walks towards the bus stop when he overhears two senior applicants talking about the bus ride as merely a trap for new applicants. Leorio joins the other two and they reach a small deserted town. Leorio comments that there is nobody around there, but Gon plainly states that there are plenty of them. A group of masked people appear and block the way with a stage where an old woman sits. She tells them that they have to undergo the quiz in order to reach the cedar tree. She posts a riddle requiring them to choose between two possible answers and giving the answer within five seconds. The three are taken aback by the question for it is something that has no correct answer. Unfortunately, refusing to partake in the quiz will disqualify them from taking the exam. A scheming participant who overheard the conversation between the captain and Gon has followed the three and goes ahead to answer. The masked people let him by as he continues up the road. The old woman then poses a similar question to the three, angering Leorio even more. It dawns on Kurapika that it is a trick question and is about to tell Leorio when the old woman forbids them from communicating with each other. When the time is up and no one has given an answer, Leorio angrily grabs a wooden stick to hit the woman, but is stopped by Kurapika. Kurapika tells Leorio to calm down for he will waste the correct answer, which is silence. A door to a tunnel opens, and they are instructed to meet the navigators living in a house by the cedar tree. Upon reaching the cedar tree, they find the navigators, a couple being attacked by a shape-shifting creature, the Kiriko. While Leorio tends to the wounded man, Gon and Kurapika go after the Kiriko who kidnaps the woman. They are able to keep up with the Kiriko and Gon hits it with his fishing rod. The Kiriko drops the woman and is saved by Kurapika, but he notices a tattoo on her arm and he becomes wary of her real identity. Leorio comes, stating that he has given the wounded man painkillers. Kurapika then attacks him. This Leorio turns out to be another Kiriko in disguise and asks how Kurapika knew. Kurapika states that even if he was Leorio, he would have still hit him for leaving a wounded person alone. The Kiriko leaves and Kurapika asks the woman who she really is. Meanwhile, Gon loses sight of the Kiriko momentarily, then it appears and he follows it. He loses sight of it again, then the Kiriko jumps from a tree and corners Gon. Gon is about to be hit when he flatly says that the Kiriko is not the one he is pursuing. The Kiriko laughs hysterically and calls out its partner. The three applicants reunite and the couple reveals themselves to be the offspring of the two Kirikos. They pass the three due to their unique characteristics and fly them to the exam site.

Episode 30 (1999) Killua × Disqualified × Forced Out (キルア×リタイア×強制送還, "Kirua × Ritaia × Kyōsei Sōkan") is the 30th episode of the original Hunter × Hunter anime. It first aired on June 3rd, 2000. Overview. "Satotz tells Gon that Killua failed the final phase. His opponent was his older brother Illumi in disguise. He thinks Killua should just be an assassin and return home. Illumi threatens to kill Gon if Killua doesn't comply. Killua murders Bodoro in the middle of a match with Leorio and is disqualified. Gon confronts Illumi and decides to look for Killua." Synopsis. Upon revealing his true identity, Illumi tells Killua that their mother was happy that Killua is all grown up. However, she expressed concern that Killua set off alone. When his older brother proceeds to ask him why he wanted to be a Hunter, Killua replies that he doesn't plan on becoming a Hunter and that he was just bored and got nothing to do. Gladly hearing Killua's words, Illumi then tries to discourage Killua from being a Hunter that his path on being an assassin is the only way. Illumi keeps on discouraging Killua then tells him that becoming a hunter is not only the reason as there are other things he wanted such as becoming friends with Gon. Illumi upon hearing further discourage Killua from his relationship with others particularly with Gon and proceeds to embed the ways of the assassin to him. Then Leorio intervenes with their discussion and tells Killua to not listen to his brother and that he doesn't need to do anything as he is already a friend of Gon. Upon hearing Leorio, Illumi tells being a friend of Gon can cause a lot of problems since assassins don't need friends which complicates things, then states that he needs to kill Gon. Killua gets frightened, Illumi then tries to go to Gon whereabouts but as soon as he tries to Leorio, Kurapika and Hanzo stand on his way preventing him from entering the quarters where Gon is resting. Then Illumi realizes that killing them including Gon won't benefit him as he will be the one failing the exam and other remaining examinees including his brother will become Hunters, then he decides to pass the exam first then kill Gon later as the committees cannot revoke it since the exam is over by then. Then threatens Killua that to save Gon he needs to beat him then reminds Killua that he doesn't stand a chance against Illumi or anyone superior to him. Approaching Killua as he continues to talk to him in a manipulative way his hand tries to reach Killua then warns him not to move then continues to threaten him. Leorio then tries to encourage Killua to beat Illumi as they will protect Gon no matter what, much to their surprise Killua surrenders. Then Illumi told Killua he is glad that he quit as he doesn't want to fight him then reveals that he is just joking as he doesn't plan on killing him. Killua's mind went blank as he sits towards a corridor lifeless. The match between Leorio and Bodoro is about to begin, Killua stabs Bodoro at the back resulting in him being disqualified and the Hunter Exam ended. Upon hearing the story, Gon rushes towards the briefing room where other Hunters are being briefed by Chairman Netero then went directly towards Illumi then demands him to apologize to Killua, Illumi refuting his words, Gon then tells Illumi that he is not qualified to be his brother, Illumi questions him if there any qualification being a brother. Gon grabs Illumi tightly and forcefully pulls him out of his seat then states that there's no qualification to be friends with someone either. Gon tightens his grip, then tells him to bring him with Killua as he wants him to bring Killua back and distance him away from his family. Illumi then tells Gon that Killua walked out of his own free will but Gon believes that Illumi brainwashed his brother. Netero then speaks and tells Gon that the matter of which Killua being brainwashed is being discussed before he enters the room as Leorio and Kurapika raise their complaint on Killua's behalf. Kurapika then talks as he explains that it became clear to them that Killua was hypnotized and that his actions were not his own, then Leorio tells everyone if Killua has the intentions of helping Leorio wins the match then they are wrong since Killua's actions made him failed the exam instead of Leorio. Then Netero, their reasons are hypothesis with no evidence to back them up then summarize the match between Leorio as he thought Leorio has the advantage towards Bodoro even if he had the experience as Leorio's youth comes to effect specially Bodoro is not on his top condition. Pokkle questions Kurapika's victory as he thought he and Hisoka had an agreement based on his conclusion towards Bodoro and Hisoka's match and his match against Hanzo, Kurapika then mocks him for winning in default. Gon speaks and tells that there is no point in arguing, as all of them passed and if one believed that they aren't deserving then it's up to them to change them then states that he believes Killua can pass the exam, but felt sorry for getting disqualified, then blames Illumi for turning his brother into an assassin and made him kill someone out of his own will, then tells him that he will take Killua away from him and his family. Illumi then tries to touch him but Gon quick in his feet backs up. Then Netero speaks and decided to not overturn any decision then announces that the current Hunter Exam is over then he congratulates all seven who passed the exam. Gon then confronts Illumi wanting to know Killua's whereabouts.

Episode 30 (2011) Fierce × And × Ferocious (ゲキトウ×ト×カットウ, "Gekitō × To × Kattō") is the 30th episode of the Hunter × Hunter 2011 series. It first aired on May 6th, 2012. Overview. "Gon and Gido's fight concludes with Gon injured and Wing upset. Kurapika, who tries to find work as a Hunter, is rejected, but runs into a mysterious man who offers to teach him Nen." Summary. As the battle between Gon and Gido continues, Gon struggles because of Gido's Nen tops. His Ten also gradually begins to fade. A hit from a top sends him outside the ring. Gon notices a top not attacking him outside the ring. He then understands that the tops simply attack anything getting in their way and gets an idea to attack Gido while ignoring the tops. But Gon fails because Gido uses another Nen ability called Tornado Top, which involves his whole body spinning like a top to improve his defense. Due to Gon's willingness to fight, he conceals his presence without knowing it with Zetsu, one of the 4 main principles of Nen. Wing is amazed, but can't stop worrying about Gon's situation. As the fight resumes, Gon dodges all of Gido's tops for a certain period of time, but eventually is warned by Killua and ends up in a no-escape situation. He gets his arm broken and loses the match. Wing is upset with Gon's decision to fight so soon. He gives him a condition that he must not practice or study Nen until he is fully recovered. Wing wraps a "promise thread" on Gon's finger to remind him about it. Killua tells Wing how Gon felt during his match against Gido, explaining how Gon becomes too excited over new challenges. He adds if Wing quits teaching them, they'll manage to find a new teacher or learn Nen by themselves. However, Wing plans to continue teaching the two. Meanwhile, Kurapika searches for a job and is tested by the Sengi Guild agent who looks up employers for Hunters. She creates a skull laughing face and asks if Kurapika could see it. But he fails to see it because of his lack of knowledge about a certain technique. As he walks, a mysterious man passes him on the street and steals Kurapika's license without him noticing. The man later tosses a piece of stone towards Kurapika in a forest, which he dodges and it hits a part of a tree and destroys it. As Kurapika stands wonder-struck, the man shows up and confronts him. He says that he cannot see it, but can sense it approaching. Kurapika then gets angry and orders him to return his Hunter License. The man dares Kurapika to get his license back from him. Later, Kurapika is seen down on both his knees, frustrated about his failure in retrieving his license. The mysterious man gives back his license, tells him his name, and says the real exam is about to begin.

Episode 31 (1999) Disband × Party × Unpleasant Ties (解散×パーティ×くされ縁, "Kaisan × Pāti × Kusare En") is the 31st episode of the original Hunter × Hunter anime. It first aired on June 10th, 2000. Overview. "Gon doesn't believe that Killua left on his own accord and wants to find him. He fights Illumi for information, and Illumi is about to kill him when Hisoka shows up. Illumi tells Gon that Killua is at the Zoldyck family home. Leorio is going to medical school, and Kurapika is to leave for his first job when they both change their minds and decide to help Gon find Killua." Synopsis. Illumi and Hisoka speak outside in the courtyard of the final exam location. Illumi expresses his disappointment in how the Hunter Exam ended so quickly. At the same time, Hisoka says he's okay with how things turned out since he found Gon as a result. Illumi explains how Gon may pose a lot of trouble for Illumi in the future, to which Hisoka calmly threatens Illumi about not touching Gon, and Illumi drops the subject and walks away. Inside the building, Beans explains the rules and benefits of the Hunter License to Gon, who missed the explanation previously due to his injuries. However, Gon is completely distracted, only thinking about confronting Illumi about Killua's whereabouts soon since the new Hunters will depart the next day. Hanzo amicably approaches Kurapika and Leorio, who are respectively using a hookah pipe and drinking tea at a table in the lobby of the hotel where the new Hunters are staying until the next day. He asks the two to join him on a trip to town to pick up some souvenirs. They both turn him down, with Leorio saying he's too broke to go, and Hanzo gets annoyed at them. Pokkle joins Hanzo's side to ask if the two are waiting for Gon. When they confirm that's why they're waiting around, Hanzo understands and leaves. Pokkle sticks around and apologizes to Kurapika for their previous argument when they were getting their Hunter Licenses. However, Pokkle is in much better spirits now and tells Kurapika and Leorio about his goal to travel around the world and discover new species of creatures. Once Pokkle walks off, Leorio expresses his envy of Pokkle's excitement. He worries over how difficult a mission it will be for them to get Killua back. Beans continues to explain things to Gon, who is clearly not paying attention. The clock strikes three, and Gon is technically free to go, so he runs for it out of the room even as Beans tries to get him to stay for the rest of the explanation. As he runs by Netero, Netero trips him and tries to test his knowledge. Initially, Gon is unable to answer, and has to return to his seat. However, Gon eventually remembers something Satotz had told him previously and manages to come up with an answer for Netero. Netero accepts the response and dismisses Gon, who runs off. In the hotel lobby, Gon speaks with the worker at the front desk before running into the elevator, trying to figure out if Illumi would still be in the hotel and where. As the doors close on Gon's elevator, he catches sight of Illumi disguised as Gittarackur and gets wedged in the closing doors trying to run out after him. He manages to get out, but Illumi is gone by then and doesn't seem to hear Gon yelling after him or likely chooses to ignore him. During the commotion, Leorio and Kurapika notice Gon and stop him from running after Illumi. Leorio tries to convince Gon that Illumi won't give him the information he's looking for and to not go after Killua alone. He warns Gon that making enemies with the Zoldycks is not a good idea, but Gon insists that he doesn't believe Killua left the exam of his own accord and needs help. Kurapika agrees that Killua seemed strange when he left but isn't entirely convinced. Gon runs off without the two, upset. Gon walks out into the courtyard, where Illumi had been waiting for him undisguised. Illumi offers to fight Gon for the information he wants about Killua. Gon immediately lunges at Illumi, but Illumi can easily dodge and grab Gon's non-broken arm. While Illumi tightly squeezes Gon's arm, Gon gets the same cold, evil feeling from being in contact with Illumi that he had gotten previously. Gon jumps out of Illumi's grasp, and Illumi repeatedly throws sets of needles at Gon, who continues to dodge them. Illumi decides against Hisoka's wishes not to kill and hits Gon with a needle. Gon falls to the ground in pain. Illumi intends to kill Gon with a needle, but Gon manages to escape the attack using his fishing rod. He swings in the air, and with Illumi temporarily unable to see Gon because of the sun, Gon slams into Illumi and knocks him over. When Illumi gets up, his mouth is bleeding and he says he was impressed with Gon's attack. Illumi insists that Killua left the exam of his own accord, despite Gon not believing him. Illumi goes to kill Gon again, paralyzed by Illumi's previous touch. However, before Illumi can throw his needle, Hisoka appears on the sidelines, and Illumi immediately backs off. While walking away, he relents and tells Gon that Killua is back home on Kukuroo Mountain. Illumi tells Gon to stop following him now that he knows where to go to find Killua. He walks off, and Leorio and Kurapika join Gon's side. The three have no clue where Kukuroo Mountain is, but once at a computer, Kurapika uses his Hunter License to surf the internet and gain some information about the place. He tells them the trip there will take three days, and Leorio asks Gon if he's serious about going. After Gon responds in the affirmative, Leorio uses his license to try and search for Gon's dad. Leorio finds a result for him, but cannot print the information about him. Kurapika claims that Ging is classified in the database and that Gon's dad must be very important. That night, on the way to the ceremony for the new Hunters, Gon stops to ask Satotz about the card given to him by Kite that he originally thought was a Hunter License. Satotz explains that it's a certification for a Double Star Hunter, belonging to Ging. Satotz tells Gon a bit more about Ging's accomplishments but claims Ging is a total mystery, and that he's never met him in person. At the ceremony, Hanzo takes pictures of the new Hunters and a drunken Menchi. Pokkle is surprised to hear that Leorio, Kurapika, and Gon will be going their separate ways. Leorio and Kurapika explain how different their goals are, while Gon stands alone on the balcony, thinking about his memories with Killua. Illumi and Hisoka are not shown at the ceremony, but show up the following day when the examiners see the new Hunters off. Hanzo hands out his business cards to Leorio, Kurapika, and Gon, telling them to keep in touch. After saying their goodbyes, everyone but Hisoka and Illumi walks off. Hisoka tells Illumi not to touch Gon again, and Illumi agrees, uninterested in making enemies. Illumi asks about Hisoka's current plans and listens to Hisoka ramble about Gon's future potential. While walking off, Gon thanks Leorio and Kurapika for all they've done and says his goodbyes. After Gon runs off, Leorio and Kurapika stumble over their goodbyes to each other and end up both agreeing that they could still pursue their dreams while helping Gon get to Kukuroo Mountain. They run off after Gon, and the three board an airship together to begin their journey to the mountain.

Episode 31 (2011) Destiny × And × Tenacity (インネン×ト×シュウネン, "In'nen × To × Shūnen") is the 31st episode of the Hunter × Hunter 2011 series. It first aired on May 13th, 2012. Overview. "Gon recovers from his injuries in a month. He wants to see the match between Hisoka and Kastro, but Wing does not allow him. Then, Killua goes to see the match and tells him what happened." Summary. One month has passed, and people are getting excited about an upcoming match. Killua walks into Gon's room, shocked to find him working out on his once broken arm and astounded Gon is completely healed. He easily walks on his hands, which is confusing, as Killua thinks it should have taken four months to heal. He calls Gon weird, much to Gon's displeasure. The real reason Killua came to visit was to give him tickets to an upcoming Hisoka fight. Killua, after getting some information, has found out Hisoka's record is 8-3, 6 KOs, all death KOs. The only losses he has are from fights he never showed up to. This means technically, Hisoka has never lost in the arena. Furthermore, out of the 8 fights, he's only given up 4 points, which is Floor Master material. Gon begins shaking with anticipation of their next fight together. Hisoka's opponent is Kastro, the man who scored the points off him. Killua hopes Gon can learn some kind of strategy to fight Hisoka during the match, but Gon worries about the promise he made to Wing about not training in Nen for 2 months. Killua says it'll be fine until right in front of them, unnoticed by the two, is Wing with Zushi. He strictly prohibits Gon from watching the match. Even though Gon is healed, the mandate still stands, so he must wait another month. He tells Gon to practice Ten in the meantime. Killua decides to go alone and see the match for himself, while Wing is glad Gon has kept his promise so far. Later that day, Gon is watching TV when an announcement for Hisoka's match comes up. He turns off the TV, looking at the thread Wing tied on his finger, remembering his promise. It was two years ago Kastro lost his match to Hisoka and is looking for revenge. Cocco, the announcer, mentions Kastro's 9-1 record, one away from the Floor Masters. Killua decides to sneak into Kastro's room to get a better feel for him. He slips past the employee guarding the floor and notices that the door to Kastro's room is slightly opened. As he gets closer, he sees Kastro sitting on a couch and activates Zetsu before approaching the door and peers inside the room. Suddenly, Kastro asks what he's doing from behind. Killua is petrified, looking back in the room to find the couch empty. He tries to wrap his brain around how this happened, but just ends up causing more questions. He playfully asks for an autograph, but Kastro already knows who he is. He even knows he's friends with Gon. He commends Killua on his Zetsu, but says he triggered it too late. Killua asks how he was able to sneak up on him, but Kastro keeps it a secret, for one day they might fight each other. Finally, Hisoka and Kastro stand in the ring together. Kastro thanks Hisoka for giving him the motivation to become stronger and that all the matches up until now have just been practice. As soon as the referee says start, Kastro charges, taking a swing at Hisoka's head. Though he dodges, Hisoka still feels a sharp clean punch to the face, with a surprised look on it. Killua sits in awe, still contemplating how Kastro was able to do that attack. Hisoka just smiles and laughs. Kastro attacks again, making it easy for Hisoka to see his left hand charging up, Hisoka dodges, but just like before, a strong swipe comes across the left side of his face. Now the whole audience was quiet. Kastro is on the attack once again with Hisoka pulling back. He blocks a kick, only for Kastro to appear behind him and hit him anyway, this time a knockdown: the score now 4-0, Kastro. Wing and Zushi are watching, Wing most likely already able to tell what's going on. The referee asks Hisoka if he can continue. He merely smiles again, the same as before and tries to understand how Kastro keeps disappearing. Kastro begins to charge his special attack, Tiger Bite Fist, causing the crowd to go wild. Hisoka mockingly gives up his left arm, but Kastro takes his right. The crowd screams as his arm flew through the air. Hisoka claims it's part of a plan, dodging another attack from Kastro and catching his arm. Hisoka has determined Kastro's Nen ability is making a double and he confirms it. In front of everyone, Kastro makes a perfect double next to himself. Wing explains that this doppelganger is a person who takes energy from the original, and though Kastro may look fine, he's using an enormous amount of Nen every time he creates one. Hisoka explains Kastro's power is better, making the double, then having it disappear so the original can attack. Kastro charges his ultimate special ability, True Tiger Bite Fist. Hisoka just licks his lips and gets excited about the challenge.

Episode 32 (1999) Sightseeing × Landmark × Killua's House (観光×名所×キルアんち, "Kankō × Meisho × Kiruanchi") is the 32nd episode of the original Hunter × Hunter anime. It first aired on June 17th, 2000. Overview. "Gon, Leorio, and Kurapika take a train towards Killua's home on Kukuroo Mountain. A tour bus takes them to the Door to Hades, a giant gate in front of the estate. A monster named Mike waits behind the gate, so Gon asks the security guard, Zebro, to call Killua and have him open it from the inside." Synopsis. Gon, Kurapika, and Leorio's airship lands, and they sit in the airport discussing what to do next on their search to find Killua's home. They plan to take a train to Dentora and then find Kukuroo Mountain from there. As well as their first-class trip on the airship, they sit within the first-class area on the train and marvel at its luxury. On the train ride, Gon and Leorio catch sight of Kukuroo Mountain from their window. Leorio and Kurapika try to plan their next steps, but Gon is under the impression that they'll easily be able to contact Killua and may be able to stay at his house. He voices this while brushing his teeth and spits toothpaste all over Leorio's tie. When in the town, they speak with one of the locals who tells them about the guided tour bus that goes right to the Zoldyck estate. The trio hops on the tour bus and listens to the guided tour by Coco Loo, ominously called the "Lamentation Tours". A few suspicious people on board ask how long the ride will be, and Coco tells them it'll be two hours. Kurapika assumes them to be bounty hunters. Once they arrive at the estate, Leorio gawks at the looming Testing Gate before their party. Gon asks Coco how they're meant to get inside, and the group is disappointed to learn that the tour doesn't go any further. When Gon tries to ask Coco again about getting inside, she warns them that they'd never make it back out again if they did. The bounty hunters step forward, disbelieving Coco's warning, and approach the Testing Gate with a handful of dynamite. The other tourists scatter out of the way as they throw it, and Zebro watches it happen from his station. When the smoke clears, everyone is surprised to see that the explosion did not damage the Testing Gate. Zebro comes out to talk to them, and the bounty hunters threaten him to get him to open the gate. He refuses them as they shake him around, and eventually, his keys fall to the ground. Zebro tries to warn the bounty hunters not to open the small door they're unlocking, but they do it anyways. The door closes behind the bounty hunters, and soon their screams fill the air. When it's finally silent, Mike drops the bones of the bounty hunters outside the door for Zebro to clean up. The tourists all scramble to leave, but the trio tells Coco they will stay behind. At Zebro's station, Zebro talks with the three boys, telling them they're the first people to visit as friends of someone in the family. Still, he tells them he can't let them in, or they'll die due to Mike. Kurapika questions how Zebro gets inside, and he tells them he doesn't use a key, which is only there to lure threats of the Zoldyck family to Mike. Kurapika discovers the main gate isn't locked, and Zebro confirms this. Once outside again, Leorio attempts to push and pull on the gate, but it doesn't budge. Zebro removes his jacket and shirt to reveal that he is very muscular and pushes on the gate with considerable effort. The first set of doors open and then slam shut once he lets go of them. Zebro explains how heavy each set of doors on the gate is, and Gon considers a different option for getting in. He asks if Zebro can call the house on the phone and tell Killua that they're there to see him. Zebro doesn't seem willing to comply with this due to specific rules of the house, so the trio sits in front of the gate in protest, swearing that they won't leave until Zebro calls. As night falls, Zebro watches Kurapika and Leorio fend off, pack off wild beasts that roam the area, and come to attack them, and Gon befriends one of the beasts. Eventually, Zebro gives in, saying he'd be upset if Killua's only friends got eaten overnight, and uses the phone at his station to make the call. The phone rings throughout the Zoldyck house.

Episode 32 (2011) A × Surprising × Win (ドッキリ×ナ×ショウリ, "Dokkiri × Na × Shōri") is the 32nd episode of the Hunter × Hunter 2011 series. It first aired on May 20th, 2012. Overview. "Hisoka and Kastro's match concludes. A female member of the Phantom Troupe appears to heal Hisoka's wounds and tell him about an important job. Gon and Killua ponder how Hisoka won his match. Hisoka reveals a secret." Summary. After severing Hisoka's right arm, Kastro states that his double isn't just an illusion and warns Hisoka that he has to face two of him. He then reveals that he has completed his Tiger Bite Fist ability through the mastery of Nen, calling it True Tiger Bite Fist. Hisoka calmly spins his own severed arm on his finger and smiles at Kastro, revealing a handkerchief and using it to cover the severed arm. He prepares to show off his powers of clairvoyance and tosses the covered arm into the air, but several playing cards are the only things under the handkerchief, with the severed arm nowhere to be found. As the cards fall to the floor, Hisoka asks Kastro to pick one of the numbers, add four, multiply it by two, subtract six, divide it by two, and then subtract the original number. With the crowd left confused, Hisoka confidently claims that he already knows Kastro's answer, suddenly reaching into the wound on his right arm and drawing the ace of spades. The announcer and audience are left in disbelief by the act, with Killua wondering how Hisoka can be so calm. Hisoka tosses the card toward Kastro, who quickly knocks it away from himself as the other remains in its stance. After Kastro vows to sever Hisoka's left arm as well, Hisoka voluntarily holds it out and offers to let him take it. One of the Kastros charges forward and immediately severs the arm, but the double quickly disappears afterwards. Hisoka tells Kastro that he expected him to attack with his double and adds that he would have countered if he himself had attacked, suddenly revealing that his right arm has been completely reattached. With everyone left stunned, Hisoka explains that it's another magic trick and asks Kastro if he can discover the secret. Kastro nervously tells himself that Hisoka must be lying and guesses that he's using Nen to achieve the feat, wondering what type it is. Hisoka walks toward Kastro and asks if he's afraid, pointing out that he doesn't understand the trick because it's magic. He then praises Kastro's ability to make a double and reveals that he understands how it works, confident that he can now predict how he will use it to attack. He continues to walk forward and reveals that he only spared Kastro's life before because of his potential, gleefully predicting that he will now die in a frenzied dance. Kastro angrily tells him to be quiet and leaps toward him with his double, but Hisoka instantly looks toward the real Kastro, causing him to freeze with fear and wonder how he knew. As Hisoka easily dodges the double's attacks, he explains to Kastro that he can't recreate every effect of a battle on his double. After Kastro looks down and sees the blood on his clothes, he charges toward Hisoka, whose severed left arm suddenly flies toward Kastro and strikes him in the face. With Kastro left dazed by the punch to his chin, Hisoka explains that he won't be able to dodge his next attack, and several playing cards suddenly fly toward Kastro, who desperately wonders where they came from. Although Kastro tries to create a double, Hisoka tells him that it takes intense focus to create a Nen double, and the playing cards pierce Kastro's body. Hisoka continues to explain Kastro's deadly mistake as his body falls to the floor. It's announced that Hisoka has won by knockout, and back in his room, Gon sits alone and gets a sudden feeling about Hisoka as he says his name aloud. Leaving the arena, Hisoka finds a woman waiting for him in the exit tunnel. She praises his victory and tells him to show her the injury, with the two making their way to Hisoka's room. Holding Hisoka's severed arms, the woman tells him that the match confirmed that he's an idiot, wondering why he would put himself in so much danger and asking if it was a performance. Hisoka gives a vague response, and the woman points out that she can't complain since she's getting paid, using threads made of Nen to first stop the bleeding. Hisoka asks her to be gentle, and the woman tells him to put away his aura, starting with his left arm and using her Nen Stitches to reattach it. Hisoka praises her skill as she fixes his right arm next, playfully saying that he should get injured more so that he can watch her work. The woman ignores the comment and asks for her payment: 20 million for his left arm, and 50 million for his right. Hisoka assures her that he will send the money to her account, and she prepares to leave, telling him that he can treat the rest of his injuries with his Bungee Gum and Texture Surprise. Hisoka first uses the former ability to attach the handkerchief to his right arm and then the latter to create a layer of skin over it. The woman is left impressed by Hisoka's speed and says to herself that it would have fooled a Nen master into thinking that his arm had actually healed. As Hisoka does the same on his left arm, the woman explains that Hisoka's Bungee Gum allows him to mold his aura into a substance similar to rubber and gum, allowing it to stretch, contract, and stick to many types of surfaces. Hisoka then tells her that he named the ability after his favorite chewing gum when he was younger. Although left uninterested by the detail, the woman says to herself that Hisoka's Texture Surprise allows him to reproduce the appearance of skin, describing it as a high-quality copy. Hisoka reveals that the ability's name comes from the stickers that were included with a once popular snack. With the woman again left uninterested, Hisoka asks her if she was impressed by his application of the two abilities during the fight against Kastro. The woman begins to analyze the fight and explains that when the playing cards went flying into the air, he used Bungee Gum to attach his severed arm to the ceiling and the handkerchief to the floor. She adds that he also had aura connected to all thirteen cards on the floor, holding the ends with his left hand. She deduces that when he threw the ace of spades at Kastro, he released the aura from his left hand and stuck the strands all over Kastro's body. Hisoka points out that Kastro never noticed, and the woman says that he used Zetsu to help conceal his aura. She adds that someone trained in Ren could have focused the Nen in their eyes to see through his plan, guessing that Hisoka used the shocking magic trick to throw Kastro off his guard and believe that Hisoka's lack of aura was a sign of confidence. She then points out that when Hisoka held out his left arm, he attached another strand to Kastro's chin, and quickly reattached his right arm when Kastro took his left. Both point out that the act made Kastro realize that Hisoka was using Nen rather than magic. The woman then notes that Hisoka took advantage of Kastro's psychological state and exposed the weakness of his double ability. Hisoka replies that Kastro would have had a chance if he had stayed calm, but the woman points out that he was overwhelmed by the mental strain and lost as a result. The woman asks Hisoka if he realizes how perfect the two abilities are for him, and Hisoka proudly says that unlike Kastro, someone knowing about his abilities is irrelevant since the two are so adaptable. The woman picks up her bag and prepares to leave, telling Hisoka not to strain himself until his arms are firmly attached. She then remembers the reason why she came and tells him that all Phantom Troupe members have to be in Yorknew City by noon on August 30th. Hisoka asks if the boss will be there as well, and the woman replies that it's very likely since it could be their biggest job yet, warning him that the boss may hunt him down personally if he skips it. Hisoka then asks the woman to join him for dinner, but she leaves before he can even finish the question. Gon is shown still sitting alone in his room and meditating when Killua returns. He asks about Hisoka's match, and Killua replies that it was boring. When Gon asks if Hisoka won, Killua honestly answers that the fight was incredible and that he has no idea how Hisoka won, telling Gon that they need to learn more about Nen. As the woman walks away from Heavens Arena, she turns back to look at the tower and says that Hisoka doesn't talk about the past since he has no interest in it, guessing that he will have forgotten Kastro's face by the next day. She adds that he doesn't associate with others and considers himself his own man since he believes himself to be the strongest. As Hisoka takes a shower in his room, a large spider tattoo with a "4" inside its abdomen is seen across his back. However, when Hisoka finishes and begins to dry himself, he says that he forgot to remove it, suddenly taking off the tattoo. He thinks about Gon and Killua as his new toys and says that it's time to hunt the Spiders, slamming the handkerchief against the mirror as the tattoo vanishes. It's revealed that Hisoka has been masquerading as a member of the Phantom Troupe and considers the group yet another target.

Episode 33 (1999) Training × Hound × Exhausted (特訓×猟犬×バタンキュー, "Tokkun × Ryōken × Batankyuu") is the 33rd episode of the original Hunter × Hunter anime. It first aired on July 1st, 2000. Overview. "Gon, Leorio, and Kurapika stay in the servants' quarters. Zebro lets them in the Testing Gate. While they stay, Seaquant trains them with weighted objects to open the main doors. They increase their strength after 20 days and open the gate themselves. Gon and Kurapika can open the first 2-ton gate, and Leorio opens the second." Synopsis. The phone rings inside the Zoldyck house. When the call is finally picked up, Zebro informs the Zoldyck family butler Gotoh on the other side that Killua's friends have come to see Killua. The call ends with Zebro dejectedly hanging up. Gon suggests that they try calling again so that Gon himself can talk this time. Gon politely asks to speak with Killua when Gotoh answers the phone. Gotoh states that Killua has no friends and hangs out. Gon tries calling a couple more times, but Gotoh is incredibly suspicious of Gon and is unwilling to risk Gon being a potential imposter or liar, and he continues to hang up on him, telling Gon to leave. Gon is very upset after this, so he attempts to climb over the Testing Gate by himself using his fishing rod as a rope. Leorio and Kurapika try to talk him out of it, and Leorio and Gon get into a fight. Zebro interrupts them and offers Gon a key to get in instead, touched by Gon's conviction of being Killua's friend. He claims that if he goes in with the trio, there is a slight chance that Mike will recognize Zebro and not eat them, which is better odds than them trying to sneak in. Zebro pushes open the Testing Gate, and the group walks through together. They are soon approached by a giant, Mike, who terrifies the boys. Zebro explains that Mike is a highly trained hunting dog and cannot be swayed through any attempt at connection or friendship with the dog. The group moves on, uneaten. Zebro brings the group to the servants' quarters, where he says the boys can stay for now. The trio is introduced to an uninterested Seaquant. Afterward, Zebro lets the boys try to open the door to the servants' quarters themselves. Gon is unable, but Leorio can push them open with tremendous effort. However, the doors slam shut in his face the second he lets up. When they get inside, the boys are given slippers to wear, and all three of them immediately fall on their faces, unaware that the slippers are weighted, as are many other things there, like the tea cups. While the group talks with Zebro over tea, Seaquant overhears their conversation about the boys being Hunters and expresses how unimpressed he is with them, especially since they couldn't open the Testing Gate themselves. Leorio's pride gets bruised, and he insists that if he can open the gate, Seaquant has to take back what he said. Gon likes the idea; however, Kurapika worries they won't have enough time to train before their 30-day tourist visa runs out. Zebro offers to help train the boys. He first makes them clean the servants' quarters since all the cleaning supplies are also weighted, and straps weights all over their bodies as well. It takes them a long time, but the boys eventually reach bed. At night, Seaquant talks to Zebro about why Zebro is helping Gon's group. Seaquant says the group will never be allowed to see Killua, but Zebro expresses hope in Gon. The next day, the boys are tasked with various chores while wearing their weights. While Gon is fetching water from the well, Seaquant comes up and helps him pull the bucket out of the well. He tells Gon about the Bounty Hunter who brought a hundred men to storm the estate, but barely made it past the gate before being killed. He warns Gon that the same fate is in store for him and his party, but despite everything Seaquant says, Gon isn't discouraged. After ten days, the boys take turns trying to open the Testing Gate. Leorio can open it a crack, but Kurapika is entirely unsuccessful. Leorio instead attempts to open the decoy door leading Mike to test his strength. However, as soon as he pushes, the door immediately breaks down, and Leorio falls beyond the gate's threshold. Mike attacks and Leorio can dodge out of the way of Mike's paw but ends up further inside, face-down in the bushes. Gon runs through the broken-down door into the grounds of the Zoldyck estate to distract Mike, who immediately runs after Gon. Seaquant runs after the both of them, with Kurapika and Leorio in tow. Gon barely outruns Mike and dodges his attacks, but eventually gets stuck in a tree while evading Mike. Seaquant saves him by shooting the branch he is caught in right before Mike strikes. Mike chases Gon to the edge of a cliff, and Kurapika begs Seaquant to do something, but Seaquant says that only a member of the Zoldyck family can call off Mike. Just before Mike is about to strike again, a whistle is heard off in the distance from the Zoldyck house. Mike runs off, and Gon is left scared and dangling off the cliff's edge until Seaquant, Leorio, and Kurapika eventually help him. Far off in the woods, Kalluto is seen petting a calm Mike. After twenty days, Coco Loo gives a tour outside the Testing Gate to a group of tourists when Gon can finally open the Testing Gate with Leorio and Kurapika cheering him on. Zebro congratulates the boys on their success. Back at the servants' quarters, the trio thanks Seaquant and Zebro for all their help and start on the path toward the Zoldyck home. Once they've left, Seaquant reveals that he was part of the group that tried to storm the Zoldyck estate before and expresses how hopeless he feels for the trio, considering he knows who they'll have to face along their way to the house. The trio walks along the path and eventually stops as Canary stands in their way.

Episode 33 (2011) An × Empty × Threat (ケイハク×ナ×キョウハク, "Keihaku × Na × Kyōhaku") is the 33rd episode of the Hunter × Hunter 2011 series. It first aired on May 27th, 2012. Overview. "Gon is healed from his wounds and begins training with Zushi and Killua. They learn Gyo, another ability of Nen. Sadaso, Gido, and Riehlvelt kidnap Zushi to force Gon and Killua's hand. Killua is able to scare Sadaso out of town." Summary. Two months have passed since Gon's match with Gido, and Gon has kept his promise to not train with Nen in that time. Wing tells him and Killua that they will start training with Zushi. Wing tells the three to practice Ren and learns Gyo, a technique that focuses the aura in one's eyes, allowing one to see hidden Nen. Zushi is able to execute Gyo in front of everybody, but quickly gets tired. Wing tells both Gon and Killua to learn Gyo before fighting again. The three practice in Gon's room. When they leave, they run into Sadaso, Gido, and Riehlvelt, who try forcing them to fight against them. After Zushi parts ways from Gon and Killua, Sadaso ambushes him with his "Aura Arm", and takes one of Zushi's shoes. Gido and Riehlvelt also arrive.
