As Soufflé grabs Terebellum's left arm and reminds him that they were told not to deal with intruders, Hinrigh throws another knife toward him, with Terebellum dodging and pushing Soufflé out of the way. As the knife heads straight for Perigord, he calmly puts out his hand and wonders how long it would take for the injury to heal. However, Orarge uses an issue of "" to stop the knife and tells Perigord that he should have avoided it, wondering why he's trying to use his ability. Terebellum criticizes Soufflé for carelessly touching him, and she apologizes before saying that she will leave and reminding them that they shouldn't fight there. Orarge reminds Perigord that he has already been chosen as the "organ" (kikan) and that Morena told him to keep his head down, with Perigord remembering and apologizing. Yokotani speaks up and confirms Hinrigh's identity, introducing himself as the Heil-Ly Family's lawyer. Terebellum then tells him to call the military and police since a crazy person is throwing knives and going on a rampage. Yokotani explains that they have committed both trespassing and bodily harm, which is as close as they can get to attempted murder. He asks if it's okay to report it to the police, and Hinrigh says that it's convenient since they're lost, wondering where they are. Yokotani replies that he can't reveal that and agrees to keep things civil if they follow his instructions. Nobunaga then gets his attention, and Yokotani recognizes him as a member of the Phantom Troupe, saying that it's a big deal for them. Before Yokotani can finish asking a question, Nobunaga uses a chain attached to the end of his "katana" to reach the Heil-Ly member and stab his head. However, Terebellum is seen with his right hand on Yokotani's shoulder, and when Nobunaga pulls back his "katana", he sees that the tip is missing, realizing that Terebellum can move the damage from other people as well. Blood begins to stream down Terebellum's left arm as he tells Yokotani to stay back. Nobunaga says that if Terebellum doesn't transfer the damage he receives with his right hand to something else with his left hand, he will receive the damage himself. He describes the ability as unselfish and adds that it doesn't suit his appearance at all. It's explained that Terebellum's Emission ability, Damage: "Sweet Home", allows him to displace damage along with the attacking object. The damage to something touched by his right hand is taken into Terebellum himself, and it can be transferred to something when he touches it with his left hand. It only works if he is touching it the moment the damage is received. Nobunaga tells Terebellum to step back and tells Yokotani to come closer again, promising to skewer all of them as aura surrounds his "katana". Yokotani apologizes and says that he didn't expect Nobunaga to abandon the spirit of a samurai, and Terebellum criticizes him for getting close to the enemy so carelessly. Yokotani realizes that he's the reason why Terebellum's ability was exposed and wonders how he can apologize, explaining that the samurai of his homeland were against the use of projectile weapons. Terebellum wonders if he will keep making excuses, and Yokotani quickly apologizes before saying that he will disappear for a while. However, Terebellum tells him that he will make the intruders disappear, reminding him that he identified himself to them and that he is a guard. Yokotani then activates his Conjuration ability, A Battle of Wits: "LSDF", which is explained to be a defensive ability that can only be used at the hideout where Morena is located. It activates when Yokotani identifies himself to an intruder who has broken the law, and while the guards he conjures cannot harm the criminal, the criminal's attacks are also ineffective. The more serious the opponent's crime, the higher the level of guards Yokotani can create. With aura swelling around them, seven puppets appear behind him and identify the two criminals, charging them with trespassing and attempted murder as they reach alert level 4. Yokotani confirms the sentence and orders them to be expelled from the premises. As the puppets run forward, Nobunaga readies his "katana" and strikes one of them, but it takes no damage and reaches the maximum alert level as its aura increases. Nobunaga realizes that its aura has been enhanced and tells Hinrigh that the puppets are most likely invincible since the two of them already met the conditions of Yokotani's ability. The puppets swarm and restrain Nobunaga, with one of them confiscating his "katana". Nobunaga tells Hinrigh to run since the puppets are on autopilot and won't stop until they remove him as well. The puppets carry Nobunaga out, and he is eventually teleported away, with Yokotani confirming his expulsion and adding that they have one more target. As the puppets sprint toward Hinrigh, Yokotani tells him that he also has two attempted murders with willful negligence and that he will be expelled, asking him to give up and leave. Based on the teleportation traps and invincible-type users, Hinrigh is confident that it's the Heil-Ly's main base, returning to the laundry room and closing the door behind him. As the puppets pound on the door, Hinrigh tells himself that he will use Nobunaga's advice and hide the transmitter there since the puppets are on autopilot and the user won't be able to see what he's doing in the room. He then puts two fingers in his mouth so that he can vomit up the transmitter. Back in Room 3101, Nobunaga realizes that entering from the front door teleports someone to the hideout and entering from the door of the hideout teleports someone to Room 3101. He adds that the Heil-Ly can kill two birds with one stone since it acts as a trap and a secret passageway. However, he says that there has to be a jump point that only members can use, wondering if it's somewhere in the room. Hinrigh then teleports back, and Nobunaga wonders how it went. Hinrigh replies that the enemy probably won't notice the transmitter thanks to his advice, telling Nobunaga that he will support him since he (Hinrigh) won't be able to use his ability anymore that day and adding that he used all his knives. Hinrigh explains that he will first get an idea of where the hideout is located on the ship's floor plan before creating descriptions for the members, looking for witnesses, and narrowing down their area of activity. He adds that he will gather together every Xi-Yu member to get the information, and Nobunaga says that the Troupe will handle the search for the transmitter. In the hideout's laundry room, the transmitter (still in the form of an oyster) is seen under one of the cabinets as it beeps twice. Hinrigh tells Nobunaga that he's counting on them and that even though the Heil-Ly looked like amateurs, they have to be cautious since they don't know what Morena can do and what one of the members meant when he said "kikan". Nobunaga agrees and adds that whoever is moving the pieces isn't stupid.

Chapter 4 Kiriko: Wicked Magical Vulpes (, "Majū Kiriko") is the 4th chapter of the Hunter × Hunter manga, written and illustrated by Yoshihiro Togashi. Synopsis. With the sun beginning to set, Leorio points out that it's been four hours even though the old woman said that it would only take two to reach the lone pine tree. He also spots another sign warning of magical beasts and wonders where the exam site is, complaining that he's hungry and needs to use the bathroom. Gon tells him to keep up, and Kurapika suddenly spots it, with a flashback showing that the old woman told them about a house under the tree in which two Navigators live. She added that if they made a good impression, they would show them to the exam site. It's then stated that since the Hunter Exam is held in a different location every year, the Navigators are aware of the exam site and guide the applicants there. It's added that it would be impossible to reach the site otherwise since the path is filled with traps and that an applicant must pass the screening, find a Navigator, and then impress them enough to prove their worth. As the three applicants reach the house, Kurapika realizes how quiet it is and wonders if they are the only ones who made it there. After Leorio knocks on the door and the three enter, they find a strange creature holding a woman hostage and repeatedly mumbling "kill" as a man lies wounded on the floor. The three immediately recognize that it's a magical beast, with Leorio drawing his switchblade and Kurapika his . However, the creature quickly makes its way past them and crashes through the front door still holding the woman. Gon and Kurapika run after the beast as Leorio stays behind to help the injured man, who begs them to save his wife. Once outside, Kurapika knows that it ran into the woods but can't determine which way it went. Gon looks all around and suddenly spots the creature's shadow, immediately running toward that direction. Kurapika can't believe that Gon was able to see its shadow in the darkness of a forest, equally stunned by Gon's quick movement as he leaps through the trees. Gon continues jumping on various branches and catches up to the creature, ordering it to release the woman. The creature suddenly talks and tells Gon to take her by force, but Gon is left more surprised by the fact that it can speak. Kurapika angrily points out that it's why they're called magical beasts and explains that the creature is a Kiriko, shapeshifters who can even take on the form of humans. Although Kurapika tells him to be careful, Gon says that it will be easy if they can talk, yelling after it and suddenly appearing right in front of it. With the Kiriko left in disbelief at his speed, Gon uses his fishing rod to strike the creature on the top of the head, telling Kurapika to catch the falling woman. Kurapika does so by hanging on to a branch and calls Gon's action reckless. As Gon chases after the Kiriko, Kurapika asks the woman how she feels, but she is more concerned about her husband. Kurapika assures her that a friend of theirs is with him, but the woman begs him to take her to her husband, holding out her right arm and revealing more tattoos. Kurapika seems to recognize something about them, but Leorio suddenly appears behind him and asks if he's fine. Kurapika tells him that Gon is chasing the creature and then asks about the man's condition. Leorio assures him that it's nothing serious and that he's sleeping after he gave him some medicine for the pain. However, Kurapika suddenly strikes him in the face with one of his "bokken" and discovers that he is a Kiriko, who asks Kurapika how he knew. Kurapika explains that he didn't and that he only struck him because he thought Leorio had abandoned his job of looking after the injured man. The creature quickly leaps away, and Kurapika then turns to the woman with his "bokken" drawn, asking her who she is as she chuckles in reply. Gon stands alone in a clearing and turns around to find the Kiriko, who praises Gon's movement and his successful strike. He then displays his sharp claws and suddenly leaps toward Gon preparing to attack in retaliation, but Gon stands completely still and gives his own name, asking for the creature's in return. With the Kiriko stopping its attack, Gon wonders where the one that he struck is and asks if they are a friend of his, confident that it isn't him. The Kiriko wonders how he figured it out, and Gon explains that the two have completely different faces and that their voices are slightly different as well. The Kiriko chuckles at first and then laughs hysterically, patting Gon on the head and telling his partner to come out. With the three applicants and four Kiriko now gathered together, one of the Kiriko says that it has been a while since a human was able to tell them apart so easily. With Leorio and Kurapika still left confused, Gon points out that he and Kurapika struck the husband. The Kiriko reveal that they are the Navigators, with the younger two revealing that they are their son and daughter. The woman shows the tattoos on her arm and explains that they signify a Sumi woman's vow of chastity that few people are able to recognize, praising Kurapika's knowledge and awareness. The man then says that while Leorio never discovered the truth, he applied extraordinary first aid with carefulness and compassion. Finally, the Kiriko praise Gon's incredible agility and perception, stating that he is one of the most naturally gifted humans they have seen. They confirm that all three applicants have passed and that they will take them directly to the exam site. After the three celebrate, the four Kiriko carry them through the sky with a full moon behind them. It's stated that while the three enjoyed the flight, they wondered what the exam itself would be like if the screening process was so rigorous.

Chapter 40 The Zoldycks: Part 1 (ゾルディック①, "Zorudikku Ke (Ichi)") is the 40th chapter of the Hunter × Hunter manga, written and illustrated by Yoshihiro Togashi. Synopsis. Gon asks Zebro for the key and threatens to climb the wall if he refuses. Leorio angrily reminds him about Mike, but Gon replies that he hates the idea of testing someone's friends and that he won't use the Testing Gate. Zebro understands his point and agrees with him, but stresses that he will be eaten if he uses the key to enter. Kurapika adds that taking a test is preferable to suicide, but Gon continues to wait for Zebro to hand him the key. As Leorio and Kurapika understand that Gon won't change his mind, Zebro says that while he won't give Gon the key, he can't allow him to climb the wall either. Zebro tells the three to wait there as he enters the guard booth and explains to someone on the phone that three of Killua's friends are waiting at the front gate. After the reply causes Zebro to apologize and quickly hang up, Gon asks if he called the mansion for him. Zebro explains that he only spoke with one of their butlers, who handle all communications for the Zoldycks. Gon asks if he can talk with the butler, and while Zebro agrees, he stresses that it won't be of any use. After the butler answers, Gon explains that he is a friend of Killua's and asks to speak with him. However, the butler says that Killua has no friends before immediately hanging up. Gon quickly calls back and angrily asks how they know that Killua has no friends, ordering the butler to put Killua on the phone. With Leorio and Kurapika left stunned, the butler confirms Gon's name and wonders how he would confirm his real identity over the phone. Gon again tells him to put Killua on the phone since he will be able to tell, but the butler says that voice is no guarantee, suddenly playing a recording of Gon's previous statement. The butler explains that voices are easy to mimic and that even if he confirmed his appearance, he could be under the influence of one of Killua's enemies. He refuses to get Killua involved and explains that the butlers' job is to prevent any of the Zoldycks' enemies from getting near them. After the butler asks Gon to leave and again hangs up, Gon calmly walks outside the booth toward the wall. Leorio realizes how angry he is, and Gon suddenly readies his fishing rod, flinging the hook and line over the wall. Leorio begs him not to do it, but Gon secures the line and tells them to wait there. As the three argue back and forth, Zebro finally gives in and hands Gon the key. Leorio and Kurapika assure him that they will change Gon's mind, but Zebro reveals that he will go through the door with Gon, explaining that there's a small chance that Mike doesn't attack since he knows him. Gon says that he doesn't want to risk Zebro's life, but Zebro replies that he wouldn't be able to face Killua again if he let one of his friends get eaten by Mike. Gon pulls back his fishing line and apologizes again. The other three smile, and Zebro internally praises Gon's character. As Zebro points out that Gon isn't afraid of Mike, he guesses that he loves animals and grew up playing in the wilderness, which Gon quickly confirms. Zebro tells the three that he will open the Testing Gate again so that they can see Mike for themselves. As the four enter the forest, Leorio wonders if it's safe, and Zebro tells him not to worry as he calls for Mike. The nearby bushes are rustled, and Gon is the first to spot the enormous wolf-like creature before them. Sweat pours down Gon's face as Mike stares at him and then lies down. Zebro asks Gon if he understands that Mike is different from any other animal he has encountered in the wild. He guesses that Gon thought he could communicate with him until he looks into his eyes, explaining that Mike is taking in the appearances and smells of people new to him. He finally describes Mike as a living machine and says that the creature would attack even him if ordered to do so, asking Gon if he thinks he could fight him. Gon quickly shakes his head and replies that Mike seriously scares him. Zebro chuckles at Gon's honesty and leads the three to the nearby servants' quarters, where they will spend the night. He changes shifts with another groundskeeper, who is surprised to see guests and says that Zebro doesn't let just anyone inside. Zebro tells Gon to push open the building's doors, but when he tries to push with his right hand, he has trouble opening it. Zebro reveals that the doors weigh 440 pounds each, explaining that they must work out constantly. After Leorio opens both doors with considerable effort, Zebro shows them slippers to wear (44 pounds each) and offers them fresh tea in cups (44 pounds). He learns that the three are on tourist visas in Padokea, telling them they can stay in the country for a month at most. He adds that they can train in the house and that while they could just head for the mountain, it would be cheating. The three smiles and Zebro adds that after one month, they should be able to work together to open the first door. The three agree that while they don't like tests, it's the only fair way to proceed. Zebro happily gives them weighted vests to wear (except while sleeping), which start at 110 pounds. He calls Leorio sturdy and says that he should be able to open the door by himself soon. After barely two weeks, Leorio is seen opening the first door as Gon cheers for him, and Kurapika can't believe that Gon's broken arm healed in only ten days (and that he is jumping up and down while wearing 220 pounds). With Zebro stunned, an exasperated Leorio says that they can now enter fair and square as he celebrates with Gon and Kurapika. Zebro happily looks on and says to himself that he never thought a real contender would appear, surprised to have three of them.

Chapter 400 Secrecy (, "Hitoku") is the 400th chapter of the Hunter × Hunter manga, written and illustrated by Yoshihiro Togashi. Synopsis. On Tier 3, Phinks and Feitan continue to use the receiver to look for the transmitter. Feitan notes that it's 100-200 meters away and the direction is unstable, remembering that it means the device is directly above or below them. He adds that only Tier 2 and Tier 4 are possible, suggesting that they go down first. Phinks says that if they reach a certain point on Tier 4, they will know if they are getting closer or farther away. Feitan says that it would be easier to find if Phinks could use his En, but Phinks reminds him that it's a bad idea both technically and strategically to use it in the middle of the crowd, adding that he isn't good at using it since it gets interrupted when he hears someone's voice, or when something moves, or while he moves. He continues by saying that the best he can do is look for stuff in the warehouse and likens putting a number of unknown people in his En to walking around the slums naked with a "shoot me" sign on his back. Nobunaga meets up with them and is surprised to see them still wandering around. Phinks wonders why he came back so quickly, but Nobunaga says that they will talk about it later, asking if the transmitter is working. Feitan confirms that it is and adds that they have to find out if it's above or below them. Phinks tells him that he only left around 10 minutes ago, and Nobunaga is surprised. Phinks explains that they think the Heil-Ly's hideout is on Tier 2 and says that they can use the Cha-R Family's hidden door once they confirm it. A soldier gives the three Troupe members permission to pass, and Nobunaga tells him to let Hinrigh know that they went to the Cha-R's hideout. With his mind lingering on Tier 2, Nobunaga feels uneasy about the situation with the Mafia. Phinks then asks if he can figure out where the hideout is located on the ship, but Nobunaga replies that he can't since their boss created the space with Nen, adding that they need to stay alert. As the three head down to Tier 4, Feitan reacts to a change on the receiver, saying that the transmitter is getting farther away and that they can confirm the Heil-Ly's hideout is on Tier 2. Nobunaga realizes why he felt uneasy and says that it means the Heil-Ly's boss is in the upper tiers and wonders how the other two families are justifying the war. Phinks says that they shouldn't get involved in a dispute with the Mafia killing each other and one of the bosses staying in their hideout, adding that the Heil-Ly could be exploiting the ancient custom. Feitan says that they should head to the Cha-R's hideout now, but Nobunaga suggests at least taking Franklin with them, explaining that they still don't know how many Heil-Ly members there are and that he didn't expect their abilities to be so refined. As his mind lingers on exploiting the ancient custom, Nobunaga adds that while they seem like a group of punks, the Heil-Ly can be dangerous depending on their advisor's ability. Phinks then reminds him that the Mafia issue is just a sideshow until they find Hisoka. Nobunaga points out that they need to secure a route to the upper tiers so they can complete their search, adding that Franklin joining them will improve their chances if they happen to find him. Phinks realizes that his reasoning makes it more likely that he's obsessed with the Heil-Ly, and Nobunaga admits that one of the members seemed interesting, with Feitan telling Nobunaga that he likes the enemy too much. An emergency broadcast suddenly plays over the intercoms and asks everyone to pay attention to sad and unfortunate news. In Room 1006, Tyson introduces one of her employees as Madwig, a handsome hitman with amnesia. He says that even though he only remembers how to use a handgun, Tyson still hired him. The second introduces himself as Himoncé, the world's biggest star, and says that Tyson is the first girl who has said he wasn't her type. The third introduces himself as Anzel and reveals that he is Tyson's little brother, adding that only he and Tyson know about it. The fourth introduces himself as Hyuga, a legendary tutor, and says that he can get you into your dream school even if you're incredibly dumb. The last introduces themselves as a prince from the planet Moony in the SR Nebula, revealing that they have come to the planet to look for a bride. Giuliano realizes that each of them is performing one of Prince's favorite roles, but Tyson playfully rebukes him and replies that they have all been reborn, telling Giuliano that the same will happen to him. She then tells him that he will be a bodyguard who looks flirtatious but is actually pure at heart, and Giuliano plays along with her request. Watching on, Izunavi says that while Giuliano isn't any different now, he becomes too calm when reading Tyson's book, guessing that it's linked to the ability of her Guardian Spirit Beast. He then wonders if they can use it to influence the King and have him put an end to the succession contest since it focuses on preaching love. He asks Tyson if she has given the book to the other Princes, and she replies that she gave it to the lower Princes and their moms, adding that while they probably didn't read it, they most likely didn't throw them away. She explains that she's in a delicate position in terms of succession order and that she has little influence. Izunavi asks if she has given it to the King, and she replies that she needs her mother's permission to see her father, hoping that she gave him a copy since she asked her about it. She reveals that it's the reason why she agreed to participate since she was going to decline at first, adding that her mother was disappointed by how she turned out and that she doesn't expect any grandchildren from her. She explains that her mother couldn't stand when the other Queens looked at her with pity, and that while her mother wants to get her revenge in the succession contest, she only fights with the power of love. Izunavi then wonders if she could ask her mother to speak to the King and have him read her book at the next banquet, emphasizing that it could change the fate of the ship. Tyson is happy to hear him say that and promises to negotiate with her mother. Outside Room 1010, two guards stand in front of the doors as four soldiers surround them. Inside, Seiko uses the phone and tells them to hold off on the regulations until she gets her personal belongings organized, wondering why she can't see Fugetsu when she's a Queen and her mother. She again expresses her concern for Fugetsu and tells them that until then, cordoning off the room is unacceptable. Saying to herself that she should let others think Kacho is alive as long as possible, she yells to the soldiers that she will speak to Fugetsu when the time is right and that they must go through her, hanging up the phone. She then says to herself that while Kacho dropping out so early is a heavy loss, she hated the way her daughter looked at her and spoke to her like she knew everything. She adds that she was an important shield for Fugetsu and says that while she can control the latter, she's too weak to face the succession contest on her own, hoping that she can stay under the Justice Bureau's protection for as long as possible. At the Justice Bureau's interrogation office, Kacho's Guardian Spirit Beast (appearing as Kacho after her death) says that she was possibly resurrected as a guardian spirit to protect Fugetsu and that even if it's her beast's ability, the fact that Fugetsu can see her means she is out of the contest. She adds that if Fugetsu's aura is being used to maintain her appearance, it must have a considerable burden on her, feeling responsible for her weakened condition and wondering if her finding out the truth will reduce the burden. Shaking and tearing up, Melody blames herself for what happened, but Kacho orders her to pull herself together and to feel bad about it when she's alone. She assures Melody that it's what she wanted and that she doesn't regret it at all, adding that it actually makes things simpler. She declares that they will make Fugetsu King and that if they can't escape, they have to fight. She explains that since everyone thinks she's dead, they can use her suddenly turning up alive to their advantage. However, she adds that they need to keep her death a secret from Fugetsu. The investigator tells Kacho that she should let Fugetsu know that the people are under the mistaken impression that she died, confident that Fugetsu will accept the explanation since she exists. He says that while he is still trying to come to grips with ghosts and Nen abilities, he was convinced by the military's reports and Melody's condition. Melody says to herself that even in such a stressful situation, he's annoyingly calm and collected. The investigator then tells Melody that her unstable state of mind will make things more difficult and that she can't disappoint a young girl who is so determined and waiting for her. Kacho asks if she is in or out, and Melody agrees to help them. The investigator starts with Melody's problem and reveals that five Princes have requested to see her. He first says that the Third and Fourth Princes wish to speak with her in their quarters and to hear her performance in person. He then says that the First, Fifth, and Seventh Princes are more obvious, offering a "pardon" and requesting an "encore" of her performance. As Kacho wonders what he means by a pardon, Melody signals for him to keep quiet, and the investigator realizes that she means not to say anything about Keeney's death. He explains that the Princes have a better understanding of Nen abilities now and realize that Melody was involved in the escape attempt, revealing that they are using her performance as leverage since she could get the death penalty if she is convicted as an accomplice. Kacho realizes that the Princes want Melody to indirectly help with assassinations and nonchalantly says that it will lead to fewer Princes. Melody is taken aback by how harsh she is, and the investigator says that the higher-ranking Princes may have restrained themselves because there are still too many of them, which means there are just as many uncertainties. He adds that if they don't have a good idea of who is targeting whom, they could end up hurting themselves. Melody reveals that her ability is only intended to heal and that the loss of consciousness is a side effect, wondering if the Princes would give up if they knew that covering their ears would prevent it. The investigator points out that it's where they can use information and tactics to bargain, guessing that they will end up auctioning off "true performance time" among the higher-ranking Princes. Melody realizes that assassination and her performance go together as a set, and the investigator says that the best way to protect Fugetsu is to deceive all the Princes who have requested a performance, suggesting that they should wipe out all the higher-ranking Princes themselves. With Melody taken aback, the investigator says that the best way would be to pour a slow-acting poison in the mouths of the unconscious Princes, assuring her that he can prepare everything if she agrees with the plan. Melody realizes that he's willing to die if the plan fails and wonders why he would go so far for them. He replies that he thought it was already clear and tells Melody that he's in love with her, explaining that he's unable to fall asleep because he keeps thinking about her and her performance. He adds that he has never felt such a throbbing in his heart before and that it perplexes him. As Melody notes that his heartbeat is as precise as an atomic clock, the investigator says that while most see him as a workaholic, he actually yearns for love more than others, adding that it’s only natural to completely prioritize the person he loves. At first worried that he's trying to trap them, Melody reminds herself that he suggested assassination and guesses that he was sent by one of the Princes. She wonders why he's going through so much trouble when he could easily get rid of the two of them at the Justice Bureau. As she says aloud that they agree to the plan, she tells herself that he must be a Manipulator posing as someone without powers and that he's manipulating himself as someone without powers and trying to use them for a hidden purpose. The investigator again says that he will get the necessary supplies and tells Melody to use the visits to get as many of the Princes as possible to attend the next banquet. Melody tells herself that assassinating the higher-ranking Princes all at once might be his real goal, wondering if the mastermind is a Prince who didn't request a meeting with her. Kacho says that she will do her part and first needs to explain to Fugetsu that everyone thinks she's dead, adding that she will convince her that the top four Princes need to be eliminated. The investigator tells Kacho to return to the interrogation room and says that he will use the door since he can't pass through walls. As Kacho begins to move through a nearby bookcase, she wonders if he should interrogate her a little, but he replies that he's more worried about Fugetsu, telling Kacho that everyone would think she remained silent anyway. He leaves with Melody and meets Kacho in the other room, escorting her out and telling himself that the VIP witness protection area is the safest on the ship and that not even the First Prince could try anything there. He then meets with Steiner and hands him a small device, telling him to press the button if the First Prince's men or the Royal Army come there. He explains that while the Justice Bureau is the most neutral institution on the ship, it will turn into a dictator's base once special martial law is declared. Steiner realizes that it involves the military temporarily taking control of the government's powers in the case of a national emergency. The investigator adds that the worst-case scenario is the power transfer happening right after numerous soldiers are sent inside the Justice Bureau, explaining that those considered to be insurgents will be charged and executed within ten minutes. Steiner realizes that it's the last check against the army going rogue, wondering if the situation with the succession contest is so dire. The investigator replies that they don't know and it's why they have to be prepared, telling Steiner that he's one of the few witnesses on board who is guaranteed to return alive and that his safety will be assured. Steiner says to himself that it seems like he's marked for death and that if he dies, it means something happened that couldn't be in the official record. Kacho returns to their quarters at the Justice Bureau, but Fugetsu doesn't respond when she calls for her. Kacho points out that they aren't allowed to leave their room since they're key witnesses, worried that Fugetsu used her ability to go somewhere else. She checks the bed and removes the comforter to find Fugetsu's outgoing door, explaining that if she's not with Fugetsu, it's supposed to be a one-way path where the entrance disappears once she passes through the exit. She wonders if Fugetsu is still inside the tunnel and worries that someone tried to attack her and that she used the ability to hide, considering the possibility that Kaiser, the Justice Bureau official, is their enemy. However, Fugetsu suddenly opens the door, and Kacho quickly grabs her hands and asks if she's okay. Fugetsu excitedly replies that she has made a breakthrough, revealing that while she could only use the ability once a day before, she can now use it multiple times. With heavy bags under eyes, she adds that the return door now appears even when she's alone and that even though she can only return to where she was, she can now explore on her own even when Kacho is resting. Kacho wonders if she's really okay, and Fugetsu excitedly assures her that she is, adding that she feels happy and empowered every time she uses her magic, hoping that the two of them can explore and use their magic skills to escape together. Left wondering if the ability really gets stronger with every use, Kacho grabs her sister's shoulders and tells her to take it easy since she's so pale. However, Fugetsu grabs Kacho's wrist as tears stream down her face, and she tells Kacho that it's her turn to protect her since she has been doing it for so many years. Taken aback, Kacho suggests that they rest and talk about it once they wake up. Kacho then meets with Melody and reveals that Fugetsu passed out, worried that it's not normal and saying that she can't figure out what's happening. Eager to help, Melody reminds her that she is also a key witness and won't be able to get anywhere near the two of them. She tells Kacho that she will have Kaiser arrange a time for her to meet with the other Princes and for Fugetsu to be interviewed so that they can pass each other in the hallway. The timing is eventually arranged, and as Melody walks by Fugetsu in the hallway, a dark presence emanates from her as buzzing insects and multiple spirits are seen floating behind her. Left frightened, Melody says that Fugetsu's aura has become as weak as Zetsu and that the unstable rhythm of her heartbeat is attracting evil spirits, wondering how it happened so quickly. Melody is unsure of what to do given the number of evil spirits and realizes the importance of finding an exorcist. The two guards tell her to go inside and that all conversations will be recorded during the 10-minute period, adding that it may be used in a court of law and that a public defender will be present. Melody wonders why Fugetsu is so weak since there's no sign of the evil spirit's body. She points out that if it's an ability that has such a powerful effect, there should be obvious traces or the body itself should be nearby. As she guesses that it's a negotiation with Fugetsu as a hostage and that someone will hint at it during the visits, she is surprised to see Zhang Lei waiting to speak with her in person. He tells her how much he wanted to show his respect and praises her performance at the banquet. He first requests to hear her performance again and then hopes that she will accept a gift. The public defender asks if she will accept it, and Melody says that she will. Once the gift is put into the box and moved across, Melody sees that it's a coin with a "1" on it. Melody is then visited by Vantine, the private military commander for the Fourth Prince, who says that while negotiations in public have no meaning, he would like to confirm a few things, with Melody noticing the mention of "negotiations". Vantine asks if she will accept the Prince's invitation to his quarters, and she replies that while she appreciates the offer, she can't make the decision on her own. Vantine wonders if it's because she was hired as a guard by Kacho, but Melody quickly answers that she can't respond to contractual matters. Vantine changes the question and asks if she herself is reluctant to play again. Melody says that speaking for herself, she would gladly perform anywhere when asked and under the right circumstances. Vantine is happy to hear it and says that the Prince will be pleased, but Melody then says that they can "negotiate" there. Vantine is left confused and says that they can talk about negotiations once she gets out. Melody tells herself that he has a heartbeat of confusion and doubt and that the Fourth Prince isn't involved, ruling out both the Third and Fourth Princes and saying that there are three left. Melody meets with Kaiser, who asks if she thinks they shouldn't carry out their plan yet even if she performs at the next banquet. She confirms that they shouldn't make any careless moves since they don't know who's responsible for the change in Fugetsu, emphasizing that they need to find the cause as soon as possible and asking Kaiser to get her released on bail. However, he explains that if they ease her confinement, they won't be able to turn down the subpoenas from the Princes and that the First Prince's men are waiting for her to leave the Justice Bureau. Melody asks him to visit Kurapika in Room 1014 and to tell him everything since he's the only one she trusts. Kaiser wonders if she really means everything, and Melody stresses that they can't waste any time, asking him to hurry. Melody then says to herself that no one's heartbeat reacted to the keyword "negotiations", wondering if there's another mastermind or if they're waiting for the right moment. She is left upset that they can't remove any of the Princes and those around them from the list of suspects. In Room 1014, as aura swirls around them, Longhi tells Kurapika that Water Divination isn't needed since they can already use Nen, asking him if he will agree to the contract after hearing what they had to say. With Bill by his side, Kurapika agrees to the deal and says that he will collaborate with Prince Tubeppa.

Chapter 41 The Zoldycks: Part 2 (ゾルディック②, "Zorudikku Ke (Ni)") is the 41st chapter of the Hunter × Hunter manga, written and illustrated by Yoshihiro Togashi Synopsis. Gon, Kurapika, and Leorio thank Zebro and Seaquant before leaving the servants' quarters. Zebro tells them to follow the path to the mountain and that they will find the Zoldyck Family mansion somewhere up there, adding that he has never been there during his 20 years of service. As the three waves goodbye, Zebro comments that they all managed to open the Testing Gate in 20 days, with Leorio even opening the second set of doors. Seaquant tells him they are professional Hunters. While Zebro guesses that they may be able to reach the mansion, Seaquant reminds him of the incident three years earlier when a Blacklist Hunter brought 100 thugs to attack the mansion. He recounts that all 100 were defeated by a single butler apprentice who was only 10 years old at the time. Zebro wittily adds that he remembers the Hunter being so impressed that he asked for a job. Seaquant takes a puff of his cigarette and says that the massacre showed him how outclassed he was. As Gon, Kurapika, and Leorio make their way toward the mountain, they eventually encounter a female butler standing at the entrance of a small wall. She tells them to leave since trespassers are not welcome on private property. Gon points out that they called ahead and entered through the Testing Gate, but the woman asks if they received permission from the butlers. Gon admits that they did not and asks how they can do so, but she replies that there has never been a precedent for it. An annoyed Gon says that trespassing is their only option, but she again orders them to leave, threatening to remove them by force if they cross the line in front of her. After Gon walks forward and crosses the line with his foot, the butler immediately knocks him back with her staff. Kurapika readies his *bokken and Leorio his switchblade, but Gon quickly tells them that he will handle it himself, explaining to the butler that they have only come because they want to see Killua. Wielding her staff, the butler says that regardless of whether they are telling the truth, she still has to follow her orders. Setting aside his fishing rod and backpack, Gon slowly walks up toward the butler, and she again strikes him hard with her staff. The barrage of strikes continues as someone watches from the bushes nearby. With his face bloody and bruised, and his left eye swollen shut, Gon continues to endure the butler's attacks, continually struggling to his feet to face her. She politely asks Gon to go away and strikes him once again after his foot crosses the line. Gon remains on his feet and again walks toward the butler, who yells at Kurapika and Leorio to stop him since they are his friends. However, the two remain exactly where they are and appear emotionless. With the butler taken aback, Gon clenches his fist and asks why they need to fight, repeating that they just want to see their friend. As he angrily asks what they are all afraid of, he destroys the nearby pillar with a punch and points out that his foot has crossed the line. Tightly gripping her staff, the butler is unable to strike him as a nervous look appears on her face. Gon then says that the difference between her and Mike is that she still has a soul even though she hides her emotions, recognizing that she appeared concerned once he mentioned Killua by name. As the butler begins to cry and begs them to help Killua, a projectile suddenly strikes her in the side of the head, drawing blood and leaving her motionless on the ground. Left stunned, the three spot a young child and a woman wearing a visor, large hat, and ornate dress in the distance. The latter says that they cannot have the help acting on their own, pointing out that as an apprentice, she doesn't understand the family dynamic well enough. The woman then focuses on Gon and confirms who he is, saying that Illumi mentioned him. She reveals that Killua knows they have been on the estate for the past three weeks and then relays a message from him, in which he thanks them for coming but apologizes for being currently indisposed. Underneath the Zoldycks' mansion, Killua is seen with numerous injuries across his face and body as he hangs shackled and chained.

Chapter 42 The Zoldycks: Part 3 (ゾルディック③, "Zorudikku Ke (San)") is the 42nd chapter of the Hunter × Hunter manga, written and illustrated by Yoshihiro Togashi. Synopsis. In a flashback, Canary introduces herself to Killua, who tells her that she doesn't have to call him master. Canary stresses that it wouldn't be appropriate since she's a servant, but Killua asks her to be his friend. Back in the present, underneath Kukuroo Mountain, Killua sleeps while hanging chained to the ceiling in a room filled with torture devices. His older brother Milluki has a cigarette in a mouth and a whip in his hand, striking Killua and ordering him to wake up. After Killua says good morning and tells him that he's early, Milluki puts out his cigarette on Killua's chest. Killua mocks him with an exaggerated apology, causing Milluki to whip him again. Killua spits out blood and smirks before Milluki's phone rings with a call from their mother. Milluki informs his brother that three of his friends are at the butlers' quarters. Killua shows no emotions in response, but when Milluki asks if he should have the butlers take care of them, Killua suddenly breaks one of the chains and stares menacingly at his brother, warning him not to do it. The grandfather of the Zoldyck Family, Zeno, then enters the room and tells Milluki that that's enough. Milluki angrily replies that Killua doesn't even feel sorry for what he did, but Zeno tells his grandson that he may leave, with Killua easily breaking the other chain and then destroying all four shackles. Saying that he feels a little stiff, Killua tells Milluki that while he doesn't regret what he did, he understands that he deserved the punishment. Zeno informs Killua that his father would like to see him, and after he leaves, Milluki slams his whip down in anger and asks Zeno why he's so lenient toward Killua. Zeno stares at him and replies that he's special, asking what he thinks of his potential. Milluki guesses that he has the most talent of any Zoldyck ever, but stresses that he's too erratic to be a good assassin. He adds that no one who runs away and makes friends is fit to be the head of a family of assassins. Zeno admits that all his points are valid, and Milluki then says that he himself will kill anyone for the right price, describing his newest bomb which he can attach to a mosquito and detonate when it sucks blood. As the two leave the dungeon, Zeno tells Milluki that he's both smart and an idiot. Elsewhere in the Zoldyck mansion, Silva asks Killua about the friends he made, and Killua replies that he enjoys being with them. Silva then asks how the Hunter Exam went, and Killua gives a vague answer. Silva tells his son to sit near him and that he wants to hear about everything that happened, just asking that he talk to him. Back outside, Kikyo introduces herself as Killua's mother and introduces the young child as Kalluto. Not saying a word in reply, Gon turns as he hears Canary wake up, with both Leorio and Kurapika relieved to see that she was only unconscious. Gon asks Kikyo why they can't see Killua, and she explains that he is in solitary confinement after attacking his brother and her and then running away. She adds that he chose to return and repent, not sure when he will want to see visitors. However, as her visor suddenly makes a noise, she angrily wonders why Zeno allowed Killua to leave. As Kikyo tells them that she has to go, Gon politely asks her to let Killua know that they will be in the area for 10 more days. She courteously agrees to do so and begins to leave, but Kalluto stays behind and continues to stare at the group of three before Kikyo orders him to catch up. Leorio bluntly comments that he has never met anyone more creepy, confident that Killua didn't choose to come back and suggesting that they follow his mother. Although he considers it, Gon worries that it will bring even more trouble to Canary, who sits up and tells the three that the butlers' quarters aren't far away. She adds that it has a phone which connects directly to the mansion, explaining that they may be able to see Killua if Zeno answers. Kikyo and Kalluto continue to sprint back toward the mansion, with the former extremely upset that no one asked her first about letting Killua leave. Back inside the mansion, Killua happily tells his father about how Gon defeated Hanzo, and after Silva says that Gon is definitely interesting, he asks Killua if he would like to see him. As Killua stays silent, Silva asks him to be honest and says that while they are father and son, there hasn't been much meaning in those words. He explains that he was raised by his own parents to be an assassin and he thought that it was how he should raise him as well. However, putting his hand on Killua's head, Silva tells him that he finally realized on the day he left that while he's his son, he is also his own person and has his own path to follow. He hopes that it will lead Killua back there, but again asks him if he wants to see his friends. Killua energetically says yes after a short pause, and Silva then bites his own thumb to draw blood, holding it out and asking him to promise that he will never betray his friends. Killua does the same and presses his thumb up against his father's, swearing that he will never betray them. Kikyo suddenly opens the doors and informs Killua that his friends have left, telling him to return to his cell. After Killua refuses to do so and says that he is leaving, Kikyo reaches out her hand to stop him, but Killua glares at her and tells her to move aside. Appearing concerned at first, Kikyo praises his cold glare as she watches him leave. She then confronts Silva and asks why they allowed him to leave after Illumi finally brought him home. Silva tries to explain that Killua needs to go his own way, but Kikyo refuses to calm down and points out that it's the most crucial point in Killua's path to become the head of the family. After Silva replies that it's why they need to allow him to leave, he suddenly chuckles and assures her that he will be back, stressing that Killua is his son.

Chapter 43 The Zoldycks: Part 4 (ゾルディック④, "Zorudikku Ke (Yon)") is the 43rd chapter of the Hunter × Hunter manga, written and illustrated by Yoshihiro Togashi. Synopsis. Canary leads Gon, Kurapika, and Leorio to the butlers' quarters where five butlers stand outside waiting and all bow to welcome them. Offering tea to their guests and bandaging Gon's injuries, they apologize for their previous hostility and assure them that they will be treated as official guests at Kikyo's request. After sitting down, they are welcomed to the butlers' quarters, and Kurapika asks if they are at the mansion, with Canary replying that they aren't even close. Leorio appreciates their generosity, but reminds them that they are there to see Killua, asking that they be taken up to the mansion. However, Gotoh assures them it won't be necessary since Killua is on his way there. With the three happy to hear the news, Gotoh suggests that they pass the time by playing a game, suddenly tossing a coin into the air and catching it with one of his hands. He asks them which hand holds the coin, and all three point to his left. After confirming this, he says that he will now do it more quickly, again flipping the coin and catching it with one of his hands. Gon answers that the coin is in his left hand, and the butlers are impressed as they applaud Gon's perception. Gotoh then says that it's time to get serious, dramatically increasing the speed of his hands as the three are taken aback by the quick movement. After Leorio is left unsure and guesses his right hand, Gotoh emphasizes that he has known Killua since he was a baby and cares about him as if he were his own son, angrily telling them that he doesn't approve of them taking him away. As the three sit in silence, he asks them to choose which hand holds the coin, and Kurapika says his left. Gotoh opens his hand, and the three see that the coin has been bent. Gotoh then recounts that Kikyo's voice was barely a whisper and that her heart is breaking at her son's departure, which is all because of them. Gotoh says that he will evaluate them using his rules before Killua arrives and that they cannot refuse. Two of the butlers suddenly pull out large knives, one of whom holds the blade at Canary's throat. Gotoh explains that if they make one mistake, they are out and that if they all make a mistake before Killua arrives, he will tell him that they just left, assuring them that they will be gone. Gon tries to ask something about Killua, but Gotoh immediately silences him, saying that he can barely stand the sight of them and that they will only speak when told to do so. Gotoh suddenly tosses the coin into the air and moves his hands even faster than before, leaving all three unsure which hand holds the coin. He gives them three seconds to answer, warning them that the butler will slit Canary's throat otherwise. Leorio yells out left, with both Gon and Kurapika answering right. Gotoh reveals that it's in his right hand, removing Leorio from the game. He immediately repeats the process, and neither Gon nor Kurapika is able to tell. After they give each other a look, Kurapika chooses right and Gon left. Gotoh reveals that it's in his left hand and eliminates Kurapika from the game. As the two stare at each other, Gotoh flips the coin to begin the next round, but Gon suddenly tells him to wait. Gotoh catches the coin and says that if he is trying to stall, one of them will receive the knife. However, Gon says that he will do it himself as he asks to borrow Leorio's switchblade. He removes the bandage from his swollen eye and cuts it with the knife. Kurapika realizes that he cut himself to reduce the swelling, and Gon puts tape around his eye to keep it open, telling Gotoh to start whenever he's ready. Gotoh quickly moves his hands around, but Gon easily sees that it's in his left hand. Slightly impressed, Gotoh stands up from his chair and says that he will increase the difficulty. As two other butlers stand beside him, he flips the coin and the three move all their hands at once, stunning Kurapika and Leorio while Gon continues to concentrate. Gotoh asks which of them has the coin, but Gon chuckles and points to the butler standing behind him, who holds out the coin in his left hand. As the five butlers applaud and congratulate Gon, Killua suddenly yells out Gon's name and Gon responds. Gotoh smiles and apologizes for taking his joke too far, but adds that it helped pass the time. Leorio checks his watch and is surprised to see that it has, also noting that it didn't seem like a joke at all. With Gon left unsure by Gotoh's cheerful expression, Killua enters the room and says all their names, forgetting Leorio's before getting quickly corrected. Both Gon and Killua jokingly comment on their injured conditions, and the latter says that they need to leave before his mother changes her mind. He then says goodbye to all the butlers and addresses Gotoh specifically, ordering him not to follow him no matter what his mother said. Gotoh bows and tells him to have a good time. The other three leave, and Gon asks Gotoh if he will miss Killua. Still bowing, Gotoh explains that their duty is to serve their employers, not to become emotionally attached to them. However, Gon sees through his lie as he sticks his tongue out in jest. Gotoh then flips a coin one last time and asks Gon to choose. Gon confidently points to his left, but Gotoh chuckles as he reveals that it's in his right. With Gon left confused, Gotoh tells him that even the most perceptive person can be fooled, asking him to be careful since the world is full of tricks. As Gon stands in silence, Gotoh bows again and asks him to look after Killua.

Chapter 44 The Heavens Arena (, "Tenkū Tōgijō") is the 44th chapter of the Hunter × Hunter manga, written and illustrated by Yoshihiro Togashi. Synopsis. Now in a small town with Kukuroo Mountain in the distance, Kurapika shows Gotoh's final coin trick to the others, catching the tossed coin and asking Gon to choose the correct hand. Gon answers with the left, but Kurapika reveals that it's in his right hand, leaving Gon dumbfounded again. Kurapika explains that he used two coins, palming one and then flipping the other before obviously catching it with his left. He adds that it takes practice and that one needs to hold their fists above the viewer's eye level, letting the left coin fall down into their sleeve undetected. After Gon finally understands how it works, Killua explains that while Gotoh knows a lot of tricks, he hates cheating. He then leans in toward Gon and angrily asks him why he is so stubborn. With Gon confused, Killua reminds him that he has a license after passing the Hunter Exam and that he can go nearly anywhere he wants without a tourist visa. Leorio points that they told him already, and Gon says that he has things he wants to do before he uses it. He first tells them that he wants to find Kite and return the license he dropped. Rummaging through his backpack, he then pulls out Hisoka's badge and says that he wants to punch him in the face and make him take it back, unable to feel like he earned his license until then. Killua asks him if he knows where to find Hisoka, but Gon's silence tells them that he has no idea. However, Kurapika reveals that Hisoka told him after the lecture. Leorio points out that he also said something during their fight, reminding Kurapika that they are all friends and allies even though it's his own business. Kurapika then reveals that during their fight, Hisoka said he knew something interesting about the Spiders. He explains that he never mentioned the Phantom Troupe to him, guessing that he heard it from them during the first phase or heard it from someone who had overheard them. He continues by saying that the Troupe is often referred to as the Spiders because it's their symbol and that Hisoka's knowledge of this piqued his interest. Leorio replies aloud that it makes sense, while internally he says that it was the reason why Kurapika put aside his pride and took the free win. Kurapika then reveals that he asked him about it after the lecture, and Hisoka replied that he would tell him in Yorknew City on September 1st. Gon points out that it's more than six months away, and Killua wonders what's happening in the city then. Leorio then realizes that it's when the largest auction in the world takes place, and Kurapika explains that during those ten days, numerous rare objects (including counterfeits and forgeries) will be bought by people with enormous amounts of wealth. Leorio asks if the Troupe will be there, and while Kurapika isn't sure, he says that there will at least be people there who know of them, including Hisoka. He promises to find Hisoka and call Gon, who happily thanks him. Kurapika then tells them that it's time for him to leave since reuniting with Killua was the last thing he needed to do before making use of his license, explaining that he will use it to earn money so that he can attend the auction. Leorio says that he is also leaving, reminding Gon about his dream and that his license will cover his tuition to a public medical school (as long as he can qualify). After Gon tells him to study hard, the four agree to meet again on September 1 in Yorknew City. After Gon and Killua say goodbye to Kurapika and Leorio at the airport, watching their airship fly off into the distance, Gon is left unsure what they should do next. Killua suggests training and sharply deduces that it would take him ten years to even get close to Hisoka's skill level, reminding him that they only have six months. He picks up a stick to draw Hisoka and Hanzo's faces in the ground, showing how far apart the two are in terms of ability. He then moves incredibly far away to show the skill gap between them and Gon on his best day. Telling himself that he should feel insulted, Gon asks Killua where he would place himself, surprised to see that Hanzo is stronger. He then calls Killua amazing, but Killua tells him not to say it so seriously since it's embarrassing. Gon asks how he compares people's strengths so easily, and Killua stresses that it's just an approximation, assuring him that it becomes easier with experience. However, he tells Gon not to rely on it too much since stronger opponents are better at hiding their strength. Killua again tells Gon that he won't be able to beat Hisoka with only six months of training, asking him how much money he has. Gon says that he is running low, and Killua reveals that they can train and make money at a place called Heavens Arena. As they travel by airship to the enormous tower, Killua says that it's the fourth tallest building in the world (3,250 feet) and on the same continent, also using the map to point out Yorknew to the south of them. He adds that they will need to earn a living since the airfare has left them with no money, asking Gon if he's ready for their new beginning. After Gon energetically says yes, the two walk out and stand in the long line of combatants waiting to compete. Killua assures him that there aren't any rules to worry about, revealing that the only objective is to knock the opponent out and that they will make more money the higher they go. Once they reach the front of the line, a woman welcomes them and hands them each a form to fill out, with Killua whispering to Gon that he should write ten years of combat experience to increase his initial ranking. The two then enter a large arena filled with sixteen small fighting platforms. Gon is left in disbelief, and Killua happily takes in the scene, saying that it hasn't changed at all. Gon asks if he has been there before, and Killua explains that his father left him there with no money when he was six and said he had to stay until he made it to the 200th floor (which took him two years). With Gon thinking about what he went through, Killua then explains that fighters as skilled as Hisoka are found much higher up the tower. Gon's number is suddenly called, causing him to feel nervous, but Killua reminds him that he opened the Testing Gate, whispering in his ear what he should do. Gon walks out to meet his opponent, an enormous man who dwarfs him in size. The audience members talk among themselves and yell out jeers toward Gon, telling him to run away and supporting his opponent. The referee explains that their conditioning will be evaluated and tells them that they have three minutes to show their skill level. After the referee gives the signal to begin, the large man immediately charges forward and promises to make it quick. However, Gon dodges his initial punch and follows Killua's advice, simply pushing him in the midsection. Reeling from the attack, the man is sent flying back and crashes into the stands. The audience is left stunned, and Gon is surprised that he has become so strong. The referee tells him to advance to the 50th floor, and Killua then wins his match as well, with the judge noting his veteran status and telling him to start on the 180th floor. However, Killua says that he will start on the 50th since he wants to take it easy at first. As the audience cheers for another fighter, Killua looks over to see a young boy who has defeated another large man, with the referee telling him to start on the 50th floor.

Chapter 45 Ren (レン, "Ren") is the 45th chapter of the Hunter × Hunter manga, written and illustrated by Yoshihiro Togashi. Synopsis. It's stated that Heavens Arena is a tower combat arena where 4,000 fighters on average come every day to test their skills, with the winners rewarded by reaching higher and higher floors. It's added that high-ranked fighters can control an entire floor and that annual attendance from spectators is over one billion, with restaurants and shops also located in the tower. A female official leads a group of fighters (including Gon and Killua) inside an elevator, explaining that the tower is divided into 20 divisions of ten floors each (up to the 200th floor). She adds that a fighter who wins on the 50th floor will move up to the 60th, while one who loses will move down to the 40th. As Killua tells Gon that a room will be provided once they reach the 100th floor, the two suddenly notice the young boy from earlier also standing in the elevator. After the three reach the 50th floor, the boy suddenly bows and introduces himself as Zushi. The two introduce themselves as well, and Zushi says that he was amazed by both their fights. Although they were unable to watch Zushi's match, the two guess that he is equally skilled. Zushi replies that he is there to improve and asks what school the two belong to, revealing that he studies Shingen-ryu . The two are left confused and simply reply that they are independent. Humbled by the self-taught fighters, Zushi bows and says that he is inadequate as his master suddenly arrives and praises his student's manners. After Zushi points out that his shirttail is untucked and introduces Gon and Killua, the man introduces himself as Wing and is surprised to see other kids besides Zushi. Killua tells him that they want to train and also make money since they're broke, with Gon pointing out that Killua has been there before. Wing recognizes that the two are skilled enough to reach the 50th floor and says that the key now is safety first. An official takes the boys' ticket stubs and gives them each 152 for winning their first fight. Zushi points out that it's just enough to buy a can of juice, which Killua does as he tells them that they will earn 50,000 if they win on the 50th floor. He then reveals that they will earn 1 million on the 100th floor and more than 10 million past the 150th floor. Gon remembers that Killua reached the 200th floor before and wonders what happened to all the money. Killua replies that he mainly spent it on snacks over the past four years, with Gon asking again about the exact amount. Killua reveals that while he qualified for the 200th floor, he quit before fighting there and made 200 million on the 190th floor. Gon and Zushi are both stunned that he spent so much on snacks, with Killua telling them that they should be able to fight at least one more match that day. After the three make their way to a locker room filled with other fighters, Killua assures them that they will be able to win and earn their 50,000. Two fighters named Maita and Chibaba are told over the intercom to report to the 55th floor before Killua and Zushi are told to make their way to the 57th floor. Zushi nervously bows and tells Killua that he is honored to fight him. Killua apologizes for having to beat him and tells Gon to meet him in the 60th floor lobby, confidently adding that it shouldn't take long. With Wing watching among the cheering crowd, the announcer introduces the two fighters and shows the replays from their previous fights. She tells the audience to make their choice with their wager buttons, and Zushi comes out as the clear favorite to win, leaving Killua annoyed. After the announcer explains that there will be three three-minute rounds and that the fight can be won by points or knockout, the referee begins the match. Zushi immediately takes a solid stance, and Killua praises it internally as he calmly walks toward him. Zushi becomes nervous and throws a hard right punch, but Killua easily dodges it and strikes Zushi in the back of the neck, apologizing and saying that he is only using that attack until the 150th floor. The referee declares a clean hit, and the announcer says that Killua now has two points, reminding the audience that a clean hit is worth one point, a critical hit two, and a knockdown one. As she adds that ten points are needed for a TKO, Killua wonders why she is telling them since the fight is over. However, once the referee checks on Zushi, the boy rises to his feet and leaves Killua surprised. Although Zushi assumes his stance again and throws a flurry of punches, Killua dodges them all and again strikes the back of his neck. As Zushi quickly recovers, Killua realizes that he will have to change his tactics, unsure how Zushi is still conscious after his powerful strikes. Zushi tells himself that while he faked Killua out, it's impossible to equal him. He then decides to resort to something as he assumes a stance that causes Killua to jump back in terror. As the announcer wonders why Killua is retreating, Wing suddenly screams out Zushi's name and causes the spectators around him to run away as they cover their ears. Killua nervously turns to look at Wing, who quickly sits down in frustration. The announcer says that the crowd's cheering seemed to drown her out before she turns their attention back to the match. Waiting in the 60th floor lobby, Gon suddenly spots Killua and shows him the 60,000 he won. He wonders what took him so long, and Killua replies that Zushi proved to be a challenge, explaining that while he has talent and promise, he's nowhere close to their levels. However, he confesses that while he easily won against Zushi, he was unable to knock him out. He then reveals that Zushi used a new stance that gave him the same bad feeling as when he faces his brother. He tells Gon that he can't figure out the technique if it is one, only knowing that it's dangerous and revealing that Wing called it Ren. In a flashback, Zushi prostrates on the floor in front of his teacher and deeply apologizes. Wing reminds him that he was told not to use Ren yet, and Zushi asks for forgiveness, adding that Killua was just too strong. Wing kneels down and tells him that while it's fine to want to win, he can't lose sight of his goal of making it to the top floor. He stresses that impatience will weaken his potential and tells Zushi to get used to losing since it will happen many times. Back in the present, Killua lingers on Wing's words and says that it's time to change their plans, telling Gon that they are going to the top of the tower. Gon confidently agrees aloud while saying to himself that it was his plan from the start.

Chapter 46 Nen (ネン, "Nen") is the 46th chapter of the Hunter × Hunter manga, written and illustrated by Yoshihiro Togashi. Synopsis. As Gon and Killua are both shown winning another fight, it's announced that in the three days since entering Heavens Arena, they have each won six matches in a row without being touched. The two then reach the 100th floor and receive their own rooms. Gon is happy that they no longer have to worry about money, but Killua warns him that it's only true as long as they keep winning, which is difficult to do since many fighters will now do anything to avoid losing. Although Killua warns Gon about certain fighters who deliberately stall, the two continue to win with one-hit victories easily. They receive even more prize money in their accounts, and Gon remembers that they were completely broke just a week earlier. Killua is annoyed that it took him two months to reach the 150th floor during his first time there, but Gon reminds him that he was only six years old. Gon then changes the subject and says that he saw one of Zushi's matches, with Killua guessing that he's still on the 50th floor. Gon thinks back to the mention of Ren and wonders why it terrified Killua so much. Killua thinks back to Zushi's stance and considers that they may encounter others who use it, but before he can say anything else, Gon points out that he can just ask Zushi about it. The two make their way to the 50th floor to question Zushi, who immediately explains that Ren is one of the Four Exercises and that these are fundamental to every martial art. He states that one learns Ten, knows Zetsu, through Ren, to attain Hatsu, all of which are needed to train for Nen. With Gon and Killua both left confused, Wing suddenly appears and tells Zushi that he isn't qualified to teach. He then tells Gon and Killua that unfocused learning can lead to even more ignorance, but Killua says that he really wants to learn it, confident that it's the secret behind his brother's powers. Wing asks if his brother knows Nen, and after Killua guesses that he does, he asks Wing to teach them and promises not to ask around anymore if he agrees to do so. After making their way to Wing's hotel room, Wing reveals that Nen of the Flame inflames the user's soul and is expressed by their strength of will. He adds that the Four Exercises harness said strength, explaining that Ten involves focusing one's mind and deciding on a goal, Zetsu putting it into words, Ren intensifying one's will, and Hatsu putting it into action. He tells Killua that he was intimidated by Zushi's Ren because it was his will to win. He then agrees to demonstrate the process and happily tells Killua that he is going to kill him, asking if that's okay. Taken aback at first, Killua says that it's fine even though he won't be able to do so. Wing first uses Ten and assumes a stance, then using Zetsu and explaining that it can be said aloud or to one's self. After Wing tells Killua that he is going to kill him, his expression suddenly changes as he glares menacingly at Killua, who becomes frozen with fear. While Gon also becomes nervous, Killua leaps back and stays in the corner of the room near the ceiling. Wing explains that he used Ren, which can function as Hatsu with enough strength and focus. He adds that it's similar to bluffing, using the example of a battle cry used to put fear into an enemy. However, he stresses that Ren needs relentless clarity for it to remain effective and that this requires a cultivated spirit. As he calmly sits down, he tells the two that they should first master Ten so that they can resist intimidation. After Killua finally jumps down, Gon thanks Wing before the two boys leave the hotel. Wing watches them from the window and tells Zushi to begin his exercises, reminding him to always start with Ten as he uses a different form of the word than the one he mentioned to Gon and Killua. Walking back to Heavens Arena, Killua tells Gon that Wing lied in his explanation, guessing that some of what he said was true and that his power is real. However, he says that it doesn't explain Zushi's resilience and reveals that he had to try harder during their match since he wouldn't stay down. In a flashback, an annoyed Killua punches Zushi hard in the midsection and sends him flying out of the ring. Killua realizes that he overdid it and apologizes internally, but Zushi somehow rises to his feet and leaves Killua stunned. However, the referee declares a critical hit and knockdown, which results in a TKO to end the match. Back in the present, Killua tells Gon that it's impossible to resist physical harm with just will, knowing that it has to involve something else. Back in Wing's hotel room, Wing reads a book and asks Zushi if something is wrong, noting that his Ten seems agitated. Zushi wonders why he misled Gon and Killua, listing the real Four Exercises and adding that they don't mean what he said. He asks his master if he decided to fool them because they're not his students, but Wing says that he told them the truth because Nen is an important discipline in training the mind for Nen (again using a different word). However, he confirms to Zushi that he only teaches Nen to his pupils and that others who ask receive the lesson suitable for everyone since it can be easily misused. He then rips out a page from the book and uses energy to straighten it out, throwing it toward a nearby can of juice and cutting through it, with the juice spilling out and the piece of paper sticking in the wall before losing its rigidity. Wing explains that by using Nen, it's possible to turn a piece of paper into a blade and that one's body can resist damage as if it were covered in steel armor. He adds that anyone can learn Nen with enough effort and application, stressing that teachers must carefully consider who will learn it. While Zushi understands his explanation, he wonders why he had to tear a page from his book and spill his juice, causing Wing to quickly apologize. Back at Heavens Arena, it's announced that Gon and Killua have won their first matches on the 190th floor.

Chapter 47 The Invisible Wall (えない, "Mienai Kabe") is the 47th chapter of the Hunter × Hunter manga, written and illustrated by Yoshihiro Togashi. Synopsis. Inside an elevator, Gon asks Killua what's on the 200th floor, but he replies that he has never actually been there. On the 50th floor, Wing is surprised by how quickly the two have progressed, and Zushi adds that they are incredible fighters. Wing then says that he may need to rethink things. Back on the 200th floor, Gon and Killua appear nervous as they look down a long hallway. Gon tells himself that even though it's just a normal hallway, he suddenly feels like he's in a jungle full of monsters. Killua takes a step forward and says that they can't stop now, but as the two begin to walk down the hallway, they suddenly feel a sinister presence, with Gon anxiously telling himself that he doesn't want to go on. Killua points out that it's intense bloodlust directed right at them, yelling out for the person ahead to show themselves. A female clerk suddenly appears and calls the two by name, explaining that registration is to her right and that they must complete it by the end of the day since their eligibility expires at midnight. She adds that there are 173 people currently waiting on the floor and that all weapon restrictions are lifted. Gon wonders if she's responsible for the bloodlust, but Killua replies that he can't be sure. As the woman explains that there will no longer be any prize money and that they are fighting for honor alone, Killua points out another person's hand suddenly appearing beside her. Hisoka finally reveals himself and, after the two wonder why he's there, explains that Heavens Arena is the perfect place for someone addicted to combat, in turn asking the two what they are doing there. He says that he already knows why and reveals that he has been waiting for them. He explains that he was able to find out when they would arrive because they used the Internet to purchase their airship tickets. He adds that he waited around the airport and then followed them, having already guessed that they would make their way to Heavens Arena. Hisoka then warns the two that they aren't ready for the 200th floor, shooing both of them away as they again feel the pressure from before. With the female official left confused, Hisoka sits down and tells them to come back later since it's not a good time, but as Killua angrily attempts to argue back, Hisoka raises his hand and stresses that they are literally unable to advance. The two again feel something that stops them in their tracks and makes them feel incredibly nervous. Wing then appears behind them and confirms that they can't overcome Hisoka's Nen. He adds that they are stuck and don't know why, warning that if they try to fight it, the effort alone will possibly kill them. Killua angrily asks if what Hisoka is using is Nen, wondering how he can stop them just by thinking he will. Wing admits that he wasn't completely honest earlier and asks the two to let him fix his mistake. As the clock reaches 8:20, Gon asks the official what will happen if they still haven't registered by midnight, and she explains that he will have to start over on the first floor. She then reveals that since Killua was there previously and didn't register, he will be deemed to lack commitment and not allowed to fight again if he doesn't register in time.
