Killua then turns to Wing and asks him if they can make it back by midnight, with Wing replying that it depends on them. The three head back to Wing's hotel room by 8:30, and Wing showcases a vase pierced with flowers as water flows out of it. He tells them that they have just witnessed Nen, explaining that it's the ability to control the life energy (aura) that suffuses their bodies. He adds that while everyone emanates a little aura, it leaks away from most unnoticed and uncontrolled. He explains that the technique Ten allows one to contain aura within the body, which strengthens it and maintains its youthful vitality. He then explains that Zetsu stops the flow of aura like a valve and allows one to hide their presence while also reducing fatigue. Next, he tells the two that Ren allows one to produce more aura, suddenly using the technique as both Gon and Killua feel the change. Gon likens it to a kind of pressure, and Killua says that it isn't ominous or sinister. As Wing mentions that it's because it has no ill-intent, he internally praises their aura sensitivity and says that while it undoubtedly involves the environment in which they grew up, both of them have amazing innate gifts. Wing continues by saying that aura is an irreducible part of their existence and that it's most effective against other humans, warning them that a defenseless person can be killed by an attack involving malicious aura. As the two continue to listen in silence, Wing explains that the only way to stay protected against such an attack is by using a Ten defense to block the opponent's strike. To show what would happen otherwise, Wing faces one of the room’s walls and puts his hand against it, suddenly causing an enormous amount of damage and reiterating that the body of a defenseless person would be shattered. Back on the 200th floor, Hisoka uses aura around his playing cards as he throws them into a nearby wall, saying that it's much too soon.

Chapter 48 Hisoka's Terms (ヒソカの, "Hisoka no Jōken") is the 48th chapter of the Hunter × Hunter manga, written and illustrated by Yoshihiro Togashi. Synopsis. As Wing stands in front of the damaged wall, he tells Gon and Killua that it also involved Nen and that the power exists within everyone. However, he explains that very few are aware of it and actually utilize it, with these individuals considered to be geniuses, psychics, or superhuman. Wing then reveals two ways to awaken someone's Nen: slowly and carefully or using force. He explains that he used the former with Zushi, who was determined and quick to learn, having mastered Ten in only six months. Killua immediately speaks up and reminds him that they need to master it by midnight in order to make it through Hisoka's Nen barrier. Wing says that using force is their only option, and Killua wonders if it will be fast enough. Wing replies that it depends on how quickly the two can learn to contain their aura. Wing tells Gon and Killua that he will first use Hatsu to transmit his aura to them, explaining that it's the same technique he used to crack the wall. The three stand in silence for a second, and Wing assures them that he has no wish to harm them and will go easy. However, he warns them that the method is drastic and likens it to jumpstarting a battery. He continues by saying that their power will be awakened and they will be able to use Ten, explaining that he is sending aura through their bodies in order to force open the nodes that are preventing the free flow of aura. He stresses that they would normally use meditation to sense the aura they have and then carefully open the nodes themselves, a process which took the gifted Zushi three months. However, he hopes that Gon and Killua will be able to do it in a week, or possibly days, if he has evaluated them correctly. He describes it as a pity that they have to take drastic measures, and Killua wonders why it's a problem, saying that he thought faster was always better. Wing replies that it's still a cheat and emphasizes that he could kill them if he were inexperienced or had any ill-intent against them. Gon makes sure that they are safe with him, and as Wing sighs in reply, Killua wonders why he decided to help them all of a sudden. Wing explains that while they are both talented, they lack the training necessary to enter the 200th floor since everyone there uses Nen. He then reveals that the fighters will initiate anyone who doesn't know Nen by attacking them once they arrive, which involves less finesse and more violence. He adds that the fighters don't care whether the initiates live or die, with those who do survive welcomed to fight as the chosen few. He tells Gon and Killua that they will see the damage the fighters suffered and why he didn't want them to advance without knowing Nen. With aura swelling around him, Wing holds out his hand and assures the two that they will awaken since they have the talent and potential. Remembering Killua's words about making it back before midnight, Wing is greatly impressed by their strength of will, telling them both to remove their jackets and turn around. He then puts his hands near each of their backs, causing aura to flow around them as well. Gon is taken aback by the warm feeling and says to himself that Wing seems to be pushing against them without even touching them. Killua describes it as an invisible water balloon against his back and likens it to Illumi's Nen, adding that his brother's was much worse. Wing then warns them in advance before opening their nodes simultaneously. Both are left stunned at first as aura flows all around their bodies. Wing explains that it's their own aura and that their nodes are completely open, including those in their eyes which allows them to see it. Still amazed by the experience, Gon compares it to steam pouring out of a kettle and Killua worries that too much is escaping from their bodies. Wing reveals that once they lose what they have left, they will be barely able to stand. Killua panics and says that they can't do anything about it, but Wing quickly gets their attention and tells them to imagine containing their aura, ordering them to close their eyes and become relaxed. He then tells them to consider their aura as the blood moving through their veins, sensing the flow throughout their entire body as it gradually slows, and then moves calmly around their core. The two immediately achieve the feat as the aura surrounds their bodies, and Wing is astounded that they not only took the best positions for Ten but mastered the flow with only a few directions, describing it as amazing and terrifying. He then tells them to open their eyes and asks how they feel. Gon says that it feels like he's in a lukewarm, viscous fluid, and Killua agrees, describing it as a weightless suit. Wing tells them to remember those feelings and that they will be able to perform Ten in their sleep once they become accustomed to it. As Wing's aura suddenly surrounds his body, he tells them to stand ready and warns that he will emit aura with malice, assuring them that his stance alone would have caused them to flee the room before. Killua is left convinced by Wing's assurance, realizing how underprepared they were for the 200th floor. The two nervously wait, and after Wing tells them to endure the attack and that they will then be ready to move through Hisoka's barrier, he sends out the malicious aura. Soon afterward, Gon and Killua return to the 200th floor and use Ten when they see Hisoka still waiting for them. As the two moves toward him, Hisoka activates his Ren, but they easily walk through it and stand confidently in front of him. Still sitting on the floor, Hisoka welcomes them back and says that they will be able to skip the initiation process. He then guesses that Gon came to Heavens Arena to train so that he could fight him, and Gon replies that he didn't expect him to be there as well, glad that it saves him the trouble. Hisoka chuckles in reply and tells him not to get overconfident now that he knows Ten, pointing out that Nen is multifaceted as he uses his aura to form a spade and then a skull between his fingertips. Rising to his feet, he assures Gon that he still has no chance against him in his current state, promising to reconsider if he wins at least one battle on the floor. As Hisoka turns and walks down a dark hallway, three disabled fighters suddenly approach Gon and Killua, quickly recognizing that they are new to the floor.

Chapter 49 The Battle Begins!! (！！, "Sentō Kaishi!!") is the 49th chapter of the Hunter × Hunter manga, written and illustrated by Yoshihiro Togashi. Synopsis. The three fighters also recognize that Gon and Killua can use Ten, but the two quickly make their way to the registration desk, where a female clerk welcomes them to the 200th floor. She hands them the registration form to sign and then asks if they would like a match, explaining that they have 90 days to do so. She adds that they can fight every day or wait until the last minute, but stresses that at least one match is necessary to earn another 90 days of preparation since their registration for the floor will be revoked if they decline to fight during that time. Gon realizes that they will be fighting multiple matches there, and she confirms that ten victories are needed to win the division, adding that four losses before ten wins will result in disqualification. She then reveals that if they do reach ten wins, they will be able to challenge a Floor Master, explaining that these 21 fighters are the highest ranked and each control an entire floor between 230 and 250. She also reveals that if they defeat a Floor Master, they will gain control of the floor and take over the title. The two wonder if that's everything, but she excitedly adds that if they become a Floor Master, they will be eligible to advance to the top floor and participate in the Battle Olympia tournament that happens every other year. The two boys are left unimpressed, and Killua asks if that's all the top floor has to offer, causing the clerk to angrily explain that the champion lives in the most exclusive penthouse in the world (3,280 feet in the air) and that there are many valuable prizes. It's pointed out that Killua lives in a house 12,000 feet above sea level, and he again expresses his disappointment to the even angrier clerk. Gon points out that he is only there to fight Hisoka, and the clerk wonders why he is even bothering with it all. Killua asks Gon if he will try to win one match right away, and Gon says that they should at least try so they can see the competition, with the disappointed clerk asking them to fill out the applications. The three fighters confront the boys again, and one of them says that they are just there to request a match. Seeing that the application requires one to write in what days work for them, Killua tells Gon that the fighters are trying to see what day he picks. As the three chuckle, Gon checks one of the boxes and hands them the form, telling them to pick any day they want. After they write in their dates, the clerk hands Gon and Killua their room keys, also telling them that they will be kept informed of their fight status. As they make their way to Gon's room, Killua understands the brutal initiation that the three fighters had to go through. After they walk inside and see how impressive the room is, Killua immediately notices that Gon's match date has been confirmed for March 11 at 3 p.m. on the 225th floor. He tells Gon that he should be ready for tomorrow and suddenly notices him using Ten. Gon smiles and says that although he doesn't expect to win, he wants to get used to Ten so he can see how it feels, with Killua not saying anything in reply. The following day, the crowd roars as the announcer introduces both fighters, saying that Gon is making his debut above the 200th floor and that Gido currently has four wins and one loss. In a flashback, Wing reminds Gon and Killua that Ten is only a defensive technique and that they must use their own skills for offense. He adds that their Ten will prove inadequate against a more proficient Nen user, ordering them not to accept any matches for their first two months and assuring them that he will teach them everything he can during that time. Back in the present, Gon apologizes and anxiously says that he just has to fight. Watching the match on a television with others around them, Wing wonders what he’s going to do with Gon as Zushi wishes him good luck. As soon as the referee begins the match and Gon activates his Ten, Gido spins a top on his finger and tells Gon that he should be glad he is his first opponent since he’s hardly a real danger. However, Gido suddenly brings out nine more tops and spins all ten covered in aura along his cane. As the announcer excitedly points out Gido’s dancing tops, he uses his Battle Waltz to send them spinning all around Gon, bouncing off each other as one strikes him right in the back. Gon realizes what happened, and the referee declares a clean hit. Gido explains that his tops will spin for hours and that even he doesn’t know what they will do. Still reeling from the attack, Gon tells himself that Gido downplayed his strength since it felt like he was hit by a sledgehammer.

Chapter 5 The First Phase Begins: Part 1 (1①, "Dai Ichi-ji Shiken Kaishi (Ichi)") is the 5th chapter of the Hunter × Hunter manga, written and illustrated by Yoshihiro Togashi. Synopsis. In Zaban City, a Kiriko in disguise leads Gon, Kurapika, and Leorio to 2-5-10 Tsubashi Street, pointing to a nearby building as the site of the Hunter Exam. The three examinees gaze up at the enormous structure, with Leorio and Kurapika nervously thinking about the other aspiring Hunters who are the best in the world. Gon, however, smiles and thinks only about his father and how he felt when he took part in his Hunter Exam. The Kiriko then gets their attention and says that he meant the building next door, pointing to a small restaurant. Leorio can't believe that all the examinees would fit into such a small place, and the Kiriko explains that they would never use a place so conspicuous. After entering the restaurant, the Kiriko asks for the steak combo, causing the chef to ask if he wants it grilled or broiled. The Kiriko replies that he wants it grilled over low flame, and another employee then shows the four to a private room with prepared food. Once the employee leaves, the Kiriko tells the three examinees that their odds of making it there were one in ten thousand, praising them for making it so far on their first attempt. He then wishes them good luck for the rest of the exam and tells them to look him up next year before he takes his leave and turns a dial. The room begins to move down an elevator shaft as Leorio eats his food and wonders if the Navigator thinks that they won't pass the exam on their first try. Kurapika says that he has heard a talented rookie passes the exam every three years on average, and it's stated that most rookies either succumb to the demands of the exam or get overwhelmed by the veterans and never retake the test. Gon wonders why so many people want to become Hunters if they have to go through so much to pass. Left speechless at first, Leorio energetically tells him that being a Hunter is the most lucrative profession while Kurapika describes it as the noblest. The two glare at each other as Gon sits nervously between them and listens to each of their arguments. Leorio focuses on the benefits of a Hunter License, which allows a Hunter to enter most countries and use nearly all available public resources. He then proclaims that 60 of the 100 richest people in the world are Hunters and that the money received from a sold license would financially secure a person's family for seven generations. On the other hand, Kurapika stresses that a Hunter's main role is securing order in society and nature, with a professional Hunter preserving cultural artifacts and tracking down criminals and poachers. He adds that a Hunter needs extensive knowledge and strong convictions, describing it as a rewarding career. The two are eager to hear what being a Hunter means to Gon, but he is left unsure and unable to answer before the elevator reaches the hundredth floor of the basement. The elevator door opens, and the three find themselves in a large tunnel filled with hundreds of examinees. Those staring at the new arrivals eventually look away, and Kurapika realizes that everyone present is one in ten thousand, adding that they are each experts in their fields. Gon wonders how many people are in the dreary tunnel, and an examinee sitting on a nearby pipe tells him he's #405. Wearing a #16 badge, the man introduces himself as Tonpa and shakes Gon's hand. After a small official gives the trio their badges, Tonpa guesses that they're new and reveals that it's his 35th attempt, adding that he started when he was 10 and happily calling himself an expert examinee. As Tonpa tells Gon to ask anything he wants to know, Kurapika and Leorio whisper between themselves about how strange it is for him to be proud of failing so many times. Gon wonders if he knows all the examinees, and Tonpa proceeds to point out some of the regulars: Bourbon (#103), a snake charmer and relentless competitor; Cherry (#76), a martial artist and the best at unarmed combat; Todo (#255), a strong wrestler who is smarter than he appears; the Amori Brothers (#197-#199) who specialize in teamwork and keep improving; and Geretta (#384), a huntsman proficient with blowdarts and clubs. After Tonpa stresses to Gon that they are only a few of the capable examinees who haven't been able to pass yet, a man suddenly screams and is shown to be missing both of his forearms. Another examinee says that no tricks were involved, telling the man to be more careful and apologize when he bumps into someone. Tonpa is disappointed to see that the man is back, telling Gon that examinee #44 is named Hisoka and explaining that he would have easily passed the previous exam if he hadn't attacked an examiner and been disqualified. Leorio is shocked that he was allowed to try again. Still, Tonpa explains that there are new examiners every year and that they choose the tests and decide who gets to take them, coyly adding that even the devil could pass the exam if an examiner allowed it. After warning the trio to avoid Hisoka since he eliminated 20 examinees during the previous exam, Tonpa offers to show them the basics as other examinees are seen chuckling and whispering that the "Rookie Crusher" Tonpa has found more victims. Tonpa then pulls out four cans of juice and asks that they toast to friendship and luck. Although Kurapika and Leorio are left unsure, Gon happily begins to drink the juice. Tonpa chuckles to himself and reveals that the drink has a powerful laxative that will leave the victim unable to take part in the exam. However, continuing to hold the juice in his mouth, Gon slowly spits it out and tells Tonpa that it tastes off, guessing that it must have gone bad. Now nervously sweating, Tonpa is left stunned since the laxative has practically no odor or taste, wondering how Gon could have tasted it. Annoying Tonpa even further, Kurapika and Leorio pour out their juice before drinking any.

Chapter 50 Zetsu (ゼツ, "Zetsu") is the 50th chapter of the Hunter × Hunter manga, written and illustrated by Yoshihiro Togashi. Synopsis. As Gido's tops continue to spin all around Gon, another one suddenly strikes him in the back as the announcer points out that Gon is facing his first real test at Heavens Arena. Gon watches the tops colliding with each other, and another strikes him in the face, sending him to the ground as the referee declares a clean hit and a knockdown. With the announcer noting that Gido already has four points, the referee asks Gon if he can continue. Gon quickly rises to his feet and confirms that he can, wondering what he should do when he can't track the tops' movement. Still watching the match, Zushi asks if Gido is using Nen, and Wing confirms that he is using a form of Hatsu to infuse his tops with aura. He explains that Nen can strengthen the function of an object and likens aura to gas or batteries, adding that more aura is needed for a bigger object and that Gido can keep the small tops spinning for hours. He then surmises that Gido gave the tops even more Nen to work as a command, explaining that someone's emotional attachment to an object improves its response. Gon continues to struggle tracking the tops and tells himself that since they are charged with Nen, he needs to sense their movement. He closes his eyes and begins to feel it, but realizes that his Ten is fading as another top strikes him in the back. The announcer declares that Gido now has six points and comments on Gon bouncing outside the ring. As Gon realizes that he can't focus on sensing the tops without neglecting his Ten, he notices one spinning outside the ring and not attacking him. The referee asks if he can continue, but Gon tells him to be quiet so he can think. The referee angrily replies that he will lose if he doesn't return to the ring in ten seconds. As the referee begins the count, Gon says to himself that he doesn't sense any sinister Nen from the top. He wonders about the others and sees that they are moving around randomly as they strike one another now and again. Gon realizes that they may not be coming after him and asks the referee why he's standing outside the ring. The referee replies that he would get hit if he were up there, and Gon realizes that it's exactly like the sumo tops game. Wing explains to Zushi that a Nen user can't give a complex command to something that's not a machine or animal, guessing that Gido ordered the tops to deflect any obstacles. He adds that since the tops can't identify obstacles, they just spin around the ring and strike anything they encounter. Realizing that he can just ignore the tops, Gon jumps back inside the ring before the count ends and charges toward Gido. However, as Gon attempts to land a kick, Gido explains that even though he realized the trick, he won't be able to attack him directly, suddenly spinning his entire body and sending Gon flying out of the ring with his Tornado Top ability. The announcer describes it as Gido's vicious technique that uses offense and defense, with the referee declaring a critical hit and a knockdown. The announcer then declares that Gon is in trouble now that Gido has nine points. Gido chuckles and says that he has never lost since being initiated on the 200th floor and getting his current body. He explains that he protects himself with his Tornado Top ability while letting his tops handle the offense, allowing him to slowly score points during the match. Killua yells out to Gon and tells him not to attack since Gido will get dizzy soon. A nearby spectator laughs and describes his advice as amateur, but when he attempts to explain that people like figure skaters can overcome it through training, Killua sends him back with a punch and wonders who he even is. Still reeling from the attack, Gon wonders what he can do with his current skills. Wing tells Zushi that Gon could either keep attacking until Gido runs out of Ten or try to overpower his defensive aura. However, he explains that Gon hasn't learned Ren yet and doesn't know how to generate aura either, guessing that he's fighting Gido five years too early. Gritting his teeth, Gon wonders how he can keep fighting and realizes that the match will end if he gives up one more point. Gido, Killua, and Zushi are all stunned when Gon suddenly stops using Ten and closes his eyes. Wing then realizes that Gon not only stopped using Ten but is somehow using Zetsu, which has closed all his nodes and left him defenseless against Nen. Wing points out that he hasn't taught it to Gon, realizing that he must have picked it up on his own like an animal learning to hunt prey. He wonders if that's what his childhood has been like, understanding how he has so much potential but left asking himself why Gon would use Zetsu now. As Killua yells out to Gon and reminds him he will be in great danger without any Nen, Gon tells himself that he needs to focus all his senses to feel the tops' movement and that using Ten would distract him. Wing then realizes that Gon never planned to win the match and is risking his own life in order to practice. As the tops bounce all around him and Gido laughingly says that he will get his death wish, Gon continues to concentrate and suddenly dodges one of the tops that would have struck him in the head. With Gido left stunned, the announcer excitedly asks if Gon will begin to make a comeback. Gon continues to sense where the tops are going and reminds himself to give everything he has to avoid them so that he can keep fighting. Watching at the back of the arena, Hisoka is seen smirking as he eagerly clenches his right fist.

Chapter 51 Ten (, "Ten") is the 51st chapter of the Hunter × Hunter manga, written and illustrated by Yoshihiro Togashi. Synopsis. After Gon's match at Heavens Arena, Killua tells him that he has a broken radius and ulna in his right arm, a cracked humerus, three broken ribs, and twelve cracks, calling him an idiot after adding that the injuries will take four months to completely heal. Gon sits up in his bed and playfully apologizes, but Killua pokes him in the forehead and angrily wonders what he's thinking about, pointing out that he could have ended up like the fighters who were initiated by Nen. He tells Gon that he was lucky and reminds him that Wing warned them not to fight. Gon replies that he guessed he wouldn't die after he took a few hits, and Killua then rests his foot on Gon's broken arm, hearing a knock at the door and wondering who it could be. Killua slowly opens the door and is surprised to see Wing, who silently approaches Gon's bed and suddenly slaps him before he can apologize. With the two left stunned, Wing angrily tells him not to apologize and wonders what he was thinking, reminding Gon again that he could have ended up like the fighters who were initiated by Nen (which Killua points out). Wing then calmly pats Gon on the shoulder and says that he's relieved his injuries aren't any worse. Gon apologizes, but Wing says that it isn't enough to get him off the hook, asking Killua how long it will take for his injuries to heal. Killua replies that the doctor said two months, putting on a cat-like smirk when Wing turns his back to him. Wing then forbids Gon from competing in any matches for two months and from training or studying Nen, refusing to teach him further if he can't keep the promise. After Gon swears to it while silently thanking Killua, Wing asks for Gon's left hand and wraps a small string around his pinky finger, explaining that it marks his pledge and telling him to look at it so he doesn't forget. As Gon continues to stare at it, Wing asks Killua if he can talk to him outside the room. Once the two leave, Wing asks Killua what their goals are at Heavens Arena. Killua replies that their plans have changed since they arrived, explaining that they only wanted pocket money before they met him and Zushi. He adds that Gon is there to train so that he can fight someone named Hisoka. He then reveals that while the top floor is the goal for most fighters on the 200th floor, the Battle Olympia tournament doesn't interest him. However, he adds that he isn't sure about Gon after seeing how much he was enjoying his fight against Gido. In a flashback to the fight, Gon continues to dodge Gido's spinning tops as the announcer wonders how long Gon can avoid almost 50 tops, pointing out that he has maintained it for over an hour. With Gido appearing weary, she stresses that he can only watch what happens like another spectator. Gon continues to dodge the tops all around him, but as Killua yells for Gon not to move in a specific direction, he is left with no place to dodge and braces for the impact when a top suddenly strikes him in his right side. Back in the present, Wing wonders how Gon was enjoying the fight when he could have died. Killua confirms that Gon was and says that while he can sometimes feel that way too, he picks and chooses his battles. He then doubts that Gon can think rationally once he becomes so invested in something, but assures Wing that Gon won't break the same promise twice. With Wing left worried, Killua says that even if he quits teaching them, they will simply find someone else or learn it themselves. He tells Wing not to blame himself and explains that they would have discovered the truth eventually since both his brother and Hisoka use Nen. Wing assures him that he doesn't plan to quit and suggests studying with Zushi back at his hotel. However, Killua politely declines by explaining that he doesn't want to get ahead of Gon. As Killua walks away, Wing tells him that Gon is allowed to practice Nen of the Flame, adding that he should also practice the focusing "Ten" exercise every day. Killua returns to Gon's room and finds him focusing in silence on his bed. Killua then sits on the floor and does the same. Gon then remembers Mito's words about Ging not abandoning him as well as Kite describing him as the best Hunter, whom he must find as his final test. Memories of Ging's picture, talking with Kite, Hisoka's face, and saying goodbye to Kon also fill his head as he hears someone call his name. Both Gon and Killua continue to focus in silence. Elsewhere, a guild agent praises Kurapika for finding the guild, but states that she cannot introduce him to their clients. She adds that it doesn't involve his inexperience since that's not an issue to the clients, but explains that he is pre-green. Kurapika is left confused and confidently states that he has a Hunter License. The agent reveals that Kurapika hasn't finished his test, asking him what he sees next to her. Although aura surrounds the woman and a skull appears beside her, she knows that Kurapika is unable to see anything, telling him to return when he meets the minimum requirement. At Wing's hotel room, Wing talks to himself and asks his master if he has awoken a monster. Zushi stops his training and looks worriedly at Wing, who has an anxious and excited expression on his face as aura surrounds him.

Chapter 52 Kastro (カストロ, "Kasutoro") is the 52nd chapter of the Hunter × Hunter manga, written and illustrated by Yoshihiro Togashi. Synopsis. Finding Gon doing a handstand in his room, Killua asks if he's already okay. Gon jumps around energetically and confirms that he's completely healed, with Killua left in disbelief that his four-month injury healed in only a month. After playfully asking what Gon is made of, Killua shows him two tickets for Hisoka's match, explaining that he was able to get them since they're on the 200th floor (although he still had to pay for them). He adds that the match is so popular that there are even ticket scalpers, who revealed that Hisoka has fought 11 matches so far and won eight of them. Killua also reveals that Hisoka's six knockouts all resulted in death and that his three losses were all default since he didn't show up for them. He stresses that Hisoka has never lost and only had four points scored against him (one knockdown and three clean hits). While Gon says that it's intimidating, Killua sees that he has an excited look on his face. He then tells Gon that Hisoka is fighting a man named Kastro, who has taken three of the four points from Hisoka and is the only one to knock him down. He says that it will be a showdown and explains that the two mutually agreed to the fight date. As Killua is eager to analyze Hisoka's skills and possibly see him get knocked down, Gon worries about his promise to Wing. Although Killua is confident that it won't count since they're only watching the match, Wing appears right behind them and explains that watching counts as studying Nen, ordering Gon to focus on improving for one more month. With the two left startled, Gon understands and Killua wonders if he was stalking them. After Wing walks away, he is able to tell from their aura that they have been performing "Ten" every day, describing it as a great but calm river. As his aura is seen around him, Wing worries that he's the one losing his calm. Killua tells Gon that they can tape the match after he sees it by himself. He also points out that one ticket cost him 150,000, which could buy a thousand chocolate robots. After internally pointing out that Killua is a billionaire and heading back to his room, Gon turns off the television and looks at the string around his finger. He tries to focus while closing his eyes, but his arm begins to shake with excitement, forcing him to stop it with his other hand as a look of determination appears on his face. Inside the arena, the announcer points out that the stadium is already full an hour before the match. After introducing Hisoka, she announces that Kastro has won nine times in a row after losing to Hisoka, leaving him one win away from challenging a Floor Master. As Killua watches his interview and says that he thought he would be a gorilla, the charming Kastro tells the interviewer that he wouldn't fight if he thought he didn't have a chance, promising to show that he has improved in the past two years. Eager to see if Kastro is as confident as he appears, Killua distracts a Heavens Arena official and makes his way to Kastro's room. He sees him sitting in a chair and moves closer to open the door even more, but Kastro suddenly appears behind him and asks if he needs any help. Killua is left stunned and tells himself that Kastro was just sitting in the now empty chair. He wonders if Kastro opened the door and somehow slipped by him, but assures himself that it's impossible since he only looked away from the door after Kastro talked to him. Killua then pretends to want an autograph, and Kastro calls him by name, saying that he knows all his rivals on the 200th floor and wondering where Gon is. Killua guesses that Kastro knows everything and explains that he just wanted to see him in person. After Killua calls him impressive, Kastro thanks him and praises his Zetsu, adding that he should have started using it before he arrived on the floor. He confirms that he was tracking him right when he left the elevator, and Killua wonders how he was able to do it, but Kastro refuses to answer since the two may fight one day. Killua assures him that he doesn't plan to fight there anymore, but Kastro replies that his aura says otherwise. He then laughs and says that he was joking, explaining that he will show him the answer during the match. Kastro asks about the autograph before leaving, but Killua says that he forgot to bring something for him to sign. Confident that Killua will make it, Kastro then says that he will be waiting at Battle Olympia, but after Kastro closes the door, Killua internally repeats that he isn't going to fight. With the match about to start, Kastro thanks Hisoka and says that he never would have become so strong without his initiation. As Hisoka wonders who became strong, Kastro reveals that he never once tried his hardest in his past nine matches, all of which were warm-ups to defeat him. After the referee begins the match, Kastro immediately leaps forward and throws a strike with his right arm. Hisoka appears to duck below it at first, but Kastro's strike makes contact and sends Hisoka back, with the referee declaring a clean hit. Hisoka is left wondering how the strike hit him, and Kastro sternly tells him to get serious.

Chapter 53 Double (ダブル, "Daburu") is the 53rd chapter of the Hunter × Hunter manga, written and illustrated by Yoshihiro Togashi. Synopsis. As the crowd roars and Hisoka recovers from the strike, Kastro explains that he has changed in the past two years ago and won't go as easy on him with the next attack. The announcer declares that Kastro has gained the first point, and Killua is left wondering if Kastro's attack was an optical illusion. After Hisoka stands up and replies that he will decide when he gets serious, Kastro tells him to decide quickly before leaping toward him once again. He swipes at Hisoka with his left hand, and although Hisoka seems to duck below it easily, he is somehow hit by the attack and left thinking that he dodged it like the previous strike. Hisoka refuses to be knocked down and leaps back from Kastro's subsequent barrage of attacks. As the wound on Hisoka's cheek bleeds from the previous strike, he sees Kastro throwing a kick and blocks it with his left arm. However, Kastro somehow appears directly behind him and slams him down with a vicious kick to the head. The referee declares a clean hit and knockdown, with the announcer declaring that Kastro now has four points as she wonders if she imagined what she just saw. Kastro then asks Hisoka if he won’t change his mind and wonders if he will die without discovering what's happening. The referee asks Hisoka if he can continue, and Hisoka rises to his feet saying that it seemed as though Kastro had vanished. As the announcer agrees, Hisoka clarifies his explanation and guesses that he's overlooking something simple. Kastro tells him that he won't be able to discover the truth if he refuses to face him, threatening to take his arm with the next attack. He then gets into a strange stance, and the crowd immediately recognizes it as his Tiger Bite Fist. Even Killua recognizes the martial art form and says that masters can use it to rip entire trees in half. He points out that Hisoka still hasn't realized what Kastro's ability is, adding that he hasn't either and guessing that Hisoka will end up dead. As Kastro announces his approach and lunges toward him, Hisoka suddenly holds out his left arm and asks him to take it. Kastro wonders whether it's stupidity or a trap, but plans to do so as he moves toward Hisoka's left arm. However, he suddenly moves behind Hisoka and uses his Tiger Bite Fist to sever his right arm instead (below the elbow). The crowd is left stunned, and Kastro tells Hisoka that he will never let him get his way. Hisoka calmly explains that everything is going as expected, leaping away from Kastro's next strike and catching his dismembered arm before it hits the floor. He then chuckles and surmises that Kastro's ability allows him to create a double. With the crowd left confused, Kastro confirms Hisoka's suspicion by revealing an exact copy of himself that leaves the spectators in disbelief. Killua understands that it wasn't a trick and points out that he thought another Kastro seemed to be superimposed on him. The announcer wonders whether she's seeing double or Kastro has a twin, but Hisoka deduces that it's a doppelganger. After Kastro confirms it, the word's entry in "The Encyclopedia of the Paranormal" is shown, explaining the term in detail and including multiple real-world accounts. Hisoka then says that he watched without evading him and that he was right to use the word "vanished" earlier. He continues to think out his explanation aloud and finally says that there were two of Kastro in the split second before he vanished. Calling Hisoka impressive, Kastro explains that he uses his Nen double to attack first while he hides in its shadows, extinguishing it once he reacts and then attacking. Killua realizes that Kastro's loose clothing creates blind spots and that it's difficult to discover how it all works during combat. Kastro assures Hisoka that the double isn't an illusion and that he felt its strike, warning him that his True Tiger Bite Fist involves facing two of him at once. He declares that he will take Hisoka's other arm next and asks if he will remain stubbornly confident. With a grin on his face and his aura swelling around him, Hisoka begins to chew part of his dismembered arm and guesses that he's more prepared for the challenge, causing Kastro to smile anxiously in reply.

Chapter 54 Cause of Defeat (, "Haiin") is the 54th chapter of the Hunter × Hunter manga, written and illustrated by Yoshihiro Togashi. Synopsis. As Hisoka chews off a piece of his severed arm and guesses that he feels more prepared for the challenge, the crowd is left disturbed by Hisoka's action. With Kastro standing ready to fight, Hisoka suddenly reveals a handkerchief and covers his severed arm with it, confidently saying that he will foresee the future. Once he removes the cloth, the arm disappears and several playing cards fly into the air before falling to the ground. Hisoka tells Kastro to choose a number from the cards, add four to that number, double the result, subtract six, divide by two, and subtract the original number. With the crowd left confused by the instructions, Hisoka explains that he already knew Kastro's answer, suddenly putting his hand deep into his open wound and pulling out the ace of spades. The announcer is petrified and points out that it doesn't gain him any points in the match, with Killua left wondering how he can be so relaxed. Hisoka tosses the card over to him, but Kastro simply knocks it aside and vows to sever Hisoka's other arm. As one of the Kastros suddenly lunges forward, Hisoka again holds out his arm and tells him that it's his to take. Kastro hesitates for a moment before quickly using his Tiger Bite Fist to remove Hisoka's other forearm, causing the announcer to wonder what Hisoka is thinking. Kastro is then stunned when his double suddenly vanishes. Hisoka confirms that Kastro used his double to attack and adds that he was planning to counterattack his real self with his right arm, suddenly revealing that it's reattached. With the announcer and spectators left stunned, Hisoka chuckles and says that it involves magic as well. Kastro assures himself that Hisoka has to be using Nen, wondering what kind of ability he has. As Hisoka begins to slowly walk forward, Kastro moves to a defensive stance, causing Hisoka to chuckle and ask if he's scared. Hisoka explains that he now knows how to respond after learning Kastro's trick, adding that he only kept Kastro alive because he had considerable talent. After Hisoka predicts that he will dance himself to death, Kastro angrily tells him to shut up before leaping forward along with his double. However, Hisoka easily spots the real Kastro and leaves him dumbfounded. Calmly evading the double's barrage of strikes, Hisoka explains that his double always stays clean because it's created from the image in his mind, which keeps him from recreating the stains that occur during combat. Hisoka continues to evade the double and uses aura around his eyes as he looks at the real Kastro, who suddenly charges forward and prepares to use his Tiger Bite Fist. However, Hisoka's severed left arm suddenly flies toward Kastro and strikes him in the face, leaving him stunned. Hisoka tells him not to try recovering quickly since the punch hit him directly on the jaw, adding that he won't be able to avoid these either. Kastro suddenly sees several playing cards flying toward him and wonders how Hisoka is doing it, telling himself that he needs to produce his double to block the cards. However, as Kastro is unable to do so, Hisoka explains that creating a Nen double requires considerable focus and that he can only achieve it in his normal state. Two cards pierce each of Kastro's arms before several more fly into his chest and legs. Hisoka explains that it's nearly impossible to use any other abilities after creating and moving something as complex as a human Nen double. Confidently walking away from Kastro's falling corpse, Hisoka calls it memory overload and tells him that the reason for his defeat was wasting his memory capacity.

Chapter 55 As for Hisoka... (ヒソカは⋯, "Hisoka wa...") is the 55th chapter of the Hunter × Hunter manga, written and illustrated by Yoshihiro Togashi. Synopsis. After Hisoka defeats Kastro, he begins to leave the loud arena and sees a woman waiting for him. She congratulates him and then tells him to show his arms to her. Back in Hisoka's room, the woman tells an armless Hisoka that the match proved to her that he's an idiot. She wonders why he put on the performance, but quickly says that it means more money for her, removing a needle from the pin cushion on her hand and using her aura to create a thread. She examines Hisoka's left arm and tells him to shut off the aura around it. She stops the bleeding and then uses her Nen Stitches to quickly sew together all the tissue, pulling it tight and reattaching the severed limb. Hisoka moves his arm around and calls her brilliant. She then moves on to his right arm and asks him to hold it while she repeats the procedure. Hisoka tells her that it's always fun to watch and playfully adds that he seems to get injured on purpose so that he can see her work up close. The woman immediately asks for 20 million for his left arm, and 50 million for his right, telling him that he can use his Bungee Gum and Texture Surprise to cover up the ragged edges. Realizing that she's right and that it will make it seem like magic, Hisoka pulls out a handkerchief and attaches it to his arm with Bungee Gum before using Texture Surprise to reproduce the texture of skin. The woman is left impressed by his speed and tells herself that most people would think that his arm healed itself. It's then stated that Hisoka's two abilities led him to victory, both of which are described in detail: with the name taken from his favorite brand of chewing gum as a kid, Bungee Gum allows Hisoka to make his aura both elastic and sticky so that he can attach it to anything and pull it off at will. Taking its name from a popular snack with funny stickers, Texture Surprise involves Hisoka adding imagery to his aura to reproduce the appearance of numerous surfaces (only possible on flat, paper-like materials). The result is compared to a photocopy, and although anyone would be able to tell that it's the wrong texture if they touched it, Hisoka finds that it makes his deception even more exciting. Hisoka's fight against Kastro is then explained: when Hisoka removed the handkerchief, he tossed up the 13 cards as a distraction so that he could also toss up his right arm, using Bungee Gum to hold it to the ceiling and the handkerchief on the ground. The strands of aura attached to both of these were connected to his right stump, and the cards were secured to the ground as well with the strands of aura attached to Hisoka's left hand. When Hisoka tossed the ace of spades toward Kastro, he simultaneously threw the 13 strands and stuck them to Kastro's body. Kastro was unable to notice this because Hisoka had used a variation of Zetsu to make his aura as invisible as it could be. It's possible for anyone who has learned Ren to focus their aura in their eyes, but Hisoka distracted Kastro with his magic tricks and masked his lack of aura with his calm indifference. After attaching the aura from his left fist onto Kastro's chin when he held it out to be severed and applying Texture Surprise to the bottom of the handkerchief, Hisoka retracted the Bungee Gum on the handkerchief and his right arm, making it seem as if his right arm had been magically healed while Kastro removed his left. Kastro then realized that Hisoka had to have used Nen to accomplish the feat, and it's stated that Texture Surprise was not essential to Hisoka's victory. Hisoka noticed the change in Kastro's attitude and deliberately distressed him with his words, eventually causing Kastro to become desperate after his *doppelganger's weaknesses were revealed. With Kastro defeated, Hisoka remained confident that his abilities were most suited to himself and that unlike Kastro's, he could reveal their secrets without reducing their effectiveness. The woman tells Hisoka that she's leaving since her job is finished, reminding him not to use his arms too much until they're healed. She then remembers that their orders have changed and that everyone is now required to meet in Yorknew City by noon on August 30th. Hisoka asks if Chrollo will be there, and the woman assumes so since it could be their biggest mission yet, warning him that Chrollo may punish him personally if he doesn't show. Hisoka pretends to be afraid and asks if she will have dinner with him, but the woman quickly leaves the room without answering. As Hisoka takes a shower and a #4 spider tattoo is revealed on his back, it's stated that Hisoka never talks about his past since he isn't interested in what has happened and that he will probably forget Kastro's appearance the very next day. As it's added that he doesn't belong to anything or anyone, Hisoka dries himself off and sees the tattoo in the mirror, saying that he forgot to remove it again. After he peels off the fake tattoo made possible by Texture Surprise, he thinks of Gon and Killua and says that it's time for him to hunt down the Spiders now that he has found new toys. It's then stated that Hisoka is his own man and confidently believes that he is the most powerful.

Chapter 56 Training Resumes (, "Shūgyō Saikai") is the 56th chapter of the Hunter × Hunter manga, written and illustrated by Yoshihiro Togashi. Synopsis. At Wing's hotel room, Wing tells Gon and Killua that they will now be studying with Zushi, also glad to see that Gon kept his promise for two months. Holding up his hand, Gon tells him that his string acted as a great reminder and allowed him to calm himself. Wing smiles and replies that he imbued it with Nen so that it would have that effect, quickly revealing that he was only joking. Killua then asks how Wing knows that Gon didn't cheat, and Wing replies that the thread hasn't been broken, asking Gon to show his Ten. As Killua wonders if he could have cheated without being caught, Gon is unsure if he can still do it but calms himself and performs the technique. Asked by Wing what he thinks, Zushi describes Gon's aura as smooth and calm yet powerful. With Gon relieved that he didn't forget, Wing compares it to riding a bicycle and adds that he must practice diligently to master it. Gon points out that he was able to do it more easily than before without practicing, but Wing explains that he was able to do so because he practiced "Ten" every day. He then tells Gon to look at his left hand, and Gon is stunned to see that the thread around his pinky is broken, with a surprised Killua adding that Gon couldn't even remove it in the bath. Wing says that he tied the thread so it would break if Gon used Nen, explaining it as a trick of his own Nen. Killua then asks Wing if he watched Hisoka's match against Kastro. Wing confirms that he did, and Killua asks about Hisoka's ability, wondering if they could also make their arm fly around and reattach itself. Wing replies that they should be methodical about it since it's a difficult question. He then asks Gon if he has seen the match footage yet, but Gon replies that he wanted to get his permission first. After Wing starts the tape and it reaches the point where Hisoka tosses his playing cards into the air, Gon and Killua are unable to see the strands of aura coming from Hisoka's left arm. Wing explains that Hisoka used an advanced application of Zetsu called In to make his aura very difficult to see. He adds that the technique makes even powerful aura invisible and that the best way to see it is to focus the aura in one's eyes by using Ren. He then tells Gon that while what he did in his match against Gido may work, he will get himself killed since he can't counterattack. Wing tells Gon and Killua that they can discover Hisoka's ability for themselves once they practice Ren enough to be able to see Hisoka's In. Zushi wonders what he should do, and Wing points out that he should already be able to see it, leaving Zushi surprised. Wing tells him to show his Ren, and Zushi calms himself before using the technique. Gon notes that it's the same size as theirs yet teeming with power. Wing tells him to focus all of it in his eyes, and Zushi strains himself to do so, eventually using the technique called Gyo. He confirms to Wing that he can see Hisoka's aura, specifically 13 strands. After Wing tells him that he's close, Zushi releases the technique and catches his breath. After praising the thankful Zushi, Wing assures him that he will be able to fight and use Gyo simultaneously with enough practice. He emphasizes how important Gyo is at determining an opponent's abilities, stressing to Gon and Killua that they need to learn Ren first and then use it to perform Gyo. He then moves on to Killua's second question about whether they can do the same thing as Hisoka, explaining that as long as it's a Nen ability, a student of Nen should be able to learn it. However, he clarifies that the possibility isn't zero and stresses that a person's individuality heavily influences their Nen. He explains that it could take him 10 years to learn what Hisoka did in five, adding that he could possibly never learn it at all. He tells the three boys that instead of imitating others, they should strive to reach their true potential and consider their own emotions and experiences, which will all be used to develop their Nen. He reminds them that they are still maturing and tells them to train both their bodies and minds, finally adding that they should enjoy their lives as much as they can. After all three energetically agree, Wing asks Gon how much time he has left before he needs to fight again. The two eventually work out that he has 28 days left, and Killua adds that he has 27 days. Wing says that they will register on the last possible day, with Killua to fight on June 9th and Gon on June 10th, and tells them to master Gyo by then. After the three boys head back to Heavens Arena, Killua comments on how much Zushi has improved, but Zushi remains modest and points out that he still hasn't passed the 90th floor. The three decide to review what they learned in Killua's room, but as they make their way by elevator to the 200th floor, each of them senses that people are waiting for them. Once the door opens and they see the same three fighters from before, Killua becomes annoyed at their persistence. One of the fighters simply tells them that they want to know when they plan to fight. Gon whispers to Zushi that the three are also fighters on the 200th floor, and Zushi wonders if Gon fought the one in the middle, with Killua adding that they only fight new fighters to gain easy wins. The fighter says that they are almost out of time and becoming desperate, agreeing to show them his ability as his aura swells around him. Gon reveals that he plans to register for June 10th, and the fighter is disappointed since his deadline is May 29th. Becoming even more annoyed, Killua tells Gon and Zushi that it's time to leave. The fighter gets Gon's attention and assures him that the two of them will fight. As the three boys turn to leave, the fighter watches Zushi and plans to keep his promise.

Chapter 57 Promise (, "Yakusoku") is the 57th chapter of the Hunter × Hunter manga, written and illustrated by Yoshihiro Togashi. Synopsis. In Killua's room at Heavens Arena, Zushi helps him and Gon with their Ren training, telling them to visualize the built-up energy and project it outward. However, the two easily perform the technique before Zushi can even finish the explanation. Gon says that they are getting the hang of it, and Killua adds that they still need to work a little on their timing for Ten to contain all the aura. Zushi is left stunned by their quick progress, saying to himself that it took him weeks to learn the timing. Gon points out that their aura is still weaker than Zushi's, and Killua suggests practicing more to increase it. Zushi quickly tells them that they have trained enough for the day and need to rest their bodies. Killua replies that he isn't too tired, but Zushi asks Killua to trust him, saying to himself that he would feel inept if they surpassed him in only half a day. Gon and Zushi say good night to Killua, who plans to see the two tomorrow and seems to be waiting for something. As Zushi makes his way back to his hotel, Sadaso suddenly appears behind him and traps him in a giant left hand made of aura, preventing him from speaking or breathing. After the unconscious Zushi falls into Riehlvelt's lap, Killua confronts the two and says that they only need to pick a day if they want to fight him, promising to give all of them a free win. He explains that Gon would feel too guilty to keep training if he broke another promise to their teacher, which he wouldn't want to happen. He tells them to work around Gon's schedule if they want to fight him since he would be more than happy to do so. Sadaso chuckles and agrees to the arrangement, with Riehlvelt explaining that they will go register now before they return Zushi unharmed. Back on the 200th floor of Heavens Arena, Killua registers for May 29th, and the two fighters return Zushi to him. Killua carries the unconscious Zushi on his back and tells them that it's the last time, stopping himself before he says what will happen to them if they don't hold up their end of the deal. As Killua stresses that they should keep their promise, Gido is seen hiding behind a nearby corner as he calls Gon and tells him to look outside his door, ordering him not to tell anyone and adding that his friend will be returned safely if he does as they say. On his way to Zushi's hotel, Killua says that it's difficult to make an honest living and to get things done without killing. Outside his room at Heavens Arena, Gon finds one of Zushi's shoes and becomes worried. The next day, Killua finds that Gon has already left his room before he heads to Wing and Zushi's hotel. In the crowded street, he hears a man selling tickets for a match between Gon and Sadaso, asking if he can buy one and wondering what Sadaso is like. The man explains that he's a one-armed fighter with a mask-like face who quickly wins once he seizes his opponent with his invisible left hand. As he adds that Sadaso is called the newbie hunter, the man recognizes the change in Killua's expression as he turns to leave. Another man asks what's going on, and the man recognizes him as Killua, pointing out that he also fights on the 200th floor. The second man realizes that Killua fights Sadaso before Gon does, adding that he's too young to stand a chance. However, the first man disagrees and bets 50,000 that Killua will win. After Killua arrives at Wing's hotel room, Wing thanks him for carrying Zushi back home. Killua asks him how he feels, and Zushi replies that he's feeling better, guessing that he must have really been tired. Gon asks if he found Zushi, and Killua lies by saying that someone called him and said his friend was sleeping by the arena’s front gate. Killua then asks Wing if he can see the video of Hisoka's match again, revealing that he has already learned Gyo and leaving both Wing and Zushi stunned. Using Ren and then Gyo while watching the match footage, Killua says that Hisoka used 15 strands of aura (13 to the cards, one to the handkerchief, and one to the arm he tossed up). Killua analyzes more of the footage with Gyo and describes Hisoka's aura as stretchy, also guessing that it may work like a magnet since his arm reattached itself and struck Kastro's jaw. He decides to go with the former observation and adds that Hisoka's aura must be similar to sticky rubber, which would explain most of his tricks. As Killua releases his Ren and catches his breath, a stunned Zushi realizes that Killua is much more skilled than he is. Impressed by his analysis, Wing tells Killua that he has passed and that he didn't expect both of them to learn Gyo in only one night. Killua turns to Gon, who confirms that he learned it as well but couldn't figure out Hisoka's ability. Wing then asks Killua if he also finished the assignment early so he could fight as soon as possible, with Gon assuring Killua that he just wanted to fight rather than get a head start on him. As Killua smiles and realizes that they both had the same idea, he tells Wing that he wants to fight on May 29th, lying that it's his birthday. With Gon left surprised by Killua’s mention of the date, Wing gives them permission to fight and says that he underestimated how quickly they would progress, telling them to practice Ten and Ren while also getting enough rest. As the two leave the hotel, Gon asks Killua if the fighters blackmailed him as well, saying that it makes him really angry. Killua confirms that they did, but points out that Wing gave them permission to fight and Zushi was returned unharmed. Although Gon doesn't mind giving up a win, he worries about Zushi being threatened again, but Killua assures him that it won't happen. With ten minutes left before the start of his match, Sadaso waits in the locker room and looks at himself in a mirror, saying that Killua and Gon will be his sixth and seventh wins, respectively. He excitedly reminds himself that he only needs three more wins to become a Floor Master. However, as Sadaso thinks about the money and fame he will gain, a knife suddenly seems to split his head in two as Killua appears behind him with a knife at the ready and warns him that he will die if he moves, uses Nen, or even speaks. Killua orders him to close his eyes and asks him if he sees what happens when he breaks his promises, telling him to open his eyes and look at him in the mirror. As Sadaso nervously sweats and breathes heavily, Killua makes it clear that he will never show his face to them again. It's then announced that Killua has won the match by default.

Chapter 58 Rematch (, "Saisen") is the 58th chapter of the Hunter × Hunter manga, written and illustrated by Yoshihiro Togashi. Synopsis. Gon is shown to have one loss (to Gido) and one win (by default to Sadaso), and Killua one win by default to Sadaso and zero losses. Sadaso calls Riehlvelt by phone and tells him about the incident with Killua, saying that it was a mistake to assume that they were only kids. He reveals that he's leaving since he doesn't want to die, telling them to be careful since they will be next. Sadaso hangs up before Riehlvelt can respond, and Gido asks what happened. Riehlvelt replies that he doesn't care and points out how close they are to becoming Floor Masters, saying that they can leave Heavens Arena then and live off the money they make from lecture and teaching jobs. As Riehlvelt guesses that Killua didn't threaten him because he was unsure about his abilities, Killua suddenly appears inside the room and tells them that their abilities are irrelevant since he planned to warn them eventually. He adds that they will never be safe, not even while sleeping or using the bathroom, and reminds them to play by the rules before calmly leaving. Riehlvelt chuckles and says that they should do what he says since cheating is wrong, with Gido quickly agreeing. At Wing's hotel room, Gon, Killua, and Zushi continue their Ren training as Wing instructs them. He then points out that both Gon and Killua have matches that day, asking how they feel. Gon is ready to go, and Wing says that he shouldn't need any advice since he has fought Gido before, asking if he has a strategy planned. Gon replies that he plans to use his fishing rod, leaving Zushi surprised as Wing smiles. Inside the arena, the announcer introduces both fighters for their rematch and reminds the crowd that Gido sent Gon to the hospital the last time they fought. She also draws their attention to Gon's fishing rod and wonders how he will use it. The referee explains that points or a knockout will decide the winner with no time limit, and once he begins the match, Gon quickly dashes forward, but Gido immediately uses his Tornado Top to stop Gon in his tracks. Gido chuckles to himself and adds that since it's nearly impossible to stop his spinning, everyone tries attacking him first. Gido asks Gon what's wrong and says that he will take the lead, suddenly using his Shotgun Blues to send out several spinning tops and leaving Gon surprised that he can use both abilities at the same time. Gido confidently tells Gon that he won't be able to dodge all the tops since unlike Battle Waltz, Shotgun Blues sends them directly at a target. However, Gon suddenly appears furious and uses his Ren to block all the tops, leaving the crowd stunned. Gido nervously realizes that Gon's Nen defenses have improved and that his tops won't be able to injure him. Watching among the crowd, Killua says that while Gon could have used his fishing rod to deflect the tops, he blocked them all head-on to rattle Gido's nerves. After Killua adds that Gon must be really upset that they used Zushi to blackmail them, Gon readies his fishing rod and prepares to counterattack. Continuing to spin, Gido realizes that Gon will most likely try to attach the hook to his clothes in order to stop his spinning. As Gido chuckles and wonders if it will work, Gon swings his fishing rod toward Gido, but the hook simply bounces off him and does no damage. Gido confidently tells Gon that he can't hook onto him when he's spinning so quickly and protected by aura. However, Gon says that it's no problem as he swings the hook past Gido, catching one of the stone tiles below him and lifting it into the air. Gido is sent flying and falls hard to the floor as he attempts to recover, but Gon stands right in front of them and appears to punch him hard in the midsection before he can surrender. However, it's revealed that Gon punched Gido’s steel leg and broke it in two, making it impossible for him to continue the fight. Gido breathes heavily while lying on the floor, and Gon tells him that they won't hold back either if his group will resort to any means, warning him that it will be his face that's broken if he even touches Zushi again. As Wing and Zushi cheer in the stands and a smiling Hisoka watches on a television screen, Killua prepares to fight in the main event against Riehlvelt.

Chapter 59 Making the Grade (, "Kyūdai") is the 59th chapter of the Hunter × Hunter manga, written and illustrated by Yoshihiro Togashi. Synopsis. The announcer introduces the main event of Killua versus Riehlvelt, excitedly wondering what sort of fight it will be. Killua tells Riehlvelt that because he broke his promise first, he won't be getting any more free wins. Riehlvelt tells himself that it doesn't matter if Killua is a professional assassin, calmly reminding himself that Heavens Arena is his domain where he will be victorious. Once the referee explains that the winner will be decided by points or knockout and begins the match, Killua immediately leaps into the air and leaves Riehlvelt wondering where he went. Riehlvelt senses that Killua is right behind him and uses his Aura Burst ability to escape in his wheelchair, barely evading Killua's strike. As the announcer excitedly comments on Riehlvelt's close escape, Killua tells himself that he missed because he jumped too high. Riehlvelt then pulls out two whips called the Two-Headed Snake-Twin Serpents and swings them all around himself in his Song of Defense. The announcer notes that the whips protect Riehlvelt as he moves closer to his opponent. Riehlvelt confidently tells Killua that another sneak attack won't work given the speed of his whips and the size of the platform. Standing his ground, Killua suddenly grabs hold of both whips and says that it looked like they were barely moving. Left speechless initially, Riehlvelt then uses Thunder Serpent as he flips the switches on the whips and sends electricity through Killua's body. He laughs maniacally and tells Killua that he is the first person to catch his whips, adding that the electricity has always dispatched any fighters who have tried to stop them. However, before Riehlvelt can finish his speech, Killua pulls hard on both whips and sends Riehlvelt flying out of his wheelchair, telling him that while electricity still hurts him, it won't incapacitate him since he has been trained to endure torture. Riehlvelt begins to fall back down and begs to be caught, and Killua happily obliges as he holds out both his hands still holding the whips and covered in electricity. Once Riehlvelt falls into Killua's arms, he passes out from the shock and the referee declares Killua the winner by knockout. Outside the arena, Gon congratulates Killua, who reminds him that he's fighting on the 10th. Gon wishes that he could have done what Killua did, and Killua stresses that even he would have fainted if he had touched the whips. Killua asks him what he will do, and Gon assures him that he has a plan, with Killua realizing that Gon watched the match in order to develop his own strategy. On June 10th, it's stated that Gido forfeited to Killua, who is seen watching among the crowd as Gon's match against Riehlvelt prepares to start. The announcer introduces the fighters and reveals that with five wins and three losses, Riehlvelt cannot afford another loss. She also notes that Riehlvelt already has his whips drawn while Gon is without his fishing rod. Once the referee begins the match, Riehlvelt immediately starts his Song of Defense to prevent Gon from attacking him, but Gon squats down and rips up one of the stone tiles, throwing it toward a terrified Riehlvelt who uses his Aura Burst to escape the attack. As Killua realizes what Gon is doing, Gon suddenly jumps in front of Riehlvelt and leaves him startled. Also watching among the crowd, Hisoka notes that Riehlvelt couldn't change directions that quickly and had to move forward, also forced to stop his whips since he lost his balance after accelerating. As Hisoka adds that it's the perfect opportunity to make a move, Gon does just that and restrains both of Riehlvelt's wrists, forcing him to drop his whips. He then picks them up and wraps the ends around Riehlvelt's neck, pretending to turn the electricity to maximum and causing Riehlvelt to pass out from fear. After the referee declares Gon the winner and he enjoys the crowd's cheering, Hisoka meets him outside the ring and congratulates him on his victory, keeping his promise as he offers to fight Gon whenever he wants. Gon appears both nervous and serious as he watches Hisoka leave the arena.

Chapter 6 The First Phase Begins: Part 2 (1②, "Dai Ichi-ji Shiken Kaishi (Ni)") is the 6th chapter of the Hunter × Hunter manga, written and illustrated by Yoshihiro Togashi. Synopsis. Tonpa falls to his knees and apologizes for the spoiled juice, but Gon says that it's lucky that he tasted it first since his time in the forest has trained him to taste anything strange. Still appearing apologetic, Tonpa is internally upset that his opening plan didn't work, as he points out that other rookies have avoided his tricks. He then thinks back to his encounter with Hanzo (#294), who immediately revealed that he's a and wants a Hunter License so he can find the "Hermit's Scroll". As Hanzo continued happily talking, Tonpa thought he had an easy target. However, when Tonpa offered him a can of juice, Hanzo quickly became serious and refused, stating that "shinobi" never eat or drink anything offered to them. Tonpa then thinks about his interaction with Nicholas (#187), who used his laptop to discover that it's Tonpa's 35th attempt at the Hunter Exam and that he holds the record for most consecutive tries at 30. Nicholas was also aware of his "Rookie Crusher" title and politely declined his juice offer. Tonpa then explains that examinee #301 was so strange that he decided not to approach him. He recalls that only one of the examinees drank his juice: a young boy named Killua (#99). He guesses that he's around the same age as Gon and chuckles as he tells himself that the laxative should take effect soon. However, Killua spots Tonpa and happily asks for another can of juice since the nerves are making him thirsty. As Killua quickly empties four more cans, Tonpa wonders how he isn't dying of dehydration. Killua then reveals that he has built up his resistance so no poison will kill him. Tonpa is left in disbelief and wonders if the boy is resistant to everything. He worries about the current rookies again, but then happily realizes that they will make the exam more fun than usual. A strange object suddenly emits a loud noise and gets the examinees' attention. A man standing on an elevated pipe clicks the object shut and states that registration has been closed, announcing that the Hunter Exam will begin. He jumps down from the pipe and directs them through the tunnel, slowly leading the way and stressing how rigorous the exam is. He adds that some examinees will even resort to sabotage. When he sees that everyone is still with him, he says that all 404 of them may enter the First Phase. Leorio notes that everyone continued besides the armless man, hoping that a few would return after the man's explanation. The examiner suddenly quickens his pace and causes the examinees to begin running. Leorio wonders why everyone is in such a hurry, and both Kurapika and Gon explain it to him. The man then introduces himself as Satotz, the examiner for the First Phase and their guide to the Second Phase. With the examinees left confused, Hanzo speaks up and wonders about the first phase. Satotz reminds him that he said the exam had started and noted that the first phase simply requires them to keep up with him. He refuses to say where they're going and how long it will take, but repeats that they just need to keep following him. While Gon thinks it's strange, Leorio is glad that it's a simple endurance test and confidently says he can keep up with anyone. However, Kurapika says to himself that since they don't know how long they will have to follow the examiner, the test also has a psychological element that will test their mental fortitude. Killua suddenly rides past the trio on his skateboard, and Leorio angrily calls him out for cheating since it's a test of endurance. Gon points out that the examiner said they only had to follow him. As Leorio becomes even angrier, Kurapika tells him to stop wasting energy and annoying him, pointing out that they were allowed to bring anything they wanted to the exam. Gon catches up to Killua, who asks how old he is. Gon replies that he's almost 12, and Killua says to himself that he is as well, suddenly kicking his skateboard up into the air and catching it before running alongside Gon. The two introduce themselves, and Killua asks for Leorio's name, thinking he's older. Leorio angrily replies that he isn't even 20 years old, leaving both Gon and Killua surprised as Kurapika doesn't want to get involved. As the examinees continue to follow Satotz, Kurapika notes that they have been running for around three hours, guessing that they have covered close to 40 kilometers. He looks back and believes that some must have given up by that point, but wonders how long they can all keep running. At the back of the group, Leorio struggles to keep up as his breathing increases and he points out that no one has dropped out after four or five hours. Gon falls back and asks how he's doing, with Leorio giving a quick thumbs-up as he focuses on his breathing. Leorio tells himself that he didn't expect the first phase to be so difficult, but then corrects himself by saying that he didn’t expect the other examinees to be so resilient. Realizing how outclassed he is, he begins to slow down and points out that an ordinary person like him had no chance. After seeing that he stopped, gon yells out Leorio's name, but Killua tells him that he's failed and that they should keep moving. Catching his breath with his hands on his knees, Leorio suddenly yells out that he came there to become a Hunter as he sprints past Gon and Kurapika. Now smiling, Gon sees that Leorio left his briefcase behind and uses his fishing rod to retrieve it quickly. Killua is impressed and says he has to try it, with Gon replying that he wants to try out his skateboard. As the four examinees continue to run, it's stated that there have been zero dropouts after 60 kilometers.

Chapter 60 Passing the Exam (, "Gōkaku") is the 60th chapter of the Hunter × Hunter manga, written and illustrated by Yoshihiro Togashi. Synopsis. At Wing's hotel room, Wing tells Gon, Killua, and Zushi that they will begin studying Hatsu, mentioning that once they have mastered the basics, they will need to improve on these and then find their own Nen. He begins by explaining that Hatsu is one's personal expression of Nen and greater than the sum of everything they have learned. He reveals that a Nen user belongs to one of six categories: Emission, Enhancement, Transmutation, Manipulation, Conjuration, or Specialization. He stresses that it's important for them to find an ability that suits them and repeats that Nen abilities are extremely personal to the user. Adding that they are shaped by nature and nurture, Wing addresses Gon and says that he was born with flexible muscles before developing his senses in the forests. He connects it back to Nen by saying that each person's aura has an affinity to one of the six categories, emphasizing that it will be difficult if they pick the wrong ability for their aura. Wing then illustrates the compatibility diagram of the six categories on a white board, along with a brief description for each. He explains that someone born as an Enhancer will learn that category the fastest, with Transmutation and Emission abilities being the next easiest since they are on either side of Enhancement. He mentions that Hisoka is a Transmuter who changes his aura into a rubber-like material and that while Gido is an Enhancer who increases rotational forces, he also had to use Manipulation to affect the tops, explaining that it wasn't very effective since the two types aren't very compatible. Wing then moves on to Kastro and highly praises his Tiger Bite Fist ability, guessing that he was born an Enhancer. However, he points out that his ability to create a double required both Conjuration and Manipulation, neither of which is compatible with Enhancement. He adds that while Kastro made it work through extensive effort and talent, he used most of his talent to learn the ability and ultimately made the wrong choice. Killua asks if they can find out to which category they belong, and Wing happily reveals a drinking glass, filling it with water and placing a single leaf in the center. He calls it Water Divination and explains that it's a Shingen-ryu screening tool that’s also used in Hatsu training. He then demonstrates the process by placing his hands around the glass and using Ren, which causes the water to overflow and surprises both Gon and Killua. After Wing explains that a change in the water’s volume means he is an Enhancer, he tells his three students to take the test as they use rock-paper-scissors to determine the order. Gon goes first and learns that he is also an Enhancer after the water trickles over the glass. The leaf moves once Zushi performs the test, and Wing tells him that he is a Manipulator. Killua goes last, but nothing in the glass changes. He worries that he doesn't have the necessary skill, but Wing tells him to taste the water. Killua finds that it's a little sweet, and Gon wonders if it's regular water, but Wing explains that a change in the water’s taste means he is a Transmuter. With his three students now aware of their Nen types, Wing tells them to focus solely on the Water Divination test for the next four weeks until they can cause a greater change.
