All three energetically agree and are then seen working to improve their results. At Heavens Arena, Hisoka receives a phone call from Gon, who tells him that he will register to fight on July 10th. Hisoka gladly agrees and says that he will be looking forward to it. Back at the hotel on the day before the match, Wing asks his three students to show him how much they have improved. Gon goes first again, calming himself before using his Ren and causing cracks to appear in the glass from the increase in water volume. Both Killua and Zushi are left astounded, and Wing praises his effort as the table is left covered in water. Once Killua performs the test, Wing and Gon taste the water, with the latter saying that it's as sweet as honey. Wing is impressed by both their efforts and reveals that each of them will graduate, also revealing to Gon that he has passed the other Hunter Exam. With all three boys left confused, Wing explains that it's necessary to learn Nen in order to be a seasoned Hunter since it's their job to act as a deterrent as they capture poachers and pillagers. However, he reveals that it's too dangerous to include the teaching of Nen as part of the official exam since it can be abused, adding that only those who have passed are tested. After Killua asks about it, Wing confirms that he planned to teach them once they showed interest, revealing that Netero is the grand master of Shingen-ryu and has told him a lot about them. He also tells Killua to retake the exam, assuring him that he is more than qualified to pass now, and Killua replies that he will if he ever feels like it. Gon then asks Wing if he knows how the other new Hunters are doing, and Wing reveals that both Hanzo and Kurapika have already learned Nen. He says that both Hisoka and Illumi already knew it, adding that Leorio will start after he applies to medical school and that Pokkle is apparently having trouble with Ren. After Wing tells Gon that he shouldn't overdo it in his match tomorrow, the two groups part ways in the street outside the hotel. Wing tells Zushi that he will practice for four more weeks, reminding him that he has learned faster than most and that Gon and Killua just have even rarer talent. Although Wing's words don't make Zushi feel better, he assures himself that he will catch up to Gon and Killua some day. As Killua is seen helping Gon with his punching technique, it's stated that the day of Gon and Hisoka's showdown has arrived.

Chapter 61 Showdown (, "Kessen") is the 61st chapter of the Hunter × Hunter manga, written and illustrated by Yoshihiro Togashi. Synopsis. As Gon and Hisoka prepare to enter the arena, the raucous crowd is eager for the match to start. The announcer introduces Gon first as he walks out, pointing out that he doesn't have his fishing rod again and noting his record of three wins and one loss. The crowd then cheers even louder as Hisoka makes his way toward the platform. The announcer states his record of nine wins and three losses, explaining that he will become a Floor Master with a win or be kicked out with a loss. With Hisoka stretching his arms, the announcer reminds the crowd that Hisoka has yet to lose as long as he shows up to fight. Gon and Hisoka stand opposite on the stone platform and stare down one another as their aura billows around them. Gon gives a determined smirk, and Hisoka internally tells Gon not to look at him like that, becoming excited by the expression. Watching among the crowd, Wing describes Hisoka's aura as ominous and again hopes that Gon doesn't overdo it. With Killua seen watching as well, the referee states that the winner will be decided by points or knockout and that there is no time limit. As soon as the match starts, Gon immediately darts forward and throws a hard right punch, but Hisoka easily dodges it and follows up with an elbow strike. Gon quickly ducks below it before unleashing a flurry of punches, all of which Hisoka evades. Gon barely dodges a palm strike from Hisoka, who follows it up with a kick that makes contact. Gon recovers from the kick by doing a handstand and then landing on his feet, immediately running behind Hisoka and throwing another punch. Hisoka easily dodges it and throws a right uppercut, which Gon ducks below before throwing yet another punch. Hisoka again dodges the attack and then strikes Gon hard in his right side with a palm strike. The announcer and crowd all gasp, but Gon remains on his feet and quickly leaps toward Hisoka with another flurry of punches. Although Hisoka dodges them all and elbows him in the face, Gon endures the strike and throws a solid kick toward Hisoka's head. However, Hisoka blocks it with his left shoulder and prepares to unleash a strong right punch, causing Gon to escape in midair as he lands several feet away. With no hesitation, Gon leaps toward Hisoka yet again and unleashes another flurry of strikes. Hisoka parries them all and appears to land a hard strike on Gon, but it's revealed that Gon blocked it with his left arm. Gon moves in closer yet again and struggles to dodge all of Hisoka's strikes. Hisoka then appears to throw a left punch, stopping before he makes contact and suddenly striking Gon hard in the face with a right punch. Gon is sent back but remains on his feet, with Hisoka taunting him to try again. After the referee declares a clean hit and gives one point to Hisoka, the crowd cheers in astonishment and the announcer points out that the fight is so incredible that she couldn't even give any commentary. Hisoka chuckles and asks Gon what's wrong, revealing that he hasn't even moved from the spot where he started. Gon can't believe it and tells himself that he shouldn't try to land every strike, reminding himself to use feints as well. Killua realizes that Hisoka is just having fun since he has considerably more combat experience than Gon. However, he also notes that Hisoka's weakness is his confidence and that Gon should take advantage of Hisoka's refusal to back away. Telling himself that he knows what to do, Gon leaps toward Hisoka and pretends to throw a right punch before using a series of feints and then dashing toward the side. He suddenly rips up one of the stone tiles to conceal himself and kicks it into a shower of debris. Hisoka is forced to block the pieces of rubble and loses track of Gon in the process. Hiding behind one of the falling stone blocks, Gon seizes his chance and strikes Hisoka in the face with a hard right punch.

Chapter 62 Like You Mean It (, "Honki") is the 62nd chapter of the Hunter × Hunter manga, written and illustrated by Yoshihiro Togashi. Synopsis. After Gon punches Hisoka in the face with a strong right and the referee declares a critical hit worth two points, the audience roars with applause, and the announcer notes that Gon now has the lead. As she adds that the strike didn't seem to injure Hisoka very much and wonders whether it should have been counted as a critical hit, a mysterious man suddenly appears beside her and says that scoring varies among the judges, with some prioritizing the amount of damage and others strategy or technique. He explains that the judge recognized Gon's use of the stone tile as a good strategy, and the announcer understands his point, also wondering who he is. As the crowd continues to cheer, Gon is proud that he finally landed a punch on Hisoka, who gives a slight smirk and begins to slowly walk toward him. The announcer notes Hisoka's expression and points out that it's the first time he has moved since the match started. Gon walks forward as well and pulls out Hisoka's #44 badge from the 287th Hunter Exam, holding it out for him to take. Once Hisoka does so, the two stare at each other before quickly moving back. With the announcer left confused, Hisoka asks how much he has learned about Nen, and Gon replies that he knows the basics. Hisoka guesses that he's an Enhancer, and Gon wonders how he knew. Hisoka chuckles in reply and says that he shouldn't admit it, with Gon angrily asking him how he could tell. Hisoka reveals that he uses his own personality analysis based on aura type and says that while it isn't science, it's similar to profiles based on blood type. He explains that Enhancers are simple and purposeful, with both Killua and Wing noting that Hisoka is right. Hisoka then reveals that he is a Transmuter and describes himself as mischievous and deceitful, which Gon and Killua both agree is true. He tells Gon that they could be great friends since opposites attract, but warns him that Transmuters can be capricious when it comes to what they value. Gon readies himself to fight, and Zushi wishes that Hisoka would say something about Manipulators. As his aura swells around him and he tells Gon not to disappoint him, Hisoka suddenly leaps toward Gon with his right fist clenched and strikes him in the face with his left elbow. The crowd is left stunned, and Hisoka quickly runs behind the falling Gon and strikes him in the back before he can even recover, with Killua realizing how fast he is. As Gon is knocked forward and tries his best to recover, Hisoka leaps toward him yet again. Gon then barely evades a strong kick from Hisoka that ends up sending a stone tile flying into the crowd. With everyone left shocked, Hisoka leaps into the air and attempts to land on Gon, who barely dodges his attack again. However, Hisoka uses the momentum to close in on Gon and strike him in the back with his fists held together. After Gon endures the hit and leaps away, the two stand several feet apart and the referee declares a critical hit for Hisoka. The announcer is left in disbelief at the speed of the fight and says that she can barely follow Hisoka's attacks. Gon hesitates and begins to circle Hisoka, who wonders what's wrong and tells him to take the initiative. Sticking out his tongue and replying that he's thinking, Gon realizes how fast Hisoka is and tells himself that while he can follow him with his eyes, his legs can't react quickly enough. Hisoka then holds up his finger and tells Gon that he will have to force him to move. With Gon left confused, Killua yells out for Gon to use Gyo. Once he does so, Gon sees that Hisoka has attached a string of aura to his cheek, and after Hisoka asks him what's about to happen, he pulls Gon toward himself and winds up for a strong punch. With Gon left helpless as the announcer continues to commentate, Hisoka slams Gon down with the strike and reveals that his ability is called Bungee Gum. He explains that he can attach and remove it at will, confidently telling Gon that he is unable to escape.

Chapter 63 Next (これから, "Kore Kara") is the 63rd chapter of the Hunter × Hunter manga, written and illustrated by Yoshihiro Togashi. Synopsis. As the announcer excitedly describes Hisoka's punch and notes that Gon has been knocked down, Hisoka stands over him with his Bungee Gum still attached to his cheek. Gon is left on his hands and knees still reeling from the strike and thinking about Hisoka's ability. After Hisoka tells Gon to stand up, the referee declares a critical hit and knockdown, announcing that the score is now 6-2 in favor of Hisoka. The announcer wonders if Hisoka will remain undefeated, and the spectators desperately tell Gon to stand up, with some shouting that the referee is biased. The referee asks Gon if he can continue, and Gon struggles to his feet as he wobbles in place. Hisoka then gives Gon a quiz and offers him a free punch if he answers correctly, asking when he attached Bungee Gum to his cheek. The three options Hisoka gives are when he struck him with his elbow, when he landed the clean hit, and when he landed the critical hit. Gon thinks about Hisoka's attacks and chooses the third option, when Hisoka hit him with both his hands. Hisoka reveals that it was actually a fourth option, explaining that he attached it when he analyzed Gon's personality. Initially upset that Hisoka was unfair with the quiz, Gon then becomes upset with himself for having not used Gyo. However, Hisoka assures Gon that while he would have seen his aura coming if he had used Gyo for the fourth option, he would have been unable to do anything for the first three since Bungee Gum can also be attached with physical attacks. Gon realizes that it's pointless to see Hisoka's hidden aura if he can't even avoid his strikes. Anxiously watching among the crowd, Killua worries that Hisoka's ability is more dangerous than he thought and that Gon will need to avoid Hisoka touching him at all. Wing also realizes that even blocking won't be effective since Bungee Gum would still stick to the limb used to block. Hisoka tells him that they have talked enough and prepares to fight, but Gon dashes toward him first and tells himself that his only option is to move forward if he can't escape. Hisoka becomes extremely excited at Gon's passion and initiative, with a look of ecstasy appearing on his face as he wishes that he could defeat him right then. Although frightened by the expression, Gon continues to move forward and punches Hisoka in the face. As Gon unleashes a flurry of punches on him, Hisoka reminds himself that he needs to stay patient and wait until his prize has reached its peak, at which point he can tear down the tower of cards. Hisoka then chuckles and uses Bungee Gum' to pull Gon's face into his left fist. With Gon left dazed, Hisoka pulls Gon toward him again and follows it up with a strong right punch to slam him into the floor. However, Gon manages to block the second strike and quickly recovers, confident that he's getting used to being pulled around. Admitting that he's scared, he tells himself not to let the fear take over since it will keep him from fighting anyone. The referee suddenly raises his hand and declares a critical hit for both fighters, with Hisoka also awarded a knockdown to bring the score to 9-4. Gon quickly points out that he stood up right away and even blocked the punch, but the referee simply shakes his head in reply. The crowd begins to angrily voice their disagreement as they throw objects toward the platform, wondering what the referee is thinking and calling him blind. The announcer agrees that the referee seems biased against Gon, who realizes that Hisoka only needs one more point to win the match. Hisoka then chuckles and tells Gon to look to the right (pointing toward Gon's right). As Gon looks in that direction, a piece of rubble comes flying from the opposite direction and strikes Gon in the head. Hisoka quickly apologizes and says that he meant his own right. With Gon knocked down, Hisoka explains that he attached his aura onto the rock while Gon was complaining to the judge, and then simply activated Bungee Gum. The referee declares a clean hit and knockdown, awarding Hisoka two points and announcing that he has won by TKO. Gon is left in disbelief that the match is over, and Hisoka stresses that while he fought well, he still lacks experience. He adds that they could have a good match if they fight ten more times in Heavens Arena. However, he assures Gon that it's their last fight in the tower and that the next time they face each other, it will be a fight to the death with no rules or points. As Hisoka leaves the arena, although Gon realizes how much stronger he is, he tells himself that he can reach him eventually. He confidently states that he will learn more about Nen and develop an ability to rival Hisoka's, clenching his fist in determination. The announcer then states that with Hisoka's tenth win, he is now able to challenge a Floor Master. She also wishes Gon luck in his future fights and says that he fought bravely, ending the coverage from the 200th floor. The referee is interviewed after the match and says that while he felt his judging was fair, he thought it was better to end the match quickly, even if he had to lower the criteria for scoring points. One spectator explains to another that technical judges score points fast to ensure that dangerous matches end sooner. Killua then tells Gon that it's time for them to leave since they met all their goals, suggesting that they head to Gon's home next and adding that he wants to meet Mito. As Gon thinks of her, his great-grandmother, and Kon, he realizes that it's been seven months since he left Whale Island. The two put on their backpacks and look up at the enormous tower, saying goodbye to Heavens Arena.

Chapter 64 Homecoming (, "Kikyō") is the 64th chapter of the Hunter × Hunter manga, written and illustrated by Yoshihiro Togashi. Synopsis. Gon travels back to his home on Whale Island with Killua, surprising Mito as she hangs laundry out to dry. Mito is upset that Gon didn't tell her that he was coming home, saying that she doesn't have anything ready. After reminding him that he hasn't called once since he passed the exam, she orders the two to give her all their laundry and to take a bath. Afterward, Mito's grandmother joins them for a meal, and Mito asks Gon about the exam. He tells her that he was one of only seven people that passed out of 400 who tried, proudly showing his Hunter License and let her handle it. Mito seems unimpressed and tries to break it in half, causing Gon to panic and tell her to give it back. Gon and Killua then head off into the forest, telling Mito that she doesn't need to pack any food since they plan to find some there. Gon tells Killua that it's where he met Kite, and Killua asks about Kon. Gon tells him that they probably won't see him since his partner would get upset if she smelled a human scent on him. He adds that since Kon is the ruler of the forest, hanging out with humans would cause the other animals to respect him less. As the two approach a body of water where Gon says they used to play often, Killua spots multiple fish on the ground and guesses that it's Kon's way of welcoming Gon back. After starting a fire and eating the meal, the two look up at the night sky and Killua asks Gon what he plans to do next. Gon replies that he will spend August on Whale Island, collect information, and then start his search for Ging at Yorknew. After Killua says that he's unsure about his own plans, Gon energetically tells him to stay and then come with him to Yorknew. Killua tells Gon that he's cool for having actual goals, lamenting the fact that he doesn't know what to do with his life. However, he is sure that he doesn't want to take over his family's business, adding that he envies Gon, who tells Killua that he enjoys hanging out with him. Gon explains that the island is an outpost for fishermen who are far away from their homes, with there being few people who live there permanently and the only other kid being a girl named Noko. He adds that he has always been homeschooled and tells Killua that he's his first friend around his own age. Killua says that his situation is the same, though he spent all his time learning how to kill. Gon asks him if he has fun when they're together, and after Killua says that he does, Gon tells him that they should stay together and see the world, which would allow him (Gon) to find his father and give Killua the chance to find what he wants to do with his life. Gon assures him that it will be fun, and Killua agrees to tag along until he finds something to do. Killua suddenly realizes that Gon never mentions his mother, and Gon says that since Mito raised him like her own son, he feels bad asking about his biological mother. He adds that if he hadn't met Kite, he probably wouldn't have tried to learn about Ging, with Killua assuring Gon that he likely would have become a Hunter anyway. Gon says that he was told his parents both died in a car accident, but after learning from Kite that his father was alive, he assumed that his mother was the one who had actually died. He clarifies that Mito will always be his real mother, so he doesn't feel the need to ask about what happened. As Killua says that he wishes he had a mom like Mito and Gon replies that she's awesome, Mito stands a short distance behind them in silence, holding a basket full of food. The next morning, while Killua makes the beds and Gon puts away dishes, Mito approaches Gon and asks him how long he plans to stay. Gon says around a month, and Mito then asks if he plans to look for Ging once he leaves. After Gon excitedly answers yes, Mito leaves the room and returns with a strange box that she sets on the table. She explains to Gon that Ging left it with her and told her to give it to him once he became a Hunter. With Gon taken aback that his father had left something for him, Mito says that she will tell him everything she knows about Ging.

Chapter 65 About Ging (ジンについて, "Jin ni Tsuite") is the 65th chapter of the Hunter × Hunter manga, written and illustrated by Yoshihiro Togashi. Synopsis. Mito begins by telling Gon that Ging is her cousin and that she was always trying to keep up with him, especially since he took the Hunter Exam before he turned 12 (just as Gon did). She remembers when Ging told her that he was leaving to become a Hunter because there was something he wanted. The two had a fight because Ging wouldn't tell her what it was, and he left the island before she could see him again. Mito's grandmother enters the room carrying drinks and says that Ging is the only son of her eldest son and Mito the only daughter of her second son. She then reveals that Mito's parents were the ones who died in an accident. Mito adds that they were on vacation when it happened, and Ging's father was also lost at sea after that. She tells Gon that she doesn't know anything about his mother, saying that Ging returned ten years later carrying a baby in his arms. Mito's grandmother says that Ging asked her if she could take care of his son for a while, and she asked in reply where the boy's mother was, with Ging only answering that they had broken up. However, she says that right as she was about to agree to take care of him, Mito criticized Ging so loudly that everyone on the island could hear her. Mito says that she didn't think Ging was fit to be a parent, and so took custody of Gon, screaming at Ging to never come back. She returns to the box left by Ging, and Mito's grandmother reminds her granddaughter how many times she threw it away. Mito tells Gon that that's all she knows about Ging and that the box is the only thing he left behind. An enthusiastic Gon asks Mito to tell him more, especially about when Ging was a kid. He feels odd calling Ging by his name, but says that it seemed more natural. Mito says that she and Ging were the only kids on the island, but Ging was always wanting to go off on his own. Mito's grandmother adds that Mito would follow Ging into the mountains, and everyone would panic when Ging came back alone. She says that even though everyone would go looking for her, Ging was always the one to find her. Because of her young age at the time, Mito wonders if that's how it was, then telling Gon about the time they went out on a boat. The next day, Gon shows the box to Killua, who wonders how to open it. Even though Gon tells him that he already tried to force it open, Killua tries his hardest to pry it open but to no avail. After he worries about smashing it since they don't know what's inside, he shakes it but doesn't hear anything move around. He realizes that Ging told Mito to give it to Gon only after he became a Hunter, asking Gon what he has now that he didn't have before. Gon proudly pulls out his license, but can't find a slot for it. Killua says that he meant Nen, and after Gon surrounds the box with aura, it suddenly lights up and breaks apart into several pieces, revealing another box that was inside. Killua picks up one of the steel sticks and notices the familiar markings, with Gon also realizing that they are the same as the ones on the thread that Wing wrapped around Gon's finger. Killua wonders how to open the second box, and Gon's initial idea to use his license proves successful as he inserts it into the slot. The two find three items inside: a ring, a cassette tape, and a memory card. They notice that the ring has the same markings inside its band, and Killua advises Gon against putting the ring on for now. They decide to listen to the tape, and as Gon gets a cassette player, Killua tells him to set it to record just in case. After Gon hits play, Ging's voice is heard and he says that Gon must have become a Hunter if he is listening to the tape. He then says that he has one question to ask: does Gon want to see him?

Chapter 66 The Tape (テープ, "Tēpu") is the 66th chapter of the Hunter × Hunter manga, written and illustrated by Yoshihiro Togashi. Synopsis. The recording of Ging tells Gon to keep listening if he wants to see him and to press the stop button if he doesn't. Gon lets the tape play, and Ging again asks Gon if he is sure, saying that Hunters are egotistical and put aside everything else to achieve what they want. He tells his son to stop the tape if he just thinks that it would be nice to see him, giving him a minute to think about it. Killua initially speaks up about what to do next, but then says that he probably doesn't need to ask Gon for his answer. After the minute passes, Ging says that he doesn't want to see him and that he doesn't know how he could face him, admitting that he quit being a parent for selfish reasons. He continues by saying that while ten years have passed since the tape's recording, he will always be the person he is. Elsewhere, Ging is seen riding a large reptilian creature, which itself is riding a larger dragon-like creature. As the latter takes flight, the recording of Ging says that he's probably off on an adventure somewhere, telling Gon to come find him if he still wants to see him. He adds that if he hears Gon coming, he will do his best to elude him, reminding Gon that he is indeed a Hunter now. As Gon smiles with excitement, Killua stops Gon from stopping the tape after he realizes that Ging is still there. Ging's voice returns and says that the last thing is about Gon's mother. He tells his son to keep listening if he wants to know, and before he can tell him to stop the tape if he doesn't, Gon does just that without hesitation. Killua says that Ging may have given some clues, but Gon replies that his gut told him otherwise, also reminding Killua that he considers Mito his mother. Gon goes to leave the room and says that they should get something to eat, but Killua suddenly notices that the tape is rewinding itself. As aura surrounds the stereo, Killua is in disbelief that Nen is involved, realizing that Ging must have imbued it ten years ago so that it started to rewind once the tape was stopped. The tape suddenly begins to record, and Killua says that Ging is trying to erase his own voice. After Gon unplugging the stereo still doesn't work, Killua tries and fails to destroy it with a punch, realizing that the Nen is protecting it. The two play the tape and hear themselves trying to stop it from recording over Ging's message. Killua says that the backup tape was also erased and that Ging wanted to make sure that no one could analyze his voice, especially with a Nen ability. They decide to examine the memory card next, and after Gon doesn't recognize it, Killua tells him that it belongs to a game console called the JoyStation.

Chapter 67 The Flesh Collector's Mansion: Part 1 (の①, "Jintai Shūshūka no Yakata (Ichi)") is the 67th chapter of the Hunter × Hunter manga, written and illustrated by Yoshihiro Togashi. Synopsis. Kurapika arrives at the Nostrade's mansion and says at the gate that the Sengi Guild referred him. After Kurapika reaches the mansion, a butler greets him and leads him inside. As Kurapika waits in a room with several others, he remembers returning to the Sengi Guild and speaking to the agent again. She said that she was surprised he had learned Nen in only six months, easily remembering Kurapika since only one person had found the agency since him. The agent asked him what kind of employer he wanted, and Kurapika replied that it had to be someone with strong connections to the Yorknew auction. She warned him that those types of clients had strict standards and were unlikely to hire people with no experience, but she found three offers involving personal protection that were willing to hire after an interview: a handgun buff, an antiques collector, and a flesh collector. As Kurapika's mind returns to the present, the butler welcomes the group to the contract briefing and directs their attention to a large screen. With two women beside him, a man appears on the screen and says that they won't ask them if they are licensed, only requiring that the applicants can get what they want. He says that the auction is in one month and that each of them needs to bring back one item from the list the butler will give them. The butler hands out the data cards, and Kurapika immediately sees that eyes from the Kurta Clan are on the list, which specifies that they must be scarlet and that a set complete with the head would be preferred. One of the other applicants says that Kurapika looks pale and tells him that all the items are legal to own, adding that they will have to acquire even worse things once they are hired. He starts to talk about one of his clients who wanted a newborn, but Kurapika tells him to be quiet and not to talk to him. The man on screen tells the applicants that once they're hired, they will be in charge of acquisitions and security. After he wishes them good luck, Kurapika tells himself that he will first earn their trust, confident that the man isn't even the actual client. He plans to get as close as he can so that he can learn their secrets, saying that collectors desire both rare items and people to whom they can show off their collection. Finally, he guesses that the various flesh collectors have ties with one another, vowing to arrest every single one of them. The applicants go to leave the room, but find that the door is locked. As the man on screen says that they need to be tough enough to make it out alive, several sword blades pierce the door and force the applicants to retreat back. Several figures shrouded in black hoods burst into the room, with two in the back pulling out handguns and firing toward the group. The applicants hide behind cover, with one of them using the butler as a human shield. Kurapika stands ready and seems to wield something in his right hand.

Chapter 68 The Flesh Collector's Mansion: Part 2 (の②, "Jintai Shūshūka no Yakata (Ni)") is the 68th chapter of the Hunter × Hunter manga, written and illustrated by Yoshihiro Togashi. Synopsis. The shrouded figures keep shooting, but Kurapika reveals chains on his right hand and stops the bullets with his Dowsing Chain on his ring finger. As the other applicants are impressed by his skill, Kurapika dodges the figures' sword strikes and leaps up onto the staircase. After he observes that there are three with guns and six with swords, two figures with swords appear behind him and prepare to strike. Kurapika barely dodges their attacks by jumping onto the large chandelier. Basho mocks the figures' fighting skills and says that he doesn't even need to use Nen, dodging one of their strikes and punching it in the face with a strong uppercut. As the figure is sent flying back and Basho seems to realize something, Kurapika observes everyone's movements and spots the one behind it all. He quickly jumps down and holds a dagger to Tocino's throat, ordering him to call off the figures in three seconds or else. After Tocino agrees to do it, the figures' suits and swords fall to the floor. Basho says that he figured Nen was involved and adds that he could tell when he punched one of them, guessing that they were masses of aura. However, he says that he didn't know it was Tocino behind it all, and Kurapika says that he could tell when he saw that Tocino was the only one not getting attacked. He adds that when he jumped onto the chandelier, two of the figures still continued to swing pointlessly at him, which meant that they must have been given the command to attack the person closest to them. He guesses that Tocino is most likely an Emitter since he was able to control eleven masses of aura, but adds that since the range was likely limited to the room, the one controlling the figures had to be among the group. Tocino smiles and introduces himself, explaining that he is a Hunter and an employee. He asks Kurapika to sheath his dagger and reveals that he was ordered to test the applicants. He admits that he didn't expect to be exposed so quickly and says that the four of them should be able to escape easily enough. Since there are five others in the room, they realize that there's another infiltrator among the group. Kurapika readies his Dowsing Chain and says that while Tocino is probably trying to sow doubt, he will find out whether there are any other infiltrators. He holds out the ball and chain, first putting it in front of Basho, and then in front of Baise (with the chain staying motionless for both of them). However, when Kurapika puts it in front of Squala, the chain sways back and forth and Kurapika is confident that he is the other infiltrator. Squala says that it doesn't mean anything, but Melody mentions that Squala's heart started to pound once he was pointed out, adding that his heart would have gradually beat faster if the accusation had been false. She says that both Tocino and Squala have the typical melody of a liar, and Basho is convinced by the evidence. After Squala protests and says that there may be three infiltrators in total, Kurapika uses his chain to test Melody, who uses her own ability to rule out Kurapika. Squala says that he can't trust either of them and that they are just wasting time by arguing with each other. Basho decides to end the discussion once and for all, pulling out a piece a paper and writing a on it. After reading it aloud and while holding the paper in his hand, he punches a chair and causes it to catch fire. He says that the haiku was a dud and mentions that the kind of poetry is found in his native country. He explains that whatever he composes actually happens, saying that the next one counts and writing out on the paper, "If you are a liar / your painful death will be swift / in a trial by fire." He then asks each of the applicants if they are an infiltrator, with Kurapika, Baise, and Melody all passing. After Tocino quickly admits to being one, Squala finally gives in and says that he has been caught. He introduces himself and says that while he isn't a Hunter, he is a Manipulator who has already given out his orders. The others ask him about the orders, but Squala refuses to tell them since it's a test, assuring them that they won't be able to torture the information out of him. All of a sudden, Baise taps Squala on the shoulder and then kisses him on the lips. This activates her Nen ability, and she explains that she is also a Manipulator, turning anyone she steals a kiss from into a manservant. Squala falls to his knees and begs Baise to step on him more. Baise pulls out a camcorder and orders him to reveal how he used his Nen. With Kurapika and Basho taken aback by the ability, Squala says that he has placed dogs around the mansion, all of which follow his orders. It's then stated that Kurapika, Basho, Baise, and Melody escaped from the mansion.

Chapter 69 Greed Island (グリードアイランド, "Gurīdo Airando") is the 69th chapter of the Hunter × Hunter manga, written and illustrated by Yoshihiro Togashi. Synopsis. Killua tells Gon that he can search for stores on the ToyLand website to order a JoyStation Console. He finds one with a memory card for same-day delivery, and Gon asks how they can find out what game it is since nothing is written on the memory card. Killua realizes that Gon has really never played video games before. The JoyStation arrives, and Killua says that it's still on the market after three generations because of the cult classic games. He shows Gon where to put the disc, but tells him to leave it empty, insert the memory card, and then turn on the console. They see that there is only a single game, but it has used up all 30 slots of memory. Killua says that it might not work, but he decides to make a spare copy. After the screen shows the name of the game, Greed Island, Gon asks Killua if he knows what it is, but Killua replies that he hasn't heard of it. He says now that they know the title of the game, they can search for it on ToyLand. However, after the search brings up no results, Killua guesses that none appeared because they wanted same day delivery. He expands the search to all stores that sell it, but again they find that no one has it in stock, with Killua guessing that it's either sold out or was never on the market. They use a website called "Game Almanac" to search for the game and learn that it was sold through legal channels. The site's information tells them that it's a hunting game exclusively for Hunters which was produced and sold by Marilyn Inc., having been released in 1987. They suddenly notice the outrageous price of 5.8 billion and can't believe it. After seeing that only 100 units were ever sold, Killua calls the company and learns that the game went out of print, with no plans for a re-release, and that its original developer no longer exists. Killua sees that the game isn't even available on any used marketplaces, and Gon realizes that they will need to find someone with a copy. Killua says that they have to post a message on an auction site and wait for someone to reply. He adds that while they have 800 million combined, they will most likely need more than the retail price since sellers usually charge more. Gon decides to make a post anyway, asking for the game and telling any sellers to name their price. They get thousands of hits within seconds, and Killua guesses that they are trying to sell fakes since so much money is involved. He thinks that they will have to abandon the auction site idea, and Gon asks him if there is anyone who knows a lot about games and the Internet. Someone comes to mind for Killua, and he says that the person may even own a copy of the game. He calls Gotoh and asks him to get "piggy" for him. He is confident that the person never leaves the house and has Gotoh tell the person that he will smash his figurines if he doesn't come to the phone in ten seconds. At the Zoldyck estate, an annoyed Milluki answers and says that he's busy, threatening to kill Killua if he touches his figurines. Killua assures his brother that he was kidding, and Gon wonders if Killua is talking to Illumi. Milluki says that he has heard of Greed Island and adds that he didn't expect Killua to be interested in rare video games. He tells Killua that he doesn't own a copy but wants one, saying that it went on sale when he was five years old. He also mentions that there were 20,000 preorders for the 100 copies and says that he was unable to track down any of the buyers. After Killua taunts him about giving up on his search, Milluki assures him that he has some leads now, but says that it isn't worth it given the amount of effort and money it would take. Killua asks his brother if he will exchange his information for a memory card with Greed Island save files, confident that Milluki could reverse engineer the game using the data. Milluki makes sure that Killua's claim is genuine and at first worries about eavesdroppers, but then tells him that it's best to start with the Hunters' Website. He says that while he could hack into the site himself, he's worried about the Net Police and Hacker Hunters tracking him. He tells Killua that he will need a Hunter License to gain access, promising to give him the URL once he gets the memory card. Milluki's second lead involves the Yorknew auction, and he tells his brother that dozens of copies will reportedly be auctioned off. He guesses that someone had been hoarding the copies, and Killua quickly ends the conversation, telling his brother that he will send the memory card using their usual way. Killua apologizes to Gon for promising to give Milluki the memory card, but Gon is fine with the exchange. He goes to use his license on his computer, but Killua quickly warns him that if his IP address got out, people would come to Whale Island looking for the license. He tells Gon that they have to use public computers and reminds him that they still need the URL. He also tells Gon about someone auctioning off numerous copies of the game, and Gon thinks that it could be Ging. Holding the memory card in his hand, Gon realizes that they still need a lot more money to get a copy and wonders what kind of game Greed Island could be if it's worth billions. Sitting in front of multiple computers and monitors, Milluki learns that in 1988, a man named Battera offered 17 billion to buy the game and 50 billion for a memory card with endgame data, but no one came forward. Milluki then smiles and says that he will bring the legend to an end.

Chapter 7 Respective Reasons (それぞれの, "Sorezore no Riyū") is the 7th chapter of the Hunter × Hunter manga, written and illustrated by Yoshihiro Togashi. Synopsis. Gasping for breath and dripping with sweat, Nicholas is left in disbelief at his failure as he desperately reminds himself that he was the best in academics and sports. As Nicholas drops his laptop and it shatters on the ground, the Amori Brothers surround the rookie and mock him incessantly. The three wonder how someone so pathetic made it that far and tell Nicholas to go home to his mother as he finally falls to his hands and knees. It's stated that Nicholas is the first dropout after 80 kilometers. Tonpa hands the brothers several bills and thanks them. The three praise Tonpa's ability to exploit an examinee's weakness, and Tonpa happily replies that he lives for it. He then thinks about the other rookies and reminds himself to stay alert since only one has dropped out so far. As the examinees turn the next corner, they find that the tunnel suddenly becomes elevated with a steep set of stairs. Satotz quickens his pace even more and leaves many examinees struggling to follow him, with Geretta guessing that it will cause the strugglers to drop out. Now shirtless, Leorio gasps for breath and tries his best to keep pace. Kurapika asks how he's doing, and Leorio replies that he found more energy once he stopped caring about his appearance, telling Kurapika to pretend not to know him if he ends up removing all his clothes. Kurapika chuckles and realizes that Leorio has a point, throwing down his tabard and running beside him. He then wants to ask a question, but Leorio tells him not to waste his energy talking. However, Kurapika asks if money is really his goal, guessing that it isn't since those driven only by money never show such tenacity. After Leorio tells him that he doesn't know anything and several examinees are seen to have dropped out, Kurapika reveals that the Kurta Clan were targeted for their Scarlet Eyes, explaining that they are the clan's special trait and become a bright hue of scarlet when their emotions are stirred. He adds that the irises remain so if they died in that state and that it's considered one of the most beautiful colors in the world. Leorio asks if it's why the Phantom Troupe attacked them, and Kurapika painfully replies that the eyes were stolen from all their bodies, confidently stating that he plans to capture the Troupe and recover the eyes of his clan. Leorio points out that they may have already been sold on the black market to wealthy clients who can't be approached by normal people, but Kurapika tells him that a Hunter working for a rich client could obtain the necessary access and information. Leorio then states that everyone hates contracted Hunters since they have no pride or honor, and only take jobs for small rewards. Kurapika calmly replies that his pride is nothing compared to how his brethren suffered. Leorio apologizes for not having such a complicated motive, again stating that he only wants money. Kurapika angrily replies that it isn’t true and reminds Leorio that not everything can be bought with money. Leorio counters by saying that everything has a price, even human lives and dreams. Kurapika can't believe his words, but Leorio states that it's a fact and finally reveals that his friend would be alive if he had been able to pay for his life. Kurapika asks if he was ill, and Leorio explains that a surgery could have saved his life, but that he couldn't afford the ridiculous cost. He reveals that he decided to become a doctor so he could cure a child with the same disease and then tell his parents that they didn't owe him anything. He angrily points out how expensive it is to even try to become a doctor and stresses that he wants money because it's needed for everything. Running behind him, Kurapika is left with a slight smile on his face. It's then stated that 37 examinees have dropped out halfway up the stairs. Gon and Killua are seen at the front of the group right behind Satotz. Killua explains that climbing slowly will tire a person out more quickly, wondering if the rest of the exam will be as tedious and boring. Gon then asks him why he wants to become a Hunter, and Killua reveals that he doesn't, explaining that he's only interested in the exam because he heard it was difficult. He expresses his disappointment with the First Phase and asks Gon the same question. Gon replies that his father is a Hunter and that he wants to be just like him. Killua asks what his father is like, but when Gon honestly replies that he doesn't know, Killua is left surprised at first and then laughs as he calls Gon weird. Gon explains that he has been raised by his aunt since he was a baby and that he has only seen a picture of his father. He then tells Killua that he eventually met a man named Kite, who told him a lot about his father. Kite had recounted many of Ging's accomplishments such as discovering the Lurka Ruins, establishing a breeding program for the Two-headed Wolf, excavating the Congo Gold Vein, and eliminating the Kute Gang of Thieves. He had also mentioned that Ging could be a Triple-Star Hunter if he actually wanted to apply for the rank. It's then explained that Triple-Star is the highest rank among Hunters, with less than ten in the world and strict requirements such as achievements with global ramifications or important historical discoveries. Killua wonders if his father is really that amazing, and Gon stresses that Kite seemed prouder of him than he did of himself, happily explaining that it's why he wants to follow in his father's footsteps. The examinees suddenly spot the exit full of sunlight, and Hanzo is eager to finally get outside, with Kurapika telling Leorio that it's only a few more steps. The examinees catch their breath and take in the view, with many of them wondering where they are. Satotz explains that it's the Milsy Wetlands, also called the "Swindler's Swamp", and that it will be the next section of the First Phase. He then warns them that the environment is filled with devious and hungry creatures that will trick them to catch their next meal. He tells the examinees to follow him and stay alert, stressing that if they are tricked, they are dead.

Chapter 70 To Yorknew (ヨークシンへ, "Yōkushin e") is the 70th chapter of the Hunter × Hunter manga, written and illustrated by Yoshihiro Togashi. Synopsis. After a hawk carrying the Hunters' Website URL from Milluki lands on Killua's arm, he and Gon head to an Internet café where they see the Hunters' Tavern screen after putting in the URL. Gon enters his license number and then swipes his license to gain access. He moves the cursor to the bartender and checks under games, eventually finding Greed Island on the list. The bartender asks for 20 million for the requested information, and after the two pay him, he first tells them that Nen users made the game. The bartender then gives them a plethora of information: the multiple creators (unknown if they are Specialists) infused all 100 copies with Nen, which activates when the game is started. After players are sucked into the game and disappear, the console will stay on if they stay alive and stop if they die. They are able to return to the real world if they find a save point. One of the game's owners gave information as long as his identity was kept hidden, saying that he hired 50 Hunters (three of whom were licensed professionals) to clear the game, but none of them returned. Gon wonders if the information is true, and Killua says that it has to be since it's on the Hunters' Website. As Gon clicks further, the two learn that seven copies have currently been registered for the Yorknew auction, with the minimum bid set at 8.9 billion. Killua can't believe how much higher the price is, but Gon wonders if they can take part by also selling. Killua agrees that they can find their own loot to auction and hopes that they can make enough with their 800 million to afford a copy of the game. The two lastly learn that while the game is considered legendary for the general public, the difficulty of finding one is ranked "H" (easiest) since it has started to show up on public auctions. It's added that the acquisition difficulty is ranked "G" (easy) because of the high cost, with the game not classified as rare because of the current number of professional Hunters (there are enough for one out of six to own a copy). Gon tells himself that acquiring a copy is his only hope of finding Ging. Killua sits down at the computer next to him and says that they should use the Internet flea markets and open auction sites first. The two buy and sell into the night, eventually making their way to a fountain in a crowded plaza. They are left with 10.84 million between themselves and argue over the deals they made, with Killua angrily saying that it took 8 hours to make only 985 and asking how long it will take to make 8 billion. Still at each other's throat, they decide to split the remaining money and see who has more by 9 p.m. on August 31. After agreeing that the loser will do one thing the winner asks, the two run off in opposite directions. At the Nostrade's Mansion, the four applicants return with a requested item: Kurapika with a lock of celebrity hair, Basho with a mummified right arm from an Egypersian tomb, Melody with skin from a patient with dracoderma, and Baise with a unicorn tribesman skull. Dalzollene, the head bodyguard, tells them that they are all hired and says that their first job will be guarding the boss on her way to Yorknew. He adds that they will deliver her safely to her hotel room and specifies that they will make a 35-hour trip by private blimp to Lingon Airport, with a 90-minute drive to the hotel. He finally tells the new recruits that they will be part of the outer formation and asks them if they have any questions. Kurapika bluntly asks if they know who is after the boss, but Dalzollene says that it's a stupid question because there are too many to count given the boss' position in the underside of society. Kurapika then asks if they know of any that might act upon their resentment toward the boss, which would allow them to create better countermeasures. Dalzollene becomes serious and tells him to assume that everyone who approaches the boss is an enemy. He then tells the new recruits that he will introduce them to her, leading them down a grand hallway where they spot a man petrified inside a large picture frame. Dalzollene tells them that it used to be human and a former colleague before he let himself be misled and put the team and the boss in danger. He tells the four recruits that they were hired in his place. After they reach the boss' room, Dalzollene knocks and tells her that he has new hires. She tells them to come in, and they find a young girl sitting on her bed. It's stated that the day of the auction has arrived.

Chapter 71 The Auction Begins!! (オークション！！, "Ōkushon Kaisai!!") is the 71st chapter of the Hunter × Hunter manga, written and illustrated by Yoshihiro Togashi. Synopsis. It's announced that the annual auction in Yorknew City is the biggest in the world, with trillions of Jenny exchanging hands over the course of ten days. It's stated that an item bought for 10,000 could sell for a hundred million the next day. Lastly, it's mentioned that while there are thousands of auction houses, many also deal in illegal goods alone. Gon and Killua make their way to a large, open market and are overwhelmed by the number of people. After someone yells out that they lost a bet, Gon turns to Killua and reminds him that gambling isn't the answer. As Killua tells him to shut up and mocks the amount of money he made, it's revealed that Gon turned his 5.42 million into 5,434,997 while Killua initially turned his share into 286 million but then lost it all. Gon says that he understands negotiation better now and reminds Killua that he now has to do one thing he says. Killua mentions that Leorio should be arriving sometime, and Gon adds that Kurapika arrived yesterday. Killua worries that Kurapika's new job won't leave him enough time, but Gon says that he would call them in that case. As Killua plans to leave his cellphone on, he sternly asks Gon why he still doesn't have one, reminding him that all Hunters should. The two head to a phone vendor, who shows off a best-selling, ultra thin phone with G.P.S. Someone behind them suddenly says that it's not very good since it has terrible range and isn't waterproof. Gon and Killua turn around to see Leorio, who suggests that they buy the Beatle-07. He says that while it may be heavy and costly, it works all over the world, translates 200 languages, and they can watch and record television on it. Killua is very impressed and tells Gon that they should both buy one. Gon comments on Leorio arriving early as well as on his new cologne. They ask the shopkeeper for the price, and he replies with 400,000 for two phones. After haggling to the point that a crowd gathers to watch and applaud, Leorio gets the price down to 110,580 for one. Gon and Killua thank him, but Leorio says that he can do even better, mentioning that he only paid 80,029 for his. Leorio changes the subject and asks if they learned Nen. They reply that they did, and Gon asks him if he plans to learn after applying to school. Leorio, however, smiles and says that he already learned it too. 24 hours before the three met at the market, Neon and her bodyguards exit a large airship. As they travel by car, Dalzollene hands her a set of papers for September. She comments on how many there are, and he replies that two men in particular wanted their fortunes. She reminds him that she warned she would quit if he added any more. He apologizes, but says that they are friends of her father. She calls him on the phone and at first says that she quits, but then says that it's the last time, stressing that she will really quit if he doesn't keep his word. After hanging up, she happily says that he will get the stuff for her, and Dalzollene is glad for her. After saying that she better get it over with, she pulls out a pen and a creature suddenly appears from Neon's aura, guiding her right hand to quickly write on the pieces of paper. Basho tells Kurapika that he heard she's an amazing fortune-teller with notable clients through her father's connection to the Mafia. Kurapika, however, guesses that her father only reached his current status by exploiting Neon's ability. He adds that it must be the reason why he fears so much for her safety. Basho reminds Kurapika of Dalzollene's words about not assuming things and that their only job is to take care of all threats. Neon finishes all the fortunes and tells Dalzollene that she wants to go shopping until the auction starts tomorrow night. Dalzollene replies that they would happy to tag along with her. As the motorcade drives toward the city, they pass a group of four individuals walking in the same direction. Sporting two swords, one of them asks the others how many years have passed since all 13 members were together. The shortest answers that while it's been three years and two months, members No. 4 and 8 are different now. The tallest asks Machi if she is sure that Hisoka is coming to the meeting. Machi shrugs off his question and says that she told him to come. The large man says that it was her job and the short one says that he doesn't like Hisoka, wondering why Chrollo lets him do as he pleases. The man with two swords praises Hisoka's Bungee Gum and says that he's tough to fight. The short man asks if he is implying that Chrollo fears Hisoka, ordering him to apologize. The large man says that he gives Hisoka too much credit, and the other man says that it's easy to talk big. After the tension lingers in the air for a few seconds, the large man and the one with swords slam their fists together and begin sparring. Machi wonders what Chrollo is planning, and the short man reminds her that they are thieves so they are coming together to steal. She wonders what he plans to steal, smiling and guessing that it will be old books since he loves them. The short man says that it's probably the game that is being auctioned off, adding that it's the most expensive and dangerous in the world. With all 13 members of the Phantom Troupe gathered together in an abandoned building, their leader Chrollo declares that they will steal all the loot from the Underground Auction. A large, hairy man asks him if he is sure since they will have to worry about making enemies of all the Mafia members. Chrollo asks the man if he's scared, but the man replies that he's elated, asking him to give the order as blood drips from his mouth. Chrollo gives them permission to kill anyone who gets in their way, and the members make their way toward the city. Elsewhere, Dalzollene speaks to someone on the phone and apologizes for interrupting their vacation. He tells them that there was something very worrying among Neon's fortunes.

Chapter 72 September 1st: Part 1 (9①, "Kugatsu Tsuitachi (Ichi)") is the 72nd chapter of the Hunter × Hunter manga, written and illustrated by Yoshihiro Togashi. Synopsis. At Kukuroo Mountain, Milluki is furious that he can't recreate Greed Island using save data from the game, at first wondering if Killua tricked him but quickly realizing that his younger brother couldn't forge a game and wouldn't double-cross him either. He guesses that either Killua was tricked or the data is real, angrily wondering why it won't work if the latter is true. He considers hacking into the Hunter website and wishes that Illumi were there to help. Desperate to discover the secret, he says that he is willing to pay anything. He checks his savings and finds a balance of 12.7 billion, saying that he would prefer to have twice that so he can beat the other bidders. After boarding a balloon vehicle with a propeller on top, he calls his father and says that he will kill 15 people if he loans him 15 billion. Using a computer, he sets the vehicle to autopilot and has it head directly to Lingon Airport, saying that he was probably ten the last time he left the house. At a hotel in Yorknew City, Dalzollene reads the first four lines from one of Neon's fortunes to her father on the phone, telling him that three other poems begin the same way. He adds that the four clients all plan to attend the Underground Auction and worries about their safety, saying that sleep-related words in the fortunes usually allude to illness or death. The boss tells Dalzollene to send the fortunes to the clients, and Dalzollene then mentions that Neon not only doesn't know what she writes, but can't tell her own future. He asks if she should still be allowed to attend the auction, and the boss tells him to bring her home immediately. Dalzollene, however, says that Neon will become furious if they try to do so since she has been looking forward to it. The boss agrees that she can stay as long as she doesn't go anywhere near the auction, telling Dalzollene to get her whatever she wants and that they must bid for the items themselves. Dalzollene meets up with all the bodyguards and tells them that their next assignment will be bidding on a list of items at the Underground Auction, stressing that money is no object. The three items are the mummy of Princess Corco, a tissue used by the actor Sonne Limarch, and a set of Scarlet Eyes from the Kurta Clan. As Kurapika looks up at the image of the last item on the projector, Dalzollene tells the group that they also received a tip about a possible attack on the auction. He tells them to prepare accordingly, but stresses that obtaining the items is their top priority. He says that the first item will be auctioned off at 9 p.m. in the Cemetery Building, assigning Ivlenkov, Tocino, and Baise to be in charge of the bidding. Basho wonders why he would assign only three of them, and Dalzollene replies that buyers have to enter in groups of three and since the Mafia runs the event, there have rarely been any problems. He stresses that since trust is everything, there are no surveillance cameras inside. He tells them to forget any rivalries, to not make any disturbances, and to not talk to anyone else. After he assigns Basho and Linssen to rear entrance surveillance, Kurapika and Melody to front entrance surveillance, and Squala (and himself) to guard Neon, Dalzollene tells the group to head out. At a hotel in the city, Leorio learns that Gon and Killua only have 5 million when the minimum bid for Greed Island is 8.9 billion. He stresses that they won't even be able to afford the entrance fee to the Southernpiece Auction House and adds that even if the game has clues about Gon's father, they can't do much if it's nearly impossible to obtain. Killua points out that it was listed as "easy" on the Hunter website and Gon says that the reason is because one only needs money to get it. Leorio then reminds them both that the world really is all about money. Killua replies that something that can be bought isn't real treasure and that anyone who calls themselves a professional Hunter should easily be able to obtain the game. As Gon and Leorio look for ideas on the computer, Killua calls them both simple and stupid, guessing that Leorio is also an Enhancer. They find information on swap meets and then read about something called a conditional auction, where the seller sets a non-monetary condition and gives the item to the first person who fulfills it. Leorio suddenly gets an idea and energetically says that he has a guaranteed way to make a profit. After the three head out to the street and Gon sits waiting at a table, Leorio announces to a growing crowd that the first one to beat the boy in arm wrestling will win a diamond ring worth 3 million. As Killua shows off the reward, Leorio tells the crowd that it only costs 10,000 to participate and enthusiastically asks them who will try first. Dozens of people eagerly hold up their money and hurry to get in line. Once the first contender sits down and puts his hand out, Gon reminds himself to be barely stronger than them and to pretend that he's suffering. As Gon easily beats several people, Killua says to himself that their scheme is pretty much hustling and that they would need 889,999 more wins to make 8.9 billion. One person in the crowd says that Gon has beaten 150 guys so far, and another wonders how old he is. Three others hope that he is close to his limit and that he doesn't lose before it's their turn. It's revealed that Gon is sweating because he feels bad for scamming so many people. Leorio then welcomes the first female contender, and it's revealed to be a member of the Phantom Troupe. The woman bows and says that she will do her best. The two lock their right hands together and once Leorio gives the signal, Gon is surprised by the woman's strength and forced to actually try as he eventually beats her. She thanks him before leaving, and Killua realizes that Gon had to actually try in order to win. As they wonder if she's the female world champion of arm wrestling, the woman meets up with two other Troupe members who ask her how it went. She says that the boy was tough and she lost. The shorter member addresses her as Shizuku and says that she is too weak. She says that she really wanted the diamond ring, and the larger member replies that she should have used her left arm. The shorter member agrees and wonders why she didn't use her strong arm. Shizuku realizes her mistake and says that she only put out her right because the boy did. She says that she wants to try again, but the other two remind her that they don't have time since they need to make their move at the auction. Elsewhere, after being told that she isn't allowed to attend the auction, Neon begins to throw things around the room and scream that she wants to go. Dalzollene is on the phone with her father and asks if he can hear her, saying that they don't know what to do.

Chapter 73 September 1st: Part 2 (9②, "Kugatsu Tsuitachi (Ni)") is the 73rd chapter of the Hunter × Hunter manga, written and illustrated by Yoshihiro Togashi. Synopsis. At the Hotel Beitacle, as Neon sleeps after her outburst. The maids pick up the mess, Dalzollene (with several bumps on his head from trying to calm Neon down) calls her father and assures him that they will win the items that she wants from the auction. However, he adds that she wanted to win them herself and that she will be disappointed once she learns that she missed it. Her father says that he will change his plans and head over to the hotel, telling Dalzollene to make sure that they acquire the mummy so Neon will be in a good mood. Dalzollene then calls Kurapika and asks how things look at the front entrance. Melody looks through binoculars from a rooftop and says that nothing has changed. Kurapika tells Dalzollene that everything is clear and that they will call if anything happens. Melody says that no one can get within 550 yards of the Cemetery Building besides the Mafia's own security. She then asks Kurapika what the Scarlet Eyes mean to him, pointing out that his heartbeat sounded ferocious when he saw the image of them. Kurapika reveals that he is a member of the Kurta Clan and that he wears black contacts to avoid detection since their eyes are usually brown and turn red when they become upset. He says that he is searching for the rest of his brethren's eyes and wants to return them to their graves, asking Melody if she plans to tell Dalzollene about him. Melody says that she doesn't want to die, recognizing that Kurapika is willing to sacrifice himself for his goals. Kurapika asks Melody why she applied for the job and says that her eyes will tell him if she's lying. Melody reveals that she is a professional Hunter as well, specifically a Music Hunter who is looking for a certain piece of music. The two make eye contact, and Kurapika says that she left out the important details, causing Melody to laugh. She then reveals that she is looking for the Sonata of Darkness, a piece supposedly composed by Satan which curses anyone who performs or listens to it. As Kurapika wonders if it's just an urban legend, Melody rolls up her sleeve and reveals the condition of her right arm. She quickly pulls it back down and says that hearing just one movement (the flute solo) was enough to harm her, asking Kurapika if he wants to see an old picture of her. She also reveals that her friend who played the solo died and that his body was completely affected, adding that his friend had only taught him on the condition that he never play it. She reveals that the two of them were drunk at the time and that she received her ability in exchange, but admits that she would give everything back if she could be the way she was again. She says that she plans to find the piece of music and destroy it so that no one has to suffer as she and her friend have, adding that she chose the job because she hoped one devil would know another. After the two end their conversation since the auction is about to start, Ivlenkov, Baise, and Tocino make their way through the metal detectors inside (where two members of the Phantom Troupe are working in disguise). Baise wonders why the capos aren't using proxies since it's just an auction, and Tocino points out that they earn points for their family, with the syndicate receiving 5% of the proceeds as a commission. He adds that some families get into bidding wars and end up bankrupt trying to show off their financial clout. As everyone takes their seats in the crowded auditorium, two more members of the Troupe walk out onto the stage. The shorter one welcomes them and says that there is no need for formal greetings since they will all die now. The larger one behind him readies his Nen, and the tips of his fingers suddenly separate and hang down from small chains. As the bullets from his Double Machine Gun ability easily rip through the attendees, Tocino uses his Eleven Black Children ability to protect himself as well as Ivlenkov and Baise. However, the bullets easily destroy the puppets and then fatally wound Tocino, who realizes that the man is using Nen bullets and is also an Emitter. The massacre continues, and Ivlenkov and Baise quickly dash away from the hail of bullets, but Shizuku waits for them outside the auditorium, crushing Ivlenkov's head into the floor with an odd-looking vacuum cleaner. Baise tries to run away, but Shizuku quickly leaps toward her and kills her in the same fashion. The three Troupe members meet up in the auditorium filled with dozens of dead Mafia members, and Shizuku uses her vacuum (called Blinky) to suck up all the corpses, blood, personal belongings, and chairs. One Mafia member is still alive and says that no matter who they are, the Mafia will track them down and kill them along with all their families. After the larger member destroys the man's body with his bullets, the shorter one coyly asks what family is.

Chapter 74 September 1st: Part 3 (9③, "Kugatsu Tsuitachi (San)") is the 74th chapter of the Hunter × Hunter manga, written and illustrated by Yoshihiro Togashi. Synopsis. Kurapika notices something going on with the Underground Auction as many armed Mafia members enter the Cemetery Building. Nervous about the situation, Kurapika notes that armed men are entering the building as Melody starts to contact Dalzollene. Upon hearing this, Dalzollene becomes furious about the situation and tells them to head into the building while he contacts Linssen and the others. Meanwhile, back in the auction house's auditorium, most of the Mafia members are baffled to see the place completely empty. Kurapika calls Dalzollene and tells him that the whole auction house is empty with no security guards or Mafia clients in it, saying that it's like they all just vanished into thin air. Down in the vault area, Mafia officials also discover that all of the contents of the vault have been stolen, guessing that the intruders made their escape from the roof. They then give out an order to every organization in Yorknew City to be on the lookout for any suspicious blimps, to shoot them down if they spot them, and that the people on board must be brought back alive, promising a huge reward to those who capture them. Dalzollene declares that they must capture the thieves, telling Kurapika and Melody that he's coming as well and will meet them at the overpass along central square. He then orders Squala to leave five guard dogs stationed at the hotel. Squala agrees and tells Neon's attendants to not leave Neon alone and to not let anyone in or out of the building before they return. As he runs to the agreed spot with Melody, Kurapika says that the reward will cause the Mafia families to fight amongst themselves, and Melody adds that it's already affected Dalzollene. At the Phantom Troupe's hideout, Chrollo is seen talking to Uvogin on the phone and asks him if it was empty. Riding in a hot-air balloon with six other Troupe members, Uvogin confirms that the vault was already empty, adding that the items were taken somewhere else according to the auctioneer. He adds that it's as if the Mafia knew that they were coming. Chrollo seems unfazed in his response, but Uvogin stresses that the timing was too perfect and that there may be a Judas among them. Chrollo assures Uvogin that there isn't and adds that he doesn't even consider Judas to be a traitor. He points out that Judas reportedly betrayed Christ for 30 silver coins, and asks Uvogin what any of them would have to gain by betraying their comrades to the Mafia. Uvogin is reluctantly convinced, and Chrollo continues by saying that the precautions taken by the Mafia were very inadequate if they had an informant, explaining that their security would have been much tighter if they knew that the Troupe was planning to attack. Chrollo goes on to theorize that the Mafia received a vague tip from a source which one of the higher-ups trusted enough to take seriously. Uvogin replies that he doesn't understand how the information is being spread, but he asks Chrollo what they should do next. Chrollo asks if they know where the merchandise went, and Uvogin says that the auctioneer refused to say even after Feitan (who says he feels most sorry for the man) tortured him severely. After Chrollo asks if the auctioneer revealed who would know where the items were taken, Uvogin confirms this and goes on to talk about the Ten Dons, the leaders of the Mafia who each has their own turf in ten regions on six continents. He explains that the auction is the one time every year that all ten gather together in one place to discuss matters and issue orders. Finally, he reveals that each don assigns their best bodyguard to a team known as the Shadow Beasts who execute their given orders. Chrollo then says since the Shadow Beasts weren't part of the security at the auction house, they most likely didn't know that they were coming. Uvogin agrees with Chrollo and says that the Mafia's security was laughably light. Chrollo asks how they moved so many items, and Uvogin replies that one of the Shadow Beasts used no tools and left empty-handed, somehow emptying the 25x25 vault which was completely full of merchandise. Uvogin says that the tall man calls himself Owl, and Chrollo guesses that he has a Nen ability similar to Shizuku's. He adds that the Mafia must be aware that Nen is being used since 500 guests somehow vanished. As the Mafia members chase after the hot-air balloon, Uvogin smirks and asks if they can fight them, with Chrollo telling them to draw enough attention to lure out the Shadow Beasts.

Chapter 75 September 1st: Part 4 (9④, "Kugatsu Tsuitachi (Yon)") is the 75th chapter of the Hunter × Hunter manga, written and illustrated by Yoshihiro Togashi. Synopsis. Several Mafia members spot the Phantom Troupe's hot-air balloon floating away from the city toward the Gordeau Desert. One of them is surprised that it's not an airship and wonders where the missing guests are. Another guesses that the Troupe's plan was more than just an armored heist, telling the others to contact the Dons so they can call in the Shadow Beasts. After tracking and shooting down the balloon, dozens of Mafia members stand in a large canyon and yell for the six Troupe members to come down from the ledge above. Shalnark is happy to see so many, and Uvogin tells the others that he will take care of all the Mafia members by himself, sliding down the cliff to face them with guns drawn. One Mafia member approaches Uvogin and points a gun right at his face, asking if he kidnapped the guests. Uvogin confirms it, and the Mafia member asks if he thought that he would get away with it, wondering who his leader is. After Uvogin just smirks in reply and the man shoots, it's shown that Uvogin caught the bullet with his teeth. Uvogin then breaks the man's neck with a single swipe, leaving the others in shock and telling himself that he wanted to be stronger than anything. As Uvogin grabs the man by his head and begins attacking the nearest Mafia members, the other Troupe members comment on how easily Uvogin will kill them, wondering why they keep trying to fight him. With several Mafia members dead, Uvogin says that it won't even count as a warm-up before the Shadow Beasts arrive. At that moment, a sniper fires and shoots Uvogin in the side of the head, but it only causes him some pain since he surrounded his body with aura. He spots the two snipers in the distance and says that he hates sneaky cowards, picking up two rocks and hurling them at the snipers. After both rocks hit their mark and kill the snipers, a Mafia member approaches with a rocket launcher and says that he will easily blow him up since the weapon can take out a tank. As Uvogin feels slighted being compared to just a tank, the man fires the weapon directly at him, causing an enormous explosion which Kurapika and Basho see as they drive up to the scene. The Mafia members are confident that they killed him, but when the smoke clears, Uvogin himself appears mostly unscathed and says that the attack hurt, with the clothes on his torso burned off and some areas on his body still smoking. The Mafia members scream in fear and begin to run away, but Uvogin chuckles and says that they have no chance of escaping. In the distance, Kurapika and the others wonder what caused the explosion. Looking through binoculars, Kurapika spots Uvogin mercilessly beheading and bisecting the Mafia members, confirming that he uses Nen and is incredibly strong. He adds that guns are useless against him, handing the binoculars to Dalzollene so that he can see the carnage for himself. Using a monocular to see the massacre, a frightened Squala refuses to fight and tells the others that the man is ripping his victims apart with his bare hands. As Dalzollene says that they have to try at least, Melody senses another heartbeat and something begins to approach the group by moving just below the ground. Kurapika and Basho jump back before a disturbing-looking person emerges and introduces himself as Worm, one of the Shadow Beasts. He asks them what family the group is from, and Dalzollene answers the Ritz Family and that they are acting as bodyguards for Mr. Nostrade. Worm tells him that they should stay away from the fight, and three more Shadow Beasts suddenly appear, calling themselves experts and calmly approaching Uvogin (with Worm burrowing back under the ground). As the other Troupe members play a game of cards, Feitan notices the three approaching and Uvogin guesses that they are the Shadow Beasts, asking them where they took the auction items. Rabid Dog in turn asks Uvogin what he did with the guests, and Uvogin calmly answers that they killed them, asking him again where the items are. As Uvogin begins to threaten the three, Worm suddenly appears behind him and punches him hard in the face. Although the punch does damage, Worm's hand is broken in the process and after praising his strike, Uvogin returns one of his own, knocking out several of Worm's teeth and popping out one of his eyes as the other Troupe members continue playing their game of cards.

Chapter 76 September 1st: Part 5 (9⑤, "Kugatsu Tsuitachi (Go)") is the 76th chapter of the Hunter × Hunter manga, written and illustrated by Yoshihiro Togashi. Synopsis. It's first explained that Franklin, an Emitter, changed his fingertips into guns that allow him to shoot chunks of aura (Nen bullets). It's added that although it was unnecessary for him to cut off his fingertips, it made the bullets more effective because restrictions can markedly improve Nen abilities.
