As Uvogin smirks after his successful punch and the three other Shadow Beasts look on with hesitation, the injured Worm suddenly grabs Uvogin's wrist and burrows beneath the ground. Holding Uvogin's left arm beneath the surface, he asks Uvogin if he wants to be killed either underground by him or above ground by the other Shadow Beasts, who begin to leap toward him. Uvogin becomes enraged and clenches his fist, telling Worm that he's the one who can't escape. The other Phantom Troupe members notice that Uvogin isn't messing around as he suddenly unleashes a Big Bang Impact directly below himself, only leaving behind Worm's lower right arm and forcing the other Shadow Beasts to jump back. The three Shadow Beasts all notice the #11 spider tattoo on Uvogin's lower back, and as the Nostrade bodyguards can't believe the destruction from Uvogin's attack, Kurapika looks through the binoculars and sees the tattoo, immediately knowing its significance. Franklin pities the dead Shadow Beast, Nobunaga praises Uvogin's attack, and Machi says that it's just a regular punch infused with Nen. Uvogin asks which of the Shadow Beasts wants to die next, and even though they recognize that he's a member of the Troupe, they charge toward him confidently. Uvogin praises their recklessness and punches at Porcupine's face, but thousands of needles suddenly appear, keeping Uvogin's fist from reaching him. Porcupine explains that he can manipulate the hair on his body and turn it into sharp needles. As Porcupine praises Uvogin's punch and tells him that it won't be able to make contact, Rabid Dog suddenly takes a small bite out of Uvogin's left shoulder. Feitan is surprised that hair and teeth were able to puncture Uvogin's skin, and Shalnark praises their discipline and Nen. The latter yells out to ask if he needs any help, but Uvogin yells back for him to stay out of it. He tries to shake off Porcupine, but the thousands of hairs keep him firmly attached. Even more enraged and declaring that he will just use him as an extension of his fist, Uvogin attempts to punch Leech, but Porcupine simply extends and softens more hairs to act as a barrier. Rabid Dog moves and takes another bite out of Uvogin's left thigh, dodging a punch from the cornered Spider. Uvogin suddenly feels uneasy and stumbles to the ground, with Rabid Dog revealing that he is experiencing the effects of his fangs' neurotoxin. He adds that it won't affect him from the neck up, still forcing him to feel fear and pain. Machi comments that they would have won if the toxin had been lethal, but Shalnark adds that they probably enjoy torture. Leech suddenly appears behind Uvogin and begins to suck on his shoulder wound. He explains that he is inserting thousands of leeches that will lay eggs in his bladder and burst through once he urinates, adding that most people die from the pain. Before Leech can finish his explanation, Uvogin quickly turns to the side and takes a large bite out of his head. As he chews on Leech's brain, he criticizes the taste and spits it out, reminding him that he's not the only one who can bite. He puts on a maniacal smile and says that as long as he can move from his neck up, he can still kill them all. He begins to enlarge his cheeks and suddenly expels a small object toward Rabid Dog, who recognizes that it's a piece of Leech's skull and holds out his hand to block the projectile, but the fragment pierces his hand and then bursts through his head. Uvogin then turns toward Porcupine, who assures himself that his hair will be able to deflect any bullets that Uvogin sends at him. But instead of shooting a projectile, Uvogin simply yells as loud as he can directly at Porcupine, forcing the other Troupe members and some of the Nostrade bodyguards to cover their ears. Blood suddenly bursts from Porcupine's eyes and ears, and Uvogin tosses his body aside, saying that needles can't deflect sound. The other Troupe members yell at him for not warning them first, and Uvogin says that he didn't want to give away his plan. He reminds them all that they're fast enough to cover their ears anyway, then asking Shizuku if she can use Blinky to suck out the poison and leeches. Shizuku replies that it can get the poison, but reminds him that it can't be used to suck up living things. Shalnark jumps down and analyzes the spotted leech, saying that it reaches the bladders of its victims in 24 hours, lays its eggs, and then dies. He confirms Leech's explanation that the pain from urination will be enough to kill him, but points out that the eggs need an alkaline environment to hatch. He explains that the eggs will pass unhatched and painlessly with the urine if the pH is too low, telling Uvogin to drink beer and urinate as much as possible in the next 24 hours (and that once his urine goes from dark to clear, he will be fine). To the dismay of the other bodyguards, Kurapika begins walking toward the Troupe members and says that he plans to capture Uvogin. Squala reminds him of the man's ferocity, and Kurapika calmly replies that it makes no difference. A gravely wounded Worm appears out of the ground elsewhere and calls someone by phone, mentioning the Spiders and telling them to bring everyone to deal with the group. At the Troupe's hideout, Hisoka tells Chrollo that he promised he would meet someone later, and Chrollo says that he can leave as long as he's back by 6 p.m. the next day. He continues reading his book and asks Hisoka if he's up to no good again, which Hisoka coyly confirms. At a lodging in Yorknew City, Leorio shows off his Nen, but when Gon tells him that what he's doing is specifically called Ten, a confused Leorio asks if there's more than just that, which doesn't surprise Killua.

Chapter 77 September 1st: Part 6 (9⑥, "Kugatsu Tsuitachi (Roku)") is the 77th chapter of the Hunter × Hunter manga, written and illustrated by Yoshihiro Togashi. Synopsis. Squala and Dalzollene try to convince Kurapika to reconsider capturing Uvogin, with Melody sensing that his heartbeat is full of anger and hatred. As Dalzollene stresses that it's an order and Kurapika continues to ignore him, they are all suddenly surrounded by fields and flowers for a split second. Melody is shown playing her flute, saying that the piece is called "A Field in Spring" and perfect for relaxation. She asks the others if they have calmed down and says that they should plan their strategy with level heads. Kurapika thanks her, but Melody senses that Kurapika is still intent on capturing Uvogin. He gets Dalzollene's attention and asks that he be allowed to try, saying that he stands a good chance. It's stated that Shizuku is a Conjurer whose conjured vacuum cleaner (named Blinky) can suck up anything except what Shizuku considers alive. It's added that it can return the last thing it sucked up, and that Shizuku herself is unaware of where all the items go. As the injured Uvogin asks Shizuku to use Blinky to suck out all the poison and Shalnark asks the other Phantom Troupe members to steal a case of beer, chains are suddenly wrapped all over Uvogin's upper body and snatch him far away from his comrades. After Machi quickly throws out a needle with thread attached to it, the others guess that another Shadow Beast is responsible for the capture. Machi says that In makes her thread invisible unless they use Gyo or catch sight of the needle, assuring the others that it will track the target anywhere they go. They hurry to give chase before the captor notices the needle and thread, hoping to take out the rest of the Shadow Beasts and also remembering to find some beer for Uvogin. As Uvogin sits chained in the back seat beside Squala, Kurapika drives the car with Melody sitting in the passenger seat. Uvogin gets Kurapika's attention and mocks his chains, adding that he will regret it later if he doesn't kill him now. After Uvogin refuses to be quiet after Kurapika orders him, the chains suddenly increase in size and strength. Kurapika turns around to face him and stresses that he needs to be quiet, with a panicked Melody telling Kurapika to keep his eyes on the road. Even though he's still paralyzed from the poison, Uvogin realizes that Kurapika has infused the Nen chain with enough power to restrain him. Kurapika confidently tells himself that he will only use his Chain Jail on the Spiders, adding that if he uses the ability on anyone else, he will immediately lose his life. He explains that he created a self-imposed restriction and says that the risk is worth the immense power in return. Basho, Linssen, and Dalzollene notice the Troupe members quickly approaching in another car. Dalzollene talks to Melody by phone and tells them to speed up. After wondering how they found them since they're moving away from the city, Kurapika uses Gyo to spot Machi's Nen thread. Melody suddenly spots something on Uvogin's left calf and orders Squala to get rid of it. Squala tosses the needle out the window, and Machi immediately recognizes that they found it. As Shalnark confidently says that they are close enough now, Owl suddenly drops down on the hood of their car and uses his Fun Fun Cloth to wrap up the car, enveloping it and shrinking it down so he can hold it between just two fingers. With only Nobunaga trapped inside, Owl faces the other Troupe members and realizes how dangerous they are if they were quick enough to escape. Feitan says that Nobunaga was only captured because he was sitting in the middle seat, and Machi finds Owl's ability fascinating and impressive. Shalnark says that it would allow Owl to carry all the auction items in his pocket and that he can turn them back to their original size. Five other Shadow Beasts suddenly arrive, with one voicing his disappointment about the Troupe because of how weak they appear. Shizuku points out that if there are ten Shadow Beasts in total, they have encountered them all. Feitan says that the person with the chain is still in the car with Uvogin, and Shizuku then wonders whether they are a Shadow Beast or not. Feitan readies his Nen and replies that they just need to ask them to find out.

Chapter 78 September 1st: Part 7 (9⑦, "Kugatsu Tsuitachi (Nana)") is the 78th chapter of the Hunter × Hunter manga, written and illustrated by Yoshihiro Togashi. Synopsis. Linssen and Basho notice that the Phantom Troupe members are no longer following them, having seen that someone landed on their car. Dalzollene guesses that it was the other Shadow Beasts and tells Kurapika that they will return to the city and change the location to their third plan. It's stated that Machi is a Transmuter and spins her aura into threads, with the tensile strength of each strand being inversely proportional to its length. It's added that if the strand is equivalent to cotton thread, it can be spun long enough to circle the globe and, if it's shorter than one meter, strong enough to hold up a weight of one ton. However, it's explained that the strength is reduced once she lets go since Conjurers and Transmuters are not proficient at Emission. Inside a large building, the Nostrade bodyguards stand around Uvogin as he awakens and finds himself restrained to a table. Wielding a "", Dalzollene asks him where he took the auction items, but Uvogin simply asks for the time and how long he was unconscious. Dalzollene yells that he will be asking the questions, driving the blade toward Uvogin's right thigh, but Uvogin activates his Nen and the blade quickly breaks before doing any damage. Impressed by Uvogin's willpower and describing him as a combat machine, Kurapika says to himself that the Troupe member's aura has no hesitation even though he's about to be tortured. Thinking to himself, Uvogin says that he is still unable to move and it will take more time. He adds that he ate dinner around 8 p.m. and guesses from the feeling in his stomach that four hours have passed. He moves his eyes toward Dalzollene and agrees to spare their lives if they let him go. A panicked Squala wonders why he isn't begging for his life, and Melody says that Uvogin means what he said. Uvogin clarifies that they only want the items from the Underground Auction and adds that none of them will be killed since they don't know where the items are. The others are surprised when Uvogin confirms that the vault was already empty when his group arrived, with Uvogin saying that the Shadow Beasts must have taken the items and not told underlings like them. Melody nervously says that she doesn't think he's lying, and Squala can't believe that he wasn't bluffing with his earlier offer. Uvogin tells them that everyone makes mistakes, pointing out that nothing has been stolen yet. He repeats his offer and adds that they ignore the plan to steal the auction items, but Kurapika asks him what happened to the guests at the auction, mentioning that their comrades were among them. Uvogin calmly tells him that they are all dead, and Kurapika proceeds to punch him right in the face, angrily asking him how many have died because of their selfish plans. Basho tries to calm Kurapika down, and Dalzollene adds that they can hand Uvogin over to the Mafia if the auction items are safe. Moving to another room, he calls someone and informs them that they captured one of the thieves. The person on the phone is astonished and reveals that not even the Shadow Beasts were able to capture any of them. Dalzollene replies that he will explain later, telling them to send someone over immediately. He is also curious about the Shadow Beasts and is stunned to learn that they are all dead. As Kurapika receives a text from Hisoka telling him to meet as promised, Dalzollene tells the others that he will stay behind with Uvogin, telling them to gas him with enough muscle relaxant for three men before they go rest. Kurapika makes his way to the agreed-upon location, and Hisoka is seen playing with his cards, noting that Kurapika is early. Kurapika says to himself that Hisoka doesn't appear to be using In, and Hisoka assures Kurapika that he doesn't plan to fight him now. Kurapika asks for information on the Troupe, and Hisoka explains that there are thirteen members in total (with each sporting a numbered tattoo as proof). He adds that members can be replaced if an applicant defeats one of them, and any other vacancies are filled by the leader himself. He says that the group usually just steals and kills, but adds that they do charity work on occasion. After Kurapika replies that he was already aware of those facts, Hisoka reveals that he replaced No. 4 a few years ago because he wanted the chance to fight the leader. However, he says that it has been difficult because of how cautious he is, always having at least two members with him and leaving without a trace once a job has been completed. He tells Kurapika that it will be difficult to achieve each of their goals on their own, promising to reveal the abilities of seven of the members if Kurapika agrees to work with him. Dalzollene receives a call and tells the Mafia members that they are in B2. One of them asks if the thief is still alive, and Dalzollene explains that they numbed his body with gas since they couldn't penetrate his skin. As they stand beside the table, Uvogin says that "the tailor makes the man" and leaves Dalzollene confused before Phinks suddenly punches through his chest, killing him instantly. Phinks tells Uvogin that he couldn't believe it when he heard about his capture. Machi, Shalnark, and Nobunaga remove their disguises as Shizuku uses Blinky to suck out the poison from Uvogin's body. Uvogin quickly sits up after it's finished and gives a loud scream, cursing the chain user and vowing to get revenge. Melody is startled by the scream as the others sleep through it.

Chapter 79 September 2nd: Part 1 (9①, "Kugatsu Futsuka (Ichi)") is the 79th chapter of the Hunter × Hunter manga, written and illustrated by Yoshihiro Togashi. Synopsis. Uvogin kicks down the door to the sleeping quarters and finds the room empty. Shalnark says that they obviously escaped and Shizuku adds that Uvogin is too loud. Shalnark says that they should head back to the hideout since they disposed of the Shadow Beasts, and Machi adds that they have the auction items as well. However, as his aura billows around him, Uvogin angrily replies that they should tell Chrollo that he won't be coming back until he evens the score with the chain user. It's stated that Uvogin is an Enhancer whose only interests are getting stronger, training, and winning street fights. It's added that his ability, Big Bang Impact, has him focus all of his aura into his fist and creates as much destruction as a small missile, which he hopes to improve to the point where the blast is equivalent to a nuclear bomb. Elsewhere, Hisoka gives Kurapika the option of either teaming up with him or doing things by himself. Kurapika's phone suddenly rings, and Hisoka tells him to answer it. Melody tells him that the Phantom Troupe member got away with help from his comrades who were disguised as Mafia members, guessing that they somehow intercepted Dalzollene's phone call. She adds that Dalzollene is most likely dead and says that they will move to plan B, telling Kurapika to come back. After hanging up, Kurapika asks Hisoka if he knows where the Scarlet Eyes are, but Hisoka quickly answers that it was before he joined. He reveals that the leader revels in his spoils before selling everything and guesses that the Scarlet Eyes were also sold. He warns Kurapika that the Troupe will keep going until their leader is dead, again asking Kurapika if he wants to team up. Kurapika tells him that he will give his answer at the same time tomorrow. Having fled to the Hotel Beitacle, the other Nostrade bodyguards try to call Dalzollene, but no one answers as Dalzollene's lifeless body is seen lying on the floor. Squala tells Melody that he has to be dead, especially after they heard Uvogin moving upstairs and yelling about the chain user. After regrouping with the others, Kurapika says that they should report back to the boss, but Basho informs him that Neon is only a boss in name since she is just a child. Squala reveals that their real employer is her father, Light Nostrade, who has been giving all the orders through Dalzollene. Kurapika and Squala wake up Neon and tell her that the auction was canceled after a group of thieves attacked it. They add that Baise, Ivlenkov, and Tocino are all dead and that Dalzollene was probably killed as well. Neon completely ignores their deaths and simply asks about the mummy she wanted, asking if it was stolen. Kurapika assures her that the items were safely moved elsewhere, and after they tell her that Dalzollene was in charge of all their communications, Neon hands them her cellphone and says that her father's number is in there. Kurapika tells Squala to call him, and Squala wonders why it should be him. Linssen speaks up and says because he has been working there the longest. Melody says that they should decide as a group and nominates Kurapika to call since he caught the Spider and is the most qualified. The others quickly agree, and Kurapika says that he will make the call and act as the go-between only until they confirm Dalzollene's death. He says to himself that he didn't think things would work out so quickly. He returns to Neon's room and asks her if she can introduce him to her father. Neon tells her father about the robbery at the auction and Dalzollene's possible death, asking him to talk to the stand-in. Light first asks about Dalzollene, and Kurapika confirms that he is most likely dead, which surprises Light since he was able to use Nen and could easily block multiple bullets fired at him. Kurapika reveals that the Phantom Troupe was involved, mentioning that he saw one of them stop a rocket with his bare hand. He then introduces himself and asks what they should do next. Light asks to hear what he thinks first, and Kurapika suggests that Neon leave the city immediately since they can't be completely sure of her safety anymore. Light agrees with his assessment but says that he also wants to respect his daughter's wishes. Kurapika says that her safety should be their top priority, and Light replies that he will arrive tomorrow evening and convince Neon personally if it comes to that. Light informs Kurapika that he will be in command now and that his first order is to keep constant watch on his daughter. After hanging up, Kurapika tells Neon that her father will be arriving tomorrow and wants her to stay in her room until then. Neon is disappointed since she wanted to go to the casino, but she excitedly asks to play cards as Kurapika leaves the room. Kurapika then calls the front desk and asks for the name under which the room registered. Elsewhere in the city, with a man lying dead on the floor, Uvogin drinks beer as Shalnark uses the computer and says that Polio & Co. Ltd., a dummy company for the Nostrade Family, owns the building where Uvogin was being held. Uvogin asks if he can find out what other buildings they own around the city, and Shalnark also checks if their men are staying at any hotels. He asks Uvogin why he still hasn't gotten a Hunter License since it allows him to buy so much information on their website. Uvogin replies that he never carries cash and just steals whatever he wants. Shalnark receives the information and learns that the Nostrade Family has two other buildings (and that their members are staying at three hotels). He assures Uvogin that he should be able to track down the chain user by tomorrow, and Uvogin thanks him by giving him a big kiss on the side of his head. Shalnark tells Uvogin that he should pay him back instead, adding that he will also dispose of the bodies. As Uvogin approaches the window to leave with several beer cans, Shalnark tells him to be careful. Uvogin leaps out of the window and downs another beer, telling himself that the chain user is probably the muscle of the family and that he should check the cheaper hotel first. Back at the Hotel Beitacle, Kurapika shows Melody and Squala the Hunter Website and says that it lists all the properties which the Nostrade Family owns as well as all their employees. Squala is taken aback, and Kurapika adds that the new recruits haven't been added to the list yet. He tells them that the room was reserved in Dalzollene's name, and since he is on the payroll for one of the dummy companies, the Troupe will find the room if they compare the employee list with the hotel registries, leaving Squala in disbelief over the network that professional Hunters use. Kurapika says that they should move Neon to another room, putting it under Basho or Melody's name. He tells them all to stay in the new room, but when Melody asks him what he plans to do, Kurapika replies that he will stay behind to wait for Uvogin. At the cheap hotel, Uvogin tortures a man for information as another lies dead on the floor. The man says that the chain user probably isn't a Mafia member but a bodyguard for the boss' daughter. He reveals that she collects all sorts of body parts and tells the fortunes for high-ranking clients in the Mafia. He adds that the information helped their boss, asking Uvogin to spare him since he's told him so much. As Uvogin reflects on the girl's ability to tell the future, he crushes the man's head against the wall and realizes that Chrollo was right when he said that there was no traitor among the Spiders.

Chapter 8 The Other Enemy (もうひとつの, "Mō Hitotsu no Teki") is the 8th chapter of the Hunter × Hunter manga, written and illustrated by Yoshihiro Togashi. Synopsis. As the examinees stare at the Milsy Wetlands, another examinee is seen crawling up the stairs of the tunnel, but the large metal door shuts before he can make it outside. Satotz addresses the silent group and repeats his warning about the swamp's deadly creatures, telling them to stay close to him and remain alert. With Leorio thankful for the warning, a wounded man suddenly appears from behind the tunnel's exit. He declares that Satotz is an imposter, stating that he's the real examiner. To prove his claim to the confused examinees, the man reveals a seemingly dead Man-faced Ape with a face very similar to Satotz's, explaining that they disguise themselves and lead humans into the swamp where they work with their fellow creatures to set a trap. The man then claims that the creatures are trying to eliminate all the examinees, but three playing cards suddenly pierce his face and leave him lying dead on the ground, revealing that he was a Man-faced Ape. After Satotz is seen to have caught four cards, Hisoka chuckles and shuffles the rest of his cards between his hands. The seemingly dead Man-faced Ape leaps up and tries to make its escape, but Hisoka quickly throws out a card and kills it with a shot to the head. Hisoka says that they can be sure that Satotz is the real examiner since they are skilled Hunters who would easily be able to dodge his attacks. Satotz takes it as a compliment, but warns Hisoka that the next attack will result in his disqualification. After Hisoka understands the warning, several birds suddenly swoop down and begin eating the dead man's body, leaving Leorio disgusted at the brutality. Satotz is impressed by the creature's trick to mislead the examinees and guesses that many of them were starting to be convinced by its claim, with Leorio and Hanzo left embarrassed. He then leads the 311 remaining examinees into the wetlands, and Leorio immediately complains about another marathon (now through wilderness). As fog suddenly appears around the examinees, Killua tells Gon that they should move to the front, and Gon agrees since they want to stay close to Satotz. Killua also points out that it will get them away from Hisoka, smiling as he guesses that he will use the fog to kill more of the examinees. With Gon taken aback, Killua reveals that he is like Hisoka and can smell his murderous intent. Gon replies that he doesn't seem like Hisoka, but Killua chuckles and says that he's just pretending to be innocent, adding that he will see. Gon then yells out for Leorio and Kurapika to move to the front, but Leorio yells back that they would if they could see where they were going. Gon tells them to try harder, but the fog becomes even thicker as they move deeper into the wetlands. Two examinees remind each other to follow the shadows in front of them, but the shadows begin to disappear and the two hear a strange sound. Seeing a strawberry at first, the examinees suddenly encounter multiple Noggin Lugging Tortoises and scream out in horror. Gon hears their cries, and Killua tells him that they are already dead. Two of the Amori Brothers realize that the 100 or so examinees behind them are all gone. It's stated that the tortoises are predators that take advantage of the fog and use the straw-man berries on their backs to lure in lost people. Several of the examinees who escaped from the tortoises are suddenly eaten alive by a Frog-In-Waiting. Others fall upon a pit of spikes after being misled by a Ruse Raven that then feeds on their corpses. Some explode after stepping on Claymore Mushrooms, which multiply by spreading their spores on their prey, and others are put to sleep by Hypnosis Butterflies, which turn their prey into live food for their larvae. Leorio and Kurapika hear the screams and cries from their fellow examinees, understanding that many of them got lost and are getting killed. As Leorio suddenly remembers that all his weapons are in his briefcase, Gon is seen carrying it on his fishing rod and hopes that his two friends are okay. Killua quickly gets Gon's attention and stresses that they need to focus on their own problems, pointing out that they can barely see the people in front of them and that they will end up dead if they get separated. However, as Killua tells Gon to assume that his friends are still alive as long as he doesn't hear their screams, several examinees are suddenly attacked by Hisoka's playing cards, including Kurapika who blocks a few with his and Leorio who screams out in pain after one pierces his left arm. Gon immediately runs back toward them and yells out Leorio's name, with Killua yelling out Gon's name as well. Leorio holds his wound and angrily questions Hisoka, who chuckles as he shuffles his cards and happily replies that he's playing examiner.

Chapter 80 September 2nd: Part 2 (9②, "Kugatsu Futsuka (Ni)") is the 80th chapter of the Hunter × Hunter manga, written and illustrated by Yoshihiro Togashi. Synopsis. Sitting in a room with Gon and Killua, Leorio adds up their 8 million budget: a diamond ring worth 3 million, 2.4 million in cash, and 2.75 million they made from challenging strangers to arm wrestling. He says that it won't be possible, through legal means, to increase it to 900 million for the minimum bid. Gon comments that their arm wrestling scheme wasn't legitimate either, and Killua adds that only people looking for a rematch wanted to challenge them in the last few hours. Gon says that the rumors will keep people away. Still, Leorio replies that he wants the rumors to be as exaggerated as possible since the arm wrestling contest is just baiting to draw out bigger opportunities. It's stated that Hisoka is a Transmuter who turns his aura into a substance like rubber and gum (calling the ability Bungee Gum). It's added that his Texture Surprise allows him to recreate various textures like a sticker and that Bungee Gum has more force the more it's stretched out, but once it's detached from his body, it will tear after it's stretched more than 10 meters. Back in the street, Leorio announces to the crowd that the first one to beat the boy at arm wrestling wins a diamond ring worth 3 million. Someone asks their friend if they want to try, but the other person says that the boy beat 500 guys yesterday. Another person adds that he broke the arms of 20 guys and was raised by a gorilla. Leorio listens to all the rumors spreading around and tells himself that there has to be a betting pool elsewhere that's gambling on the outcome. A giant man suddenly walks toward Leorio and says that he will do it. However, once he sits down and puts his arm out, he asks how it will work since Gon's arm isn't big enough. Leorio tells Gon to switch with him, but an associate of the challenger says that those weren't the rules. Leorio then includes 5 million in addition to the ring, and the two men agree to the deal. Leorio and the large man lock hands, and once the signal is given, Leorio immediately smashes his arm down and breaks the table, leaving the challenger and crowd dumbfounded. Leorio realizes that no one else will want to challenge them now, but the man's associate praises Leorio, who then replies that the two boys are even stronger. The man is impressed and gives Leorio a card with directions, telling him to come by around 5:00 p.m. if he has the time. Leorio says that they may have stumbled on a big opportunity, and after the three make their way through a large crowd of people, they approach a curtain with two men standing in front of it. Leorio hands them the card, and they tell him to take the elevator all the way down. The three arrive at a large arena with a fighting ring in the center and a murmuring crowd sitting in the stands. Killua notes that the crowd wants blood, and once the clock hits 5:00, an announcer steps out and welcomes them to the conditional auction. He says that the game will be hide and seek, leaving Leorio confused. Assistants begin to hand out pieces of paper, and the announcer explains that the seven people pictured are their targets. The flyer has small pictures and descriptions for Uvogin, Shizuku, Shalnark, Feitan, Machi, Franklin, and Nobunaga. Leorio then remembers that Shikuzu was the woman who wrestled Gon earlier. The announcer reveals that they will pay 200 million for each target that they capture and bring back, adding that the game has no deadline and the targets can be dead or alive. Gon and Leorio are excited at the opportunity to make as much as 1.4 billion, but an unsure Killua continues to look over the targets. The announcer says that it costs 5 million to register and asks them to give back the flyer if they refuse to participate. As the other participants begin their search, Leorio seems eager to keep up with them, but Killua reminds him that even the Mafia is having a hard time capturing them. Leorio is left confused, and Killua explains that the contest was clearly set up by the Mafia since they can't capture the targets by themselves. He reminds Leorio about the fighting ring and guesses that they originally planned to have a mindless brawl. He also points out that the prize was a check, and Leorio realizes that the targets were the ones who stole the items that would have been used as the prizes. Killua says that one would have to be crazy to steal from the Mafia, and the only people crazy enough to do it are the Phantom Troupe. Gon then asks where Kurapika is, and Killua realizes that he should be in the city by now, wondering why he hasn't called. Gon uses his Beatle-07 to contact Kurapika, but the phone continues to ring as Kurapika waits inside the Hotel Beitacle and Uvogin slowly makes his way up the stairs. Once the ringing stops, Uvogin opens the door to the hotel room and is impressed that Kurapika stayed behind by himself, asking him to choose where he wants to die. Kurapika replies that he would prefer somewhere isolated since he is confident that Uvogin's death will be noisy. After Gon hangs up and guesses that Kurapika must be working, Leorio asks him what the job is and Gon replies that he's working as a bodyguard. Leorio guesses that it's for a V.I.P. client in the underworld since Kurapika is looking for the Scarlet Eyes. Gon wonders if Kurapika went to the auction and got caught up in the crime, but Leorio replies that Kurapika would have gotten himself involved if the Troupe is actually behind things. He chuckles and says that Kurapika may have already captured a few of them, and Gon says that he hopes that's the case. Killua then reveals that his father once killed one of the Spiders for a job. However, he adds that his father gave the task his highest compliment when he complained that the pay wasn't worth it, also telling him and his siblings three years ago to stay away from the Troupe. Leorio asks if he told Kurapika, and Killua says that there wasn't any point. Gon wonders what they should do and eventually decides to track down the Troupe members on the list.

Chapter 81 September 2nd: Part 3 (9③, "Kugatsu Futsuka (San)") is the 81st chapter of the Hunter × Hunter manga, written and illustrated by Yoshihiro Togashi. Synopsis. Using their Beatle-07 phones in different places around the city, Gon reports no sign of the targets at point A, Leorio does the same at point B, and Killua the same at point C. After waiting for four hours, they come back together and Killua points out that they shouldn't expect thieves wanted by the Mafia to appear in public, adding that the Phantom Troupe may not even be in the city anymore. Leorio reminds them that the Hunter Website is charging 100 million for information on the group, and Killua guesses that it would cost even more for details on each member. Gon says that they will have to find the Troupe members on their own, and Leorio suggests going door-to-door, but Killua replies that it wouldn't work with only three of them. Leorio asks if Kurapika has answered his phone yet, but Killua guesses that he turned it off. Leorio is certain that Kurapika would have more information on the Troupe, but Killua says that he would have to be willing to share it with them. Leorio is left confused, and Killua adds that Kurapika probably doesn't want their help in fighting the Troupe since he would have called if he did. Gon assures them that they will be able to contact Kurapika when they really need his help and Kurapika will do the same if he's in trouble. After Leorio and Killua agree, the three decide to check their home codes to see if they received any tips. In the Gordeau Desert, Uvogin is seen urinating and finally clearing his system of the spotted leech eggs. He apologizes to Kurapika for taking so long, and when Kurapika readies his Nen, Uvogin does the same and then asks who he is, saying that he senses incredible determination in his Nen. Kurapika says that he first needs to answer his question, removing his tabard and asking Uvogin if he remembers the people he has killed. Uvogin replies that he remembers the ones who leave an impression, realizing that Kurapika must be doing this to avenge someone. Kurapika replies that he is avenging the Kurta Clan, but Uvogin doesn't recognize the name. Kurapika explains that they lived in the Lukso Province and that the Troupe attacked them five years ago for their Scarlet Eyes. Uvogin again doesn't recognize the term and asks if it's a kind of jewel. He adds that while he doesn't remember, he would have been there since he was in the Troupe five years ago. Kurapika asks him what he thinks about when he kills people who haven't wronged him, and Uvogin simply replies that he thinks about nothing. As Kurapika's eyes widen, he calls Uvogin scum and tells him to pay for his sins with his life. Uvogin squints his eyes in anger and suddenly unleashes his Nen for the coming fight.

Chapter 82 September 2nd: Part 4 (9④, "Kugatsu Futsuka (Yon)") is the 82nd chapter of the Hunter × Hunter manga, written and illustrated by Yoshihiro Togashi. Synopsis. As he charges up his Nen, Uvogin happily says that killing people is so addictive and denying them revenge gives him the most pleasure. He unleashes a punch and sends of flurry of rocks toward Kurapika, who quickly jumps back and sends out his Chain Jail. Uvogin barely leaps away from the chain's strike and recognizes that it's infused with an incredible amount of Nen. As he dodges Kurapika's chain throws, he tells himself that offense is the best defense and quickly lunges forward, punching Kurapika hard in his left arm. Uvogin is confident that the strike did damage, but Kurapika flings his chain toward Uvogin before crashing into the side of a cliff. Having barely dodged the attack, Uvogin is impressed that Kurapika still had the energy to strike back after being punched. He tells himself that Kurapika's left arm is broken, but as Kurapika stands up and easily moves the arm, Uvogin is left in disbelief and wonders how he could have infused so much Nen in his chains (something only a Manipulator or Conjurer could have done) and also reinforced his left arm enough to block the punch (something only an Enhancer could have done). Kurapika bluntly asks if Uvogin's punch is the best he can do, causing Uvogin to chuckle and reply that it was only 20% of his strength. He then says that he will use 50%, suddenly dashing toward Kurapika and throwing a strong right punch. However, Kurapika quickly dodges and appears right behind him, punching him in the back of the head and kicking him hard in the back. As Uvogin angrily reels from the attack, Kurapika jumps into the air and double kicks Uvogin in the back. Uvogin tries to retaliate with a strike, but Kurapika quickly jumps away and mocks him by guessing what he would have said next. Kurapika tells him to stop wasting his time and use his full power. Uvogin becomes serious and suddenly yells out as his aura spikes all around him. Kurapika recognizes the intensity of his aura, and Uvogin slams his fist into the ground, causing a cloud of dust and rubble to envelop the area. At the moment Kurapika no longer senses his aura and realizes that he's using In, Uvogin suddenly appears behind him and punches Kurapika's left arm again as he attempts to block the strike. This time, however, the arm is clearly broken by the punch as Kurapika is sent flying into the air. Uvogin is completely confident that he shattered Kurapika's arm, saying that no exposed flesh is strong enough to stop his Big Bang Impact. He tells Kurapika that the punch was supposed to break his backbone, praising his quickness and awareness in the cloud of dust. Kurapika replies that he was surprised Uvogin could use In, realizing that he must have used it to erase all signs of his attack. As Kurapika reveals that he can also use In, Uvogin uses Gyo and suddenly finds himself wrapped in Kurapika's Chain Jail. Kurapika recognizes his use of Gyo before landing on the ground and revealing that his chain is conjured out of Nen, which allows him to make it invisible. Uvogin realizes that Kurapika always had his chain conjured so that people would think they were actual chains. Kurapika confirms this and adds that if he pretended to be a Manipulator with real chains, his opponents would only look out for chains that they could see. He reveals that the chain was around Uvogin before he made his bluff. Uvogin then feels a jolt through his entire body, and Kurapika says that the capture phase is complete.

Chapter 83 September 2nd: Part 5 (9⑤, "Kugatsu Futsuka (Go)") is the 83rd chapter of the Hunter × Hunter manga, written and illustrated by Yoshihiro Togashi. Synopsis. In a flashback with his Nen teacher, Kurapika takes the Water Divination test and learns that he's a Conjurer. The man tells him that it means he will be good at materializing things, and Kurapika says that he was hoping to be an Enhancer. He tells Kurapika that while he can't change what he was born with, he can still learn Enhancement techniques. Back in the present, completely restrained by Kurapika's Chain Jail, Uvogin wonders how Kurapika maximized both his Enhancement and Conjuration proficiency since a Nen user can only achieve 100% mastery in the type they were born with. Kurapika says that he will explain it to Uvogin as a parting gift before he sends him to hell, removing his contact lenses and revealing that he is a Specialist. In the flashback, the Nen teacher explains that as a Conjurer, Kurapika can achieve 100% mastery of Conjuration, 80% of Transmutation, 60% of Manipulation and Enhancement, and 40% of Emission. He adds that the further away a type is from his own, the more difficult it will be to master it. Kurapika asks why Specialization is at 0%, and the man explains that it's a trait that's inherited, not learned. He adds that Conjurers and Manipulators are more likely to turn into Specialists later in life, saying that Kurapika still has a chance. His teacher then mentions that Kurapika had talked earlier about wanting to be able to fight to the end by himself, agreeing that Enhancement abilities should be a priority since they are useful for offense, defense, and healing. However, he stresses that since Kurapika is a Conjurer, he will only be able to master half of the Enhancement abilities at half their effectiveness. He gives an example of Kurapika fighting an Enhancer who has 100% mastery, saying that if they both had a strength value of 100 and the Enhancer reinforced his fist with all of his Nen, he would be able to output 200 points of damage (100 from the punch and 100 from Nen reinforcement). He continues by saying that Kurapika would only be able to reinforce his body with 60% efficiency and defend with 160 overall (100 from physical defense and 60 from Nen reinforcement), causing him to take 40 points of damage even if he blocked. He stresses that he is simplifying things to make his point, adding that so many other factors must be considered in a battle involving Nen. He reveals that every emotion has an effect on a person's Nen and that it can enable something beyond 100%. However, he emphasizes that using power beyond one's capacity is never a good thing and could become a fatal weakness, saying that consistent power should be Kurapika's priority. Kurapika asks if he would fare better against a master Enhancer if he were consistent as a Conjurer. His teacher replies that Enhancers are more balanced in offense and defense, but Conjurers can be difficult to deal with if they find their groove. He then poses a question, asking Kurapika if it's possible to conjure a sword that can cut anything. Kurapika says that it isn't since it goes beyond human capacity. The teacher confirms this and says that it would be preferable just to buy a high-quality sword to use, but adds that a conjured sword could be made to appear and disappear at will. His teacher says that while it's pointless to conjure things that already exist, one also can't conjure things that are too supernatural, which makes it difficult for Conjurers to be effective in combat. He tells Kurapika to be careful in thinking about what he wants to conjure since it will take an enormous amount of concentration and training. Kurapika quickly answers that he wants chains, saying that it was the first thing he thought of when he learned that he was a Conjurer. His teacher wonders why he wants chains, and Kurapika replies that there are people who need to be chained to hell. After his teacher says that he thought Kurapika was the one who was bound, Kurapika angrily scoffs at his remark and begins to walk away. His teacher then reveals that while he told him it was impossible to conjure an unbreakable chain, it is possible to come close to achieving that. Kurapika stops to listen and suddenly turns around at the revelation, asking if it's really possible. He asks what he has to do, and his teacher says that he needs to make a contract with self-imposed restrictions. Back in the present, Kurapika reveals that he becomes a Specialist when his eyes turn scarlet. Uvogin suddenly remembers the Troupe’s attack on the Kurta Clan and adds that Chrollo was particularly fond of the eyes. He describes it as a difficult task because of the Kurta's power, guessing that Kurapika is the last member and asking if his grudge is stronger than himself. Kurapika insults him and sternly assures him that he can never break the chains around him. A confident Uvogin tries with everything he has, but Kurapika easily tightens the chains around his entire body. In the flashback, Kurapika's teacher tells him that to create a contract, he needs to decide on a condition and swear that he will not break it. He adds that his ability will become stronger if the limitation is stricter. Using the equation analogy, he explains that applying Nen adds to one's power and making a Nen contract multiplies it. He warns Kurapika about the double-edged nature and tells him that if he breaks the vow, he could completely lose his Nen abilities. Kurapika says that because he intends to capture the Spiders and to find the eyes of his clan, he wants his chains to hold only them and never allow them to escape. His teacher replies that only restricting his target is somewhat weak, but as Kurapika adds that he will stake his life on it and his eyes suddenly turn red, his teacher notices a spike in his aura and urgently tells him to take the Water Divination test again. Back in the present, as Uvogin wonders how Kurapika's chain is still restraining him, Kurapika reveals that his Specialist ability, Emperor Time, allows him to utilize 100% of all Nen types.

Chapter 84 September 2nd: Part 6 (9⑥, "Kugatsu Futsuka (Roku)") is the 84th chapter of the Hunter × Hunter manga, written and illustrated by Yoshihiro Togashi. Synopsis. Uvogin is shocked to learn that Kurapika can use every Nen type, and Kurapika confirms this by using his Holy Chain to heal his broken arm instantly. As Uvogin can't believe that he healed the smashed bones so quickly, Kurapika says that he chose him as his first victim because when he fought the three Shadow Beasts by himself, it showed that he likes fighting alone. He lists the feats of Uvogin's physical strength and says that he had to fight him first to test whether his Chain Jail would work against every member of the Phantom Troupe. Kurapika then reveals that Chain Jail enforces Zetsu on the Spider it captures, and Uvogin realizes that it's the reason why he can't produce any aura. As Uvogin struggles to break free, Kurapika explains that only brute force will work and that if the strongest member of the Troupe is unable to escape, then the others will also be helpless. Uvogin again struggles to break free, but Chain Jail remains intact. He tells himself how dangerous enforced Zetsu is and says that if he can't use his aura, his abilities are useless. As Uvogin internally praises Kurapika's plan and says that he thought everything out, Kurapika suddenly appears right in front of him and strikes him hard in the midsection with a Nen-enhanced punch. Uvogin stumbles as he coughs up blood, and Kurapika says that he can kill him with his bare hands now that he's restrained. He orders Uvogin to tell him everything he knows, punching him again in the midsection and asking where the other members are, but Uvogin simply tells Kurapika to kill him. Kurapika then punches him in his left arm and asks what abilities they have, with Uvogin simply repeating that Kurapika should kill him. After several more punches, Kurapika is disgusted by the noises from Uvogin and the smell of blood, angrily asking him how he is unable to think or feel anything. Uvogin once again tells Kurapika to kill him, and Kurapika suddenly stabs Uvogin in the chest with his Judgment Chain, wrapping it around his heart and explaining that the chain will crush it if he breaks the rule he's about to set. He says that Uvogin must answer his questions truthfully, assuring him that he will keep him alive a while longer if he does so. However, when Kurapika asks where the other members are, Uvogin just smirks and tells him to get lost, causing the chain to activate and kill him. Uvogin falls with all his weight toward the ground, and Kurapika's eyes return to normal as he suddenly feels uneasy and says that he may have taken too long. He calls Melody and tells her that he will be there in an hour, with Melody glad to hear it and saying that Neon's father has been delayed. Kurapika then digs a shallow grave for Uvogin and buries him in the earth, walking toward a nearby car to head back to the city. At an Internet café, Leorio and Killua both say that they haven't received one useful e-mail or voicemail. Killua says that they don't have the intelligence network to catch the Spiders, and Gon adds that no one would give them a tip without a reward. Killua says that they would also receive a lot of fake tips if they offered a reward, and Leorio realizes that they would waste time sorting through them all. With three days left until the auction on September 6, Gon says that if they can catch just one Spider, they could interrogate them and force them to say where the others are. He suggests asking more concrete information like their whereabouts and offering a big reward, but Leorio points out that they only have the ring left and Killua adds that others were offering 8 million. After Gon replies that they will offer 15 million, and Leorio and Killua wonder where they will get the money, he holds up his Hunter License. At the Troupe's hideout, Feitan keeps watch near a tortured Owl tied to a chair. Shalnark enters the room and asks if Uvogin is back. Feitan tells him not to worry since Uvogin wouldn't die so easily. The two regroup with the others, and Chrollo says that the perpetrator uses a chain and is probably a Manipulator or Conjurer. He adds that while Uvogin can defeat almost anyone, either of these would best him in a one-on-one fight since the former could manipulate him and the latter could enhance items to nullify his strength. Shalnark blames himself for not going with him, and Chrollo tells the group that if Uvogin isn't back by morning, they will change their plans. At a pawn shop, a woman uses Gon's license to access the Hunter Website, confirming its authenticity and lending him 100 million. She tells him that the interest rate is 0% and the amount is due on September 10. An upset Killua wonders whether Gon really wants to pawn his license, reminding him that he will never get it back if he forfeits it. Gon replies that he can't sell it and that a bank wouldn't lend them as much. After Gon signs the paper and says that there's no turning back, both Killua and Leorio think that he's crazy. Trivia. Feitan is seen looking at a book by the artist .

Chapter 85 September 3rd: Part 1 (93①, "Kugatsu Mikka (Ichi)") is the 85th chapter of the Hunter × Hunter manga, written and illustrated by Yoshihiro Togashi. Synopsis. After receiving a 100 million loan for Gon's Hunter License, Gon, Killua, and Leorio decide to purchase a catalog to the Southernpiece Auction. Leorio explains that it's the leading auction house in Yorknew City and that the catalog (which costs 12 million) acts as the admission ticket. He adds that while the auctions happen between September 6-10, they will need the catalog to know when specific items are being auctioned. As they walk through the building, he reminds Gon and Killua to look things up before they get there. A receptionist welcomes them, and another receptionist asks how they plan to pay for the catalog, surprised to see that Gon is the one signing the bank transfer. The first receptionist hands him the large catalog and explains where to find the items being auctioned, also showing him his admission ticket which allows up to five people to enter during the five days. However, she clarifies that the card can only be registered under one name, and Gon happily tells her to register it under Gon Freecss. The three immediately flip to the "G" section and find Greed Island, learning basic information about the game and that the auction house has acquired and authenticated seven copies through multiple means. The entry also includes a scan of the game's instruction manual, which explains that play cannot be interrupted once the start games and that players should only start playing if they can do so for at least a week. It adds that death is a real danger and that players could become trapped in the game world indefinitely (with the creators not responsible for any resulting problems). Finally, it mentions that while the number of players isn't limited, the game is only for Hunters and is accessed by putting the disc into a JoyStation and performing Ren with one's hands beside the console. Leorio reads that a copy is being auctioned every day between September 6-8, and then two on September 10. He says that now they just need to raise the money to reach the minimum bid of 8.9 billion. Gon replies that they only have 90 million, including the diamond ring, and Killua coyly adds that they still have Leorio's Hunter License. The three decide to put an ad on a message board with a 15 million reward for the whereabouts of a member of the Phantom Troupe, hoping to force them to reveal where the rest of the members are. Gon says that they should call it Operation Lemming, and Killua reminds him that they need to be wary of fake information. Leorio points out that they can ask the people exactly where they caught sight of the Spiders. Killua worries that the Troupe may not even be in the city anymore, but Leorio is confident that the Mafia is watching every transportation route so that the Troupe can't escape with the stolen auction items. After returning to their hotel and posting the ad, the three head to the Bull Market and Gon catches sight of items on display with pieces of paper next to them. Leorio explains that it's a silent auction stand where buyers write down their offers and the person with the highest bid before the time limit wins the item. He adds that the vendors will sell the item before the time limit if the two agree on a price, likening the process to garage sales and flea markets. However, as Leorio says that these types of places are filled with mostly junk, Gon suddenly spots an odd-looking knife and the vendor says that he will sell it if there are no other buyers by noon. Killua is reminded of Leorio's haggling skills and asks him if he can acquire it right now. Leorio is confident in his ability and says that he will offer 100 since the knife looks old. The seller refuses, and Leorio immediately begins to walk away, with the seller urgently asking if 500 works. Leorio then offers 300, and after they buy the item, Killua confirms that it's a genuine Ben's knife. Gon has never heard the term before, and Killua explains that a serial murderer named Benny Delon from 100 years ago would forge a numbered knife every time he killed someone. He adds that the swordsmith made 288 in total and sold them along with his regular weapons, but explains that they are undervalued because of their criminal connection. He says that there are many people who collect them and that his father likes them. Leorio asks how much they usually cost, and Killua says that they sell for at least 5 million. They ask Gon how he knew about the knife, and he replies that he used Gyo to see a slight aura around it. Killua explains Gyo to Leorio and then uses it to look at the knife. Leorio is unable to see it, and Gon tells him that he needs to practice his Ren. Killua then realizes that they can use Nen to spot hidden deals, remembering Wing's words about geniuses unknowingly using it. Gon agrees and says that they should call it Operation "Easy Money with Nen". Leorio tells them that he will watch the bulletin board and call them if they receive any tips. Gon and Killua say that they will go look for more items, and the three go their separate ways. Back at the auction house, Milluki approaches the receptionist and asks for a catalog.

Chapter 86 September 3rd: Part 2 (93②, "Kugatsu Mikka (Ni)") is the 86th chapter of the Hunter × Hunter manga, written and illustrated by Yoshihiro Togashi. Synopsis. After Gon calls him to see if they've received any tips about the Phantom Troupe, Leorio tells him that it's only been red herrings so far, with one kid calling as a prank and claiming to be No. 6. He adds that he changed the ad to read "specify location" so that they can reduce the number of fake tips. He asks about their search for more hidden items, and Gon says that they found four with traces of aura. In a flashback, Gon spots a vase with aura around it and sees that it has a bid of 500 from someone named Zepile. He remembers Killua's words about raising the price by 250% if there's a previous bid so that things aren't drawn out in a bidding war. However, Gon isn't sure what 250% of 500 is, guessing that it's 1,750. He returns to another stand and checks out a picture that he says still looks like a bunch of scribbles. Having crossed out the initial bid of 1,000, Gon sees that his 2,500 bid was crossed out by Zepile and replaced by a new 10,000 bid. Killua calls Gon with his Beatle-07 and tells him that someone named Zepile quadrupled his bid on two items, realizing that he's using the same strategy to find rare items. Gon wonders what they should do, and Killua replies that they should put in a bid right before noon, hoping that they can win at least two items. Back in the present, Gon tells Leorio that they won three items while Zepile won the vase. As Gon and Killua head to register at an auction, a silhouette is seen watching them in the distance. At the auction house, a man apologizes to Gon and Killua, telling them that their current catalog was finished six months ago and that they are considering items for next year. He explains that determining the authenticity of items takes time, adding that most of the other auction houses will tell them the same thing. Killua says that they want to sell their items by September 5, and the man suggests visiting an antiques dealer. Gon says that they prefer an auction, and while the man doesn't advise it, he says that they can show them at a dealers market, which is explained to be an auction for middlemen who only need a certificate to participate. It's added that bidding is limited to the items on display and that items can be added at the last minute, with bidders needing to use their judgment and appraisal skills to score the best deal. The man explains that the prices will be lower than at public auctions, but that they can get a higher price compared to an antique shop. He warns them that the business is full of shady and untrustworthy people, telling them to make sure that their broker isn't lying or misinformed. The two thank him before leaving and realize that the dealers market is the only way to find out the value of the items they bought. They enter a building and decide to have the broker just take a look at the items. The man first looks at the picture and asks them if they brought it from home, with Killua saying that they found the items in an old storehouse and pretending that he got his parents' permission to sell them if they could get a good price. The man explains that the picture is a signed lithograph by Mukatolini and that he only signed the ones he really liked. He authenticates the signature and says that it could sell for around 150,000, with Gon and Killua realizing that they can make a profit of 139,000. The man then examines the handmade antique doll and praises its condition, revealing that it could sell for 300,000 (a profit of 249,500). The last item, however, the man says is worthless since the box is clearly newer than the statue itself. Killua guesses that their strategy wasn't foolproof, and Gon says that maybe the artist wasn't famous. The man explains that the carving on the statue is rough and that without even the sculptor's name as a hallmark, it's probably just the work of someone having fun a couple hundred years ago. He says that 1,500 would be a generous offer, and Gon and Killua feel bad about possibly losing 5,500. However, the man then reveals that the wood itself is valuable since modern sculptors treasure it, saying that he knows someone who would pay 100,000 for it. He agrees to buy the wood for 80,000 if they sell the other two items for 420,000. Gon and Killua ask for a minute to think it over, and the man adds that no merchant would pay more than 450,000 for them, walking away to analyze the wood. Gon thinks that it may be better to sell them than pay the auction fees, and Killua adds that they could come back after getting a second opinion. Another man suddenly enters and orders the broker to put the statue down, telling Gon and Killua that while he was telling truth about the first two items, he lied about the statue. He says that no antiques dealer would pay 80,000 for the wood and that what the man actually wants are the statue's contents. He explains that it's a wooden vault once used for tax evasion by wealthy people 300 years ago, adding that they are so well made that they are often sold by mistake. He guesses that the vault's seal is still intact, pointing to the seam and saying that only a professional can see it. He tells Gon and Killua that it should be full of riches and that the broker was probably planning to replace the contents while he pretended to analyze its age. The broker begins to stammer as the unknown man smiles and chuckles.

Chapter 87 September 3rd: Part 3 (93③, "Kugatsu Mikka (San)") is the 87th chapter of the Hunter × Hunter manga, written and illustrated by Yoshihiro Togashi. Synopsis. While Gon and Killua thank him for exposing the broker's scheme, Zepile says that he only wants twenty percent in return when they sell the wooden vault. Gon is fine with the exchange, but Killua is adamantly against it since they need every Jenny they can get. He instead offers to treat him to lunch, and Zepile quickly agrees, saying that he knows a good place and leaving the two boys confused by how easily he changed his mind. As Zepile devours several dishes of food and asks the restaurant waitress for more, Gon feels bad and says that they should pay him a commission, with Killua telling him to drop it already. Zepile assures him that the food is enough, asking the waitress for yet another dish. He then asks the two how they went about appraising the three items, and after Killua reveals that they didn't, Zepile is in disbelief and wonders how they chose those three from among all the items. Gon wonders if it's okay to reveal the truth, and Killua thinks that it's better than paying him. After they tell him the truth, Zepile is left confused by the terms Nen and aura. Killua explains that they received training to see it, and Zepile realizes that it makes sense why they chose the vault over some of the other valuable items such as trading cards and collectibles. He asks them why they're trying to make so much money, but Killua first says that they want to bid on a certain item in an auction, asking him how much they can make from the vault's contents. Zepile replies that he can't be entirely sure without knowing exactly what's inside, but tells them that it should sell for at least 100 million. He then asks them what item they want, and Killua replies that it's a video game called Greed Island. Zepile says that it will be difficult because of the expensive price, and Killua asks him how much the weird vase sitting beside him would make. Zepile reveals that it's just a worthless piece of junk, asking them why they want the game and remembering that it cost 6 billion previously. Gon replies that he's hoping to find clues in the game that help him locate his father. Killua asks Zepile why he chose the vase over the vault, and Zepile reveals that he's actually the one who made it. Gon apologizes for calling it weird, and Zepile laughs it off, adding that it's a counterfeit and that he’s vowed to buy them all back after he used to make them when he was barely making enough money to eat. Killua asks Zepile how much a real vase would make, but Zepile says that it's his turn for a question, asking Gon what his father does. Gon replies that he's a professional Hunter, and Killua quickly repeats his question, with Zepile saying 40,000-50,000 since rookie counterfeiters wouldn't get high-end jobs. Zepile mentions that he has met a few Hunters involved in antiques and trade, describing them as crazy and wondering how a kid would be able to track one down. Gon stuns Zepile by revealing that he's also a professional Hunter. Saying that it will be his last question, Zepile asks if the two need help with anything and offers to help with appraising items. Gon asks in reply why he wants to help them, and Zepile says that he first saw them as potential clients but was also flattered that they bid on the junk vase he made. Gon is adamant that it isn't junk since it's filled with his Nen, revealing that while anyone can produce aura, it's difficult to control. He explains that using Ten to surround something with aura takes concentration and training, which Zepile was able to do without even knowing about Nen. Zepile smiles and says that he can judge both buyers and sellers very well after being in the business for so long, telling the two that he wants to work with them. Gon and Killua agree and say that they can decide on what to pay him after they see his skills in action. Back in Zepile's apartment, he holds the vault between his feet and uses a hammer and chisel to carefully crack open the seal, revealing the numerous pieces of treasure inside. As Gon and Killua immediately notice the aura, Zepile inspects the pieces and says that they are genuine, guessing that it will make at least 300 million. However, he explains that dealers markets are cash only so an item so expensive won’t get any bids if it's entered at the last minute. Killua asks him what they should do, and Zepile replies that they should take it to an auction preview, which is a place where items that miss the catalog deadline are showcased. He warns them that the item may be undervalued if the dealers pull any tricks, leaving Gon and Killua confused. At the Preview Market, the gallery director named Taloon welcomes them and examines the vault's contents, praising each piece and saying that they are in pristine condition. Zepile tells him that they want to preview it for the auction tomorrow, and Taloon offers to pay 250 million for it, but Zepile quickly declines. Taloon isn't surprised since it will easily make more at the auction. He leads the three to the preview floor where a conveyor belt moves items along as people appraise them. Zepile notices three men enter the room as the vault appears on the conveyor. Everyone is impressed and believes that it's completely genuine. However, one of the men who recently entered says that while the wooden vault could be real, its contents might not be. As Gon and Killua look surprised, Zepile realizes that a new scheme has started.

Chapter 88 September 3rd: Part 4 (93④, "Kugatsu Mikka (Yon)") is the 88th chapter of the Hunter × Hunter manga, written and illustrated by Yoshihiro Togashi. Synopsis. At the Preview Market, a man claims that while the wooden vault itself may be real, the jewelry inside might not be. However, another person speaks up and says that they confirmed with their magnifying glasses that they are genuine antiques. The first man says that he hasn't checked them all and that even if they are all real, it doesn't necessarily mean that they are the same age as the vault itself. Killua asks Zepile what the man is doing, and he replies that he's sowing doubt to lower the price. Killua wonders if they should stop them, but Zepile says that it's common at previews since everyone wants the best deal. Zepile tells Gon and Killua to watch people closely and ask if they need any help. Gon approaches and stares up at the man who initially spoke. The man holds a ring in his hand and asks if it belongs to him, assuring Gon that he won't switch them since each item has a gallery tag. Zepile says that the tags wouldn't stop anyone from doing so, and the man asks him who he is. Zepile tells him that the kids are his clients and that he can confirm that both the vault and jewelry are genuine. One of the men asks if they have a certificate of authenticity, and Zepile replies that they don't, with the two men saying that it's a waste of time if they're supposed to take him at his word. The other appraisers ask him why he didn't get one, and Zepile says that they didn't have enough time before the auction and that his clients need the money before the end of the year. As he tells the appraisers that they will withdraw the item if it doesn't reach the price they want, Gon wonders why Zepile said by the end of the year and Killua tells him that the appraisers would try to scam them if they thought that they needed the money right then. Zepile then assures them that they can get an independent appraisal after the auction and that they will give the buyer a full refund if the item turns out to be fake. The appraisers seem convinced by the offer, but the initial objector again speaks up and says that wooden vaults are tricky to appraise because of the numerous doctoring methods. He explains that the contents in the vault could have been replaced, and then lists out five kinds of transplants to show his knowledge of the topic. He adds that it will be difficult to authenticate the vault as well since while the wood itself may be over 300 years old, it doesn't mean it was carved 300 years ago (called a facelift). As the other appraisers mutter amongst themselves, Zepile pushes back and says that it isn't a facelift since the glue on the seam is old and oxidized, with no trace of a second layer. The man counters by saying that the glue that was previously used melts under heat, and that it's used during appraisals as well as in scams. Zepile realizes that the man is well informed, and he continues by explaining that a forger would melt the glue and then reuse it, with the seal appearing still intact (called cauterization). The other appraisers again mutter amongst themselves and begin to further doubt the authenticity of the item. Zepile tries to assure them that cauterization would leave scorch marks and that the glue would have slight discoloration, but the man replies that said discoloration can only be seen by the naked eye and that even professionals fail to see it sometimes. The appraisers talk amongst themselves even more, and Zepile realizes that they are starting to hesitate. After some time passes and the three leave the market, Zepile blows a puff of smoke from his cigarette, upset that they had to give a lecture on scams in front of everyone and guessing that they're the type to drive down prices as much as possible. He adds that they criticize items to cause controversy, even adding poorer items while they pretend to appraise the others, and Gon remembers that Zepile warned them about people pulling tricks. He asks if they will make a good profit, and Zepile replies that they won't know until the start of the auction since it depends on the item order. He adds that there were a few good appraisers in the group and that a bidding war for the item could start among them. Gon then asks about other doctoring methods, eager to learn about them since they're like magic tricks. As Killua playfully slaps his face and reminds him that they're trying to make money, Zepile realizes why Gon is so intriguing to him, telling himself that the boy doesn't care whether something is good or bad. He remembers that Gon didn't show any sign of disapproval or greed when he mentioned making counterfeits or when the dealers were lecturing about the wooden vault. He says that Gon is just purely curious about things as long as they impress him, worried that he's walking a fine line and saying that there would be no point trying to appraise him. Zepile agrees to teach them more about doctoring methods, buying a toy in a capsule and explaining that the container is the hardest to appraise when examining a wooden vault. He adds that the carving is usually imprecise because it was designed to hide the riches inside, which is why one can't use quality to authenticate it. After opening the capsule and closing it again, Killua points out that the seam is the key. Zepile confirms this and says that it was cleverly hidden with wood shavings and paint. Killua says that if the oxidation looks the right age, it's the real thing, but Gon brings up the concept of cauterization. Zepile says that Gon is right and that the vault's contents could have been replaced and then the seam glued again since even professionals struggle to identify heat discoloration. He adds that if scammers use this technique too often, people begin to avoid sealed vaults and the market dries up. However, he explains that the scammers then showcase a real vault opened and replace the contents with cheap jewelry (called an autopsy). He says that even expert appraisers can be fooled by the scam since it's assumed that one wouldn't have it opened if it were fake. He then says that when that scam becomes overused, another one is employed that fools even the most observant appraisers. Killua asks if the vaults were sealed, and Zepile says that they were never opened and the seams weren't cauterized. They guess that the jewelry was fake, but Zepile says that it's the wrong answer. Killua then realizes that they must have taken the jewelry out through another hole, and Zepile goes through the process of ostomy in detail, explaining that they would create another hole away from the seam, replace the real jewelry with fake ones, and then patch up the hole. He says that while the process may be simple, it can fool even the most veteran of appraisers since they assume that the contents have to be real if the glue isn't discolored. Gon lets out a big sigh and says that he's impressed, and Zepile explains that it's why appraisers are so suspicious when items look too perfect. Gon's Beatle-07 phone suddenly rings with a call from Leorio, who reveals that an informant is tailing members of the Phantom Troupe and sending him pictures with his cell phone camera. He receives an image of Machi and Nobunaga with a message from the informant asking him to respond. Gon and Killua quickly make their way through the marketplace to meet up with Leorio.

Chapter 89 September 3rd: Part 5 (93⑤, "Kugatsu Mikka (Go)") is the 89th chapter of the Hunter × Hunter manga, written and illustrated by Yoshihiro Togashi. Synopsis. Leorio tells Gon and Killua that their two targets are a man and a woman, saying that he will meet them at the location. As the two boys quickly begin to leave, Zepile wonders what they want to do about the auction, with Gon saying that they trust him and Killua telling him to get them the best price. Zepile seems unsure at first, but confidently tells them to leave it to him. In a crowded area of the city, Nobunaga and Machi are seen sitting at a table as the two informants nervously watch them from the table beside them. Nobunaga asks if Uvogin could really be dead, and Machi says that it's probably the case and that they are there to find out. Nobunaga points out that Uvogin isn't stupid, confident that he can handle himself even if he's outclassed. Leorio calls the informants and tells them that he's the person who posted the ad. The girl wonders why he is so late to call them, and Leorio assures them that he is wiring the money now, confirming that the Phantom Troupe members are the two sitting behind her boyfriend. After the informants receive the 15 million and immediately leave, Machi asks if Uvogin has ever been late before, and Nobunaga reminds her that he said he wouldn't come back until he settled things with the chain user. Machi then reminds him that she said probably, and Nobunaga remembers that her hunches are usually correct, declaring that they will track down the chain user and kill him. As Leorio and Gon wonder how they will capture the two Spiders, Killua points out that they stand no chance against them. Leorio raises his voice and says that they can't know until they try, but Killua tells him to stay quiet before they're noticed, saying that he didn't realize how strong they were until he saw them with his own eyes. He adds that he has improved since his father warned him about the Troupe, but tells Leorio and Gon that both of them are just as strong as Hisoka. Leorio and Gon quickly understand Killua's point, and he adds that the two are hanging out in a public place because they want to be able to keep an eye on their surroundings. He says that they knew about the couple sitting behind them and will sense them if they move any closer, telling Leorio and Gon not to look in their direction. Killua says that he thought they were so wary because the Mafia was chasing after them, but he realizes that they are out in public because they are trying to catch prey (either the Mafia or someone else). Nobunaga senses that they are being watched, and Machi says that the people aren't amateurs, wondering if it's the chain user. Nobunaga says that he can't be sure, but reminds her that they can act as they please according to Chrollo's orders. Machi guesses that Chrollo wants the chain user to join the Troupe, but Nobunaga reminds her that Chrollo said to find him and bring him back, asking if she remembers the unspoken rule. Machi replies that it's to use any means necessary and that he can be dead or alive. Nobunaga doesn't care about her interpretation and tells her to stop telling him what to think. Machi questions his tone and says that he is the one who is telling her what to do. Killua, Gon, and Leorio all feel the increased tension between the two, with Leorio worried that they have been spotted. They assure him that they haven't been noticed, but Leorio points out that he can't use Zetsu like them.
