Episode 76 (1999) Take × Taken × Card Hell (奪る×奪られる×カード地獄, "Toru × Torareru × Kādo Jigoku") is the 76th episode of the original Hunter × Hunter anime and the 6th episode of the Greed Island OVA series. It was released on DVD on March 19th, 2003. Overview. "Gon and Killua continue playing, but some more experienced players steal the card they won. Members of the Phantom Troupe make game plans." Synopsis. Shizuku waits by herself outside of a cabin. Eventually, Shalnark comes out and apologizes for him and Kortopi taking so long. A man they had tied up inside appears severely beaten, and Shalnark explains how they were able to obtain some rare cards from him. Shizuku asks if Shalnark thinks he'll be able to clear the game, and Shalnark says he will as long as they use their personal methods. At a trade shop in Antokiba, Killua trades in four Galgaida cards in exchange for 120,000. While out in public talking about their newly earned money and Sword of Truth card, the boys notice other people watching them and realize they've likely become targets after winning the tournament. The people start following them and are not subtle about it, which amuses the boys. Killua assures Gon that even though they don't have any spell cards themselves, he believes he knows a way they can protect their cards from spell cards used on them. One of the men following the boys, Motaricke, hides behind a tree, feeling bad about trying to steal from two happy children but needing the money. He plans to use a Thief card he acquired to steal one card from the boys' collections randomly. He jumps out and confronts Gon and Killua, claiming he won't hurt them if they hand over their Sword of Truth. Killua brushes him off, completely unintimidated, and the two boys turn to keep walking away. Motaricke summons his book and uses Thief on Killua, but the card fails, as Thief works by stealing a card from its designated slot, and Killua stores it in his free slot instead. After Motarick's failure, Arka approaches, intending to use Pickpocket to steal from Killua's free slot, but his card fails as well, as Killua didn't actually place Sword of Truth in his binder at all and has nothing in his free slot. Arka then targets Gon with another Pickpocket card, but only steals a Rock card from him and doesn't turn a profit at all. Degiro steps up and has already used Clairvoyance to view Killua's book and Peek to check Gon's free slots. He intends to use Mug to steal the exact card he wants from Gon, but before he can activate it, Gon darts forward and snatches it from Degiro's hand. However, he immediately gives Degiro his card back, but warns that he'll take it for real if Degiro tries that again. Killua warns him that Gon is a professional Hunter, and although Degiro considers trying to use his card again, he ultimately decides not to. As Gon and Killua continue walking through town, they plan to obtain defensive spell cards for protection in the future. They are interrupted when a group of stronger players comes out and surrounds them. Killua identifies that they're probably Pros at the game. They steal Killua's Sword of Truth and leave. Gon and Killua plan to head to Masadora next to get spell cards of their own. Despite just being robbed, Gon remains very upbeat and excited at the idea of getting to use spells himself. The two stock up before leaving the town and purchase a simple map card. The map doesn't tell them much, so they return to the trade shop to speak with the Antokiba Trade Shop NPC, who accepts 3,000 in exchange for the location of Masadora and the route to get there. The shop NPC warns them of bandits and monsters that they'll likely run into along the way, which only excites Gon and Killua. The two quickly leave town, but are stopped by Biscuit. She asks if she can join them and tries to appear cute and shy to win their favor. However, Killua refuses, saying she'd just get in their way, and Biscuit is internally enraged, swearing to herself to ruin their friendship. She pleads with them to wait for her, but they have already started walking away. In Rubicuta, Shalnark explains the basics of Greed Island that he had learned to Shizuku and Kortopi. He also explains that, based on his findings, it's possible that Greed Island isn't actually in virtual reality, but rather taking place somewhere in the real world. If his suspicions are correct, then he believes there may be a way for them to take home as much treasure as they can, not just the three designated items of their choosing that the game promises to reward. This gets Shizuku's attention, and she happily agrees to help Shalnark collect cards. They agree to start by finding either Eye of God or Analysis to aid them and head to Masadora, and hopefully unite with Phinks and the others. Elsewhere, Feitan knocks out Latarza, and he and Phinks look through his cards. They agree to split up for a while and meet in Masadora in a week's time. They also have a contest to see who can kill the most players, but Feitan reminds Phinks to steal their cards before killing them. As he says this, Latarza dies on the ground, and his stuff disappears with him. Elsewhere, Hisoka gets a phone call from Chrollo.

Episode 76 (2011) Reunion × And × Understanding (サイカイ×ト×リカイ, "Saikai × To × Rikai") is the 76th episode of the Hunter × Hunter 2011 series. It first aired on April 21st, 2013. Overview. "Gon and Killua use Accompany on the player known as "Nigg," hoping him to be Ging. Instead, they are transported to one of his friends, Kite. Gon and Kite reminisce about how Kite saved Gon from a Foxbear when Gon was a child. Kite then explains his story about how he met Ging and became a Hunter. Meanwhile, a giant Ant feeds in a cave alone." Summary. Gon and Killua use the "Accompany" they took out of the Greed Island game to transport to the player named "Nigg." They both appear in a quite foggy-like environment with a figure leaning against a tree, fishing. Gon takes a step towards the mysterious person, but his footstep alerts them to their presence. He drops his fishing rod and assaults both Gon and Killua. He then uses his Nen ability, Crazy Slots. He draws a gun and opens fire at Gon. Killua quickly dives to pull Gon out of the way. Killua notices an injured ant on the ground. The figure quickly explains that he was preventing them from being attacked, and that the ant he shot was actually a Chimera Ant, an aggressive insect currently under a class-1 quarantine. The injured ant attacks Killua and Kite quickly kills it. The man reveals that they were actually standing next to a Chimera Ant's nest. If he hadn't intervened, a whole ant army would have attacked them. Gon says that this person isn't Ging, but is actually someone he met on Whale Island before he set out to be a Hunter. The man is revealed to be Kite, a student of Ging's. Sitting around a campfire, Kite begins to tell his story, about how he met Ging, and how he managed to track him down. Kite tells them how he used to be a thief and would steal bread with the aid of some animals. When he returned to his hideout in the sewers, he found Ging there. Kite asked Ging to train him and soon developed his own Nen. Ging told Kite to try and catch him if he can. The journey Kite went on to find Ging was long and hard. On his journey, he traveled to Whale Island in order to find clues to Ging's whereabouts. When he finally finds him, Ging says that the boy he saved on Whale Island was Gon, his son. Kite suspects that Ging has set it all up. Gon agrees and explains how Ging set up the fight with Razor. Gon asks if Kite had ever been to Greed Island and Kite confirms he was taken into the game, but wasn't sure if he used the alias "Nigg." It then becomes apparent that Ging asked Elena to make the Accompany card, if used, take Gon to Kite, and "Magnetic Force" take him to himself. His reasons being he doesn't want Gon with friends when he first meets him. When Kite asks whether Gon wants to know his father’s current whereabouts, he refuses, as he wants to find Ging without cheating. Kite tells Gon that his father is capable of being a Triple-Star Hunter, but remains a Double-Star because he's uninterested in the paperwork. Meanwhile, we see a mysterious creature in a cave eating fish, trying to recover her strength. She is the Queen, and she must give birth to the King.

Episode 77 (1999) Bandit × Monster × Biscuit (山賊×怪物×ビスケット, "Sanzoku × Kaibutsu × Bisuketto") is the 77th episode of the original Hunter × Hunter anime and the 7th episode of the Greed Island OVA series. It was released on DVD on April 16th, 2003. Overview. "Gon and Killua head toward the city of Masadora. They encounter bandits and monsters along the way. Biscuit follows them, gets frustrated with their lack of skill, and insists on being their teacher." Synopsis. Chrollo sits alone in an abandoned building with a stolen JoyStation Console running beside him. Hisoka shows up, and Chrollo smiles. Killua and Gon run through a forest, making their way to Masadora, with Biscuit following not far behind them. The boys hope to lose Biscuit when they run into the bandits or monsters they expect, assuming she'll just run away if things get difficult. The boys are surprised that she's actually able to keep up with them while they're running, and Biscuit thinks to herself that the boys have decent stamina as well, if only because of their young age. All three of them come to a stop when bandits come out from behind the trees to block their path. Gon and Killua ready themselves to fight, but the bandits immediately start begging for their help instead. Gon, Killua, and Biscuit are brought to a cabin housing a sick child in a village, where they are told of the constant illness the sick villagers have been afflicted with. Needing expensive medicine to cure themselves and their dying child, they beg Gon and Killua for money. Killua assumes that the NPCs will likely reward them if they help them out, so Gon asks how much it would cost them. A villager tells them it'll be 80,000, which is almost all the money Gon and Killua have left. Biscuit offers to help pay, but Killua tells her to be quiet, and Gon hands the bandits over 80,000. However, without being able to get the medicine until the following day, the villagers worry their child will die overnight from the cold, so Gon and Killua begrudgingly offer up their clothes for the child. Killua becomes quite annoyed when, even after giving up their clothes, the villagers still offer the boys nothing in return. Gon and Killua leave the village in just their undershirts and shorts, unhappy. However, the two continue their journey, still excited by the potential monster-fighting they might get to do. After clearing the mountain forest area, the boys reach the badlands, which they jump into. Once in the depths of the badlands, they are surrounded by cyclopes who start attacking them. Gon and Killua can dodge their attacks, but just barely. Gon can land a punch on a Cyclops, but it barely does anything. After dodging an attack, Killua can run up one of the Cyclops' arms and strike them in the eye, which instantly defeats the Cyclops and leaves behind a Giant Cyclops card that Killua obtains. Gon and Killua can clear out the rest of the cyclopes together. Biscuit watches over them from above, assessing their fighting capabilities. The boys prepare to continue heading to Masadora, but a giant lizard appears before them. Gon and Killua scream, run away and hide until the lizard leaves. After it is gone, the boys come out of hiding and continue on their way, with Killua estimating that a beast that strong must be Rank A. Biscuit defeats the lizard easily on her own, and the card she receives classifies it as only Rank E. The Phantom Troupe members in Greed Island gather at the Shiso Tree, and Shalnark informs the others of what he has learned about the game possibly not being a virtual world at all. Along their way through the badlands, Gon and Killua encounter an Hyper Puffball, who, upon seeing them, throws its whole body forward to hit Gon in the face. It bounces off the canyon walls rapidly, too fast for Killua or Gon to catch it, continuing to strike the two as it goes. Biscuit gets annoyed watching them struggle from afar and disappointed when, after ten minutes, the boys make no progress, and the Hyper Puffball bounces away from them and leaves. Soon after, the boys come across a Bubble Horse, which they find to be very stupid-looking. The horse blows a bunch of bubbles and fans them towards the boys. The white bubbles explode upon impact with them. When the boys look again, the horse is gone. Biscuit notices that the white bubbles are likely Nen-activated, as they don't explode when they hit boulders, and the red bubbles burst when the person is in a Zetsu state, as they tend to burst when touching inanimate objects. The boys notice none of this and continue on their way with the horse gone. Another Melanin Lizard chases after Gon and Killua, and they once again choose to run away. They encounter a few other unnamed monsters on their way through the badlands, but they also do not defeat them. Biscuit gets extremely frustrated watching Gon and Killua get beaten up and run away repeatedly, as she sees a lot of potential in them that they aren't doing anything with. She also worried they'll die as soon as a difficult monster or player appears. When faced with a monster in a suit of armor, Biscuit gives up staying silent any longer and shouts out to the boys to use Gyo. Gon notices how different Biscuit's personality seems compared to before. Using Gyo, the boys can see that the armor was just a decoy for the monster hiding elsewhere. Gon finds the Radio Rat controlling the armor, and it turns into a card as soon as it is spotted. Biscuit confronts the boys about why they haven't been using Gyo this whole time if they've known how to use it all along. The boys struggle to answer her, having forgotten about the ability. She yells at the boys to use Gyo again and tests them on what number she creates with her Nen. She says that she'll continue testing them, but the boys should always use Gyo if they notice something strange. Biscuit appoints herself as their coach, to which Killua initially protests. Biscuit holds up her finger while he is talking, and Gon quickly answers what number she has created, but Killua does not, and she punishes him with two hundred push-ups. Instead of doing the push-ups, Killua yells at her, and Biscuit punches a hole into the cliff beside her, silencing the boys. When she tells them she has been a Pro Hunter before they were even born, they inquire about her age. Upon learning that she is actually fifty-seven years old, Killua starts bad-mouthing her, and Biscuit punches him so hard that he goes flying. She finally introduces herself to Gon and Killua, telling them to call her Bisky. Killua is still completely against her teaching them, as they don't know her at all, and Gon agrees since they already have Wing as their teacher. Upon hearing the mention of Wing's name, Biscuit informs them that she is Wing's teacher and has the right to teach them as well. After still not completely winning them over, Biscuit summons her book and shows them cards of the monsters they couldn't defeat earlier and how low rank they were. She claims that many strong players in the game currently can defeat these monsters and will easily kill Gon and Killua as well. From a distance, Binolt watches the three of them with the desire to kill them.

Episode 77 (2011) Unease × And × Sighting (フアン×ト×シュツゲン, "Fuan × To × Shutsugen") is the 77th episode of the Hunter × Hunter 2011 series. It first aired on April 28th, 2013. Overview. "Kite introduces Gon and Killua to the rest of his team. Kite and the gang then reveal to Gon and Killua what their current mission is. Meanwhile, the Chimera Ant Queen continues to eat whatever it can get its hands on, which unfortunately leads to a taste for humans." Summary. The Chimera Ant Queen eats in the cave, already planning the birth of the King. The next morning, Gon and Killua talk with Kite. He tells them he is a biological surveyor of new species and about the Camp Tiger. This animal uses the horn on its head to pierce through its food and cook it over a fire. Killua asks about the Chimera Ants, and Kite tells him they're Class-1, a very dangerous insect. He was studying the anthill until he had to kill them all. Just then, Kite's partners Stick Dinner, Banana Kavaro, Spinner Clow, and Monta Yuras head toward the group. They are Amateur Hunters in the same field as Kite. They introduce themselves and Spinner recognizes Gon's last name as the same as Ging's. They also recognize Killua's surname, Zoldyck, for the assassin family. Learning the two boys are also pro Hunters, the group is even more shocked. They say they've been with Kite for three years and Lin Koshi and Podungo Lapoy are two other surveyors in the group. Monta shows Kite a Chimera Ant Queen claw, which is abnormally big. Kite doesn't know why it's so large but is obviously worried. It was found on the Azian Continent and a researcher named Wong told them about the new Ant species. He hired them to find more information, as they need a Hunter to identify it. The surveyors walked into a vault and under glass found an insect arm as big as a human's. This is where they got the sample to study from. Kite brings the boys along to the south of Yorknew City where the Ant arm was found. While walking, Kite sees the similarities between Gon and Ging, smiling at the thought of his friend. He thinks Gon will find Ging soon. Back at the cave, the Queen eats a bat but needs bigger prey. The group is now driving to the new location. They discuss further why the Ant grew as big as it did. Banana thinks it has something to do with the way they reproduce, phagogenesis, which is the process of eating an organism, giving birth, and the next generation gaining its abilities. An Ant can lay up to 5 eggs at a time, so the generations could grow larger with each new metamorphosis. Killua figures by the size of the claw, the Ant could be more than 6 feet tall and easily able to eat a human. In the woods, a boy named Kurt protects his sister Reina from a snake. Later, they're home with their mother, Haruna, and have dinner. He promises to keep them both safe from harm. At the same time, the Queen looks over her eggs, now more than a few dozen hanging from the ceiling of the cave. The soldiers hatch, in the form of a bat, fish, crab, etc. She telepathically orders them to find new food so she can give birth to the King. Now morning, Reina and Kurt have caught a lot of fish and head home. Suddenly, a crab Ant comes out of nowhere. Kurt tries to attack it, but it's no use. The Queen eats, happy about this new food. Kurt and Reina's clothes lay by her feet. She wants more. The surveyors and the boys make it to the beach. They scout out the area, wondering if it went into the forest. Banana uses her dog to find out where the Queen might have gone. Gon also joins in. They don't find anything and Kite suggests they look around other nearby shores. They split up and spend all day searching, but with no luck. Meanwhile, a new Ant is born, this one more human-looking than others. The Queen orders him to take the Ant army and bring her more human food.

Episode 78 (1999) Training × Raw Ore × Scissor Hands (修行×原石×シザーハンズ, "Shūgyou × Genseki × Shizā Hanzu") is the 78th episode of the original Hunter × Hunter anime and the 8th episode of the Greed Island OVA series. It was released on DVD on April 16th, 2003. Overview. "Gon, Killua, and Biscuit are stalked by Binolt, a bounty hunter. Biscuit subdues Binolt and gives him a chance to live, using him to train Gon and Killua over a two-week period." Synopsis. Biscuit instructs Gon and Killua to pretend like they are chatting with her and quietly warns them of an enemy that is behind her in hiding. She tells them he appears to be very experienced with a lot of blood lust while Gon tries to feign having a friendly chat with Biscuit. When asked what they believe their course of action should be, Gon and Killua suggest that they travel together to keep their enemy on his guard. Although Biscuit agrees it is a good plan, she tells them to separate from her for a bit, as the enemy will likely go after her instead of them if they all separate. She gives them a checkpoint to reach before circling back and then pretends to get into an argument with them and storms off on her own. After Biscuit part ways with the boys, Killua admits to Gon that Biscuit is amazing, as when she slapped him during their fake argument, she moved so quickly that Killua didn't even realize it had happened until it was over. Biscuit, on the other hand, worries about the two boys since they hadn't noticed an enemy approaching them at all and is certain they would have been dead by now if not for her. Gon and Killua reach their checkpoint and start heading back, while Binolt attacks Biscuit by cutting off one of her twintails, and she feigns being weak and shrieks. Using his Nen ability, Scissor Hands Binolt can learn about her true strength and quickly goes from laughing to being shocked. He puts his scissors away and removes his utility belt before respectfully requesting a martial arts fight with her instead. Binolt lunges at Biscuit, but she easily grabs his arm and throws him into the air before striking him with a kick, causing him to go flying and hit the ground. Gon and Killua come out of hiding when prompted by Biscuit. The two boys independently think to themselves how strong Biscuit is compared to her opponent, who had not been weak, and Gon immediately starts to address her more respectfully. Gon asks Biscuit about her motives for playing Greed Island, and she admits that she wants to clear the game and claim the reward, but that she is also after a rare jewel called Blue Planet. Gon tells Biscuit about his desire to find his father, one of the creators of Greed Island, and asks Biscuit if she knows him. She says that she has heard of him but cannot provide any details on how he might find him. Gon asks Biscuit to be their teacher, and she happily agrees, but warns that she will not go easy on them. Biscuit sits Binolt down and tells him that if he can avoid Gon and Killua's attacks for two weeks, she'll let Binolt go free, but if he fails and becomes unable to fight or leaves the small rock enclosure surrounding them, Biscuit will kill him. She also tells Gon and Killua that they are not allowed to leave the area either. Both parties agree to the terms, and the challenge begins. Binolt kneels down and shudders from his injuries, and Gon and Killua hesitate to attack him until Biscuit yells at them for wasting an opportunity. Killua gets behind Binolt and lunges at him to attack, but Binolt easily reacts, even while kneeling down, and slices Killua across the cheek with a pair of his scissors. Killua is shocked, realizing if Binolt hadn't been injured during that attack, Killua probably would have lost his eyes. Gon also tries to attack, but Binolt keeps him at bay with his scissors. The two boys circle Binolt but make no progress. Killua considers using his new electricity Nen on him. But decides against it because it hasn't been thoroughly tested yet. Instead, Killua tells Gon to rest while Killua tries wearing Binolt down with rock attacks and that Gon can tag in and out every six hours with him, hoping to win a battle of endurance against Binolt. However, Binolt believes he can easily last a week without sleep while fending off the boys while his injuries heal. Gon agrees to use rocks, but instead of sitting back, he uses his new Nen ability to punch through a large boulder nearby and shatter it into smaller boulders. He picks one of them up and uses it as a shield while he flies at Binolt, who has no choice but to dodge out of the way, with his scissors being useless against the rock. Killua follows Gon's lead and picks up one of the small boulders, and the two boys work together to attack Binolt. Biscuit is happy with their new strategy, even if they can't yet land a hit on Binolt and still have a lot of training to do; she even gets herself worked up with excitement at the idea of getting to train them to their full potential. The boys manage to trap Binolt in a field of the boulders they threw at him, with Gon able to hide and wait behind one while Killua strikes to distract him. Gon shatters the boulder he had been hiding behind, sending rocks flying at Binolt that strike him down. Killua manages to get on top of Binolt, prepared to strike the final blow, but Gon talks him out of it, insisting that they should continue practicing against Binolt for the next two weeks until they can each take him on one-on-one. Gon agrees with Binolt that both parties should rest until the following day to recover their strength. Binolt attempts to sneak over to Gon and Killua, but the boys cannot detect him coming, and Binolt returns to his resting spot. In a nightmare of when Binolt was a child, Binolt picked up a woman's wallet that she accidentally dropped. However, when he goes to return it to her, she and her partner get incredibly angry at him, likely believing he is trying to steal from them. They end up leaving Binolt completely battered and bruised in the alleyway. Binolt awakes with a startle, and Gon and Killua are already waiting for him. Gon and Binolt face off, and both can dodge each other's attacks; Killua's face-off against Binolt results in the same. Killua notices how much faster they've gotten already. After some time, Gon and Killua can almost strike Binolt alone, but stop short of doing so. Binolt admits defeat, falls to his knees, and asks to be killed. Instead, Gon thanks Binolt for fighting them and helping them improve. Binolt asks if they will let him go, and he promises to turn himself in, and Biscuit lets him go. Biscuit calls Gon flawless in her head, but also considers how much danger the kids' potential puts them in. Gon looks out over the sunrise and remembers his father's words to him, ready to move forward.

Episode 78 (2011) Very × Rapid × Reproduction (キュウソク×ナ×ゾウショク, "Kyuusoku × Na × Zoushoku") is the 78th episode of the Hunter × Hunter 2011 series. It first aired on May 5th, 2013. Overview. "The Chimera Ant Queen orders Colt to bring her more humans. She feeds on humans and gives birth to more squadron leaders, soldiers and carpenter ants. The carpenter ants build a nest. As the ants bring more humans for the Queen, Kite, Gon, Killua and the amateur Hunters search for the Chimera Ant." Summary. The Queen orders Colt to lead all her soldiers to capture more food, especially highly nutritious specimens. The narrator comments that Chimera Ants are Class-1 quarantined, carnivorous insects: once they have grown beyond two meters in length, humans do not stand a chance against them. While working the fields, a man in a village sights a swarm approaching. Befuddled, he asks what it is. When they finally see the Chimera Ants descending on them, the villagers run away in terror. Colt commands the soldiers to capture only the fully grown individuals since they provide more nutrition. Colt flies back to the Queen with his underlings. It is explained Chimera Ant Queens move around until they find a place they like; at that point, they birth more and more ants to form an army, and then carpenter ants to build a nest at incredible speed. The queen will remain in the nest until her death. Assuming one grew to two meters and began to target humans, there should be entire towns missing. However, Spinner, at the computer in a hotel room, informs Kite, Gon and Killua that she cannot find anything, and in six months, the largest group of missing people numbered ten. Gon inquires whether it is possible to look up single people individually, but she replies that there are way too many. She tries to check which areas have the highest concentration of missing people, but the data is two years old. Gon and Killua suggest they search for sightings, again to no avail. Banana begins to suspect they are getting worked up over nothing, to which Spinner agrees. However, Kite asks her to bring up the tidal data from when the arm was found. She does so, and Kite tells her to go back ten days, to locate any currents that might have carried it in that time, as he believes it could have been severed when the ant made landfall. Spinner says it might come from the Balsa Islands, including the Mitene Union, where NGL is located. Aside from NGL, there is also the Republic of East Gorteau, and there is no getting any sort of information out of those two countries. Killua asks what NGL is, and Banana replies it is an acronym standing for Neo-Green Life. It is a country founded by people who wanted to live in nature. Bringing machinery into its borders is a crime, and, according to Spinner, when in '82, three journalists attempted to trespass, one of them was sentenced to death, and the others are still in jail. The Amateur Hunters ask what NGL people would do if they were to come in contact with the Chimera Ants. Kite replies they would probably do nothing, as they let epidemics run their course rather than letting international doctors in. Even if they tried to spread the news, the underdeveloped means of transport and communication would make it impossible for them to succeed before it is too late. If that arm belonged to a Queen, she might have already constructed her nest. In the nest, Alligator challenges Colt to capture more humans than him. His assertive behavior prompts Colt to remind him that he follows only orders issued by the Queen. Alligator says he is just afraid of losing since his squadron is made up of the elite, and reckons he should let the other Squadron Leaders in. Moreover, by competing, everyone will capture more prey. Upon hearing this, Colt agrees, but remarks that the quality is also important before leaving. Alligator comments that he is too stiff, but Turtle asserts it is part of his charm, and Peggy adds that the human he once was must have been pretty zealous. Back at Kurt and Reina's home, their mother Haruna offers a bowl of broth to a deity and starts to weep for her children. On the table are the other three bowls. She wanders off into the forest despite being told to rest by the other villagers. They also mention that she searches the forest for her children from morning to night every day. While playing, some children in the village notice big insects flying toward them. After hearing a scream, Haruna runs back to the village and shields a child from Colt. Colt stops and is slightly taken aback, but after a moment, he flies over them before grabbing another male adult and leaving. The other surviving villagers tell Haruna that there's no doubt that her children were taken by those monsters, leaving the mother in shock. In another village, Turtle and his squad are seen rounding up humans for the Queen when suddenly, the soldier ants start getting shot down by humans with guns. They state that they had orders to eliminate the ants from Gyro, who they say is their king. Turtle manages to escape by rolling away in his shell. Meanwhile, Gon, Killua, Kite, and the amateur hunters plan their route to the NGL. Stick makes a pun about getting into the country with nasty rumors. When Gon and Killua ask about it, Kite tells them about D², a drug that is rumored to be manufactured in the NGL. Spinner also adds that when people try to get in to investigate those rumors, they get executed. At the same time, in a different location, Pokkle is seen talking to Balda and Pekuba about a reporter that wasn't executed after entering the NGL as they were not investigating the dark rumors. Ponzu is also with them, listening to the conversation. Pekuba adds that the reporter was secretly wearing a wire, and they were able to intercept their final message. In the recording, the reporter is heard screaming about monsters and giant bugs before the message is cut off. Although Pokkle says that it's not much to go on, he wants to see it for himself as a Hunter of Fantastic Beasts. Ponzu expresses her desire to go with them to the NGL. At first, Pokkle refuses as it would be too dangerous. Still, once Ponzu reminds them of the NGL's strict no-technology policy, she is able to convince them that her bees will be useful for communication. At the airport, Kite asks Gon and Killua if they're sure about coming with them to the NGL. They confirm, and Kite also mentions that if anything were to happen, he would prioritize saving the amateur hunters and that the kids would need to be responsible for protecting themselves. Kite adds that if he himself were to be in danger, they must leave him and escape. Back at the Chimera Ant Nest, more human bodies are added to a pile to be fed to the Queen. Alligator approaches Colt and boasts about his squad bringing in more, but the latter responds that quality is more important than quantity. Alligator takes this moment to mention that Turtle ran into a human resistance. Turtle is currently with Peggy asking for information, to which the latter tells him about weapons called guns. Turtle then asks about whether humans also have armies, and also about names. Colt and Alligator are seen listening in on the conversation. The squadron leaders receive a signal from the Queen. As they make their way over to her, they comment that the signal she sends out makes their heads hurt, and Zazan wishes that she could talk like they can. Once gathered, the Queen informs them that she will now focus entirely on giving birth to the King. Turtle asks to speak and informs her of the human resistance, but the Queen leaves the issue to them. He also asks for permission to have names and explains the concept. The Queen gives permission, and the squadron leaders are dismissed. The Queen finds their behavior fascinating and wonders if she may have human blood as well. She enters a section of the nest with three large eggs hanging from the ceiling for the Royal Guards and says that she will name them herself. Meanwhile, Gon and Killua have a talk in the airship on their way to the Mitene Union. Despite what Kite said at the airport, Gon declares that he won't run away and asks Killua what he would do. Killua just tells him that it depends and he will decide when the time comes. Kite is nearby, overhearing their conversation but does not intervene.

Episode 79 (1999) Masadora × Big Strides × Bomb Devil (マサドラ×躍進×爆発魔, "Masadora × Yakushin × Bakuhatsu Ma") is the 79th episode of the original Hunter × Hunter anime and the 1st episode of the Greed Island final OVA series. It was released on DVD on February 18th, 2004. Overview. "Biscuit teaches Gon and Killua several Nen techniques while they train in the badlands. The Phantom Troupe gets kicked off Greed Island. Genthru exposes himself as the Bomber." Synopsis. Biscuit, Gon, and Killua continue through the badlands on their way to Masadora. Biscuit continues to test their use of Gyo along the way, forcing them to do copious amounts of push-ups if they respond too slowly. They pass through a deserted village and run along a stretch of beach on their way. When they finally arrive in the strange city, Biscuit temporarily goes off alone, and the boys wait for her. Biscuit returns with her hair fixed up in a high ponytail to cover the uneven haircut she received from Binolt's attack; Gon compliments her on her new look. Although the boys are eager to purchase spell cards of their own, Biscuit has them search for a department store first. While she's busy looking around for supplies, Gon and Killua get directions on where to buy spell cards, but when they meet up with Biscuit to tell her, she asks if they are tired, and when they tell her they still have a lot of energy, she makes them go back out to train for another two and a half hours instead. After returning to the badlands again, Biscuit uses some of the item cards she picked up at the department store to generate some digging equipment, telling the boys they'll return to Masadora now. Still, this time, they must go directly through the mountains by digging through themselves. Although initially shocked, the boys quickly get busy without much complaint. However, shoveling through one mountain thoroughly strains their bodies; despite only moving about two hundred meters, they collapse onto the ground upon reaching the other side. Biscuit makes them rest holding two long poles of rope with big rocks attached at the top, saying that is how they will sleep from then on; if they let go of the rope poles, they will get crushed by the rocks. Biscuit also says she'll occasionally throw knives at the ropes to cut them, which they'll have to avoid, so they'll need to stay alert even while they're resting. Initially, Gon is worried about the idea, but Killua has no trouble resting, as he remembers when his father used the same training method with him. At night, Gon accidentally lets go of the rope in his sleep, and his rock hits him on the head. Biscuit makes him put the rock back himself before continuing. This happens several times through the night, leaving Gon worn down by the next day, while Killua is fairly well rested. Biscuit gives them a bigger rock each night. One day, Gon hits a particularly hard rock section while digging, and he can't get through with his shovel alone. Gon considers using his Nen to punch through, but instead realizes that his Nen also encompasses his shovel when he's holding it. Gon and Killua can then use their Nen to make digging a lot easier for themselves. Biscuit is proud of them for finally discovering Shu, but also knows they will wear themselves out much quicker while using it if they are not careful. Just like she predicted, Gon and Killua exhaust themselves not long after. Eventually, the boys can work much quicker through the mountains, and Gon also significantly improves at holding up his rock in his sleep; when Biscuit throws a knife to cut Gon's rope, he is easily able to dodge out of the way to avoid getting hit by his rock. The boys are excited to finally reach Masadora, but as soon as they get there, Biscuit tells them they'll be returning to the badlands. This time, however, the boys are instructed to collect monster cards by defeating the monsters they encounter. She cringes at some of their poor attempts to catch monsters, but doesn't say anything to them about it. She's also impressed by how well Greed Island is programmed to help players improve and wonders if maybe Ging worked on this project to train his son. Although it takes them some time, the boys can eventually get cards of monsters they were previously unable to defeat, like the Bubble Horse. Biscuit switches over to training the boys in defense, starting with using Ko to strengthen her attacks while making the boys block her attacks without allowing them to dodge. She teaches the boys how to use Ken to defend against her. Despite attacking very slowly, Biscuit's hit still causes Gon to fly backward, much to Gon and Killua's shock. She tries to get him to defend against her again, but using Ken tires Gon out too much, and he falls to his knees. Over the course of a month, Gon and Killua continue to train by digging and practicing to sustain their Ken for longer periods of time. By the end, Gon still gets knocked back by Biscuit's attack, but is able to remain on his feet and sustain Ken for a full thirty minutes. Biscuit then has the boys train in combat against each other, focusing on using Ryu. Afterward, Biscuit allows them a break while she explains the final stage of their training. She gets them to train for Enhancement skills, having Gon and Killua break a thousand rocks using one single rock of their own. Neither make it to two hundred before their own rocks break. Killua gets bored easily and wants to move on to Transmutation training, but is told to wait for another day. Gon and Killua also get into a rock-paper-scissors match, and Biscuit goes into a bit of the history of martial arts, as she claims rock-paper-scissors originated from martial arts. With this, Gon starts to understand what he wants his Nen ability to be and works on developing his technique Rock. The small group of Phantom Troupe members traversing through Greed Island manage to get to the island through alternative methods to prove their theory that Greed Island exists in the real world. Razor appears, approaching their group to discuss their trespassing. Razor introduces himself as one of the game's creators and tells them he has to kick them out for trespassing. Although angry about it, Phinks gladly accepts Razor's invitation to come back and fight him if they enter the game through legitimate means, reminding himself that Razor appears to be very strong. Razor expels the group using the card Eliminate, and they're teleported elsewhere. He also serves a ball of energy in the shape of a volleyball at a ship idling in the ocean nearby, destroying it. At Nickes' Alliance's hideout, Nickes announces to the members of his group that they have reached 90 of the designated cards that they need. He hypes them up for their job well done, and the crowd cheers. Genthru speaks up, wanting to tell the group something, and reveals to them that he is the Bomber. He informs everyone that he has placed bombs on each of them and that he will trade each of their lives for a designated card.

Episode 79 (2011) No × Good × NGL (NG × ナ × NGL, "NG × Na × NGL") is the 79th episode of the Hunter × Hunter 2011 series. It first aired on May 12th, 2013. Overview. "The NGL allows Kite, Gon, Killua and two other members to enter their country due to strict regulations inside their borders. Meanwhile, the second team of Hunters is attacked by the Chimera Ants whose human DNA triggers a sense of individuality that brings conflict among their ranks." Summary. Ten Hunter groups have already reached NGL, including Pokkle's team. Kite, Gon, Killua and the others are the last ones to arrive. Meanwhile, the Chimera Ant Squadron Leaders have finally adapted the naming system. It turns out that many of the Chimera Ants who have the ability to talk and are appointed as Squadron Leaders prefer to do things their own way. They have invaded many large towns and are easily able to fulfill their quota. In the forest, Yunju and two other Chimera Ants are seen attacking Gyro's men. At the NGL Border Stop, Kite's team has trouble getting through because they uphold strict policies for not allowing any kind of manufactured or artificial material inside their borders, so anything not from nature is not allowed in NGL. After many medical tests on each member of the group, only Kite, Gon, Killua, Stick Dinner and Podungo Lapoy were able to go inside NGL. Somewhere inside the NGL, Pokkle's group examines the dead body of one of Gyro's men. Suddenly they're attacked by three Ant soldiers. Pokkle uses his Red Arrow Nen ability to shoot red arrows that burns one in the face and they all run away. Ponzu trips and is almost attacked, but Pokkle is able to save her by launching two red arrows at the same time, taking out both aggressors. In the end, Gyro's base is attacked by Yunju's team.

Setl City Setl City (, "Setoru-shi") is a city within the Republic of Rokario. Overview. The city of Setl is a city that's located in the Republic of Rokario and is close to the Bilgai Desert. Plot. Chimera Ant arc. The location of Setl City appears on Killua's Beatle-07 map.

Sevanti Hui Guo Rou Sevanti Hui Guo Rou (セヴァンチ＝ホイコーロ, "Sevanchi Hoikōro") is the Seventh Queen of the Kakin Empire and seventh wife of King Nasubi. She gave birth to one son, Marayam, and one daughter, Momoze. Appearance. Sevanti is a young woman with an elaborate hairstyle, with two locks crossing on her forehead and framing her face. She wears long robes. Personality. Despite being a mother to two Kakin princes, Sevanti only cares for the well-being of her youngest child, Prince Marayam. She keeps ensuring that her son is safe and comfortable, while not feeling scared by the presence of his many guards. She also takes her daughter Momoze's guards, leaving her only with the guards sent by other queens, claiming that Marayam's safety was more important in her daughter's presence. She seems remorseful for letting Momoze's bodyguards switch over to Marayam as she acts pensive and morose. Plot. Succession Contest arc. On the day of departure, Sevanti participates in the dinner banquet and constantly accompanies her young son, smiling at the onlookers. Later, while in the Prince Residential Area, Sevanti tells the guards that her son's safety is more important than Momoze's, thereby transferring most of Momoze's guards to Marayam. She asks Momoze if she can look after herself, and Prince Momoze assures her mother she can take care of herself. Sevanti enjoys a meal with her son, lightly scolding him for spilling his food, and helps him finish the food off his plate, while oblivious to the large Guardian Spirit Beast behind them. Later, unbeknownst to Queen Sevanti, Queen Oito spies on Queen Sevanti and her son, using her borrowed Nen ability. After the unexpected death of her daughter, Sevanti pleads the case to King Nasubi, angrily blaming Momoze's six bodyguards for conspiring her death. She later sends Belerainte and Barrigen to attend Kurapika's Nen lesson the next day. She orders the guards to learn Nen effectively and report back to her. Queen Sevanti, devastated by the loss of her daughter, sits at a table by her son as he watches his beloved pet hamster. As Vergei contacts Kurapika, she's seen again playing again with her son Marayam with his toys on his play-mat. Queen Sevanti appears on an information board of all of the Kakin Queens and to what respective child they gave birth to. The following day before the time for the scheduled Nen Training meeting, Vergei voices his disdain for sending Belerainte for further Nen training to Queen Sevanti as she stays by Marayam's side and agrees with Vergei's reasoning. A Hunter and guard of Prince Marayam speaks to Vergei and Biscuit about the fact that the servants who left to perform at the banquet won't be able to return to the Nen space. Vergei explains that it's for the best since a servant backing out of the banquet at the last minute could be seen as a threat, possibly leading to Marayam and Queen Sevanti having to go back to the real room for questioning. He hopes that they will be able to stay hidden until they reach their destination. Biscuit agrees but suggests moving the Hunters to the real room in order to make things seem more natural as well as to lessen the burden on the servants. Sevanti's Royal Guards. "Active/Alive" • "Deceased" • "Former/Arrested"

Seventh Election for the 13th Hunter Chairman The Seventh Election for the 13th Hunter Chairman took place after the sixth election failed to meet the specified conditions. Location. The election took place in the Hunter Association Headquarters. Results. Re-election with the top 4 candidates.

Shachmono Tocino Shachmono Tocino (シャッチモーノ=トチーノ, "Shacchimōno Tochīno") was a Hunter and a senior member of Neon Nostrade's bodyguards. Appearance. Tocino was a man of average height and slender build who had orange hair with sideburns that curled at the end. His casual attire consisted of a green, pinstriped shirt with a black, pinstriped vest over it and a pair of gray pants along with brown shoes. When attending the Underground Auction, he wore a standard black suit with a tie (dark green in the 2011 anime adaptation). Personality. Tocino had confidence in his Nen ability when he used it against the group of potential new bodyguard recruits, However, he admitted that he did not expect to be exposed so quickly by Kurapika. He also was knowledgeable about pertinent information regarding the Underground Auction and showed a valiant effort to try and save his comrades from harm during the massacre. Background. At some point during his life, Tocino took and passed the Hunter Exam to obtain a Hunter License. He was also hired as a bodyguard for the Nostrade Family. Plot. Yorknew City arc. Along with five other applicants for the Nostrade Family bodyguard position, Tocino waits in a room at the Nostrade's Mansion. The butler plays a video introducing the supposed boss who details the requirements for the position. The applicants are given a data card with specific items listed on it and instructed to retrieve one of them. When Basho tries to leave but finds that the door is locked, they are all suddenly ambushed by eleven hooded assailants wielding guns and swords. During the assault, Tocino sticks with the applicant Melody until Kurapika holds him hostage with a knife and gives him three seconds to stop the assailants. Once Tocino yields to Kurapika's demand, the assailants suddenly fall empty to the floor. When Tocino asks how Kurapika knew that it was him, Kurapika explains that he figured it out after observing the assault from above on the chandelier, having deduced that he was in control of them since he was the only one not getting attacked. He also describes the irregularity of their movement and guesses that they can only follow simple commands, having guessed that the user was an Emitter and would need to be in the room given the amount of aura being consumed. Impressed by Kurapika's deduction, Tocino confirms it and introduces himself as a Hunter and an employee for the Nostrade Family. He points that he is Kurapika's senior and asks him to put away his dagger, admitting that he was ordered to test them with real threats. After sitting down, Tocino also admits that he didn't expect to be exposed so quickly, saying that the four of them should be able to easily escape the mansion. This bewilders the applicants as Tocino gives a small smile. Kurapika chuckles and tells Tocino that his attempt to cause confusion was the wrong choice since he can easily find out whether there are any more infiltrators. Kurapika then uses his Dowsing Chain on the other applicants and eventually determines that Squala is the other one. Squala tries to defend himself, but Melody supports Kurapika's claim by explaining that he and Tocino both have heartbeats that are typical of a liar. After taking the situation into his own hands, Basho uses his Great Haiku ability on the others. After Tocino repeats that he is an infiltrator, Squala eventually admits the truth as well. On August 31st, Tocino, Dalzollene, Linssen, Ivlenkov, and Squala escort Neon Nostrade by airship to Lingon Airport and then make their way by car to Yorknew City. On the night of the Underground Auction, Dalzollene instructs the bodyguards at the Hotel Beitacle on what they have to do during the auction. Tocino, Baise, and Ivlenkov are assigned to bid on the mummy. Inside the Cemetery Building, after Baise wonders why so many of the Mafia members are attending the auction in person, Tocino explains that they can earn points for their family and that the community receives 5% of the proceeds as a commission. He adds that it's a way for them to show how wealthy they are, explaining that some families even end up bankrupt after getting into a bidding war. At the start of the auction, a short man and a tall man walk out onto the stage. The short man approaches the podium and quickly welcomes the attendees before saying that they can skip the formal greeting, announcing that they will all die. The large man suddenly begins shooting bullets from his fingertips and massacring dozens of the auction attendees. During the onslaught, Tocino tells Ivlenkov and Baise to get behind him as he summons his Eleven Black Children to act as a shield. However, the puppets are quickly ripped apart by the bullets, and as Tocino himself is mortally wounded, he realizes that the shooter is using Nen bullets and is also an Emitter. As Tocino yells for Ivlenkov and Baise to escape and says that they need to tell the others what's happening, a bullet hits him directly in the head as he is ripped apart. His corpse is then inhaled by Shizuku's vacuum cleaner. Kurapika briefly mentions Tocino, Baise, Ivlenkov, and Dalzollene to Neon as bodyguards who were killed at the auction. However, Neon shows no remorse for them and only asks whether the mummy was stolen. When Kurapika checks the Hunter Website, he sees pictures and descriptions for Neon, Tocino, and the other bodyguards (besides himself and Melody). Abilities & Powers. Tocino has all the benefits granted by his status as a Hunter. Nen. Tocino is an Emitter. He can also use Manipulation to give orders to the puppets he creates, although he might be unable to give them more than one.

Shadow The Shadow (, "Kage") was the Hunter Association's secret Special Operations squad, which carried out covert missions across several different countries. Members. Original. Jed is the only member of the original Shadow to be named, although at least eighteen other members' silhouettes were seen. It is unknown exactly how many members there were in total. All original members of the Shadow are deceased.

Shadow Beasts The Shadow Beasts (, "Injū") were a special group consisting of the ten most powerful Nen users within the Mafia Community. Overview. Under the direct command of the Ten Dons, every beast had their own unique code name that derives from the animal that inspired them to develop their Nen abilities. Each beast was chosen by their Don and assigned to the team to carry out the group's orders. The group ceased to exist after the Phantom Troupe killed them all out without mercy over the course of a single night, with the exception of Owl who was taken to be interrogated and whose ability Chrollo stole. Plot. Yorknew City arc. After a large number of Mafia members and auction clients in Yorknew City are massacred by the Phantom Troupe, the Ten Dons quickly dispatch the Shadow Beasts to deal with them, not knowing who they are. Uvogin faces four of them by himself, and quickly defeats them. Besides Owl, the remaining Shadow Beasts are subsequently killed, causing the Ten Dons to place bounties on the Spiders' heads and to hire professional assassins to eliminate them. Illumi later kills the Ten Dons and controls their corpses to restart the Underground Auction and cancel the bounties on the Troupe.

Shaiapouf Shaiapouf (シャウアプフ, "Shauapufu"), nicknamed Pouf (プフ, "Pufu"), was a butterfly-humanoid Chimera Ant and one of the Chimera Ant King's Royal Guards. He also served as one of the main antagonists of the Chimera Ant arc. Appearance. Unlike the other Royal Guards, Shaiapouf bore a more human resemblance. He looked like a young adult, with a tall and lanky frame, thistle purple skin, and short dark blond hair, covering up his forehead and ears. The only insect parts that Pouf had were his multi-colored butterfly wings and antennae. He wore a frilly white shirt, black pants and a pair of black shoes. Personality. Shaiapouf posited himself as the calmest and rational of the three Royal Guards, often speaking about the importance of logic and reasoning, more than his emotions. However, his intense devotion to the Chimera Ant King clouded his judgment. He held a preconceived absolute ideal to live up to, with no room for amendment. Pouf also held the King to a similarly impossible ideal, manifesting in mad fanatical monologues and treacherous action when it appeared that his lord was being led astray. He was often seen reading books and playing his violin; he usually played this instrument while talking or whenever he was agitated. Shaiapouf vehemently loathed Komugi. He believed the woman to be holding back the King from his supposed right to world domination, as the pinnacle of evolution. A master of psychological games and subterfuge, Shaiapouf was willing to deceive, betray, and murder anyone in order to preserve his image to the King. In crises involving the Chimera Ant King, Pouf forsook delegated duty and acted solely according to the sway of his emotions. Shaiapouf was indeed the most irrational of the three Royal Guards; manic and demented by his magnification and love for the King. In the end, Shaiapouf became loyal only to his "version" of the King, not Meruem himself, and would always try to change the King to that version while getting privately enraged when it did not happen. Of the three Guards, Pouf was the only one genuinely disloyal to the King himself and grew the least out of the three. Even though he had absolute love and devotion towards the King, he still held Neferpitou and Menthuthuyoupi rather close. He was pleased to know that Menthuthuyoupi had the same negative sentiment towards Komugi. Upon seeing Menthuthuyoupi's dead body, Shaiapouf was left in shock and mourning for his fellow comrade and was in a frantic state of mind when trying to look for Neferpitou, demonstrating the bond he shared with them. Background. Just like the other Royal Guards and the King, Shaiapouf seemed to have no memories of a past life, suggesting that he didn't originate from an existing consciousness. He was named personally by the Queen. Plot. Chimera Ant arc. Shaiapouf is the second Royal Guard to be born. After hatching, he reaches Neferpitou at the top of the nest, and, sensing their emotions, suggests they wait and see what their enemies are planning. His ability to divine their thoughts perplexes Neferpitou, who asks him to introduce himself. Shaiapouf complies and informs him Menthuthuyoupi will be born soon. When he does, Shaiapouf is playing the violin. Hearing the Queen scream, the three Royal Guards understand the King is about to be born. Kneeling down, they pledge their loyalty and service to him and take him to the top of the nest, where they have prepared his meal, which Shaiapouf livens up with his violin. When the King wants to eat rare prey, he and the Royal Guards leave the nest, with Shaiapouf carrying him. They stop briefly so the King can hunt three humans, then reach the Royal Palace of the Republic of East Gorteau. They escort him as he massacres the guards and makes his way to Ming Jol-ik. Shaiapouf explains to his liege that among humans the incompetent rise to power through heredity or connections. The King kills the dictator and the Chimera Ants install themselves in the palace. Shaiapouf advises Neferpitou to leave the assassin who is interfering with the "Sorting" to Leol's Squad, having recently given its high-ranking members Nen abilities. He also puts the 5,000 survivors of the initial "Sorting", along with Cheetu, Welfin, and Bloster into cocoons to the same end. When the King starts playing strategy board games to hone his skills in analysis, Shaiapouf watches over him while selecting the games and reading about them. Six days prior to the "Sorting", he commends the King on his extraordinary progress on the games before introducing him to Gungi, adding that East Gorteau has yet to lose a world championship. He reads quietly while the King learns the rules in preparation to play against Komugi, the girl who holds the title of World Champion. After the King notices Komugi is unconscious, Pouf explains to him why she had fainted. Shaiapouf is surprised that, no matter how many games they play, the King cannot win, and confesses his unease to Neferpitou. During one of their games, the Royal Guard notices Komugi hesitate for the first time. When the King enquires about the reason, he thinks to himself that the wrong answer would result in Komugi's death. Although the King proclaims to be bored with her explanation, Shaiapouf observes that he had never listened to someone for that long before. When the King tears off his own arm as an apology for using petty tactics, Pouf reacts in horror. He bandages the King's arm, but his concern is rewarded with a lash from the King's tail. Shaiapouf demands that he at least let Neferpitou tend to him as he plays, and that should the King not be satisfied with his concession, he should chop off his head. The King caves when Komugi refuses to play until he is healed, so Shaiapouf is sent to call Neferpitou. Since Neferpitou is unable to use their En and "puppets" for the duration of the surgery, Shaiapouf takes lookout duty and activates his own En, which reaches no farther than the central stairway to the second floor. Unbeknownst to the Chimera Ants, Knov, who was in the process of infiltrating the palace, is terrified by the sight of Shaiapouf's aura When, two or three hours later, the operation is completed, Neferpitou reactivates their puppets and En and perceive the presence of Palm, who infiltrated the palace by tricking Bizeff. The woman stabs herself, but, intrigued by her aura, Neferpitou saves them. They and Shaiapouf make her into a new type of human-Ant soldier where they attempt to sever the connection between her memories and her emotional responses. Two days before the "Sorting," the King, noticing Komugi's exhaustion, goes back on his word and allows her to take a break. Concerned that she will become a liability in the future, Shaiapouf considers killing her, but upon the realization that doing so would forever deny the King any victory over her, he bursts into tears and swears to end his own life after helping the King attain complete dominion. He later tries to update the King on the "Sorting" and "Unification" projects, but he is left in charge of the matter and impatiently chased out. He sits next to Menthuthuyoupi, who suffered the same fate. The latter is optimistic that the King will soon defeat Komugi, but Shaiapouf states that both are progressing at astounding speed and that he can no longer predict the outcome. Two nights before the "Sorting", the King summons his Royal Guards and asks them what is his name. Shaiapouf states he is the King, and that after the "Unification" he will be the only one associated with that word. The King objects that it is a title, not a name. Shaiapouf suggests choosing his name after the "Sorting." Sensing his unease, he urges him to confide in them. The King starts talking about Komugi's awakening to Nen, the fact he bothered to learn the girl's name upsetting Shaiapouf. The Royal Guard silently begs him not to repent his actions as he speaks of "other strengths," but halfway through his speech, the King smiles a frightening smile and declares his own strength, violence, the ultimate power in the world. When he leaves, Shaiapouf bursts into tears, declaring himself a failure as a Royal Guard for insulting the King with his thoughts. Menthuthuyoupi remarks he simply thinks too much while Neferpitou admits the King did change since the arrival of Komugi, both of which Shaiapouf concedes. Menthuthuyoupi suggests killing the girl if he deems her dangerous, to Shaiapouf's chagrin for having had the same idea. 25 hours before the "Sorting," the Royal Guards discuss what to do when the project starts. Shaiapouf states the King wants to participate himself and that one of them will have to watch over him subtly so as not to aggravate him. By process of exclusion, Shaiapouf resigns himself to take care of it himself. Neferpitou alerts the other Royal Guards he can no longer feel the aura of their enemies. A few hours later, as the first battery of citizens marches towards the palace, Shaiapouf flies into the highs and releases his scales in the direction of the gathered citizens, hypnotizing them so they will follow the military's command more easily and won't flee when the "Sorting" starts. That night, the Royal Guards gather on the roof. With access to the second floor barred to all, Shaiapouf suggests Menthuthuyoupi guard the central staircase. The Royal Guard comments on the King's bad mood, which he attributes to losing in Gungi. Shaiapouf, however, seems to think differently, but is unwilling to use Spiritual Message on the King, as that would be an unforgivable insult. The changes he senses in his liege elicit terrible, unchecked anxiety and dread in him. About two minutes before midnight, Shaiapouf senses Neferpitou's En disappear. Seeing it climbing upwards, he spots a dragon of aura coming down from the sky, and two men riding it: Zeno Zoldyck and Isaac Netero. When the dragon breaks into a rain of arrows, Shaiapouf dashes to the throne room, ignoring the King's ban. Upon reaching it and finding it empty, he smiles out of self-contempt, because he did not know where the King was; even worse, he admits he knew he would probably be in Komugi's quarters, but did not want to accept it, and so rushed to the King's room anyway. He considers himself a traitor, scum, and to have failed as a Royal Guard, his self-deprecatory musings punctuated by frenzied dancing, tears, and laughter. When, a few seconds later, he pulls himself together, he resolves to go to the King but finds Morel standing in front of him, his despair having hampered his awareness. He immediately tries to fly away but bounces off the Hunter's Smoky Jail. Realizing Morel won't let him go, Shaiapouf scatters his scales and activates Spiritual Message. As he introduces himself, he analyzes Morel's mental state. He envelops himself in his wings, claiming he will be reborn soon. He does not even reply when Menthuthuyoupi calls him out, continuing to study his opponent while inside the cocoon, and determining that his unwavering confidence and resolve will inhibit his decision-making, he begins escaping Smoky Jail by dividing his body into trillions of microscopic segments which little by little slip through the particles of smoke with his Beelzebub ability. While recomposing himself outside of the prison, he thinks that Morel's hesitation is proof of his excellence as a soldier. Against Shaiapouf's predictions, Morel attacks the pupa and, finding it seemingly empty, deactivates Smoky Jail. The Royal Guard, who is standing right outside, chuckles. He declares he expected Morel to hesitate for fifteen minutes, during which time he could have killed some of his allies. When the Hunter states he underestimated him, Shaiapouf retorts he actually gave him too much credit and demonstrates Beelzebub. He taunts Morel for his decision, cryptically confessing that the confinement was problematic for him. The Hunter's Smoke Troopers break up some of the segments, but they recompose themselves before escaping. While Morel tries to figure out where to head next, Shaiapouf reforms himself behind him. The Royal Guard kicks him down and flies away with his giant pipe, cackling. Shaiapouf throws the pipe into a river and thinks to himself that if Morel hadn't been so hasty, even if the Royal Guard's clone might have killed some of his allies, if any of them was as skilled as the Hunter they would eventually determine the true nature of his ability and try to seek out his true body, leading to Morel squashing him when he was at his most vulnerable. Shaiapouf splits up again and sends his segments to scour all over the palace in order to assess the situation and find the King. He is concerned about Menthuthuyoupi when he sees an aura explosion, but, wondering why Gon does not attack Neferpitou while the latter is healing Komugi, he recomposes himself and tries to sneak behind the Hunter. Neferpitou, however, stops him, claiming Gon was aware of his presence and would have killed Komugi if he had closed in with murderous intent. Shaiapouf dismisses his fear as irrational, arguing that Gon would most likely want to save her, but he is silenced by the boy. When his attempt to hypnotize Gon is seen through and Neferpitou implores him to obey the Hunter, Shaiapouf expresses his frustration. The other Royal Guard explains they are doing it for the sake of the King. Shaiapouf agrees to stay put if they tell him what happened, implying that if Neferpitou fails to relay where the King is, there will be a bloodbath. Pouf decides to leave the situation to Neferpitou but Gon didn't allow him to leave. Neferpitou successfully reveals the King headed south. Shaiapouf leaves a clone of his main body so Gon will not grow suspicious, while his core and 6/7ths of his cells head to the King. On the way, Shaiapouf finds Menthuthuyoupi in the meat orchard. While he reforms himself, he explains the situation to him, realizing how much he has grown up. To test him, he asks him what they should do. Menthuthuyoupi replies they should go to the King's side, and the two depart. Elsewhere, a miniature clone is controlling a newly born Chimera Ant Palm into killing Killua, but the hybrid rebels and crushes the segment instead. The failure frustrates Shaiapouf, who however concludes soldiers with both memories and emotions will be necessary at some point, while Neferpitou will cease to be. In a third part of the palace, Knuckle confronts Shaiapouf's shell, who accepts to fight him, but reveals in fact that he is a clone in order to find out why Menthuthuyoupi's opponent survived. His honesty convinces Knuckle, but not Gon, who demands proof. Worried by Gon's unwavering determination, he states he cannot provide it without putting himself in a very precarious position. He declares Gon will have to decide what to do next and separates himself, telling Knuckle he will wait for him at the entrance of the palace for ten minutes. Shortly after, Shaiapouf and Menthuthuyoupi see a rose-shaped pyrocumulus cloud. Filled with dread, they speed up their advance, while the Royal Guard's clone, who has been reached by Knuckle, briefly shows the true form of a Chimera Ant and leaves the place without explanation. The two Royal Guards arrive at the epicenter of the explosion. At Menthuthuyoupi's suggestion, who rouses him from his shock, Shaiapouf splits himself up and searches around the crater. Menthuthuyoupi's scream fills him with despair before he even sees the King's mangled body. Discovering he is still alive, Shaiapouf feeds him his own cells, which resuscitate him. The King's praise leaves him in ecstasy, and when Meruem reveals his name, they are filled with unconditional motherly love, becoming equal to Chimera Ant Queens. Soon the King is well again, and even more powerful than before, with the two Royal Guards now sharing an empathic bond with him. Thanks to it, they become aware of his confusion and realize he is suffering from amnesia, which Shaiapouf attributes to the explosion. Estimating the King will not make it back to the palace before 20 minutes, Shaiapouf sends his clone back to get rid of Komugi. However, the King grows wings and carries the two weakened Ants, with Shaiapouf reckoning he will arrive at the palace in no more than five minutes. When his clone enters Komugi's room, it finds it empty. It ambushed by Knuckle, who, hidden with Meleoron's ability, activates Hakoware, causing A.P.R. to appear next to the Royal Guard's main body. Having realized this, the King and the Guards hurry to the palace. Shaiapouf watches in awe as the King attacks A.P.R. with a powerful aura blast. When Menthuthuyoupi admits he knows of the ability because he spared its user, Shaiapouf rebukes him for not removing a threat to the King due to his personal feelings. The King, however, forgives him and states the three of them are linked in mind and body. Shaiapouf wonders if the King is implying he can sense his guilt, but resolves to carry on even if he should be executed. He splits his clone and sends his segments to scour the palace. He ignores Knuckle when he appears in front of him. He surmises that the Extermination Team will think he returned to kill Meleoron, who might be hiding Komugi, and protect him instead of her since they have no reason to suspect his real goal. He sees Palm open the entrance to the underground hangar, and understands they want to disperse his segments, but then notices Killua carrying Komugi. Out of time, he decides to target her. However, his clone cannot keep up with Killua's Godspeed. Splitting up into multiple segments, he chases Killua away from the palace while promising to spare him. As he planned, Komugi begins to struggle, slowing Killua down for a moment, which Shaiapouf seizes to reform himself and strike. However, Killua manages to avoid his attack. After knocking Komugi out, he draws a circle with his aura, promising Shaiapouf to kill him if he steps inside. The clone attacks but Killua incinerates its cells with an electric shock. In the meanwhile, Shaiapouf rejects the King's offer to assist him and shows him the rows of hypnotized humans in front of the palace, trying to remind him of his supreme goal of ruling overall life. To his dismay, the King states something is missing. Shaiapouf remembers the Gungi board in the throne room. He splits his clone into segments, which he sends to dispose of it. While his main body guides the King through the meat orchard, Shaiapouf has some of his segments remove the Gungi board and pieces, while others look for Welfin and spy on Killua, Komugi, and Palm, who is aware of Beelzebub's weakness. Soon, his segments find Welfin and have him phone Neferpitou, telling them he rescued Komugi. Shaiapouf alters his facial structure and voice to mimic hers and trick the Royal Guard. With her Wink Blue, Palms discovers that Neferpitou is about to attack Gon. Shaiapouf offers to stop Neferpitou if they give him the girl, but Killua burns his segment. Shaiapouf and Menthuthuyoupi agree not to remind the King of Komugi. In discussing the "Sorting", Shaiapouf remembers he has not yet hypnotized the latest battery of humans. The other Royal Guard mentions Neferpitou, jogging Meruem's memory of them. While the two Royal Guards carry out their tasks, the King intends to chase down the Extermination Team. Shaiapouf objects that he would be by himself, but Meruem's outstanding aura output convinces him he would never be beaten. The King uses En and disappears, then A.P.R. also does. He returns with Knuckle and Meleoron, whom he has rendered unconscious so as to question them later. He adds that he sensed two more, and Shaiapouf realizes one of them must be carrying Komugi. Shaiapouf comes up with the idea to make a competition with Meruem and gain some time. He suggests that he and Menthuthuyoupi look for Neferpitou, while the King will start to hunt down the intruders after he is done spreading his scales. In the interest of fair play, he requests that the King use En only once more. Meruem accepts, on the condition that if he wins, they will tell him their secret. The two Royal Guards depart and, confident Neferpitou is about to return, Shaiapouf tells Menthuthuyoupi to just wait by the tower. As he spreads the scales, Shaiapouf notices his power has diminished due to giving most of his body to the King, and that Neferpitou's puppets have disappeared, which leads him to wonder how fierce a battle they are involved in. When he finishes, he returns to the tower and finds Menthuthuyoupi's corpse. In a panic, he tells the King to suspend the game. However, the latter states that it would result in his victory. Seeing he has drawn a Gungi board on the floor, Shaiapouf accepts to continue and goes looking for Neferpitou. Shortly after, he starts coughing up blood. Meruem senses his shock, but Shaiapouf pretends nothing is wrong. Meruem uses his En again and finds Welfin, whom the Royal Guard fears for what he might say. Before he can dispose of him, Meruem senses his emotions, which causes Shaiapouf to feel awed by his power again; and yet, anxiety keeps welling up inside of him. He claims Welfin is involved in his secret, so the King cannot question him. Meruem is about to react violently upon hearing Welfin's malice towards him may be linked to Shaiapouf, but the latter's insane devotion gives him pause. When the King is on the verge of eating Welfin, out of sheer terror the former Squadron Leader utters the word "Komugi". Meruem recovers his memory, much to Shaiapouf's dismay, who falls to his knees and bursts into tears upon feeling the immensity of Meruem's affection for her through their psychic bond. He finally admits to Meruem that Komugi was the secret he tried so desperately to hide. Expecting to be executed, Shaiapouf is surprised when he's told to find Neferpitou; he was also told to interrogate Knuckle and Meleoron, if they have a clue on Neferpitou's whereabouts, and allow them to go free. When Welfin states that Gyro is the only one he would call his king and that Meruem was his enemy, Meruem states that he had hoped Welfin would find his king and adds that he hopes if Welfin can return living as a human; Shaiapouf begins to cry upon hearing those words. He is later seen to have finally fallen down to the floor, unable to fulfill the task he was given by his King, and succumb to the Miniature Rose's poison. 13th Hunter Chairman Election arc. When the effects of Pouf's scales terminated, 46,613 civilians died from bodily failure, Soon after the King's death, Pariston Hill sent blimps to recover the 5,000 cocoons created by Pouf. Ging Freecss estimates the human-Chimera Ant hybrids to have hatched by the time of the 8th round of the chairman election, with each of them being capable of using Nen. Abilities & Powers. As a Chimera Ant Royal Guard, Shaiapouf is one of the four most powerful Chimera Ants in Meruem's colony, and one of the strongest characters in the series. Colt believed him to be capable of defeating Chairman Netero, considered the world's strongest Hunter in his prime and by some the most powerful Hunter even in his old age. Although Shaiapouf is endowed with superhuman strength and durability, his main weapons are his Nen abilities, the capacity to fly at high speed, and his aptitude for manipulation. Coupled with Beelzebub, his physiology allowed him to survive with only a fraction of his original body mass after donating 6/7ths of his cells to the King. However, this caused his power to drop considerably. Flight: Shaiapouf's butterfly genes grant him flight capabilities with the aid of his wings. He can fly at very high speed, which he can further enhance with aura. Immense Strength: Shaiapouf, being a Royal Guard, has an immense level of strength, he was able to knock down Morel with a surprise kick and stole his weapon. He broke several big rocks with ease, with a series of punches and kicks, as he was opening his way to see the King after Zeno's Dragon Dive started to fall upon them. He also was confident that he would be able to kill Gon with a sneak attack, and kill Welfin, before he could say anything dangerous to Meruem. Pouf also stated to Meruem that if he had his full strength, he would be able to easily kill the Extermination Team. Immense Speed and Reflexes: While flying, Shaiapouf can cover long distances within short periods. He is fast and agile enough to evade the aura shards from Zeno's Dragon Dive. He was able to strike Morel from behind and take his giant pipe before the latter could react. It seems he can use his aura to accelerate. Pouf was also fast enough to almost strike Komugi while Godspeed Killua was carrying her. Unfathomable Stamina: Shaiapouf did not sleep for at least a whole week before the "Sorting" and never showed any signs of fatigue. Unfathomable Durability: Shaiapouf managed to survive a head-on tail whip from Meruem, ending up with just a bruise and some bleeding on his face, while taking little damage from being sent crashing into a wall. Even as a clone, he was able to easily withstand an attack from Knuckle, and endure the intense scorching heat of a nuclear explosion minutes after the detonation.
