After Oito finishes her observance in Marayam's room, she manipulates the cockroach towards Prince Momoze's room. She watches as one of Momoze's guards suffocates her while she is sleeping. Horrified, Oito screams and demands that they should go over to the room and help Momoze. However, since it is not easy to reach the prince, they are too late. Military men arrive to take Momoze's body while Oito slumps on the bed, crying. When Babimyna asks why the queen would risk harm to herself by helping, Oito only answers that she has nothing to say to him. After a while, Oito resumes her observation to the other Princes, saying that she is doing it for Woble. When Kurapika passes out from fatigue, the same happens to Oito. They regain consciousness only 9 hours later. Kurapika asks Oito to keep investigating with the ability he gave her, but when he requests she visit the 4th Prince instead of the 12th, she grows suspicious of his motives. He explains his reasons and once more pledges the Queen and the prince's safety is his first priority. Oito is unconvinced at first, but when Woble reaches for Kurapika, she accepts to do as he says. With the aid of a blueprint of the floor, she directs the cockroach towards Tserriednich's apartment, but his Guardian Spirit Beast appears and kills it, causing Oito to scream in terror. After Kurapika dismisses the guards who came running, she tells him what she saw. She then asks Kurapika to teach her Nen, only to be told she can already use aura as a consequence of being exposed to his ability. While Kurapika begins his Nen lessons with the princes' bodyguards, Bill supervises Oito's Nen training. After Silent Majority kills Barrigen, Kurapika takes Oito to another room. Fifteen minutes later the lessons resume. As Bill observes the students for Kurapika, Oito asks Shimano why she is staying, as the compensation could not be worth the risk. The two begin to chat about their respective families. Soon after talking with Shimano, Oito continues her Nen training under Bill's tutelage. The following day, Silent Majority makes another victim during the lecture. Hearing him scream, Oito grabs Woble while Bill locks them in her bedroom. On Monday morning, Oito listens to Kurapika and Bill discussing the massive surge of rumbling aura from one of the odd-numbered rooms. She then moves back to the main bedroom with Woble, where Kurapika opens the Aura Nodes of four of his students with Stealth Dolphin. She falls asleep next to her daughter before the end of the session. The following day, at 11:30, she feels the surging aura again. Abilities & Powers. As a spouse of Nasubi's, Oito has moderate political and economical power by proxy, albeit she is the lowest of all wives. She has proven to be highly intelligent, developing a strategy that would force Halkenburg to spare Woble's life should he win the Succession War, surmising other princes or queens may have thought the same, and seeking to hire those who wish Halkenburg harm, deducing they might know his mental processes to an extent. She successfully passed off as Halkenburg in an attempt to hire any such people. She also demonstrated quick thinking when she pretended to be disgusted at the sight of a cockroach so her guards could catch it. Nen. As a consequence of being exposed to Kurapika's Nen ability, Oito's Aura Nodes were opened and she became capable of seeing and sensing aura. Thanks to him, she was briefly able to utilize Sayird's Nen ability. According to Bill, she is likely to be a slow learner.

Omokage Omokage (オモカゲ, "Omokage") was the first #4 member of the Phantom Troupe, who was later replaced by Hisoka. Appearance. Omokage's appearance was pretty archaic Gothic. He had long, flowing silver hair and turquoise eyes. He wore a piercing in his lower lip, eyebrow, and ears. Omokage's clothing was reminiscent of the Kurta's in design, although not identical as it was much darker. He wore dark-colored pants, a dark cape with white patterns over a long black top, and black shoes. His spider tattoo was located on the palm of his right hand, with the number 4 on the spider's abdomen. Personality. Omokage was depicted as a cold, twisted man with the sole desire of making puppets out of people. However, despite killing and making a puppet out of his younger sister Retz, he still cared for her to some degree, and would become angry and distressed at the insinuation that his sister was sad with her life as a puppet. He claimed his love of puppets was sparked by his sister. He believed that life only had meaning if it was eternal, and thought of humans as they were to be rotten and imperfect. He often remarked on the beauty of his puppets, and claimed to take pleasure in creating combinations of different types of people and eyes, like matching Kurapika's eyes with Pairo's body and Gon's eyes with Illumi. He also had a superiority complex, as he called other people "humans," and himself the "Divine Puppeteer." Omokage was also obsessed with creating and witnessing tragedy in different ways, especially through his puppets. He even stated that the Kurta Clan massacre was an incredible day, and that he loved killing them. Background. When he was younger, he worked as a doll maker, with Retz as his assistant. Later in his life, Omokage was once member #4 of the Phantom Troupe, joining the group before the Kurta Clan massacre. Two years before the beginning of the series, he was replaced by Hisoka, who defeated a Soul Doll that had the appearance of Omokage. The only reason Omokage joined the Phantom Troupe was to make Soul Dolls out of the other Phantom Troupe members; once he completed his collection of Soul Dolls, he left the Phantom Troupe. Plot. Phantom Rouge. "Note: Events occurring in the movie do not constitute canon material." Omokage first appears in in Kurapika's vision after Omokage's Soul Doll of Pairo has stolen Kurapika's eyes. Through his eyes in Pairo's body, Kurapika can see Omokage holding the Soul Doll of Pairo in his arms, remarking on his beauty, saying it is almost enough to drive himself to sickness. He carries the doll to a room with a large window and sets Pairo down in a throne-like chair to watch out over the sunset with his newly acquired eyes. Before Kurapika can get much information from the vision about where Omokage is located, Omokage steps in front of the Pairo doll and orders him to go to sleep, reaching out towards Pairo and revealing his spider tattoo on his hand. Later on, while Omokage's sister Retz is at dinner with Gon and Killua, Retz mentions her brother to them, citing him as her inspiration for wanting to become a puppeteer. At this time, Gon and Killua are unaware that Retz's brother is Omokage. Omokage's name is mentioned for the first time after Nobunaga fights the Soul Doll of Uvogin, and calls Omokage out for messing with the Phantom Troupe. Omokage then appears standing on top of a building in the square he is in, laughing. During this stand-off with Nobunaga, Omokage claims that he thought Nobunaga would thank him for reviving Uvogin as a puppet, rather than being upset with him. He then reveals several more puppets he created in the image of Pakunoda, and most of the Shadow Beasts, and leaves to let them fight with Nobunaga. After the fight, Nobunaga wraps up Uvogin's eyes and claims that Omokage likely dug up Uvogin's grave in order to obtain them. While this fight is occurring, Hisoka explains to Kurapika and Leorio that Omokage is the person behind the theft of Kurapika's eyes, and was the troupe member that Hisoka replaced two or three years ago. He explains that Omokage's power works by him slipping into people's hearts to discover their passion in order to create a puppet based on the person's deepest attachments. The puppets become Omokage's personal servants, said to obey him without question. Even still, Hisoka says the puppets retain their memories from when they were alive, because they contain an exact copy of the person's heart. He claims that Omokage enjoys the tragedy he creates through his puppets, particularly when they must obey him against their own will. When Hisoka defeated him years ago in order to replace him in the Phantom Troupe, he discovered it was actually only a puppet of Omokage. Before leaving, he warns Kurapika and Leorio that Omokage is very dangerous. After Gon and Killua fight with the Soul Doll of Illumi, Gon tells Killua that he knew for some time that Retz' eyes weren't her own, but rather her brother's, explaining that that was likely how Omokage was able to create a Soul Doll of Illumi; he was able to see through his own eyes being used by Retz and create his Illumi puppet from Killua's soul. Later that night, while Gon and Killua are reuniting with Kurapika and Leorio, Omokage is seen at his hideout standing with his sister and his Soul Doll of Illumi. He talks about how beautiful the eyes he stole from Gon are. Despite Retz pleading with Omokage to stop collecting eyes, Omokage seems to be fully under the delusion that his actions are benefitting his sister, and claims he is doing it for her sake, even as it continues to distress her. He holds Retz's face in his hands, and credits Retz as the reason he became the Divine Puppeteer. In a flashback, Omokage is seen in his workshop, standing before the real Retz with a Retz puppet sitting beside him. Retz had apparently been his first sacrifice, allowing him to hone his skill at transferring eyes from real humans to his puppet creations. Unfortunately, this led to him losing Retz's eyes, because he had not yet perfected the skill when he had attempted to transfer them. He kills his sister in this process in order to revive her as a doll. In the present, he apologizes to his sister for being the reason she has no eyes, before taking back his own from her to go meet Gon, Killua, Kurapika, and Leorio, who have all arrived downstairs. Kurapika interrogates Omokage about his involvement in the Kurta Clan massacre, to which he laughs and recalls the memory of it fondly. However, he claims that the only Kurta eyes he has taken are Kurapika's. He also confirms that he, in fact, led the quartet to his hideout in order to take Killua and Leorio's eyes as well. He then calls on his puppets in a dramatic fashion, instigating a fight between them and Gon's group. After Gon and Killua have defeated the Soul Doll of Illumi, and Kurapika and Leorio, the Soul Doll of Pairo, Omokage claps, amused by the angst and struggle he witnessed in the fights. He tells the quartet that he had only joined the Spiders in order to make puppets out of their members, and left once his collection had been completed. This explanation causes the coffins around the room to burst open, revealing the puppets Omokage had created of the Phantom Troupe members. He then orders the puppets to fight Gon's group, certain that the four of them will not be able to defeat the dolls of the Troupe. Hisoka arrives to aid in the fight, telling Gon's group that it is foolish to fight Omokage's puppets, and should instead be trying to stop Omokage himself. Omokage simply seems amused at Hisoka's appearance and expresses a desire to make a puppet out of Hisoka. Kurapika demands that Omokage stop making puppets of people, which falls on deaf ears. It is only once Gon brings up Retz being sad does Omokage's expression change, but he only ends up angry when Gon continues to try to get through to him. Once Kurapika calls upon Emperor Time, Omokage himself joins the fight, using Doll Catcher to call back a few of his dolls of the Troupe in order to use their abilities himself. Hisoka, Gon, Killua, Leorio, and Kurapika work together to fight against Omokage, who becomes enraged when Hisoka destroys his puppet of Chrollo. Eventually, the team is able to create enough of a distraction to allow Kurapika to get close enough to Omokage to capture him in Chain Jail. Despite being locked in Chain Jail with Kurapika about to insert a chain into his heart, Omokage continues to bicker and banter with him, seemingly amused by Kurapika's attempt at cornering him. He doesn't seem to take his impending death very seriously, but gets angry when Gon once again tries to convince him that his actions only hurt his sister. Kurapika attempts to put the condition on Omokage that he can live if he no longer uses any Nen abilities ever again, but Omokage cannot stand the thought of not being able to make puppets anymore; he claims that if he cannot make puppets, then he is as good as dead. He also does not seem too upset about dying, because he claims his puppets will live on without him, and so he emphatically and excitedly declines Kurapika's condition. However, just before Kurapika kills Omokage, Killua steps in to stop him, claiming he should be the one to kill Omokage. While Kurapika and Killua disagree, Retz runs up behind her brother and stabs him in the back with a Ben's Knife. In his final moments, Omokage begs his sister to tell him why she would kill him, and she explains that if she were still alive, it was what she would have wanted. Omokage is still confused as to why Retz would be unhappy with the everlasting life he gave her as a puppet. Retz tells Omokage that he is not the Divine Puppeteer, and wraps her arms around him in a final hug. Omokage, while embraced by his sister and with his last breaths, tells the group how rotten he thinks humans are. His remaining puppets of the Troupe come to life around him as he slumps over dead. After the actual Phantom Troupe shows up to fight their puppet doubles, Retz carries her brother's body up to a balcony, where she lays him down. She claims that she can now finally be free to live her life, not as her brother's puppet, but in people's memories. After Gon's group has left, Omokage's body and Retz remain inside as the building goes up in flames. Abilities & Powers. Omokage was a collector, and Hisoka described him as a very dangerous individual. He seems to prefer only to use his Nen abilities in combat and has never been seen fighting in hand-to-hand combat. Enhanced Speed and Reflexes: Omokage was fast enough to casually avoid attacks from Gon, Killua, Kurapika, and Leorio simultaneously. However, he was not fast enough to avoid Kurapika's Chain Jail. Nen. Omokage is a Specialist, and the only techniques he has been seen using are the Four Major Principles. Omokage's Nen ability involves manipulating dolls, but despite claiming himself as the "doll maker of the gods", it was shown that his Soul Dolls have some defects. Their Nen abilities, combat skills, physical strength, and durability were far inferior to the originals. This can be seen when Hisoka single-handedly "slew" Soul Dolls Machi, Feitan, Shalnark and Chrollo with little effort. Also, all the dolls have no eyes of their own, thus limiting their power. Furthermore, the dolls were also able to develop feelings of their own and would betray their creator if they disagreed with him, given Retz's case.

On On (, "On"; "Malice") is one of the defining features of the movie . It is the opposite of Nen. Instead of utilizing life energy, the aura from On is derived from hatred and can be considered "death energy." On grants one immense strength, with each user being able to utilize abilities similar to Nen at 100% efficiency. Unlike Nen, this aura is said to be the stronger of the two and has no categories; meaning, one who masters On has the ability of an Enhancer, Transmuter, Conjurer, Emitter, Manipulator, and Specialist. It can be used after having contact with Jed's blood and making a contract to obtain On. However, the use of On will kill the user after the user breaks its contract (or, most likely, fails the contract). Jed, Gaki, Shura, Rengoku, and Gon are all On users in the movie.
On a Journey ~ Ending On a Journey ~ Ending (旅立ち~エンディング, "Tabidachi~endingu") is a song from the Musical Hunter × Hunter, sung by as Gon Freecss.

Onior Longbao Onior Longbao (オニオール＝ロンポウ, "Oniōro Ronpou") is the Boss of the Xi-Yu Family and an illegitimate half-brother to King Nasubi Hui Guo Rou. Appearance. Onior is a corpulent man with prominent wrinkles in his cheeks, small eyebrows and a tuft of fair hair sticking out at the top of his head. Two long, parallel scars run horizontally across his forehead. Overall, he bears a strong resemblance to his half-brother, Nasubi. Personality. Onior regards life, resources, and power as a struggle for supremacy, in which the few haves must protect themselves from a majority of have-nots, an order that he considers a form of balance, which he thus prioritizes. Background. Due to not being an official child of the King of the Kakin Empire, Onior received two scars on his face as soon as he was born and was allowed to live under the condition that he never appears in public or concerned himself with politics. Plot. Succession Contest arc. Onior boards the Black Whale and resides in the VIP area of Tier 1. On the fourth day of the voyage, during one of his meals, he is called by Brocco Li, who informs him that the Phantom Troupe is on the ship. After sharing his views on balance, Onior comments that their behavior reminds him of Morena. The two half-brothers resolve to let the Heil-Ly Family and the Spiders destroy each other, taking care to control when they will do so. He then summons his Underboss Hinrigh and orders him to find Hisoka before the Phantom Troupe does. On the seventh day at around 10:30 pm, Onior is served a plate of food. On Tuesday he is visited by Prince Zhang Lei Hui Guo Rou, who asks him about Guardian Spirit Beasts and Nen. Onior responds that he has never heard about either, but that some subordinates of his have special powers. He recommends that the prince does like his father at the time of his own succession contest and wait, at least until Onior can offer him the information he seeks. When Zhang Lei leaves, he phones Hinrigh, who updates him on the massacres of the Heil-Ly Family and the Spiders, surprising him with the news that they are actually helping them look for Morena, although Onior is afraid they said so only to get in their hideout. After the Underboss assures him that Hisoka is not in Tier 4, he decides to allow them to search the deck, tasking Hinrigh with continuing the manhunt in Tier 3 and kill Morena. Abilities & Powers. As the Boss of the Xi-Yu Family, Onior commands one of the three most powerful forces of the Kakin underground and has authority over a number of subordinates. His mafia faction has the vastest amount of financial power and henchmen of the three, and it is also supported by Prince Zhang Lei. It is in control of Tier 4 of the Black Whale, making its profit from human trafficking and the distribution of goods.

Orarge Orarge (オラルジ, "Oraruji") is a member of the Heil-Ly Family. Appearance. Orarge has distinctive black marks below his eyes and at the corners of his mouth and distinctive eyebrows. He has long hair tied in a ponytail and wears a bandana with an intricate design. He is seen wearing a black shirt with a patterned vest and striped pants. Personality. Orarge appears to be an obedient Heil-Ly member. He made sure to ask Yokotani a question regarding the law and chastised Perigord for forgetting Morena's instructions. Like his fellow Heil-Ly members, he seems to have sadistic tendencies and no qualms about killing people. Plot. Succession Contest arc. Orarge is seen with the other Heil-Ly members as Morena uses her Contagion on them one at a time and explains how her Nen ability works. Orarge is one of the four members who congratulate Bille after he kills Tassi and reaches level 21. During a meeting with Morena in the Heil-Ly's hideout, one member tells her that the butler they left in the VVIP area as a liaison to the Fourth Prince has gone quiet. With four members standing in front of her, Morena guesses that Tserriednich may be on to them and adds that their hideout will be discovered soon based on Gateaume's report. She proposes bringing one of Tserriednich's personal soldiers over to their side, revealing that one of them will go with Dogman to capture a guard. After Matvere (level 21) says that he would prefer to be the "organ", a back-alley doctor, hitman, and Manipulator named Sodom (level 31) volunteers for the mission. Morena says that while Tserriednich will want to deal with her personally for betraying him, it's unclear when and how he will make his move since the succession contest is still ongoing. She reveals that she wants to infect someone on his side with Contagion so that she can track his movements. She gives them a list and tells them to bring any soldiers they find to the hideout, adding that they should use door C since they can no longer use Room 3101. She then tells Orarge and Yokotani to continue guarding the door, adding that they will only get military and yakuza now. She also tells them to invite Tserriednich's men there if they get any of them. A waste disposal contractor and Enhancer, Orarge (level 21), says that dealing with the First Prince's soldiers would be bad, wondering if they can turn them away on legal grounds. An unscrupulous lawyer and Conjurer, Yokotani (level 27) continues to smile and says that they cannot. After Hinrigh and Nobunaga the Heil-Ly's hideout, Hinrigh throws a knife that heads straight for Perigord, who calmly puts out his hand and wonders how long it would take for the injury to heal. However, Orarge uses an issue of "" to stop the knife and tells Perigord that he should have avoided it, wondering why he's trying to use his ability. Orarge then reminds him that he has already been chosen as the "organ" and that Morena told him to keep his head down, with Perigord remembering and apologizing. Abilities & Powers. Nen. Orarge is an Enhancer. Having reached level 21 with Morena's Nen ability, Orarge's aura amount and output have been increased. He also obtained a Nen ability, which remains unknown.

Orau Orau (オラーウ, "Orāu") is a high-ranking soldier in the Royal Army of the Kakin Empire, and one of the personal soldiers of Prince Benjamin. He is now among Prince Tyson's bodyguards under direct orders from Prince Benjamin. Appearance. Orau wears the standard Kakin military attire of a zipper jacket, pants, and dark combat boots. He wears an earpiece in his left ear. Background. As one of the First Prince's soldiers, Orau graduated from Kakin's Royal Military Academy and became a part of his army. Plot. Succession Contest arc. Orau is among the other thirteen soldiers working under Prince Benjamin, that is present during Balsamilco's explanation before the journey's start. Later, Prince Benjamin orders his fourteen soldiers to both act as bodyguards and spies, to all the other princes, and to report any information regarding the Princes' Guardian Spirit Beasts and the Hunters' abilities. He is assigned to Prince Tyson and her Nen beast spawns takes no interest in him. When Tyson and her staff surprise Giuliano on his birthday, Orau can be seen behind them with his hands still held behind his back. Abilities & Powers. Orau has received military training. Nen. Orau is a Nen user, although his superior Balsamilco believes him to be less knowledgeable than Hunters in that regard.

Origin (G.I card) Origin (lit., rom. "Depāchā") is a spell card that can be found in the Greed Island game. It allows for a player to transport the target player back to the starting position. Summary. This spell lets the user transport the target player back to the game's starting point. This card can be used to send an attacking player away from the user, or on a fellow teammate if expecting a player returning from the outside world.

Ortho Siblings The Ortho Siblings (, "Oroso Kyōdai") were a pair of Chimera Ant siblings who resided in an Underground Lake in the Republic of East Gorteau. Appearance. They were humanoids and had features of aquatic animals. Both of them had scales covering their legs as well as webbed feet. Scales also covered the older brother's arms while the sister's arms were left bare; though in the 2011 anime adaptation, there is no such distinction and both of them had scales covering their arms. Personality. The brother was quite sadistic, wondering why Killua wasn't screaming, and expressing that he wanted Killua to die in fear. The sister was very trusting of her brother, and was proud of his abilities. They both loved each other very much and their confidence spawned from it. However, once defeated and decapitated by Killua, they lost all respect for each other and began bickering. Plot. Chimera Ant arc. After Remora successfully attaches the "Bar Double Bull" badge on Killua, the Ortho siblings are revealed and the brother begins their conjoined Nen ability Darts De Darts. After Killua washes ashore, a sound goes off in his head; he's immediately hit with two large fish like darts on his left hand and chest and realizes his entire body has become a dartboard. The brother then telepathically speaks to Killua and inquires if he has any clue of what's happening to him. In the siblings base, the brother removes the darts, off the dartboard and re-throws the darts, piercing Killua's right shoulder and both of his thighs. As the brother pierces more of Killua's body with the "fish darts", he asks if he's figured out what kind of attack he's being struck with. Killua manages to get near and look into a nearby pool of water to deduce it's a game of darts and the brother confirms it. The brother then explains to Killua that he can't do anything against his ability even if he knows it because his darts only materialize when in contact with the target and after a dart pierces Killua's left shoulder, he details it was worth 54 points and the targets on his board are linked to various parts of his body. The brother pierces Killua's elbow worth 27 points, the back of his right hand worth 18 points, making a total of 99 points. Back at the siblings base as the brother continues to rack up points, the sister, seated upon a bar stool, praises him. The brother then boasts that the two of them are invincible and the sister claims it's because they're bound by a strong sense of trust. With the game close to the end, the sister asks her brother if they should tell Killua about it. However the brother rejects the idea to torture him further so he could have better concentration playing and continues to throw a dart onto the board hitting Killua's left arm, chest and right leg. On the final turn, the brother hits Killua's left ear for 18 points, the right calf for 7 points, and finally the forehead for 20 points. This ends the game and the siblings win, celebrating with their special clap together. The siblings then leave their base to check the body of Killua who lies on the ground with a dart sticking out of his forehead. The brother contacts Flutter and informs him of their accomplishments. Flutter praises their actions and informs the siblings he'll inform Leol and convince him to have them promoted to Assistant Squadron Leaders. The siblings celebrate the fact they'll become higher ranked and then start to perform their special clap again only to have their heads severed by Killua at the end. The brother demands to know how Killua managed to survive when a dart is sticking out of his head. Killua pulls the dart from his head reveals he used a suction cup from an octopus. The brother then asks how Killua was able to pull off such a trick when his darts are impossible to dodge. Killua explains he didn't dodge the final dart. After figuring out the final dart was aimed at his head, he cultivated a new Nen ability named Godspeed to optimize his reaction speed, allowing him to stop the dart the moment it touches his skin. The brother inquires about Killua's darting experience. Killua replies that at age six, he mastered the game. The siblings then bicker among each other and when Ikalgo rescues the incapacitated Killua, the siblings try to convince him to save them instead, but only anger him for calling him an octopus. Abilities & Powers. Being Chimera Ants with the genes of fish, the Ortho siblings could breathe underwater and were immune to water pressure to a certain degree. Like other Chimera Ants, they seem to feel no pain even if mutilated, as their heads continued to bicker after being severed. The brother was exceptional at throwing darts. Nen. The Ortho siblings' combine their Conjuration skills in a single Nen ability, which means they are at least capable of performing Hatsu.

Orzny Orzny (オルズニー, "Oruzunī") is a member of Queen Unma's Royal Guard. He spied on Prince Halkenburg, but was recalled back to Prince Benjamin. Plot. Succession Contest arc. Upon Halkenburg's return from the departure banquet, Halkenburg's bodyguards are seen lying unconscious on the floor. However, later that day, the bodyguards are shown to be fine. Following Kurapika's broadcast on the emergency channel, Benjamin orders the members of his own private army to work in shifts with Queen Unma's bodyguards to monitor the other Princes. Orzny is thus removed from Prince Halkenburg's guard and assigned to Benjamin. Shikaku, the soldier with whom he switched shifts, says that just like Halkenburg's own guards, Orzny also received a mark of the feather from Halkenburg's Guardian Spirit Beast, but that it disappeared after ten minutes. Shikaku speculates that the ability does not have any effect on those who, like Orzny, have no loyalty to Halkenburg. He further states that like the other guards, Orzny has no memory of receiving the mark, guessing that it involves memory revision from a Manipulator attack.

Rengoku Rengoku (, "Rengoku"—lit. "Purgatory") was an On user and one of Jed's right hands in . Appearance. Rengoku was a short, young woman with fair skin. She was often seen wearing a dark grey, hooded cloak similar to her comrades'. However, she also sported a dark red clasp on the front, similar to Jed's, and an additional flounce over her shoulders. Underneath, she wore a black, skin-tight, full-body undersuit. Also, Rengoku's boots were shorter than her comrades and only reached her mid-calves. She also possessed a Kanan Prison Camp mark on the left side of the back of her neck. She was also depicted wearing a beige and dark red dress with dark boots as a child and a grey hooded cloak with pockets and dark baggy pants underneath as an adolescent. Personality. Rengoku was often depicted as quiet and calm, speaking far less than Gaki and Shura, and she retained her composure even in difficult situations as an adult. She was also shown to be kind to those who were not Hunters. She shared the same hatred and revenge-filled mind that Shura and Gaki had, leading to her contract with On. However, she was also capable of much more compassion than Shura, being able to empathize with Gon and Killua and helping them by freeing Netero when she saw that the boys really needed her, even after having given her own life to seal away his Nen in the first place. Background. Rengoku, being a descendant of members of the Shadow, was banished to live in a village in the mountains after the Shadow itself and its members were destroyed by Netero. Rengoku, along with Shura and Gaki, were described as living peacefully as children in their mountain village until eventually, the nation and Garcia no longer wanted any descendants of the Shadow to exist, and so they were persecuted, which later led to them revolting. Garcia then insisted on removing the descendants completely. Rengoku was captured as a child by hunters and the other descendants and put into Kanan Prison Camp, where Rengoku was branded on the back of her neck with a Kanan Prison Camp mark. Her living and working conditions there were described as harsh and depraved. Although many of the descendants of the Shadow died while living in the prison camp, Rengoku, along with Shura and Gaki, escaped as children. These events led Rengoku, Shura, and Gaki to seek a way to revive On throughout their lives. This led to the reincarnation of Jed, whom they then made a contract with by offering up their lives in order to achieve the revenge they sought against the Hunter Association. Plot. The Last Mission. Rengoku, Gaki, Shura, and Jed trudge through the snow to arrive at a small outpost town during a blizzard. She and her comrades free the prisoners imprisoned there in order for them to join their team for their upcoming mission at Heavens Arena, where they plan to take the people there hostage, in order to force the Hunter Association to release the Black Report to the public. On the first day of the Battle Olympia, Rengoku and her comrades walk through the alleys of the Heavens Arena city to get to the tournament. They are later seen in the crowd inside Heavens Arena while Netero makes his opening announcement. While the group stands around, a little girl runs into Rengoku and the two stare at each other. The girl is frightened until Rengoku softly smiles at her, which seems to help the little girl's mood, who then goes off to sit with her mother. After Cocco finishes introducing the Battle Olympia event and the mascots come out to dance, Rengoku and her group are still in the crowd. Gaki reaches his hand out towards Rengoku, perhaps trying to instigate a fight, but she slaps him away with little effort. Shura remarks how strong she is, to which she silently nods. Shura stares at her softly and tells the group to meet again in Nirvana once their mission is over, although his comment seems to be aimed at Rengoku specifically, knowing that she is about to die. Rengoku, Shura, and Gaki then dash off in different directions. While Gon and Killua are upstairs having tea with Netero, Netero senses Rengoku's presence even before she arrives, although the boys are oblivious to this, unable to sense her coming. The elevator doors to Netero's floor then open, and Rengoku steps out, with the elevator operator lying on the floor, either unconscious or dead. Netero stands and stares at the closed door to his room, already recognizing the aura coming off of the approaching Rengoku as On, although he is in disbelief. As Rengoku walks down the hall to Netero's room, she counts down with each step she takes, stopping when she reaches fifty at Netero's door. She opens it to reveal herself to Netero, Gon, and Killua. Netero starts questioning her, but before he can finish, she pulls a blade out from her cloak sleeve, holds it out with both hands, and shouts her ability, Onbasara, before stabbing herself in the abdomen. She falls to her knees as her On releases from her body in the shape of dark wings that sprout out of her back. Her On rushes towards Netero, holding him up and restricting him in the air in order to seal his aura, preventing him from using his Nen. Rengoku remains on her knees, bloodied and dead on the floor. Later, Jed brings Rengoku and Netero up to the roof of Heavens Arena. Garcia is brought to Jed, who throws him at the feet of Rengoku. Her On strangles him while lifting him up in the air as a result of him getting too close to Netero. While Garcia is up in the air, he notices the brand on Rengoku's neck from her time in Kanan Prison Camp. Garcia confesses to giving the order to the hunters to capture the descendants of the Shadow and put them in a prison camp, claiming it was intended to be kept a secret. Rengoku's aura then drops Garcia, and he falls to the ground. Rengoku is also seen in a flashback alongside Shura and Gaki, where the trio escapes the hunters who are taking away the other descendants of the Shadow. When the trio has aged into adults, they find a man in the desert who inform them about potentially being able to bring back Jed. They then go to the desert rock where Netero first massacred the Shadow and formed a contract with the reincarnation of Jed, vowing a lifelong loyalty to serve him and take revenge on all Hunters. In the present, during Gon and Killua's attempt to fight Jed on the roof, after Gon has been seriously hurt, Killua turns to Rengoku in a last-ditch effort. He rushes towards her and can break through the On barrier surrounding her using much of his strength. He falls to his knees in front of her, holding onto her shoulders, trying to get her to sympathize with his plight. He begs her to end this, and a tear rolls down Rengoku's cheek, which falls onto the blade plunged into her abdomen. The On disappears from her eyes, and they fall shut as her ability's grip on Netero vanishes. She falls forward into Killua's arms. After Jed is defeated and On is gone forever, it is assumed that whatever part of Rengoku's soul or desires were being kept alive by On to be able to control her ability is then permanently dead. Abilities & Powers. Shura described Rengoku as being very physically strong, and she could even overpower Gaki in casual settings. However, her fighting capabilities were never seen in the film, as she was never shown in serious combat. Rengoku's primary ability was her On, which she used by sacrificing her life. On. As an On user, Rengoku had access to all Nen categories.

Renko Renko (レンコ, "Renko") is an inhabitant of Meteor City's Kirimori Valley. She worked as an embalmer and was Machi's mentor in the art of Nen. Appearance. At the time of her appearance, Renko was a fairly tall woman with a petite build and long, light-colored hair. She wore a broad-brimmed hat with two horn-like ears sticking out from it as well as a completely black outfit; her full-skirt midi dress with sleeves also served as a mask that covered the lower half of her face, revealing only her eyes. Personality. Renko is mysterious and withdrawn, appearing at Sarasa's funeral and standing back quietly while the children mourn for their friend. While she seemed jealous of Machi's eyes and made a comment about precocious kids, she was willing to embalm Sarasa's body and offered Machi a way to learn Nen. The inhabitants of Meteor City are also stated to share remarkable bonds that have been described as "thinner than water, and yet thicker than blood". Plot. Succession Contest arc. After Sarasa's death, the children gather around her body lying in a casket at the church, calling her beautiful and saying that it's like she's still alive. Lisores tells them that it's called embalming, explaining that it's a technique used to restore and keep a person's body as close as possible to how it was when they were alive. He adds that it's a miracle that her body was able to be restored so well, given the condition it was in, asking them to thank the embalmer, Ms. Renko. Machi looks back to see a mysterious woman dressed in black with a large hat that has pointed ears. She then approaches Renko and asks if she can learn to embalm like that, but Renko replies that she cannot, explaining that her technique is a special ability. Machi wonders if the ability has something to do with why her body is glowing so much, and Renko quickly asks if she can see aura. Machi stares at her with a determined look, and the jealous Renko comments on her pretty eyes. She then tosses Machi a small piece of paper with a specific design, explaining that she can visit anytime if the caretakers give her permission. She tells her to get on the last bus and ask for Kirimori Valley, adding that if she shows them the piece of paper, they will take her there for free. As Renko walks away, the word "aura" lingers in Machi's mind. Abilities & Powers. Renko is a Nen user, as Machi was able to see her aura.

Republic of East Gorteau The Republic of East Gorteau (, "Higashi Gorutō Kyōwakoku") was one of the nations in the Mitene Union, formerly bordered by the Republic of West Gorteau. Its last Supreme Leader was Ming Jol-ik before the Chimera Ant King dethroned him. It used to be an isolationist nation, with its capital city being Peijin. The Royal Palace rests outside of Peijin in the wilderness. The country ceases to exist after the Chimera Incident. Overview. The Republic of East Gorteau was a dictatorship, possibly of the or type. Apparently, all powers (government, legislation, army) were held by the sole figure of the Supreme Leader, Ming Jol-ik, making him an absolute ruler with unlimited authority over the citizens. In reality, Ming Jol-ik had not been involved in the government of the country for thirty years: a dead ringer resided in the palace and talked to the nation in his stead, while the individual who actually controlled the country from behind the shadows was Bizeff. It originally counted over 5.000.000 inhabitants, all of whom became refugees. History. This form of government derived from a bloody revolt that established the new ruling class, which is said to be extremely wealthy whereas most of the population lives in poverty. However, TV stations report that "in other countries, more than half the people starve to death before the age of 10". Financial aid received from other countries is not used for the impoverished but is spent in luxury goods for the rich and war equipment. There are also rumors that East Gorteau has cut ties with all other nations in order to increase the entity of the financial aids received through negotiations, and that part of the money is used to build nuclear weapons. Following the events of the Chimera Ant crisis, the Republic of East Gorteau ceased to exist and the territory being absorbed by other countries members of the Mitene Union. As a result, the country is now jointly governed by the other countries in the Mitene Union. The Chimera Ants' existence and incidents were covered up by the international governments and the Hunter Association by accusing the deceased Ming Jol-ik of luring the citizen of the country to the palace to be massacred through forced mass suicide. Locations. The Republic of East Gorteau was located in the Balsa Islands. Notable places in this country were: Spy System. An intricate and efficient system to detect spies was in effect in the country, information on which can be found on Hunter Website. Gon described it as a "carrot and stick system". A very potent informant system called "finger-pointing group" regulated the information. The reward money was given for discovering spies, uncovering evidence of a revolution and catching defectors in the act. If the informant points surpassed a certain amount, the ranks of all the members of the group would increase. On the other hand, if a report turned out to be false or a member of the group was revealed to be a traitor, the entire group was punished. Family members were divided into different groups, so if a group attempted to escape to another country, the rest of their families were sentenced to death or imprisoned for life; if an entire family was caught defecting, they were executed without questioning.

Republic of Hass Republic of Hass (, "Hasu Kyōwakoku") is one of the nations of the Mitene Union. It is bordered by the Republic of Rokario on the west and the Republic of West Gorteau at the east. Background. After the Chimera Ant crisis was over this country took over part of the Republic of East Gorteau with other parts being taken over by the Republic of Rokario and the Republic of West Gorteau.

Republic of Padokea The Republic of Padokea (, "Padokia Kyōwakoku"), in the Hunter × Hunter world, is a country composed of several parts including the Dentora Region (, "Dentora-chiku") where Kukuroo Mountain is located. Access to the country is free, with no special conditions to be met.

Republic of Rokario Republic of Rokario (, "Rokario Kyōwakoku") is one of the nations of the Mitene Union. It is bordered by the NGL on the west and the Republic of Hass at the east. It was in this country Gon and Killua first meet Palm, Knuckle, and Shoot. Background. After the Chimera Ant crisis was over this country took over part of the Republic of East Gorteau with other parts being taken over by the Republic of Hass and the Republic of West Gorteau. Locations. Known places in this country are:

Republic of West Gorteau Republic of West Gorteau (西ゴルトー共和国, "Nishi Gorutō Kyōwakoku") is one of the nations of the Mitene Union. It is bordered by the Republic of Hass on the west and the Republic of East Gorteau at the east. Background. After the Chimera Ant crisis was over this country took over part of the Republic of East Gorteau with other parts being taken over by the Republic of Rokario and the Republic of Hass.
Reset (G.I card) Reset (, rom. "Risetto") is a card exclusive to the physical Greed Island card set.

Restricted Voyage Agencies The Restricted Voyage Agencies (, "Tokkō"—lit. "Special Travel Departments") are five departments that regulate travel to the Dark Continent in each of the Five Modern Nations. Currently, all RVAs are coordinated by Steiner, the Deputy Secretary of the International Permit Agency (IPA). Overview. In order to reach the Dark Continent, it is necessary to send an application to the Ministers of Foreign Affairs of each of the members of the V5, from which the applicant is redirected to the corresponding Restricted Voyage Agency, a process of finishing contracts, briefings and other procedures that require about five months or half a year. Then, the applicant must meet the Section Chief of the RVAs, for which they need introduction letters from three members of their country's congress, all of which still does not guarantee acceptance by the International Permit Agency. Plot. Dark Continent Expedition arc. After Nasubi Hui Guo Rou reveals his colonization project, which ignores the normal procedures, the IPA Deputy Secretary is put in charge of a team coordinating all RVAs.

Return (G.I card) Return (, rom. "Ritān") is a spell card that can be found in the Greed Island game. It allows for a player to instantly transport back to a previously visited city. Summary. This card allows the caster to transport to any city or village that they have previously visited. This spell is particularly useful when the user needs to return to a city for any reason. The most common use for this card would be to transport to Masadora to buy more spell cards. It can also be used to escape other players before they can cast short-range spells or physically attack.

Retz Retz (レツ, "Retsu") was a travelling puppeteer and the younger sister of Omokage. Appearance. Retz had long blonde hair and turquoise eyes. For all of, the eyes she had were actually her brother's, but her original disembodied eyes are seen in a flashback and shared the same color as her brother's. When she was disguised as a boy, her hair seemed significantly shorter, hidden under a light-blue skull cap. She also wore light-blue overalls, blue gloves, and yellow sneakers. Later in the movie, Retz wore a red and black Gothic- dress and a red ribbon on her head. She also wore black stockings and gray shoes. Personality. Retz was a young puppeteer who disguised herself as a boy by dressing in typical boys' clothes and hiding her long hair under a hat. She was often a very sweet and happy girl, although was often seen as argumentative and determined when dealing with Killua. Retz claimed to be jealous of Gon and Killua’s relationship. She was also afraid of her brother, who had revived her as a manipulable doll that he could control if he needed to. She constantly wondered what "true life" really was. Despite being a living puppet, she had developed her own feelings and intentions through her interactions with Gon and Killua, and grew to be genuinely fond of them. Plot. Phantom Rouge. Retz first appears in while busking with her puppet in a small town in the Totoria District, where her performance has attracted a large crowd of people who are in awe of her puppetry skills, including Gon. After the performance, a young girl goes to give Retz a few coins, but stumbles while running away, prompting a horse-drawn cart to lose control and almost crush the young girl. Retz runs to her rescue and shields her with her body, before Gon runs to their aid. Once the two are alone, Retz thanks Gon for his help and introduces herself as a puppeteer. Gon remarks how awesome Retz's show was and how life-like her puppet seemed. The comment prompts Retz to look wistful, but she thanks Gon nonetheless, and he notices something strange happen in her eyes. The moment passes, and Gon pulls out his scrawled picture to ask Retz if she can help him locate the place Kurapika saw in his vision. By nightfall, Retz and Gon are talking in the streets of town when Killua returns looking for Gon. Gon introduces Retz as his friend to Killua, under the assumption that Retz is a boy. Killua is instantly jealous of the quick bond that Gon and Retz have already formed. He remarks that she seems shady and is probably just a petty thief, which angers Retz and causes her to yell at him, demanding an apology. In a burst of anger, Killua yells back at Retz and pushes her to the ground by forcing his hand against her chest. She falls back, and while Gon goes to her aid, Killua looks at his hand and hesitantly asks Retz if she is a girl. Gon is flabbergasted by the question, but Retz doesn't deny it. Over a meal at a restaurant, Retz explains that she wasn't trying to trick them, but that she was merely trying to protect herself, as she claims it's dangerous for girls to travel on their own like she is, and that she often pretends to be a boy for this reason. She remarks how close Killua and Gon seem to be, and tells them she is jealous of their friendship. She holds her hand-made puppet close to her chest, calling it her best friend. She also tells the boys about her brother, Omokage, who is a puppeteer, and her inspiration for wanting to become one herself. Killua remarks that her puppet has beautiful eyes, which prompts Retz to tell them that the eyes are the hardest thing on a puppet to make, but can give the puppet the most life. She claims that getting the eyes perfect can actually give the puppet a soul. Killua seems to be aware of Retz's true nature after her explanation, but says nothing about it to Gon. While the trio rests for the night, a puppet of Uvogin attacks the house they are in, startling Retz from her slumber. Gon carries Retz as the trio makes their escape from their shared room. Gon and Killua tell Retz to go somewhere safer while they deal with Uvogin, and she heeds their advice and runs off. The next morning, Retz searches through the rubble of the destroyed house with Gon and Killua to find her puppet, which managed to stay in one piece thanks to being hidden away in a protective box. The rest of Retz's belongings were apparently destroyed in the attack, as she is left wearing only her nightgown; Gon tells Killua they should get Retz some clothes, so the trio make their way to a shop called Heavens Angels, located in the town. There, the shop owner styles Retz in a dark lolita-esque outfit, and the two boys stare in awe at her appearance. The stylist remarks that Retz looks like a porcelain doll, which seems to visibly distress her. Killua and Retz get into a spat while in the shop, in which Killua warns Retz that she shouldn't come with them anymore on their journey because it could be fatal to her. She remarks that she'd rather take action than do nothing at all. She tells them that she has longed for the day where she felt like she could live a real life. The boys are confused by her comments, and Killua pulls Gon outside to talk to him. While Retz is alone in the shop, she calls on her Soul Doll, the puppet in her arms, which jumps to life and follows after the boys to spy on their conversation. Killua tells Gon that he doesn't trust Retz, after which she runs after them to confront Killua in the alleyway. She expresses an intense desire to help the boys with their mission, even if it means just showing them the place they're trying to find and leaving. Gon manages to convince Killua to let Retz help them. She leads the boys into a large open graveyard, where they can see the hideout they were looking for in the distance. Her and Killua get into another fight after he rudely tells her to leave now that she has fulfilled her promise to them, but Gon manages to calm her down. She expresses to Gon that she enjoys having him be so nice to her, implying that she is usually treated much less kindly when she is pretending to be a boy. After the boys struggle to fight the Illumi puppet located inside the hideout and are chased out, Retz rushes to Gon's aid after he is left eyeless and lying on the ground. Later that night, while Gon and Killua are reuniting with Kurapika and Leorio, Retz stands behind her brother at his hideout while he monologues about the eyes his Illumi puppet stole from Gon, claiming that they wouldn't be a good fit for her. She begs her brother to stop, but he says that he's doing all of this for her sake, and cites her as the reason he became the divine puppeteer. He corroborates what Retz told the boys about a puppet needing human eyes to have a soul. In a flashback, Retz is seen standing before her brother in Omokage's workshop with an eyeless, clothesless puppet made in Retz' image sitting beside them. She is then seen sprawled out on the floor with a pair of bloody eyeballs laying on the ground. Omokage apologizes to Retz, stating that he hadn't perfected the technique of transferring eyes yet when he had killed her to make her into a puppet, which is what led to her eyes being lost. In the present, she begs her brother to give Gon his eyes back, but he simply laughs her off. It is revealed that Retz' current blue eyes were actually her brother's that he had been loaning to her, and he takes them back before going to meet the boys who have arrived at the hideout. Downstairs, Gon, Killua, Kurapika, and Leorio confront Omokage, who reveals Retz sitting on a throne-like chair behind him, informing them that she is his sister and a living puppet. Omokage tells the group that they should give her some eyes, but Gon insists that that would never make her happy. After the group fights Omokage's puppets with Hisoka's help, and then Omokage himself, the chair Retz was sitting in is shown to be empty. Gon tries to tell Omokage that his desire to give Retz new eyes is only hurting Retz, but he refuses to believe him. Kurapika and Killua argue about which one of them should kill Omokage, but before either of them can do it, Retz runs up and stabs her brother in the back with a Ben's Knife. With his last few breaths, Omokage begs Retz to tell him why she killed him. She claims that if she were still alive herself, it was what she would have wanted. In his last moments, she tells her brother that he is not the divine puppeteer and wraps her arms around him in a final hug. After the Phantom Troupe arrives to fight their puppet doubles, the building bursts into flames, and the boys turn to see Retz sitting up on her throne with her brother dead in her arms. She thanks the boys for all that they have done, claiming that she can now live a real life, not as a puppet but alive in people's memories. Killua tries to go after her, but Gon holds him back. Once the quartet is outside, the building burns to the ground with Retz and her brother still inside. Abilities & Powers. Nen. It is shown that she can move her puppet without any strings attached. Given that she possesses the Soul Doll ability, as she creates a doll based on Illumi Zoldyck with her puppet, she is likely to be a Specialist as her brother.

Revenge Shop (G.I card) Revenge Shop (しかえししょうてん, "Shikaeshi Shōten") is a card found in the Greed Island game. It is one of the game's 100 designated slot cards and is required for a player to complete the game. Summary. Revenge Shop (仕返し商店): This card when used summons a revenge shop. This shop allows for players to report any grudges you might have to the manager of the establishment. They will then use any means deemed necessary to retaliate back to whatever caused the grudge. The severity of the retaliation is determined by the level of grievance by the user. You can also pay extra for a more... severe attack.

Rhino Rhino (サイ, "Sai") was a Chimera Ant Soldier from Leol's Squad. Appearance. Rhino had the appearance of a humanoid rhinoceros with two horns on his head and two along his snout. He had shaggy dark blue hair and wore a . Personality. He was a boastful Chimera Ant who was also very confident in his abilities. He believed that since Baro was defeated, he was trash. Plot. Chimera Ant arc. Rhino fights Killua in a one on one match after being called up by a lottery ticket. The Ant boasts that he's ten times stronger than Baro. Off screen, Rhino is dealt with and Killua inquires if any of the other Ants are stronger than their deceased ally. Abilities & Powers. As a Chimera Ant, Rhino is already stronger than the average human, and he claims to be 10 times stronger than Baro. Due to his rhinoceros genes, he has very hard skin that cannot be penetrated by normal means, and was durable enough to withstand Killua's clawed strike at first. Despite this, he was completely overwhelmed by Killua and unable to follow his movements whatsoever. He also used his horns on one occasion to try and impale Killua.

Rice Rice (ライス, "Raisu") is one of Queen Duazul's personal soldiers that's assigned to Prince Luzurus Hui Guo Rou. Appearance. Rice has round eyes, thick lips, a funnel nose, and neatly combed parted to the right medium-length dark hair. He sports a small, rectangular and a goatee. As a Royal Bodyguard, he wears a black suit and a tie. Plot. Succession Contest arc. On the ninth day of the Black Whale's departure, Rice answers the door when Prince Benjamin's personal soldier Shikaku rings the doorbell to the Seventh Prince's room. He asks Shikaku for his purpose, but Shikaku merely salutes and declares his loyalty to Prince Benjamin, before shooting himself in the head. Rice is visibly shaken and perplexed by the sudden suicide. He has calmed down by the time Kanjidol asks him to repeat his account, however, Rice cannot provide an explanation as to why Shikaku would kill himself in front of Room 1007.

Richard Hackett Richard Hackett (リチヤード=ハケット, "Richiyādo Haketto") is a former Greed Island player. Appearance. Richard has short hair, a crooked nose, and thin eyebrows. He wore a white dress shirt under a vest. Plot. Greed Island arc. Desperate to get out of the game, he exchanges a rare card with Biscuit for a "Leave" card in front of the spell card shop in Masadora. Richard's name is mentioned later in Gon's binder. Abilities & Powers. Nen. Due to being able to access Greed Island, Richard Hackett is capable of utilizing Nen.

Ridge Ridge (リッジ, "Rijji") is a Hunter and Royal Bodyguard for Prince Luzurus. Appearance. Ridge has dark skin, a big nose, and thick lips. His dark hair is arranged in a ridge-like haircut. He has a dark, vertical line resembling a tear painted or tattooed under each of his eyes. During his rap battle performance, he wore a black long-sleeved shirt underneath a patterned shirt, whereas he dons a black suit with a white tie while on duty as a bodyguard. Personality. Little is known about Ridge's personality, but he seems to take freestyle rap battles rather seriously. Plot. Succession Contest arc. Because of Kurapika's announcement through the emergency channel that revealed the existence of Nen beasts, Prince Luzurus summons his hired Hunters Ridge, Scairt, and Basho to learn more about his Guardian Spirit Beast and Nen. Scairt informs the Prince about the conditions of a Nen beast and how it would take approximately a year to master Nen. Disinterested in learning Nen, the prince, informs the Hunters that their original plan involving his older sister Prince Tubeppa will proceed. He also notes his delight that a stalemate could happen because of the Nen beasts and they could dominate the competition if the other prince's guards are ignorant of Nen. The prince then orders the Hunters to guard him in rotations and report to him if they witness a Nen beast. During the first banquet, Ridge participates in a freestyle rap battle against Basho. The following day, he is sitting on a sofa by a table with Basho. After a rumbling noise, the doorbell rings and it's "Shikaku" who pledges his allegiance to Prince Benjamin and then commits suicide. Under Famule's orders, Ridge and Basho stay in the Prince's room while the personal bodyguards search and examine the area of Shikaku's suicide. He is present when Kanjidol questions him and the other bodyguards to further elaborate any information they have on his comrade's abrupt suicide. Abilities & Powers. Ridge has all the benefits granted by his status as a Hunter. Nen. As a Hunter, Ridge is capable of using Nen to an unknown degree.

Riehlvelt Riehlvelt (リールベルト, "Rīruberuto") is one of the three fighters who challenge Gon and Killua on the 200th floor of Heavens Arena. Appearance. Riehlvelt is a man of average size, he has purple spiky hair and often wears a yellow colored head gear. Due to becoming paralyzed from his "initiation", he is seen moving around in a large big wheeled motorized wheelchair. Personality. Riehlvelt has a ruthless personality, resorting even to kidnapping and blackmailing to get his way. He is intent on becoming a Floor Master in order to live off the money and fame of the rank despite lacking the necessary strength, for which reason he only fights opponents weaker than himself. He was nonetheless brave enough to face Killua in combat despite the ease with which the former assassin threatened him. He seems to have a sadistic side as well, bursting into laughter when electrocuting his opponent. However, when faced with the prospect of being electrocuted, he passed out from the fear of it. Background. At some point in his life, Riehlvelt reached the 200th floor of the Heavens Arena without knowing Nen. He was thus "initiated" by an opponent whose malicious aura attack paralyzed him from the waist down. Prior to fighting Gon and Killua, he totalized five wins and two losses. None of his opponents ever succeeded in catching his whips. Plot. Heavens Arena arc. By the time Gon and Killua learn how to use Nen and reach the 200th floor, Riehlvelt, Gido, and Sadaso confront them, waiting for them to register to pick them as their next opponents. Two months later, after Gon has recovered from his fight against Gido and restarts his Nen training, the trio confronts the boys again but Gon refuses to fight before June 10th. To force his hand, they kidnap Zushi but immediately run into Killua, who accepts to give each of them a free win. They set Zushi free, and Killua departs with him but warns them not to break their promise. However, against Killua's terms, they blackmail Gon into arranging a fight against each of them. Killua discovers the fraud, and, on May 29th, the day of his match against Sadaso, threatens to kill him if he does not leave the Heavens Arena. The following day, Sadaso contacts Riehlvelt from outside Heavens Arena to inform him of Killua's warning. Riehlvelt insists on not giving up, speculating Killua did not come to him because he does not know his ability. Killua, however, reveals to be in the room with him and Gido, stating that is not the case and proving he can surprise them anytime. When he leaves, Riehlvelt resolves to fight fair and square. On June 6th, he prepares to fight Killua. Despite being intimidated by Killua, Riehlvelt is confident that the rules of the Heavens Arena give him the advantage. As soon as the match begins, Killua disappears from his sight, and he manages to avoid a sneak attack from above by propelling himself away with Aura Burst. He tries to push Killua out of bounds with "Song of Defense", but the boy easily catches his whips. Riehlvelt thus electrocutes him with "Thunder Snake", but Killua, who has been trained to withstand electricity, flings him high in the air. Riehlvelt begs Killua to catch him, which he does while holding "Twin Snake". Riehlvelt ends up being electrocuted and falls to the floor, unconscious. Six days later, he faces Gon. He starts the match with "Song of Defense", but Gon forces him to interrupt the attack by hurling a flagstone at him. Riehlvelt propels himself away, which Gon exploits to stop his wheelchair and break his wrists. He coils the whips around Riehlvelt's neck and turns the electricity to the max before pretending to press the button. Riehlvelt faints from the fear. Having totalized four losses, Riehlvelt is disqualified from the Heavens Arena. Equipment. Wheelchair: Riehlvelt uses a motorized wheelchair as his primary means of locomotion, through which he can also channel his Nen ability. Abilities & Powers. In the past, Riehlvelt must have been a capable martial artist, having reached the 200th floor of the Heavens Arena without knowing Nen and without the use of weapons. However, after his injury he fought only opponents new to Nen, and he was easily defeated by Gon and Killua when they had only mastered three of the Four Major Principles. His fighting style is centered on his weapons and Nen abilities and capitalizes on the restrictions in place at the Heavens Arena. His reactions are quick enough for him to evade a sneak attack from Killua, although the boy admitted he had jumped too high. Proficient Weapon Specialist: Riehlvelt is adept at using two bullwhips as his primary means of offense. He exploits their range to cover a large portion of the ring and push the opponent out of bounds. He considers his lashes too fast to keep up with, although Killua caught them with ease. Nen. Riehlvelt is a skilled enough Nen user to have developed one Nen ability, which presumably makes use of Emission.

Rihan Rihan (リハン, "Rihan") is a high-ranking soldier in the Royal Army of the Kakin Empire, and one of the personal soldiers of Prince Benjamin. He was among Prince Salé-salé's bodyguards under orders from Prince Benjamin, but has since been reassigned to Prince Tubeppa. Appearance. Rihan wears his hair in a style and has slited eyes. He wears the standard Kakin military attire of a zipper jacket, pants, and dark combat boots. He also uses an earpiece in his left ear. Personality. Rihan is a very perceptive individual. He can deduce the nature and ability of someone's Guardian Spirit Beast by simply being around it, even for only a short amount of time. He is quite confident in his ability to counteract against Prince Salé-salé's Guardian Beast. Background. As one of the First Prince's soldiers, Rihan graduated from Kakin's Royal Military Academy and became a part of his army. Plot. Succession Contest arc. Rihan is among the other thirteen soldiers working under Prince Benjamin that is present during Balsamilco's explanation before the journey's start. Later, Prince Benjamin orders his fourteen soldiers to act as both bodyguards and spies to all the other princes, and to report any information regarding the Princes' Guardian Spirit Beasts and the Hunters' abilities. Rihan becomes the Eighth Prince Salé-salé's bodyguard. On the second day of the voyage, while in the Eighth Prince's bedroom as Salé-salé secretly hints to two women what he intends to do at the banquet, Rihan observes that his Guardian Spirit Beast is tied to his libido and disappears on three occasions, which would potentially allow Rihan to terminate his mission in an instant. In the course of his 16-hour shift, he also analyzes the abilities of the prince's Guardian Spirit Beast, determining that when his fellow bodyguard is affected, he will have enough information to activate Predator. He estimates that if his ability can neutralize a Guardian Spirit Beast, he will be of great use to Prince Benjamin. Roughly 54 hours later, a small clone of Prince Salé-salé's Guardian Spirit Beast appears above Koroabde's head, Rihan determines that he has all the information he needs and activates his ability, which swallows the Guardian Spirit Beast as well as its clone. Having cleared his mission and being prevented from using any Nen for the following two days, Rihan contacts his superior to relay his success and request that his security shift be swapped with Yushohi's so the latter can assassinate the defenseless prince. He then talks directly to Yushohi, who claims that it is almost confirmed that Prince Fugetsu's Guardian Spirit Beast has teleportation capabilities. After Rihan is moved to Prince Tubeppa's room, Balsamilco tells him to lay low for a while before taking out Halkenburg's Guardian Spirit Beast. He warns Rihan that he might be misinterpreting the Ninth Prince's ability, but cannot say anything more due to the conditions of Predator. As a hint, he reminds him that Shikaku was a Manipulator. Nonetheless, Rihan feels that his ability is being wasted since Tubeppa's Guardian Spirit Beast will not show itself, and since there is no guarantee that it is less dangerous than Halkenburg's. Noticing that Maor's Aura Nodes have been fully opened, he wishes to use Predator on Kurapika, but understands that due to the number of unknown abilities he has it would be ineffective. He thinks that Balsamilco is being overly cautious due to Shikaku's suicide and begins to reflect on it, realizing that the extremely powerful aura he felt would make defending oneself impossible. He wonders if Shikaku offered his own life in exchange for Benjamin's, but rejects the possibility due to the prince's personality. Abilities & Powers. Rihan has received military training. He has proven himself to be astute and analytical. Nen. Rihan is a Nen user, although his superior Balsamilco believes him to be less knowledgeable than Hunters in that regard. Nonetheless, he appears to be profoundly knowledgeable about Manipulation Nen as well as Nen beasts. He has at least the ability to use Hatsu.

Rising Dragon Tattoo Hide The Rising Dragon Tattoo Hide (, "Zenshin Irezumi Gawa no Shō Ryū-zu Goku Bihin") is a collectible body part. Plot. Yorknew City arc. At the Sengi Guild, its agent manages to find three job offers that match Kurapika's request. One of the offers involves a flesh collector seeking the rare item.

Risky Dice The Risky Dice (リスキーダイス, "Risukī Daisu") is an icosahedron dice that can only be found in Greed Island. Appearance. The Risky Dice is an icosahedron dice that has 19 sides with a star for very good/excellent luck (✩) and 1 side with a skull and crossbones (☠) for great misfortune. Plot. Greed Island arc. At the Dorias casino slot machines, Killua rolls a Risky Dice to increase his luck and wins a "Rainbow Diamond". Figuring he can win more cards with the dice, Killua gives all of the cards in his binder to Gon. This was a precautionary move in case he was to roll a ☠, however, he was confident he wouldn't. At that moment a Greed Island player dies due to the repercussion from the dice. On the other hand, Killua brushes it off and challenges the Casino King. He wins against him earns the "Fledgling Gambler" card. Adamant to use the dice again, Biscuit knocks him out before he could. Meanwhile, the Bombers force one of their hostages Motaricke to roll a Risky Dice again a fourth time. The Bombers' goal was to gain a "Wild Luck Alexandrite" card through a Lottery, this however fails. In order to stay on top of the other players, Bara devises a plan using the Risky Dice in conjunction with the Tax Collector's Gauntlet. Genthru notes the risk of the plan and suggests they use the slaves to do their handy work. However, Sub and Bara are resolute to take the risk associated with the dice. This makes Genthru take the Risky Dice and rolls it himself, perturbing his teammates. The Risky Dice, however, lands on a ✩ and Genthru notes the risk factor is low so the plan should work perfectly. Afterward, Genthru trades with Tsezguerra's team, while Sub and Bara hide in the background awaiting their chance to make their ambush after they roll the Risky Dice. Card. The "Risky Dice" card designated number is 25. It has a rank-limit of B-30.

Risky Dice (G.I card) Risky Dice (リスキーダイス, "Risukī Daisu") is a card found in the Greed Island game. It is one of the game's 100 designated slot cards and is required for a player to complete the game. It allows the user the chance to increase their luck... but at a risk of course. Summary. When this card is 'gained', the player obtains a 20-sided (icosahedron) dice. 19 of the sides, if rolled, give the player very good luck, but if the player rolls on the 'very bad luck' side, the resulting bad luck is bad enough to counteract all the good luck all players on the island have accumulated since the last bad roll, often resulting in the death of the thrower. This dice can be used for nearly any situation where you wish to increase your odds at winning. For example, this dice is the key to winning valuable cards in the City of Gambling, Dorias. Translation Notes. In the 2011 anime and manga, the dice has "kanji" written on each surface 大吉 <- pronounced "Daikichi" here. It means "Very good/excellent Luck" 大凶 <- pronounced "Daikyō" here. It means "Great misfortune"

Ritz Family The Ritz Family (リッツファミリー, "Rittsu Famirī") is a Mafia clan. Background. The Ritz Family is an overarching Mafia clan, directly under the order of one of the Ten Dons. The Nostrade Family is associated with this clan. Plot. Yorknew City arc. Immediately after Worm appears in front of the Nostrade bodyguards, he introduces himself and asks what family they are from. Dalzollene answers the Ritz Family and adds that they are bodyguards for Light Nostrade.

Roaming Ruby (G.I card) Roaming Ruby (さまようルビー) is a card found in the Greed Island game. It is one of the game's 100 designated slot cards and is required for a player to complete the game. Summary. Roaming Ruby さまようルビー - This card when used, summons forth a beautiful Ruby. The owner of it will become immensely wealthy, with the condition that the owner cannot remain in the same place for more than a week. The ruby will break if this condition is broken. Your entire fortune as part of this card's effect, will also disappear.

Rock (G.I card) Rock (石) is a card found in the Greed Island game. This is a standard card that can be obtained by the player. These cards can be placed in the player's "Free Slots". Summary. This is a simple rock. It can be of any quality, material density and size.

Rock Toss (G.I card) Rock Toss (lit., rom. "Sutōn Surō") is a spell card found in the Greed Island game. It allows a player to destroy a random card from another player's free slots. Summary. This spell allows the caster to destroy a single card from another player's free slots.

Rodo Memorial Plates The Rodo [Company] Memorial Plates (, "Rodo-sha-sei Kinen Zara") is a series of collectable plates. Plot. Yorknew City arc. At the Sengi Guild, its agent manages to find three job offers that match Kurapika's request. One of the offers involves an antique collector seeking the plates from 1655 and 1657.

Rodriot Rodriot (ロドリオット, "Rodoriotto") is a professional Hunter hired by Battera to clear the game Greed Island. Appearance. Rodriot is a rotund man with a snub nose and dark skin. He wears a plain bandana until the dodgeball game against Razor, which reveals that he has short, fair hair on top and shaved sides. He wears the bandana again when he partakes in the first round of the 13th Hunter Chairman Election. He is most commonly seen wearing the same military-like attire as his teammates. Personality. He seems to be the most volatile among Tsezguerra's teammates. Background. At some point in his life, Rodriot took and passed a Hunter Exam and learned Nen. He, Barry, and Kess have been working with Tsezguerra for 20 years, and were hired by Battera to clear Greed Island. Plot. Greed Island arc. While on Greed Island, the team collects as many as 95 different specified slot cards before contacting the Bomber to trade. During the trade, Genthru diverts the team's attention while Sub and Bara steal two cards from each of them, breaking their monopolies and acquiring rare cards, among which are Rodriot's "Pre-Order Vouchers" and "Hypothetical T.V.". The Bombers then escape to Masadora. Rodriot urges Tsezguerra to give chase, but the Single-Star Hunter is against it, realizing that Genthru is in fact the Bomber. They resolve to find "Plot of Beach" before him and establish a monopoly. They thus head to Soufrabi. They are, however, unable to discover how to acquire the card. Not long after, Tsezguerra is contacted by Goreinu, who meets up with him and Rodriot to negotiate an alliance to get the card while Kess and Barry hide in the bushes. After listening to Goreinu's explanation of Razor's challenges, Rodriot volunteers for bowling. He and Kess go look for filler players while the others train for the rest of the week, after which the alliance confronts Razor and his pirates. Rodriot is the second to compete, defeating his opponent. Because of their victories in the previous matches, Kess, Rodriot, and Barry are unable to participate in the dodgeball game, so they watch from the sidelines, administering first aid to Tsezguerra and Gon. After their victory, Gon takes the original "Plot of Beach" while Tsezguerra's team settles for a copy. The Bombers immediately find out and threaten Tsezguerra, assuming that he has the original. He strikes a deal with Gon's group to hold off the Bomber for three weeks in return for "Wild Luck Alexandrite". They restock on transportation spells before meeting up with the Bombers. Tsezguerra's team refuses to hand over the card, and they take cards from the Bombers before escaping. Goreinu gives them the transportation spells he has collected. Nine days later, Rodriot checks the number of transportation spells in the Bombers' possession by feeding a "Chidon" card to a "Clairvoyant Snake". One week later, the Bombers fly to Tsezguerra's team. When they run out of transportation spells, they leave the game, only to find Battera's mansion empty except for Sabazushi and the billionaire himself, who has canceled the reward and locked himself in his room without explanation. When the Bombers arrive, Tsezguerra's team escape with Battera, quitting the game for good. They learn that Battera offered a reward for clearing the game so that he could save his comatose lover, but she died one month earlier. 13th Hunter Chairman Election arc. After the death of Chairman Netero, Rodriot and his teammates all take part in the first round of the 13th Hunter Chairman Election. Abilities & Powers. Rodriot is capable enough to have passed the notoriously difficult Hunter Exam. As one of the Hunters hired by Battera and a member of Tsezguerra's team, he is at least a decent Nen user, as confirmed later when Gon's team and Goreinu enlisted the help of other players to acquire "Plot of Beach". He is also a skilled bowling player, having defeated one of Razor's pirates. Nen. Due to being able to access Greed Island and being a Hunter, Rodriot is capable of utilizing Nen. Before the bowling game against one of Razor's pirates, Rodriot implied that he had a Nen ability particularly suited to that challenge.

Romaria Romaria (ロマリア, "Romaria") is an investigation officer at the Midonite Government Environment Protection Bureau, and while investigating ruins, she requests the work of the Hunter Association. She is a video game-only character from . Appearance. Romaria is a woman of average height, she has navy blue eyes, long cerulean-colored hair that is kept in place by a yellow headband, and three bang strands that are on the left, right, and middle side of her head as well as long sideburns, and she has an almond-shaped head. She wears a navy-colored blazer over a white long-sleeved shirt, plain tan pants, and brown shoes. Personality.
