For the most part, Romaria keeps a professional persona and is never afraid to use her position as a government official in sticky situations. She also has an intellectual side as she has extensive knowledge of the ruins she was tasked to inspect and preserve by her government. Plot. Altar of Dragon Vein. In the Wollow Forest, Romaria and Ponzu are surrounded by three men. Romaria tries to reason with the men; however, Ponzu sees the futility in that. At that moment, Gon and Killua arrive and defeat the men. One of the men warns the group not to enter the forest and flee. With the hostile situation settled, Romaria thanks the two and learns they are associated with the Hunter Association. The group then meets with Chairman Netero in his airship, and they are now accompanied by Leorio. Romario introduces herself to Netero as an agent of the Midonite Government Environment Protection Bureau and gives her reason for being in the Wollow Forest. Furthermore, Ponzu details that she was assigned to protect Romaria as her special mission. Romaria then elaborates on the request from her government to investigate and protect a newly discovered ruins within the Wollow Forest. However, strange forces at work impede their process, which is why they seek the assistance of the Hunter Association. Gon chimes in and deduces that the men in the forest who attacked her may be connected to said forces, to which, Romaria agrees. She believes the men were hired bounty hunters while the blue wolves were cooperating with them and that they all belong to some secret organization. Killua then asks Romaria why to hire rookies like them, whereas, Netero answers it's cheaper to hire Rookie Hunters. Continuing with the topic at hand, Romaria gives the Hunter group their first assignment of investigating the Forest Ruins in the Wollow Forest. In the group's report, it's revealed that they weren't able to investigate the ruins, but they did encounter a boy named Sabaki and Hisoka. Curious as to why anyone would want to impede the ruin's research, Netero believes that they know what is inside the ruins and want it for themselves. He also believes that the ruins entrance may be sealed by Nen; Romaria inquires what that is, and Netero briefly explains it. Romaria ponders that Nen may seal the entrance, though Gon thinks otherwise. Netero then advises the boys not to try and open the door by force, and Gon asks Romaria if she has any clues that could help. Romaria then gives details of another ruin on a rocky wall and believes it's related to the Forest Ruins. However, she has no other information on the location as forces also impede on that location as well. When the group returns from their excursion from the Underground Ruins, they return with Kurapika, who, although injured in their encounter, recovers quickly and offers his services. Thankful for his offer, Romaria tries to mention that she is unable to pay for his services; Kurapika offers them for free as he has a score to settle with Amane. In response to the group's desire to explore other ruins, Romaria details that she has no further information on any other new ruins. Kurapika chimes in and claims that he knows of an abandoned mansion where the newly mentioned leader of the impeding forces Zegin is. After exploring Zegin's Mansion, it's learned that Zegin's group objective is the Dragon Vein. Hearing this, Romaria deducts that the Dragon Vein is connected with the art of and elaborates on its concept involving an energy force known as 'Ki'. Basically, a Dragon Vein is a culmination of Ki produced from the surrounding earth, water, and terrain. Though this is all, she has learned in her tenure as a case officer in the government. In Netero's perspective, 'Ki' is a nuance of Nen. Romaria then discloses that the unnatural energy force they found congregates close to the Forest Ruins and theorizes that the location is an underground cave and lake area. In contrast, it acts as a giant 'Ki' storehouse. Netero then discloses that their primary objective is to keep the doors to the Forest Ruins sealed. Sometime after Zegin infiltrates the Hunter Association airship, it's revealed that Zegin's primary goal is to use the Dragon Vein as an aura amplifier. Learning Zegin's goal Romaria admonishes that if the government had not explored the ruins beforehand, Zegin would not have discovered the Dragon Vein. On the other hand, Netero reassures her that he already knew beforehand and compliments Romaria for her vital information that had gotten them this far. With the incident in the Forest Ruins behind them, the group brings Sabaki back to the airship infirmary, and Romaria looks after him. She details that she did what she could and suggests that he be treated in a hospital. Though the altar the Dragon Vein was stored in was destroyed, she concludes that the government would have sealed the ruins to prevent further meddling from people with evil goals like Zegin and his group. She plans to give a full report to her superiors, and until then, she decides to look after Sabaki while the Hunter group gives their information to Netero. The moment Sabaki awakens from his coma, he goes on a rampage and destroys the interior and the airship's 2nd engine. The Hunter group encounters Romaria in the airship hallway, and she informs them when she lets Sabaki out of her sight for a few moments, he vanishes and goes on the rampage. Taking the initiative, Gon confronts Sabaki; though Romaria tries to dissuade Gon, Netero allows it. The Hunter group with Netero and Romario, all in a brand new airship, with the prior one destroyed by Sabaki's rampage, discuss the matters at hand. Feeling guilty for all the unforeseen events due to her request, she humbly apologizes. Netero, on the other hand, thanks her since, had she not posted the request, Zegin would have gotten away with his plan. Upon Gon and Killua's brief excursion in the Wollow Forest, they meet and befriend a fellow Hunter named Ogyu, who joins them on the airship. Ogyu introduces himself and his occupation as a Card Hunter, which perplexes Romaria. The Hunter then details the profession and explains his goal of collecting the 5 Goddess Advent Cards and that four of the Goddess Advent Cards he managed to collect were stolen from him. This perturbs Romaria, which is why Ogyu is so frantic about the situation. So Ogyu teams up with the Hunter group and manages to retrieve four of the goddess cards that were stolen from him. Romario compliments the artwork of each card as mystical. While all seemed well, Ogyu makes an astounding revelation that one of the cards wasn't one of them that he managed to collect. The disclosure of this turn of event has Ogyu and the Hunter group hunt and locate the final card with the help of a reluctant Sabaki. With all five Goddess Advent Cards at hand, Ogyu makes his wish. Concerned if Ogyu was satisfied with his wish, Ogyu reassures her that he is. So with the departure of Sabaki, Romaria excuses herself, and her report for the Preservation Department of the Midonite Government Environment Protection Bureau is complete, so Ogyu offers to take her to her destination in his car, and she agrees. The two watch as the Hunter airship takes off and heads off to places unknown.

Rorgo Rorgo ("ローゴ, Roogo") is an antagonist in the video game "" with connections to the Four Heavenly Kings and the darker side of Sunaka. He appears in Kurapika's route and briefly Leorio's. He is interested in the Scarlet Eyes and is one of the mafiosos in Sunaka. Appearance. Rorgo is a well-built man with a tan complexion. His most notable characteristic is his blonde and red hair bearing a ponytail at the back. A mustache can be seen on his lip. Clothing-wise, his outfit consists of white martial arts attire and a red belt. Personality. Rorgo is a man interested in the Scarlet Eyes. He is described as an 'Eyeball Collector' and kidnapped Clario after mistaking her for Kurapika. When in public, he puts on a formal facade. However, he is a cruel mafioso who easily bypasses the law. He also desires to fight Kurapika alone, refusing to kill him when Tron and Izunavi get involved. Background. One of Don Gappai's Four Heavenly Kings, Rorgo is a man obsessed with collecting eyeballs akin to Neon. He also leads his own group of men, consisting of Doro, Shives, Surirao, and Donal. Rorgo and his subordinates are all Nen users. Prior to the game event, Rorgo met Chrollo. This would cause him to become interested in the troupe and the Scarlet Eyes. He is skilled in Emission. He uses seven aura-based boomerangs as weapons. </poem> </tabber> Plot. "Each One's Determination". Rorgo is first mentioned in Kurapika's first chapter. The rookie hunter at a local Cyber Cafe attempts to find more information on Sunaka. After unlocking the website, various results appear. Among them are those of a man named Rorgo and pages on the Scarlet Eyes. Kurapika concludes that Rorgo has some form of connection to them. Later, as he talks to Clario, she accidentally reveals him as a guest attending the VIP party. A morning news report further confirms this. When Kurapika tracks down Sansho, the fake hunter threatens to have Rorgo get involved, which only angers the former. Here, Sansho claims that he does, in fact, have the eyes and runs off. At the VIP party, a disguised Kurapika briefly talks to Rorgo. He attempts to question him on his eyeball collection. However, this only results in Rorgo dismissing it as a 'trivial hobby.' After Clario is found and chased after, she accidentally tears apart the collector's shirt. On his back, a spider tattoo can be seen. Unbeknownst to Kurapika, this results in his own eyes becoming scarlet. Sometime after Kurapika finishes his Nen training, Rorgo kidnaps Clario. This is from him mistaking her for Kurapika. Learning the truth, he considers killing her until he realizes she could be used as bait. Thus, he keeps her alive and has her interrogated. After Kurapika and Clario run away from the collapsing mansion, Rorgo follows them. Kurapika attempts to use his newfound chain abilities against him. However, they are easily destroyed by them lacking any Nen restrictions. Tron and Izunavi are forced to step in to help. Rorgo declares that he will be at Logos Island, waiting for Kurapika. The group thus manages to escape from Rorgo. A week later, Kurapika arrives via boat. He is told by Majtani that Rorgo refuses to fight him until he deals with his henchmen first. After defeating each one, Kurapika finds a spider tattoo with a code letter and message. The boy presumes Rorgo is attempting to anger him and cause his eyes to turn scarlet. Once he uses the code at a nearby waterfall, Rorgo appears at the top. The duo proceeds to fight each other. After the first round, Rorgo commends him, claiming that the Phantom Troupe struggled to kill the other Kurta Clan members. This has Kurapika realize that he knows the brigade. Before he can question him, the mafioso uses the opportunity to use Seventh Boomerang multiple times throughout. After a few more rounds, Kurapika questions him one last time about his connection to the troupe and his spider tattoo. This gives Rorgo the idea to lie about being a member, outright claiming to have helped during the Kurta Clan massacre. This results in Kurapika becoming enraged and using Emperor Time against him. With Rorgo properly defeated, Kurapika demands to know where the other members are. This causes Rorgo to admit he is not actually a member. After meeting them, he became inspired and wished to join their ranks. He describes himself as being a fan of theirs. When Kurapika begins questioning him on his Scarlet Eyes collection, Rorgo jumps into the nearby waterfall. Believing him to be dead, Kurapika somberly leaves. While Kurapika attempts to be hired by the Nostrade family, it is revealed that Rorgo survived. Once Kurapika obtains Sara's hair, the two run into each other near the family's mansion. Rorgo claims to be there for Don Gappai, his boss. He then comments that the Kurta member underestimated him and proceeds to fight him for multiple rounds. Rorgo then attempts to use his black boomerang against him. However, the younger boy catches it and survives. As Rorgo approaches, Kurapika then uses Emperor Time. After defeating him, Rorgo is questioned about the Scarlet Eyes. Rorgo claims to have never had them to begin with, then taunts Kurapika. He then passes out in front of him. In Leorio's route, Rorgo is briefly seen talking to Donal. The duo discusses the cloning procedures conducted by Donal, with Rorgo mentioning him not meeting his quota. He orders him to get to work and leaves the facility. Abilities & Powers. In-game, he is skilled in the likes of Nen and can overpower his opponents through his physical strength. His martial arts outfit implies that he is proficient in the field. He is also occasionally shown using a knife in battle. For his Cyber Mobile description, he is described as being an Emitter.

Roto Mountains Roto Mountains (, "Rōto Sanmyaku") are mountains in the Republic of Rokario. Overview. The mountains of Roto are a group of mountains that are located in the central-southern part of the Republic of Rokario and that intersects into the Republic of Hass. Plot. Chimera Ant arc. The Roto Mountains' location appears on Killua's Beatle-07 map.

Rottfelli Rottfelli (ロットフェリ, "Rottoferi") is a Mafioso and a new client of Neon Nostrade. Plot. Yorknew City arc. En route to her hotel in Yorknew City, Neon receives her September assignments and complains about them since there are more than usual. Dalzollene explains that Mr. Rottfelli and Mr. Trink wanted their fortunes told. He assures Neon that they are close friends of her father.

Round Turtle The Round Turtle is an anime-only animal in the 1999 anime adaptation. Appearance. The Round Turtle has a sphere-shaped shell, an elongated neck, drowsy eyes, and a beak. Behavior. When a Round Turtle starts rolling it tends to not stop. Plot. Hunter Exam arc. A tour guide to the animal show held on Whale Island introduces the Round Turtle and details that once it starts rolling it doesn't stop and that its name is "Kameira-"chan"". Later, Gon releases all of the caged animals at the animal show.

Rover Rover (コロ, "Koro") was a "human-dog" of Yunju. Rover's name was given by the latter upon subjugating and owning him as a "pet", his real name is unknown. Appearance. He is an average man who is practically bald, presumably because of the extreme amount of stress from being cruelly abused by Yunju as well as the constant impending doom of being executed by the latter. He also wore no clothes, with only a collar and leash around his neck, as per the Chimera Ant's will. Much like Spot, his tears never stopped in his appearances. Personality. With his mind, body, and spirit were broken by being "tamed" by Yunju, he and Spot acted like a 'human-dog' and was constantly fearful and terrified for his life. Together, they did everything in their power to try and survive under the cruel reign of Yunju, no matter how pitiful it was. Background. He was one of Gyro's men until being made into a pet by Yunju. Plot. Chimera Ant arc. After Yunju's team attack the hidden D² Manufacturing Plant in NGL, Spot and him are made human-dogs by the Chimera Ant Squadron Leader. When Kite, Gon and Killua arrive at the plant, Spot begs for help. Yunju intervenes by killing Spot and then decides to kill Rover as well. Not wanting to be killed, Rover attempts to act like a dog in hopes of pleasing the cruel Chimera Ant, but doing so only has made Yunju want to kill him even more. Before dying, Rover screams for help to Kite and his group, but is immediately killed there after.

Royal Glam Hotel Royal Glam Hotel (ロイヤルグラムホテル, "Roiyaru Guramu Hoteru") is the highest-class hotel in Glam Gas Land. Overview. The Royal Glam Hotel can seat over a thousand people for performances held there and it has the largest and grandest stage in all of the land. Putting on a successful performance on that stage guarantees you success in the entertainment world and all performers dream of performing on there, even if just once. All performances are witnessed by the head of the Glam Clan and any applause given by him are extolling and is said to be the tantamount of being recognized as a global level. Plot. Hisoka's Past spin-off. The Moritonio Troupe put on a spectacular performance in the Royal Glam Hotel and earn unbridled applause from not only the audience but also the head of the Royal Glam Clan.

Royal Guards The Elite Royal Guards (, "Ō Chokuzoku Goei-gun"—lit. "King Immediate Guard Force"; formerly, "Joō Chokuzoku Goei-gun"—lit. "Queen Immediate Guard Force") were three Chimera Ants entrusted with the responsibility of protecting the Ant King Meruem from enemies and any harm. Furthermore, they offered their assistance and counsel to help him fulfill the biological project laid out for him by his mother. In the case of the Royal Guards serving Meruem, however, the latter's imperative began to threaten the integrity of the trio when the King's wishes began to change. Background. Like other Chimera Ants, the Royal Guards are born through phagogenesis, but are genetically stronger than any other soldier Ant due to their position on the Chimera Ant hierarchy, and hatch with the ability to use Nen. The Royal Guards are designed to protect and serve their King, and to enforce this, they require more power than common Ants. The Chimera Ant Queen in NGL devoured hundreds of normal and Nen-using humans, and gave birth to Ants far stronger than average ones. Their genetic destiny gave the Royal Guards more strength, aura, and talent in Nen than their subordinates. As a result, dozens of other Chimera Ants refer to them as 'special beings', because of the power they possess. The guards assigned to Meruem were: They are supposed to fight the Ant King's enemies and fulfill his every wish. Despite their loyalty to the biological project of domination laid out by the Chimera Ant Queen, they have no use for her person or interest in her well-being whatsoever after the birth of the King, leaving her to die despite having the power to save her. Plot. Chimera Ant arc. Amid the Chimera Ant Queen's founding of her NGL nest, she conceives the three Royal Guards. One day, she summons all her Squadron Leaders and demands them to deliver her 50 humans a day. Turtle asks the Queen if they might have names and explains their meaning to the Queen. After giving her consent, the Queen goes to where the eggs of the Royal Guards and amusedly decides to name the Guards herself. The eldest of the Guards, Neferpitou, awakens during Pokkle's confinement within the nest. Their sinister aura is immediately recognized by their fellow Ants, such as Rammot and Peggy. Neferpitou asks Rammot about "gifts", to which Rammot is happy to explain to them. However, Neferpitou senses Pokkle's presence and has him killed. They start rummaging through Pokkle's brain in search of answers about the "gifts", which they consequently learn as "Nen". Under Pitou's supervision, Rammot takes the Water Divination test. Pitou also participates, revealing them to be a Specialist. During the initiation of the Squadron Leaders, Pitou senses Kite's aura and leaves the nest to battle him. The next morning, Pitou orders for the Ants to create a freezer to preserve Kite's corpse, while Kite's head is resting on their lap. Once back in the nest, Pitou's desire to battle once again with Kite manifests in their Nen ability, Doctor Blythe. Chairman Netero's team arrives near the nest, but they cannot go further due to Neferpitou's vast, irregular En. Morel Mackernasey uses his smoke to create bunnies that can determine how many Ants are present in the nest. While Pitou contemplates their actions about them, a second Royal Guard suggests that they wait and see. He introduces himself as Shaiapouf, and tells Pitou that Menthuthuyoupi will also awaken soon. In the next few days, more and more squadrons mysteriously disappear. Colt and Peggy ask Pitou for advice, but Pitou allows them to handle everything outside the nest. Moreover, they say that the Royal Guard will defend the nest. Sometime in between, the youngest of the Guards, Menthuthuyoupi, is already born. Suddenly, the Queen feels intense pain. Shaiapouf and Neferpitou immediately identify it as the birth of the King. After the newly born King Meruem kills some of his subordinates, the three Guards appear and introduce themselves to him. They have also prepared his food. The King follows his Guards, leaving the Queen writhing in pain. Colt runs after the Guards and begs for Pitou to heal the Queen with the same ability they used to heal Kite. However, Pitou refuses, since they needed Kite and the Queen means nothing to the Royal Guards, now that the King is born. Ignoring Colt, Pitou explains that the King's meal is outside. Meruem punches a hole in the wall and climbs to the top. His Guards follow suit, Shaiapouf flying and Menthuthuyoupi copying Pouf's wings. The King, finding the food bland, demands to eat the same delicious food the Queen ate. Pitou identifies them as the "rares" and grants the King's demand. The King and his Royal Guards fly over the fields and come upon a small farm. Meruem feeds on the surrounding humans but remains unsatisfied. Neferpitou offers some more advice, to which the King hits them with his tail for Pitou's mockery. The King explains how he knows, and also commends Pitou for surviving his attack. Back in the nest, Colt has successfully enlisted Morel and Knov's help to give the Queen medical assistance. However, her injuries are too severe. In her last moments, the Queen states that her son's name is Meruem and that it means "light that illuminates all". As the Queen lies lifeless, Colt discovers that there is a small baby left inside the Queen's womb. He vows to protect the child, with Morel also promising to protect both of them as long as they do not eat humans anymore. Crossing over countries, the King and his entourage reach the Republic of East Gorteau. Soldiers arrive to confront the Ants, but the King kills them effortlessly and feeds on one of the rare human soldiers. They later find Ming Jol-ik hosting entertainment in a room. After the dictator's series of threats, the King kills him and Neferpitou suggests they can use the corpse to control the humans. Meruem finds a courtyard behind the palace, and, liking the view, decides it will be a meat orchard wherein to process humans to Chimera Ant soldiers. Shortly afterward, Pitou starts using the corpse to manipulate the East Gorteau citizens into rallying in the palace within ten days. Morel informs the others that Colt thinks it might be some kind of ploy. With a time limit of ten days, the Chimera Ant Extermination Team splits into four groups: Gon Freecss and Killua Zoldyck versus Neferpitou; Knuckle Bine and Shoot McMahon against Menthuthuyoupi; Morel and Knov against Shaiapouf; and Chairman Netero against Meruem. Nine days before the selection, Pitou senses someone disabling their puppets. They decide whether it is an assassin and a decoy, but after getting frustrated at being unable to fight, they go and ask for Pouf's advice. Shaiapouf suggests that Pitou should not go, thinking it only as a ploy of their enemies to lure them. Instead of fighting the enemies themselves, Pouf suggests to let others take care of it, while the Royal Guards focus on protecting the King. Leol's Squad comes forward and receives an order from Pitou to get rid of the assassin. Once they leave, Youpi asks Pitou if it is okay to trust Leol, but Pitou knows they want to earn their trust first, before finding the opportunity to stab them in the back. Two days later, the King begins challenging champions of various board games. Shaiapouf accompanies him and introduces the champions, while Menthuthuyoupi drags them one after the other. The King keeps playing games, until the Gungi world champion Komugi enters and defeats him in every single match. At length, Shaiapouf becomes concerned with the King's continuous losses and his listening to Komugi, but he decides to ignore it for now. In the next game, the King proposes a bet, where he would give anything Komugi wants if she wins but would take her life if she loses. Komugi, on the other hand, offers her life instead, explaining that she is useless to her family if she ever loses in Gungi. Realizing that Komugi might have asked for his life, the King calls himself imprudent and proceeds to rip his left arm as a form of apology. Shaiapouf immediately reacts and asks the King to have it tended. Meruem insists on playing and subsequently hits the Royal Guard when Pouf proves to be stubborn. Komugi refuses to play as well, telling the King that she would not play until his arm is better. Annoyed, the King sends for Neferpitou. Neferpitou summons Doctor Blythe and tends to the King wound, while the latter continues playing Gungi. In the room's corner, the two Royal Guards confide to each other: since Doctor Blythe requires Pitou's energy, they cannot use the puppets or En to monitor the area. Shaiapouf, although admitting that his En is nowhere near Pitou's range, proposes that he would be on the lookout for the time being. Unbeknownst to them, one of the Hunters—Knov—has managed to infiltrate the palace grounds during the absence of Pitou's En. Knov reaches until the central stairway, where he senses a sinister smoke-like aura from the second floor. Knowing that he cannot proceed any further, he places an exit by the staircase. He successfully exits the palace, though the previous encounter with Pouf's aura gives him a mental breakdown. Deep underground, another Hunter—Palm Siberia—infiltrates the palace due through Bizeff, and after drugging him, takes an elevator that leads to the palace. Three days before the selection, Shaiapouf notices that Komugi is at her physical and mental limit, which would ensure the victory of the King in the next game. However, Meruem allows the girl to have a break and leaves the room. Perceiving that she is a liability and might pose problems in the future, an idea crosses Pouf's mind. He stops himself before he could do anything rash, thinking that he if kills her now, then Meruem would never be able to defeat her in Gungi anymore. The next day, Shaiapouf gives reports to the King, but the latter scolds him and orders the Guards to do everything. Chased out of the room, Pouf joins Youpi outside, who is amused to see him. Pouf expresses his worry about the King's losses, but Youpi assures him that there is no need to worry. On their post, Neferpitou senses that someone disables their puppets, whom they identify as someone who uses smoke puppets. They express their want to fight him, but they cannot leave their post. On the last night before the selection, Komugi requests to take a break, to which the King allows. Before she can leave the room, he asks for her name. She answers and asks for his name as well. Realizing that he has no name of his own, the King summons his three Royal Guards to answer his question. Shaiapouf answers that he is the one and only "King", Menthuthuyoupi deems himself unable to provide for an answer, while Neferpitou proposes that the King can choose a name he feels personal. The King falls silent for a while, and after some encouragement from Pouf, he confides that Komugi's body was bathed in light. He starts to understand the capacity of his powers, which reduces Pouf to tears. Pouf admits that he failed as a Royal Guard for nearly insulting the King. The two other Guards acknowledge the change in the King since Komugi's arrival; Youpi suggests that if she becomes too much a problem, then they should kill her, much to Pouf's relief. The next day, the citizens receive instructions to gather in front of the palace at 3 PM. The Royal Guards are gathered in a balcony overlooking the fields. Pitou informs them that they sense new enemies, and all three conclude that the most dangerous part of the selection is during the sorting. Since the King wants to participate personally, the Guards decide that someone should stay by the King's side, despite the latter's annoyance of their presence. Shaiapouf proposes to be the one to do the job. Later that day, the King confronts Pitou about the previous attack of a hawk on Komugi and orders them to watch over Komugi as well. Once the citizens are outside the palace, Pouf uses his scales to hypnotize them. Despite the King's annoyance, Menthuthuyoupi follows him, which earns him a smack to the face. Neferpitou amusedly notes that all three Royal Guards are now hit by the King. Youpi flies towards Pitou and informs them that the King is irritated with the latter's En. The King and Pitou come to the conclusion that the Guard could only use En on the palace's first floor, so as not to invade the King's privacy. Due to the change of plans, Shaiapouf posts Youpi to guard the central stairway for any underground attacks. Welfin encounters Youpi on the staircase while investigating an intruder's trails. The Guard warns him of going upstairs. Welfin questions Youpi about the extent of Pitou's En, and learns that Pouf had been in charge of the security when the King was injured. Neferpitou notices something and suddenly looks up into the skies. They direct their aura towards the skies; both Pitou and Pouf see that the creature descending towards the palace is a shining dragon, from which two riders jump off. Confronted by Zeno Zoldyck and Isaac Netero, Pitou becomes excited and turns off their En to prepare for battle. However, their plan backfires when the dragon splits into a multitude of smaller dragons raining to the palace. Pouf immediately defies the King's orders and flies to his location. Unable to find the two humans, Pitou leaps into the air and comes across Netero. They use their Terpsichora to fight, but Netero only chuckles and tells the Guard that they chose a bad move. Netero uses his 100-Type Guanyin Bodhisattva to force Pitou to several miles away. To keep themself in the fight, Pitou summons Doctor Blythe, its restrictions stopping Pitou. They watch as the dragons penetrate the palace. Meanwhile, the Extermination Team encounters Youpi on the stairway, when the dragons rain upon them. Youpi transforms himself to counter the danger at hand. Unbeknownst to him, the invisible Knuckle and Meleoron approach and hit him, thereby activating Knuckle's Hakoware. Shaiapouf arrives in the throne room and finds no King, but he smiles silently to himself. A confused Youpi thinks about the sudden attack on him, but he doesn't find anything detrimental. With the Hunters passing him by, he transforms yet again, producing numerous eyes on his head and arms. The transformation leaves Knuckle in awe, who believes that the Guard's aura might be limitless. Outside the palace, Pitou uses En to locate the King, realizing that the two enemies are also using En to locate him. Pitou rushes to the King but regrets it when they feel the King's negative aura. Once inside, Pitou finds the King holding Komugi's wounded body. After gently laying Komugi's body on the floor, the King asks for Pitou to heal her. With tears in their eyes, Pitou complies. The King suggests that they should fight somewhere else. Netero agrees for he enlisted Zeno's help for that sole purpose. When Pitou activates their aura, Netero and Zeno are momentarily distracted that it allows the King to easily walk past them. Then, the central stairway crashes under Youpi's strength, splitting the intruders. Morel's Deep Purple attacks Youpi, while Knuckle punches the Guard one more time. Another unseen attack enrages Youpi. Shoot keeps Youpi occupied while giving Morel the chance to find his opponent, Shaiapouf. In the throne room, Pouf has a breakdown, scolding himself for failing as a Royal Guard; he knew from the start where the King is, but still did not go there. When he finally decides to go, Morel confronts him and traps themselves inside Smoky Jail. In retaliation, Pouf uses his Spiritual Message. Netero and Zeno separate the King from his Royal Guards. While Gon and Killua enter the tower where Pitou is, Shoot continues evading Youpi's attacks and manages to take a single eye from the Guard's shoulder and store it in his Hotel Rafflesia. Youpi's increasing caution makes his attacks deadlier, to the point where he almost whittles Shoot's life. Knuckle and Meleoron watch invisibly in the sidelines as the onslaught continues. After ten seconds, Knuckle becomes impatient and decides to attack Youpi. Meleoron stops him from attacking recklessly. One of Youpi's claws nicks Knuckle on the cheek, and the interest in A.P.R is cut in half. The two of them hide for a moment to let Meleoron catch his breath. Just then, Youpi notices the presence of A.P.R.. Agitated, Youpi believes Shoot is the source and fires needles made from his own body. Shoot, knowing that he cannot dodge it, uses his two floating hands to punch him and propel him backward. As Shoot is approaching his limit, Knuckle suddenly shows himself and calls out for the Guard. Youpi then realizes that A.P.R. actually belongs to Knuckle. Morel confronts Shaiapouf in the throne room. Enveloped by Smoky Jail, Pouf takes the opportunity to use Spiritual Message to read Morel's emotions—vigilance, resolve, and confidence. Pouf introduces himself but receives no reply from Morel. He resorts to enveloping himself inside a cocoon and asks for the Hunter to wait for his rebirth, but Morel remains confident despite whatever creature might emerge afterward. After encountering Zeno, Gon and Killua proceed to Neferpitou. Gon angrily introduces himself, but Pitou does not hear him. Instead, the Guard is focused on completing the King's orders and protect Komugi. Killua tries to analyze why Pitou is not summoning any aura to fight Gon and is reminded that Pitou appears to be protecting Komugi. Gon, however, only sees a dismantled Kite in place of Komugi and demands Pitou to fight him. Pitou lays both hands on the ground in a sign of surrender and begs for Gon to wait. Killua realizes that Komugi must have been hurt during Zeno's Dragon Dive and it is the King's order that Pitou should heal her. As Gon closes in on Pitou, they keep imploring for him to wait, explaining that they have to save the girl, that she is someone special to the King. Gon is conflicted with the situation and directs his increasing anger to both Killua and Neferpitou. Pitou then breaks their left arm and offers to break any part of their body that is not required for the healing. They beg again to let them save Komugi. Gon breaks down and releases a strong surge of aura, ignoring Pitou and Killua's pleads. Gon prepares to use his Jajanken, but Killua once again distracts him, reminding him that they cannot save Kite if Pitou is dead. Gon dismisses Killua's calmness and tells him that the mission means nothing to Killua anyway. He asks Pitou how long he has to wait; Pitou answers they need at least four hours, but Gon deems that too long. Pitou begs for an hour to stabilize her to ensure her survival. Gon makes Pitou promise that they will go to Peijin in an hour, to fix Kite. Then he sits in front of Pitou to wait for an hour, while Killua disappears from the room. Menthuthuyoupi remains occupied with the Hunters and attacks A.P.R.. He demands an answer from Knuckle, but Knuckle runs away from him. Shoot collapses to the ground, but Meleoron is unable to help him since his mission is to help others with his abilities. He leaves the room and spots Morel's Smoky Jail, concluding that Morel and Pouf must be in battle. He later decides to assist Gon and Killua but encounters Welfin on the way. Meanwhile, Youpi ceases his assault on Knuckle and goes to the first floor, looking for the King. He comes upon the Smoky Jail and calls out for the King and the two other Guards. Morel, hearing Youpi's voice, starts to question whether their plan is going in the right direction. Shaiapouf reads Morel's emotions and identifies suspicion, anxiety, and impatience, but those are not enough to sway Morel's resolve—an admirable feat deemed by Pouf. Getting more irritated, Youpi returns to his original position and finds Knuckle waiting for him there. In his anger, Youpi begins to change forms and attacks Knuckle. His sheer strength destroys the entire building. His rage keeps building up and explodes in the area, creating a massive crater. Youpi starts to understand the nature of his own power, and he detaches himself from his ego to fight with passion for his master and with a presence of mind. He calls out for his opponents, drawing them to him with his false rage. Shaiapouf disperses himself as microscopic bugs small enough to slip between Morel's smoke. Without Morel noticing, Pouf escapes Smoky Jail. Knuckle plans that he has to confront Youpi again. With his target on sight, Youpi keeps raging and pretending to be extremely angry, shouting at both Knuckle and A.P.R.. The Guard starts morphing again and Knuckle takes the opportunity to land another hit on Youpi. However, as Knuckle swoops in for the punch, Youpi suddenly reverts to his normal self and catches the Hunter off-guard. Youpi's hand morphs into a gigantic fist and attempts to kill Knuckle with a single punch. Suddenly, Killua's Thunderbolt hits Youpi, which renders him paralyzed for a few moments. Then Knuckle takes advantage of Youpi's dazed moment to punch him on the face. He assaults Youpi with a barrage of punches, before escaping once again. More confused now, Youpi tries to analyze the situation and looks up to see Killua approaching him. Killua bombards him with his electric attacks, making it impossible for Youpi to either attack or transform. Finally, Killua uses all his aura and attempts to escape as well. Youpi chases after him but loses Killua's trace in an instant. He figures it is an ability that lets them disappear at will. Morel destroys the cocoon, much to Pouf's surprise, as he did not think the Hunter would do it. Morel deactivates his Smoky Jail and finds Pouf outside the throne room. He explains that it is Shaiapouf's lack of reaction that made Morel understand that he was not inside. In his defense, Pouf explains that it was his plan to kill the other Hunters one-by-one, while Morel is distracted inside the smoke. Morel laughs it off, stating that Pouf has a low opinion of him. However, Pouf disagrees, countering that he gives Morel too much credit. Then, Pouf disperses himself again to thousands of particles, transforming them into smaller versions of himself. Morel attacks the smaller versions with his Deep Purple, but Pouf's clones can divide and reassemble once destroyed. The real Shaiapouf appears behind him and steals his pipe, then he knocks Morel to the ground as he flies away. Without his pipe, Morel is practically defenseless. Youpi then appears behind him and asks if he is the teleporter. Knuckle also appears behind Youpi and demands what happened to Shoot, who has disappeared from his original post. Morel transforms his smoke to resemble Knuckle and uses them to assault Youpi. Youpi produces several tentacles to fight the smoke, anticipating that the real Knuckle would attack him. He is confident that he can impale Knuckle and tactfully leaves an opening for Knuckle to hit. One clone comes close to the opening, but when Youpi hits it, it disperses into smoke. All the Knuckle clones disappear, with Morel taunting Youpi that there never was a real one. Extremely angered, Youpi starts transforming again. The real Knuckle lands a punch just before the Guard could explode. Shaiapouf discards Morel's pipe in a nearby river. He plans to locate the King and uses his Beelzebub ability to find him. His clones find Neferpitou tending to Komugi, with a boy sitting next to them, identified as an enemy. Other clones fine Hina with Shidore and Bizeff stalked behind by Welfin. He also identifies the human captured a few days earlier and Youpi fighting about 50 enemies. Feeling confident with Youpi, Pouf decides to go to Pitou. Neferpitou begs that he shouldn't come any closer. Pouf questions why Pitou should be fearful when he could have killed Gon from behind. Pitou explains that they cannot risk Komugi's safety. As the two Guards discuss, Gon demands Pouf to shut up. Sensing that he is needed, Pouf attempts to leave, but Gon stops him since he can manipulate people with his scales. Again, Pitou begs to Pouf's compliance. Despite his confusion with Pitou's sudden change in behavior, Pouf agrees to stay as long as they inform him of what happened. Pouf wants Pitou to give subtle hints regarding the King's whereabouts, else there would be bloodshed in the room. In the field, Youpi studies his powers and starts to understand the consequences. Again, he feigns extreme anger to the point that his rage manifests into a new ability, Rage Incarnate. Upon witnesses the transformation, Morel and Knuckle are impressed with Youpi's inexhaustible aura. Youpi keeps attacking the smoke clones, while the two Hunters are merely waiting for Youpi to "bust". Neferpitou explains to Shaiapouf everything, subtly pointing to where the King and his enemies left. As Pouf realizes they went south, his clones disperse from his main body to go to the King. With Morel's energy vastly depleted, he could no longer move by the time all his smoke puppets are destroyed. Youpi acknowledges his admiration and respect for their strength. He moves to land a final blow to Morel, but Morel suddenly disappears. Again, he knows it is the teleporting ability and observes the blood on his blade. He follows the trail Morel leaves behind as Meleoron tries carrying him away. Knuckle shows himself to Youpi and pleads to let Morel and Meleoron go. Youpi refuses as it is not a fair trade. He would consider the offer if Knuckle removes A.P.R. on him. Meleoron leaves Morel to become visible. Faced with the consequence to save Morel's life, Knuckle removes A.P.R. as they all know they have no means to defeat Youpi now. Knuckle challenges the Guard to a fight. Youpi refuses and goads them to take Morel to a hospital, while he will go in search for the King. As he searches around the area, Youpi comes across Pouf, who explains everything that happened thus far. Together, they leave the palace. Meanwhile, Knuckle finds Shaiapouf's clone waiting with Gon and Pitou, and challenges him to a fight. Elsewhere, one of Pouf's smaller clones finds a confrontation between Killua and Palm, who was captured a few days before and was turned into "Experimental Specimen Number One". The clone urges Palm to finish Killua, but Palm, retaining her memories as human, crushes the clone instead. The real Shaiapouf senses the failed experiment. His other clone accepts Knuckle's challenge. However, the clone admits that his real body is on the way to the King. Knuckle confirms it since Morel told him earlier about Pouf's ability. He also asks why Pouf would tell him so, to which the Guard says to convince Gon. Gon, on the other hand, calls him a liar because Pouf initially wanted to kill Gon. He continues to warn Knuckle not to be tricked since it could be the real Shaiapouf standing with them, and not his clone. Everyone in the room realizes Gon's unwavering determination, and Pouf is mentally relieved that the boy is preoccupied with Pitou. Suddenly, the clone disperses into hundreds of smaller clones and tells everyone that he will be waiting at the front gates. In a panic, Pitou apologizes for Pouf's behavior. Gon orders them to heal Komugi ten minutes faster than what they agreed. With Komugi's healing time actually only one hour, Pitou agrees to the changes. They start thinking when and how to kill Gon without risking Komugi's safety since both their fellow Guards do not care for the girl. Gon then reassures Knuckle that he can handle the situation here. As the Poor Man's Rose detonates, Menthuthuyoupi and Shaiapouf watch it blaze from afar. They immediately understand the situation and rush faster. At the same time, Pouf's clone meets Knuckle but it escapes. The two Royal Guards arrive at the mouth of the explosion; Youpi goes inside the melting epicenter while he urges Pouf to search the area if ever the blast threw the King away. Youpi transforms yet again into a creature with multiple tentacles and eyes. As he searches the center, he finds something and starts to scream. Pouf cries before he could even reach Youpi, who now holds an extremely deformed and burned body of the King. Meruem opens his eyes, giving his Guards a little relief, but Youpi exclaims that they cannot take him back to Pitou in time. Instead, Pouf offers himself and orders his cells to heal the King. The latter becomes somewhat animated a little and describes the taste as an exquisite delicacy. He continues that now he has tastes as such, nothing else could satisfy him—which brings Pouf extreme happiness. Youpi also offers himself to the King, liquefying his cells. Meruem describes the taste like a rich depth of flavor, akin to dewdrops of angels. He demands more of these, to which his Guards are honored to provide, prompting them to tears. Then the King persuades them to call him "Meruem", as it is the name given by his mother. In the palace, Gon senses that the surgery is finished and demands Pitou to stand. Komugi awakens, asking what happened to her. Pitou starts to speak out, but Gon threatens to kill Komugi if Pitou speaks out of line again. As they are leaving, Knuckle, Killua, and Palm block the exit. Knuckle asks if he should use Hakoware on Pitou, but Gon declines as he trusts Pitou. Instead, he asks them to watch over Komugi, much to Pitou's horror. They both leave the palace and head towards Peijin to heal Kite. The King regenerates from his previous state and becomes stronger. Since Pouf and Youpi shared their cells to the King, they could feel him, as if sharing his body. That same moment they realize that the King is confused. They ask how the King feels or if he wants to feed again, but Meruem answers that he cannot remember why he is there. Then he asks why they both look small; Pouf answers that they sent their segments to find the enemies. Meruem threatens Pouf about lying to him. Pouf starts questioning him about his memories, and Meruem states that he remembers both of them but not recent events, leading Pouf to believe that the explosion must have caused a temporary memory loss. Pouf explains that the King had been in a battle with one of the enemies and tried cheating on him, but Meruem's memory conjures a blurry image of a different kind of battle. Youpi suggests that they should return to the palace so that the King could recover his memories faster. Pouf's clone, which was on its way to the palace, immediately turns back in an attempt to kill Komugi before the King remembers her. Meruem produces wings similar to that of Youpi's and flies towards the palace. Pouf fears that the King's speed would take him a mere five minutes to arrive. His clones reach the room but finds no Komugi there. Suddenly, an invisible Knuckle punches him, activating A.P.R.. Palm can also see Pouf through her abilities, giving him nothing to hide. Then, the King notices A.P.R. by Pouf's side, asking what it is. Pouf explains that one of his clones is hit by the enemies. By then the Hunters realize that the King is still alive. While the Hunters scramble for ideas on how to defeat the King, Youpi explains that A.P.R. is the enemy's ability and would not disappear until the enemy himself is hurt. To test that, Meruem uses Youpi's Rage Blast on the mascot, which surprises Youpi. He realizes that his power is not his own, but for the King. A.P.R. emerges unscathed from the attack. It leads Meruem to think that the ability was used on Youpi before. The Guard confirms this, and further explains that he let the enemy escape on the condition that Youpi lets his other friend live. Pouf scolds him for passing the opportunity to eliminate a threat. Youpi apologizes and accepts punishment, but the King says otherwise, only commending Youpi for answering his question truthfully. He goes on to say that since they share bodies now, they cannot keep secrets to each other. Pouf feels guilt but that does not stop him for searching for Komugi. His clones realize that Meleoron is a traitor and helps the enemies by turning them invisible. Palm tries to lure his clones into the underground warehouse, but Killua shows himself carrying Komugi on his back. Choosing between hunting after the traitor or the girl, Pouf's clones aim for Komugi. Killua dodges the attack, making Pouf aware of his incredible speed. Instead of chasing Killua with full power, the clone disperses into smaller clones and chase Killua away from the palace. Pouf exclaims that Killua should release the hostage, which makes Komugi suspicious of Killua. Furthermore, she recognizes Pouf's voice as someone from the palace. She starts struggling against Killua, giving Pouf the opportunity to attack the girl. The attack knocks her unconscious. Killua creates a circle around Komugi and himself and dares the clone to come closer. When it does, Killua's electricity burns away the cells. Finally, the King and his Royal Guards arrive above the palace. Pouf shows him the citizens hypnotized earlier and explains that it is the King's destiny to rule over them. However, the King feels something is amiss and demands that they show him the place where he usually stayed. Understanding that the Gungi pieces could trigger his memories, Pouf's clone abandons its attack on Killua and returns to the throne room to discard the Gungi board and pieces. At the same time, Gon and Neferpitou arrive in Peijin. One of Shaiapouf's clones overhears a conversation between Palm and Killua. He uses that to his advantage and manipulates also Welfin into calling Neferpitou and claiming that they have Komugi back. Using his Body Reconstruction ability, Pouf copies Komugi's face and voice to assure Pitou that Komugi is indeed "safe" with Welfin. Pitou understands and ends the call. Gon shows them Kite's body waiting inside a room. Since Gon respected their wishes earlier, they want to be honest as well, revealing that Kite is already dead. They explain that Kite died during their fight, and their ability could only keep the body from rotting and manipulate it. They apologize to Gon. While Gon suffers from a breakdown, Pitou summons Doctor Blythe to heal their broken left arm. Palm reacts to the sudden changes, and then Pouf's clone emerges from hiding and says that Pitou already believes Komugi is safe. Killua attacks the clone and leaves Komugi with Palm, while he himself uses Speed of Lightning to get to Gon. After Pitou's arm heals, they apologize once again and claim that they need to kill Gon for the King. Gon calls them a liar and starts summoning a powerful surge of aura, making Pitou summon Terpsichora. Pitou attacks Gon, but he disappears. They head outside the building, where they find a transformed Gon waiting by the door. Gon invites them to fight somewhere else. Pitou senses that Gon's power transformed himself to an age when he could defeat Pitou. They charge at Gon, who easily dodges it, and delivers a powerful Jajanken: Rock at the Guard. On the edge of losing consciousness, Pitou feels relief that Gon sacrificed never to use Nen again to achieve this kind of power, and that they will be the one to bear his rage. Killua catches up to Peijin, where he could see flashing lights. He finds Gon continuously using Rock to batter Neferpitou's already broken body. As Gon acknowledges Killua's presence, Terpsichora manipulates Pitou's body into attacking Gon. It successfully severs Gon's right arm, making Gon relieved that he could be the same as Kite. Pitou's Nen, after death, makes it a puppet with the sole purpose of killing Gon. Gon stabs Pitou through the chest using his own arm and then summons another surge of aura. Killua begs for Gon to stop, ending an explosion within the forest. Back in the palace, Youpi and Pouf come into a mental agreement never to let the King see Komugi. Pouf asks permission to hypnotize the humans again, while Youpi tells the King he would search for Pitou. At the mention of the name, Meruem remembers Pitou as one of his Royal Guards. Both Youpi and Pouf agree once more not to mention Komugi's name. The King orders Youpi to bring Pitou at once, while he would hunt down the remaining enemies. Pouf insists that the Guard should be with the King, but Meruem demands if any of them could defeat him. He then uses En to sense the enemies, immediately knocking both Knuckle and Meleoron unconscious and bringing them back in the throne room. He claims that two more reacted to his En, which makes Pouf believe that one of them has Komugi. To buy himself more time, Shaiapouf proposes a game to the King: Youpi and himself would search for Pitou, while the King looks for the two remaining enemies. This time, the King could only use En one more time. The King agrees and adds that he will grant them one wish if his Guards win. If they lose, however, he wants to know what they are hiding from him. He claims he can feel not only their feelings of guilt but also their strong devotion. Pouf promises that he would not stall for time while he is spreading his scales to the humans. Additionally, should Pitou come back, he would persuade Pitou into hiding. Meruem agrees and adds that the two enemies he sensed were an octopus and a human carrying something. Then the two Guards proceed into the game while the King stays in the room. Pouf disperses his scales before the humans could fully gain their consciousness. Meanwhile, at the west tower, Youpi waits for Pitou's arrival when he notices a truck leaving the underground warehouse. Welfin tells Youpi that Komugi is in the warehouse and asks him to tell the King right away. Deeming the Ants enemies now, Welfin asks the Guard if he remembers his past. Youpi answers that he is no one but a Royal Guard. Welfin asks another question and threatens that he will fight back if Youpi attacks. Annoyed, Youpi calls him a punk while blood drips from his nose. Shaiapouf finishes his task and heads back to the palace when he comes upon Youpi's corpse on the field. He immediately returns to the King and notifies him on Youpi's death. Since Pitou has not yet arrived, the King wants to commence the game, but Pouf tries to stop him. He is surprised the King has drawn a Gungi board on the ground, and later follows him outside the palace, desperate for Pitou's arrival. Then he stars coughing out blood. The King senses surprise but Pouf redirects his concern by asking if he has reconsidered. Instead, the King simply wants to hunt the enemies and uses En again, sensing several things all at once, including Youpi's corpse, an abandoned truck, footprints, and the open underground warehouse door. Then he senses someone new reacting to him and quickly identifies Welfin, demanding if he had been the one to kill Youpi. Welfin denies the allegation and explains that Youpi started coughing blood and died. The King claims that his En can now sense emotions, identifying dear and hostility towards the King in Welfin. Perceiving that Welfin's words could be trouble, Pouf convinces the King that Welfin is privy to his secret, therefore it could be spoiled. Meruem then demands if Welfin's malice has something to do with Pouf's secret, and the Guard only answers that he has no words to say. Suddenly, the King claims he is hungry and turns back to Welfin. Seized with extreme fear, Welfin instantly ages a hundred years. He forces himself to speak one word that could reveal Shaiapouf's secret, which he later utters as "Komugi". Pouf collapses into tears and accepts any punishment from the King. Meruem does not blame him and orders him to continue searching for Pitou, and then ask the two hostages and let them go afterward. He also thanks Welfin for letting him remember and asks where Komugi might be. Although Welfin answers, he shouts that he has no other King but Gyro. Meruem understands and coaxes Welfin to find Gyro and live a human life, shattering Pouf's ideals for his King. Meruem leaves in search of Komugi. Back in the field, Shaiapouf succumbs to the Miniature Rose's poison, dying alone. In his final moments with Komugi, the King reminisces his Royal Guards and says that they were too good for him.

Royal Palace of East Gorteau The Royal Palace of East Gorteau is a large estate located in the former Republic of East Gorteau just outside of the capital city of Peijin. It was the residence of Ming Jol-ik. Appearance. The palace is enclosed within tall, stone walls and surrounded by a wide courtyard. Located on the grounds are ten large trees with 500 cocoons each. There is a central stairway that leads to the throne room on the third floor. Plot. Chimera Ant arc. After leaving the nest, Meruem and the Royal Guards make their way to the palace in East Gorteau, with the King easily slaughtering all the soldiers outside. As Ming Jol-ik tells the remaining soldiers not to bother him about the intruders, a soldier capable of using Nen confronts the four Chimera Ants. After killing and eating him, Meruem then slaughters Ming Jol-ik and decides that the palace is large enough for their human processing plant. Meruem is next seen sitting in the throne room of the palace, with nine days left until the sorting. Neferpitou is seen sensing someone interfering with the sorting by disabling their puppets. They become annoyed, but Shaiapouf assures them that it's simply a diversion. After receiving Nen abilities, Leol, Flutter, and Hina volunteer to deal with the lone assassin. Pitou calls Leol and gives them the whereabouts of the assassin so that they can prepare an ambush. Leol then meets up with Cheetu and tells him that Pouf will prepare a new ability for him and teach him how to master it once he reaches the palace. Meruem then defeats and kills the East Gorteau Shogi Champion before challenging the East Gorteau Go Champion. After he allows the Go champion to take a break, Meruem learns about Gungi from Pouf and begins his matches against the current champion: Komugi. He then learns from Youpi that the Go player hanged himself. As Pitou sends out Welfin and Bloster to help Leol deal with Knov, Meruem continues his Gungi matches against Komugi. Welfin and Bloster marvel at the 5,000 cocoons as they leave the palace, with Meruem preparing to disrupt Komugi's rhythm. However, he continues to lose against her and takes a break, stressing that there won't be any more afterwards. After losing to Morel, Cheetu tells him that he will get another ability from Pouf as he heads back to the palace. Meruem resumes his matches against Komugi and underestimates her willpower, ripping off his own arm as an apology and eventually agreeing to let Pitou heal it while they continue to play. With Pitou's puppets and En gone, Morel and Knov realize that it may be their only chance to break in so that the latter can set the entrances and exits with his ability. As Pitou uses Doctor Blythe to heal Meruem's arm, Pouf offers to use his En in the meantime. Knov sneaks toward the palace and determines the entrances and exits he will set so that the Extermination Team can successfully invade. Bizeff is shown working inside, and it's stated that he was the only human allowed to stay by the King's side given his ability to maintain the country's facade. It's added that the Royal Guards decided to have no human guards since they would be useless against Nen and would create opportunities for enemy infiltration. At the time of Knov's reconnaissance, three humans (besides those kept for food) and eleven Ants inhabited the palace. As Bizeff looks through pictures of various women on his laptop and chooses five of them, Palm works with Marcos as she prepares to infiltrate the palace. Knov eventually sets the exits and kills Taragetter before glimpsing Pouf's En and setting the last exit by the central staircase. As Marcos arrives with Bizeff's women, Knov escapes the palace and has a mental breakdown, saying that he can't go back and hoping that Palm doesn't get caught. Bizeff drives the five women to the southeast underground hangar in Area D and tells them that they only need to obey his orders. Palm tells herself that she needs to look upon the King and Royal Guards, willing to kill herself if she gets caught. Palm eventually sleeps with Bizeff and uses the elevator to make her way up to the palace. As Gon wonders about Palm, Shoot tells the group that she could be in the underground hangar beyond the range of Pitou's En. Morel tells them that Knov was able to set the exits and that they have three days left until the invasion. Inside the palace, after Komugi wins once again, Meruem allows her to take a break after seeing that she's fatigued, with Pouf restraining himself from killing her after Meruem leaves the room. Elsewhere, the Extermination Team discusses their invasion of the palace in detail. Inside the palace, Meruem leaves the details for the sorting to Pouf as he continues playing Gungi with Komugi. Pitou continues to monitor Morel and his smoke puppets in Peijin, eager to fight him but unable to leave their post. The Extermination Team continue to discuss the invasion, but with only one day remaining, Killua tells himself that something isn't right. Still unable to defeat Komugi, Meruem realizes that he doesn't know his own name as he confronts the Royal Guards about it. Although he appears to waver at first, he revels in his extraordinary power and prepares to kill Komugi. However, he finds an eagle attacking her and kills it to protect her, wondering what he wants to do with her. As Gon, Killua, and Ikalgo discuss the situation within the palace, they come to the conclusion that Pitou used their healing ability on the King, who harmed himself. In Peijin, Morel gazes toward the palace and worries that something will go wrong. The military begins the forced march toward the palace, and the Royal Guards discuss a possible infiltration during the sorting. As the team discusses the invasion, Knov watches the palace from afar and notices Pouf using his scales on the gathering crowd, realizing that it has a hypnotic effect that will keep them obedient during the sorting. Inside Knov's mansion, the team members discuss and think about the invasion. As Meruem questions his existence, the team members look toward the palace in the distance and prepare to strike in ten minutes. The team members decide to invade the palace from the exit near the central staircase. Inside, Hina complains to Shidore about how much her exorcism ability is affecting her appearance. Welfin offers to help a desperate Bizeff look for Palm, but he soon finds dirty shoes and Taragetter's blood, following the intruder's tracks further into the palace. As Komugi longs to play Gungi with him, Meruem laughs at his situation and strikes Youpi when he tries to follow him. After complaining about Pitou's En, Meruem tells them to only use it up to the first floor and to forbid anyone from coming up to the second. As the team members discuss Palm and the situation inside the palace, Welfin continues to look for the intruder and analyzes the situation in detail after talking to Youpi. With less than one minute until the team's invasion, it's stated that two minutes earlier two men jumped from an enormous creature flying high above East Gorteau. When Pitou senses the incoming threat, they direct their En up toward the sky. Pitou and Pouf spot the enormous dragon, which Netero and Zeno are seen riding. As Pitou turns off their En to prepare for battle and the dragon breaks apart into a multitude of arrows, the clock strikes midnight and the team sprints toward the exit. Pouf flies desperately toward the throne room, and Netero uses his 100-Type Guanyin Bodhisattva to send Pitou flying away from the palace, with the Extermination Team making their entrance. As Pitou uses Doctor Blythe to stay near the palace and watches the rain of dragons strike the palace, Youpi prepares to confront the intruders. As Pouf reaches the empty throne room, Knuckle makes use of Meleoron's God's Accomplice and punches Youpi, activating A.P.R. on him. Pitou then directs their En toward the palace, causing the Hunters to hesitate and allowing Youpi to destroy the central staircase. After spotting Meruem, Komugi, Netero, and Zeno, Pitou leaps toward Meruem who is seen holding a wounded Komugi in his arms. Meruem asks Pitou to heal Komugi and tells Netero and Zeno that the three of them should go somewhere else. As the transformed Youpi guards the top of the destroyed staircase, Morel uses his ability to distract him so that Knuckle can land another punch. Shoot then confronts Youpi and recovers Morel's pipe so that the latter can head toward Pouf in the throne room. As Killua kills two soldier Ants with his yo-yos to protect Ikalgo, Gon sees the throne room surrounded with smoke. Inside, Pouf laments his status as a Royal Guard, with Morel trapping him inside his Smoky Jail. Gon sees Netero and Zeno following Meruem on a nearby rooftop, with the Chairman pointing back toward Pitou's location. As Zeno uses Dragon Head to transport Netero and Meruem away from the palace, Shoot continues to fight Youpi, with each trying to keep the other away from Meruem. After Ikalgo (disguised as Flutter) accidentally uses Leol's old name, Welfin and Bloster realize that something is wrong. Knuckle then reveals himself to Youpi in order to save Shoot’s life. Inside the throne room, Pouf analyzes Morel and then wraps himself in order to be reborn. As Ikalgo heads to the basement to look for Palm, Gon and Killua find Pitou using Doctor Blythe to heal Komugi. After Gon becomes enraged when Pitou begs him to let them heal Komugi, Killua reminds him that they need Pitou in order to heal Kite, with Gon giving Pitou one hour. Meleoron briefly encounters Welfin and then meets up with Killua. Knuckle eventually decide to fight Youpi after he passed by the wounded Shoot. With Morel left unsure by Pouf's plot, an enraged Youpi attacks Knuckle and destroys the base of the central tower in the process, revealing to Knuckle that too much anger causes the Royal Guard to unleash an explosion. Outside the palace, Cheetu confronts Zeno but is quickly killed by Silva, with the two Zoldycks riding off on a dragon. As Pouf slowly escapes Morel's Smoky Jail, Ikalgo continues his search for Palm and as he worries that she may be dead, he is attacked by Bloster and Flutter's corpse is destroyed. Youpi uses his fake rage against Knuckle, drawing the Hunter in and leaving him defenseless as he prepares to kill him with a single punch. But high above in the sky, making use of God's Accomplice, Killua unleashes Thunderbolt on Youpi, immobilizing the Royal Guard as Knuckle punches him hard in the face. After Knuckle finishes attacking Youpi and runs away, Killua uses his Godspeed to overwhelm the Royal Guard, but runs out of electricity and escapes with Meleoron's God's Accomplice. In the palace's basement, Ikalgo struggles to kill Bloster, eventually knocking him unconscious with sleeping gas but unable to pull the trigger. Morel finally destroys Pouf's cocoon and deactivates Smoky Jail, with Pouf splitting into hundreds of clones and thanking the Hunter for setting him free. After Pouf steals his pipe and flies away, he encounters Youpi and Knuckle, with the two Hunters using their smoke clone strategy to fight the Royal Guard. As Hina and Shidore rescue Bizeff from the fallen rubble, Morel and Knuckle trick Youpi twice, allowing Knuckle to land a punch on the Royal Guard just before he explodes. With Shoot saved by Knov, Killua tells Meleoron to assess the situation with Morel and Knuckle, adding that he will go back to Gon. After finding Gon and Pitou, Pouf attempts to find out Meruem's location. Youpi harnesses his rage and transforms into a centaur-like creature, destroying Morel's smoke clones as the interest from A.P.R. continues to increase. After learning Meruem's location, Pouf plays along with Gon's orders and secretly sends most of himself to assist the King. Morel reaches his limit, but is saved by Meleoron when Youpi tries to kill him. Knuckle reveals himself and deactivates A.P.R. in exchange for Youpi letting Morel and Meleoron live. After a bald Knov arrives and takes Morel to safety, Knuckle and Meleoron team up to take on the other Royal Guards. Youpi and Pouf find one another and make their way toward Meruem. Having been turned into a Chimera Ant, Palm confronts and fights Killua, who eventually breaks down sobbing and tells Palm that only she can help Gon now. Palm ignores Pouf's commands and assures Killua that he is the one Gon needs. Elsewhere, Knuckle confronts Pouf and asks him to fight, and the Royal Guard disobeys Gon and flies away after bursting into hundreds of clones. Pitou panics and Gon tells them that they have ten fewer minutes to heal Komugi. Pitou realizes how dangerous Gon is and resolves to kill him to protect Meruem. In the palace's basement, Welfin confronts and attacks Ikalgo, who fights against the centipedes from Welfin's Missileman and eventually learns that Palm may still be alive. Knuckle sees Pouf's face show the true nature of the Ants as the Royal Guard's segment races toward Meruem. Ikalgo, Killua, Palm, Knuckle, and Meleoron meet up and decide to fight until the end. Pitou finishes healing Komugi, and after Gon threatens to kill the girl, he and Pitou make their way to Peijin to heal Kite, with Komugi left behind as a hostage. As Meruem, Youpi, and Pouf prepare to head back to the palace to hopefully awaken the King's memory, Pouf seizes his chance and has his shell fly back to kill Komugi before Meruem can reunite with her. After Knuckle activates his A.P.R. and Palm uses her Wink Blue, the others learn that the King is still alive. As Pouf uses his clones to look for Komugi, Killua holds her on his shoulders and eventually realizes that the Royal Guard is trying to kill her. After Killua fights him back, Pouf leaves to hide the Gungi board and pieces so that they don't trigger Meruem's memory. He then works with Welfin and mimics Komugi's voice so that Pitou believes she is safe. After destroying one of Pouf's clones, Killua leaves Komugi with Palm and races toward Gon. Still trying to regain his memory, Meruem unleashes his En to search the palace and then incapacitates both Knuckle and Meleoron. While Palm and Ikalgo hide Komugi underneath the palace, Welfin acts as a messenger and confronts Youpi. As his nose begins to bleed, Meruem spots a lone Gungi piece and remembers his game with someone. Pouf finds Youpi lying dead and informs Meruem, who orders Pouf to tell him everything. Affected by the Poor Man's Rose's poison, Pouf begins coughing up blood, and Meruem decides to continue their game, once again using his En and then confronting Welfin among the hypnotized crowd. As Meruem's bloodlust grows, Welfin desperately searches his mind for the answer and finally says Komugi's name aloud, causing the King to remember playing Gungi with her. Meruem spares Pouf and asks Welfin where the other intruders are. In Area D, Meruem uses his refined En to locate Palm, assuring her that their side has won and that all he desires is to spend his remaining time with Komugi. After Palm agrees to tell him under the condition that she can watch the two with her ability, Meruem locates the sleeping Komugi and wakes her up so that the two can play again. Outside, Pouf is seen lying dead among the hypnotized crowd. Hunter Association airships descend upon the destroyed palace, and as news reports discuss the situation in East Gorteau, the real Ming Jol-ik enjoys a simple life elsewhere. Meruem and Komugi spend their time playing Gungi, and the King reveals that he has been poisoned. Even after being told that it's contagious, Komugi is happy to stay by his side. The two continue playing until their deaths, with Meruem never winning against her. 13th Hunter Chairman Election arc. In Area D, Meruem and Komugi are shown with their hands still together, with two Gungi pieces beside them. Inhabitants. Before the Extermination Team's invasion, the Royal Palace had 14 inhabitants:

Rubicuta Rubicuta (ルビキュータ, "Rubikyūta") is a town on Greed Island. It is located near the center of the island, to the south of the Shiso Tree. Overview. Little was shown from Rubicuta but it is populated by at least 100 non-player characters (NPCs). Due to its location near the starting point of the island, the town can be considered an alternative to Antokiba as a place to go at the beginning of the game. Plot. Greed Island arc. Phantom Troupe members, Shalnark, Kortopi, and Shizuku go around the town of Rubicuta, asking its citizens for information. Hypothesizing over three exhibitory facts, Shalnark deduces that the game Greed Island doesn't take place in a virtual reality, but in the real world. This is all due to the facets of Nen utilized by one or more Game Master.

Ruler's Blessing (G.I card) Ruler's Blessing (支配者の祝福) is a card found in the Greed Island game. It is one of the game's 100 designated slot cards and is required for a player to complete the game. This is the rarest, hardest and last card a player needs to collect. Summary. Ruler's Blessing 支配者の祝福 - This card contains a castle awarded to the game player who got the highest ranking score in the end-game quiz. It comes with the capital city Limeiro, and 10,000 residents. Each one will obey any commands or laws you give. This is card number #000 from the game's designated slots. As such, this card is required by any player in order to complete the game. This card is presented to the player by a Game Master at the capital city of Limeiro. This card is only available to a single game player and can only be earned by using the card Ruler's Invitation, awarded by winning the 'end of game' quiz. The quiz only becomes available when a player has collected cards #001 to #099. As such, this card is the last one a player needs to collect.

Ruler's Invitation (G.I card) Ruler's Invitation 支配者からの招待 - is a card found in the Greed Island game. This is a standard card that can be obtained by the player. These cards can be placed in the player's "Free Slots". Summary. Ruler's Invitation 支配者からの招待 - A warm invitation to visit the game's capital city, Limeiro is enclosed within this letter. This invite is also extended to visit the Gamer Master's Castle which resides within it.

Ruse Raven Ruse Ravens (ホラガラス, "Horagarasu") are a species of bird capable of mimicking the voices of others. Appearance. Ruse Ravens look like normal ravens only with wonky eyes, two long strands of hair sticking out of the top of their heads, and a split tongue which enables them to replicate human speech. Behavior. Ruse Ravens spews lies to lure prey into deadly traps so they can feed upon their prey's remains. Plot. Hunter Exam arc. During the 287th Hunter Exam in the Milsy Wetlands, the ravens use their ability to mimic Satotz's voice and lure unsuspecting Hunter examinees into dangerous traps that ultimately kills them. The ravens then proceed to scavenge the corpses of the victims.

Ryoji Ryoji (リョウジ, "Ryouji") is a Royal Bodyguard for Prince Fugetsu. Appearance. Ryoji has a chiseled chin, narrow eyes, and wears his hair slicked back. Like the other Royal Bodyguards, he wears a black suit and a tie. Personality. Ryoji presents himself as calm, stoic, and overall quiet. He seems to care about Prince Fugetsu Hui Guo Rou, as he, along with Bachaem, are the only bodyguards genuinely trying to protect her. Plot. Succession Contest arc. Ryoji and Bachaem stand guard in Prince Fugetsu's room, realizing they're the only ones that truly want to protect the Prince. Ryoji along with Yushohi stand guard by Prince Kacho's bedside and soon are caught by surprise by Melody and Keeney who come to check up on the Prince's safety. Sometime afterward, Ryoji continues to stand guard by Prince Fugetsu's room. At the same time, Yushohi places the "Stinger Ball" of his How to Get Away with Murder Nen ability close to Ryoji's ears to provoke a response with its buzzing. Ryoji does not react to the construct's noise, leading Yushohi to conclude that he cannot use Nen.

Ryu Ryu (リュウ, "Ryuu") was examinee #34 in the 287th Hunter Exam. Appearance. Ryu is a man of average build and height. He has spiky hair and a celestial nose. He wears a tunic over a long sleeve shirt, a belt that carries his sheathed broadsword, plain pants, and boots. Plot. Hunter Exam arc. Ryu first appears during the 287th Hunter Exam. Nothing is known about him, except that he is one of the 24 candidates who reached the Fourth Phase of the exam on Zevil Island. During the Fourth Phase he fights with Bodoro and is defeated, failing to pass this phase in the process. Abilities & Powers. Not much is known about Ryu's fighting style, but going off the sword he's always seen carrying around, it may be inferred he is a swordsman. Having passed the First Phase of the Hunter Exam, he is sure to have above-average stamina.
Ryubihhi Ryubihhi (リュビッヒ, "Ryubihhi") is a Royal Bodyguard for Prince Tubeppa.

Sabaki Sabaki (サバキ, "Sabaki") is a character from the video game and an associate of Zegin Highline who seeks to gain entry into a locked ruin to acquire the "Dragon Vein" from within. Appearance. Sabaki is a young man with a tan complexion, blonde hair, and blue eyes. He is about average height and weight. His clothing comprises a short-sleeved orange jacket with white segments, an orange bandana, a blue undershirt, black gloves, and blue jeans. Personality. Sabaki is an impulsive young individual. He lets his emotions get the best of him and can occasionally be rash. He also has a deep hatred for hunters due to his father. However, he is also clever enough to destroy the Dragon Vein Zegin was using and to utilize an ability that rids Nen users of their aura Background. Around five years before the game's events, Sabaki's father abandoned him and his dying mother to participate in the 282nd Hunter Exam; however, it was Zegin who murdered his father. These events would cause Sabaki to despise the Hunter Association. Eventually, he learned Nen and aimed for revenge against all hunters, starting with Zegin. He became allies with him in hopes of eventually avenging his father. Plot. "Altar of Dragon Vein". Gon and his friends first encounter Sabaki at the Forest Ruins. As Killua notes the door entrance to be locked off, Sabaki confronts them. Realizing Gon to be a hunter, he reveals to them that he 'hunts' hunters. From this, a fight breaks out. As Sabaki nearly defeats them, Hisoka interferes. Sabaki questions if he's their friend, which he denies. He then offers to become allies with the blonde boy. Sabaki refuses this and leaves, proclaiming that he will put an end to all hunters in the association, causing Hisoka to take interest in him. Sabaki is briefly seen at Zegin's Mansion. He helps drive the jeep carrying Zegin and Sabaki. He then appears after Amane fights the Hunter group in the Crystal Cave. He proceeds to knock Amane unconscious because he is a liability. Sabaki also reveals his intentions to them and his troubled past. He aims to kill Zegin before anyone else can. He also claims that he would still despise hunters even if this hadn't happened.
