Also as a show of unity, he and Loupe will vote for Teradein and implores all who agree with their purposes to vote for Teradein. When the Fifth Election for the 13th Hunter Chairman results come in after the broadcast, both Bushidora and Loupe place in 15th and are eliminated for not making the top 8 candidates. Soon after the 5th election, Teradein, Loupe, and Bushidora try to get in contact with the groups of more than 20 Hunters they were in contact with, including the Hunters Latoon and Kenzaki. Bushidora boasts his capable abilities as Captain. When inquired about the votes from Loupe, Bushidora states anyone who's free to vote, go and vote, as long as Teradein makes the top 4. Although Teradein voices his concern about the prediction of where the votes will go and doesn't want to sway the election through absentees, Loupe suggests they hire a group of Temp Hunters in order to reduce the number of moderate voters for Pariston Hill. Bushidora and Teradein both agree with the plan, unbeknownst to them that it's really a clever ploy to kill off the Temp Hunters by the enemy making them absent in the next election. Loupe also contemplates that Teradein is too honest, while Bushidora is too careless. However after confronting Hisoka, Bushidora along with everyone who accompanied him were killed. In a broadcast made by Teradein, Bushidora is mentioned that he was killed in the line of action, by the Evil Hunters. Bushidora is briefly mentioned when Pariston calls for an emergency motion to have the Hunter Bylaws revised, as once proclaimed by the late Teradein and Bushidora.

Butch Butch (ブッチ, "Bucchi") is a high-ranking soldier in the Royal Army of the Kakin Empire, and one of the personal soldiers of Prince Benjamin. He was now among Prince Tubeppa's bodyguards under direct orders from Prince Benjamin. It is currently unknown what Prince he has been reassigned to protect. Appearance. Butch has a round face and a bald head. He wears the standard Kakin military attire of zipper jacket, pants, and dark combat boots. He wears an earpiece in his left ear. Background. As one of the First Prince's soldiers, Butch graduated from Kakin's Royal Military Academy and became a part of his army. Plot. Succession Contest arc. Butch is among the other thirteen soldiers working under Prince Benjamin that is present during Balsamilco's explanation before the journey's start. Later, Prince Benjamin orders his fourteen soldiers to both act as bodyguards and spies to all the other princes, and to report any information regarding the the Princes' Guardian Spirit Beasts and the Hunters' abilities. Stationed near by Prince Tubeppa in her room, Butch receives a transmission from Babimyna that he's currently carrying out his mission. Abilities & Powers. Butch has received military training. Nen. Butch is a Nen user, although his superior Balsamilco believes him to be less knowledgeable than Hunters in that regard.

Camilla Hui Guo Rou Camilla Hui Guo Rou (カミーラ゠ホイコーロ, "Kamīra Hoikōro") is the Second Prince of the Kakin Empire and the daughter of her father's second wife, Queen Duazul. She is the eldest female among the 14 siblings. Appearance. Camilla is a beautiful woman with long, fair hair worn in an intricate hairstyle, with some locks falling on her back, others were tied above the nape of her neck and four framing her face. She has clear eyes and long eyelashes. In her first appearance, she is seen wearing a necked dress and a tiara. In general, she seems to wear fancy dresses. During the ceremony, Camilla wears a mermaid dress, and for the formal party, she wears a splendid long dress with sophisticated embroidery and two luxurious necklaces. Her hairstyle during the party is also different, resembling a large beehive style, though some of her locks are still falling around her face. When Camilla sets out to eliminate Benjamin, she wears a simple dress with a bolero jacket and long, black boots. Her natural hair is rather messy. Personality. In outward appearance, she seems to have charming and elegant mannerisms. However, like her elder brother, Camilla has no problem in eliminating her siblings in a sadistic way, though she prefers to do it through easy, but heartless methods; for instance, she orders her own mother to assassinate her biological younger brother. According to Shimano, Camilla only listens to the King. She is also a spendthrift, as she is fond of shopping on branded, expensive and limited edition items, and collects the entire series of them. During her meal with her mother, she orders her to buy several of them. Because of this, her sister Tubeppa feels that she is greedy and despises her for it. Camilla refers to herself in the third person and using the nickname "Cammy", although she also refers to herself in the first person at times. She is actually a conceited woman who wants others to think the way as she does—such as thinking she would be the next king while her siblings should just die on their own. She has no respect for her older brother Benjamin and ignores her father's order to show deference. She views herself as someone who could change the "wrong" world. Background. Camilla gave the Have-Nots of Kakin the chance to become her private guards. She had a special district built on her private property where they can enjoy privileges equal to those of the military, which earned her the support of the group. Plot. Succession Contest arc. Camilla participates to the ceremony on the eve of the beginning of the expedition. She then attends a formal party. Like the rest of her family, she resides in the 1st deck of the Black Whale. Camilla's Guardian Spirit Beast is revealed during the party she attends. During one of the parties, she approaches her father and asks him to clarify the interpretation of "survival" and "dropped out" from the Succession War. Nasubi informs her that the 3rd Prince Zhang Lei already asked the same question, so Nasubi would give the same answer: the one sole survivor is the official heir to the throne and Camilla is free to interpret what it means, as it is also part of the war. Benjamin overhears the conversation and tells Camilla that if she wants to be king, she does not need to worry about others' interpretations. Camilla exclaims that she only wants people to do as she wants, including for her siblings to die on their own. Benjamin calls her conceited and unfit to the throne. She curses at him, but their father orders her to show respect for her older brother. Instead of conceding, Camilla merely brushes them both and walks away. Her Guardian Spirit Beast begins to transform as she thinks the world is unfair. Later, Camilla orders her bodyguards to kill anyone who comes near and to call her mother, Queen Duazul. In her room, Camilla dines with her mother while talking about buying clothes (from Musen, Coachpie, and Harryweb's Noctiluca line). She pivots the conversation and discusses her plans to kill Benjamin first and then Halkenburg, ordering her mother to get closer to Halkenburg. When Queen Duazul expresses her misgivings, Camilla sternly orders her to follow. Camilla rejects Kurapika's offer to have her Royal Bodyguards learn Nen. On the second day, she acts to kill Benjamin. Confronting Musse, she divulges her plans to kill the First Prince, demanding her guard join her, offering the soldier the chance to choose between assisting her or dying. Noting she is in a state of Zetsu, Musse surmises she must have a counter-type ability and attacks her with lethal force. He touches her body to activate his ability, but is killed by her Cat's Name. The Nen beast resurrects Camilla with Musse's life energy before disappearing. Camilla then heads for Benjamin's quarters with a gun in her hand. She shoots one of his guards and Furykov, killing the former. When Benjamin lets her in, she declares she is after the soldier who tried to kill her. She fires her gun at Benjamin, who deflects all the bullets with Ken. She then taunts the guards to shoot her, but Furykov takes charge and breaks her arm. She vows to kill his family, to which the soldier replies Benjamin is his only family. Camilla is thus thrown into jail while being monitored by Musse's Secret Window. Benjamin and Camilla stand trial before Supreme Magistrate Cleapatro. Their fate depending on what became of Musse, the judge sentences that the quarters of both princes be searched by the royal army, until which time the two will be confined to the VVIP area and placed under surveillance. The court is adjourned and Camilla leaves, escorted by two of her private soldiers. On the day of the banquet, Prince Camilla is briefly transfixed by the music of Melody's flute performance. Equipment. Handgun: Camilla briefly wielded Musse's gun after his death. She used it as a weapon as well as a way to get the opponent to attack her in order to activate her Nen ability. The handgun was confiscated following her arrest. Abilities & Powers. Camilla's status as one of the senior Princes of Kakin grants her significant political influences and assets that give her benefits to win the throne. Camilla is confident enough in herself to the point of not fearing her elder brother, Benjamin. She is moderately intelligent, enough to use Musse's disappearance to gain entrance to Benjamin's quarters as well as to defend herself in court. Enhanced Endurance: Camilla withstood having her arm broken with only a slight change in expression and an increase in perspiration. Proficient Marksman: Camilla is a trained shooter. She is able to shoot two targets in the head in very quick succession. Nen. Camilla is a powerful Nen user. Her knowledge of post-mortem Nen allows her to employ it in her counteractive Nen ability, which makes even Benjamin hesitant about killing her. She is at least capable of using Hatsu and Zetsu. Guardian Spirit Beast. Like the rest of her siblings, Camilla received an egg from which a Guardian Spirit Beast hatched to protect her. Since it is a parasitic-type ability, she has no control over it. The Nen beast is subjected to two rule-like instincts: it is unable to fight other Guardian Spirit Beasts as well as to directly attack the host of one. It is known to be a Manipulator with a coercive-type ability that takes complete control of a target who fulfills certain conditions.

Camp Tiger Camp Tiger (キャンプタイガー, "Kyanpu Taigā") is a species of tiger that impales its prey with its horn and uses fire to cook its food. It was discovered by Kite during a biological survey in the Kakin Empire. Appearance. A Camp Tiger looks like an ordinary tiger, only that it has a long sharp, and narrow horn attached to its head that it uses to cook its prey on a fire. Behavior. Camp Tigers seem to be intelligent creatures, opting to use their horns and cook their food over a fire, implying that the tigers know how to start a fire. Plot. Chimera Ant arc. Banana claims it is one of the best finds on the Amateur Hunters biological survey. Spin details that it's a type of tiger that uses a campfire started by a bolt of lightning. According to Banana, even if Camp Tigers are Magical Beasts, it's the first known non-two-legged creature capable of using fire to cook raw meat.
Can't Meet Right Now Can't Meet Right Now (今は会えない, "Ima wa aenai") is a song from the, sung by as Killua Zoldyck.

Canary Canary (カナリア, "Kanaria") is an apprentice butler of the Zoldyck Family. Anyone attempting to pass her post on the estate will be expelled via force. Appearance. Canary is in her early teens. She has grey eyes and dark purple hair pulled into thick bunches, each tied with a string towards the tip, which vaguely resembles stars. She has a round face, a small nose, and thick lips. Her skin is dark brown. She wears the standard Zoldyck butler suit. In the 1999 anime, Canary's hair is mostly red, her eyes are green, and her skin is lighter. Personality. Canary is very loyal to the Zoldyck Family. She is initially introduced as a ruthless guardian who does not hesitate to attack trespassers, but, as noted by Gon, she is not as heartless as she pretends to be, and just for a fraction of a second, her eyes convey gentleness or concern, although she tries to suppress it. She was deeply moved by his attempts to reach Killua, due to her feeling affection for her young master. Killua was kind to her and wanted them to be friends, but she declined due to her station. Her loyalty to Killua has caused her to disobey her orders to different degrees on more than one occasion. Background. , a junkyard city inhabited by outcasts. People who live there do not exist in any official records and the existence of the city itself is known to very few people. When she was ten years old, within minutes, she took down a Blacklist Hunter together with a hundred of his men attempting to go through her post. Plot. Zoldyck Family arc. As Gon, Leorio, and Kurapika walk down the pathway to the Zoldyck residence, they approach Canary, who orders them to leave as they're trespassing on private property. Gon tries to reason with Canary saying they called in advance and managed to go through the Testing Gate, but Canary still refuses as they're all still trespassing on the property. Gon persists in inquiring how they can pass because they're Killua's friends. However, due to them not having any permission from her seniors and no precedent, Canary refuses to let them pass. Seeing no alternative, Gon chooses to trespass further, and Canary warns Gon that if he crosses the line, he'll be removed by force. Gon does so, and his face is struck by Canary's cane, sending him backward. Gon gets back up and stops Leorio and Kurapika from retaliating against Canary. Gon then tries to reason with Canary that all they wish to do is see Killua, but Canary still refuses. This continues throughout the day as Gon's face becomes severely bruised and swollen. Trying to hold back her emotions, she tries to ask Gon to go away, but Gon refuses and is struck again by Canary's cane. She then implores Leorio and Kurapika to stop Gon, but they continue to observe silently. Hesitant as Gon approaches her, he asks Canary why she won't allow them to see Killua, as he then smashes the pillar she stood beside. Gon then claims he's crossed the line again and has yet to be hit. Canary reluctantly tries to, but is too frightened, as Gon explains that she's different from Mike the guard dog, because while she suppresses her emotions, she has a soul. Canary, moved by Gon's words, tries to request that he save Killua, but is shot in the head by a very tall woman accompanied by her child. The tall woman introduces herself as Killua's mother and the child as Killua's younger sibling Kalluto as Leorio examines Canary stating she's merely knocked unconscious. Canary regains consciousness after Killua's mother and younger brother leave. She informs the group that the butlers' quarters are close by, and there's a telephone that's connected to the mansion, and if master Zeno answers, then they may see Killua. The group reaches the quarters at night and is greeted by Gotoh and his fellow butlers. Inside the mansion, Gotoh proposes a coin game to help pass the time. Gon and their friends win the game three times, but to raise the stakes, Canary is held hostage, and if they were to lose, then Canary would die. Kurapika and Leorio are both eliminated in the first and second rounds, but Gon wins the last round, and Canary's life is spared. 13th Hunter Chairman Election arc. Canary returns alongside Gotoh as Killua's guardian for the requirements of the Level 4 Restriction placed upon him after he released Alluka out of the Zoldyck Estate. The senior butler Tsubone and her granddaughter Amane also were assigned to accompany them. Although Killua becomes nervous and distraught by Tsubone's presence, Canary promises to protect {Killua, even if it means losing her position or life. Amane then presents herself in front of Canary, and the two introduce one another. Tsubone shocks everyone by giving Alluka her pinky nail. Tsubone takes her leave but not before promising that she'll keep a close eye on Killua. Canary was in charge of driving the limousine to the hospital Gon was stationed at. When Illumi contacts Killua, he surmises a family and butler relationship diagram where Canary and Gotoh, along with Tsubone and Amane, are mutually cautious of one another. At the same time, Zeno is Canary and Gotoh's employer, and they both trust Killua. After Killua challenges his older brother, he sends a car and a truck with manipulated drivers after them. This causes Canary to lose control of the limousine, sending it off a cliff and crashing down below. Everyone in the car manages to escape unharmed, but due to Amane failing to gain Killua's trust, he uses his Godspeed Nen ability to escape. Surprised by Killua vanishing with Alluka, Gotoh contacts someone to update said person on the current situation. The group is then confronted by Hisoka, and Gotoh orders Canary and Amane to go after Killua as he'll deal with Hisoka. The two comply and leave. As soon as Tsubone contacts Canary, informing her she lost sight of Killua, Amane has Canary follow her, claiming it's faster to ride on her grandmother's bike. Canary, perplexed by Tsubone actually being the motorcycle, rides down the highway road and manages to catch up to Killua. However, he leaps into the forest in order to lose them again. Discussing the situation over they decide to intercept Killua at Parasta Airport. This impresses Killua, who meets Canary and Amane at the airport and is informed that they have reserved a blimp for him. Killua argues that he needs 5-6 blimps to lose the Illumi track. So as Amane reserves said blimps, Canary pesters her for Killua to escape, much to Amane's dismay. Frustrated by Canary's actions, Amane demands that they go after Killua, but Canary refuses in order to pilot one of the decoy blimps. As Amane begins to pout, Canary points out that she's cute when she expresses her emotions. In the decoy blimp Canary tries to contact Gotoh but to no avail. Later that night, Killua contacts Canary and is informed she couldn't get in contact with Gotoh either. So Killua orders her to get in contact with Hishita to send three cars to specified points. Canary informs Killua that four cars are already heading his way. Canary is shown to be shocked by the overpowering feeling from Alluka's ability to heal Gon. Back at Kukuroo Mountain, after Gon reunites with his father, Canary and Amane visit Gotoh's grave. Canary informs Amane that Gotoh's death is unknown to him, and she also learns that the Kiriko's son was hired to impersonate the departed Gotoh. Abilities & Powers. , her existence is not recorded in any database, which makes obtaining information about her nearly impossible. Her weapon is a rod that she always carries with her. In the 2011 anime adaptation, she is shown to be adept with assassination techniques like Shadow Step, although she was not aware of its name and claimed she might have learned during her days in Meteor City. It is later shown she is adept at learning quickly, as seen when Killua demonstrated the Rhythm Echo once, and precisely executed the technique moments later during an attack by Seaquant and about 100 of his henchmen. Preternatural Perception: Canary was able to notice that there were intruders on the mountain, and unlike Killua, she also noticed that Kikyo was watching them from afar. Enhanced Strength: Canary is strong enough to send enemies flying with just one attack. As a butler of the Zoldycks, she is also able to open the Testing Gates, although the number of doors she can open is unknown. Enhanced Speed and Reflexes: Canary was able to react quickly in a car crash, and she was also fast enough to keep up with Killua, Amane, and Gotoh at a high speed. Master Hand-to-Hand Combatant: As an apprentice butler of the Zoldyck Family, she is an expert fighter. She can defeat a Hunter and his 100 henchmen trying to intrude on the Zoldyck estate in mere minutes without breaking a sweat. Rhythm Echo: The Rhythm Echo is an advanced art of assassination, thanks to which the user creates several after-images of his body through a variable cadence of steps. There is a total absence of noise during the movement. According to Netero it is the advanced version of the "Silent Gaits" technique. Skilled Driver: Canary is an excellent driver, as seen by how she managed to avoid most obstacles in the car crash caused by Illumi. Nen. So far, she has not shown any Nen abilities of her own; however, since she used her aura to fuel Tsubone's motorcycle, its clear that Canary knows how to use Nen, and consequently, uses Ten. She was also able to sense Illumi's Ren and she saw the aura unleashed by Nanika while healing Gon.

Capricious Remote (G.I card) Capricious Remote 移り気リモコン - is a card found in the Greed Island game. It is one of the game's 100 designated slot cards and so is required for a player to complete the game. This remote allows the user to change 10 emotions of another person. Summary. Capricious Remote 移り気リモコン - This card allows the caster to manipulate 10 emotions that somebody has towards another person. You can change each emotion with the intensity scale of 1 to 10, with 10 being the most intense. This card can't be used on yourself or one someone else's feelings towards you. There is nothing in the rules however, that prevents a friend from using it on another person to alter their feelings toward you.

Captain The unnamed Captain (船長, "Senchō") is the head of the ship which transports the main protagonists to the mainland where the 287th Hunter Exam is being held—Dolle Harbor. Appearance. The Captain is a fairly elderly man with a short and stocky build. He has a beard that extends down and around his face with an integrated mustache. His eyebrows are similarly shaggy. His nose is permanently red, most likely attributed to his constant drinking as he carries around a bottle of alcohol. His attire consists of a sea captain's hat adorned with a whale emblem, a jacket covering a V-neck top with a belt, trousers, and black rubber boots. During the initial storm, he is seen with a pipe. In the 1999 anime adaptation, his hat is white, his jacket dark blue, his trousers brown, his belt green, and his top beige. His facial hair is black and the rest of his hair is greying and his complexion is tanned. Personality. The Captain is a kind and generous man, opting to bring Gon, Leorio, and Kurapika to the closest port to the exam hall and teaches Gon the basics of steering a ship. He can be critical of others at times, as on the ship he calls all the seasick passengers pathetic. His experience seems to have educated him, as he is capable of accurately predicting when a storm is going to hit, hours in advance and navigating a ship through vicious storms. From his appearances on the ship, it would appear he is an avid drinker and is a smoker. Background. ﻿The Captain has taken part in the Hunter Exam and commanded a ship for some time, as it is shown he also transported Gon's father, Ging Freecss to one of the ports 10 years prior to the storyline after leaving his son on Whale Island. Plot. Hunter Exam arc. As Gon embarks on his journey to becoming a Hunter, he boards the ship going to the mainland on which the Hunter Exam takes place from the harbor on Whale Island. The ship is commanded by the Captain, who is first seen navigating the ship through a perilous storm at sea, hurling the majority of the passengers aboard to and fro. As the storm subsides, the Captain relinquishes the helm to take a look around the ship to see the effects of the storm on the passengers or "supercargo" as he calls them. He goes to have a talk with the unscathed Gon on the bow and is very impressed that he detects a second, larger storm is on its way. This triggers déjà vu, and the Captain sees an apparition of Gon's father, Ging Freecss, in the shadow of his son, who presumably told the Captain a similar thing when he traveled on his ship 10 years beforehand. He then invites Gon to the bridge to show him how to steer the ship, much to Gon's pleasure. Announcing to the ship a little later on that a second greater storm is on its way and there are lifeboats available for anyone who would like to give up, the Captain finds only three passengers are left aboard are Leorio, Gon, and Kurapika. He asks them what their reasons are for becoming Hunters and reveals that he himself is an agent of the Hunter Exam. As sparks fly between Leorio and Kurapika, the Captain shows concern that one of them may be finished if they go overboard during their fight on the deck. The Captain takes a shine to the trio as they save one of his employees from the brink of death going overboard and decides to take them to the nearest port to the examination hall, Dolle Harbor. He then continues his steering teaching with Gon. Upon disembarking in Dolle Harbor, the Captain shakes hands with Gon and advises him to head in the direction of a lone pine tree atop a hill. Waving goodbye, the Captain utters that Ging has a fine son.

Carabid Beetle Carabid Beetle (ゴミムシ, "Gomimushi") is a Chimera Ant and former Captain of Leol's Squad who carries the genes of the and a . He ambushes Killua along with other Ants under Flutter's command. Appearance. He is a beetle-like Chimera Ant with a rather anthropomorphic look. He is bald, with two antlers on his head and two much longer ones protruding from his scapulae. His body is a light shade of beige in color, except for his head and fingers, which are white. He also has a black shell on each shoulder. He wears maroon pants with a belt. Plot. Chimera Ant arc. Carabid Beetle tries to roll a giant dung-ball at Killua, but realizes that the boy is far too powerful for him to face and tries to flee. Killua pursues him, only for the Ant to use its special ability on him. His whereabouts are currently unknown. Abilities & Powers. As a Chimera Ant, he is stronger than normal humans. He can also stand and run atop a huge ball of dung which, due to its weight and speed, has enough kinetic energy to bring down trees standing in its path. Enhanced Durability: His body is considerably durable, since a punch from a Nen-using Rammot did not leave him with any permanent or visible injury. Nen. After being violently "initiated", Carabid Beetle learned Nen.
Carry On Carry On is the first OVA ending theme and the fourth ending theme overall of the Hunter × Hunter 1999 anime adaptation. It was sung by, who also sang the first OVA opening theme.

Cashew Cashew (カシュー, "Kashū") is a member of the Heil-Ly Family. Appearance. Cashew is a young woman with fair hair on top, but dark on the sides and back. She has a long fringe that falls on the left side of her face. She has droopy eyes, thick lips, and prominent lower lashes. Personality. Like her fellow Heil-Ly members, Cashew has sadistic tendencies and no qualms about killing people. Unlike Luini's desire to level up quickly, Cashew wants to take her time to deceive the investigation team so that she can have fun. She is very deceptive while doing so, able to lie and cry in Mizaistom's presence. Plot. Succession Contest arc. Cashew is seen with the other Heil-Ly members as Morena uses her Contagion on them one at a time and explains how her Nen ability works. In the general passenger area on Tier 3, several soldiers cordon off the area as a large crowd begins to gather. An official tells them to stay back and that the area will be off-limits until forensics is done with the scene. Mizaistom asks someone how many victims there are, and the person says twenty, adding that the perpetrator entered the room disguised as Royal Army and killed quickly. Mizaistom wonders if Nen was involved, but the person replies that they only know a blade was used, with no sign of an ability. Mizaistom describes it as a random attack and asks if there are any witnesses. The person says that there is a witness who described the perpetrator as in his twenties, slender, 6' to 6'2", with a crescent scar on his left cheek. They add that canvassing the area didn't return any eyewitness accounts of someone who fits that description, guessing that their testimony may be flawed because of confusion from shock. Mizaistom then sternly asks to speak to the witness. Mizaistom eventually goes to the scene of the crime, and Cashew begins to recount what happened. She first says that she heard a knock, and the victim went to the door. Once she opened it, Cashew then heard someone collapse, calling out but getting no answer. As Cashew opened the bathroom, she saw the perpetrator standing there before he quickly ordered her to move and threatened to kill her if she made a noise. After seeing the victim's body on the floor, Cashew emphasizes how afraid she was and says that she made sure to focus on following his orders so that he would spare her life. As she was desperately hoping that he wouldn't kill her, she remembers the man talking about levels and how many people he needed to kill. She then heard a scream outside the room and the sounds of people running, pounding on doors, and more screams. She tells Mizaistom that the man locked the bathroom door from the inside, and Mizaistom is left confused. She explains that she sat there until the Royal Army pried the door open, revealing that he had somehow escaped. Mizaistom points out that the pipes aren't even big enough for a rat, and Cashew is certain that he didn't come out, adding that the soldiers confirmed the door was locked. She then pleads with Mizaistom to catch the man and ask him. Mizaistom begins to analyze the situation with himself, wondering why he would have left a witness alive and emphasizing that the various words the man used are clues to the mystery. Mizaistom asks how she knew the victim, and Cashew replies that they hit it off right away after they happened to sit next to each other to eat. She then begins to cry, saying that the woman wanted advice about her personal life and she didn't get to give it to her. Mizaistom kneels down beside her and tells her to go rest in her cabin, adding that they will talk to her again. After Mizaistom escorts her away from the scene, Cashew's expression instantly changes, and it's revealed that she is a level 1 member of the Heil-Ly Family. In a flashback, Cashew explains her plan to Luini, saying that she will mix the truth with lies and make sure that it hints at why she wasn't killed. Luini praises her idea and tells her to describe his scar accurately. Cashew asks if he's sure, and Luini replies that he wants to know their investigative ability, clarifying that he wants to know how long it takes between being identified and getting found. Cashew again asks if he's sure, pointing out that he will be put to death if he is caught. Luini assures her that he won't get caught and adds that even if he does, he will escape. He then remembers Morena's line about their ability providing for them if they wish hard enough. With aura swelling around him, he finally says that he has been bestowed with a gift and the power will take him where he wants to go. Back in the present, Cashew says that Luini disappeared from the bathroom after that, guessing it's a transportation ability and saying that she doesn't care for it. She asks herself if it's fun to get it over with so quickly, adding that she will level up slowly and ask for the gift. Lastly, she says that she has succeeded in contacting the investigators and will now get to know them better, licking her lips with delight. At 10 a.m. on the fourth day of the voyage, Cashew is shown to be in a standard cabin on Tier 3.

Casino King The Casino King (, "Kajino-ō") is a (NPC) of the Greed Island game, who gambles with players that dare challenge him in Dorias. Appearance. The Casino King wears his hair in a massive pompadour style haircut and dresses in a plain dress-shirt, pants, and shoes. Personality. The Casino King portrayed himself as a cool and confident gambler, until he was beaten by Killua. Plot. Greed Island arc. In the casino area at Dorias, Killua challenges the Casino King to a game of Poker. The latter disparages Killua for challenging him, however, thanks to a successful roll on the Risky Dice, Killua beats the Casino King with a "Broadway Straight" thereby winning the "Fledgling Gambler" card.

Castor Line The Castor [Station] Line (, "Kasushīru-eki Hōmen") is a train line that runs in Yorknew City. Overview. The Castor Line is a train line that runs through Yorknew City and one of its destinations leads to the city's downtown. Plot. Yorknew City arc. Half of the Phantom Troupe members take this train line to Lipa Station while they are unknowingly tailed by Killua (in the last car) and Melody (in the same car).

Cat Diner NPC The Cat Diner NPCs are a group of non-player characters that run the Caveau de Riquewihr restaurant in Antokiba on Greed Island. Appearance. The Cat Diner NPC appears as a large built anthropomorphic cat wearing a traditional chef's uniform. The bears a cat symbol with only a pair of eyes. The Cat Diner NPC seems to have a tail with a dark-colored end. Personality. The Cat Diner NPC accommodates Gon and Killua when they partake in the restaurant's eating challenge. They only know a few key phrases and ask "What's that?" to the words they are not familiar with. They are strict about getting paid for their food. Plot. Greed Island arc. They provide basic information about the monthly contests, cards, and money when Gon and Killua ask about them. Their restaurant challenges players to eat a large serving of pasta within 30 minutes. The prizes are the pasta will be free of charge and a "Galgaida" card. Gon and Killua manage to finish the pasta within 10 to 13 minutes, thus redeeming the prizes. But they are unable to pay for their sodas because they only have paper money and not in the card form. Cat Diner NPC starts calling for the police. In the end, Gon and Killua wash dishes to compensate for their unpaid drinks.

Caveau de Riquewihr Dopff au Moulin, Caveau de Riquewihr is a restaurant run by the Cat Diner NPCs and is located in Antokiba on Greed Island. Overview. The restaurant offers a "Galgaida" card prize to whoever is able to eat a large plate of spaghetti within half an hour. Plot. Greed Island arc. Gon and Killua eat here and win the spaghetti eating challenge, however, due to the fact that they could not pay for their sodas with the in-game currency, they wash dishes to conpensate.

Cavic Cavic (カビッチ, "Kabitchi") is a Private Guard of the Second Prince Camilla and the one formerly in charge of killing the Twelfth Prince Momoze through a Nen curse. Appearance. Cavic has short, fair hair with a few longer locks in the cowlick on their high forehead. They have big, round eyes, long eyelashes, and a small nose with large nostrils. They wear the standard uniform of Camilla's private guards. Personality. Like their Have-Nots comrades, Cavic is a staunch supporter of Prince Camilla. They would go as far as to sacrifice their life to curse one of the other Princes in order to secure their Prince's position as the Kakin's newest King. Plot. Succession Contest arc. Cavic and the other personal soldiers of Prince Camilla attend a meeting held by Sarahell about the recent suicide of Shikaku. The meeting concerns the possibility of him also being able to cast a Nen curse similar to their own. As their curse target, the Twelfth Prince Momoze, was assassinated by Tuffdy, they and Nukuocon are reassigned by Sarahell to spy on enemy camps to find out if they have any exorcists on their side. This task should also help them not cause any trouble for their Prince Camilla. Abilities & Powers. Nen. Cavic is a Nen user and can cast the same curse as the other Have-Nots in Prince Camilla's employ.

Celadon Porcelain Vase The Celadon Porcelain Vase (, "Seijiki Seiun Montsubo") is an item that was auctioned off at the Underground Auction. Appearance. The Celadon Porcelain Vase is a vase of average size with a stout body. As its name suggests, it is celadon in color and its base material is porcelain. Background. The vase is from the Lai Dynasty and the last of its kind still intact. Plot. Yorknew City arc. Following the successful bid on the Solid-Gold Execution Sword, the Underground Auction auctioneer (controlled by Shalnark) introduces the Celadon Porcelain Vase and briefly details its origin. Backstage, Shizuku finds the real vase and has Kortopi create a copy using his Gallery Fake ability. Once the item is brought out on stage, the bidding quickly climbs to 380 million.

Cemetery Building The Cemetery Building (セメタリービル, "Semetarī Biru") is a large building located in Yorknew City. Overview. The building is where the Mafia Community's annual Underground Auction is held. Plot. Yorknew City arc. On the night of September 1st, the mummy of Princess Corco was to be sold at the Underground Auction held in the Cemetery Building. However, the auction is interrupted after the Phantom Troupe massacres the attendees during their plan to steal all the items. They utilize Shizuku's Nen ability to remove any traces of the massacre. By the time back-up arrives at the building, mass hysteria reaches a fever-pitch within the Mafia Community, with both the attendees and auction items all missing. It is later revealed in a phone conversation between Chrollo and Uvogin that the missing auction items were moved elsewhere by one of the Shadow Beasts named Owl. Two days after the massacre, it is announced that the Underground Auction will be held again in the Cemetery Building that very night and that precautions have been taken by the Ten Dons to prevent another incident. A conversation between Light Nostrade and Kurapika reveals that there will be many important figures of the Mafia Community present and that it will be protected by a large number of Mafia members and even police officers, who have created a perimeter of one kilometer around the building. Anyone who tries to enter without permission will be killed on sight. Before the start of the auction, Neon is accompanied by a disguised Chrollo who helps her get past the barriers. The two briefly talk at a restaurant inside the building, and Chrollo has his fortune told by Neon. Soon after, he knocks her unconscious and then assassinates most of the professional assassins hired by the Ten Dons to eliminate the Troupe. Meanwhile, following Chrollo's orders, the other Troupe members massacre every single Mafia member and police officer they encounter outside the Cemetery Building. In the basement of the building, Chrollo faces off against Silva and Zeno Zoldyck, but the fight ends in a draw after the Ten Dons (who hired the two Zoldycks) are assassinated by Illumi with the help of Kalluto and Maha. As Bean assures the Mafia members inside that everything is fine and leads them to the auction hall, Illumi manipulates the Dons' corpses and has one of them assure the Mafia members that the Troupe's leader has been killed and that the others will be eliminated as well. After he tells them to enjoy the auction and the Mafia members celebrate, it's revealed that the Troupe is controlling the auction backstage as they make copies of every item. After the Troupe members fake their deaths, Kurapika arrives at the auction hall just as the announcer introduces the last item: a pair of Scarlet Eyes. He gets permission from Light to spend as much as he needs to win them, and after Kurapika gets into a bidding war against Zenji, Light is stunned to learn that the final bid reached 2.9 billion. Kurapika picks up the item and delivers them to Light and Neon after dealing with an enraged Zenji. At Neon's hospital, after giving the eyes to his daughter, Light tells the Nostrade bodyguards that the last item left to bid on is the tissue used by a celebrity, which will be auctioned off the next day.

Centipede Centipede (ムカデ, "Mukade") was a Chimera Ant Soldier from Yunju's Squad division. Appearance. Centipede was a Chimera Ant that resembled a humanoid centipede with sixteen arms, yellow skin, and mannequin-like articulations. He was bald, with three black spots on his forehead, and had a goatee. His eyes were oval that contained green sclerae and cruciform black pupils. Personality. He displays confidence with his "Thousand-Hand Fist" move. He's also a bit logical, cunning, and observant. Plot. Chimera Ant arc. Gon, Killua, and Kite meet Yunju's division inside a hidden drug factory of NGL. They start to fight and Centipede is sent after Gon. During the fight, Centipede is amazed by Gon's enormous physical strength and starts to feel his Nen. Afraid that he cannot escape as his leader is watching, he decides to battle Gon. Centipede, intimidated by Gon's power, runs a simulation where he assumes that Gon will use his fist to attack him and that he would parry it at the cost of one side of his arms in order to bite him. Unfortunately for Centipede, Gon, instead of his fists, uses his Janken: Scissors Nen ability and bifurcates him. Fatally injured but not dead, Centipede waits on the floor for Gon to come near him so that he can at least poison him with his fangs, but is shot dead by Kite, who tells Gon that he needs to crush the Chimera Ants' head to be sure that they are dead. Abilities & Powers. Centipede, like all Chimera Ants, is stronger than normal humans. In battle, he uses his numerous arms to deliver a barrage of fists against his enemies. As a last resort, Centipede can also poison them with his poisonous fangs.

Cha-R Family The Cha-R Family (, "Sha A Ikka") is one of the three largest Mafia families in the Kakin Empire. Its Boss is Brocco Li. Seventh Prince Luzurus Hui Guo Rou is one of their benefactors. Plot. Succession Contest arc. About 250 members of the Cha-R Family boarded the Black Whale in order to secure territory on the New Continent. The boss is a VIP on Tier 1 of the ship. The underlings are scheming to whittle down the numbers of the two rival families, Xi-Yu and Heil-Ly. They control Tier 5 and all its commodities. A large group from the Cha-R Family approaches the Phantom Troupe and rudely asks them to leave. Though Chrollo Lucilfer initially refuses, the Troupe members relent after the group's leader informs the Spiders that their previous rampage in Yorknew City made things easier for the Mafia families to get to the New Continent. The leader asks the Troupe to join them, but Chrollo politely declines. After the Spiders leave, the leader decides to inform their Underboss about the situation and plans to dispose of the Troupe. After a phone call with Onior Longbao, Brocco Li orders Ken'i to find Hisoka before the Phantom Troupe. A mysterious assassin kills the Cha-R men guarding the storehouse where Nobunaga Hazama, Phinks Magcub, and Feitan Portor head to recover their weapons after receiving the family's permission. Ken'i confronts them before the door of the family's hideout. Still, after learning that the assassin infiltrated it and tried to access the passage to the upper tiers before vanishing, as well as hearing of Ittoku's conversation with Franklin Bordeau, he becomes convinced of their innocence. Despite considering them loose cannons to be taken out as soon as possible, the Underboss suggests teaming up. The three Spiders are welcomed into the hideout. Nobunaga offers to kill the teleporting assassin in return for being allowed to open the door he wanted to get through. The Spiders are thus inserted into the surveillance rounds. Over the next few days, the Cha-R Family has eight of its members searching for Hisoka killed by an assassin, and the Xi-Yu Family loses as many as 300. That Saturday night, Ken'i and Vice Boss Tajao conclude the responsible is someone from the Heil-Ly Family, but they are unable to locate Morena, whose presence on Tier 3 following the attacks would be interpreted as the signal to start an all-out war. Tajao then meets the three Spiders, who receive confirmation that the door inside the hideout indeed leads to Tier 1. Nobunaga and Phinks volunteer to kill the teleporting assassin as well as Morena. Members. There are about 250 members of the family who boarded the Black Whale, including fringe members.

Chameleon Cat (G.I card) Chameleon Cat (カメレオンキャット, "Kamereon Kyatto") is a card found in the Greed Island game. It is one of the game's 100 designated slot cards and is required for a player to complete the game. This cat is able to shape-shift into any other animal. Summary. Chameleon Cat カメレオンキャット - This card when activated, allows the user to bring forth a Chameleon Cat. This endangered species once tamed, can freely transform into any animal. It does however, retain its original size and mass. This means that if it were to transform into an elephant, it would still be the same size (and weight) of the original cat.

Chapter 1 The Day of Departure (の, "Shuppatsu no Hi") is the 1st chapter of the Hunter × Hunter manga, written and illustrated by Yoshihiro Togashi. Synopsis. It's first stated that there exist strange creatures, secret treasures, and unexplored places in the world and that individuals called Hunters are captivated by this mysterious unknown. On Whale Island, a young boy is seen sitting high up in a tree and waiting to catch a creature with his fishing rod. Once the lure bobs in the water below, the boy grips the fishing rod tightly and tries his best to hold on as the creature moves on the hook. He bides his time and suddenly lifts up on the line, sending the enormous creature into the air as he celebrates. Carrying the fish on his back, the boy happily returns to town and sets his catch down in front of a gathering crowd. The onlookers are impressed that the Master of the Swamp has finally been caught, with one man adding that he thought it wouldn't happen for years. The boy turns to his aunt named Mito and tells her that she has to keep her end of the deal, holding out an application card for the Hunter Exam. With Mito appearing worried, two men assure her that it's just an exam and that Gon can definitely pass it, causing her to angrily rebuke them. Gon is seen still holding out the application and again reminds Mito of their deal. Letting out a sigh, Mito signs the application for him before returning home, with Gon thanking her and happily running in the opposite direction. Inside their house, Mito is left distraught with her hands over her face as an old woman looks at a picture of a man in front of a motorcycle and says that blood will tell. Mito then slams her fists down on the table and points out that she never told Gon that his father was a Hunter and that Gon never asked, wondering why he is so eager to become one as well. The old woman replies that while it wasn't a big secret, it doesn't matter why, and that she knew the day would come, adding that she can tell by the gleam in his eyes how much determination Gon has. Elsewhere on the island, Gon tells himself that while Mito tried to keep it quiet, he learned about his father a long time ago. After taking the application to a small console along the road, Gon heads further into the woods and lets out a whistle, causing a large creature to suddenly appear and happily embrace him as the two fall into the nearby stream. With his clothes hanging up to dry above a small fire, Gon uses his fishing rod to catch fish. With the creature happily eating one, Gon holds a small card in his hand and looks at it intently as the shadow of an angry creature appears metaphorically on his head. In a flashback to three years earlier, an angry creature roars at Gon in the woods as he lies crying on the ground with a wound to his left shoulder. With a cub standing behind it, the creature prepares to strike Gon with one of its claws, but a man with a "katana" suddenly appears and stops its claw with the sheathed weapon as a small card falls from his person. Preparing to unsheathe the sword, he recognizes that the animal is a foxbear with a cub and that any creature who tries to kill a human must be put down, suddenly killing the adult foxbear with a single strike. He asks Gon if he can stand, and as Gon approaches him holding his injured shoulder, the man punches him and sends him flying back, angrily calling him an idiot for wandering around a Snakebeech Forest at that time of year. He points to the foxbear's territorial markings on a nearby tree and wonders if his father even taught him anything, adding that a speckled squirrel's warning call made him aware of the attack and lamenting that he had to pointlessly kill an animal. Gon then tells the man that both his father and mother died in an accident after he was born, adding that he lives with his aunt. The man shows some sympathy and tosses Gon an antiseptic for his wound before approaching the cub near its mother's body. As the cub angrily roars at them and its fur bristles, Gon asks what he plans to do with it, and the man quickly replies that he will have to put it down as well, explaining that it will starve to death since it hasn't been weaned or that it could hold a grudge against humans if it does manage to survive. Gon quickly runs toward the cub and holds it in his arms, offering to take care of it. The man tries to explain that foxbears are completely wild, and the cub then begins to claw into Gon's right arm as the boy turns toward the man with tears and a determined gleam in his eyes. Taken aback, the man asks Gon if his father was named Ging. After Gon puts down the cub and asks him if he knows his father, the man reveals that his father is the reason he's there on the island, explaining that he came to his birthplace looking for leads. The two sit down on a log, and the man tells Gon that he is a Hunter named Kite. He explains that Ging is his teacher and that his final test involves finding him. He continues by saying that there's no other Hunter like Ging and that he would've died long ago if he hadn't met him. As the two continue to happily talk, Kite assures Gon that Ging is alive and that his aunt only wanted to protect him by not telling him the truth. He tells Gon that blood tells and that he can easily see that he is Ging's son, finally adding that all good Hunters get along well with animals before taking his leave. The foxbear cub then playfully approaches Gon as the small card that fell from Kite rests in the grass nearby. Back in the present, Gon holds the card in his hand and sits up, telling the now older foxbear named Kon that he is going to be a Hunter. He explains that Hunters sometimes do things that animals don't like or even hate, adding that an animal who befriends a Hunter can't be king of the forest. Gon gives Kon this title and says that he doesn't want it to change, asking if he understands. Kon stares at Gon before turning and walking away. Gon is left unsure, but several animals of the forest suddenly appear with Kon. Gon then happily says goodbye to Kon and tells him that he rules as Kon and the other animals wave goodbye. After sprinting back home, Gon finds Mito drinking before she quickly asks him when he leaves. Gon’s reply is the first of next week, and Mito understands that he knew his father's profession all along. She then asks him if he knows that Ging left him with her when he was still a baby, wondering if he still plans to leave. However, Gon unexpectedly replies that being a Hunter must be so important that family comes second. With Mito quickly turning around to look at him and her glass crashing, Gon smiles and adds that weaklings aren't able to become Hunters. Taken aback by Gon’s comments, Mito storms off and says that he really is Ging's son, slamming the door to her room. Gon cleans up the spilled drink and apologizes to Mito internally, but repeats that he is Ging's son. He then remembers Kite's words about passing Ging's final test and that Ging is unlike any other Hunter. With Gon intent on finding his father, the day of his departure arrives and he makes his way to the harbor. One of the townspeople gives him a gift, and another tells him to take care of himself. Mito suddenly appears at the dock, and Gon happily runs toward her, thanking her for everything. Mito quickly apologizes before telling Gon that she lied about Ging abandoning him, revealing that she made Ging give him up. Gon replies that he guessed it was the case and, as Mito embraces him, that she never looks him in the eye when she lies. Once aboard the ship, Gon waves goodbye to Mito and confidently tells her that he will come back as a great Hunter. With the ship moving further and further away from Whale Island, one of the applicants chuckles and mocks Gon's words, pointing out that the dozen of them on the deck are only a fraction of those who apply for the yearly exam and that only a handful of those are accepted. The man then tells Gon that even if he gets accepted, the exam will most likely be the last thing he attempts in his life, adding that he shouldn't be so confident. With Gon now appearing uneasy, it's stated that Gon's journey to find his father and become a Hunter has begun. The captain's words about the journey being rough are quoted, and it's said that these linger in Gon's mind.

Chapter 10 An Unexpected Task (な, "Igai na Kadai") is the 10th chapter of the Hunter × Hunter manga, written and illustrated by Yoshihiro Togashi. Synopsis. In the Milsy Wetlands, Cherry's corpse is seen hanging upside down on a tree, with playing cards stuck in his neck and forehead as several birds approach the meal. With the two unaware of this, Gon and Kurapika run to catch up with the rest of the examinees. Gon sniffs the air and says that they need to keep heading in the same direction. A confused Kurapika tries to smell the air as well and asks Gon if he can really smell Leorio. Gon explains that the scent of Leorio's cologne carries for miles, also pointing out the multiple dead animals along the way and guessing that they tried to attack Hisoka as he was carrying him. Gon then asks Kurapika what Hisoka meant when he said that he and Leorio passed, repeating Hisoka's words about being done with Leorio. Kurapika replies that Hisoka sees himself as an examiner and that he was grading them, but Gon says that Hisoka only looked at him for a second. Kurapika reminds Gon that he was the only one to land a hit on Hisoka, but Gon wonders how Leorio passed after getting knocked out by Hisoka's punch. Kurapika guesses that Hisoka is relying on his instincts, and Gon immediately thinks of Killua, who was able to smell Hisoka's bloodlust. While Kurapika reveals that he thinks Hisoka is too bloodthirsty to become a Hunter, he praises his technique and describes his dexterity as close to superhuman. He also speaks highly of Hisoka's skill in combat and guesses that he used his intuition and experience to recognize Gon's potential. He adds that Hisoka may have decided not to kill Gon yet, but quickly apologizes and says that he was out of line. Not upset by the remark, Gon says that he was terrified by all the corpses around him and Hisoka walking toward him, revealing that he was too afraid to even run and that he thought he was dead. However, even though he was afraid of dying, he also describes the feeling as exciting. At the site of the Second Phase, a strange noise is heard inside a lone building. Outside, Satotz congratulates the examinees for making it through the wetlands and arriving at the Visca Forest Preserve. As the examinees catch their breath, Satotz takes his leave and wishes them good luck. He then tells himself that he didn't expect 150 to make it through the First Phase, having guessed that it would be less than 100 and praising the quality of the year's applicants. However, he feels bad that Buhara and Menchi are the Second Phase examiners, guessing that the number will fall to at least 50 and deciding to watch what happens. Gon and Kurapika finally catch up with the others, and both desperately look for Hisoka or Leorio among the crowd. Gon suddenly gets a feeling from directly behind him and turns around to see Hisoka, who happily points to Gon's left where they find Leorio sitting up against a tree. Kurapika is happy to see that Leorio is fine besides his swollen face and the wound to his arm. Gon asks him when he regained consciousness, and Leorio replies that he just woke up, wondering how he got knocked out and admitting that he can't remember much after they entered the wetlands. After the two agree not to tell Leorio anything about what happened, Gon wonders why everyone is standing around outside the building, and Killua tells him that they can't get inside. Gon is ecstatic to see him, and Killua is stunned that Gon made it there by following the scent of Leorio's cologne, guessing that he must be half dog. Gon wonders why they can't get inside, and Killua points to the sign above the door which states that the Second Phase begins at noon. The noises continue to emanate from the building, and Killua adds that they have no clue what's making them. With the examinees left in suspense, the clock finally reaches noon and the double doors open, revealing a woman sitting in front of an enormous man whose stomach is loudly growling. Menchi explains that the Second Phase will involve cooking and reveals that they are both Gourmet Hunters. It's stated that Gourmet Hunters, who are usually world-class chefs, travel around the world looking for rare and exotic food to create new delicacies. With the examinees left confused, Buhara tells them that they will first make a dish for him, and Menchi adds that they will then make one for her if Buhara passes them. The two examiners add that they will only pass the Second Phase once both of them are satisfied and that once they have eaten enough, the testing period will end. A few of the examinees guess that while Buhara could eat entire buffets, Menchi probably doesn't have nearly as big an appetite. Among those worrying about the test is Leorio, who says that he has never cooked in his life. With the examinees left wondering what they will have to make, Buhara eagerly reveals that he wants whole roast pigs and that any pig in the preserve will work. Once they are told to get cooking, the 148 examinees all run toward the forest, and while Gon and Leorio are confident that it will be easy, Kurapika reminds them that they still need to hurry before Buhara's appetite is satiated. Menchi chuckles and tells Buhara that his comment was mean since Visca Forest only has one kind of pig. After heading deep enough into the forest, the three examinees are the first to come across a herd of Great Stamps, which Buhara calls the most ferocious pig in the world. The pigs charge toward the trio and use their large snouts to send them flying into the air. Still in midair, Gon likens the thrill to what he experienced with Hisoka, but says that it still doesn't compare, using his fishing rod to strike one of the Great Stamps on the forehead. The three safely land, and Leorio guesses that Gon found their soft spot, with Kurapika adding that they probably developed their snouts to protect their foreheads. After hearing the squealing and rumbling in the distance, Buhara suddenly sees multiple examinees carrying roasted Great Stamps on their backs. As Buhara drools with excitement and prepares to start eating, Satotz is seen watching high up in a nearby tree and again mentions how exceptional the group of applicants is.

Chapter 100 September 3rd: Part 16 (93⑯, "Kugatsu Mikka (Jū Roku)") is the 100th chapter of the Hunter × Hunter manga, written and illustrated by Yoshihiro Togashi. Synopsis. As the blast continues to shake the Cemetery Building and smoke billows out from the first floor, Bean tries his best to calm down the worried Mafia members, telling them to follow him to the auction hall to watch a live video from the Ten Dons. One of the members makes sure that it's not being held in the basement, and Bean assures him that they moved it to the tenth floor. The man is glad that they will be able to follow Neon's fortune about avoiding stairs that they haven't already climbed, with two others confirming the accuracy of her fortunes. In the crowded auction hall, a member of the Ten Dons appears on screen and reveals that the Phantom Troupe's leader has been killed, causing the Mafia members to cheer and applaud. The Don assures them that the other members will be killed in due time, adding that he and the other Dons will watch the auction as the camera shows all of them sitting around a table. However, at the Dons' location, a fly suddenly lands on one of their eyes as several of Illumi's needles are shown in the back of his head. Illumi appears in the doorway and activates the Zoldyck personal transmitter. Back in the Cemetery Building, as the smoke clears around them, Silva says that the device only rings when an assassination has been successfully completed. After Silva answers and Illumi asks where his client is, Chrollo and Zeno are shown freeing themselves from the rubble. Illumi asks if they were just now fighting, glad to hear that Chrollo is still alive and relaying the message that they have dealt with the Ten Dons. As Illumi tells him to wire the money, Kalluto and a short, old man are also seen at the Dons' location. Zeno is relieved to be through with the fight, and Chrollo asks him if he plans to finish him off. Zeno tells him that since the Dons were their clients and they're no longer alive, any arrangement with them is now void. The tattered Chrollo replies that he won't get another chance to fight and kill him, and Zeno asks if he thinks that they do jobs for fun, adding that they don't enjoy killing and that he doesn't want to work or die for nothing. Chrollo then asks who would have won if they were fighting one-on-one, and Zeno confidently replies that he would have, but adds that it would be a different matter if Chrollo were actually trying to kill him. After the two Zoldycks leave the ruined room, Chrollo falls exhausted to the floor and tells himself that he wouldn't have been able to steal his ability. As Neon rests in a room with Light by her side, Melody calls Kurapika and asks if they should wait at the hospital, which Kurapika confirms since things are too dangerous at the Cemetery Building. The doctor says that the unconscious Neon should be fine, but still advises taking her to the hospital since it would be safer. Light worries about moving her, but Kurapika assures him that the Troupe would have already attacked the ambulance if they had wanted to do so. As the ambulance transports Neon to the hospital, Chrollo exits the building and takes off his headband, telling the other members by phone to forget about the ambulance and continue with the plan. Inside the auction hall, the announcer begins the event with the first item as the crowd cheers and applauds. Bean walks backstage and pulls out a cigarette, happy that the frightening situation is now resolved and none of the capos were hurt. He has trouble finding his lighter, and someone suddenly holds it up from the darkness, with the light revealing Hisoka's face. Before Bean can react, Machi quickly appears and hangs him with her thread. The announcer introduces the first item, a Solid-Gold Execution Sword from the Yul National Treasury, which Pakunoda wheels out onto the stage. As the bid reaches 50 million, it's revealed that Shalnark is using his Black Voice ability to control the announcer. The manipulated announcer then introduces a Celadon Porcelain Vase from the Lai Dynasty, which the Troupe members find among the items. Shizuku hands it to Kortopi, who uses his Gallery Fake ability to create an exact copy of it. The announcer starts the bidding on the fake item at 100 million, and the amount quickly climbs to 380 million. Kurapika approaches two Mafia members and asks them if the auction has started. The two inform him that the Troupe's leader was killed and that the assassins are looking for the others. Zenji approaches the confused Kurapika and says that the two Zoldycks took care of the job while he was wasting time with the ambulance. He mockingly tells him to go fawn over Neon at the hospital or hotel, but as he asks if he wants to hold his master's hand, Kurapika suddenly punches him directly in the face. As the bloody Zenji falls to the floor, Kurapika tells himself that he won't believe the leader of the Troupe to be dead until he sees it with his own eyes.

Chapter 101 September 3rd: Part 17 (93⑰, "Kugatsu Mikka (Jū Nana)") is the 101st chapter of the Hunter × Hunter manga, written and illustrated by Yoshihiro Togashi. Synopsis. Kurapika is left stunned when he sees Chrollo's mangled corpse up against a piece of rubble. One Mafia member asks where Bean is as several others stand around Chrollo's body. Grabbing Chrollo by the hair, one is surprised that he is the Phantom Troupe's leader and another says that he's just a punk. The others tell them not to cause any more damage to his face since they plan to put a picture of him on the Internet. After the bodies of Shalnark, Shizuku, Feitan, and Machi are found together, they also find the body of Franklin slumped against a wall. One member tells the others to use dental records, DNA, and fingerprints to find out the identities of all six and then to kill all their friends and loved ones to serve as a warning. After Kurapika hurries back to the auction, the announcer introduces the last item: a set of Scarlet Eyes. Pakunoda wheels the item onto the stage, and the announcer says that there are only 36 pairs in existence after the Kurta Clan was wiped out. As he praises their exceptional color and starts the bidding at 100 million, Kurapika calls Light to inform him about the Troupe leader's death and the auction, asking if he should bid on the eyes. Light adamantly tells him to win them, and Kurapika asks if he has a bidding limit, with Light replying that he doesn't care what he has to pay. The bid rises to 310 million and then quickly to 371 million before Kurapika raises it to 500 million. However, Zenji suddenly appears and raises it to 1 billion, leaving Kurapika and the crowd stunned. After some time passes, Light learns that Kurapika had to raise the bid to 2.9 billion to beat out Zenji. Light curses him internally, but assures himself that the money will go back to the community and only increase his prestige. As he praises Kurapika, he tells himself that it's an investment since he will easily make the money back with Neon's fortunes. He looks at his sleeping daughter and says that he only needs to keep her in a good mood to have all the money and power he wants. The announcer confirms that Kurapika is from the Nostrade Family, and Phinks and Pakunoda prepare the eyes in a box for him as Hisoka snickers in disguise. After Kurapika goes to a bathroom to take out his contact lenses and wash his face, he carries the eyes to the hospital and suddenly runs into Zenji holding a gun. Zenji asks him if he thought he could get away from him, pointing the gun at him and threatening to shoot if he doesn't stop. With his aura swelling around him and his eyes turning scarlet, Kurapika warns him that if he doesn't move aside, he could become his new target. Zenji begins to sweat and is left frozen with fear, asking himself how Kurapika could frighten him so much. After Kurapika calmly walks by him, Zenji catches his breath and is left dumbstruck as he wonders who he is. Gon and Killua return to their hotel room to find Leorio and Zepile laughing and drinking together. Killua asks if the two of them have been sitting around while they were captured. Leorio is surprised that it's already night, and Zepile tells them to have a drink. Killua tells Leorio that he thought he was a minor, and Leorio replies that the drinking age is 16 in his country, adding that he started when he was only 12. He says that he's glad they made it back alive, and Zepile asks about how dangerous the Troupe is. Gon happily tells him that the doctoring methods he taught them were helpful, and Zepile adds that experience allows people to learn about their blind spots, also guessing that forgery would be useful against the Troupe. Leorio says that Zepile also taught him about forgery, then asking Gon and Killua if they plan to go to the auction tomorrow. The two reply that while they would like to go, they need to meet up with Kurapika so he can teach them more about Nen. Leorio points out that Kurapika himself just learned Nen recently as well, but Gon reveals that he already killed one of Troupe members. Leorio can't believe it, and Killua guesses that there's more to Nen than just experience and power. At the hospital, Neon receives the Scarlet Eyes and happily thanks her father. He asks if she forgives him for lying about the auction, and she replies that she does. Light leaves the room and tells the bodyguards that they will return to the hotel since Neon is fine. He also says that they just need to win the celebrity tissues at the auction tomorrow and that while he will be leaving the day after tomorrow, Neon can stay behind to shop more, with both Melody and Basho remembering how draining it is to look after her. Melody assures Kurapika that he can rest while they deal with the auction and Neon's shopping. After Kurapika thanks her and walks away, Basho asks Melody if he's okay. Gon's phone rings, and Kurapika tells him that they don't need to help him stop the Troupe anymore since its members are dead. He hangs up before Gon can say anything in reply, and Killua can't believe it when Gon tells him what Kurapika said. At the Troupe's hideout, Hisoka tries to call Kurapika but is unable to get through, guessing that he turned off his phone. As he says that he was going to cheer him up, the Troupe members are seen drinking and celebrating with the stolen auction items behind them.

Chapter 102 September 4th: Part 1 (94①, "Kugatsu Yokka (Ichi)") is the 102nd chapter of the Hunter × Hunter manga, written and illustrated by Yoshihiro Togashi. Synopsis. Throughout the city, people talk about the video of the Phantom Troupe's dismembered bodies, with one mentioning that the people may have had bounties on their heads. Kurapika receives a text from Gon and Killua telling him that they will be waiting at Dayroad Park. It's then stated that Shalnark is a Manipulator whose ability allows him to attach an antenna to his target and completely control them with a unique cell phone until the antenna is removed. Elsewhere, two Mafia members become upset with a hacker since he hasn't been able identify the dead Troupe members in six hours. The man tells them that the Troupe members don't exist, explaining that he checked various records going back 60 years and found that they never existed. The Mafia member asks if they deleted their records, but the hacker assures him that it's a severe offense to even try to hack into the International Human Databank. He adds that because of the databank's complex system, any deletions or changes would be fixed within seconds. The hacker again repeats that the Troupe members don't exist, but the other Mafia member angrily reminds him that they have their bodies. The hacker coyly replies that they don't exist according to society and that their births were never officially acknowledged. The first Mafia member counters by saying that even babies who are abandoned receive an ID and have to register, but the hacker reveals that there is one place exempt from all that: Meteor City. He explains that the city's residents will accept anything abandoned there, from trash to dead bodies to babies. As the Mafia members continue to listen, the hacker says that eight million people reportedly live there and that the area is around the size of the Lapet Republic (6,000 km2). However, he adds that no one officially lives there since it's been considered the world's dump for 1,500 years. Although he is unsure what life is like in the city and what its citizens are taught or believe in, he says that they only have one message to the rest of the world: they will accept anything that is left there, but no one must ever take anything away from them. He then recounts an incident that happened ten years earlier: a homeless man with no ID was arrested for murder, and the officials could find no trace of his existence. He told them that he was from Meteor City and assured them that he was innocent, but was prosecuted and found guilty after not being given sufficient defense. Three years later, after a drug addict was arrested and it was discovered that he was behind the earlier murder, 31 people involved in the case were all killed, with the aforementioned message left near their bodies. The hacker warns the two Mafia members to avoid fighting the Troupe if they're actually from Meteor City, further explaining that the city's residents used suicide bombers to blow up all 31 targets simultaneously. He stresses that if they are willing to sacrifice 31 of their own to kill 31 others because one of their own was unfairly detained, they should not be confronted. Lastly, he adds that the Ten Dons would agree with his assessment. At the Troupe's hideout, Chrollo tells the group that they will be leaving the city that night after they take the rest of the auction's loot. Even after hearing Chrollo's full order, Nobunaga refuses to accept it and says that they still need to find the chain user. Chrollo tells him not to worry about it, but Nobunaga refuses to back down. Franklin tells him to drop it and follow Chrollo's order, but as his aura swells around him, Nobunaga asks Chrollo if he's really speaking as their leader. In a flashback to Meteor City, Chrollo remembers tossing around a videotape with a young Franklin and Shalnark, saying that they just wanted something in the beginning but not completing his thought. At Dayroad Park, as Kurapika approaches his two friends having an eating contest, Gon opens his mouth to say Kurapika's name and causes food to fly across Killua's face. Gon runs to meet him and notices his somber expression, but before Kurapika can say anything, Gon says that he's happy for him since he can focus on finding the eyes of his people now that the Spiders are dead. Before Gon can finish his offer to help, Killua appears behind him and smashes a piece of food all over his face. As the two tussle on the ground, Kurapika lets out a sigh of relief and begins to laugh.

Chapter 103 September 4th: Part 2 (94②, "Kugatsu Yokka (Ni)") is the 103rd chapter of the Hunter × Hunter manga, written and illustrated by Yoshihiro Togashi. Synopsis. At the Preview Market, the announcer says that the final bid for the wooden vault is 355 million. While Zepile is disappointed that it didn't make more and confident that it could have reached 400 million with a better time slot, Leorio remains ecstatic from the amount of money and jokingly says that they would each have 170 million if they just took it all. Zepile assures himself that he will have more chances if he continues to team up with the two boys, telling Leorio that the experience will be priceless. As Leorio smiles and agrees with him, his phone suddenly rings with a call from Kurapika. It's stated that Kortopi is a Conjurer whose ability allows him to create an exact copy of an object with his right hand by touching the original with his left. It's added that he can only replicate living things as inanimate objects and that regardless of the object's size, any copies will vanish after 24 hours. After the four meet at an extravagant hotel, Gon happily says that it's been a while since they have all been together, wondering where Zepile is. Leorio tells him that he's picking up the money and looking for more items to sell. He then turns to Kurapika and says that his presence seems stronger, with Kurapika telling him that he hasn't changed much. Quickly shrugging off the remark, Leorio brings up the fact that Kurapika killed a Phantom Troupe member, asking him how he did it so soon after learning Nen. Kurapika says that he refuses to help him if he wants to catch one as well, and while Gon replies that they do want to capture some of the Spiders, he adds that they also want to learn more about Nen. However, Kurapika reveals that his ability can only be used against the Troupe before the four continue their conversation in one of the hotel's rooms. He explains the concept of a contract with limitations and that Nen becomes more powerful and the risk greater if the user is more determined. He then reveals that he vowed to use most of his ability only when fighting the Spiders and that if he uses his chains on anyone else, the Nen dagger in his heart will kill him. As the others continue to listen in shock, Kurapika says that because his ability was born from hatred, it will only work against the Spiders. He says that he is only revealing this much because he trusts them, telling them to keep it all a secret. Killua suddenly stands up and angrily asks why he would reveal something so important. Kurapika wonders why as well and guesses that it was because he felt disheartened after learning that the Troupe's leader is dead. Killua points out that not all the members are dead and that one of them has the ability to read memories by touching her target. As Killua worries that they will find out Kurapika's secret, Gon assures him that the memory reader didn't find out when she read them. However, Killua reminds him that both of them didn't know that the chain user was Kurapika at the time. Leorio thinks that they should be fine as long as they stay away from her, guessing that they won't be checked again since they're no longer suspects. However, Killua stresses that Nobunaga is the real problem since he won't stop looking for both them and Kurapika. Although Leorio points out that Nobunaga doesn't know how they're connected, Kurapika reveals that he has been in contact with Hisoka and that he knows he's the chain user. He explains that while they had an alliance, he can't be sure what Hisoka will do now that the Troupe's leader is dead. Killua proposes hunting the others down since it's too dangerous to stay on the defensive. Although he worries about Nobunaga tracking them down, he says that they now have Kurapika's help. He insists that they should stop the remaining Troupe members before they disappear and regroup, adding that it becomes more likely the longer they wait. Killua hides his face from Kurapika and gives a wry smile toward Gon, telling himself that it's the only way to capture the Spiders and obtain the money they need. Back at the Troupe's hideout, in response to Nobunaga's question, Chrollo suddenly conjures his book and tells him to answer his questions.

Chapter 104 September 4th: Part 3 (94③, "Kugatsu Yokka (San)") is the 104th chapter of the Hunter × Hunter manga, written and illustrated by Yoshihiro Togashi. Synopsis. At the Phantom Troupe's hideout, Chrollo asks Nobunaga for his birthday, but a confused Nobunaga wonders why he's asking him. Chrollo rephrases the question and asks him when he was born, with Nobunaga saying September 8, 1970. Chrollo then asks for his blood type and name, and Nobunaga answers with B and Nobunaga Hazama, wondering why Chrollo is asking him if he already knows it. After Nobunaga writes the information down on a piece of paper, Chrollo uses Neon's Lovely Ghostwriter ability to tell Nobunaga's fortune. The first two sections differ slightly from Chrollo's as Nobunaga reads through his fortune.
