Once their airship lands at Lingon Airport, Hisoka reveals to her that his real fortune had said he would fight Chrollo on Tuesday and the Troupe would lose half its limbs by the time he left. He says that every action they take changes their fate, saying goodbye as he turns to leave. Walking back to the hideout in the rain, Pakunoda spots a small cat in an alley and playfully meows back at it. Once she returns and stands in front of the Troupe members with her gun at the ready, she tells Phinks that Chrollo can't come back there. Phinks angrily asks her if she's joking and orders her to explain, threatening to use violence if they don't like her answer. Pakunoda readies her aura and gun, telling herself that she can fire six shots at once, which is the same number of founding members. She asks Feitan, Phinks, Machi, Nobunaga, Shalnark, and Franklin if they trust her as she aims her gun toward them. As Pakunoda prepares to use her Memory Bomb ability and shoot out all her memories, Phinks worries that she is being manipulated, but Nobunaga gets his attention and tells him that it's really her. After Pakunoda fires one shot into each of their heads, Kurapika's Judgment Chain activates around her heart and kills her as she falls to the ground and asks that she be the last Troupe member to die. With the members left stunned, all of Pakunoda's memories suddenly flood into their minds. Shizuku checks on Pakunoda and confirms that she's dead, asking the others how it happened. Phinks says that he will explain everything and begins to tell the others why Pakunoda made her decision. Now alone, Chrollo looks toward the east and prepares to fulfill the final part of his fortune.

Chapter 12 The Chairman Arrives (, "Kaichō Sanjō") is the 12th chapter of the Hunter × Hunter manga, written and illustrated by Yoshihiro Togashi. Synopsis. Talking with someone on the phone, Menchi refuses to redo the test and becomes upset when told that she didn't adhere to the established criteria, pointing out that she judged according to her taste. Buhara adds that it also depended on the examinees' ability to understand her hints, and Menchi angrily tells him to mind his own business. She then tells the person on the phone that a certain examinee revealed the basics to the others and caused the issue, with Hanzo looking on nervously. After repeating that she doesn't have to redo the test, she announces to the examinees that they have all failed, causing the group to mutter amongst themselves and leaving them unsure about what to do. At a hotel in a unknown city, the small official who handed out the Hunter Exam badges tries to call Menchi again but finds that she has turned off her cell phone. He asks the Chairman what they should do, and an old man is seen crouching as he balances a drink on his foot. He points out that she won't budge from her position, and the official stresses that there are too many irregularities and that Menchi simply stopped testing the examinees. The Chairman prepares to make his way to the site of the Second Phase, and the official apologizes for inconveniencing him, but the old man replies that it's the job of a Chairman and that similar situations have happened before. He explains that while Hunters can be stubborn and there have been years where no one has passed, they can't allow it to happen because of one examiner's ego. As the two travel by airship to the exam site, Todo smashes a table and proclaims that he's there to become a Hunter, not to cook sushi. He adds that he plans to become a Blacklist Hunter and wants a real test, mocking the idea of a Gourmet Hunter. Menchi again refuses to back down and wishes him better luck next year, enraging Todo even more and causing him to charge toward her. However, Buhara uses a powerful slap to send the examinee out of the building before he lands bloody and unconscious on the ground. Menchi tells him that the attack was uncalled for, but Buhara points out that Menchi would have killed Todo if he hadn't intervened. Revealing two blades and spinning them in her hands, Menchi replies that he may be right and then mocks Todo's aspiration to become a Blacklist Hunter, pointing out that even Gourmet Hunters have to be proficient in the martial arts. Now wielding four knives, she explains that they often journey to distant places to obtain rare foods and that they also deal with poachers, stressing to the examinees that they should have a burning desire to challenge the unknown. A voice is suddenly heard over a loudspeaker asking Menchi about her questionable decision, and the examinees all look up to see an airship with the Hunter Association logo, recognizing that it's the judging committee. The Chairman leaps down from the airship and leaves the examinees in disbelief that he jumped down nearly 60 feet. Menchi addresses him as Chairman Netero, the head of the Exam Commission. Menchi obediently listens to Netero, which all the examinees recognize, and Netero proceeds to ask her if she failed them because they lacked the desire to challenge the unknown, also telling himself how cute she is. Menchi admits that she became upset when an examinee disparaged the test and then became even more upset when all the examinees learned how to make the dish in question, which made her lose her appetite. She also adds that she is very emotional about food and admits that she failed as an examiner, offering to resign and withdraw her decision. As Todo awakens in pain nearby, Netero stresses that continuing the present test would compromise the exam results, suggesting that Menchi continue as the examiner and asking her to participate in a new test to set an example. With Menchi left unsure, Netero explains that it will let the examinees know that it's possible to complete it. As Todo stands up and tells himself that he won't forget the humiliation he suffered, Menchi accepts the offer and proposes boiled eggs, asking Netero to transport everyone by airship to Split Mountain. Netero happily agrees to the proposal, and the examinees travel to the nearby mountain where Menchi shows them the deepest ravine in the area. After explaining that a river at the bottom will take a person to the sea, Menchi takes off her shoes and suddenly jumps down into the ravine, leaving the examinees stunned and thinking that she's dead. However, Netero points out that she headed for the nesting area of Spider Eagles, which spin their webs across the ravine and use them to safely store their eggs. Menchi grabs one of the strands and then hangs upside down, using her legs to hold on and grabbing an egg before climbing back up to the top. After she happily tells them that they just need to boil it in order to pass, Todo tells himself that she made it look easy, but wonders why any sane person would attempt it. Gon and Killua are eager to try, and Leorio adds that it seems much better than cooking. Several examinees then leap down into the ravine and collect their eggs as others stay behind out of fear. Netero tells them that there's no shame in recognizing one's limits and that they can take the exam another time. The eggs are boiled in a large pot over a fire, and Menchi shows them the difference between a chicken egg and a Spider Eagle egg. The examinees can't believe the difference in taste and describe the latter as having a creamy texture, calling the former a rubber ball in comparison. Menchi hopes that they now understand that Gourmet Hunters seek treasures beyond just jewels or artifacts. Todo gets permission from Gon to try a bite of the egg and, after experiencing the taste, says that he will try again next year. With Menchi left smiling, it's stated that 42 examinees passed the Second Phase.

Chapter 120 September 6th: Part 1 (96①, "Kugatsu Muika (Ichi)") is the 120th chapter of the Hunter × Hunter manga, written and illustrated by Yoshihiro Togashi. Synopsis. As Kurapika succumbs to a fever, Leorio notes that it hasn't gone down at all even though a day has already passed. Zepile says that Kurapika should rest, while Melody mentions that her flute did not work on him, so Kurapika's fever is not due to simple fatigue. Meanwhile, Killua and Gon are seen sitting in a room. Gon says that he hopes Kurapika's fever doesn't go down because if the auction passes while Kurapika is asleep, Kurapika will not have to face the Phantom Troupe. Gon adds that Kurapika should not try to fight the Spiders anymore. Killua says that if Kurapika really wanted to kill the Spiders, he would have done it already, but Gon replies that Kurapika would not do that. They then discuss Kurapika's ability. Gon thinks Kurapika would have picked a different ability if he wanted revenge because of the ability's indirect approach. Killua reasons that Kurapika's ability is crafted solely for revenge because he has many targets and his approach helps get information. They then agree that Kurapika should stay still for a while because the Spiders will be on the hunt for him. Killua checks online to see if there is a bounty on their heads, but finds nothing. Gon says that they should be extra careful on the way to the auction. Then Killua inquires about Gon's idea. Gon reassures Killua that it's a good plan with a 50-50 chance. Nevertheless, Killua insists that Gon tells him the plan, so Gon finally divulges it. After listening, Killua commends the idea and says that they will probably have an 80% chance of success. Later that night, Killua, Gon, and Zepile attend the auction. They see Battera, a multi-billionaire, entering the venue, and being interviewed. Battera says that the reason for collecting the Greed Island game is love. As Gon, Killua, and Zepile enter the hall and go to their seats, they encounter Phinks and Feitan, and make a run for it. The two Spiders immediately block their path, with Feitan assuring the two that they mean no harm. Phinks informs them that they have no reason to pursue the "Chain Dude." He explains that since Chrollo was stabbed with a Nen sword, killing the "Chain Dude" will lead to the "Chain Dude"'s Nen, which stemmed from hatred, becoming stronger after death. The Nen will seek out the object of hatred, and since the Nen has already cursed Chrollo, he is vulnerable and may even be killed. Then Phinks looks at Feitan and understands that they should not say anything about Nen exorcism and the fact that Chrollo might already be looking for an exorcist at the moment. He adds that the other Spiders have gone back to their home. Gon asks about Pakunoda, and Phinks candidly says that she's dead, recalling her memories with Gon and Killua. He then leaves with Feitan while telling Gon and Killua that Pakunoda was thankful to them. Inside the auditorium, the auctioneer announces that the auction is open and that bidding will begin.

Chapter 121 September 6th: Part 2 (96②, "Kugatsu Muika (Ni)") is the 121st chapter of the Hunter × Hunter manga, written and illustrated by Yoshihiro Togashi. Synopsis. The Southernpiece Auction begins. Meanwhile, Kurapika wakes up and immediately asks about the Underground Auction and Neon. Melody informs him that the auction was canceled due to the previous events involving the Phantom Troupe, so it will be held online instead. She adds that Neon reluctantly complied. Thinking that Melody is lying, Kurapika says that Neon will not give up easily because of her persistent nature. Melody then mentions the death of Squala and how his girlfriend is overcome with grief. She adds that the Scarlet Eyes were also stolen during that time, but Neon is more upset over Eliza. She finally urges Kurapika to rest more. At the auction, a JoyStation Console containing the Greed Island game is introduced by the auctioneer, who displays its special features and contents. A picture of a professional Hunter named Jeitsari is shown on the screen, and he is introduced as a player of Greed Island. He owns seven cartridges of the game, priced 5.8 billion each. The auctioneer says that Jeitsari left a contract with his lawyer that said if he and the other players have not cleared the game by January 1, 2000, even if they are still inside, he would consign the seven cartridges and consoles to the Southernpiece Auction. She says that two of the players have already lost, and their corpses were found beside the game, so death in the game means death in real life. The auctioneer warns that the game is highly dangerous and those who bid should be prepared for the consequences. The bidding starts, and a bidding war between Milluki and Battera ensues. As the bid gets up to 1.2 billion, Gon accidentally doubles it while asking for the meaning of a hand signal. Then Battera keeps on bidding and eventually wins. After the events, Battera, with his bodyguards, is approached by Gon and Killua. They introduce themselves as Hunters and offer to clear the game for Battera. However, they fail to show their licenses. Battera believes that they are not ordinary children because they have managed to come to the auction. He admits that he is hiring professional Hunters to play the game, but says there is a limit to the number of players, so he cannot hire them on the spot. Killua starts to reassess their plan of approaching Battera and asking him to help clear the game. Gon mentions that the catalog said that the number of players was unlimited, but Battera clarifies that they will need a memory card, and only one person's file can be saved per card, so eight players per cartridge are the maximum. Gon tells Killua that all 30 blocks of the memory card are filled up. Battera asks how Gon knew, and Gon says that they have a save file for Greed Island. Battera then inquires if they have played before, and Gon replies that they only have the card. Battera then says that the game is guarded by Nen and it cannot be reset and the memory card cannot be pulled out. He adds that if Gon and Killua's memory card is real, they will need another item to pull it out. Killua mentions the ring. Battera is then convinced that they are capable and says they deserve an interview as he calls for Tsezguerra, who tells Gon and Killua to show their Ren, and they promptly comply. Battera asks what Tsezguerra thinks, and Tsezguerra says that they are no good and will only end up dead.

Chapter 122 September 6th: Part 3 (96③, "Kugatsu Muika (San)") is the 122nd chapter of the Hunter × Hunter manga, written and illustrated by Yoshihiro Togashi. Synopsis. Tsezguerra tells Battera that Gon and Killua will only end up dead if they play the game Greed Island. Gon complains about how Tsezguerra can tell that before they try, and Tsezguerra replies that it will be too late by then. But he says that it is still better to die than survive in the game, explaining that if a player is alive, it will be impossible to reset or remove the memory card, and if the slots are full, there will be no place to put in new ones. New players will not be able to save, so they will lose all their data once they return to the real world. Battera mentions that he owns 32 copies of the game, including the one he won in the auction, and has hired around 100 players, both professional and amateur Hunters. Some are still playing inside, but half of them (still alive) already gave up. They refuse to return to the real world and their stats on-screen show no change in months, even years. Battera then says that this is the reason they are careful in their selection of new players. They need players who can, at the minimum, return to reality. Gon and Killua still insist and ask them why they cannot play the game. Battera says that Tsezguerra is a professional Hunter and has attempted to complete the game several times. Tsezguerra says that he made five round trips in six months, and from his experience, Gon and Killua will die before they can obtain the item needed to leave the game in their current state. Gon asks if Tsezguerra has completed the game, and Tsezguerra answers that he is 80% through. Tsezguerra announces that he will go back inside the game after the tryouts and will not return until after he clears it. Battera then says that he intends to win all seven copies of Greed Island at the auction and that he is also recruiting players. He adds that he has placed a notice online for the tryouts that will be held on September 10. Tsezguerra says that they have four days to work on their Nen. As Gon and Killua leave, Tsezguerra asks about where they got their memory card, and Gon refuses to answer. Gon and Killua get fired up to ace the tryouts. Battera asks Tsezguerra about what he really thinks about the two. Tsezguerra replies that he is telling the truth that at their current state, Gon and Killua will only get killed, but with their potential, anything can happen in four days. Meanwhile, Phinks and Feitan are seen eavesdropping on the conversation. Gon is still angry about the rejection, while Killua explains that they need to train and take it to the next level to attain their Nen ability or special attack. Killua mentions Kurapika's ability about how he had to risk sacrificing his life and face the consequences that came with achieving it. Killua says that they need to think of an ability that will have appropriate restrictions and suitability to their Nen type. Gon has a hard time thinking up an ability, even though Killua tries to help him. Killua then reveals to Gon that he already has an idea about his ability, but refuses to tell him. Killua says that he will be training on his own to master his special attack, and he urges Gon to think about his own technique too. Killua challenges Gon by saying that maybe he will pass without Gon. Killua starts his training and uses a taser on himself, refining his Nen and releasing a small amount of electricity between his fingertips. As Gon sits alone and tries to come up with a new ability, Tsezguerra's words linger in his mind and irritate him, causing him to unleash his Ren in anger. Meanwhile, Feitan and Phinks are seen in front of a burning car with two dead bodies in the road. The two Troupe members steal a copy of Greed Island and intend to take it back to their hideout to play.

Chapter 123 September 6th: Part 4 (96④, "Kugatsu Muika (Yon)") is the 123rd chapter of the Hunter × Hunter manga, written and illustrated by Yoshihiro Togashi. Synopsis. Back at their base, Phinks and Feitan figure out how to enter Greed Island. After Feitan enters the game first, Franklin, Machi, Shizuku, Kortopi and Shalnark approach Phinks and he tells them that it is the Greed Island game. Phinks invites them to play, then suddenly disappearing as he enters the game. The remaining Spiders ask about the game, and Shalnark reads the catalog. Meanwhile, still mad about Tsezguerra, Gon continues to train. Kurapika approaches him and the two have a conversation. Gon urges Kurapika to rest more, but Kurapika says that he has too much to do. Kurapika inquires about the auction and in the end, Gon tells him about the tryouts. Gon then asks Kurapika what kind of training he did to obtain his Nen ability. Kurapika tells him that after he decided on chains, he began imagery training. He first fiddled with real chains, as his teacher told him to do nothing but play with them. Then his teacher took away the chains as Kurapika began to dream about them, and eventually, he started hallucinating about the chains. Then one day he conjured real chains, and in addition to that, he also practiced Ten and Ren every day. Gon asks Kurapika to be his trainer, but Kurapika refuses because his boss already left Yorknew City, so he needs to follow them. Kurapika adds that he still hasn't settled his business with the Phantom Troupe, but they might have already left, and his priority should be acquiring his clan's Scarlet Eyes. Kurapika then tells Gon to ask his original trainer for advice. Later, Gon calls Wing to get advice, and Wing answers that Enhancers don't need any special attacks since they are the most balanced in terms of attack and defense. Wing says that if Gon continues to practice Ren and Ten, he will eventually become stronger. Wing also tells Gon that even though he does not know much about his situation, Gon should not follow Kurapika's example. Wing then encourages Gon to practice his Ren and Ten every day, but Gon insists that he does not have enough time. Wing says that if he were the judge, he would be disappointed by a special attack hastily thrown together. He continues to encourage Gon by saying that he was already capable when he was at Heavens Arena. He then says that Gon should reflect on everything he is capable of to get the answer he needs. Gon insists that Wing should give him a hint, so Wing finally says that Gon should show everything he has learned at the same time. After the conversation, Gon practices Ten, Zetsu, and Ren as he starts thinking about his special attack. Killua, on the other hand, keeps progressing. He worries about Gon and thinks that he should get it together, because if Gon takes too long, he will be far ahead of him. Meanwhile, Gon looks tired as he tries to figure out what Wing said to him. Gon recalls the time he learned about Nen and thinks about all the techniques he has learned. Gon suddenly remembers Gyo and uses the technique, realizing that he was only focusing on his eyes with not much thought about the rest of his body. Gaining confidence, he attempts to use the technique with his right fist.

Chapter 124 September 7th: Part 1 to September 10th: Part 1 (97①—910①, "Kugatsu Nanoka (Ichi) - Kugatsu Tōka (Ichi)") is the 124th chapter of the Hunter × Hunter manga, written and illustrated by Yoshihiro Togashi. Synopsis. Gon focuses his aura around his fist, but maintains it only for a few seconds before quickly tiring out. He details the application of the principles of Nen in the technique, and after saying that he is only practicing with his normal aura, he starts to wonder how much power he can get once he starts using Ren. But he remembers Wing's advice to stay patient and decides to master the Ten-Gyo-Zetsu sequence first. Continuing his electricity training in the other room, Killua hears Gon finally making progress. Meanwhile, Leorio is reading a newspaper and learns that Battera has won another copy of Greed Island in the auction and has spent a total of over 200 billion. He also reads some rumors about the reason behind Battera's obsession with the game. Kurapika calls out to Leorio, and Leorio asks if Kurapika is sure that he does not want to tell Gon and Killua that he's leaving. Kurapika says that every minute of their training counts, and he then bids Leorio farewell. Leorio approaches Melody and tells her to watch over Kurapika since he seems to trust her. Melody says that Leorio is very uplifting, and among the people she met in the city, he has the nicest heartbeat. She also tells Leorio that he is fit to become a teacher or a doctor and recommends a change of career. Leorio then says that he will think about it, and decides that he should continue studying. Gon and Killua are shown continuing their training, Leorio studying, and Zepile participating at a local auction. Battera also keeps up his wins by acquiring another Greed Island cartridge at the auction. Milluki is annoyed with this, as he figures that Battera knows his budget limit. Leorio goes back to where Gon and Killua are and tells them about Kurapika's departure. Zepile walks in and tells Gon that he made their 80 million into 100 million as promised to get back Gon's Hunter License. Gon praises Zepile, and Zepile says that it isn't hard with 80 million as seed money. He adds that he did the best he could in five days, as Gon entrusted his entire fortune to him. Leorio and Gon express their gratitude, and Zepile says that there's no need because he kept 50% of the profits, as stated in their contract. Gon calculates that Zepile earned 40 million in five days. Zepile says that he is a pro in this line of work and they can contact him anytime if they need him. After they bid their farewells, Zepile admits to himself that he was just showing off. In truth, he only made 15 million, so he needed to make an illegal 5 million loan with his organs as collateral. He regrets promising an earlier date than Gon had asked, but says that he couldn't ask for an extension after seeming so confident. He decides not to make counterfeits anymore and just use seed money to deal in antiques, thinking that he should have borrowed another million. He admires the Hunter License because a pawnshop chain immediately offered 100 million in cash for it, and thinks that the license can sell for 100 times as much. Then he finally decides to become a Pro Hunter to sell his license, confident that he can live off the interest for life. As he runs off, he says to himself that he should come up with a strategy soon for the Hunter Exam. While Gon and Killua are still training, Battera has managed to win all seven copies of Greed Island, and a rumor spreads that he has spent almost half of his fortune. A reporter announces that the tryouts will take place that same day at the Southernpiece Auction venue. Elsewhere, Milluki finishes eating and decides to go back home.

Chapter 125 September 10th: Part 2 (910②, "Kugatsu Tōka (Ni)") is the 125th chapter of the Hunter × Hunter manga, written and illustrated by Yoshihiro Togashi. Synopsis. At Battera's tryouts, an announcer tells the applicants that players will be chosen for six cartridges, adding that they all have paid the 12 million and reminding them that they need to know Nen to play the game. He introduces Tsezguerra as the judge, who tells them that they will come up one at a time and show him their Ren behind shutters and a curtain. After he tells them that he will end the tryouts once they reach a maximum of 32 people, the curtain closes and many of the applicants rush to form a line. Killua stays seated and analyzes the situation in extreme detail, noting that 100 are waiting in line, around 50 are clustering around the line, and about 20 are staying in their seats. He sees ten applicants go behind the curtain and worries that he and Gon should maybe join the line. One of the applicants, however, begins talking with the two boys and tells them that the ones waiting around the line won't make it. Killua eventually realizes that it's not "first-come, first-served," and the man says that while Battera has 32 slots available, he will inevitably leave open slots in case more talented applicants show up. He guesses that only around 20 people will be chosen for now, and the ones with any chance either lined up first or remained in their seats. Gon had guessed as much and expected that they would allow everyone to be interviewed, and the man commends Gon's logic, introducing himself as Puhat before going up to the stage. Killua realizes that the man is right, telling himself that he needs to take chances in order to advance. Gon wishes him good luck, and Killua goes behind the curtain and shutters, remembering his father's words about not overreaching his limits and staying patient until he knows for sure that he can make the kill. As Tsezguerra asks him to show his Ren, Killua tells himself that he's not an assassin anymore, but a (self-proclaimed) Hunter. He asks if he can show his Hatsu instead, and Tsezguerra says of course, explaining that "show me your Ren" is a code among Hunters to display the results of one's training and what they're capable of. All of a sudden, lightning arcs between Killua's hands, and he directs it toward the floor. Tsezguerra doesn't need to see anymore and quickly passes him, in disbelief that he learned it in only four days. He confronts Killua about it, saying that he would have needed to be exposed to electric shocks for years to endure it, and Killua casually explains that because of family circumstances, he has been since he was a baby.

Chapter 126 September 10th: Part 3 (910③, "Kugatsu Tōka (San)") is the 126th chapter of the Hunter × Hunter manga, written and illustrated by Yoshihiro Togashi. Synopsis. Having passed the selection test, Killua walks to where the seven applicants who have passed before him are waiting. As he takes a seat, a loud noise is heard that gets everyone's attention, and moments later Gon enters the room and meets up with Killua. Gon tells him that his huge sound was due to punching a wall. Back in the testing area, a large part of the wall is cracked, and Tsezguerra realizes Gon's terrifying potential. While Gon teases Killua and keeps his special attack a secret, Tsezguerra appears and congratulates the 21 applicants who passed the selection test. After telling them that Battera will the pay 50 billion to the person who can clear the game, he gives them the contract with all the details and says that they will leave Yorknew at 5 p.m. Gon and Killua celebrate with Leorio as Gon asks him to read the contents of the contract. Leorio highlights the main points: 1) Battera can't be sued if they are hurt or killed; 2) any items obtained from the game will belong to Battera; 3) the person who clears the game gets a 50 billion reward. After the two sign their contracts, Leorio says that he should get going, and Gon wishes him luck on his exams, saying that he will be a doctor the next time they meet (with Leorio wondering if Gon thinks they won't see each other for four years). As Leorio rides away in a taxi, Killua is curious about the thing that can be brought back from the game, confident that Battera wants it at all costs. All the applicants make their way by train to an old castle, and Tsezguerra leads them to a room full of JoyStation Consoles and monitors. He explains to them how the game works, saying that they will all end up in the same place and likening it to an . As Killua tries his best to explain it to Gon, Tsezguerra gives out memory cards to those who don't have one and tells them to choose the order in which they will enter in order to avoid any arguments inside, since each person will have the system explained to them upon entering. The group decides the order based on rock-paper-scissors, and Gon ends up the winner. After Tsezguerra assures him that he will end up in the same place as the others, Gon decides to use the memory card and ring that Ging gave him. Before entering, he thinks about Ging and the game he created, and even though he isn't sure what lies ahead, he trusts his father and knows this was his message. After Killua tells Gon to wait for him at the starting point, an aura surrounds Gon and he quickly disappears and enters the game. Tsezguerra says that once "now playing" is shown on the screen, the next player can enter. Inside the game, Gon is seen standing on a design of circles on the floor and looking toward a set of double doors.

Chapter 127 September 10th: Part 4 (910④, "Kugatsu Tōka (Yon)") is the 127th chapter of the Hunter × Hunter manga, written and illustrated by Yoshihiro Togashi. Synopsis. Gon enters Greed Island's Starting Point and walks down a hallway, eventually meeting a woman sitting in a floating mechanism and wearing headgear. She immediately welcomes him to Greed Island and asks if he is Gon, which he confirms. Before they start, the woman tells Gon that Ging has left a voice message for him. Ging congratulates Gon and tells him that he is in a game, he created with his friends, adding that Gon shouldn't expect any clues to find his location and that he just wanted to show off the game they made together. Ging also tells him that he won't be able to leave the game until he finds a special item, and Gon wonders if the only thing Ging wanted to do was show off the game. After Gon hears his father's message, the woman starts to explain the rules, telling him that a player who has the special ring can use two spells: "Book" and "Gain." She tells him to hold out his hand with the ring and to say "Book," which causes a floating book to appear in front of Gon. She explains that he can convert every item he finds into a card and that the cards are stored in the book, adding that he will need to complete it to clear the game. She then asks Gon to open his book to the first page, and he sees empty slots with numbers on each of them. The woman explains that each slot will only accept that specific card. As Gon keeps turning the pages and finds slots with no numbers, she explains that those are called "free slots" and can hold cards of any number, adding that there are 100 specific slots (000 to 099) and 45 free slots. She concludes this part of her explanation by saying that to clear the game, Gon will need to collect all 100 specified slot cards. The woman clarifies that he will be collecting 100 items and turning them into cards, explaining that if he finds a sword and touches it, it will immediately turn into a card. She adds that if he puts the card in his book, he won't be able to use it as a weapon unless he uses the spell "Gain." However, she explains that once a card has been "gained," it can never be turned into a card again, which would force a player to find the same sword again if he wanted the card. With Gon just barely following along, she explains that there are two other times when an item cannot be turned into a card. The first is when the item has reached its conversion limit, which can range from as few as three to more than 100. She gives an example of an item with a limit of three cards, explaining that if three players each have one in their binder, a fourth player cannot convert it into an item when he finds it. The second is that cards must be kept in the book and that if a card is left out for 60 seconds, it reverts into the item and can never be converted into a card again. As Gon begins to reach his memorization limit, she stresses that if a player dies, their book and ring will be destroyed, and all the cards inside will disappear. She says that these are only the basic rules and that he will have to discover more details by playing the game, finally wishing him good luck and showing him the stairs that lead down below. Gon walks down the stairs and finds himself looking out across a huge, grassy plain. He then senses that something is watching him, but doesn't see any sign of people. Another player enters the game and walks past Gon, and two other players meet up and also sense that they're being watched, with one realizing that it must be a human and adding that they must not be any good since they're being so obvious. As the two make their way across the plain, Gon is filled with excitement as he begins to play the game his father made.

Chapter 128 September 10th: Part 5 (910⑤, "Kugatsu Tōka (Go)") is the 128th chapter of the Hunter × Hunter manga, written and illustrated by Yoshihiro Togashi. Synopsis. Killua meets up with Gon and thanks him for waiting, also sensing that they're being watched. Gon says that everyone else went in one of two directions, and Killua correctly guesses both of them, saying that that's where he feels the eyes from. The two decide by rock-paper-scissors which way to go, and making their way across the plain, Gon tells Killua that Ging only left behind a message telling him to enjoy the game. The two discuss the information about the game they got from the woman at the Starting Point, with Killua still confused as to how they even get items. Gon says that they need to gather information, and so they need to find a town. Back in Battera's Castle, after the last player enters the game, Battera asks Tsezguerra about the current batch, and Tsezguerra says that he will need to stay focused. He checks his watch and says that he should return to the game since he will lose his memory card data if he doesn't get back within ten days. Elsewhere, at the Phantom Troupe's hideout, Shalnark looks up information about the game and asks Shizuku and Kortopi if they want to come with him. He tells Shizuku that it's not to clear the game, and that the two of them may be safer there for the upcoming week. In the end, Shizuku and Kortopi agree to accompany him. Back in the game, as Gon hears something in the distance, the two suddenly spot something in the sky rocketing toward them. With his book open once he lands, another player confronts them and easily recognizes that the two kids are new since they didn't open their books as well. He uses "Peek" to learn both their names and that Killua has no cards in his free slots. After deciding that using "Cling" on them would be a waste, he gleefully activates "Trace" on Killua, who tries his best to dodge the spell, but it quickly strikes him. The player is happy with his decision at first, saying to himself that gathering information on other players is crucial to the game, but Killua's bloodlust soon frightens him so much that he uses "Return" to flee, rocketing toward Masadora.

Chapter 129 Antokiba, Town of Prizes (アントキバ, "Kenshō Toshi Antokiba") is the 129th chapter of the Hunter × Hunter manga, written and illustrated by Yoshihiro Togashi. Synopsis. A news anchor reports on the last day of the auction in Yorknew City, stating that multiple terrorist attacks on the third day decreased attendance to 60% of the average year. Even though the mayor announced that the terrorists are dead and everyone is now safe, some of the general public still refrained from attending the auction. As Gon spots a town in the distance, he asks Killua if he feels any different after the attack and if he thinks it involved Nen. Killua says that he's fine and that it must have been a game ability, describing it as magic that can be cast inside the game and confident that they will be able to use it as well. The two arrive in Antokiba and wander around the town, first coming across a reward board and then finding the monthly contest list. They learn that a rock-paper-scissors tournament will be held for September, also confirming that the date in the game is the same as the real world (the 11th). A tournament is held every month on the 15th, and the two decide to enter in order to win a prize called the Sword of Truth. While waiting for the tournament to start in four days, they plan to enter other contests and gather information at the same time, finding a restaurant where they can win a card by finishing a meal in half an hour. Killua tries to gather information from the chef, but he eventually realizes that he's just an and that they'll need to ask around more. They finish their meals within the 30 minutes, and the chef returns with two "Galgaida" cards, explaining that the number on the left is the item's card number while the letter on the right is the difficulty rating (ranging from H to SS) and adding that the number after the difficulty rating is the card's conversion limit. The two realize that the card isn't very good, but as Killua thanks him for the meal and prepares to leave, the chef says that while the meal was free, they need to pay for the three sodas they had. Killua attempts to pay with paper money, but the chef says that they only accept money in the form of cards, holding out a 10,000 card. The two look at each other nervously as the chef begins to call the police, but they end up washing dishes to pay off the amount. They worry about filling up their 45 free slots too quickly, wondering how they even earn money in the game, and the chef replies that they can earn it by defeating monsters. After they finish washing dishes, the two go outside and suddenly hear screaming around the corner. They see a large crowd gathered together and find a man lying dead on the ground, with blood covering his midsection. The two recognize him as one of the players hired by Battera and had seen him earlier at the monthly contest list, learning from one of the onlookers that he suddenly exploded from the inside. As Gon is left stunned and says that it doesn't seem at all like a game, the corpse vanishes and returns to the real world, with Gon now worrying about the spell cast on Killua. A man overhears their conversation and assures them that the player wasn't killed by a spell, but by the Nen of another player. Killua asks why players would be killing each other, and the man says that it's because of the card conversion limit system, where only a certain amount of copies of a card can exist at the same time, with the rarest cards having the fewest. He explains that the more players there are, the less likely it is for a player to find cards. After he tells them that his group is the opposite, fighting with numbers and never killing, he asks Gon and Killua if they want to join, promising that his group has a perfect strategy to clear the game.

Chapter 13 A Game at Midnight: Part 1 (のゲーム①, "Mayonaka no Gēmu (Ichi)") is the 13th chapter of the Hunter × Hunter manga, written and illustrated by Yoshihiro Togashi. Synopsis. Aboard the airship at night, Netero introduces himself to the 42 remaining examinees, explaining that he is the chairman of the selection committee for the year's Hunter Exam and that he will happily accompany them during the trip. Also present, the small official tells them that they will reach their destination at 8 a.m. the next day and that they can relax until then. While Gon and Killua eagerly run off to explore the airship, Leorio and Kurapika are both ready to rest after the long, exhausting day. Kurapika then wonders how many phases are left, and as Leorio mentions that they still don't know, Tonpa arrives to say that it changes every year depending on the examiners and tests involved, adding that it has averaged five or six phases during his attempts. Leorio realizes that the exam isn't even halfway done, and Kurapika adds that they really need to get rest. However, Tonpa warns them that the airship may be the site of the Third Phase and that it could possibly start at any moment, telling them not to let their guard down if they want to pass. With Leorio and Kurapika left giving each other a look, Tonpa walks away chuckling to himself and hopes that they become too nervous to sleep. As the examinees are seen eating food and resting, the three examiners are eating at the same table and wonder how many examinees will pass. Buhara mentions that it depends on what the subsequent phases are, and Menchi adds that she noted a few examinees with powerful auras. She then asks Satotz what he thinks, and he replies that he is impressed by the current rookies. Menchi quickly agrees with his assessment and praises Hanzo in particular, adding that he also knew sushi. Satotz says that his favorite so far is Killua, but Menchi calls him obnoxious and guesses that his blood type is B. When asked what he thinks, Buhara says that he believes Hisoka has the best chance, even though he isn't a rookie. He also points out the bloodlust shown by Hisoka when Todo was upset during the Second Phase. Menchi replies that she noticed it as well and that he could barely contain it, adding that he seems to be putting it out there as a subtle threat to the examiners. She continues by describing it as a constant undercurrent of provocation and says that it's one of the reasons why she was on edge. Satotz agrees with Menchi's assessment and says that they definitely need to keep an eye on Hisoka since his talent is in the same league as their own. Satotz continues his analysis and says that while Hunters all seek the hunt that fulfills their desires, Hisoka is an anomaly that appears occasionally, explaining that the exam is only one way he seeks satisfaction and that he would do the opposite of what they would deem wise. In a corner of the airship, Hisoka is seen to have built a tower of playing cards before deliberately knocking it down. He seems to feel pleasure from the moment and chuckles out loud, causing the nearby examinees to stay clear of him. Looking out a window on the airship, Killua energetically points to the bright city below and describes it as a web of jewels. Gon asks about Killua's parents, but before he can finish the question, Killua guesses that he plans to ask if they're alive, replying that he's pretty sure they are. Gon then asks what they do for a living, and Killua nonchalantly replies with mass murder. Instead of appearing surprised, Gon simply asks if both his parents are mass murderers, causing Killua to laugh and pretend that it was all a joke. However, Gon is sure that he was telling the truth, and Killua is again left surprised by Gon's intuition, noting that his "cute kid" act is about making people wonder whether he's being serious or not. Killua then reveals that every member of his family is an assassin and that while his parents have focused on his extraordinary potential, he doesn't think he should have to live up to their expectations. He explains that they got upset when he told them that he would decide his own future, causing his mother to cry and tell him that he was throwing his life away. He then reveals that he slashed his mother in the face and stabbed his older brother in the side before running away from home, joyously adding that he plans to hunt them all down and collect the bounties after he gets a Hunter License. Netero spots the two boys talking and widens his eyes, causing both to turn around and leaving them confused when they find no one there. However, Netero suddenly appears behind them and asks what's going on. Gon points in the other direction and asks Netero if he saw anyone down the hallway, but Killua realizes Netero's trick and calls him fast. Netero replies that he was just off on a stroll, but Killua becomes annoyed at his game and wonders if he's trying to kill time before the final phase. Netero clarifies that he's just passing the time and asks the two youngest rookies what they think of the exam so far. Gon says that it's fun because it has action and no written test, but Killua calls it disappointing and says that he hoped it would be more challenging, asking if there are any on the way. Netero gives a nonanswer, and Killua realizes that it most likely means no, telling Gon that it's time for them to leave. However, Netero quickly gets their attention and asks if they want to play a game, revealing that he will issue both of them licenses if they are able to beat him two against one. In a new room, Netero has taken off his jacket and is seen wearing a black tank top as he holds a ball in his hand. He explains to Gon and Killua that they simply need to take the ball away from him before the airship arrives at its destination, adding that they can use any tactics they want and he will only be defensive. Killua offers to try first and suddenly creates multiple images of himself that walk around Netero, leaving both him and Gon surprised. Impressed that Killua knows it at such a young age, Netero recognizes it as "Rhythm Echo", which is stated to be an assassination art used to entrance an enemy with afterimages. With Gon still left confused by the technique, the real Killua suddenly leaps forward from the group and tries to grab the ball multiple times, but Netero expertly dodges his attempts as he balances the ball on various parts of his body. After being left in disbelief by how quick Netero is and noting that he can't even touch his body, Killua decides to perform a leg strike to undercut him, swinging his leg to strike the shin on Netero's pivot leg. Although Killua expects it to be successful, Netero is left unfazed while Killua suddenly feels the pain in his own leg, with Netero telling himself that it would have shattered a normal leg. Killua tells Gon that it felt like hitting an iron post, and the two then swap places. Gon quickly stretches and then darts toward Netero, who is impressed by Gon's speed but notes that he is charging forward too foolishly. Gon suddenly leaps up into the air right in front of Netero, leaving him surprised, but jumps too high and hits his head on the ceiling. Killua tells him that he needs to gauge the distance better and points out that he had Netero off guard, with Netero nervously confirming the observation to himself. The Chairman then adds that while Gon may seem mature, he has a sound mind and may be a viable playmate. Elsewhere on the airship, Tonpa finds Leorio and Kurapika sleeping soundly beside each other, disappointed that they ignored his fake warning.

Chapter 130 The Reason for the Recruitment (の, "Kanyū no Wake") is the 130th chapter of the Hunter × Hunter manga, written and illustrated by Yoshihiro Togashi. Synopsis. Nickes wants to introduce Gon and Killua to his group, but Killua thinks the offer sounds too good and tells Gon they should reject it. Before the two can leave, Nickes brings up the fact that Killua was affected by a spell from another player. Killua asks if he has been watching them, and Nickes says that his job is surveillance and recruitment. He says that he will tell them why people keep watch on the Starting Point as well as more about the spell used to attack Killua if they at least agree to hear their pitch. He stresses the difficulty and brutality of the game and says that they would find the information worthwhile since they're new players. Killua asks why he thinks that they're new, saying that although they came from the Starting Point, they could have just been coming back after leaving. Nickes offers them a demonstration by quickly summoning his book, which causes Gon and Killua to jump back. Nickes explains that experienced players immediately take out their own books once someone else does, stressing that only spells can defend against other spells. He adds that even if they don't have any cards, they should take out their books since bluffing is an important strategy. He once again asks them to hear him out, and Gon convinces Killua that it's worth doing. Nickes takes the two to the town's plaza and meets up with the rest of his group, who have invited three other new players. Nickes tells the others that a player they arrived with was just killed, saying that the two boys saw him and that it was the work of the Bomber. One member with glasses from Nickes' group explains that of the 40 spell cards in the game, none of them do any harm or kill. He explains that the spells cast on them were either "Trace" or "Cling", allowing another player to know their current location and what cards they have in their book. He explains that some players keep an eye on the Starting Point and cast these spells on new players, waiting until they get a valuable card and then coming to take it from them. He continues by saying that there are at least four players going around hunting and killing other players, and the one known as the Bomber (who they believe to be an Emitter or Manipulator) is responsible for the latest one. Lastly, he says that the game came out more than 10 years ago, and the situation is getting worse. Another member from Nickes' group asks the new players for the three main categories to getting item cards. Gon says to find them yourself, another player says to trade them with others, and Killua says to take them from others. The member continues by saying that more and more players have been using the third way because of acquisition difficulty and the card conversion limit, attacking other players until they take out their books and killing those who refuse. He says that they won't be able to get their cards if a player dies, but more items will be able to be converted. After Killua uses an example to explain it Gon, Nickes speaks up and promises to put an end to the killings by using strategy, asking for their help. Puhat asks which of the ways to get cards they use, and Nickes says the third one, but stresses that they don't use violence when taking cards. He explains that there are offensive and defensive spells, and their plan involves monopolizing these cards and using the conversion limit to their advantage. He says that they need 1900 spell cards for a monopoly, needing at least 45 people to store them in their free slots while others monitor, recruit, and collect cards. He adds that they currently have 53 people (70 would be ideal) and around 800 spell cards. The member with glasses says that they currently have 67 unique specified slot cards (70% of total cards if they combine all of them). The other member says that they started five years ago and struggled at first, but their members and cards have doubled recently, adding that they plan to go on the offensive once they reach 1300 cards. Another member says that this is the last time they will recruit for more members since they should be able to collect all the cards in a month once they have enough to go on the offensive. After their extensive appeal, Nickes asks the new players whether they will join.

Chapter 131 The Answer (, "Kaitō") is the 131st chapter of the Hunter × Hunter manga, written and illustrated by Yoshihiro Togashi. Synopsis. Nickes and his group continue to plead with the new players to join them, stressing that it's the only way to stop the killings. After each of the four members who are present offers the benefits of joining, Puhat brings up the reward for clearing the game and asks how splitting it would work. One of the members says that they were also hired by Battera, and Nickes jumps in and says that each of them will get around 200 million, with 20 of the 50 billion being split among the ten founders of the group and the rest being handed out according to how long someone has been a member and what their job was. He says that soon the recruiters will switch to collecting cards, allowing them to collect the 500 spell cards they need and to clear the game in three months. The member with glasses promises to undo any spells that were cast on them, saying that the only other way to undo them is to leave the game, which requires certain conditions to achieve. Puhat agrees to join, saying that he knew it would take years to clear the game alone or in teams of two or three. He's disappointed that the 50 billion payoff will have to be split, but he says that it will be worth it to be able to clear the game in only three months. Another new player asks whether he would get a bigger share if he found a valuable item and after Nickes says that they are offering 500 million for SS-rank cards, he agrees to join. When Nickes turns to Gon and Killua, Gon first apologizes to Killua and then declines Nickes' offer, saying that he wants to play on his own. Killua follows his lead and declines as well, with the two leaving the town's plaza. As Killua walks behind Gon and asks him to talk to him, Gon lets out a sigh and says that he couldn't sit there anymore, apologizing again since Killua will be stuck with that spell. Killua doesn't worry about it, but wonders why Gon seemed mad when he rejected Nickes' offer. Gon says that he didn't like how they were describing Ging's game as one of slaughter, adding that he's decided to just enjoy the game as Ging told him. He says the scariest thing about the game is how quickly other players are willing to hurt others and take their cards. Killua replies that as long as killing isn't involved, it's okay to take cards from others as long as the confrontation is upfront (which Gon is fine with). Killua understands that people casting spells and forming alliances are only natural parts of the game, but he agrees with Gon and says they should enjoy it alone. Gon quickly thanks him and adds that he's not only glad to be here with him, but glad to have met him. Killua shrugs off Gon's compliment and says to himself that he's the one who's glad to have him as a friend. Sitting on a balcony behind them, the young girl who was also present during Nickes' appeal, listens in on their conversation and understands why the two didn't join the group. She says that little boys are innocent and gleefully adds that ruining their friendships will be fun. Outside Antokiba, Nickes' group tells the new recruits that one of their members will be there in two minutes, adding that they (the new recruits) will need to exit the game temporarily and then wait by the Starting Point. Nickes asks them to hand over any cards in their free slots since those cards will be lost forever if they leave the game, clarifying that cards in the specified slots get saved automatically, but will also be destroyed if one doesn't return to the game within 10 days. He tells the two that if they don't return in half an hour, he will assume that they have quit. The member arrives and says that they should get started since they don't know who could be watching. He pulls out a "Leave" card, which he says is pretty rare. Puhat asks him how he arrived like that, and the member says that it's a card called "Magnetic Force," which sends a player to another player's location. He adds that there's also a card called "Return," which sends a player to a town they've been before, but says that it only goes to the town's entrance, which is risky to use because of ambushes. After he uses "Leave" on the two players, he tells the others that Contarch recruited eight players (bringing their group's total to 63). They bring up the fact that some members may be unhappy that their share will decrease, and Nickes says that they may need to decrease the share for the ten founders. However, the member with glasses is quick to disagree, saying that they would only make more demands. A member gets the two to stop fighting before their conversation is overheard. Back in Antokiba, Gon and Killua practice rock-paper-scissors for the upcoming tournament, with the latter becoming more and more frustrated at losing. Gon tells Killua that there's a trick to it that a fisherman who came to Whale Island taught him. A flashback to the fisherman, who tells Gon that the trick is to "prime" by saying, "Show me rock." He says that at the moment his opponent begins swinging his fist down, his hand will already start to take shape, with the hand opening ever so slightly if it's not rock. He adds that if it's closed or if he can see the hand, he should counter with a stronger move, telling him to use scissors otherwise and he will never lose. He continues by saying that by starting with the "show me rock" line, it will force his opponent to present his fist, making it easier to see and allowing one to win 90% of the time. Killua becomes angry at Gon for cheating during all their bouts, but Gon doesn't want the others to overhear. He tells Killua that it seems simple, but takes a lot of talent and practice, adding that Leorio couldn't do it. Killua still calls it cheating, but isn't against it in order to win the Sword of Truth.

Chapter 132 The Forty Spells (40の, "Yonjū Shu no Superu") is the 132nd chapter of the Hunter × Hunter manga, written and illustrated by Yoshihiro Togashi. Synopsis. The ten new recruits wait around the Starting Point, and Jispa arrives to take them to the group's hideout, using "Accompany" to travel to Kosofftro. Wearing a large-brimmed hat and carrying a sword, the man welcomes the new members and tells them to remember his name since they'll need it to get to the base with a spell. Abengane realizes how cautious the group is being, transporting them to a player and not directly to their base in order to keep it secret. The new members are told that they will have the spell system explained to them and then travel to Masadora to buy spell cards. As they make their way further into the forest, Jispa tells them that the cards come in packs of three, each costing 10,000. He adds that if one collects all 40 spell cards, they can be traded in for a rank-SS specified slot card called "Angel's Breath," a card so rare that no one owns it. Abengane asks him how he knows that, and Jispa says that "List" can be used to find out a card's current conversion number and the number of people who have it. He then tells them that their group has managed to collect all 40 spell cards, saying that they want to exchange them for "Angel's Breath" as soon as possible. However, he adds that they need a card called "Fortress" first, telling the new members that the card is their top priority. The group eventually reaches the hideout inside a cave, with one member explaining that there are close and long-range spells. The former has a radius of 20 meters, while the latter works anywhere on the island. The member stresses being able to estimate the distance for close-range spells, especially when encountering an opponent. He tells them that as long as they have their binder open when attacked, and they have a defensive spell, there will be a 15-second delay for the attack spell while they decide whether they want to use their own spell or not. Another member hands out sheets of paper with all 40 spells on them, telling the new recruits to memorize them in one hour since the information is vital to their plan. Reading through the list, Puhat notes that while there are more defensive spell cards than attack spell cards, the most valuable of the former is still vulnerable against an attack. A member reminds them of the one-hour time frame and says that those who don't memorize them will be assigned to running errands for the group. He also stresses as Jispa said earlier, that the card they need most at the moment is "Fortress," which protects a page of nine specified slot cards from spells. Abengane and Puhat are the first to finish memorizing the list, and the member asks them to name the defensive spells they monopolize as well as the total conversion limits of those cards. While Abengane whispers the answers to him and passes, Puhat confidently asks for a tougher question, and the member asks him to name all the spell cards that can be destroyed by "Compromise," as well as all the spell cards that can be gained in exchange. Puhat whispers the answer to him, but the member says that "Holy Water" cannot be destroyed, telling him to learn them over again. Meanwhile, back in Antokiba, Gon and Killua face each other in the finals of the rock-paper-scissors tournament, and Killua clinches the win by using rock with his left hand. The judge presents him with the Sword of Truth, which immediately transforms into the card once Killua touches it. He sees that it's a specified slot card, and the two rejoice that it's their first one.

Chapter 133 How to Defend Yourself Without Spells (の, "Superu Igai no Gādo Hō") is the 133rd chapter of the Hunter × Hunter manga, written and illustrated by Yoshihiro Togashi. Synopsis. After winning the "Sword of Truth" from the tournament, Gon and Killua start to think about how to protect the card since they don't have any spell cards. They also realize that other players saw them win the card, with Killua saying that several are already tailing them. Gon knows they can't let their guard down since they're still defenseless against spells. Killua, however, says that he may be able to guess their spells and defend against them even without any of their own. He takes the advice that he learned from Nickes' group, and the two work together to devise a strategy. A certain player who has been following them seems hesitant to steal a card from kids, but thinks about his wife and needing to provide for her. He gets distracted remembering how many years he has spent inside the game, but eventually turns his focus back to the card and says that it would be worth at least 10 million in game, allowing him to not have to worry about money in game ever again. He has a "Thief" card in his possession and knows that he has to seize the opportunity before someone else does. The man suddenly comes out from hiding and orders the two to hand over the "Sword of Truth" card, but Killua just says no and continues walking away. As the man summons his book and the two summon theirs, he says that they are bluffing and only have the one specified slot card, quickly using his "Thief" card and telling it to attack Killua and take his "Sword of Truth." However, the "Thief" card simply vanishes, and the man learns that Killua had no cards in his specified slots, meaning that he had moved it to his free slots. Another player seizes his chance and uses a "Pickpocket" card to try to take a card from Killua's free slots. However, the "Pickpocket card" vanishes, and the man is in disbelief that Killua didn't have any cards in his free slots either. Killua tells him that just because he won the card doesn't mean he put it in his own book, and Gon gives a big grin. The man quickly uses another "Pickpocket," but as he looks at the card he received, he can't believe it's just a "Rock" card, in dismay that two new players would take advantage of strategies like shuffle guard and full-slot guard. The player tells himself that he has one more "Pickpocket," but he knows that Gon's free slots are most likely filled with more junk, saying that it may not be worth taking the chance. As he continues to waver, a third player confidently approaches and says that he used "Clairvoyance" to check Killua's book and "Peek" to confirm that the card is in Gon's free slots. He pulls out a "Mug" card, but before he can finish the utterance, Gon dashes toward him and swipes the card right out of his hand, leaving the man stunned. However, Gon returns the card and says that he will take it for good next time. Killua warns him that Gon is a professional Hunter, adding that he has become too reliant on spell cards. As the two leave, the man says that their tactics won't last forever and that they will inevitably run into stronger players. As Gon and Killua agree that the third player was right and that they need to find defensive spell cards, a group of players suddenly ambushes them and says that they can't run away. They play rock-paper-scissors among themselves to decide the order to cast spells, and one of the players says that only idiots enter the contests. After the card is taken from them, Gon sulks at the loss, but Killua tells him to forget it and be glad that the players didn't use violence. The two agree that it's time to head to Masadora for spell cards.

Chapter 134 The Island's Secret (の, "Gēmu no Himitsu") is the 134th chapter of the Hunter × Hunter manga, written and illustrated by Yoshihiro Togashi. Synopsis. At a shop in Antokiba, Gon and Killua sell four "Gargaida" cards and earn 120,000. Gon suggests buying food and water so they can head to Masadora as soon as possible, but Killua tells him that they still need a map. The two return to the shop and decide whether they should buy the detailed or empty map. Gon opts for the latter since it will be more fun to find locations on their own. They pay 30,000 to the shopkeeper for information on Masadora, and he gives them specific directions, but warns them about bandits and monsters. This excites the two as they make their way toward the city. But right as they begin their journey, the young girl who was spying on them earlier after listening to Nickes' offer approaches and asks if she can join them. After Killua rejects her and says that she would just slow them down, the girl does her best to hold back her anger while still begging them to let her tag along. Having entered the game, Shalnark, Shizuku, and Kortopi have made their way south to Rubicuta. Shalnark has been gathering information and observed that the 100 townspeople they interacted with were all . He summons his book and takes out a "Rock" card, also holding out one that Kortopi copied. He utters "Gain" and while the real card changes into a rock, Kortopi's copy doesn't. He surmises that it's either beyond the game's programming or the game has an anti-cheating system to prevent such things. He reminds them that Shizuku's Blinky was able to vacuum up things brought from outside the game, or things like the rock, but not special items (even if they were inanimate). He guesses that it's also to prevent people from using Nen abilities to collect cards and items too easily. Shizuku wonders what his point is, and Shalnark says that there could be another possibility, hypothesizing that the game doesn't involve virtual reality, but is happening somewhere in the real world. Shalnark tells them that all of it can be proven or explained with Nen, surmising that the NPCs are dolls being manipulated or conjured by the game master. He guesses that key items are also conjured, reminding them that Kortopi can't duplicate other abilities and Blinky can't vacuum up things made with Nen. He says that he initially became suspicious when Feitan and Phinks' bodies disappeared completely, adding that if the game were really taking place in virtual reality, only their souls would have entered the game and their bodies would have stayed behind. He continues by saying that the software doesn't involve playing the game, but is simply used to teleport the players to the island. He looks at their empty map and thinks that the island is as big as the Kotoritana Republic, adding that there is probably more than one game master. Shizuku again wonders what his point is, and Shalnark reminds her of what they learned the reward was for clearing the game. Kortopi jumps in and says that they will be allowed to take back three specified slot cards and use them in real life. Shalnark explains that the items will work outside the island and that they don't need to actually clear the game if it's taking place somewhere in the real world. He pulls out a "Toraemon" card and says that they may be able to steal everything. Shizuku thinks that it may be worth trying, and Shalnark says that they should find out which items are the most valuable, telling them that they need to get hold of an "Eye of God" or "Analysis" card, and then find Phinks and Feitan. Farther north, Phinks and Feitan take a cheap map and several spell cards from a player they killed (the one who first confronted Gon and Killua). They agree to split up and then meet back in Masadora after one week. Phinks says that it's a contest to see how many players they can kill, but Feitan reminds him to take their cards first.

Chapter 135 To Masadora! Part 1 (いざマサドラへ！①, "Iza Masadora e! (Ichi)") is the 135th chapter of the Hunter × Hunter manga, written and illustrated by Yoshihiro Togashi. Synopsis. As Gon and Killua make their way toward Masadora, they remember the shopkeeper's words about the bandits along the route. Gon asks Killua what they should do about her, and the young girl from before is seen trailing behind them. Killua tells him to ignore her and that they can lose her when encountering the bandits. But even with the two running at a quick pace, the girl could keep up with them, saying to herself that their stamina isn't bad for kids. Several bandits suddenly confront the three of them, leaping toward them as if to attack but quickly falling to their knees and begging for help. The men lead the three back to their village and explain that they're being afflicted with a disease endemic to the island. They say that it starts with a low fever that will eventually become fatal if not treated in a month. However, they add that each dose of the necessary medicine only lasts for a week, allowing the fever to return, and since the pills are expensive and they've run out of money, everyone has become ill and no one can work. They plead with him to save a young boy's life who will die in a few days, asking for any money the two can spare. Gon and Killua analyze the situation like the game that it is, hoping to get items or information in return. The girl offers to help, but Killua just tells her to stay quiet (forcing her to conceal her bloodlust again). Gon offers the 80,000 for the man's sick son, who begins to complain about being so cold that he will die during the night. The two offer their overshirts, but get nothing in return for them or the money, which was the last they had. Killua remembers that there are monsters beyond the mountains and that they can convert them into cards to sell. As the two come out of the forest and reach an area filled with large stone pillars, they immediately encounter multiple giant Cyclops, dodging their attacks and trying to land their own. Gon's punch to one of their faces does no damage, and Killua tells him to aim for the eye, climbing his way up one and kicking it in its weak point. The monster turns into its card and Killua quickly collects it, with him and Gon dispatching so many that some even revert back to unconscious monsters. Killua says that every monster will have a pattern and weakness, telling Gon that they just need to stay calm and find the answers during combat. Gon assures him that Ging wouldn't have made a game that was unreasonable. As the two continue confidently toward Masadora, they soon encounter an enormous lizard that begins chasing after them.

Chapter 136 To Masadora! Part 2 (いざマサドラへ！②, "Iza Masadora e! (Ni)") is the 136th chapter of the Hunter × Hunter manga, written and illustrated by Yoshihiro Togashi. Synopsis. Gon and Killua hide behind the stone pillars until the giant lizard eventually leaves. Killua wonders how they're supposed to fight it, guessing it's much higher ranked than the Cyclops. Their strategy was to attack when they got an opening and then to run away when things got dangerous, but they could not find its weakness. The young girl continues to observe the two and, as she holds the card in her hand, says that the monster is only one rank higher than the Cyclops. She adds that they would have noticed the lizard protecting its weak point if they had paid closer attention, again commenting that the two are still young. As they make their way through the canyon, Gon is struck in the face by a ball-like creature which begins to dart all around them so quickly that it cannot be caught. The girl observes them struggling to catch it and says to herself that they should be aiming for where it's going rather than where it is. The two give up after ten minutes, but then immediately run into a horse-like creature that sends out bubbles. Some of the bubbles pop around them, making a loud sound but not doing any harm. Gon notes that the red ones don't pop, and the young girl observes that the white ones most likely pop when they hit human aura and the red ones on things without aura (or on people in Zetsu). She continues by noting that someone would need to keep track of the two kinds and then switch between Zetsu and Ten if they are unable to dodge them. After the giant lizard returns, Gon and Killua are seen either running away from or being puzzled by various monsters, with the girl becoming increasingly frustrated that the two are wasting their talents. She describes them as rough gemstones that need a little polish to shine, but worries that it will be game over if they encounter a malicious player or monster. As the boys encounter a monster covered in armor and holding a sword and shield, the girl is unable to restrain herself any longer and yells out to them to use Gyo and not take their eyes off it. They use the technique and see a trail of aura exiting the armor, with the girl explaining that the armor is just a puppet unable to be hurt by their attacks. They dodge the monster's initial strike, and while Killua keeps its attention, Gon follows the trail of aura around the corner and finds the Radio Rat. After it changes into its card and the suit of armor falls apart, the young girl approaches them and asks why they didn't use Gyo if they knew how. They both clearly forgot, and she holds up her finger, again yelling for them to use the technique. They see the number "1" formed with aura, and she tells them that whenever she points her finger up (or they see something suspicious), they will use Gyo. She says that it will only improve with constant practice and should be as natural as their eyes shifting focus. Finally, she offers to teach them for free, but says that she won't go easy. As Killua is too busy being angry, the girl raises her finger, and Gon answers with the correct number. She orders Killua to do 200 pushups, and as the two of them get into an argument, another player stealthily observes the three and twirls a pair of scissors in his hand, proclaiming that he will rip them apart with his Scissor Hands.

Chapter 137 To Masadora! Part 3 (いざマサドラへ！③, "Iza Masadora e! (San)") is the 137th chapter of the Hunter × Hunter manga, written and illustrated by Yoshihiro Togashi. Synopsis. Gon and Killua are shocked to learn that the young-looking girl is 57 years old. Killua calls her ancient, and she punches him far back, saying that she learned Nen 40 years ago and telling them to be grateful for the free teaching. Killua still has a problem since they don't even know who she is, and she introduces herself as Biscuit Krueger, a professional Hunter. Killua is still against being taught by her, and Gon adds that they have Wing as their teacher. Biscuit recognizes the name, describing him and saying he was once one of her students. She asks if the two of them are Hunters as well, but Gon replies that only he is, with Biscuit remembering when she was an examiner for the secret test. Killua seems more content now, and Biscuit summons her book and pulls out the "Hyper Puffball" card for the creature that Gon and Killua couldn't catch earlier. She points out that the card's rank is only "D", adding that it's not even a specified slot card. She stresses that there are many other players who can get the card and are better at combat than them. As she asks them what would happen if these players wanted to hurt them, she suddenly senses something, and the player with scissors is shown still stalking them, eager to use his Scissor Hands. Biscuit tells them to sit down close to her and to open their books so it looks like they're chatting. She says that an enemy is behind her and tells them to not try to sense him, since he would see them tensing up. Both had no clue that he was there, and Biscuit says that he let a little bloodlust slip out because they all look like kids, who are very rarely skilled with abilities in combat. She stresses how dangerous he is, and Killua asks her what they should do. Biscuit asks them what they think, now that they know the enemy is intelligent and can adjust. The two agree that they should all stick together, and while Biscuit says that that's the standard answer, she tells them that she will go off by herself, confident that he will come after her alone. She says that she will go south while they go north, telling them to walk for around 500 meters and then to shut off their aura and quickly head back. Killua understands her plan, but Biscuit suddenly slaps him across the face and pretends to get into an argument with him. They go their separate ways, and Killua says that Biscuit is amazing, explaining that even though he was prepared for the faintest indication of danger, he didn't know what she had done until he felt his cheek hurting. After they all walk the 500 meters and quickly head back, they find that the player has cut Biscuit's hair with his scissors. The man proceeds to eat it, explaining that by doing so he can learn minute details about the person even they don't know. He is stunned to find out that not only is the young-looking girl 57 years old, but her body is like forged steel, realizing that she has trained for years to surpass her physical limits. He sets down his belt full of scissors and asks to spar with her. Taking off her gloves, Biscuit is glad to know that he isn't just a cannibal. The man attempts to strike her, but Biscuit easily dodges and grabs his arm, flinging him above herself and striking him hard in the back. As he spews out blood on the ground, Biscuit says that he should consider himself lucky since he would be dead if it were a battle involving Nen.
