After the roll is successful and Genthru confidently says that the strategy will work, they are contacted by Tsezguerra again and agree to take the deal.

Chapter 153 Success (, "Seikō") is the 153rd chapter of the Hunter × Hunter manga, written and illustrated by Yoshihiro Togashi. Synopsis. The Bombers and Tsezguerra's team meet at the appointed place and complete the trade. However, as Tsezguerra begins to walk away, Genthru comments that the trade isn't fair. Tsezguerra's teammates yell that it is fair since they gave him three cards, but Genthru replies it isn't fair for them, and he feels like he is being given charity. In reality, Genthru is merely stalling for time as Bara and Sub, camouflaged behind the other team, come out of hiding and roll Risky Dice, each with a Tax Collector's Gauntlet on their wrist. As Genthru proposes that Tsezguerra chooses one of the two cards he is holding, one being useless and the other being "Angel's Breath," their rolls are successful and Bara and Sub charge toward Tsezguerra's team. Before their opponents can react, they use their gauntlets to cast "Levy" and steal eight cards, with all three then using "Return" to flee to Masadora. Baffled, one of Tsezguerra's teammates wants to go after them immediately, but they check their books first and discover that they are missing valuable cards, two of which they had monopolies on. Tsezguerra sees that they were all *specified slot cards and realizes that Genthru's men must have rolled the Risky Dice. It's revealed that the two who looked like Bara and Sub were actually the Bombers' captives who had their appearances altered through an item. Tsezguerra's teammates want to use an "Accompany" to go after them, but Tsezguerra orders his team to wait and asks the two captives if Genthru is the Bomber. One of the captives says that he doesn't know, but the other assumes that it's possible since Genthru blew off the head of the guy who was caught with him. Tsezguerra's teammates are startled by the revelation, and Tsezguerra explains that Genthru used to work with the large group of players that suddenly died all at once. He remembers Genthru bringing up the Bomber during a previous encounter and says that his segue was awkward, surmising that it's a keyword used to activate his ability. Because of Genthru's dangerous ability, Tsezguerra warns his men that confronting Genthru directly would not be a good idea. The others worry that Genthru will clear the game, but Tsezguerra uses "List" and confirms that no one has acquired "Plot of Bleach" yet, stressing that they need to find it first. His teammates bring up that they can get a monopoly with "Clone" and Mimic," also mentioning that they still have their "Voucher." Tsezguerra and his comrades then use an "Accompany" to travel to Soufrabi. In Masadora, the Bombers congratulate each other on the mission's success. Bara says that they have 93 cards now, but Sub corrects him by replying that it's 92 since they reverted one, with Genthru focusing on the fact that they broke Tsezguerra's monopolies. Bara adds that they're waiting for Hagakushi and Tokharone to revert two of the remaining seven cards, and Sub says that the card they reverted was "Mad Scientist's Plastic Surgery," but he is confident that they can get it again. Genthru says that the main issue is "Plot of Beach," but they decide to retrieve "Mad Scientist's Plastic Surgery," "X-Ray Goggles," and "Tree of Plenty" first, then going after "Plot of Bleach" and finally taking "Wild Luck Alexandrite" from someone else. He confidently adds that they should decide what three cards they want to take back and how they will spend the reward money. Meanwhile, Gon's Paladin's Necklace dispels a "Fake" spell placed on a "Favor Cushion" during a trade, and the owner apologizes and gives him the real one. Killua complains that some players are such cheats, and Biscuit comments that the necklace is quite handy. Gon wants to confirm if it lifts curses on things he touches, and Killua says that it works on cards. Gon seems disappointed, and Killua wonders what he had in mind. Gon explains that he hoped to use the necklace to cure the Sick Villagers, guessing that they might be cursed. After realizing that he means the ninja from before, Biscuit comments that since they aren't cards, it probably won't work, but Killua replies that it may be worth trying. The three return to the village and ask the inhabitants if they will trust them and put their lives in their care. After one of them relays their gratitude and agrees to trust them, all the villagers turn into the "Sick Villagers" card, but when Gon uses the necklace, it turns into "Healthy Villagers." As a token of their gratitude, the villagers present Gon with a small box. Inside is a Wild Luck Alexandrite ring that transforms into a "Wild Luck Alexandrite" card.

Chapter 154 Common Cause (, "Kyōdō Sensen") is the 154th chapter of the Hunter × Hunter manga, written and illustrated by Yoshihiro Togashi. Synopsis. After obtaining "Wild Luck Alexandrite", Gon's team now has 55 cards, but Killua points out that they're all A and B-rank. Biscuit adds that they've used up all their "Analysis" and "Guidepost" cards, prompting Killua to wish that they had an "Eye of God" card. Gon is suddenly contacted by Kazsule, and although Gon offers to trade "Tome of a Thousand Tales" and "Pearl Locusts," Kazsule says that the trade can wait, asking them to meet up and talk. He explains that a three-man team led by Genthru is getting close to clearing the game. He says that he has invited others as well to meet two kilometers northeast of Masadora, adding that they should at least come to exchange information. Including Kazsule and his two teammates, fifteen players attend the meeting. After Kazsule repeats his reason for summoning them, he reveals that Genthru's team has 96 cards and stresses that they need to come up with a strategy. Killua speaks up and asks how one finds out the rankings, which annoys a player named Asta who wants to return to the subject at hand. Kazsule and his team stress that information exchange is also a purpose of the meeting, and Kazsule explains that one can find out who has the most cards by asking a trade shop, adding that if they pay extra, they can find out which cards people have. Asta jumps in and adds that they still have to meet the new players to be able to cast "Contact" or "Fluoroscopy." Nick Cue says that they know Genthru is working with Sub and Bara, with Genthru holding all 96 cards and the other two holding duplicates. He stresses that they only need four more cards to clear the game, and Kazsule starts with No. 000, which they believe to be an event card that can only be obtained after someone collects 99 cards (meaning that Genthru's team only needs three more cards). He urges that they need to monopolize one of the remaining three before Genthru's team collects it. Asta suggests overwhelming them with spells, but Kazsule explains that since Genthru's team already has "Paladin's Necklace," the only attack spell worth using would be "Levy," which would also be ineffective in certain situations. Gon wonders what those would be, and Montreux says that when someone has a "Fortress" and 11 "Clone" or "Mimic" cards. Nick Cue explains that not even "Levy" can affect a page protected by "Fortress," which would make their spells useless if Genthru's team is protecting all their pages. Asta then suggests using force, but Yabibi replies that they don't know what abilities the three of them have. The group agrees that the most realistic option is to work together and monopolize a card, but Asta speaks up and says that while she agrees with the plan, she doesn't approve of all the members, pointing toward Gon and Killua. Kazsule reminds her that all six teams met the prerequisite of holding more than 50 cards, but Asta says that they also need to offer something useful to the group. Gon reveals that they know Genthru's ability, and Killua adds that they have one of the three remaining cards. Asta is content and asks them about Genthru's ability, but Killua turns the tables and asks if she has anything useful for them. Asta says that her group has 71 cards, then offering to give Killua an A-rank card in exchange for the information. Killua quickly declines the offer and says that they need two S-rank cards or information just as useful. The two continue to argue back and forth over the details, but Kazsule finally jumps in and asks them to work together. The two groups eventually convince Killua and Asta respectively to work together, and Gon's group receives "Pregnancy Stones" and "Shield of Faith" for the information on Genthru. Gon explains that Genthru's abilities are Countdown and Little Flower, both of which he uses to blow up his targets, stressing that they all should do their best to keep their distance from him. Both Asta and Hanse realize that Genthru touched them, with Killua and Biscuit eager to collect more cards in exchange for more information. Asta asks how the ability can be removed, and Gon says that they have to say, "I caught the Bomber" while touching Genthru. Killua yells at Gon for ruining their plan, but Gon says that he didn't want another fight, further telling Asta that the bomb's timer starts after Genthru explains his ability and that she should be safe if she stays away from him. Asta feels compelled to share information in exchange, explaining that the two ways to cast spells are to say them aloud and to put them on the last page of their book. Gon says that they already knew both ways, but Asta adds that if they have the spell on the last page, it can be canceled out. She uses an example with "Fluoroscopy" and says that the list of players they've met will come up on the screen, but if they take the card out without hitting "enter," the spell won't get cast and they can keep seeing the list of players again and again with that same card. She also reveals that all B-rank cards can be bought at trade shops, explaining that they need to shop at the same one more than 50 times and the shopkeeper will mention it. Killua realizes that that's how they get the monthly prizes, and Asta continues by asking them if they have multiple "X-Ray Goggles." Gon says yes, and she explains that it will make getting "Beauty Magnet Emerald" and "Mystery Pond" easier (both of which are S-rank cards). She offers another card, but Gon politely refuses, which angers both Killua and Biscuit. After Yabibi and Goreinu also provide information, Kazsule gets the group's attention again and asks which of the three cards they should monopolize. Killua reveals that they have "Wild Luck Alexandrite," but says that it may not be practical to monopolize since only one can be obtained per team and the conversion limit is 20 (which is too many for a monopoly). Several members are impressed and already begin asking if they can trade Killua for the card, but Kazsule tells them to do that later. Others also mention that getting 19 "Clones" so quickly will be impossible and worry about if someone else already has the card. Someone uses "List" to check and sees that five others have it. Hanse checks "Tree of Plenty" and sees that three people already have it, while Montreux sees that no one has obtained No. 2 yet. Amana uses "Guidepost" and learns that the card is in Soufrabi. The group then uses an "Accompany" card to travel there.

Chapter 155 The Captain and His 14 Devils (と14の, "Senchō to Jū Yo Nin no Akuma") is the 155th chapter of the Hunter × Hunter manga, written and illustrated by Yoshihiro Togashi. Synopsis. When the group arrives in Soufrabi, Kazsule explains the usual steps to acquire SS-rank items, which are finding an with information regarding the card in question, doing a task in exchange for the information, and then finding out whether the information received is true or not (and finally doing a quest to acquire the item). After the group splits up, Killua tells Gon and Biscuit that they will start from the edge of town, stressing that finding the crucial information could take several weeks. But surprising Killua, Goreinu says that he's found someone and leads them to an older NPC, but the man simply tells them to stop looking for the "Plot of Bleach" and warns that they are asking to get killed. The other members talk to various NPCs, who give similar warnings. Nick Cue notes that they checked the town months ago, but didn't receive any clues. Manheim guesses that it might be triggered at a certain point during the year. Eventually, Kazsule and the others come across a female NPC who asks for help. She tells them that "Plot of Beach" is the entrance to Poseidon's Cavern, which is said to hold an enormous treasure. Attracted by it, a group of fifteen pirates came to the town and now run things: Razor and his 14 Devils. She explains that they tortured and killed fishermen who knew about the secret, including her father and brother. She reveals that her brother told her the location before he died, promising to tell them if they can drive the pirates out of the town. The others wonder why the girl wouldn't talk to them before, and Amana guesses that it was triggered by the number of players they have, which is the same as the fifteen pirates. Souheil asks how the NPCs would know that, and Killua says that it must have been the use of an "Accompany" card. They conclude that the event trigger is using "Accompany" on a group of 15 or more players to travel to Soufrabi. Yabibi and Montreux are surprised and excited, while Goreinu seems troubled by the situation. Killua hears his comment about it being cruel and asks him about it, but Goreinu simply waves it off, leaving him puzzled. Kazsule finally asks the female NPC where they can find the pirates. The group enters an abandoned bar where three people are drinking and another is standing behind the counter. The largest of them asks the group who they are and says that it's a private party, but Kazsule replies that they have come to talk, then asking if they can leave the town. Taken aback at first, the pirates burst out laughing and say that they haven't heard that line in a while, warning them that all those people ended up as fish food. The large pirate becomes serious and approaches the group, saying that even though he could squash them right now, his captain makes the decisions. He tells them that words won't work and begins to pour alcohol in a circle around himself, using a lighter to ignite it. He makes a deal with the group: if they can force him outside the ring, he will take them to his captain.

Chapter 156 Face-Off: Part 1 (①, "Taiketsu (Ichi)") is the 156th chapter of the Hunter × Hunter manga, written and illustrated by Yoshihiro Togashi. Synopsis. Bopobo explains that the match starts when one of them enters the circle, adding that they can attack all at once. After he reminds them that all they have to do is force him outside and he will take them to his captain, Zeho volunteers and states that since he's an Enhancer, he will have the best chance. He focuses his breathing, and his aura and muscles increase in size, but Killua sees that he's out of practice since it took him far too long to build up Ren that small. Zeho charges into the circle and tries to move Bopobo back, but the pirate doesn't budge, impressed by Zeho's muscles. As Killua thinks to himself that he could personally beat Zeho without Nen, Bopobo grabs hold of Zeho and lifts him off the ground, squeezing him hard as Zeho begs him to stop and says that he wins. Bopobo doesn't relent and licks his lips with delight, but Gon jumps in and kicks him in the face, forcing him to release Zeho. Bopobo reminds him that a person loses when they step outside the circle, not when they start to beg and plead. He then says that since Gon came over the flames to kick him and then jumped out, he loses as well. Realizing his mistake, Gon asks Bopobo to let him try again, and Bopobo replies that he doesn't mind and will even give him a handicap by staying right at the edge. However, Killua gets Gon's attention and stops him, whispering that it wouldn't be a good idea to use his ability in front of everyone else. Gon argues that no one else but them can beat Bopobo, especially with Biscuit pretending to be scared. Killua says to leave it to him and confidently approaches the ring of fire. He says that he's pretty tough and asks Bopobo if he's ready for him. Bopobo replies that he will let Killua win if he can move him just one step. Instead of walking into the circle, Killua strolls to the bar counter and asks the pirate if he works there. The pirate says that of course he doesn't and adds that the real owner is "sleeping" in the back. Killua then grabs a liquor bottle, promising to pay for it later, and breaks the top off it. Bopobo seems to realize what Killua is planning to do and warns him against it, but Killua quickly jumps onto his back and pours the liquor on his head, disorienting him as he uses his electricity to light his head on fire. As Bopobo screams out in pain and falls to his knees, his comrades try to enter the ring to help him, but Killua yells at them to stay back, reminding them that the only way to lose is to step outside the ring. Bopobo then rolls outside the boundary and yells at the others to put out the fire. Once it's extinguished, he turns toward Killua with a furious expression and begins charging toward him, but one of his comrades kicks him in the face before he can reach Killua, reminding him of his promise to the group. Bopobo apologizes, and the other pirate tells them to follow him. The group is taken to a lighthouse by the coast, with the pirates explaining that it was converted into a fortress and that it was previously used to spot smugglers. Before they enter, Bopobo warns Killua that he will kill him, but Killua remains unfazed by the threat. The players are then led inside and surprised to find a sports facility. After Razor learns about the group and why they are there, he proposes a best-of-fifteen contest, explaining that each person can win a single point and the first team to reach eight points will be the winner. He says that they (Razor's group) will decide what they play and that if they (Razor's group) lose, they will leave the island. Goreinu speaks up and asks what happens if their group loses, and Razor assures them that they only have to leave the lighthouse. Razor explains that the contest will involve a variety of sports, and Bopobo immediately challenges Killua to a sumo bout, but Killua tells him that they will fight last after his team has seven wins. One of the pirates calms Bopobo down and says that he will go first, telling them that his sport is boxing and then waiting for an opponent at the center of the ring. Razor repeats that each player can compete only once. After Kazsule confirms that they are allowed to use Nen, Montreux volunteers to fight.

Chapter 157 Face-Off: Part 2 (②, "Taiketsu (Ni)") is the 157th chapter of the Hunter × Hunter manga, written and illustrated by Yoshihiro Togashi. Synopsis. The pirate boxer makes sure that Montreux knows the rules of boxing, and Razor adds that there are special rules, saying that conjured objects are allowed. Some members of the group worry about guns being used, but the pirate boxer assures them that he will fight with his fists, with the rule being in place more so to help the challengers. After the pirate boxer makes sure that Montreux still wants to fight, Razor explains that each round will be three minutes, with the match continuing until someone is knocked out. The bell rings, and Montreux says that he knows why the pirate picked boxing, then throwing a single punch that shoots a ball of Nen past the pirate's cheek. He guesses that the pirate is also an Emitter and that the ring is the perfect arena for them, but confidently adds that he is better, throwing a flurry of punches that strike the pirate and send him to the canvas. The group members begin to rejoice over the easy win, but as Gon and Killua say that it's a draw, Montreux suddenly looks injured and falls down as well, leaving the group in disbelief. Razor begins the count and the pirate boxer rises to his feet and is fine to keep fighting. Montreux doesn't regain consciousness before the ten-count, and Razor declares the pirate boxer to be the winner. Kazsule asks Killua to explain what happened, and as Killua thinks to himself that the group members are hopeless, he says that the pirate used teleportation to throw a short uppercut right below Montreux's chin. The pirate boxer is surprised that someone figured out his attack, and Killua adds that Montreux's jabs were weak in comparison to the pirate's counterpunch, which was both sudden and powerful. As the next pirate steps up and says that his sport is soccer juggling, Killua whispers something to Gon and Biscuit, who agree that that's a smart decision. Biscuit volunteers to challenge him, and the pirate says that he will have to be careful not to harm a girl. He tosses her a ball and says that whoever juggles their ball the longest wins, explaining that Nen attacks are allowed. He adds that the ball cannot be touched with their hands and that the entire room is the arena. After he mentions that the ball can't hit their allies either, the two begin the match, but Biscuit's ball hits the floor after a single bounce and she playfully says that it was more difficult than she thought. Killua volunteers to go next and asks Bopobo if he's ready. Bopobo is eager to start the sumo match, and Killua asks if the rules are the same, with Bopobo explaining that weapons and Nen are allowed and the match is over when a part of someone's body touches outside the ring. He tells Killua to take off his shoes and adds that one of their bodies must touch outside the ring, which will allow him to slam Killua around as many times as he wants. As Bopobo continues to explain the rules, Razor realizes what the group's plan is. After some time, the pirates reach eight points and win the contest, ordering the group to leave as Bopobo yells at Killua for losing on purpose. Killua smiles and says that he will be back. Speaking to himself, Razor commends their strategy of losing on purpose to gather as much information as possible, knowing that they will be back with more powerful allies. Outside the lighthouse, Kazsule says that they can't retry the quest with the same party members, but it's not a big problem since only one person needs to be different. However, Asta speaks up and says that her team is dropping out, explaining that there is no way the Bombers will be able to get a team of 15 players together to complete the quest. She tells the other players to stay away as well and says that the Bombers will only come after them if they get the card. The others seem to agree with her line of thinking and they all leave the lighthouse, but Goreinu remains with Gon, Killua, and Biscuit. He tells them that they need to look for stronger allies if they want to win, saying that it's actually better to obtain the card as soon as possible. Killua jumps in and says that it would lower the chances of infighting. Gon wonders what they mean, and Killua explains that they need a party of 15 to complete the quest, but the card's conversion limit is only three. He understands what Goreinu meant earlier when he said that the quest was cruel, and Goreinu says that they need at least four more people and preferably a single group of 11. Gon asks why, and Killua says that it would allow them to split the three cards among the three teams without any fighting.

Chapter 158 Two of a Kind +1 (た2+1, "Nitamono Dōshi no Jijō Purasu Ichi") is the 158th chapter of the Hunter × Hunter manga, written and illustrated by Yoshihiro Togashi. Synopsis. In a restaurant, Goreinu asks Gon, Killua, and Biscuit if they know anyone to recruit, reminding them that they can't afford to waste any of the five "Magnetic Force" and "Accompany" cards they have. Killua asks Goreinu if he knows anyone, but Goreinu replies that that's the reason why he was playing the game by himself. Gon says he has trouble remembering all of the players they've encountered thus far. Still, Killua adds that while the list is constantly growing, "Chrollo" would be the strongest among them, even though Kurapika was confident that it wasn't him. Gon gets the idea of asking Binolt, but Killua isn't sure if he's still around, and after they check Gon's book, they see that the light beside his name is off, which Goreinu says means that he either left the game or died. He reminds them of Jeet's death in Antokiba and says that his name should also be in Gon's book. Gon and Killua look through the long list of names by having a "Peek" card in the slot, noticing that many of the lights have gone dark. Goreinu asks to take a look and recognizes Gashta, Cuzco, and Zenju, fellow Hunters also hired by Battera. Killua asks him if he knows everyone Battera hired, but Goreinu says that he only knows a few he met through work. He tells them that Gashta and Zetsk are brothers (known as the Bellam Brothers), but while both are skilled, they wouldn't work with anyone. He also mentions that Sakisuke is skilled in combat, but not as good as himself, and since he's a greedy person, he would demand more than his share. Killua says that they should keep him in mind for the time being and points out that Latarza was the player who cast a spell on him, saying that the three players between him and Nickes are the ones they must have passed on the street. As the two continue looking through the list and try to remember when they met certain players, Goreinu reminds them that they're looking for strong allies, but Gon and Killua can't remember if any of them would be worth recruiting. Biscuit speaks up and says that someone they haven't met in the game yet may be a good candidate: Tsezguerra. However, Goreinu says that he would prefer not to ask him since his group has just as many cards as the Bomber, so it's unlikely they would help without receiving one of the cards. Killua says that the other option is to use "Collision" to speak with random players, but it may not be a good idea. Gon suggests finding out the identity of "Chrollo" first, and Killua says that the person has to be a member of the Phantom Troupe, guessing that they took the JoyStation Console that was reported stolen. Gon wonders why they didn't use their own name, and Killua says that he's used the name "Evans" before, but says that Gon's question is important to figure out. They wonder why the person is playing the game, with both assuming that the person is there to clear the game like they are, but Goreinu says that they should find out whether that's their actual purpose or not. He suggests casting "Clairvoyance" on the player and says that since they've been in the game a while, they'll be able to tell if the person really cares about collecting cards. They check the player's collection and see that they have no specified slot cards and only six free slot cards, all of which are food and water. They are certain that the person is in the game to do something else, and Goreinu says that if they team up with them, they won't have to give the person the card once they complete the quest. Gon worries about them being a Troupe member, but says that they need to talk to them. As he and Killua argue back and forth about whether they should meet with the person, Goreinu asks Biscuit if the two are okay, and she assures him that it happens all the time. Gon wins out in the end, and as they prepare to travel to the player, Goreinu becomes worried about the two friends bickering, saying to himself that Gon's performance at the tryouts and the number of cards they have are the only things keeping him from leaving. The group uses an "Accompany" card to travel to "Chrollo Lucilfer," but when they land near a pool of water, they find a naked Hisoka bathing. He is happy to see Gon and Killua, emitting some bloodlust which causes the two to display their Ren. He sees that both of them have matured and guesses that they have found a good teacher. He is eager for them to ripen into sweet fruit, and Goreinu asks who the pervert is and if he's Chrollo. Gon and Killua both say no, and Hisoka first asks Goreinu if he's their teacher, but then sees a drooling Biscuit, who runs away embarrassed and hides behind a tree. Hisoka thinks to himself that she must be their teacher and guesses that she's a Transmuter, asking aloud what they wanted with Chrollo. Gon asks him what he's doing in Greed Island, and Hisoka wonders what to say, thinking that if he tells them the truth, they may stop him from meeting the Exorcist. He considers it, but says that he doesn't want his battle with Chrollo to be delayed any longer. Finally, he answers that he's looking for Chrollo, telling them that there's a way to remove Kurapika's Nen called Exorcism. He says that he wanted to tell Chrollo about it and remembered that some of the Troupe members were interested in the game, which is why he used Chrollo's name to get their attention. Gon and Killua both remember that Hisoka was only pretending to be a member of the Troupe before. Hisoka says that while Chrollo may already know about Exorcism and finding a good Exorcist is incredibly difficult, he wants to do everything he can to get Chrollo to fight him. He then asks them why they traveled to him, saying that it couldn't have been just to ask why he's in the game, but Gon says that that was the only reason. Killua adds that Gon wanted to see who was using Chrollo's name, and Gon remembers the warning Gotoh gave him before about being deceived. Putting on an innocent act, Biscuit speaks up and says that they are looking for strong allies, politely asking for Hisoka's help. Hisoka agrees to help, but wonders why they are looking for someone strong. Goreinu isn't sure about Hisoka, and Killua says that she doesn't know what he's like. With her back turned to Hisoka, she says that she feels a connection to him, but uses her aura to tell them that he's lying. As she begins to explain the situation to Hisoka, Goreinu becomes even more worried about teaming up with him.

Chapter 159 Aiai, the City of Love (アイアイ, "Ren'ai Toshi Aiai") is the 159th chapter of the Hunter × Hunter manga, written and illustrated by Yoshihiro Togashi. Synopsis. After explaining the situation to Hisoka, Biscuit tells Gon and Killua that he is hiding the truth rather than lying outright, which she can sense after lying for 50 years herself. She says that they should stay with Hisoka to see if he's actually hiding something about Chrollo, confirming with Gon and Killua that he would also be a strong ally. As the group makes their way through a forest, Hisoka is at the back and lasciviously watches Gon and Killua, who feel him staring at them and order him to walk in front. Hisoka confirms with Goreinu that they need ten more people, and Goreinu says that people who aren't interested in collecting cards are the best candidates. He asks Hisoka if he has anyone in mind, but Hisoka says that most people are there to clear the game, so it will difficult to find people like himself. Maintaining her innocent act, Biscuit still senses that Hisoka is hiding something, and he asks if they used someone's ability to travel to him. Goreinu explains that it was a spell, which Hisoka has heard can be purchased at shops. As Goreinu adds, there are 40 spells, and it's difficult to get specific ones because of the nature of card packs; Killua becomes suspicious and tries to figure out what Hisoka is hiding. Hisoka leads the group to Aiai, the city of love, and they first run into a girl on her hands and knees, looking for her glasses on the ground. Hisoka tells the two boys that they can get to know her by helping her, saying that the city is full of clichés. As he tells Goreinu to watch the corners, Goreinu runs into a young girl eating a piece of bread and saying that she is going to be late before running off. Hisoka says that Goreinu shouldn't have apologized and that if he had gotten into an argument with her, she would have remembered him. A man approaches Biscuit and says that he needs a model for his hair salon, but Killua reminds the eager Biscuit of their mission. Gon then sees a young girl being attacked by three large men, but before he can intervene, both Killua and Biscuit punch him in the back of the head and wonder why he had to choose the most cliché scenario of them all. Gon remains concerned for the girl, but Killua reminds him that she's just an and that he can help her when they have more time. The group realizes how distracting the city is, and Killua suggests that they go somewhere else, but Hisoka remarks that it's great to alleviate boredom. Hisoka's mention of being bored causes Killua to think about where they found Hisoka, asking himself what he would do if he entered the game to find someone. He knows that players learn early on how important spell cards are and remembers that Gon and Biscuit met Hisoka while he was taking the Hunter Exam, adding that since they were training around Masadora, Hisoka has most likely been to the city. He adds that most players have to travel to Masadora to buy spell cards and that if Hisoka had really been looking for the Spiders, he would have stayed there to meet them. Hisoka's comment about being bored enters Killua's mind again, and he says that Hisoka either isn't looking for the Spiders or he has possibly found them already. He decides that the latter must be what Hisoka is hiding and wonders what he is waiting for now. He suddenly realizes that there must be an Exorcist on Greed Island, a fact which both Hisoka and the Spiders already know. As Killua processes his discovery, Gon gets his attention and asks him if anything is wrong. Hisoka tells Biscuit and Goreinu that they can get a rare card if they go out with the princess, and Killua realizes that he can't reveal the truth to Gon since he won't be able to keep the secret, with Gon left wondering if Killua is still mad from their argument earlier. Killua realizes that Hisoka will leave their group if he finds out that they learned the truth, adding that he doesn't want to lose a strong ally and ability to keep an eye on him. Gon gets Killua's attention again and says that Tsezguerra may be the best option since he has a team around him and it will easier to negotiate with him. He suggests at least meeting him and putting him on their list, and as Killua agrees that they should see what he's doing, he realizes that if they can check Hisoka's list, they will be able to tell if he's already met the Spiders. Gon suddenly asks Hisoka if they can look at his list to see if he has encountered a player named Tsezguerra. As Hisoka asks Gon how to check it, Killua realizes the great timing since Hisoka would have become suspicious if he (Killua) had asked to check his list. Gon tells Hisoka to put a certain card in the last page of his book, and Killua knows that if Hisoka doesn't let them see his list, then his theory will be even more likely. Hisoka summons his book and sees Tsezguerra on his list, allowing both Gon and Killua to look through all the names. Killua is surprised to see that none of the Spiders' names are there, asking himself if he was being too paranoid and considering that Hisoka may really be looking for them. Gon talks with Goreinu, who says that teaming up with Tsezguerra is practical but adds that they should have him share part of the reward if his team clears the game first. Gon gives Hisoka a "Contact" card and tells him to cast it on Tsezguerra, saying that they will do the negotiating. As Gon and Killua talk with Tsezguerra, Hisoka chuckles to himself and hides his right hand behind his back, commenting on how useful Texture Surprise can be.

Chapter 16 Enter the Taskmasters (, "Shirenkan Tōjō") is the 16th chapter of the Hunter × Hunter manga, written and illustrated by Yoshihiro Togashi. Synopsis. With 69 hours and 17 minutes left to reach the bottom of Trick Tower alive, the five examinees prepare to set out. Once Tonpa puts on his wrist timer and causes a door to appear, both Kurapika and Leorio realize that it was programmed to happen the moment all five timers were put on. Tonpa takes charge of the group, and Leorio wonders who made him the leader. The five see that the door requires them to vote on whether they want to open it or not, and Leorio is surprised that they have to agree already, saying that the choice is obvious. The door opens after they cast their votes, but it's revealed that one person voted no, with Leorio asking if the person wants to speak up. Tonpa playfully apologizes and explains that his finger must have slipped, which causes Leorio to happily forgive him before angrily telling him not to let it happen again. Gon tells him that the door is open, but Leorio stresses that they all need to work together, mocking Tonpa's excuse that his finger slipped. Kurapika tells him that they are wasting time, and Killua points out that it doesn't matter if Tonpa wants to be in the minority since they have the majority of the votes. After Leorio glares at Tonpa and agrees to move on, the five examinees quickly find themselves in another locked room, now asked whether they want to go right or left. Leorio votes left and says that the process could become monotonous, and Kurapika agrees that it will if they have to vote every couple of feet. Three of them vote to go right, two to go left, and Leorio can't believe it, angrily pointing out that it's important to go left in a maze and that going right makes him nervous. However, Kurapika counters by saying that according to research, people who are lost tend to unconsciously go left, with Killua adding that he has also heard of it. Leorio scoffs at the research and asks which direction they chose, with both saying right. Tonpa agrees with their reasoning and says that the examiners may know the rule as well, possibly using it to trip up naive examinees. After Leorio tries to bond with Gon over their votes, the five move forward and find themselves in a large room with a small stone platform in the center. Killua quickly points out the shrouded figures waiting on the other side, and one of the prisoners looks at the camera above them, saying that the examinees have arrived and asking that his handcuffs be unlocked. After the restraints fall to the floor and the man removes the shroud from his head, he addresses the examinees and explains that the committee has chosen them as their taskmasters, adding that the five of them will challenge the five prisoners. He continues by saying that the fights will be one-on-one and they can only fight once, telling them to choose their order and adding that they will pass if they win a majority of the matches. The prisoner also reveals that they can fight however they want and that there will be no draws, with the winner being declared once an opponent admits defeat. He tells the examinees to vote on whether they want to compete or not, and while Leorio can't believe that they have to vote again, he tells the group that they should make sure the vote is unanimous, glaring at Tonpa who quickly agrees with his assessment. All five examinees vote yes, and Leorio eagerly yells over that they accept the challenge. The prisoner agrees to go first and tells them to choose their fighter. Tonpa unexpectedly steps forward and explains that he will take the opportunity to see what their opponents are capable of. He adds that since he has given them reasons not to trust him, he will make sure that he gets his match out of the way so things don't depend on him winning if they have to go to a tiebreaker. Thin walkways extend from both sides of the arena, and the prisoner tells the examinees that only the contender can make his way to the platform. After Tonpa looks nervously at the pit below him, he makes his way onto the platform and stands opposite the prisoner, who proposes that they fight until one of them either admits defeat or dies. Tonpa eventually agrees to the deal, and Leorio is left stunned by his choice. After telling Tonpa that he respects his determination, the prisoner suddenly lunges toward him to attack, but Tonpa immediately falls to his hands and knees, surrendering and admitting that he has been beaten. The other four can't believe how quickly Tonpa gave up and wonder if he's trying to trick the prisoner, who asks Tonpa to repeat what he said. Tonpa embarrassingly says that he has been beaten, causing Leorio to glare in anger and the prisoner to chuckle as he returns to his side of the arena. He explains that their side only needs two more wins before they fail the exam, asking them if they still want to continue. Tonpa returns to his side and explains that the prisoner looked a lot more imposing up close. Leorio quickly grabs him by the collar and rebukes him for messing with others and enjoying it. Tonpa smugly admits to it and asks what he plans to do about it. As the two continue to quarrel, another prisoner chuckles at the examinees fighting among themselves and realizes how easily they can win now. Tonpa then reveals to the others that he has no interest in becoming a Hunter.

Chapter 160 Face-Off: Part 3 (③, "Taiketsu (San)") is the 160th chapter of the Hunter × Hunter manga, written and illustrated by Yoshihiro Togashi. Synopsis. As the rest of the group waits for him, Hisoka undoes his Texture Surprise on the list of names, revealing both "Shizuku" and "Phinks" as he smiles. The five of them use an "Accompany" card to travel to Tsezguerra, and Goreinu first tells him that they want 10% of the 50 billion reward in exchange for information on "Plot of Bleach." Tsezguerra is hesitant, and Goreinu stresses that it will be almost impossible to discover it otherwise. Tsezguerra replies that they obtained "Patch of Forest" through luck, explaining that they bought a cloned copy from someone who took it from another person who won it using "Lottery." He makes sure that they don't have the card yet, and Goreinu says that if they had the card, they wouldn't be asking for so much in return. Tsezguerra agrees to the deal, and Goreinu explains the situation regarding the card. Tsezguerra realizes why they wanted to meet in person and asks if they want to team up to acquire the card. He notes Goreinu's group of five and says that he has four including himself, which will make a total of nine, asking what they should do about the rest. Goreinu replies that they can just recruit players who are having trouble returning to the real world, and Tsezguerra realizes that they won't have to share any cards with them. He asks if the nine of them can win the eight matches, and Goreinu says that while they can't be completely sure, they should be stronger than all the pirates except their boss. After he adds that they can retry with a different team if they fail, Killua jumps in and asks Tsezguerra to prove that he's worth recruiting. After Tsezguerra recognizes that the tables have turned since Battera's tryouts, he readies himself and leaps high up into the air, hovering in place as Gon and Killua look on in amazement. He chuckles and says that he could jump even higher, telling them that his personal best is over 16 meters. Killua realizes that he must have focused his aura in his feet before he launched, and Gon says that they should try it. The two ready themselves and leap into the air, easily going higher than Tsezguerra as he wonders in disbelief how they improved so quickly. All three land and Tsezguerra says that he could still go higher, with Gon adamant about trying it again and again to beat Killua, who tells Tsezguerra that he passes. Goreinu apologizes for their childishness as the two repeatedly leap into the air. He tells Tsezguerra that while they trust his skills, the quest involves playing sports and so determining who will play what is vital. Tsezguerra asks about them, and Goreinu goes through the eight they have confirmed, guessing that the pirates may change them up if they start to lose. Tsezguerra chooses beach volleyball, Goreinu goes with wrestling, Killua volunteers for sumo again (as Gon keeps challenging him to the jumping contest). Barry says that he has a strategy for boxing, and Gon is left wondering what he will do. Rodriot chooses bowling, confident that he can have a perfect game using Nen while also countering any tricks his opponent uses. Hisoka picks soccer juggling and says that his Bungee Gum will make things a lot easier. As two others choose free throw shooting and ping pong, Gon is left without anything, but Tsezguerra approaches him and says that he can be his partner in beach volleyball, confident in Gon's jumping ability but adding that he needs to practice. Barry checks his book and suddenly sees that Genthru has reached 97 cards. Both Gon and Killua realize that Genthru's team only needs "Plot of Bleach" and "Wild Luck Alexandrite" to clear the game. After recruiting six more players and practicing for one week, the group of fifteen stands outside the lighthouse, and Tsezguerra says that they can't afford to lose now that Genthru is so close. They walk inside the large gymnasium, and Barry enters the ring to take on the pirate boxer. He immediately moves in close, and the pirate boxer realizes that he no longer has the advantage as an Emitter. The pirate boxer does his best to guard, but as Barry lands a hard strike to his gut, Tsezguerra explains that the pattern on the canvas is called Divine Script and augments Nen. He adds that it took the boxer hours to apply it and surmises that his teleportation only works there, which means he isn't an opponent to worry about. Barry's punches overwhelm the boxer, and he wins the group their first point. Rodriot then wins in bowling and Kess wins in free throw shooting. Razor eyes Gon, Killua, Biscuit, Hisoka, Goreinu, and Tsezguerra, recognizing their strength and saying that they will make things interesting. He gives the pirates the signal to lose their matches on purpose, assuring them that he has things under control. The others follow his command, but Bopobo refuses to cooperate and throws his cap down in anger. He challenges Killua to a fight and threatens to kill him on the spot, but Razor reminds Bopobo of the contract and that he will return to jail. Bopobo remains agitated and says that he's tired of playing the game. The new recruits look on in confusion, and Bopobo says that they can take Razor down if they all work together, adding that they can then use a boat to escape the island. However, Razor suddenly forms a ball of aura and throws it toward Bopobo's head, shattering his skull open as his body falls to the floor. The main six put on serious expressions, and Razor explains that breaking the taboo is deserving of punishment, wondering why Bopobo disobeyed him if he was aware of that fact. The six recruits are terrified by the carnage, and Razor says that it's his turn to compete.

Chapter 161 Face-Off: Part 4 (④, "Taiketsu (Yon)") is the 161st chapter of the Hunter × Hunter manga, written and illustrated by Yoshihiro Togashi. Synopsis. As Bopobo's body lies on the floor, the new recruits are terrified that the pirates are killing one another. They start to walk out, but Goreinu assures them that they won't have to fight at all, with Tsezguerra adding that they can quit if the main nine aren't able to get the eight wins. As he tells them aloud that they will be safe, he says to himself that weak players like them don't deserve to be in the game and act like they're Double-Star Hunters. He turns his attention to Razor, who he says has more aura than anyone present, confident that he must be one of the Game Masters. Killua speaks up and asks what will happen to the sumo match with Bopobo dead, and Razor says that Killua gets the win. Killua playfully replies that they hadn't decided who would compete in the sumo match, and Razor says that he can just give the win to one of the filler players. After Killua gifts the win to one of them and the group reaches four points, the pirates carry away Bopobo's body as Gon nervously watches them. Razor gets their attention and tells them that his sport of choice, dodgeball, requires eight people. He suddenly summons seven Nen beasts and says that he already has his team. Goreinu and Barry wonder how the points will be decided, and Razor replies that whoever wins will gain eight points (one for each team member). Tsezguerra realizes Razor's strategy and remembers the story about his "14 devils," understanding that it must be his ability. As the new recruits again express their fear and consider leaving, Rodriot and the others tell them that they can just get hit on purpose, but the weak players point out what happened to Bopobo. Razor clarifies that they will just be using a regular ball, but since Nen is allowed, it will make it equally destructive. Some of the new recruits run away in fear as Killua unsuccessfully tries to convince them to come back. Tsezguerra says that since they only have six now, they will need to recruit two weaklings no matter what. As he tries to think of a way to bring two of them back, Gon says that they can fight Razor by themselves, asking him if using only six players is allowed. Razor says that it isn't since it would defeat the point of bringing together a group of 15 people. Gon becomes angry and points out that Razor is by himself, wondering if he should even be arguing with an . He furiously asks if Bopobo was his friend and what he could have done to deserve being killed. Razor calmly answers that he committed robbery, rape, and murder (11 known cases at least). Hisoka speaks up and says that the game is taking place in reality, leaving Gon confused. Tsezguerra confirms that Greed Island is an actual place in the real world, explaining that it's a taboo to tell players that they're not in a game and that Bopobo was killed for breaking it. He says that Razor is not only a real person, but a game master as well, adding that Bopobo and the other pirates are death row convicts, who are sometimes hired by Hunters as long as they are absolutely obedient. He explains that since Bopobo not only refused Razor's orders, but tried to convince his comrades to do the same, his execution was necessary because Razor would have been punished if he had let Bopobo's actions slide. Gon continues to grapple with the fact that the game is taking place in reality, and both Killua and Biscuit never considered it either. Razor bounces the ball on the floor to get their attention and says that it doesn't make much difference, but Gon eagerly asks if Ging is on the island. Goreinu wonders who he's talking about, but the name immediately gets Razor's attention. As he guesses that Gon must be Ging's son, his aura suddenly spikes around him and, putting on an ominous smile, he says that Ging told him not to go easy on him when he arrived. Gon is frightened at first, but becomes excited and puts on an anxious smile. The rest of the new recruits run away in fear, and as Rodriot tries to convince them to stay, Goreinu tells him to let them leave, suddenly summoning two gorilla-like Nen beasts and confirming with Razor that it's allowed. The two teams are decided, and Razor begins to explain the rules: Gon is left slightly confused, and Killua just tells him to dodge or catch the ball. Razor asks if they have any questions, and Killua wonders if retrievers can take out other players. Razor says that they can, but reminds him that only one per team can come back inside the court. An eighth Nen beast of Razor's, Number 0, introduces itself as the referee and begins the match. Number 1 starts as the retriever for Razor's side, and Goreinu's white Nen beast for Gon's. The referee tosses the ball up at the center of the court, and Killua easily wins the exchange, hitting the ball back to Goreinu. Standing ready with his Nen beasts, Razor says that they can have the first shot, with Goreinu confidently winding up for a throw.

Chapter 162 Face-Off: Part 5 (⑤, "Taiketsu (Go)") is the 162nd chapter of the Hunter × Hunter manga, written and illustrated by Yoshihiro Togashi. Synopsis. As everyone waits for the first move, Goreinu gets a running start and says that this is a greeting, throwing the ball fast toward one of Razor's Nen beasts and easily knocking it down. His white gorilla throws the ball back to him, and he quickly takes out another, with Rodriot and Kess commenting on how easy the match will be. With three of his devils now standing outside the court, Razor says that they are ready to defeat their team, but Goreinu winds up again and throws it straight toward Razor, telling him to try if he can. However, Razor easily catches the shot with one hand and prepares for a counterattack. Goreinu becomes incredibly nervous and wonders if Razor is passing from far back in the court as he starts to wind up. Razor suddenly hurls the ball at incredible speed directly toward Goreinu, who realizes that if he doesn't dodge it, he will undoubtedly be killed. He uses his White Goreinu ability to switch positions with his white gorilla, who takes the hit and is decapitated, slowly breaking apart. The others are left stunned as Razor catches the rebound and an exasperated Goreinu kneels outside the court. Razor understands Goreinu's ability, and the white gorilla disappears entirely. Biscuit and Tsezguerra both realize that after enduring that level of fear from Razor's attack, Goreinu won't be able to help much anymore. Killua confirms with the referee that only the white gorilla is out, and the referee also reminds them that Goreinu will need to use "back" to return inside the court (unless he uses the ability on his other Nen beast). As Goreinu tells himself that he isn't done yet, Razor suddenly passes the ball quickly to one of his devils outside the court, and they begin passing it among themselves so quickly that the others can't follow its movement. One of the devils gets behind Tsezguerra and throws the ball toward his back, with both Gon and Killua warning him to look out. The ball strikes Tsezguerra hard as he braces for the impact and then falls to the floor. Killua picks up the ball and can't believe how heavy it feels, likening it to being hit by a bowling ball. Biscuit attends to Tsezguerra as he coughs up blood, and Razor says that he was able to avoid being killed by focusing his aura in his back after he heard their warning. He adds that broken bones may have punctured his organs, ordering his pirates to give him first aid, but Tsezguerra adamantly refuses as he rises to his feet before quickly sitting down. The referee informs Tsezguerra that if he can't continue playing because of an injury, he will be removed from the game. He adds that if they win, he will still be counted for his team and so they will still receive all eight points. Rodriot and Kess check on him, and Tsezguerra realizes how out of shape he is, lamenting how cautious he has been and saying that it will take months to get his instincts back. He jealously looks toward Gon and Killua, saying that while his combat skills are better than theirs overall, their agility and reflexes have surpassed his. He calms down and thinks back to training with Gon for beach volleyball, realizing that he hasn't practiced the basics in years and that he will have to start all over again. Still holding the ball, Killua thinks to himself that they should find a way to keep eliminating the other team while not giving up possession of the ball. Gon suddenly gets Hisoka's attention, and he understands what Gon wants, asking for the ball from Killua, who realizes that his Bungee Gum is the perfect technique for that strategy. Hisoka attaches his ability to the ball and hurls it toward one of the devils, easily knocking it down and retracting the ball right back to his hand. He asks to let himself have fun, playfully wondering if the match will end so easily. Razor chuckles and tells Hisoka to bring it on as he and his devils ready themselves for the next throw.

Chapter 163 Face-Off: Part 6 (⑥, "Taiketsu (Roku)") is the 163rd chapter of the Hunter × Hunter manga, written and illustrated by Yoshihiro Togashi. Synopsis. As Kess, Rodriot, and Barry celebrate Hisoka's successful strike, Killua realizes just how effective the strategy will be and wonders who Hisoka should attack next. He asks the referee if the last person inside the court is allowed to say "back" the moment they get hit, but Number 0 says that it isn't allowed since there would technically be no one inside the court for a split second. He adds, however, that someone else can say "back" right when the last person gets hit (which would allow the person who said it to come back inside the court). Killua gets Hisoka's attention, and Hisoka understands that they need to leave Razor for last. Razor recognizes Hisoka's skill and doubts that his three remaining devils inside the court can catch the ball. Hisoka throws another hard strike, but as Killua hopes that it will take out both Numbers 6 and 7, the two suddenly merge together into a larger Number 13 who hangs on tight to the ball. Hisoka is unable to pull it back with his Bungee Gum, undoing it after he realizes how tough the devil is. Killua gets the referee's attention and angrily asks if merging is allowed, and the referee says that it is. Killua wonders if splitting is also allowed, and the referee says that it is as long as the player count doesn't exceed the original total number. Gon and Killua know that they will have to get the ball back from Razor, with both using Ken to prepare for the strike. Tsezguerra notes how smooth and beautiful their auras are, realizing how much the two have been practicing and how easily they will be able to adapt in battle. However, he worries that their Ken won't be enough if Razor throws at full strength, adding that taking damage to get the ball back is only inevitable. Razor is glad to see that they can use Ken, saying that they shouldn't die if they're lucky. He asks Gon if he's ready, and Gon tells him to bring it on. As Razor winds up and throws the ball incredibly fast toward them, Tsezguerra realizes that their plan may backfire, but Gon puts his hands in front of his head and uses Ko to block the incoming shot, sending him flying back into the wall as both his shoes come off. Everyone wonders where the ball went, eventually seeing that it's lodged into the ceiling, and Razor comments that he had it built thick for that reason. Killua and Biscuit run to check on Gon, who is adamant that he's fine as blood runs down his forehead. He says that even though he used Ko on his head and hands, his legs weren't strong enough to take the impact. He smiles and says that he can still move his hands, confident that he will catch Razor's next throw, with both Killua and Biscuit left anxious. The referee notes where the ball would fall and declares that Gon's team will gain possession. However, he adds that since the ceiling is an extension of the floor and walls, Gon is considered out. Gon adamantly tells Killua and: Biscuit that he will be the one to use "back." The two eventually agree, but tell him that he can only do so once their team is down to two players. The referee restarts the match, and Killua tells Gon to get first aid, throwing the ball back and forth with Goreinu in the meantime. After Gon tells Kess and Rodriot that he's fine, Goreinu angrily looks toward Razor and says that he needs to get payback, getting a running start and winding up for a strong throw. Killua notices the black gorilla suddenly disappear and reappear in front of him, and Goreinu throws the ball toward the gorilla. He then uses his Black Goreinu ability to switch its position with Razor, who gets hit right in the face as he realizes that the two gorillas have different abilities.

Chapter 164 Face-Off: Part 7 (⑦, "Taiketsu (Nana)") is the 164th chapter of the Hunter × Hunter manga, written and illustrated by Yoshihiro Togashi. Synopsis. As the ball flies into the air and Goreinu begins to celebrate, Killua is glad that they will force Razor to use "back" early. Suddenly, Number 13 throws Number 2 toward the ball, and the smaller devil keeps it from touching the floor and tosses it back. With the others left stunned, Number 13 throws the ball and hits a speechless Goreinu in the face, knocking him unconscious. Razor catches the rebound and praises Goreinu's ability, telling him to nurture it. Biscuit protests in anger, but Razor calmly says that they didn't break any rules and headshots are legal, adding that if the ball had touched the floor, he (Razor) would have been out. Goreinu's black gorilla vanishes and Razor understands that the ability was being controlled remotely, informing them that if Goreinu wakes up during the match, the black gorilla can start inside the court. He doubts that that will happen, and the referee adds that if they run out of players before then, they will lose the match. Kess and Rodriot examine Goreinu's injuries, with the latter saying that he won't be strong enough to conjure his Nen beast even if he does wake up. While both teams are down to three players inside the court, Rodriot knows that theirs is struggling more, with half of them sitting out and an injured Gon acting as the retriever. He adds that their opponents have multiple retrievers, Razor is not only still inside the court, but also hasn't used his free out yet, and his team has possession of the ball. As Killua, Biscuit, and Hisoka ready themselves for the next strike, Razor uses an underarm throw and hurls the ball directly toward Killua. He realizes that he won't be able to catch it, but when he goes to dodge, the ball suddenly changes course and curves toward Biscuit and Hisoka. Biscuit quickly jumps out of the way and Hisoka barely dodges the strike, but a devil catches the throw and hurls it at point-blank range toward Hisoka's face. The others are left worried, but Hisoka expertly uses his Bungee Gum to slow the ball's momentum and catch it, leaving him with a bloody nose and a cut above his left eye. After realizing that Razor was trying to take out both Biscuit and Hisoka at once, a tense Killua knows that if he had moved to the left, the ball would have undoubtedly hit him. The referee suddenly declares that Biscuit is out, ordering her to step outside the court. Rodriot and Barry are confused by the decision, and as part of Biscuit's dress is shown to be torn, she angrily realizes that clothing counts as being hit. Gon uses the team's "back" and returns inside the court, with Barry assuring Rodriot that he is more than just a kid since he's the only one who has tried to block a throw from Razor. Biscuit asks Gon if he's okay and tells him not to go too far, but Gon just keeps repeating "yeah." She even asks him what the answer to 1+1 is, but he gives the same reply. She finally gives in and tells him to beat Razor even if he kills him, with Gon sternly answering that he will. After Gon tells Killua that he's fine, Hisoka says that he learned that the ball becomes less destructive once it goes to a retriever, and he shows only two broken fingers on his right hand from not using Ko. Hisoka realigns his broken fingers, and while Killua says that their priority should be to dodge Razor's throws, Gon disagrees and replies that it wouldn't be a true victory. Killua seems both confused and angry, telling Gon that he should just be happy with a win, but Gon points out that if Killua had moved to the left earlier, he would have been killed by Razor's throw. With his anger boiling inside him, he tells them that a cheap win won't be good enough, determined to achieve a complete victory over Razor. He says that he has an idea, getting the ball from Hisoka and telling Killua to stand in the middle of the court. He then tells him to bend his knees and to hold the ball out to his side. Killua realizes what the plan is, and Gon begins charging up Rock as the others look on with nervous anticipation.

Chapter 165 Face-Off: Part 8 (⑧, "Taiketsu (Hachi)") is the 165th chapter of the Hunter × Hunter manga, written and illustrated by Yoshihiro Togashi. Synopsis. As Razor sees the enormous increase in aura on the other side of the court, Gon finishes his chant and uses Rock to send the ball flying from Killua's hands toward the largest of Razor's devils. Number 13 catches the shot, but the force is so great that it knocks the devil outside the court. The others wait for an announcement, and the referee says that Number 13 is out since it caught the ball while touching outside the court, adding that Gon's team will also have possession. The members of Tsezguerra's team loudly cheer after the successful strike, but Gon says that it wasn't good enough, with Barry chuckling at how crazy Gon's standards are. Gon says to himself that the strike won't be strong enough to push Razor out, adamant that he needs more power. Biscuit tosses the ball to Killua, who gets into position again and holds the ball out to his side, confidently telling Gon that they will go after Razor next. Gon repeats that he needs more power to beat Razor, suddenly expanding his Ren so much that the others are left in disbelief. Standing behind him, Biscuit tells Razor that he chose the wrong sport since Gon can build up his Ren as long as he wants. She advises him to move out of the way, but Razor shrugs it off and prepares for the incoming strike. Gon tells himself to take the aura he has amassed and to focus it into his fist, and the others watch with varying emotions as he charges up another Rock and unleashes it to send the ball flying yet again. Killua says that it was a perfect strike and that there's no way Razor can catch it, but the Game Master bends his knees and readies his arms as if to receive a volleyball spike, bumping the ball high up into the air and doing a backflip to land on his feet. Hisoka notes his strategy to eliminate the ball's momentum, and Biscuit comments on how perfect his timing was, realizing how skilled Razor really is. Gon is left motionless at first, but he then gives a big smile and can't believe how awesome Razor's block was. Grinning back, Razor says that there's more than just dodging and catching, even though the bump wasn't that helpful. Kess and Rodriot comment on how effective Razor's bump was at eliminating the momentum of Gon's strike, but as the ball is seen falling above Razor's head, Hisoka suddenly uses his Bungee Gum to snatch it out of the air. He playfully reminds Razor that he needs to hang on to the ball, and the referee declares that with the cushion rule in effect, Razor is now out. A grinning Razor immediately uses his team's "back" before even leaving the court.

Chapter 166 Face-Off: Part 9 (⑨, "Taiketsu (Kyū)") is the 166th chapter of the Hunter × Hunter manga, written and illustrated by Yoshihiro Togashi. Synopsis. The referee confirms Razor's use of "back" and says that he will remain inside the court. Kess and Rodriot are confident that their team has the advantage now, but Tsezguerra disagrees and says that their team is in worse shape, with Hisoka's throwing hand injured and Gon having used up almost all of his aura. Kess asks if Killua is the only one left who is fine, but Tsezguerra reveals that Killua is actually the one who is the most injured. As Tsezguerra's teammates wonder what he means, sweat pours down Gon's face as he lets out an exhausted sigh. Killua wonders how he's doing, and Gon says that his next strike may be the last one he can do, adding that he will use everything he has left. Killua smiles and tells him to make it a good one, but internally he tries to assure himself that he can bear through one more strike, hiding both his hands in his pockets. Tsezguerra tells his comrades that Killua hasn't been using any Nen to protect his hands when Gon hits the ball, and Kess can't believe it since Gon's strike is like a cannon. Tsezguerra explains that Killua's hands are acting as the cannon's barrel, and if he used aura to protect them, it would slow the strike's momentum. He reveals that both of Killua's hands are most likely in worse condition than Hisoka's right hand, leaving his comrades very worried. He regrets being knocked out early and chides himself for not being on the court with them, confident that he could use his aura on his hands the very moment the ball is struck. As Tsezguerra seems to realize something, Biscuit stands outside the court and asks Hisoka for the ball, saying that she isn't good at throwing but accurately striking Razor's last devil on the foot and taking it out. The ball lands at Razor's feet, and he smiles as he picks it up. Tsezguerra calls a timeout and asks the referee if a player inside the court is allowed to freely step outside. The referee says that they can, but they will then have to stay outside. Tsezguerra takes Gon to the side and says that he can hold the ball for him if he steps outside the court. He explains that Killua won't be able to hold it well enough given how injured his hands are, while he (Tsezguerra) will be able to put aura around his hands quickly enough. He assures Gon that it's the only way to defeat Razor and win, but both Gon and Killua say that it would be copping out. Tsezguerra wonders why they care about that, but he begins to cough with pain, and Killua tells him that he is hurt as well, adding that he shouldn't make it any worse. He assures Tsezguerra that his hands aren't as badly injured as he thinks, but when Tsezguerra tells him to show them, Killua refuses and adamantly repeats that he's fine. Biscuit, however, comes up behind him and pulls his arm back, revealing a severely swollen and bruised right hand. Tsezguerra asks Killua if he can even feel anything except pain, but Killua assures Gon that he can hold the ball one more time. Tsezguerra tries to get Gon to convince Killua otherwise, but Gon reveals that he knew all along about Killua's hands. With Tsezguerra in shock, Gon tells him that he isn't stepping out, apologizing, and saying that only Killua can hold the ball. He explains that he's only able to focus completely on hitting the ball because Killua is the one helping him. Killua gives an embarrassed smile and tells Tsezguerra to go rest. After Tsezguerra wishes them good luck and walks away, Killua reminds Gon that they still need to get the ball back from Razor, but Gon already has something in mind, whispering it to him and Hisoka. Chuckling, Hisoka says that it would be fun and is willing to try it, but Killua is left unsure, telling Gon that he thinks up the weirdest ideas. A smiling Gon tells Killua that he is counting on him, and the referee then resumes the match. Razor suddenly undoes all his conjured devils and takes back all his dispersed aura, with Hisoka saying that they will see his true power now. Gon gives a nervous smile, and Razor holds the ball out in front of him, focusing his aura around it and saying to himself that he didn't think he would have to use a certain move. As he comments that he hasn't felt so good in a long time, he tosses the ball high into the air and the others realize that he's planning to spike it like a volleyball. Kess quickly directs their attention to Gon, Killua, and Hisoka, who are seen crouching together to receive Razor's strike.

Chapter 167 Face-Off: Part 10 (⑩, "Taiketsu (Jū)") is the 167th chapter of the Hunter × Hunter manga, written and illustrated by Yoshihiro Togashi. Synopsis. As Razor leaps into the air and prepares to spike the ball, Kess gets the group's attention and tells them to look at Gon, Killua, and Hisoka, who are shown crouched together waiting to receive the attack. Saying to himself that he knows what the three of them are trying to do, Razor spikes the ball with tremendous force and sends it rocketing toward them. As the ball makes contact, Gon attempts to stop it, Hisoka traps it with his Bungee Gum, and Killua acts as the group's brace, straining hard with his legs. The three struggle to contain the force of the strike, but as the smoke clears and everyone looks on, Gon is seen holding the blood-smeared ball, with the wounds on Hisoka's face opened up and Killua lying on the floor, his hands still visibly injured. Tsezguerra's teammates begin to loudly cheer, and Gon gives them a wave of recognition. Razor is impressed by the group's accomplishment and begins to analyze their strategy internally, admitting that their skills proved more effective than his power and revealing that Killua was the key to their success. He says that Gon put all his aura in his hands to stop the ball's momentum, praising his bravery and focus to take the strike without fear. Next, he says that Hisoka was able to cover the ball with his ability right when it struck, praising his quickness which prevented the ball from bouncing away. Finally, Razor says that Killua acted as a cushion and support by expertly shifting his aura between his body and legs. He explains that too little of the former would have caused the group to be crushed by the ball and too little of the latter would have sent them flying outside the court. He praises Killua's preciseness and says that the margin of error must have been less than 1%, stressing that the shifting of aura is the most important aspect of Nen combat. Biscuit also praises Killua's talent internally, saying that she didn't reach his level until she was in her late 20's. Razor is confident that he could attack the group until they're exhausted, but he worries about the amount of time it would take, deciding instead to defeat the group right after their next attack. He praises the power of Gon's strikes, but remains confident that he can catch the ball without getting knocked out, planning to take the group out one by one. After Gon wipes the sweat and blood off his face, he says to himself that he needs more power, suddenly expanding his Ren even more as it billows around his body. Tsezguerra is frightened by the display of power, and Razor realizes that his last use wasn't his strongest. As Gon gives a sly smile, Razor says to himself that Gon is a monster, adding that Ging can be proud of his son's strength. Gon tells Killua that he plans to go all out, and Killua replies that he would have told him off if he hadn't. Gon begins his chant, and as the others look on with nervous anticipation, he fiercely unleashes his Rock to strike the ball.

Chapter 168 Face-Off: Part 11 (⑪, "Taiketsu (Jū Ichi)") is the 168th chapter of the Hunter × Hunter manga, written and illustrated by Yoshihiro Togashi. Synopsis. As Gon makes contact with the ball, Razor bends his knees and readies himself for the attack, still coming to grips with Gon's power and worried that the force would push him outside the court if he catches the ball. However, he doesn't back down once the ball starts to rocket toward him. As he seems to prepare for another bump, Tsezguerra's teammates see this and confidently say that Hisoka will use his Bungee Gum to snatch the ball out of the air again. Now grinning, Razor receives the strike and, instead of bumping it up into the air, redirects it right back toward Gon, making the others anxious and causing Tsezguerra to yell for Gon to duck since it will still allow him to win. Razor says to himself that Gon won't duck since it isn't the way he wants to win, but Gon suddenly falls down as the ball passes over him. As Gon lies unconscious on the floor, Razor is left stunned and Tsezguerra recognizes that Gon used up all of his aura during the fight, adding that he can be proud of his victory over Razor. However, Hisoka says that it's not over yet, suddenly readying his Bungee Gum. Tsezguerra yells out in confusion over Hisoka's decision, but as the smiling Hisoka says that Gon wanted to defeat Razor completely, he uses his ability to contain the force of Razor's redirect, injuring both his hands to redirect the ball right back. Barry and Rodriot are amazed that Hisoka bounced it back, and Razor is happy to have a volleying contest to see who can last the longest. However, when the ball makes contact with his arms and he prepares to bump it back, the ball immediately sticks there, leaving Razor in disbelief. As Hisoka explains that his Bungee Gum has the properties of both rubber and gum, the force of Hisoka's redirect pushes Razor outside the court, with the ball still stuck to his arms. The others eagerly wait for the call, and the referee announces that since Razor caught the ball while part of his body is touching outside the court, he is now out. As Gon's team is declared the winner of the match, Hisoka sees that both of his hands are busted, a smiling Killua sits on the floor, and Gon regains consciousness, wondering what happened as Tsezguerra's teammates begin to wildly cheer. The ball falls from Razor's arms, and he seems happy that Gon achieved his total victory. Gon learns that Hisoka was the one who sealed the win, but Hisoka says that they all worked together, which they point out seems very out of character for him. With one of his shoes split open, Razor approaches Gon and Killua and says that he and his pirates will leave the town now. Both Gon and Killua forgot that that was the goal of the quest, but before leaving, Razor says that he will answer Gon's questions about Ging, causing Gon's eyes to widen with surprise.

Chapter 169 Declaration of War (, "Sensen Fukoku") is the 169th chapter of the Hunter × Hunter manga, written and illustrated by Yoshihiro Togashi. Synopsis. Gon makes sure that he didn't mishear Razor, who confirms that he will tell Gon about Ging, asking to talk with him in private. Biscuit patches up Killua's injured hands and worries that they may not work right again. She tries to get his attention, but Killua glances over at Gon and Razor in the corner of the gymnasium. Razor starts by revealing that Ging isn't on Greed Island and that he doesn't know where he is. Although he seems disappointed, Gon states that he figured as much. Razor then offers to tell him some old stories, and Gon is eager to hear them. To Gon's shock, Razor reveals that he's also a death row convict and has killed as many people as Bopobo did. He says that Ging caught him and put him in jail, but after his sentence, Ging hired him and brought him to the island. He reflects on Ging's kindness, saying that he taught him that if a single person in the world believes in you, you can be redeemed. A flashback to a younger Ging, who tells Razor that his son will come to Greed Island one day. He orders Razor not to hold back and to use everything he has. The younger Razor chuckles and asks if it's okay to kill him, but Ging smirks and tells him not to underestimate the boy since he's his son. He pats Razor on the shoulder and says that he's counting on him. Back in the present, Razor holds his own hand to his shoulder and says that he thought Ging was crazy for talking about a game for hours and then hiring a convict to fight his son. Razor then remembers when he was a boy himself, with various people talking down to him and calling him everything but his name. He remembers Ging's use of his name and his words of encouragement, saying that he envied Gon. He tells him that it felt like the first time someone had called him by his name before. Finally, he says that he believed in Gon just as Ging had, assuring Gon that he went all out during the match.
