Gon points out that he only won because of the help from his teammates, and Razor praises their teamwork. As he turns to walk away, Razor says that he hopes Gon can see Ging one day, and Gon enthusiastically thanks him. After leaving the gymnasium, the group follows the Plot of Beach NPC to the top of the lighthouse. According to her, the entrance was in front of the pirates all along, and she leads the group to a window through which the shore can be seen. Tsezguerra and Goreinu wonder how they can get to the sea cave from the lighthouse, and the NPC reaches out through the window and pushes in one of the bricks on the wall below. As both Gon and Killua realize that it's a button, a beam of light shoots out from the lighthouse's beacon and hits a particular spot on the ocean. The NPC says that an underwater cave lies right beneath the spot, but then reveals that no treasure is there, apologizing to the group for lying to them. She adds that since the location is sacred, it isn't told to many fishermen, which caused the rumors about treasure to spread. She says that the pirates didn't believe them, wondering if they should have told them about the location (though she knows that they would have thought they were lying). As she continues to stress that the fishermen didn't reveal the location to anyone since they couldn't let the ocean be defiled, Gon listens intently to the woman, but Killua has to remind himself that it's just a story in a game. The NPC is happy to have the view from the window again, taking in the sunrise, the boats, and the light shimmering across the water. After describing it as the greatest treasure, she suddenly transforms into the "Plot of Bleach" card. Gon celebrates and Killua says that they should quickly use "Clone" on it. They give the two copies to Goreinu and Tsezguerra, the latter of whom says that Gon deserves to keep the original. Gon makes sure that Hisoka doesn't want anything before he leaves, but Hisoka assures them that he has had enough fun. Killua asks aloud if he wants to stay with the group, saying to himself that they should keep an eye on him, but Hisoka says that he isn't interested if they are going back to collecting cards. He tells them to use a "Contact" card if they need him, adding that he will use "Accompany" or "Magnetic Force" to reach them. As Hisoka walks down the stairs and vanishes from sight, Killua suddenly realizes that he must have known about spell cards before they met up with him, since they never cast "Magnetic Force" in front of him. Biscuit tells Killua that the two of them are the type of liars who lie for a reason, while Hisoka is the type who doesn't have a reason sometimes, stressing that he shouldn't over-analyze Hisoka's motive. Outside the lighthouse, Goreinu reveals that he has joined Tsezguerra's team, and Tsezguerra asks the three if they want to join as well. He reminds him of the inevitable fight they will have to have with Genthru, stressing that his ability will put them at a severe disadvantage. Once Tsezguerra adds that Genthru must have initially learned Nen to kill people, a player suddenly uses "Contact" on Tsezguerra and asks if he recognizes his voice. Tsezguerra immediately knows that it's Genthru and asks what he wants. Genthru first congratulates them, but when Tsezguerra asks what he's talking about, Genthru tells him not to play dumb, watching the group with a spyglass and saying that he used "List" to confirm that they acquired "Plot of Bleach." He tells them that they can live if they hand over the card, but as Tsezguerra quickly refuses, Genthru hears something off in his voice, asking if he's injured or bluffing. He remains confident in his combat ability and tells Tsezguerra to come alone to the gate at Masadora in one hour if he agrees to the deal. He warns Tsezguerra that they won't be able to run or hide since they have plenty of "Accompany" cards. Tsezguerra is left frustrated and can't believe how fast they learned that his group had acquired the card. Genthru gives six names and asks if they were part of the original group of fifteen, telling the group to check those names in their books. Gon quickly summons his book and sees that the light beside those six and even more are out. Gon yells Genthru's name and Genthru wonders who he is. Gon yells his full name in reply and angrily declares that he will fight Genthru, surprising both Killua and Biscuit. Elsewhere, Phinks contacts Hisoka and says that they found "him," adding that they will fly over right away. Hisoka chuckles as he looks at his opened book.

Chapter 17 Disparate Choice (な2, "Fujiyū na Nitaku") is the 17th chapter of the Hunter × Hunter manga, written and illustrated by Yoshihiro Togashi. Synopsis. With Leorio still angrily holding his collar, Tonpa says that he has no interest in passing the Hunter Exam since he only does it for the thrills. He explains that he watches the dangerous examinees carefully to avoid being taken out, revealing that he finds it entertaining to see people's dreams fall to pieces and that he deliberately trips up rookies to watch them suffer. He reiterates that becoming a Hunter would be pointless and explains that he usually quits the exam at this point since he doesn't want to press his luck when things become more dangerous. With Leorio in disbelief at his explanation, Tonpa adds that he can't quit yet since he's involved in the path of majority rules, asking which of the group wants to fight next. On the other side of the arena inside Trick Tower, the prisoners chuckle at the examinees quarreling with each other and hope that they continue to waste time, revealing that it will shorten their prison terms even more. As one of the Third Phase examiners, Lippo the Blacklist Hunter and prison warden, sits in front of several monitors and eagerly watches all the examinees throughout the tower, it's revealed that the five prisoners are each serving consecutive sentences that total over 100 years and that he has promised to shorten their sentences by one year for every hour that they can delay an examinee. Putting his handcuffs back on, Bendot wishes he could have toyed with Tonpa for longer, and it's revealed that he has a total sentence of 199 years for robbery and murder. Two other prisoners comment on how pitiful Tonpa was, but one of them stresses that they only need two more wins to ensure that the examinees will be stranded there for the rest of the phase, allowing them to remove 72 years from their sentences. Bendot is also confident since two of the examinees are children. The next prisoner asks Lippo to remove his handcuffs before taking off the shroud from his head. After overhearing part of the prisoners' conversation, Kurapika tells the others about the situation and guesses that the reduction of their sentences is based on how long they can delay them, adding that their in-fighting is only helping the prisoners. Killua tells Tonpa that surrendering was actually the smart move since Bendot, who he guesses is ex-military and a mercenary, would have crushed his windpipe and then tortured him for as long as he wanted without killing him. Tonpa chuckles nervously and says that he was aware of that, but Leorio points out that he looks like he's going to be sick. Killua asks which of them wants to go next, and Gon happily volunteers, with the others left surprised by how carefree he is. Killua asks Gon if he's sure and wonders if anything ever fazes him, but Gon points out that the next prisoner doesn't look too tough. Killua gazes at the other side and agrees that he isn't as intimidating as Bendot. After the two make their way to the stone platform, it's revealed that the prisoner's name is Sedokan and that he has a total sentence of 149 years for serial bombing. He comments on his own unassuming appearance and assures Gon that strength and speed are not his forte. Gon replies that he likes them and prefers action over thinking. Sedokan then proposes a simple game and holds out two candles in his hands, explaining that they will each take one, light it, and that the first one to lose their flame will lose the match. Gon likes the game's simplicity and agrees to the challenge. However, Sedokan suddenly reveals that one candle is longer than the other and asks them to vote on which one Gon will use. The group worries that it's a trap since the long candle is the obvious choice, and Kurapika points out that they may have a "disparate choice" on their hands. It's explained that an obvious choice causes people to be suspicious and slows down their decision-making, also affecting them psychologically and making them even more worried about choosing the wrong option. Sedokan calmly sits on the ground and happily tells the examinees to take as much time as they want to discuss their choice. Leorio realizes how well the plan works for the prisoners, but Kurapika gets Gon's attention and tells him to decide, explaining that second-guessing is pointless and that they will follow his instincts. Gon quickly chooses the long candle and happily explains that it will burn longer because of its length. After all five examinees vote for the long candle, Sedokan tosses it to Gon and keeps the short one for himself. The two then use the nearby torches to light their candles at the same time, and the simple game begins. The drafts inside the large room cause Gon's flame to move, and he realizes how close it was to going out, breathing a sigh of relief as he holds his hand near it. With 68 hours and 55 minutes left to reach the bottom of the tower alive, Killua wonders how long the candles will burn, and Kurapika guesses five to six hours. Another draft blows through the room, and Leorio says that the two will need to move as little as possible and watch their flames constantly. Gon's flame suddenly flares up and begins to burn down the candle more quickly. Leorio realizes that an accelerant must have been used and sees that Gon's candle is already down to a stub, guessing that it will only last a few more minutes. Although Leorio believes that Gon made the wrong choice, Sedokan chuckles and says to himself that he actually had four candles, having used the disparate choice to conceal his real trap. He continues to happily detail his plan by saying that he had an oil-soaked version of each length so that it didn't matter which one Gon chose. However, Gon puts on a big smile and sets his candle down on the ground, saying that his flame is so strong that it would take a hurricane to extinguish it. With Sedokan now nervous, Gon suddenly dashes toward him and appears right in front of him. Sedokan is caught completely off guard and left unable to believe how fast he is. Gon then simply blows out Sedokan's candle and happily says that he has won. Kurapika and Killua are left smiling at Gon's quick thinking, and Lippo is impressed by his victory.

Chapter 170 Three-Way Struggle: Part 1 (つの①, "Mitsu Domoe no Kōbō (Ichi)") is the 170th chapter of the Hunter × Hunter manga, written and illustrated by Yoshihiro Togashi. Synopsis. Genthru recognizes Gon's name and says he knows that his group has "Wild Luck Alexandrite." He threatens to kill Gon after Tsezguerra, but asks him if he will hand over his cards now. Gon yells back that he should come to them, threatening to fight him now and almost revealing that he has "Plot of Bleach" as well, but Biscuit holds him back and drowns him out, with Killua telling Tsezguerra to talk somewhere else. However, Tsezguerra tells them that the time limit for "Contact" ran out. Still watching the group from a cliff in the distance, Genthru discusses the situation with Sub and Bara, the latter of whom suggests that they take a copy of "Plot of Beach" from the kids. Genthru points out that it would be a cloned copy, adding that they need to use "Paladin's Necklace" to check if it's fake, which will also change back a cloned card. He is sure that Gon will back down once Tsezguerra surrenders, saying that Gon is only confident because Tsezguerra is protecting him. He tells his two comrades that they can't allow Tsezguerra any time to recover, especially since he's a Single-Star Hunter and they don't know his ability. Back outside the lighthouse, Tsezguerra tells the three that Genthru is assuming that his team will have the original "Plot of Beach," explaining that while Paladin's Necklace reveals faked cards, it ruins actual cards made with "Clone" and "Mimic." He says that they will use Genthru's wrong assumption to their advantage, promising to buy Gon as much time as possible while he heals his injuries. He reminds Gon that a fight is inevitable and that his group has the best chance of defeating Genthru. He then becomes serious and chastises Gon for not controlling his emotions, asking him what would have happened to Killua with his injuries if Genthru's team had met them like he wanted. He also reminds Gon that he used up all his aura and won't be able to move until tomorrow, again stressing that he put not only himself at risk but his friends as well. After an ashamed Gon apologizes, Tsezguerra moves on to the plan and says that they don't want to run away from Genthru's team for too long or they may get suspicious and target Gon instead. He promises to hold off Genthru's team for no longer than a week, and Killua thinks to himself that it won't be enough time, also worried that Genthru's team will come after them before then. Goreinu brings up the subject of joining forces with Tsezguerra's team and again asks the three what they think, but Tsezguerra says that forming an alliance has few benefits now that the situation has changed. He adds that any surprise attacks would be pointless now and that the two remaining cards that Genthru's team needs shouldn't be kept in one group. Tsezguerra then proposes a trade and offers to buy Gon's team three weeks in exchange for "Wild Luck Alexandrite." Killua is confused since one week was the maximum before, but Tsezguerra says that it was the maximum if they were trying to run away, explaining that if they go on the offensive, the risk will increase but Genthru's team will keep their focus on them in a war of attrition. Killua says that they can just tell them how to acquire the card, but Tsezguerra replies that they already know how, explaining that everyone in their group (including Goreinu) has few empty slots, which makes it impossible for them to give all their cards to the villagers. He says that three weeks won't be enough time for Killua's hands to heal or for them to match Genthru's power, and Killua realizes that they need to form a strategy during that time. Tsezguerra confirms this and says that they need to create a situation where they will have the advantage over Genthru's team. Gon agrees to the deal of three weeks, and Tsezguerra reminds him that the Bombers have killed over 50 players, stressing that they have to fight them if they want to clear the game. After Tsezguerra and his team leave, Biscuit knows that the three weeks won't be enough, but she takes charge and tells Killua to focus on healing his hands and puts him in charge of coming up with a strategy. She tells Gon that he will practice with her and stresses that he needs to be able to avoid Genthru's Little Flower at the minimum. Elsewhere, Phinks and Hisoka use "Accompany" to travel to the other Troupe members. Hisoka asks where their friend is, and Shalnark says that Machi and Nobunaga are following him, holding one of Machi's threads and telling him to follow it. Phinks says that the negotiation with the exorcist is up to him, adding that they will pay the exorcist whatever he asks. He tells Hisoka to get the job done, and Hisoka knows that it's his only way to be able to fight Chrollo. Meeting up with Machi and Nobunaga, he uses a spyglass to see the exorcist in disguise at a restaurant. After Hisoka asks how they found him, Nobunaga quickly refuses to tell him, but Hisoka senses something lurking behind him and asks if it was their ability. Nobunaga calls him a freak for sensing the person without using Nen, and a chuckling Hisoka says that a recent fight has left him sensitized, adding that he would be happy to ravage someone to soothe his urge. Machi tells the person to come out, and Kalluto reveals himself, asking if his Zetsu wasn't good enough. They assure him that Hisoka is just abnormal, and Nobunaga introduces Kalluto as Hisoka's replacement in the Troupe. Kalluto says that he used his ability to find the exorcist, but refuses to tell Hisoka how he did it. Hisoka describes him as tasty, and the two other Spiders warn Kalluto that Hisoka will go after anything. Nobunaga bugs Hisoka about making a deal with the exorcist, and Hisoka replies that he will get it done for his own sake. Machi asks him if he really plans to fight Chrollo, and Hisoka asks her who she wants to live. She quickly answers that Hisoka can drop dead after he completes the job, but when he asks her what she will do if he kills Chrollo, a fire ignites in her eyes and she calmly tells him that she will chase him down and kill him herself. In Masadora, Tsezguerra tells his team that since Genthru is monopolizing "Angel's Breath," they need to force him to use one so they can convert their "Voucher" card. He says that the ideal way would be to steal it, but explains that getting it with "Levy" isn't very likely. He adds that other methods are dangerous and have a low chance to succeed. Barry speaks up and says that it's why Gon's team is vital. Tsezguerra is confident that whether Gon's team wins or not, they will surely injure one of the Bombers, forcing them to use just one of their "Angel's Breath" cards to heal their comrade. Tsezguerra says that their "Voucher" will immediately transform into the card, with just "Wild Luck Alexandrite" left. Barry and Rodriot interject, saying that they will get the latter first because they will have bought Gon's team three weeks of time. Kess wonders what the plan will be if Genthru's team doesn't have to use an "Angel's Breath," and Tsezguerra replies that it all depends on the No. 0 event, but he keeps their focus on the mission at hand. He tells them that it's time, and the four original members meet up with the Bombers, standing opposite with all their books open.

Chapter 171 Three-Way Struggle: Part 2 (つの②, "Mitsu Domoe no Kōbō (Ni)") is the 171st chapter of the Hunter × Hunter manga, written and illustrated by Yoshihiro Togashi. Summary. With three cards left to collect (No. 0, "Plot of Beach," and "Wild Luck Alexandrite"), Genthru reminds Tsezguerra that he told him to come alone. With four cards left to collect (No. 0, "Angel's Breath," "Wild Luck Alexandrite," and "Blue Planet"), Tsezguerra replies that his team couldn't agree and were still discussing things, but he suddenly reveals that they have decided to fight. They all pull out cards, and as Tsezguerra leaps far back, Kess, Barry, and Rodriot cast "Levy" before Tsezguerra uses "Accompany" to transport them all back to Masadora. Genthru opens his book and tells Sub and Bara to check their cards. Both confirm that they only got useless cards from their free slots. Genthru says the same, and Sub decides that it's time to take their cards and kill them. Genthru, however, thinks that it will difficult since Tsezguerra seems completely determined now. In a forest, Goreinu meets up with the team and gives them six "Accompany" cards, nine "Drawbridge" cards, two "Magnetic Force" cards, and 24 "Return" cards, saying that he used all the money he had. They tell him that they will see him again in three days and that he should earn money to buy more cards. After Goreinu leaves, they wonder if Genthru will come after them, but Tsezguerra replies that he won't yet since he can easily use "Clairvoyant Snake" to see that they have twice as many as "Accompany" cards. He then confidently says to himself that he will show Genthru what a Single-Star Hunter can do. In the badlands, Gon and Biscuit are seen trading strikes, with Biscuit suddenly grabbing Gon's wrist. Gon uses Gyo around the area, but Biscuit reprimands him for being too slow, telling him that he needs to react once he feels his skin being touched and not to wait for his mind to catch up. Killua watches the two as they train some more, but Biscuit then tells Gon to take a ten-minute break and to prepare for Emission practice. She thinks to herself that while Gon's stamina is good enough, they won't have enough time if they have to focus so much on defensive training. She realizes that they need another weapon in the upcoming fight. Biscuit begins level two Emission training and calls it floating hand, doing a handstand and holding the position. She then emits aura from her palm and propels herself around a foot off the ground. She says that Gon passes when he can reach the same height. Gon gets into position and tries his best, but doesn't move at all. She tells him to keep trying as long as he can maintain the position. As Gon tries over and over again, Biscuit asks Killua about his hands, and he replies that it hurts to move them at all, worried that they aren't getting better. Killua comments on the Emission exercise and says that it seems a lot harder for just being one level up. Biscuit then reveals that it's actually level five Emission training, explaining that if Gon fails to learn it, they will have wasted three weeks, but that going at the normal pace won't be enough to face Genthru. She adds that he needs to be able to push someone back at least 12 feet for the attack to be an effective weapon. Killua mentions that the attack won't be a finishing blow since it's just level five, and Biscuit confirms that it's just meant to give them more options. Killua asks about Biscuit's ability and says that knowing it will make it easier to come up with a strategy. Biscuit suddenly forms a woman out of aura and introduces her as Cookie. Biscuit explains that Cookie's massage techniques melt away fat and make the recipient feel refreshed. She adds that aura can be transmuted into a special lotion that smooths and revitalizes skin. Lastly, she says that Cookie's shiatsu massage improves blood circulation and eases constipation and stiff muscles. Killua is left speechless and asks if that's all her ability does, but Biscuit happily tells him that she also does Swedish and rolling massages (and much more). As the two yell back and forth about whether the ability is useless or the best ever, Gon keeps trying to pass the level five Emission exercise. In a forest, Genthru, Sub, and Bara are seen sleeping up against the trunk of a large tree. As Bara awakens and suddenly senses something, someone throws an arrow right toward Sub, but Bara catches it before it can reach him. The two wonder if it's Tsezguerra's team, and as Genthru tells them not to bother, someone in the distance uses a "Return" card to travel back to Soufrabi. Bara breaks the arrow in half out of anger and says that they are getting bolder since the throw was clearly meant to kill. Sub worries less about that and more about how they keep finding them. He says that they obviously aren't using "Accompany" or "Magnetic Force," and they haven't cast "Trace" on them either. Genthru surmises that someone in their group has an ability that works like radar. Bara and Sub ask him what they should do if there's no way to stop them, and Genthru says that it may be time to use drastic measures.

Chapter 172 Three-Way Struggle: Part 3 (つの③, "Mitsu Domoe no Kōbō (San)") is the 172nd chapter of the Hunter × Hunter manga, written and illustrated by Yoshihiro Togashi. Summary. In Masadora, a player is seen leaving the spell card shop and checking his book, saying that he can't seem to get a "Leave" card. Smiling, the three Bombers approach him, but after some time passes, the player is seen lying bruised and bloody in the forest outside the city. He pleads with them to spare his life and shows him his book after they ask. Bara is happy to see an "Accompany" card, and Genthru tells him to take any C-rank cards as well. Bara and Sub then use "Peek" to check his list of encountered players, learning that he hasn't met "him" and that he's innocent. Genthru asks the player if he has heard of the Bomber, and he says that he's just heard rumors. Genthru reveals that it's the three of them and tells the player that he has set a bomb on his body that he can detonate at any time. He orders the player to bring them one "Magnetic Force" or two "Accompany" cards, and then they will disarm it. After they tell him to use "Contact" once he has the card(s), the player makes his way back to Masadora and the Bombers take another hostage soon after, stealing yet another "Accompany" card. However, when Bara and Sub use "Peek" to check the player's book, they see that he has met Tsezguerra. All three seem upset at first, but they then put on smiles and yell "busted!!" The player wonders what's going on, but an explosion suddenly goes off and Genthru says that all suspects have to be punished. As the player's corpse vanishes and the Bombers make their way back to Masadora, Goreinu watches from the shadows and can't believe their ruthlessness. He contacts Tsezguerra and tells him that the Bombers are waiting around the spell card shop and attacking everyone that buys spell cards. He guesses that Genthru's team has learned that a player is supplying Tsezguerra with spell cards, explaining that the three are checking the books of the players that enter the shop and killing those that have met Tsezguerra in the game. He adds that they are taking cards from the players and, if they don't kill them, forcing them to collect more cards for them. After Goreinu thanks them and says that he would have been caught if they hadn't warned him, Tsezguerra says that they will follow the Bombers' movement, telling Goreinu to keep his distance for now. He addresses Kess with the name "Dopple," and Kess understands the cue, using his Silent Worker ability to locate Genthru and his team. He says that they are staying in Masadora, and after Tsezguerra adds that they need to check their cards, Rodriot uses "Clairvoyant Snake" and feeds a card to it, learning that Genthru's team has 16 "Accompany" cards and two "Magnetic Force" cards. Tsezguerra says that while they have 27 "Accompany" cards and four "Magnetic Force" cards, Genthru's team will catch up in four or five days if they keep attacking other players. Rodriot points out that their own team also has 36 "Return" cards, but Tsezguerra replies that Genthru's team is aware of that. He is confident that things are looking good and says that they need to delay them for twelve more days. In the badlands, Gon is seen still trying the Emission exercise, but he falls back from exhaustion after another failed attempt. He remembers Biscuit's advice to think about it like a water gun and to collect all the aura in his body and push it out from his hand. She had also told him to open the nodes in his hand all at once, stressing that he needs to use power, speed, and timing in unison. As Gon looks at his hand in frustration, Killua along with Biscuit note his lack of progress, with Killua saying that he should have gone step by step since he hasn't improved any in ten days. Biscuit reminds him that they have ten more days left, but Killua replies that it all depends on Tsezguerra, worried that the trade won't be worth it since they still have 30 cards to collect while Tsezguerra's team will only need two (besides No. 0) once they receive No. 75. Biscuit proposes just using force to take the cards from Genthru's team, but Killua is sure that Gon won't agree to it. He focuses their attention on the plan, and as the two gaze up at an enormous rock, Biscuit asks if it will be big enough and Killua confirms it will be. In Battera's Castle, the multi-billionaire is seen alone in his room looking at a television screen and crying. Back in the game, Gon tries his best to make progress in the Emission training, Tsezguerra makes a trade with another player, and Genthru and his team continue their torture of other players, bringing their total number of "Accompany" cards to 48. He tells Bara and Sub that Tsezguerra's team only has 45 equivalents of "Accompany," "Return," and "Magnetic Force," confident that the three of them will easily win the game of tag. As he uses an "Accompany" card to travel to Tsezguerra, Kess gets the group's attention and tells them that Genthru's team is on the move. They all look up toward the sky, and Tsezguerra says that they are already there.

Chapter 173 Three-Way Struggle: Part 4 (つの④, "Mitsu Domoe no Kōbō (Yon)") is the 173rd chapter of the Hunter × Hunter manga, written and illustrated by Yoshihiro Togashi. Summary. As the Bombers arrive, Tsezguerra reminds his team to stick to the plan. Genthru is seen with his book open, and Tsezguerra opens his as well, quickly using "Accompany" to transport his team to Masadora. Genthru follows and uses an "Accompany" on Tsezguerra to chase them. They continue to run away from the Bombers, and after Tsezguerra runs out of "Accompany" cards, Barry uses one to transport the group to Soufrabi. In a forest, the group has seven "Accompany" cards left, and Rodriot says that the Bombers have stopped chasing them, wondering if they gave up. Tsezguerra replies that they changed the pace in order to keep them guessing. Kess tells Rodriot to use "Return" once they run out of "Accompany" cards, and Rodriot adds that they will alternate between Aiai and Soufrabi. Tsezguerra contacts Goreinu and asks how things are going. Goreinu says that Sub and Bara are looking for him (Goreinu) at the spell card shop, with Genthru using two imposters like before. He guesses that the group was betting he would try to use the shop while the two groups were chasing each other. Tsezguerra tells them that they won't fall for the same trick again. The others are eager to make a stand against Genthru since he will be alone, but Tsezguerra remains confident in their plan. With Aiai in the distance, the group hears Genthru traveling to them and prepares to flee again. At the badlands, Gon continues struggling with the Emission exercise, aware that they only have five days left. Killua asks Biscuit if she can give Gon some advice, but she says that it's different for everyone, worried that she may give him preconceptions and confuse him even more. Killua approaches Gon and tells him to stop practicing since his time is up. Gon says that they still have five days, but Killua says that they have created a strategy to beat the Bombers. Gon tries to assure them that he's close to completing the exercise, but they know that he isn't and tell him that they can't use something they can't rely on. Biscuit holds up a card and says that they will use it, with Killua adding that Gon will practice every day to perfect it. The group then sits down together, and Killua explains the plan to Gon. As Tsezguerra's team lands outside Masadora with their last "Accompany" and plans to use "Return," Genthru and the imposters land seconds later. They use their "Return" to travel back to Aiai, and Genthru says that with the group out of "Accompany" cards, they have reached the endgame. He rockets after them and contacts Sub and Bara to ask them if they got any more cards. Sub tells them that word has spread that the Bomber is hunting players around the shop, and so hardly anyone is showing up. He guesses that they already killed the person who was buying cards for Tsezguerra. Genthru says maybe and tells the two to meet him in Soufrabi, revealing that Tsezguerra's team is out of cards and luck. Tsezguerra tells his team that their last option is to use a "Leave" card and confront Genthru's team in the castle if they come after them. He adds that if they stop chasing them, they can just wait until the deadline. Kess and Barry agree to the plan, with the former saying that they should pick the three cards they want as prizes and the latter saying that they should ask Battera which ones he wants. The four hear Genthru approaching and all use "Leave" to exit the game. However, once inside the castle, they find that all the armed guards are gone. Tsezguerra beckons Sabazushi, who comes around a corner and says that he was sleeping. He tells the group that everyone left since Battera cancelled the contract, and while he already received his cancellation fee, he stayed behind to tell them what happened. Tsezguerra is left speechless and heads for Battera's room, banging on the door and demanding to know why he called things off when they were so close to clearing the game. The multi-billionaire mutters that he doesn't care anymore, and Tsezguerra is left confused after all the years of work they put in as a group. Battera says that he will pay them through his lawyer and that they can do whatever they want with the three cards, finally telling them to leave him alone. As Tsezguerra and his team stand confused outside his room, they hear a scream down the hallway and Genthru is seen to have killed Sabazushi with Little Flower, saying that they can kill anyone they want since they won't lose their card data.

Chapter 174 Three-Way Struggle: Part 5 (つの⑤, "Mitsu Domoe no Kōbō (Go)") is the 174th chapter of the Hunter × Hunter manga, written and illustrated by Yoshihiro Togashi. Summary. In the badlands, as Gon maintains his Ren and holds a stopwatch in his hand; Killua and Biscuit look through the list of players and see that Tsezguerra and his team left the game 10 days ago. Biscuit wonders what's going on and says that the three-week deadline passed five days ago. Killua adds that they will lose their card data if they don't return that day, telling Biscuit that they need to wait for Goreinu to contact them. Gon stops the watch and celebrates, saying that he can do it perfectly every time and asking the two if he can go back to the Emission exercise. However, both Killua and Biscuit say that he needs a margin of error less than 0.1 seconds. As a disappointed Gon clicks the stopwatch again, Goreinu uses "Contact" on Killua and apologizes for not getting in touch sooner. Using a telescope in the distance, he reveals that Tsezguerra and the others probably won't be coming back since the Bombers are waiting at the Starting Point. He adds that they won't return unless he sends a messenger to their hideout, and Biscuit points out that Tsezguerra will lose all his card data. Goreinu says that he (Goreinu) has the rare cards, but Biscuit worries that Genthru used "Clairvoyance" to check their cards and saw that they weren't carrying any rare ones. Outside the Starting Point, Sub says that Tsezguerra and his team will lose their card data if they don't return in the next five minutes. Genthru replies that they should wait to make sure that they don't make it back in time, and Bara wonders if the group would really quit. Sub points out that the four have been working together for 20 years, and Genthru notes that they gave up after their ambush plan failed, guessing that they ran away with Battera to keep them from getting the reward money. They say that they used "Clairvoyance" to check their cards and confirmed that they had the 96 among them. Bara wonders why Battera sent the soldiers away, but Genthru says that it would have been more of an issue if Tsezguerra had done so. After he tells the two that they should stop speculating, the five minutes pass and the three celebrate their victory over Tsezguerra. Genthru pulls out an "Accompany" card and tells them that it's time to get "Plot of Beach" from the kids. Sub and Bara agree that they should head to Masadora first to buy more "Accompany" cards, with the three rocketing toward the city soon after. Goreinu reveals to Killua that they used "Fake" on around 30 of the 96 cards and that he is carrying all 96 (as well as "Voucher" and the Blue Planets waiting to be converted). He says that he wants Tsezguerra's gamble to pay off and tells Killua that he won't be able to help them in their fight against Genthru. Killua understands and asks him when he wants to pick up "Wild Luck Alexandrite." Goreinu replies that it can wait until after they beat Genthru, wishing the three of them good luck before suddenly seeing Genthru and his team rocket away from the Starting Point. Goreinu quickly asks Killua where they are, and Killua says that they're near Soufrabi. Goreinu guesses that the Bombers are heading to Masadora to stock up on cards, warning Killua that they will head for them soon and asking if his hands have recovered. Killua replies that they are good thanks to them, but Biscuit says to herself that his hands didn't heal completely and their plan rests upon Gon. She gets Gon's attention and makes sure that he didn't get distracted during the call, asking him about the stopwatch. Gon first looks at the watch with a blank expression, but then turns it toward Killua and Biscuit with a smile on his face, showing the watch stopped at exactly one second. Both put on a smile, and Biscuit lets out a sigh of relief. Meanwhile, inside a hotel in an unknown city, Tsezguerra and the others ask the multi-billionaire why he gave up on clearing the game. Battera remains silent and Tsezguerra shows a photo he found in Battera's room. He wonders if the reason involves the young woman in the photo and asks if she is his daughter or granddaughter. Battera finally speaks and reveals that she was his fiancée, telling them that she was in a coma for a long time. He had hoped that she would wake up, but he painfully says that she passed away last month. Tsezguerra and his men listen intently, and Battera says that because she didn't want others to think she was after his money, she didn't want any expensive gifts (preferring things like the picture frame that Battera made himself). Battera says that they were perfectly happy with just one another and that they had decided to give away all his wealth and get married, but she was in an accident that caused the coma. As he begins to weep, he says it looked like she was sleeping and that all the best doctors could do nothing but keep her on life support. With tears streaming down his face, he says that he heard about Greed Island one day and learned that he could acquire spells to heal and pills to make one young again if he could clear the game. He finally adds that he used his money and influence to keep details about the game a secret from the world, but he tells them that it's over since none of it matters anymore.

Chapter 175 Three-Way Struggle: Part 6 (つの⑥, "Mitsu Domoe no Kōbō (Roku)") is the 175th chapter of the Hunter × Hunter manga, written and illustrated by Yoshihiro Togashi. Summary. The Bombers check Gon, Killua, and Biscuit's cards, learning that they have three "Accompany" cards and each has one "Return" card. Genthru says that while the three kids have four options to escape, their group has six to chase them, and he asks Sub and Bara if they are ready to go. He adds that he will fight the one with black hair if force is needed, telling Sub to take the white-haired kid and Bara to fight the girl. He then uses "Accompany" on Gon, and the three rocket toward Gon's location in the badlands. Standing opposite them, Gon, Killua, and Biscuit all look nervous and on edge, while the Bombers appear calm and confident. Gon asks them what they want, and Genthru replies that they have only come to negotiate. As Killua refuses to do so, Biscuit says to herself that they can't show any sign that they are completely prepared. Genthru tries his best to negotiate and says that even Tsezguerra agreed to the deal. He asks to move closer, but Gon yells at him to speak from where he is, with Biscuit internally praising Gon and saying that they need to appear scared and ignorant. She also says to herself that they need to make it seem like they arrived at a certain location after being chased there. Genthru says that he and his team will clear the game and then split the reward with them after returning to Battera. Killua replies that he can't trust him after all his threats, but Genthru assures him that they have changed, adding that Tsezguerra has returned to the real world already. Killua says that they already know and that it doesn't prove that they made a deal with him. Genthru suddenly becomes serious, pushing up his glasses and asking them if they want to die where they stand. He threatens to kill them if they don't hand over their cards, but they quickly back away and Gon uses "Accompany" to escape to Soufrabi. Genthru chuckles and says that with no "Magnetic Force" or "Leave" cards, Gon's group only has two "Accompany" cards left. The Bombers chase after them and force them to use the two remaining cards, with Gon, Killua, and Biscuit each using their "Return" card to head back to Masadora. Bara wonders if they plan to get more spell cards, but Genthru is confident that they are heading west and plan to leave through the harbor. He uses "Accompany" to chase after them, but when they land outside Masadora, they don't see the three of them anywhere. Genthru guesses that they are hiding and says that he didn't think of that. Gon, Killua, and Biscuit watch the Bombers from the dense forest, and Genthru says that they need to keep an eye on the shop to make sure Gon's group doesn't get any cards. As the Bombers stake out the shop and don't see any sign of the three, Genthru says that they must have headed west, but Bara adds that they could still be hiding. After Genthru uses another "Accompany" on Gon, the Bombers chase after the three, and Genthru tells Sub and Bara not to lose them since that "Accompany" card was their last one. Gon, Killua, and Biscuit lead them deeper into the forest, with Sub and Bara impressed by their speed. As they wonder how long they can maintain it, all three suddenly stop in their tracks and confront the Bombers. Genthru playfully asks if it's over and again orders them to hand over their cards. Gon refuses to give in, and Biscuit says to herself that as they expected, the Bombers want to have one-on-one fights. Gon adds that he would fight before handing his cards over to them, and Killua tries to stop him aloud, but says to himself that now they need to separate the three of them. As Killua begins to move and Sub mirrors him, Killua aims a kick toward his head, but Sub blocks it with his arm and punches him back. Killua says to himself that while he can't use his hands, they won't hinder him. Biscuit watches the two fighting, and Killua dramatically tells her to run away and save herself, with Bara running after her and yelling that she won't get away. Gon internally wishes the two of them good luck, but as he turns his attention back to Genthru, the Bomber quickly reaches out his hand to attack him.

Chapter 176 Three-Way Struggle: Part 7 (つの⑦, "Mitsu Domoe no Kōbō (Nana)") is the 176th chapter of the Hunter × Hunter manga, written and illustrated by Yoshihiro Togashi. Summary. As Genthru moves in close to strike, Gon deflects his arm with his left hand and quickly jumps back as Genthru prepares to use Little Flower with his other hand. While Genthru thinks to himself that Gon is quick on his feet, he asks aloud if Gon already knows that he is the Bomber. After an anxious Gon says that Tsezguerra told him, Genthru becomes serious and asks who told him about his ability. A shiver runs down Gon's spine, and he can't believe how quickly Genthru figured out that he knew, recognizing his much more experience. Genthru warns Gon that few who have learned about his ability have lived to tell anyone about it. However, Gon stays calm and opens his book, reminding himself to not allow Genthru to control the situation. He tells Genthru that he hates people taking cards by force and sternly orders him to promise that the one who surrenders first hands over all his cards. Genthru replies that Gon shouldn't be making demands in his position, but Gon angrily says that without a deal, he won't open his book again even if it results in his death. After calling Gon crazy like himself, Genthru agrees to the deal and opens his own book, saying that he has 131 cards and 97 unique specified slot cards. Gon says that he has 102 cards and 71 unique specified slot cards, and Genthru confirms that Gon is carrying both "Plot of Beach" and "Wild Luck Alexandrite." Satisfied with the arrangement, Genthru readies for battle again and Gon charges up his Ren opposite him. Genthru says to himself that while Gon's Ren is good, he has a long way to go, charging up his own Ren in reply. Gon is taken aback at first but quickly refocuses, suddenly charging toward Genthru and remembering Biscuit's advice. She had told him that offense is the best defense and that if he uses 90% of his aura in his fists, they will receive minimal damage from Genthru's Little Flower. As Gon also remembers her advice to not be afraid to attack, he throws a punch and a kick but Genthru easily dodges both. He quickly regroups and throws another kick down on Genthru, who blocks the strike with both arms. Genthru internally praises Gon's cleverness but describes the control of his aura flow as basic and unable to match the speed of his attacks. He also says to himself that Gon has no actual combat experience, but Gon remembers more of Biscuit's advice, with her saying that Genthru has considerably more aura and experience than him. She had added that while he won't be able to hurt Genthru much, he should keep attacking anyway. Gon charges toward the Bomber again and slides down before charging back up to throw another punch, but Genthru easily anticipates it and strikes him in the face with a hard right. Sent flying far back, Gon coughs up blood on the ground and Genthru again asks who told him about his ability. He quickly changes his mind and says that the answer doesn't matter since he won't even have to use his ability against someone like him. As Gon continues coughing up blood, he says to himself that things are going according to plan, remembering Biscuit's words that he needs to seem as weak as possible so that he can lead Genthru into the trap. However, Gon clenches his fist in anger and turns to fight Genthru again, saying to himself that he hates being on the losing end and adding that the plan can wait until he makes Genthru use his ability. Genthru smirks and says that Gon looks like he wants to feel more pain. He quickly throws a hard kick, and even though Gon blocks it with both arms, he is left stunned by the strike and Genthru follows up with a strong punch to his midsection, causing him to cough up even more blood.

Chapter 177 Three-Way Struggle: Part 8 (つの⑧, "Mitsu Domoe no Kōbō (Hachi)") is the 177th chapter of the Hunter × Hunter manga, written and illustrated by Yoshihiro Togashi. Summary. After punching Gon hard in the stomach, Genthru quickly follows up with a punch to his face and then kicks him far back, causing Gon to cough up blood once again. However, Gon quickly gets to his feet and prepares to fight, angrily saying to himself that he will show something after Genthru tries him. Genthru, however, seems to know what Gon is thinking and internally declares that he won't use his Little Flower ability, suddenly dashing toward Gon and missing a strike with his right leg but making contact with his left. Gon is able to block the attack but is sent back, quickly recovering and ready for the next strike. Genthru seems to become more aggravated and follows up with a hard left punch to Gon's face. Elsewhere in the forest, as Biscuit continues running away from Bara, he says that she is faster than he thought, but he remains confident that he will catch up to her eventually. Biscuit suddenly opens her book, and Bara is confused since she doesn't have any more transport spells. Biscuit takes out a card and it transforms once she touches it, with Bara realizing that she has a Paladin's Necklace. Biscuit then uses the "Accompany" card to transport the two of them to Soufrabi, and Bara is left even more confused, asking himself why she would use that card. After the two land on a beach beside the city, Biscuit puts away her book and Bara says that she didn't even have an ambush ready, wondering why she took all those steps to be alone with him. Biscuit simply replies that it keeps him from asking his friends for help. Bara still doesn't understand her reasoning, but as Biscuit tells him that it means she is far superior to him, she suddenly vanishes and appears behind him, kicking him hard in the back of his head. With Bara now stunned, she follows up with a punch and drives his face into the sand. Bara quickly rises to his feet to attack, but Biscuit counters with a kick to his face and follows up with a strike to his throat, a kick to his midsection, and a punch to his face. As blood flies all around him, Bara begins to laugh and says that her attacks only tickle, adding that a little girl like her has no chance of beating him. Biscuit recognizes his strength and charges toward him, but Bara easily knocks her to the ground, saying that he won't go easy on her. As her body begins to increase in size, Biscuit chuckles and replies that that's her line, telling Bara that she usually lets her opponents get one hit in since she ends up killing them with her unrestrained punches. At that moment, a large fist punches Bara directly in his face and sends him high up into the air before he crashes back down. Bara struggles to breathe as he coughs up blood, and Biscuit is surprised that he's still alive. Bara pitifully asks her why she would hide her true strength, and Biscuit first says that one should never show their hand, adding that she hates how muscular she is. She tries to ask Bara if he agrees, but as she picks him up, she sees that he passed out. Elsewhere, Killua and Sub are seen crouching opposite each other as they prepare to fight.

Chapter 178 Three-Way Struggle: Part 9 (つの⑨, "Mitsu Domoe no Kōbō (Kyū)") is the 178th chapter of the Hunter × Hunter manga, written and illustrated by Yoshihiro Togashi. Summary. Sub chases after Killua and wonders why he used an "Accompany" card to leave his comrades, but tells himself that he is completely fine with a one-on-one fight. Killua says to himself that while he has the advantage in physical strength, Sub has much more aura. He adds that the latter is vital to both offense and defense, which means he won't be able to hurt Sub directly. As Killua then plans to test something, Sub unleashes a strong punch and Killua barely dodges it, receiving a scratch on his cheek and realizing that taking a direct strike would be bad. Sub follows up with a kick and another punch, with Killua blocking the latter with his left elbow. He says to himself that while his elbow hurts, the pain to his hands feels like a knife to his brain. Understanding that he can't waste time, he uses "Rhythm Echo" and confuses Sub, who attacks the wrong Killua and leaves himself wide open. Killua seizes his chance and carries out his first experiment, striking Sub's midsection with Lightning Palm and sending a shock throughout his body. Sent back by the attack, a confused Sub asks if he was hiding a stun gun, and Killua says to himself that while the technique won't knock him out, it will leave him stunned for a few seconds. He then prepares to test his second experiment, pulling out a yo-yo and asking Sub if he's ready. Sub is confused at first, but says to himself that it must be rigged. Killua swings it fast toward Sub's head and he easily dodges it, with the yo-yo slamming into a nearby tree and doing enough damage to make it fall. Sub can't believe the yo-yo's power and asks what it's made of. Swinging the yo-yo around himself, Killua replies that it's a custom alloy from his brother, adding that it weighs around 50 kilograms. He suddenly slings it toward Sub, who dodges the initial attack but is hit in the face after Killua redirects it. Resting on one knee, Sub realizes that he won't be able to block the yo-yo's power and points out that Killua has (what Sub thinks to be) a stun gun for close range and the yo-yo for long range. He picks up a small rock and conceals it in his hand, saying that he has to get rid of the yo-yo first. He also tells himself that he needs to exploit Killua's weakness of leaving his right side exposed, which he will do once his yo-yo is gone. As Killua swings the yo-yo low toward the ground, Sub jumps up into the air to dodge the attack and quickly hurls the stone toward Killua's shoulder, causing the harness attached to the yo-yo to fly off his arm. Sub seizes his chance after landing and dashes toward Killua, throwing a hard right hook that Killua blocks with his left elbow. He spots the exposed right side and unleashes a hard kick there, causing Killua to grimace in pain. However, as Sub says that Killua probably broke a few ribs, another yo-yo strikes him in the back of his head as Killua is seen swinging it around another nearby tree. Killua then playfully asks if he forgot to mention that he has two yo-yos, surprised to see that Sub is still conscious after the strike. With his vision blurred, Sub looks up at Killua and asks if he had everything planned out. Killua replies that when Sub kicks, his opposite arm moves up and exposes his own blind spot. He reveals that his habit was a fake-out to get Sub to kick him, that he let go of his first yo-yo because he knew Sub was going to throw something, and that he used "Accompany" because he knew Sub would focus too much on the one-on-one aspect and not pay enough attention to their surroundings. Sub can't believe that Killua was able to set up three traps so quickly, but as Killua replies that the whole thing was a trap, he raises both his yo-yos into the air and slams them down onto Sub's head, sending electricity through them to shock his entire body. With multiple bumps on his head, Sub sits unconscious and tied up by one of the yo-yos as Killua toys around with the other, happily saying that they both worked. Back in the forest, Gon staggers to his feet once again and Genthru asks him why he doesn't just give up since he doesn't stand a chance. With his left eye swelling shut, Gon says that he isn't done yet as he stands ready to fight. The two glare at each other, and Genthru tells Gon that he takes back what he said, acknowledging his strength and agreeing to show him his ability. He also says to himself that he misjudged the fight and wrongly thought it was a physical one, concluding that he has to break Gon's spirit.

Chapter 179 Three-Way Struggle: Part 10 (つの⑩, "Mitsu Domoe no Kōbō (Jū)") is the 179th chapter of the Hunter × Hunter manga, written and illustrated by Yoshihiro Togashi. Summary. Genthru repeats to himself that he has to break Gon's spirit so he doesn't have the will to fight anymore. As the two stand opposite each other in the forest, Genthru knows that Gon won't admit defeat otherwise and says to himself that he will show him how meaningless effort and confidence are. He suddenly charges toward Gon and takes him off guard, grabbing his right wrist and using Little Flower to cause an explosion. Gon is unable to deflect the strike, but when the smoke clears, Gon smiles and his wrist is only slightly burned by the attack. Genthru realizes that Gon used Gyo to increase his defenses around the area right when he grabbed it, guessing that Gon has practiced it multiple times since his aura seems smoother. Now irritated, Genthru makes another charge and says to himself that Gon shouldn't assume that his plan will work. He throws a flurry of punches and grabs Gon's wrist again, but instead of using Little Flower, he uses his other hand to punch Gon hard in the midsection. As Gon screams out and doubles over in pain, Genthru reminds him that using Gyo on his wrist leaves the rest of his body defenseless, telling him that all his practice backfired. However, Gon rises to his feet and begins to chuckle, saying to himself that things are happening just as Biscuit said they would. Genthru becomes even more irritated and says that he will wipe the smile off Gon's face, charging toward him and throwing another flurry of punches. He grabs Gon's left wrist as if he's going to use Little Flower, but again punches Gon in the midsection. This time, however, Gon seems much less affected by the strike and throws a punch back, which a confused Genthru dodges. He wonders how Gon was able to fight back when the second punch to his midsection was harder than the first. He realizes that Gon didn't use Gyo on his wrist but used his normal defenses, asking himself if Gon just guessed correctly. When he sees Gon's determined face, he knows that Gon knew exactly what he was doing. Gon then thinks back to his training with Biscuit in the badlands before the fight, asking her how Genthru doesn't burn himself with his own explosions. She replies that he envelops his hand in more aura than he uses for the explosion. As Killua bounces his yo-yo on his foot, Gon clarifies by asking if Genthru causes the explosion after he uses Gyo on his hands. Biscuit confirms this and says that he must have a considerable amount of aura to make it work. She uses the opportunity to practice with Gon, suddenly grabbing his wrist and causing him to use Gyo once she does. She praises his reaction time and repeats the exercise, but Gon notices that Biscuit used less aura the second time. Biscuit praises him again and says that the fight will be easier if he can tell the difference. Gon wonders what she means, and Biscuit explains that Genthru uses Gyo on his hands when he activates Little Flower, but he aims elsewhere and doesn't use Gyo when he's only pretending to activate the ability. She says that if he can tell whether Genthru is protecting his hand with Gyo or not, he will be able to block and counter some of Genthru's attacks. Back in the present, Genthru internally wonders if his own Gyo is the key to Gon's plan, recognizing that he doesn't use it if he doesn't plan to activate Little Flower. He stares menacingly at Gon and says that he will fight using Gyo on both hands from now on, suddenly enveloping both his hands in aura. He again tells Gon that his rushed strategy will backfire, saying that if he uses Little Flower on a body with insufficient defenses, the target's face will be blown off, the skin on their limbs will be burned off and the nerves and muscles damaged. He adds that the explosion will blow off fingers and that normal punches will damage bones and organs, with a strike to the head dealing brain damage. He assures Gon that it's impossible for him to use Gyo to defend against all his Gyo attacks, giving him the opportunity to surrender and saying that he has talent and potential. As Genthru asks Gon if it's worth throwing those away for his pride, he internally calls Gon a maggot and tells him to give up. Gon remembers Biscuit's words about following the plan once Genthru starts to use Little Flower with both hands, but Gon apologizes to her and says that while it may be selfish, he has to improvise and follow his gut after coming up with a great idea. He readies to fight and in turn orders Genthru to surrender. Genthru sighs and guesses that Gon believes that he won't kill him since he needs the cards in his book. However, he says that he plans to teach Gon that there are fates worse than death, telling him that he will blow up both his arms with Little Flower. He tells him to protect with Gyo the one he wants to keep, adding that he will then blow up that remaining arm and his left leg. He adds that the same process will follow until only Gon's head is left. As Gon angrily dares Genthru to try it, the Bomber quickly leaps toward him with both hands outstretched.

Chapter 18 The Two Aces in the Hole (つのり, "Futatsu no Kirifuda") is the 18th chapter of the Hunter × Hunter manga, written and illustrated by Yoshihiro Togashi. Synopsis. Leorio celebrates Gon's victory over Sedokan, adding that he and Kurapika will beat the next two prisoners to win the contest. Another prisoner calls Sedokan an idiot for using trick candles and tells him to watch what proper deception looks like as he prepares to face Kurapika. With both on the stone platform, the prisoner's handcuffs fall to the floor as he removes the shroud to reveal a strange-looking face and a well-muscled physique. Leorio is taken aback by his appearance while Kurapika's face doesn't change. The prisoner points to the 19 small hearts tattooed on his chest and explains that it's the number of people he has killed so far, happily adding that he wants to get it to an even number. As Leorio can't believe that they have to deal with serial killers now, the prisoner continues by saying that he kills violently and enjoys mayhem with blood and guts. Kurapika is unfazed by his words and simply says that he will accept whatever contest he chooses. Disappointed that Kurapika didn't react to his facade, the prisoner proposes a fight to the death, but warns him that even admitting defeat won't necessarily stop his killing intent. After Kurapika removes his tabard and calmly asks if he wants to start, the prisoner is left in disbelief by Kurapika's composure and makes sure to point out that no weapons are allowed. Kurapika tosses aside his and asks again if he wants to start the match. The prisoner begins to anxiously analyze Kurapika and wonders how strong he really is, guessing that he's either putting on an act or too stupid to be frightened by his appearance. He then tells himself that it doesn't matter since he has his two secret weapons: his right hand and his back. While Leorio worries about the prisoner, Killua tells himself that it's obvious he's a fraud and hasn't killed anyone before. As the match begins, Gon says that they don't need to worry since he isn't sensing any danger from the prisoner, leaving Leorio confused and causing Killua to give a slight smile.The prisoner prepares to use his big bluff and suddenly leaps high into the air, clenching his right fist and punching the ground near Kurapika. Rubble flies all around the platform, and Leorio can't believe that the prisoner punched the stone floor with his bare fist. Kurapika appears shocked, and it's then shown that the prisoner has a large spider tattoo on his back. Leorio seems to recognize the significance of the 12-legged spider, but Gon is left confused. The prisoner chuckles and says to himself that every aspiring Hunter will recognize the tattoo as the mark of the infamous band of thieves known as the Phantom Troupe. Leorio explains the meaning to Gon and adds that Kurapika told him about some of the more obscure details. The prisoner revels in his two secret weapons—steel knuckles embedded in his right hand and the Troupe tattoo—and adds that they destroy the morale of the toughest fighters. The prisoner guesses that Kurapika is frozen with fear and reveals that his name is Majtani, adding that he is one of the four devas of the Troupe. Although Majtani assures him that he can still surrender and live, Kurapika's expression and changed eyes make him nervous, leaving him speechless before he wonders what's wrong with him. Kurapika suddenly disappears right in front of Majtani and then grabs him by the face. Majtani desperately tells him to wait, but before he can finish his explanation, Kurapika punches his face into the ground and leaves the other examinees shocked by his strength. He then tells Majtani to remember three things well: a genuine Troupe tattoo has the member's number on it, Troupe members don't keep track of how many people they have killed, and he will kill him if he ever mentions the Troupe again. Kurapika puts his tabard back on and calmly leaves the stone platform, with Leorio asking if he's okay. Kurapika replies that he isn't hurt, but Leorio wonders if they should stay away from him. Kurapika assures him that he has nothing to fear as long as he doesn't attempt such a scam, revealing that while he knew the tattoo was fake, his emotions took over and caused him to see all red. He then reveals that he becomes completely irrational and primal when he sees any kind of spider, surprising both Gon and Leorio. Kurapika sits down and chuckles, happily assuring himself that it means the rage inside him still hasn't faded. Gon whispers to Leorio that they need to remember that Kurapika and spiders don't go together. As Majtani lies unconscious on the ground, it's stated that his total sentence is 108 years for fraud and blackmail convictions, with the added note that his face appears scarred because of failed plastic surgeries. The other prisoners can't believe how useless Majtani is, and Bendot reminds them that they have now lost two in a row. The next prisoner is aware of the score and prepares to beat Leorio, who plans to win the contest for the group.

Chapter 180 Three-Way Struggle: Part 11 (つの⑪, "Mitsu Domoe no Kōbō (Jū Ichi)") is the 180th chapter of the Hunter × Hunter manga, written and illustrated by Yoshihiro Togashi. Summary. Genthru grabs Gon's wrists and uses Little Flower to detonate an explosion on both of them, but he suddenly stumbles back, and his vision becomes blurred. He notices blood on the ground and wonders if it's his, panicking and asking himself if he was attacked. He looks up at Gon, who begins charging up a Rock as the smoke clears. Genthru is taken aback by the spike in aura and tries to move his legs to get out of the way. Genthru luckily trips and falls as Gon throws his punch to avoid the strike. He realizes his luck and wonders how things happened the way they did. He hears Gon struggling and sees that he sacrificed both arms, his right severely damaged around the wrist and his left completely missing below the wrist. Bleeding from his mouth, Genthru rises to his feet and realizes that Gon didn't use any aura on his left arm and only used 30% on his right so he could put the remaining 70% in his foot to kick him in the jaw. He tells himself that Gon exploited the fact that his body was defenseless since he had to set off two explosions and protect both his hands, but he can't believe that someone was crazy enough to try it. Gon tells himself that he got Genthru good, grimacing from the pain in his right wrist, but clenches his fist and says that he can still move it. He begins to chuckle and says aloud that it's enough, with Genthru asking himself if the boy is giving up. He hopes that Gon has satisfied his pride, but Gon tells him that they are at the good part as he prepares to continue the fight and orders Genthru to continue. Genthru totters back and realizes how crazy Gon is, but Gon suddenly opens his book and takes out a single card. Genthru assures himself that they checked all their cards with "Clairvoyance" and that the six "Clone" cards don't matter now. The card reverts to another in Gon's hand, and Genthru realizes that the Paladin's Necklace is involved in his plan. Gon gives him one last chance to surrender, warning him that he could die if he doesn't. Genthru first says to himself that Gon is bluffing, but he realizes that he can seize his chance since Gon's book won't close until he says "book" again. He plans to crush his throat, knock him unconscious, and then take all his cards. To Gon's surprise, Genthru opens his book and seems to admit defeat, saying that he can't make Gon surrender. He first tells Gon to take his cards, but asks to let him keep a particular one, pointing to it in his book. As Gon moves in closer to look, Genthru quickly jabs Gon's throat and causes him to cough up blood, then striking him in the back of his neck. He realizes that Gon protected his neck, but remains confident since Gon can no longer say "book" or "gain" with his damaged throat. Gon, however, says to himself that Genthru made a big mistake and crossed the line, adding that the one minute is up. The card Gon had taken out of his book transforms back into the item, a glass container full of liquid, and Gon punches it to cover Genthru in the substance. Genthru immediately recognizes the smell of gasoline, and after grimacing in pain, Gon tells Genthru that he can no longer use Little Flower, angrily swearing that he will kick his ass.

Chapter 181 Three-Way Struggle: Part 12 (つの⑫, "Mitsu Domoe no Kōbō (Jū Ni)") is the 181st chapter of the Hunter × Hunter manga, written and illustrated by Yoshihiro Togashi. Summary. Genthru puts away his book and praises Gon's plan involving gasoline, admitting that he can no longer use Little Flower. However, he reveals that he has another ability that allows him to place a bomb on his target's body by saying "the Bomber" and touching them. He further explains the ability to Gon and says that it's ten times stronger than Little Flower, assuring Gon that his Nen won't be able to protect him. As Gon continues to listen, Genthru adds that he has to explain the rules to his target if he wants to activate the ability. He finally says that he's ready and reminds Gon that all he has to do is touch him and say the keyword, which will cause the bomb to start counting down. As Genthru tells Gon to run if he can, Gon struggles to talk but begins charging up Rock, saying to himself that he's the one who's ready. Genthru is again taken aback by the spike in aura and wonders if Gon is using it to keep him at a distance. Gon finishes his chant and unleashes the strike right toward the ground, causing a massive pit to form as the two fall to the bottom. Genthru looks up and sees that it's too high to climb out, but assures himself that Gon can't either and wonders if Gon is the one in more trouble. After Genthru looks back down and sees that Gon is missing, Gon calls his name and is seen standing inside a tunnel in the side of the pit. He throws a card up into the air and says "one minute" before disappearing into the tunnel. The card suddenly reverts to an enormous rock that begins falling toward Genthru, who looks up in disbelief and quickly hurries into the tunnel. As Genthru tries to catch his breath, Gon stands in front of him and begins charging up Rock. Although Genthru desperately says that he surrenders, Gon unleashes the attack right into his midsection. Genthru coughs up a considerable amount of blood and falls unconscious, with Gon catching his breath and yelling out "osu" after his victory. Gon drags the unconscious Genthru out through the tunnel and uses "Contact" on Killua, telling him that he had to sacrifice his left hand. Killua says that he can't understand what he's saying, and Biscuit guesses that Genthru crushed his throat. Tied up along with Sub and Bara, Genthru wakes up and is ordered to give back all the cards he stole. He agrees to do so on the condition that they use "Angel's Breath" to heal Bara, adding that he has a "Clone" card. Killua tells him that that was their plan from the start, and Biscuit adds that they prepared six "Clone" cards for all of them. Genthru doesn't say anything in reply and opens his book.

Chapter 182 Three-Way Struggle: Part 13 (つの⑬, "Mitsu Domoe no Kōbō (Jū San)") is the 182nd chapter of the Hunter × Hunter manga, written and illustrated by Yoshihiro Togashi. Summary. Biscuit activates "Angel's Breath" and the summoned angel asks what they wish from her. Killua speaks up and first asks if she can heal Gon's hands and throat, but then tells her just to fix all his injuries. The angel replies that it can easily be done, sending magical dust all around Gon and instantly healing him. As the angel says goodbye and vanishes, Gon celebrates and Biscuit gives him the other duplicate card. After Gon activates it and has the angel heal Bara, Genthru makes sure that he's okay. Biscuit tells Killua that he will be healed next and says to Genthru that she will use his book. With "Angel's Breath" as the only card in his book, Biscuit uses "Clone" on Genthru, but it's announced that "Angel's Breath" is maxed out and that the "Clone" card will be destroyed. As the card vanishes in her hand, Biscuit panics and tells Killua that she did everything exactly as he said, asking him if it's her fault. Killua replies that Goreinu must have duplicated his "Voucher" with "Clone" or "Mimic," which caused both "Voucher" cards to turn into "Angel's Breath" cards once they used them. Just then, Goreinu uses "Contact" on Gon and recognizes that they beat the three Bombers. Killua asks if he was watching them, and Goreinu replies that he has been checking their cards. Gon asks if he wants to meet them, and Goreinu replies that that was his plan, adding that he only has a "Return" card and asking them what the closest town is. After meeting up with them, Goreinu stands over the Bombers and wonders why Gon's group wants to waste an "Angel's Breath" on them. Genthru continues to cough from his injuries, and Goreinu reminds Gon's team that many players have died at the Bombers' hands. He tells them that he won't trade if they plan to use the card on them, but Killua asks if he would use it on him. Goreinu says that of course he would, even offering to give the card to him for free. Killua then asks Goreinu if he would hand over card even after learning that he has killed more people than the Bombers. He continues by saying that while everyone comes to Greed Island prepared to risk their lives (though it doesn't make murder okay), he never allowed the people he killed to make that choice. He asks if that makes him worse, but Goreinu assures Killua that he isn't like the Bombers. The two go back and forth, and Biscuit jumps in to say that she wouldn't let them die just because she doesn't like them. Goreinu tries to clarify what he means, but Biscuit then stresses that while a duel is life or death, things change once the fight is over. Gon adds that he won't forgive them for killing so many players, but tells Goreinu that the three of them decided before the battle to have six "Clone" cards ready. He says that he doesn't remember how they reached that decision, but they all agreed to use "Angel's Breath" on anyone that got injured. He tells Goreinu that he can understand his feelings, but he refuses to break the agreement they made. As Gon apologizes to Killua and asks if he can wait, Killua says that he is completely fine with having his hands heal on their own. Gon then apologizes to Genthru and says that since they can't use "Clone" anymore, there is only one "Angel's Breath" left. Goreinu can't believe that they plan to use their original copy, and Sub tells them to use it on Genthru, saying that he doesn't even feel nauseous or dizzy. As Genthru lies in shock beside him, Sub adds that his only injury is a big bump on his head. Gon activates the card and asks the angel to heal Genthru, with Goreinu left stunned by Gon's decision. As the three prepare to head to Masadora, Goreinu quickly tells them to wait and declares that they can have his "Angel's Breath" card. Gon asks him if he's sure, and Goreinu replies that he planned to give it to them even before he arrived. He then tells the group that he plans to give them all the cards—a decision that Tsezguerra and the others agreed to after quitting the game. As Killua looks at his hands healed by "Angel's Breath," Gon realizes that Battera called off the arrangement, and Goreinu says that he plans to pay out 70% of the reward money since he breached the contract. He tells them that he was able to get four billion, even though he tried to get more, and Biscuit orders him to share some of it. Goreinu says that the four of them are obviously splitting it, with each getting one billion. The three are left speechless, and Goreinu says that it was only by teaming up with them that he was able to earn it. As Biscuit begins to sob and praise Goreinu, Gon and Killua say that they really didn't do much to deserve it. Biscuit yells at the two and says that they would be crazy to refuse their shares, offering to take them if they won't. After Goreinu says that they can decide how to split their three billion among themselves, he tells them that he will give them all the cards he has as long as they make sure to clear the game. Gon and Killua both agree, and Goreinu says that they will now have 99 specified slot cards, with only No. 000 left. He wonders what will happen when someone gets 99 cards and tells them that every player is eager to find out. Gon puts one card at a time into his book and after inserting the last card ("Panda Maid"), Eta makes an announcement to all the players on the island, telling them that someone has collected 99 specified slot cards. She says that a quiz contest consisting of 100 questions about the cards will be held in ten minutes, revealing that the player with the most correct answers will receive the final card, "Ruler's Blessing." As the players are told to wait with their books open, Killua guesses that the questions are about the specified slot cards in order to prevent players who took cards by force from being able to answer them correctly. He also guesses that they can answer 70-80% correctly, giving them the best chance among all the players since Tsezguerra is no longer in the game. Gon suddenly senses something, and they all see someone rocketing toward them. As they spot several more in the sky, the players land all around and have them surrounded.

Chapter 183 Three-Way Struggle: Part 14 (つの⑭, "Mitsu Domoe no Kōbō (Jū Yon)") is the 183rd chapter of the Hunter × Hunter manga, written and illustrated by Yoshihiro Togashi. Summary. Surrounded by the other players with their books open, Gon's group stands with their backs to one another and waits to see what they will do. However, two of the players speak up and assure them that they're there to help, asking the group if they will buy the card from them for 2.5 billion if one of them wins the quiz. They add that the amount isn't unreasonable since it's only 5% of the reward, and Killua realizes that they don't know about the situation with Battera. Killua tells one of the players that they will pay him for the card if he wins, but the player seems dishonest about why he's there, leaving Killua confused. A few others approach Gon and congratulate him, adding that they just traveled to him to watch and asking if they can look at his full book. Killua guesses that the rest are there to negotiate for the card, and Biscuit agrees with him and asks if they should work together on the quiz like the others are preparing to do. Gon says that they should complete it on their own, with him and Killua betting on which of them will get the better score. Biscuit watches the two and says to herself that both seem so calm especially after the life-or-death fight against the Bombers. She guesses that they enjoyed the game more than any other player, internally wishing them good luck on the quiz while she doesn't participate (since she hates quizzes). Eta begins the event and asks the first question about "Patch of Forest," with Killua already overwhelmed by the five choices. As Eta asks the second question about "Liquor Spring" and the third about "Angel's Breath," the disguised Abengane approaches Genthru still tied up on the ground and touches him on the shoulder. He utters the phrase, "I caught the Bomber" and the Nen beast underneath the disguise vanishes into smoke, leaving Genthru confused as Abengane walks away. Eta asks about "Paladin's Necklace," and Gon is confident that he answered correctly. She finally reaches the last question, asking what No. 000 is called.
