He reveals that he plans to push Majtani off and that he will simply fall if he's really unconscious. Leroute protests his decision, but Leorio proposes that if Majtani yells out while falling, Kurapika will take a loss for his match. Leroute agrees to the deal, and Majtani can't believe that she's betting with his life so casually, causing his heartbeat to quicken. However, Leroute changes her bet and puts 40 hours on Majtani waking up. Leorio knows that he caused her to show her hand, and when he goes to push him off the side, Majtani finally gives up the act and runs off the platform, calling both of them crazy and admitting that he lost. After Leroute says that he knew Majtani was awake, Leorio explains that since he's pre-med, he's able to tell if someone's awake by checking their eye movement. The score on the monitor then changes, with Leroute at 80 hours and Leorio at 20. The match score also changes and gives a second win to the examinees. Leorio tells her that it's her turn to make a bet, and Leroute removes the shroud from her head as the handcuffs fall to the ground, proposing that they bet on whether she is a man or a woman. Interested at first and then taken aback by the wager, Leorio wonders how he will know for certain if he chooses the wrong option, and Leroute offers to let him check. Kurapika and Killua immediately know that Leorio will choose the former option, with Gon left confused by the conversation. Leorio bets 10 hours on her being a man, and the two are immediately proven right, with Gon still left wondering what's happening. Leorio tells himself that he couldn't pass up the opportunity and thinks about what will happen if he's wrong. Killua asks Gon if he understands now, which he quickly does. Even though Leroute tells him that she's a woman, Leorio is still left unsure, but she quickly allows him to confirm it. As the score changes and Leorio has only 10 hours remaining, he is left smiling and tells himself that he doesn't regret it. Tonpa scoffs at Leorio's decision and says that he will definitely lose. Gon asks him why, and Tonpa explains that he's more focused on what he could lose instead of considering the odds of winning or losing. With Leorio left nervous by the scoreboard, Leroute tells herself that she can read Leorio like a book and that he won't get any more joy out of the contest. Leorio wonders how he will make a comeback and decides to try his luck, proposing that they bet on a game of rock-paper-scissors. With no hesitation, Leroute bets 80 hours that she will win and tells Leorio that while he doesn't have to match it, he also can't raise. With Leorio left stunned by her confidence, Leroute analyzes the situation with herself and stresses the importance of probability, noting that it's more likely for someone to win or tie. However, she adds that statistics and psychology also play a role, mentioning that people tend to use scissors first. On their first throw, both Leroute and Leorio use rock. While Leroute notes that using rock increases the probability of a win or draw, Leorio nervously wonders what he should do next. Leroute continues to analyze the situation and guesses that Leorio will use rock or paper. She chooses paper as her best option since it should result in a win or draw, and her analysis pays off when Leorio chooses rock.

Chapter 200 Stipulation (, "Jōken") is the 200th chapter of the Hunter × Hunter manga, written and illustrated by Yoshihiro Togashi. Synopsis. While wandering the streets, Killua explains to Gon that the broken tiles are a rook and a bishop from . He goes on to say that it comes from the practice of splitting wood or bamboo in half across its marking and then matching it later to prove one's identity. Gon asks about the purpose of the tiles for them, and Killua explains that their "rivals" have the other halves, so they need to defeat them to take the pieces. They return to the train station and find that the message has been erased, meaning that they read Killua's response of agreeing to fight. Behind them, a woman with long, black hair introduces herself as Palm. Her creepy appearance shocks the two boys, but she tells them not to be so nervous, knowing that Netero didn't tell them much and inviting them for coffee so she can go over the details. Palm explains that she is a student of Knov, and begins a monologue on how cool and collected her master is, implying that she has some sort of crush on him. As she continues to be embarrassed by her infatuation, she fills her cup of coffee with a considerable amount of sugar and drinks it, which both Gon and Killua find incredibly gross. Killua gets her back on the topic, asking if he and Gon are supposed to fight her. Palm apologizes for going off on a tangent and clarifies the situation, saying that Netero and Knov didn't want anyone else to join the Extermination Team, but after she insisted so much, Knov eventually gave in but with a stipulation. She begins to adore Knov again, and after Killua interrupts her tangent, she says that the stipulation is that they have to defeat Knuckle and Shoot. Palm unleashes her hatred for the two Hunters and uses her Hatsu, causing her coffee to overflow onto the table. Gon quickly calms her down and realizes that she's an Enhancer as well. Palm goes on to say that Gon and Killua will be the ones fighting Knuckle and Shoot, both of whom are Morel's students and were also given stipulations, though she isn't aware of what they are. Finally, she tells the two boys that only one of their groups will be allowed to go to NGL, adding that they have one month to accomplish the task. In the Chimera Ant Nest, the corpse of Kite frozen in a block of ice has been laid out. Neferpitou sits beside it and describes their fight as feeling like a dream, admitting that they want to experience the same thrill again. They suddenly get an idea and say that all they need to do is fix him. As Pitou decides that that will be their ability, an incredibly ominous aura with a face in the center begins to form in front of Pitou. Elsewhere, in a crowded bar filled with smoke, Shoot says that they have to hold on to their tiles for one month, guessing that someone will try to take them. He somehow fuses his half of the tile into the palm of his hand, asking his partner what they should do. Sitting on a sofa, the delinquent-looking Knuckle confidently replies that they find their opponents and destroy them.

Chapter 201 Reunion (, "Saikai") is the 201st chapter of the Hunter × Hunter manga, written and illustrated by Yoshihiro Togashi. Synopsis. In order to lure out his unknown opponents, the Beast Hunter Knuckle Bine strolls through the city with a megaphone and banner, announcing that he is challenging the two other candidates for the Extermination Team. He shouts that the time will be midnight and that he will be waiting to fight them fair and square. However, he forgets to mention the location of the fight, with several passersby quick to point out the omission. Unknown to Knuckle, Killua pretends to be a civilian and just walks past him. Later in a restaurant, Killua tells Gon that Knuckle's announcement has to be a trap and that Knuckle's partner might be stalking anyone who had an unusual reaction since according to Palm, the two don't even know their names. Despite calling Knuckle stupid, Killua admits that he looked pretty strong. Gon asks how long it would take to defeat Knuckle, and Killua reminds him of what Morel told him earlier: a battle involving Nen has no certainties. Morel had also told him that he shouldn't worry so much about the odds of victory, but Killua disagrees, telling Gon that they need to improve their basic skills and figure out the opponents' abilities in order to win. Gon disagrees with the second part, and Killua asks him why they should take that risk. Gon calmly says that that's normal in NGL, reminding Killua that their goal is not to defeat Knuckle and Shoot, but to get stronger so they can go back to NGL and rescue Kite. Continuing to argue over the details, Killua reminds him that they only have a month to improve, but Gon says that they will improve in one week and return to NGL by then. As Killua is left in disbelief by the statement, a punch suddenly flies toward them and strikes Gon, sending him to the ground. The two boys look up to see Biscuit and wonder why she's there. Palm tells them that she called her, saying that she used her ability to find information on the two of them. Palm's expression becomes twisted, and she insists that they start plotting to kill Morel's students, with Gon and Killua quickly declining. Before starting their training, Biscuit punches Gon again and scolds him for what he said earlier, telling him that Netero is known for having unreasonable expectations and that when he gives a deadline of a month, it would be difficult to accomplish the task in one year, let alone just one week. Gon tells her all about the situation with Kite and Biscuit says that it's all the more important that he doesn't rush things since he could fail again. Killua stands by and silently comments about Biscuit being an old woman good at giving criticism. Gon realizes that Biscuit's nagging was right, and they move on to Nen training. The two show her their Ren, and she tells them to maintain it for three hours, surprising both of them. Gon asks Killua how long he has gone for, and Killua says that his maximum is 55 minutes on a good day. Biscuit tells them that they won't move on to the next step until they reach three hours. Less than an hour later, Gon has already collapsed on the floor while Killua continues using Ren for a few minutes longer. When he gives up, Biscuit also continues reading her magazine and informs them that prolonging Ren for only 10 minutes could require a month, stressing that they can't waste any time for sleep. In a park, Knuckle becomes furious that his opponents didn't show up, calling them cowards and saying that they deserve to die. While waiting, he befriends a puppy and asks him where his owner is, saying that they should be around to pick up after him. After training, Biscuit tells the two that they can sleep for the night, but that tomorrow starts in half an hour. Gon and Killua fall asleep right on the floor, and Biscuit manifests Cookie and uses Piano Massage on Gon first. She says that it will allow them to get eight hours of rest in just 30 minutes. Palm politely interrupts, but quickly turns to her ominous self, telling Biscuit that if she has to wait so long and doesn't get to go to NGL, she may kill all three of them. Biscuit asks her if it's a threat, but Palm calmly replies that it's a warning, asking her to give up on the two boys if she thinks they have no chance. Biscuit says that she should be telling Gon and Killua that (once they wake up). After his rest, Gon assures Palm that they will win and take her to NGL, asking her for any advice as he continues his Ren training. Biscuit tells her to have faith in Gon, and Palm suddenly becomes infatuated with his determination, embarrassed to show it. Biscuit says that she's worried about the ones in NGL already, asking Palm what Netero will be doing for the next month. Palm answers that they plan to determine the strength of the enemy and chip away at it. She adds that since the experts can't agree on the time left until the King's birth, the group is assuming that it could be as early as two months away. In NGL, Netero looks toward the Chimera Ant Nest, putting his hand around his right eye to get a clearer view. He spots Neferpitou and immediately becomes worried, saying that the Ant looks stronger than him.

Chapter 202 Duel (, "Kettō") is the 202nd chapter of the Hunter × Hunter manga, written and illustrated by Yoshihiro Togashi. Synopsis. Morel and Knov are shocked by Netero's statement that their enemy could be stronger than him. They think that if his statement were true, no Hunter in the world would have a chance. Netero reminds them that it's been more than 50 years since he was considered the most powerful Nen master, saying that they are probably evenly matched with him now. But Knov assures him that he is still strong enough, telling him to be more confident. Netero quips about how aging sucks and Morel asks him if he is still willing to take on the enemy, and Netero says that he would prefer not to fight at all, reminding them that the Queen is their only target. Observing the nest in the distance, Netero says that it will tough to slip past Pitou's En and that the problem is how to win, asking them for any suggestions. Knov recognizes that Netero already knows their answer, and he tells him that they will take them out silently one at a time. He suddenly opens a portal in the ground and pulls out a large object, throwing it to Morel who unwraps it to reveal a very large pipe. Morel uses the pipe and blows out smoke to form dozens of rabbits, saying that they should take it slowly and enjoy it. He hopes to find out how many of the enemies there are, sending out the rabbits in the direction of the nest. Sitting on guard outside the nest, Pitou senses something and sees multiple targets moving closer, unable to tell what they are exactly but knowing that they aren't living things. As Pitou wonders if it's an enemy ability, an unknown figure approaches and says that it may be best to wait and see, adding that the targets can simply be eliminated if they get too close. Pitou agrees that they could be decoys and wonders if they were talking out loud, but the figure says that they just thought they were. Pitou asks who they are, and the Chimera Ant introduces himself as a fellow Royal Guard named Shaiapouf. He tells them that Menthuthuyoupi will awaken soon as well, and Pitou thinks that he is a little strange, which Pouf acknowledges. Meanwhile, Gon and Killua manage to maintain their Ren for three hours. Biscuit congratulates them, and the two immediately collapse from exhaustion, but she doesn't allow them to rest, stating that they have to go see Knuckle. The boys wonder what she means exactly, and she bluntly states that they're going to fight him. Palm looks on as the two boys quickly object and complain, but Biscuit manages to calm them down by stating that if they think they are going to lose, they just need to run away and then have a rematch the next day. She informs them that they will practice Ren for three hours every day and then go challenge Knuckle until they win, which leaves both boys nervous. Knuckle is once again in the park, waiting for his opponents to show up and feeding the stray dog he came across earlier. When he sees Gon and Killua approaching him, he is in disbelief that his opponents are two kids, smirking maniacally and saying that he has never felt so insulted.

Chapter 203 Gyro (ジャイロ, "Jairo") is the 203rd chapter of the Hunter × Hunter manga, written and illustrated by Yoshihiro Togashi. Synopsis. Knuckle walks towards the two boys and looms over them, unable to believe that his superiors think he's no better than two kids. His overwhelming presence terrifies Killua, who wants to attack but can't move an inch. Knuckle lectures the two on how dangerous duels are, saying that it's best to fight five hours after a good night's sleep, not when they're exhausted. He wonders if the two of them are even taking things seriously, leaning in and declaring that he would never lose to them. But Gon and Killua suddenly see that Knuckle has tears in his eyes, pointing it out to him, but Knuckle quickly denies it and covers his face, saying that it's from laughing too hard as he threatens to kill the two if they tell anyone. He turns away to wipe away the tears, but quickly turns back around and yells at them to hit him, explaining that it will illustrate the difference in power between them. He adds that he doesn't even need to dodge their weak punches, saying that they can hit him until they're satisfied, but telling them that if he doesn't budge an inch, they have to give up their tiles. Gon yells out against his insults, but internally admits that Knuckle's assessment is right, realizing that he can't overcome the situation with just willpower and thinking back to what happened with Kite. Knowing that he doesn't have anything to say in reply, Gon slowly approaches Knuckle and begins charging up Rock. Knuckle is confident at first, but the sudden increase in Gon's aura leaves him panicking. At first, he thinks that he should guard with Gyo, but immediately switches it to Ko. He knows that he has to correctly guess which part of his body to defend or he could actually die. He begins to sweat profusely, finally deciding to defend his stomach since it's the most likely choice. After Gon throws the punch and sends him back several feet, Knuckle lies on the ground and tells Gon that he knew he could count on him before falling unconscious. Gon wonders what's with him, and Killua guesses that he's just a complete moron. Knuckle wakes up and finds himself at their hotel as Gon and Killua practice maintaining their Ren beside him. Knuckle admits that he underestimated Gon and realizes that he still has his half of the tile, asking Gon why he didn't just take it and leave him. Gon replies that it's not the tiles they want, but the ability to beat Knuckle in an honest fight. He then asks Knuckle why he became a Beast Hunter, but Knuckle says that it's a long and sad story. Gon then asks why he volunteered for the Extermination Team, and Knuckle reveals that he joined to not get them exterminated. He explains that he hates the blanket policy of getting rid of things, for which his master calls him naive, but he questions how they can decide until they see the enemy in person and better understand them. As Gon smiles and Killua thinks that Knuckle would be dead at that point, Knuckle says that Gon is a nice kid and that he could tell only after they fought. Gon feels the same about Knuckle and points him to something moving under his blanket. The dog that Knuckle had befriended reveals himself, and Gon explains that he wouldn't leave his side the whole time, adding that good Hunters are liked by animals. Knuckle begins to cry, but again assures them that he's not, giving them the same warning as before. Later during their meal, Knuckle agrees to fight them as many times as they want, but tells them that they won't be able to beat him in the remaining 20 days, with both Gon and Killua smiling at his deal. It's stated that one of the newly born Chimera Ant soldiers has a will of his own and subsequently rejected the Queen's orders. The man's human name was Gyro, and he was the kingpin of NGL, with his malevolence and determination being his two strongest attributes. As Gyro walks down a street wearing a large, dark overcoat with his hood up, it's revealed that he is in the same town as Gon and Killua.

Chapter 204 Gyro's Story (ジャイロは, "Jairo wa") is the 204th chapter of the Hunter × Hunter manga, written and illustrated by Yoshihiro Togashi. Synopsis. Gyro, the leader of NGL, grew up in a construction camp until he was 12. There he learned how to mix concrete and lay bricks before even learning how to speak. His abusive father was a man of few words who spent his time after work drinking cheap booze. Because of this, Gyro only learned how to talk when he was seven years old. Furthermore, he was forced to stay on his top bunk after work, only allowed to go to the communal bathroom two times a day (and not after 9 p.m.). He was also forced to learn how to sleep quietly, for the noise of his creaking bed upset his father sleeping below him. Gyro learned only one thing from his father: never be a nuisance for others. Despite his father's cruelty, Gyro treasured these words and idolized him. He had two reasons for this: his father had never ordered him to leave and his father helped him cope with a bad fever when he was five, which required him to stay up caring for his son the entire night. However, these beliefs were shattered when a man who regularly bullied him, whom he had never done anything against due to his father's lesson of not causing problems for others, tormented him by telling him the truth about the situation of his life. This truth was that his father only kept him around to exploit his labor. This knowledge causes Gyro to attack the man in a rage. Then the man, while he has his foot on Gyro's head, shatters his last belief as he tells him that the person who took care of him when he was sick wasn't his father, but his old next-door neighbor, who argued with his drunken father over it. And Gyro's father told the old man that he didn't care whether his son died or not. While trying to process these truths he had just heard, he saw his father look at him and just pass him by without doing a thing. This was the moment that Gyro learned that the universe couldn't care less about his existence. Everything he believed was a lie, and this caused him to become misanthropic and realize that the only reason his father told him never to become a nuisance for others was to get him to not be a nuisance to him. But one day, after finding his father drinking in their room, he picked up a hammer and smashed his skull in. He then stole all his money and left the construction camp. Nine years later, he established NGL, and nine years after that, he turned it into an officially recognized nation and became its king, now fully disconnected from the human race. Gyro's goal had become to spread evil throughout the world and in order to do this, he developed a drug called D² which was manufactured in NGL. He had been planning to do many more evil things before his nation was invaded by the Chimera Ants and he was devoured by the Queen. Yet, when he was reborn into a new body, he could not forget his human memories or his pride in having been a king himself. And as he walks through the town Gon and Killua were currently in, he says to himself he will start over. He knew that such preparations were necessary for major undertakings, with his experience in construction making him rational and productive. But he wasn't in a hurry, leaving town without ever encountering Gon. But whether this proved to be fortunate for either of them will only be known when the two eventually meet. In the Chimera Ant Nest, Colt and Peggy are discussing the disappearance of Chiona and Reikei and their troops, deducing that the humans are fighting back and targeting those who are going out to collect food for the Queen. Peggy wonders if they should get the Queen to move and if they should inform Neferpitou. Colt is against the former idea and isn't keen on the latter, but they do so anyway and Pitou tells them to worry about the outside, since the Royal Guards will defend the fortress. Colt and Peggy then discuss their collective strength, and it is shown that there are 28 Squadron Leaders left who are each in control of four to five officers, who in turn are each in command of 10 to 15 peon soldiers. Also, each is organized differently and many have become arrogant since learning Nen. This leads them to conclude to use the others as bait to fight and trap the humans, since it's unlikely that they would listen to any advice. Far outside the nest, Netero guesses this exact strategy and Knov predicts their next move, telling Morel that they should target the Ant troops indiscriminately regardless of whether they are bait or not, in order to maximize the chaos. He then expresses that they know their next move too and can possibly finish them off before reinforcements arrive. Back in town, after training with Biscuit, Gon and Killua again challenge Knuckle, who is impressed that the two boys are still fighting while so exhausted. He knows that he can't let them gain any confidence, sending both of them flying with a hard punch. Shoot watches from the shadows and worries that given his soft personality, Knuckle has already been won over. He worries that Knuckle's tongue will slip, revealing information about him, so he decides to ambush Gon and Killua on their way back to the hotel.

Chapter 205 Time Remaining (り, "Nokori Jikan") is the 205th chapter of the Hunter × Hunter manga, written and illustrated by Yoshihiro Togashi. Synopsis. Injured and limping along with sticks to support them, Gon and Killua drag themselves back toward the hotel. Killua says that they have no chance against Knuckle, and Gon adds that he isn't even using half his strength, but tells Killua that they have to keep trying. As the two boys slowly make their way back, Shoot is seen watching them from behind a tree, saying that it's his opportunity to strike since no one else is around. But as Gon and Killua pass by him, he begins to shake and sweat profusely. He tells himself that he has to seize his chance, but he still doesn't move as his expression becomes despondent and tears run down his face. It's stated that his full name is Shoot McMahon, 28 years old, with AB blood type. He is an Unidentified Beast Hunter, and a coward. Back at the hotel, Gon asks Killua why Knuckle can't go to NGL, saying that he's really tough and likening his physical strength to that of Kite. Killua thinks that maybe it has something to do with his personality, saying that his generous nature doesn't mesh with the extermination plan and citing how close he gets with animals. As the two boys talk while maintaining their Ren, Biscuit looks on and is happy to see that they can maintain it for two hours without concentrating. She considers letting them fight once they can maintain it for three hours and when the two of them are well-rested. She believes that Knuckle will be forced to use his full strength, hoping that Gon and Killua can figure out what they lack in combat. However, she says that they would only be halfway there, worrying about the deadline approaching and saying that it would take ten more days to even get to that point. As she continues to worry, she glances over at Palm, who is chopping food with a knife. Her eyes suddenly widen, and she touches the knife's edge, turning toward Biscuit with a dreadful glare. Biscuit realizes that she should come up with an escape plan for herself if things go south. Palm finishes preparing dinner, and the others thank her for the meal. As Gon scarfs down his food, Palm asks him how it is, and Gon says that it's really good as he continues to chew. Palm replies that she wasn't talking about the food, reminding him that they have ten days left. She guesses that Gon is two-thirds of the way to improving his basics so that Knuckle will use his full strength. Biscuit and Killua look on with fear and suspicion, and Gon turns to Biscuit to ask her if it's true, but she just quietly sips her drink. Gon assures Palm that they will still win before the deadline. Palm, however, is convinced that Gon won't be able to defeat Knuckle in time, revealing that staring at her knife calms her down and telling Gon that if he runs away now, she probably won't kill him. Killua and Biscuit think that their meals would be great if it weren't for Palm's creepy remarks, but Gon assures her that he won't run away, promising to pinkie swear. Palm is confused at first, but Gon quickly links their pinkies together and swears to defeat Knuckle and Shoot before the deadline, uttering the usual rhyme. Gon adds that the next step is what they (he, Mito, and Noko) do on Whale Island, saying that a kiss between their pinkies seals the promise. As Gon asks Palm about the meal she prepared, Killua and Biscuit continue eating. Killua is happy to see that Gon is getting better at handling Palm, but Biscuit reminds him that they have ten days left, with Killua telling her not to say it like their days are numbered. Meanwhile, back in NGL, the Chimera Ants have difficulty contacting one another due to Morel's smoke surrounding them. Baital tries to contact Goran telepathically, but gets no response, worried that the enemy already got him. Their communications become more and more confused, and Baital has no clue what's going on in the dense smoke. Two Ants suddenly disappear, and Knov sits reading a book in a cave up above, and Morel asks him if their strategy is really fair, saying that all they have to do is send them to Netero who does the dirty work. Knov says that the plan is flawless, adding that although Netero was trying to be humble earlier, he is not only much stronger than them, but ready to fight. Netero contacts them by phone, and at an undisclosed location, he is shown surrounded by Chimera Ant corpses, asking the two to send down more and adding that he's getting in the groove again. In the Chimera Ant Nest, Peggy tells Colt that Baital and Gaftz's squads haven't returned, and Colt says that they have just 14 left. In the hotel, Biscuit watches Gon and Killua maintaining their Ren and says that they have seven days left. Back in the nest, surrounded by skulls, the gravid Queen feels her son moving and asks him if he wants to come out.

Chapter 206 A Real Fight (, "Shōbu") is the 206th chapter of the Hunter × Hunter manga, written and illustrated by Yoshihiro Togashi. Synopsis. After Killua and Gon maintain their Ren for three hours, they get ready to go challenge Knuckle, but Biscuit stops them and tells them to rest for 30 minutes. The two boys are confused, but Biscuit says that she wants them to be well-rested so they can have a good chance against Knuckle, especially since there's only one day left before the deadline. As Gon and Killua talk with each other to pass the time, Biscuit thinks to herself that no matter the outcome of the fight, they will have to accept the results if they give it their all, adding that she will be happy as long as they figure out where they're lacking. In the background, Palm is seen drawing rough sketches of Gon and Killua, stabbing them repeatedly with her pen, and Biscuit realizes that she now has to come up with an escape plan for Gon and Killua as well. Knuckle is seen kneeling in a clearing as he feeds multiple dogs and assures them that there's enough. Both Knuckle and the dogs sense something, and the latter runs away as Gon and Killua slowly approach Knuckle. Aura swells around the two boys, and Knuckle knows that they are serious now. In the Chimera Ant nest, Youpi finally awakens and he is greeted by Pitou, with Pouf playing his violin and Kite sitting off to the side. Before they start to fight, Gon asks where Shoot is. Knuckle replies that it's pointless for them to know since he will beat them himself. Gon says that they need both tiles, and Knuckle chuckles, replying that he will tell them where Shoot is if they beat him. Killua points out that he won't be able to tell them if he's unconscious. Knuckle puts on a maniacal smile, but quickly becomes serious, saying that Killua's comment wasn't funny. Gon's aura swells around him, and he suddenly leaps forward and gets behind Knuckle. As Gon goes to throw a punch, Knuckle easily dodges and throws a hard right, sending Gon far back even though he blocked the strike. Gon feels the impact throughout his whole body and says that if he weren't using Ken, Knuckle's attacks would instantly knock him unconscious. Knuckle calmly stretches out his shoulder, saying that he needs four or five warm-up punches. He tells Gon to watch out and warns him that he will get better as the fight goes on. Meanwhile, back in NGL, Knov confirms to Netero by phone that the Chimera Ants are still staying inside their nest. Knov asks if they should take action, but Netero tells them to wait since the deadline is so close. He says that the Ants will need to restock on food in about a week, during which time they can take out a few more of their soldiers. Knov informs Morel that they will wait for the students, but Morel says that he doesn't see the point since they can't count on them for the current battle, adding that they might be useful as bait. Knov asks Morel if he would like to bet on whose students will arrive, and Morel bets 100,000 on Knuckle and Shoot, adding that if he and Knov both lose, the pot goes to Netero. Knov makes an undisclosed bet of one million, and Morel says that there's no way that happens, in disbelief that Knov would just throw away his money. Knov replies that he enjoys gambling as well, especially when long shots are involved. As the Royal Guards, Squadron Leaders, Queen, and the members of the Extermination Team are each shown, Netero thinks to himself that the mission may not be successful without sacrificing someone.

Chapter 207 Weakness: Part 1 (①, "Jakuten (Ichi)") is the 207th chapter of the Hunter × Hunter manga, written and illustrated by Yoshihiro Togashi. Synopsis. Knuckle punches Gon with a hard right, disorienting him and following it up with a strong kick to his side. He then uses that opportunity to move behind him and land a hard punch to his back, with Gon reeling from the strike and Killua having trouble watching. Gon tries his best to recover and can't believe that Knuckle is just warming up. Knuckle wonders if he will use his "show me rock" attack, betting that Gon can't because of how flawed it is. He warns Gon that he will prevent him from using it, especially in a one-on-one fight, stating that his signature move has two flaws. But before pointing them out, Knuckle asks for the technique's name. As Gon realizes that he never came up with one for it, he stutters out "Ja-- janken" on the spot, and Knuckle notes the meaning of "rock-paper-scissors," believing that the extra "Ja" was intentional to give it flair, like saying, "Ta-da!" Gon thinks to himself that he actually just stuttered, but Knuckle compliments him on the name, with Gon not telling him the truth and Killua in disbelief at the exchange. Knuckle then states Jajanken's two big weaknesses: first, it takes a considerable amount of time to charge up, and he adds that the few seconds before a move during combat is like a lifetime, which means he won't get many chances to utilize it (and Gon knows this); second, it puts Gon in considerable jeopardy because the more aura he concentrates around his fists means the less he will have to protect the rest of his body. Knuckle stresses that Gon will end up dead if someone strikes where he's vulnerable, but Gon replies that he is aware of the risks, saying that he trained over the past month so he could compensate for them. After making his declaration, Gon unleashes his Ren and his aura swells around him, impressing Knuckle who thinks that he has as much as a mid-ranking Hunter. But as Knuckle says to himself that Gon still lacks experience, he sends him back with a hard punch. Gon quickly recovers, but Knuckle throws another punch and sends him back again, knowing that Gon hasn't fought enough in real combat. While he compliments Gon's decisiveness and natural talent, he thinks that the flow of aura around his body is too rough, allowing him to easily tell what Gon is protecting and what he will do next. Knuckle is confident in his analysis and lands another punch, leaving Gon holding his side after the strike. Killua realizes that Knuckle is easily reading Gon's aura, and Knuckle says that he's done warming up, telling Gon not to blame him if he dies. Gon understands how generous Knuckle was being to him by warning him in advance and giving him advice. He realizes that the fight would have been over in seconds if Knuckle hadn't been teaching him how to get stronger. But he thinks that Knuckle is being too generous, suddenly clenching his fist and charging up Rock. Knuckle immediately runs forward and kicks Gon hard in the face, reminding him about his warning and asking him if he's mocking him. Gon staggers to his feet and asks Knuckle if that's all he has, reminding Knuckle that the two are supposed to be fighting for real and angrily ordering him to attack like he's going to kill him. As Knuckle stands in silence, Gon begins charging up another Rock, with Knuckle unable to believe how fearless the boy is.

Chapter 208 Weakness: Part 2 (②, "Jakuten (Ni)") is the 208th chapter of the Hunter × Hunter manga, written and illustrated by Yoshihiro Togashi. Synopsis. As Gon once again starts to charge his Jajanken, Knuckle tries to stop him by punching him, but Gon dodges out the way and appears behind him. Knuckle swings his arm to strike him, but Gon ducks below the attack and kicks Knuckle in the leg, causing him to lose his footing. And before Knuckle can fall, Gon punches him in the face and begins to charge his Jajanken once again, but Knuckle quickly recovers and kicks Gon in the chin, causing him to fall along with himself. Knuckle sits up shocked and realizes that Gon used his Jajanken as a feint. Gon stands up and states that he could clearly see that Knuckle was trying to prevent his attack, so it was easy to counter his obvious punch. Killua mentally praises Gon for using Jajanken's long windup to his advantage by messing with Knuckle's mind. He observes that, to Knuckle, Gon's Jajanken is like a perfect pitch right over the plate that a baseball batter eagerly looks for. But because the batter is so eager to make contact, he tries too hard and tenses up, resulting in a poor hit. Killua says that it's the same for aura, which focuses in a specific spot where someone tenses up and then balloons right as they go to attack He adds that if an inexperienced Nen user gets too excited or panics during a fight, his aura and plan of attack becomes readable and too predictable. And he says that since Gon rattled Knuckle earlier by pointing out his soft side, he made the feint more successful, adding that Gon's strategy is more effective against someone who is aware of Jajanken since they know how dangerous it is when he starts charging it up. Killua also understands that the strategy is effective even if the enemy jumps back to avoid Rock, because Gon can then use Scissors or Paper to attack them at a distance. He realizes that he was wrong about Jajanken being harder to use if the enemy already knew about it, saying that Gon can use it in various ways. He points out that Gon has gotten better control of his aura during the fight and that Knuckle will have a harder time differentiating between a feint and the actual thing, amazed at how quickly Gon was able to learn and improve during combat. Meanwhile, Gon is finding it harder to maintain Ken, even though it hasn't even been twenty minutes since the fight started. He realizes that the way he was fighting was using up large amounts of energy, deducing that if one hour of training translates to ten minutes in combat, he only has ten minutes left before completely exhausting himself. He resolves to finish the fight with his Jajanken before he runs out of aura and inevitably loses. Gon and Knuckle continue to fight hand-to-hand, fiercely trading blows as Killua observes that Knuckle still has the edge, but seeing that Gon is gradually starting to hold his own. He recognizes that Gon is using more aura for a defense to minimize the damage from Knuckle's strikes, as well as adjusting to Knuckle's speed and not falling prey to any surprise attacks. But he recognizes that Gon is out of time, seeing that his stamina is at its limit because Jajanken requires so much aura to activate, while Knuckle is conserving his energy by only using simple attacks. Killua points out that Gon spent a considerable amount of aura in the feints alone, saying that he's used Jajanken three times already and that if he uses it again, he would only last another minute or two after that. Knuckle punches Gon with a hard right, and Gon is sent far back even after blocking it, having trouble catching his breath as he recovers from the strike. Knuckle addresses Gon and says that he isn't worth using his full strength on. As Knuckle starts to call Gon weak, Gon interrupts him by once again starting to charge his Jajanken, preparing to throw Rock and surprising both Knuckle and Killua.

Chapter 209 ? (？, "?") is the 209th chapter of the Hunter × Hunter manga, written and illustrated by Yoshihiro Togashi. Synopsis. As Gon continues charging up his Jajanken, Killua wonders why he's using it when it won't be effective from so far away. After Knuckle realizes that it will be last attack, Gon begins his chant, but instead of ending with Rock, he says Paper and sends out a ball of aura. Knuckle is surprised by the Emission attack, but quickly recognizes how weak it is compared to Rock. He remains confident and easily bats the aura ball back, but Gon suddenly says Round 2 and appears right behind Knuckle, who realizes that Gon used Paper as a distraction to create a Jajanken combo attack. Gon seems to unleash Rock right into the back of Knuckle, who appears reeling from the attack, but Gon suddenly falls to the ground and Knuckle stands motionless. Gon lies unconscious and Knuckle recognizes that he used up all his aura before he could throw Rock, realizing that Gon would have beaten him if he had been able to use the attack. As Killua picks up Gon and puts him on his back, Knuckle asks him why he isn't going to fight, saying that he can easily take him. Killua says that Gon will fight him again tomorrow, but things will go differently, adding that he will fight Shoot. Knuckle asks Killua to tell Gon that he will fight him for real tomorrow, saying that he better be ready to die. Killua scoffs at his promise and says that his victory won't matter if he doesn't give it his all. He suddenly puts on a menacing glare and tells Knuckle that if he loses without using all his strength, he will never forgive him. Killua walks away carrying Gon, and Shoot reveals himself from the nearby forest, commenting on how soft Knuckle is for helping the enemy. He asks Knuckle why he doesn't just give his tile to them if he doesn't want to go to NGL, though he adds that the boys wouldn't accept it anyway. Knuckle becomes angry and calls out Shoot for acting superior while hiding in the shadows for the past month, but Shoot declares that he will fight tomorrow. Back in the hotel, Gon lies snoring in bed, and Biscuit assures Killua that he will be fully recovered by tomorrow since she used Piano Massage on him. She says to herself that she's actually more worried about Killua since he didn't get to fight during the entire month. She suddenly throws off her overdress and tells Killua to spar with her right there.

Chapter 21 Resolution (, "Ketchaku") is the 21st chapter of the Hunter × Hunter manga, written and illustrated by Yoshihiro Togashi. Synopsis. After winning the game of rock-paper-scissors, Leroute celebrates her victory over Leorio, who is visibly upset by the loss. While Tonpa notes that the score is now tied at two each, Kurapika focuses more on the fact that they have 50 fewer hours to reach the bottom of Trick Tower alive. Leroute asks Lippo how much time the examinees had left, and he answers 59 hours and 45 minutes. Bendot notes that they now have less than 10 hours, but the last prisoner to fight says that it's pointless since his opponent will die and the examinees will fail. Leorio apologizes to the group and says that he thought he was decent at gambling. Tonpa asks him why he thought that, and Leorio shrugs off the comment, replying that it doesn't matter now. Killua prepares to fight the last prisoner, causing Leorio to criticize himself even more since he believes the team is now doomed. Killua angrily tells him that they should see the prisoner first and that he can hold his own as long as it doesn't involve math. The prisoner's handcuffs fall to the floor, and once he removes the shroud from his head, Leorio immediately recognizes him and nervously tells Killua not to fight him, not caring if the team loses now. It's then stated that the prisoner is known as Johness the Dissector, the most infamous mass murderer in Zaban City's history whose 146 victims had no significant connections or common traits to create a pattern or motive. It's revealed that some of the victims' bodies were so dismembered that all the pieces couldn't be cleared from the scene, with an 11-year-old boy having been gutted alive. Every victim was torn apart in at least 50 pieces, and Johness committed the murders by using only his bare hands. In a flashback, although Johness is finally arrested and surrenders peacefully, one of the police officers goes to start his car and suddenly has a piece of his left arm ripped off. With the officer screaming in pain, Johness sits handcuffed in the backseat while holding the piece of flesh in his hand. It's finally stated that Johness' M.O. was to quickly pluck his victims' flesh from their bones with his incredibly strong fingers. Back in the present, Johness grabs a part of the wall and rips it off with his hand, crushing it into small pieces and saying that he has missed the feel of flesh. Leorio again warns Killua not to fight Johness and that they can try to pass the Hunter Exam next year. However, Killua walks away without a word and meets Johness on the platform, asking him how he wants to fight. It's stated that Johness' sentence totals 968 years for mass murder, and he reveals that he doesn't care about the exam or reducing his sentence, only intent on tearing Killua to pieces and feeling the flesh in his hands as he hears his screams. Killua calmly agrees that the loser will die, but before Johness can even finish his reply, Killua walks past him and appears to take something from him. As a bloody spot appears on Johness' shirt, Killua is seen holding his still beating heart in his hand. Johness anxiously asks him to give it back, but Killua coldly smiles and crushes it, causing Johness to drop dead before he can reach it. With everyone left stunned, Killua confirms that they have won the contest, but Bendot reminds him that they have to spend 50 hours waiting in a small room nearby before they can continue the Third Phase. Killua remembers that Bendot didn't have to fight Tonpa and asks if he wants to fight now, but Bendot politely declines, leaving Killua with a smile on his face. As Leorio and Kurapika wonder who Killua really is, Gon reveals that he's from a family of assassins. The five examinees eventually make their way past the prisoners and arrive at the aforementioned room. Lippo tells them that they will be allowed to leave in 50 hours, and the five spend their time drinking, reading, and relaxing. As Killua begins to read a book, Kurapika asks him how he pulled off the trick against Johness. However, Killua explains that it wasn't a trick and that he simply removed his heart, suddenly revealing that he can adjust his hand to sharpen his nails. With Gon and Leorio taken aback by the feat, Killua says that he used to be a professional murderer while Johness was only an amateur, adding that his father can do the same without leaving any blood on the wound. Gon is left curious about Killua's cat-like claws, and Kurapika is relieved that Killua is on their side. Once the 50 hours have elapsed and the group quickly leaves the room, Leorio checks the timer to see that they have nine hours and 43 minutes remaining. As they turn the corner, they find two staircases—one going up, the other going down—and again have to make a choice by voting.

Chapter 210 Weakness: Part 3 (③, "Jakuten (San)") is the 210th chapter of the Hunter × Hunter manga, written and illustrated by Yoshihiro Togashi. Synopsis. When Gon wakes up in the morning, he finds Killua with a swollen and beaten-up face. When Gon asks what happened to him, Killua replies that he was training with Biscuit since he's going to fight tomorrow too. He asks Gon how he's feeling, and Gon happily replies that he feels rejuvenated. Killua says that it was because of Biscuit's Piano Massage, and almost reveals something that he shouldn't, with Biscuit's face entering his mind and threatening him with more punishment if he tells Gon. Killua then thinks back to his sparring session with the muscular Biscuit the previous night and how she easily overpowered him. Biscuit points out his weakness, which she says is that he gives up too quickly and is too cautious in battle. She then elaborates that he underestimates himself, and when he faces an opponent that he perceives as stronger, he immediately prepares to run away. This causes Killua to think back to the confrontation with Pitou when he knocked Gon unconscious so the two of them could escape safely. Biscuit then adds that the habit isn't his fault, but rather the fault of the one who taught him. She tells him, however, that if he doesn't change his way of thinking, he will eventually let down Gon and leave him to die, leaving Killua in shock. She states that he always considers the worst-case scenario and assumes his opponents are fighting at their peak. She goes on to say that even if he's fighting someone equal to him in strength, he lets negative thoughts creep into his mind, and if the opponent is only a little stronger than him, he considers escape his only option. Biscuit instructs him to overcome his habit of always thinking that he's the underdog and to force himself to challenge someone more powerful. Finally, she gives Killua an ultimatum: if he is unable to beat Shoot tomorrow, he has to stay out of Gon's life. Back in the present, Biscuit sees the boys off for the fight that night, and as the two walk away, she thinks to herself that Killua's guardians must have been overprotective, coming from a source of obsessive and distorted love that has now become a burden difficult to shake off. As she says that Killua will need to work hard to break the spell, Palm slowly opens the door of the hotel behind her and looks out with a menacing glare. Biscuit feels Palm's sinister aura and says that she isn't sure how the fights will turn out, prepared to make a run for it if things go south. The boys reach Knuckle and Shoot, and all four know that the loser has to give up their tile. Killua and Shoot head off into the forest surrounding the clearing, while Gon and Knuckle stay behind to fight out in the open. Knuckle shouts that, as promised, he is giving it his all from the start of the fight, aggressively throwing off his shirt. Gon knows that he can't handle Knuckle's speed, saying that his only option is to counter his attacks. Knuckle charges toward him, but begins to dart around so quickly that Gon can't keep track of him. He reminds himself not to follow with his eyes, but to use his aura to feel Knuckle's presence. He suddenly senses Knuckle's fist drawing close to his head, but Knuckle's punch still lands, and Gon's counter falls short as he's sent reeling back. Gon recovers from the hit, saying that he was too slow to counter it, but oddly feels himself brimming with power. He's left confused, but suddenly notices a small creature hanging onto his left arm, with the number "210" displayed on its forehead. It announces that it's time and tells Gon that he has accrued interest. The number increases to 231, and Gon is left even more confused as he quickly asks what it is. Knuckle explains that he lent Gon his aura, saying that the interest is ten percent every ten seconds and revealing that if Gon doesn't pay him back quickly, he will go bankrupt.

Chapter 211 Loan Shark (トイチ, "Toichi"—lit. "10% Interest Every 10 Days") is the 211th chapter of the Hunter × Hunter manga, written and illustrated by Yoshihiro Togashi. Synopsis. The interest piles up once again, and the numbers on the creature's forehead increase to 254. Knuckle informs Gon that the name of his ability is Hakoware and that the little mascot is called A.P.R. ("Amortizing Power Redirector"). Gon punches A.P.R., but Knuckle says that it's pointless to attack him since he's only there to announce the increase in interest, adding that he's both harmless and indestructible. The interest increases once again, and as the announcement distracts Gon, Knuckle quickly rushes in and punches him hard in the face. Gon notes that he again didn't feel any pain from the attack, but instead feels himself overflowing with aura. The interest goes up yet again, but the amount nearly doubles, leaving Gon shocked. Knuckle explains that it was because he lent him around 180 aura, and with Gon still confused about the different numbers, Knuckle further explains that 180 aura is a numerical expression of his energy. As aura is stored inside a person's body, the maximum amount a person has varies based on training (so too with the amount of aura someone can release at once). Knuckle says that even if Gon has a lot of potential aura power, his lack of training means he can release less actual aura power. Gon is confused by the various terms, and Knuckle says that Gon's maximum actual aura power he can use through Ken seems to be around 1,800. A.P.R.'s interest continues to increase, and Knuckle explains that in preparing for combat, a person expends around 1 aura per second, but once they start to employ more advanced techniques like Gyo and Ryu, consumption can increase six to ten times more. He tells Gon that since he can't control his aura well, he expends about 10 a second, thereby using 600 aura every minute during combat. And since Gon ran out after 20 minutes during their last fight, Knuckle says that he spent around 12,000 aura. He adds that Gon also used Jajanken four times, which caused his aura to spike and used up 5,500 in his first three attempts. With Gon reaching the limit of his comprehension, Knuckle continues to give the details about his aura and finally arrives at the conclusion that Gon's maximum potential aura power is around 21,500. All the calculations make Gon dizzy, and Knuckle playfully comments on how mathematics must not be his best subject, but becomes serious again and gets to the important part of his explanation: when the borrowed aura (with interest) becomes greater than Gon's remaining potential aura power, he will go bankrupt. He tells Gon to look at A.P.R., and Gon is shocked to see that not only has the mascot itself increased in size, but the number is now at 1,586. Gon wonders how it could triple after only a few minutes, and Knuckle says that it's actually only been 120 seconds, going through the calculations and explaining how fast debt can add up. A.P.R. announces another increase (going up to 1,745), and Knuckle reveals that even if Gon just stands there and does nothing, he will still go bankrupt in 4 minutes and 20 seconds. The interest increases to 1,920, and Gon asks what will happen then. Knuckle explains that A.P.R. will transform into I.R.S. ("Individual Ren Suppressor") and force Gon to stay in Zetsu for a period of 30 days, leaving him unable to use Nen. Knuckle says that it's too late for any regrets, and Gon realizes that Knuckle didn't use his ability until now in order to help him grow, quietly thanking him for it. He quickly charges in, and the two exchange blows, with Knuckle explaining that Gon still took an aura loss and saying that until he pays back all the debt, he won't take any damage from Gon's attacks. A.P.R. increases to 2,356, and Knuckle eggs Gon on and said that he will go bankrupt in four minutes. The two exchange a series of furious strikes, but Knuckle says that Gon only repaid about 100 aura, which is only a drop in the bucket. He realizes that he can't let himself get hit by Gon's Jajanken, knowing that he will win once Gon's debt goes past 10,000. A.P.R. makes another announcement and increases to 2,717. Elsewhere, Killua and Shoot stand opposite each other in a forest, both ready for their battle. Killua reminds himself not to fear Shoot and that he doesn't know his ability either. Shoot tells Killua that he doesn't like to hurt people, explaining to himself that his ability only activates when he inflicts damage and that he only uses it against people he doesn't mind hurting. Shoot removes his left sleeve and reveals that he has no left arm, but instead was keeping concealed three levitating, disembodied hands and a cage. He tells Killua that he and Gon showed him that sometimes one has to fight out of respect for another.

Chapter 212 Water Breaking (, "Hasui") is the 212th chapter of the Hunter × Hunter manga, written and illustrated by Yoshihiro Togashi. Synopsis. Killua begins his battle with Shoot, unnerved by the three floating hands. He wonders what Shoot's ability is and if he should attack first, but quickly calms himself and uses Gyo, confirming that Shoot isn't using In and that the three hands are really floating. He deduces that Shoot is a Manipulator and worries about the floating cage, wondering why he would need it if he uses the hands to attack. He knows that he can't let the hands touch him, pulling out his yo-yos and spinning them around himself. Shoot takes note of them and sends in the three hands to attack, but Killua deftly deflects all the incoming strikes. Impressed by Killua's skill, Shoot suddenly rushes forward right in front of him, and as Killua worries that the hands were just decoys, Illumi's face and voice suddenly enter his mind and tell him to jump back. Killua tries to fight against it and says that he should zap him, but Shoot lands a powerful strike to Killua's face, sending him far back. Killua says that his body can't move, and Shoot notices that his reaction speed wavered. Killua describes it as Illumi's spell and is internally conflicted over what to do, but realizes that he has to break the habit, adding that he has to give it his all since Shoot deserves that respect. But all of sudden, the vision in Killua's left eye appears blurry, and the left side of his face is shown to be missing. Shoot rushes in and attempts to land a hard right, but Killua quickly dodges back, confused and in disbelief about what's happened to his face. Shoot realizes that Killua's reaction time has returned and wonders if the earlier moment was a fluke. Illumi's instructions to flee after taking unknown damage fill Killua's head and Killua says that the spell saved him, but he can't win that way. Shoot sends in his flying hands again, and Killua uses his yo-yos to fend them off, but suddenly spots Shoot in his blind spot, quickly dodging another of his punches. Killua realizes that he's doing nothing but running away, and that he has never really fought any of his battles. He then drops his yo-yos and suddenly charges at Shoot, fending off the flying hands with his fists and declaring to himself that he won't run away anymore. He secretly prepares an electric shock behind his back, but Shoot says it out loud before Killua can use it and quickly backs away to avoid the trap. Illumi's words flood Killua's mind again, telling him not to follow too far, and as Killua fights against his brother's spell, he asks Shoot how he knew about the electricity. Meanwhile, in the nest of the Chimera Ants, the Queen unexpectedly goes into labor, screaming out in pain. Shaiapouf asks Neferpitou if it's time, and they say that the birth of the King has arrived. The Queen, however, says that it's too early and tells her son to wait, but he replies back from inside the womb and silences her, suddenly punching his way out and leaving the Queen screaming in agony.

Chapter 213 Birth (, "Tanjō") is the 213th chapter of the Hunter × Hunter manga, written and illustrated by Yoshihiro Togashi. Synopsis. Eager to be born, the King forcefully rips open the Queen's womb, causing severe injuries to his mother. All the Squadron Leaders rush to her aid when they hear her screams, but the King pays no attention to his dying mother, ordering the gathered Ants to prepare him a feast. When Peggy does not heed his order and rushes to the Queen's side without hesitation, the newly-born King beheads him with his tail. Colt looks on in terror, and the King tells them to not make him repeat himself, ordering them to prepare a feast. As the King comments on how filthy the nest is, telling them to show him a bigger and brighter room, he spots Colt and orders him to wipe the blood off his tail. Seeing an opportunity to get in the King's good graces, Turtle offers to clean it with his handkerchief, but is decapitated as well. The King once again orders Colt to clean his tail, warning him not to make him say it twice. Colt obeys as the terrified Squadron Leaders look on. After his tail is cleaned and he once again asks for his food, the three Royal Guards arrive and kneel before him, stating that his meal has been prepared. Each stresses that they are there to provide whatever he needs and to obey his every order, and the King accompanies them away from the others. The Squadron Leaders rush to the Queen's side, who is now in critical condition. Colt asks Octopus how she looks, and he says that it's very bad, revealing that several of her organs have been crushed beyond repair and that she won't last long. Desperate, Colt rushes after Neferpitou and pleads them for help, saying that their power was able to fix a certain human. Pitou slowly turns around to look at him and says that they only fixed the human because they needed him, but since the King has now been born, they don't need the Queen anymore, referring to her as a thing and leaving Colt in shock. Pitou informs the King that his meal has been prepared at the top of the nest, adding that it has a nice view. The King says that it will be faster to go from the outside, and he punches an enormous opening in the side of the nest and uses his tail to propel himself to the top, spotting something flying away from the nest. Shaiapouf follows, opening his butterfly wings and using them to gracefully fly up. Following suit, Menthuthuyoupi manifests a pair of wings on his back and tries to follow Shaiapouf, but is unable to maintain balance and crashes into the side of the nest, realizing that he needs to practice. When the King bites into the meat prepared for him, he quickly spits it out and complains that it tastes bland, saying that when he was in his mother's womb, he would occasionally be treated to a delicious meal. Neferpitou tells him that it was the meat of a rare human, and the King continues to crave it. Elsewhere, Morel and Knov are seen in a nearby cave and spot something approaching them in the distance. Knov prepares a portal for them to hide in, but Morel tells him to wait, and as the figure gets closer, it's revealed to be Colt carrying a white flag. He tells the two Hunters that the Ants will surrender on the condition that they save the Queen's life. He tells them that she can't give birth anymore and that the King has already been born, leaving Morel and Knov in shock since it's too early. As the King and his Royal Guards leave the nest, Colt describes them as evil.

Chapter 214 Results (, "Ketchaku") is the 214th chapter of the Hunter × Hunter manga, written and illustrated by Yoshihiro Togashi. Synopsis. The King and his Royal Guards continue moving away from the Chimera Ant Nest, and the former spots three humans working in a field. Dropping down, he slowly approaches a man and woman and beheads them both with a single swipe of his tail, laughing at how easily he could kill them. He takes a bite out of their flesh and immediately spits it out, complaining about how bland it is. Neferpitou approaches and informs him that the brain is the most delicious part of the human body, telling him that it would be best to kill without harming the head. The King takes this into account and kills the child, who was too shocked to run away and screams out in fear as the King's tail strikes her in the abdomen. Pitou applauds his kill, and the King eats a bit of her brain, agreeing that it was a bit tastier, but spits it out, saying that it still doesn't compare to the flesh of rare humans. Pitou tries to give him more advice, this time about how to distinguish the rare humans from the rest, but the King suddenly strikes them hard across the face with his tail. He warns Pitou to not take him as a fool and informs them that he already knows that it's possible to see the energy around the body by focusing the eyes. Pitou quickly apologizes, and the King goes on to say that he finds pleasure in not knowing whether a human is rare until he takes a bite. He says that his hunger is satisfied for now and commends Pitou's strength, revealing that he had struck them with the intention to kill. Back inside the nest, Bihorn is still shocked at how the King killed and ate his own kind. Small Bear states that the King is an entirely different creature from the rest of the Ants and that he probably considers everything aside from himself as his prey. Cheetu ponders out loud what they should do next, saying that it would be meaningless for them to continue staying in the nest if the Queen dies. The other Squadron Leaders walk in, and both Hagya and Zazan point out that staying has already become pointless since the Queen has lost her ability to reproduce. Furthermore, with the Queen no longer able to maintain her kingdom, Hagya suggests that they should all split up and individually try to become kings. Bihorn gets enraged by this idea and snaps at Hagya, questioning if he thought that he would be left free to do as he pleases. Hagya is silently supported by the other Squadron Leaders, revealing that the only ones still loyal to the Queen are Bihorn and Small Bear. In the meantime, Colt desperately begs Morel and Knov to save the Queen, reasoning that if she dies, the other Ants will no longer be tied together. Knov asks him the specifics of what would happen, and Colt replies that they would try to build kingdoms of their own, saying that the Ants would spread out and destroy local ecosystems. Morel asks if the soldier Ants can reproduce, and Knov confirms that they can forcibly mate with the females of other species, saying that there have been reports that when a Queen dies, the soldier Ants will leave the nest and begin reproducing. He doubts that Colt is lying to them, and Morel asks for his name. Colt quickly answers, and Morel says that they will take him to see their leader and that he will tell him the same story. However, he tells Colt that he can't guarantee that their leader will believe his story or, if he does believe it, spare his life. Colt does not hesitate and urges the two Hunters to hurry. As Knov opens his portal, he reminds Morel that their apprentices are supposed to arrive soon. Morel says that he almost forgot that he bet 100k on Knuckle and Shoot making it, while Knov bet a million on all five of them. Elsewhere, Gon, Killua, Shoot, and Knuckle arrive at NGL's border stop. Looking despondent, Gon gets Knuckle's attention and begs him to promise to save Kite and bring him back. Knuckle confidently says that they will, swearing on the complete token. Knuckle and Shoot leave the two boys, and with I.R.S. resting on his shoulder, Gon says that he's weak, suddenly breaking down into tears. Killua looks on in silence, and Gon begins to sob, realizing how frustrating weakness can be and causing Killua to cry as well. On the drive back to the city, Gon sits huddled up in silence, and Killua says to himself that no matter what happens, he will do anything to protect Gon for the 30 days that he can't use Nen. But he says that, in accordance with his agreement with Biscuit, the two of them will part ways after that.

Chapter 215 Last Words (, "Yuigon") is the 215th chapter of the Hunter × Hunter manga, written and illustrated by Yoshihiro Togashi. Synopsis. Chairman Netero speaks to someone over the phone and informs them that the King has already been born. He asks them to send the Chimera Ant research team and Dr. Lee so that she can assemble a team of surgeons and artificial organ specialists. After the call, he tells Morel and Knov that they will leave in four hours. He then suddenly cuts his hair and requests Colt's cooperation. Changing into his "heart" t-shirt, which Knov says Netero only wears when he fights for real, he unleashes a tremendous amount of aura and asks Colt to compare his to the King's. Morel is astonished by Netero's aura, and Colt answers that Netero probably couldn't even touch the King, adding that he would be killed by one of the Royal Guards first. Chuckling, Netero is thrilled to have a challenger at his age, and his expression becomes sinister and frightens the two Hunters. He instructs Morel to take his students and the doctors with Colt back to the Chimera Ant Nest. He begins to leave, and Morel becomes worried that he's going to fight the King by himself, but Netero assures him that he's going to see an old friend. Inside the Ants' nest, Colt learns from Bihorn and Small Bear that most of the soldiers have already left and joined other troops, with only some of them, including Koala, choosing to stay behind. Dr. Lee and her team tend to the Queen and proceed to attach artificial organs within her abdomen. Colt offers his organs and blood, but Dr. Lee explains that Chimera Ants differ in each generation, making donations impossible. She tells him that he should pray for the organs to be successful, and Colt feels helpless as he sits beside the Queen. Suddenly, the Queen starts talking telepathically. She asks if her son was born healthy, and Colt assures her that the King and his Royal Guards are looking for herbs to save her. Octopus reveals to the doctors and Hunters that the King killed and ate some of the Squadron Leaders before leaving, saying that he probably won't return since he doesn't care about the Queen's well-being at all. The Queen worries about her son being born prematurely, but Colt reassures her that he was born healthy, leaving her glad that her destiny has been fulfilled. Colt pleads with her and says that the rest of them will be lost without her, but the Queen tells him that her injuries are fatal. Colt again begs Dr. Lee to let them use his organs, but she tells him to listen to the Queen and respect her wishes. The Queen tells them that she has one last request, saying that she thought of a name for her son: Meruem, which means "light that illuminates all". She asks them to let him know, and upon revealing his name, she thinks of her beloved son and dies soon after. Colt becomes devastated, claiming that he couldn't save her again and angry that he can't save anyone. When Knov asks if something happened before, Small Bear explains that Colt must be mixing it up with his human memories, and Morel is shocked that they still have them. Small Bear explains that it can vary, but says that their previous personalities affect them greatly, with some of them even able to remember their human names. As Small Bear says that it also allowed them to learn speech so quickly, the group notices something moving inside the Queen's womb. Small Bear moves in closer, but Colt orders him not to touch her, saying that he will get it out. He reaches inside and takes out a tiny baby, holding it in the palm of his hand. The baby begins to move and cry, causing Colt himself to cry with a smile on his face. He swears to protect the baby, but Morel suddenly approaches him and holds his pipe right beside Colt's head. Knov is confused, but Morel asks Colt if he can swear that he and the baby will never eat a human, telling him to leave if he can't. But he says that if Colt can swear to it, he will protect the both of them as long as he lives. After making his promise, Morel starts to cry as well, and so does Knuckle, chuckling and saying that he inherited his soft side from his master. Colt then briefly thinks back to his human life as Kurt, with his mother and sister Reina.

Chapter 216 Republic of East Gorteau (ゴルトー, "Higashi Gorutō Kyōwakoku") is the 216th chapter of the Hunter × Hunter manga, written and illustrated by Yoshihiro Togashi. Synopsis. After dropping off Knuckle and Shoot at NGL, Gon and Killua travel back to town with Spin. Gon stands up and screams, declaring that he is over his defeat and expressing his confidence that Knuckle will be able to rescue Kite. He then resolves to get stronger to not disappoint Kite when he returns. Calmly reading a book and chewing her gum, Spin is relieved that he got over himself and says that even though Gon has known Kite longer, she and the other companions of Kite have spent more time with him. She tells Gon that she would have kicked him off the truck if he kept moping around, saying that Kite wouldn't want to see him like that and assuring Gon that Kite is still alive. She continues to explain what Kite would want to see from him, citing wits and determination, telling Gon to train right there if he's weak. While doing handstand push-ups, Gon asks her why she wants to become a Hunter. Spin explains that she needs money to pay off an enormous debt. She then asks if they know about the Small-billed Swan, explaining that it only lives near a certain mine, the reason for which is not yet known. As kids, she and Stick wanted to save them from extinction and their home from changing into an industrial site, so they bought the mountain the mine was a part of as well as the surrounding land. She says that Kite financed it for them and that he was the first grown-up to listen to them, even though they were just some little kids with nothing to their name. Their most vivid memory of their home is of thousands of swans taking flight with the rising of the sun. Kite told them that he envied them since he doesn't have a place to call home and he also doesn't know where he was born. She then tells them that she will take them there when their mission is over. Meanwhile, each of the Squadron Leaders go their separate ways: Cheetu crosses NGL's border stop and kills the humans working at the entrance, crowning himself the "King of Speed". Alligator thinks about Cheetu's speed, but says that he will take things slow, telling himself that he only cares about eating and crowning himself the "King of the Eaters" as he reaches the shore and looks out over the ocean. Some of the other Squadron Leaders are seen setting off on their own journeys to become king, with Alligator swimming through the ocean, and Hagya, Meleoron, Zazan, and Mantis all shown in various locations. Elsewhere, the King and his Royal Guards arrive at the royal palace in East Gorteau at the opposite end of the Mitene Union from NGL. The King lands in a courtyard and is given a warning to leave by the soldiers, who think that the Ants are just wearing costumes. He then goes on a rampage and easily kills them all. Inside, Ming Jol-ik—the dictator in charge of the nation—who is watching a troupe of scantily clad dancing girls perform for him while he is eating dinner, gets a call from one of the soldiers that there are intruders inside the palace. He tells them to get rid of them and not to bother him with such trifles. He continues eating and enjoying himself while he slams down the phone. The King and Royal Guards, meanwhile, come face to face with a group a strong looking soldiers, one of whom threatens the group with a painful death for stepping inside the palace. Neferpitou gets the King's attention, but he already recognizes the fact that the soldier can use Nen, saying that he felt it without even focusing his eyes. He remarks that the soldier is a "rare" and that he looks tasty. At the same time, back in the Chimera Ant Nest in NGL, Knuckle and Shoot seem to find something very disturbing.

Chapter 217 Meat Orchard (, "Niku Juen") is the 217th chapter of the Hunter × Hunter manga, written and illustrated by Yoshihiro Togashi. Synopsis. Inside East Gorteau's royal palace, the King has killed and eaten the brains of the Nen-using soldier and feels his power coursing through him and making him stronger. Neferpitou realizes that the King's ability is to absorb someone else's aura and use it as his own, saying that the more he eats, the stronger he will become. A bit later, the King and his Royal Guards proceed to where Ming Jol-ik is enjoying his dinner and entertainment. He asks them who they are as they enter, while wondering where his guards are. They ignore him, for the King finds Ming Jol-ik weak and asks his Royal Guards why Ming Jol-ik claims himself to be a king. Shaiapouf explains that it is a common feat among the humans to rise in power due to hereditary titles or their personal connections. The King replies that that is ridiculous and only imbeciles would endorse such a practice. The King states that they should keep humans on a short leash, and Neferpitou agrees, stating that as food their meat is of high quality and since they can take care of themselves, husbandry would be simple and that even the common humans are good enough to feed their soldiers. Ming Jol-ik then threatens them, telling them to get out or face his divine wrath. The King immediately kills Ming Jol-ik, leaving his mutilated body on the floor, and Pitou tells him that they will take care of the corpse since the dictator can be used to control the other humans. The King, after commenting on how quickly Ming broke apart, tells Pitou to do as they like. Some of the cowering dancers then ask for mercy from the King, but he merely laughs at them and reminds them of the fact that the prayers of the swine and cows they always slaughter also fall on deaf ears. Later, he looks outside and goes to the courtyard, looking out over it and declaring that he wants to turn it into a meat orchard for processing humans. Gon and Killua return to the apartment they share with Palm. An ominous aura leaks from within the house, and Killua thinks to himself that he should first find a way to protect Gon from Palm. They find her crouched amongst dozens of Gon-like dolls that have all been heavily slashed and cut up. She angrily reminds Gon of his promise to take her to NGL, but knows there's no point in having him swallow needles. Gon calmly asks her what he could do for her instead. Palm wants him to do anything she says, and Gon immediately agrees. Killua yells at her, saying that she has no idea what Gon has gone through. Palm then states that she wants him to go out with her, adding that she wants to be his girlfriend. Despite Killua's protests, Gon still agrees to go out with her. Palm says that there's a place she really wants to go to right now. But Gon says that he can't today, telling Palm that he needs to train with Killua and asking her to join them. This prompts another angry possessive outburst from her, in which she asks if Gon understands the meaning and importance of a first date. Calmly outwitting Palm, Gon explains to her that he needs time to properly prepare for it. She wonders how he must prepare for it, but Gon tells her that it's a secret that will be saved for the next day. Palm then calms down and agrees to meet Gon tomorrow at the bulletin board. In the gym, Killua admits that Gon is amazing at handling Palm and asks if he has ever been on a date before. Gon confirms that he has, but that most of them were with his aunt Mito. Killua then asks who the others were, and Gon explains that some ships only have all-female crews and that some of them only like going out with younger guys, adding that these women are called cougars. He says that these cougars took him into town and taught him all kinds of things, leaving Killua in disbelief. Gon then asks Killua the same question, but he claims that he has never been on a date, having spent most of his time training as an assassin and accompanying Gon after that. He then sadly thinks to himself that the two of them would have stayed together, but due to his promise to Biscuit, he can't. Gon's phone rings, and Knuckle tells him that they found and retrieved Kite.
