He then states that Kite might still be under the control of the enemy, but that there most likely will be a way to undo it. Gon celebrates this and is positive that they can find a way to get Kite back to normal. Knuckle adds that they will be back in three days and tells them to be careful since other soldier Ants have spread out in all directions. After ending the phone call, Gon cheers with joy, and Killua remarks to himself that all he needs to do is protect Gon for a month. Meanwhile, Cheetu arrives in a town to the stares of the people there, with some young women even taking photos of him with their phones. He remarks to himself that he has found a lovely feeding ground.

Chapter 218 Confession (, "Kokuhaku") is the 218th chapter of the Hunter × Hunter manga, written and illustrated by Yoshihiro Togashi. Synopsis. Gon and Killua are outside of town in a forest, where Gon is looking for some kind of gift for Palm. Killua questions if he is sure, saying that she will go berserk when she gets it. He then tells Gon they should go back to town while thinking that if a Chimera Ant finds them there, they will be done for, but if they are back in town they could make a run for it while it kills other people. Then while looking at Knuckle's I.R.S. on Gon's shoulder, he thinks about the fact that Gon can't use Nen and that he would sacrifice everything to protect him. They then see an eight-legged dog come out of the bushes, but ignore it and walk on. Meanwhile, in the suburbs of Pata City, police cars are racing towards Cheetu who has killed four people. The police surround him and give him three seconds to throw down his weapons and lie down on the ground with his hands behind his head. They start counting and, as they get to one, Cheetu smiles and prepares for their attack. Then as multiple police officers open fire upon him, he uses his incredible speed to simultaneously dodge the bullets and rip off the fingers of the shooting cops. He then throws all the fingers in his mouth and, after eating them, remarks that they are slow and clumsy and not a challenge at all. A strange gothic-looking female newscaster reports on the encounter, stating that Cheetu killed seven people in total and has escaped into the Miera Mountains at 125 mph after telling the cops to bring someone faster the next day. She further reports that nearby citizens have been given a mandatory evacuation order and that the government has made a capture request to the Hunter Association. Killua, watching this report, checks the map of the Republic of Rokario to find out that Pata City is two towns away from where they are (in Doli City), thinking that they should be fine. He then turns off the TV as Gon comes out of the shower telling him that it's his turn. The following day, Killua tells Gon that he will be at the gym all day while he goes on his date with Palm. In actuality, he disguises himself with a big knit poof-ball and large-brimmed cap. Gon meets up with Palm, who has completely altered her appearance, surprising both Gon and the stalking Killua. Gon tells Palm she looks pretty, and she gets embarrassed by this. While following them, Killua realizes that he looks like a stalker, but he shrugs this off since he is doing it to protect Gon. Palm and Gon have walked into the forest outside of town, and still tailing them, Killua notices the aura of a nearby Chimera Ant and wonders whether to warn the two, but he decides against it as he watches them sit down on two tiny foldable chairs at a nice lake. Killua thinks to himself that Gon most likely would attack any Ant without a second thought and that Palm would flip out if their date got interrupted, saying that he can't let them know about the nearby Ant and that he has to take care of it himself. At the lake with a huge tree growing out of the center, Gon gives Palm a leafless twig, telling her it is the prettiest bouquet in the world. He explains that Sea Fireflies live near brackish water and are now in their mating season. He tells her to give it a second, and the fireflies then start to land all over the twig, making it look like a bouquet of light, surprising Palm. Gon explains that the tree-sap from the twig mimics their pheromones and attracts them. Palm loves it and thanks him for it. Gon tells her that he can't give her what she wants, which is spending time together, saying that he wants to get stronger so that he can defeat the Chimera Ants and adding that he needs to train really hard. Killua, meanwhile, heads towards the aura of the Chimera Ant which he realizes is coming their way. Gon further explains to Palm that Kite will soon be back, but that they will need to fight the one who is controlling him and that he likes to focus on training, at least until the time that the Ants are exterminated. He then asks if that's alright with her, but Palm's expression completely changes as murderous aura emanates from her and she asks him what he means.

Chapter 219 Awakening (, "Kakusei") is the 219th chapter of the Hunter × Hunter manga, written and illustrated by Yoshihiro Togashi. Synopsis. Killua is leading the nearby Chimera Ant away from Palm and Gon on their date. Rammot then reveals himself, stating that he smelled a human and remembers Killua. He tells Killua that he will suffer the pains of hell and asks where Gon is, rightly deducing that since they are generally together, he must be nearby. He then says that he will just yell while swinging his severed head around in order to get Gon to come out. Killua, meanwhile, is glad he was able to lead Rammot away, but realizes that Rammot is right and that leading him away does nothing if he also can't defeat him. Illumi's aura then numbs Killua's mind and tells him to run away. He tries to fight it, but the fear takes hold of him. This excites Rammot who tells Killua that he has to kill him now and that he will crush him into a bloody pulp. Killua tries to overcome his fear, but his brother's words ring through his head telling him to avoid battles he can't win. He screams trying to overcome it, but Rammot attacks him with a massive punch, sending him flying. Rammot becomes orgasmic at the realization that Killua is paralyzed by fear, telling himself that he wants to kill him but also savoring the feeling. He then punches and kicks Killua multiple times. Killua gets up thinking he must protect Gon since he is his best friend. With a surprised expression on his face, Rammot tells him not to look at him like that since it's making him want to kill Killua immediately. Killua again feels Illumi's aura and is reminded to run away over and over again. Rammot runs over towards Killua to take off his head, which he wants to save while eating only the tongue. Killua still feels pressured to run away, but the thought of not wanting to lose to Rammot and his friendship with Gon slowly push this feeling away as he remembers all the great, wonderful and just normal times he had with Gon during their travels and adventures. Blood then squirts from Killua's head as he dodges Rammot's attack. Rammot is surprised by this, and Killua is seen bleeding from his forehead while he holds something in his closed fist. He opens his fist to reveal a tiny thin needle and tells Rammot that it has been inside of his brain all along, wondering when Illumi planted it there. A confused Rammot asks him how he got away, but he remembers that he saw Killua stab his forehead with his finger before disappearing. Killua wipes his face on his sleeve and tells Rammot that he feels much better, now that's he's fully awake and free. Rammot then looks shocked and tries to calm himself by thinking that all Killua did was move out of the way, yet he now is the one that has become paralyzed by fear. As he looks at the murderous aura coming from Killua, he "sees" a giant snake (his hare part's natural predator) baring down on him. Killua says that Rammot should tell the other Ants that they can expect to end up dead if they ever come near them again. Rammot angrily shouts out against his threat, but Killua stops him midscream by instantly ripping off his head, which continues to have its mouth wide open. Telling Rammot to die and saying that he doesn't care, Killua then crushes his head into a bloody pulp with his hand before the body even gets the chance to fall to the ground.

Chapter 22 The Last Question (の, "Saigo no Mondai") is the 22nd chapter of the Hunter × Hunter manga, written and illustrated by Yoshihiro Togashi. Synopsis. After 30 minutes, the five examinees eventually end up back inside the arena, and while Killua says that they obviously should have gone down, Leorio angrily points out that he also voted to go up. As the group runs away from a giant stone, it's stated that they had to endure trials such as a quiz with electric shocks and a life-sized backgammon board filled with mines and that they had less than one hour remaining even though they passed every challenge. With the group now exhausted, they again reach a door that simply asks them if they want to open it. However, once Leorio sees that someone voted no, he immediately grabs Tonpa by the collar and angrily rebukes him for trying to sabotage the votes. Even though Leorio doesn't believe Tonpa when he replies that he voted yes, Gon speaks up and reveals that he was the one who pressed the wrong button by mistake. Although Leorio tries to walk away, Tonpa demands an apology from him, but Leorio quickly refuses. Tonpa then points out that he isn't the only one holding back the group, reminding Leorio that he lost them 50 hours of time. Kurapika tells them to stop, but the two continue to argue, with Leorio preparing to draw his switchblade and Tonpa readying his fists. As Gon tells the two to calm down, Killua points out that the door is opening and tells them that they must be close to the exit. All five run forward and find an ominous statue hanging between two doors. Called "the Last Crossroad", it's said to be the last fork for the path, and the group is asked to vote if they are ready. Someone again votes no, but before Leorio can reprimand Tonpa, Kurapika angrily tells him that they don't have any time to waste. A voice comes from the statue and explains to the examinees that one path is long and difficult, which the whole group can take, and that the other is short and easy, which only three of them can take. The voice adds that the long path will take them at least 45 hours, while the short one will take around three minutes. It's made clear that if they vote for the short path, two of them must be chained to the wall before the door will open and that those two won't complete the exam. Leorio honestly tells the others that he plans to vote for the short route and that he isn't going to be chained to the wall, adamant that he is moving forward. With the others left speechless, he adds that the examiners planned ahead by placing weapons all around the room to help them settle the issue. However, Gon says that he will vote for the long path since it's only fair that they all pass, but Killua reminds him that they don't even have one hour left, checking his timer to see 57 minutes and 25 seconds. He agrees with Leorio's decision and says that they will have to fight it out. At the bottom of Trick Tower, 18 examinees have passed the Third Phase with three minutes and 45 seconds remaining. Another examinee arrives, but he suddenly collapses and dies from his wounds. The Amori Brothers surround his body and say that he should have given up and tried next year. Another examinee arrives, and it's announced that there is one minute remaining. Hisoka is seen staring at the door as it opens and Gon, Killua, and Kurapika arrive. Killua says that his butt hurts, and Gon adds that he didn't expect the short path to be a slide. Hisoka notes that there are only three, and it's announced that there are thirty seconds remaining. Gon is glad that they made it just in time, and as Kurapika looks at his blistered hands, Leorio and Tonpa suddenly arrive. Leorio calls it a long shot, but says that all five of them were able to make it because of the simple plan that only Gon considered. It's then revealed that all five voted for the long path and then destroyed a section of the wall in order to make their way into the short one. Kurapika comments on how effective the plan was, and Gon points out that since the taskmasters broke walls and floors with their bare hands, he guessed that they could use the weapons to do the same thing. Both Killua and Kurapika are silently impressed by Gon's quick-thinking and ingenuity. Time finally runs out, and it's announced that 25 examinees (including one deceased) have passed the Third Phase. After the group makes their way outside the tower, Lippo greets and congratulates them. He reveals that the exam has two phases left and that the Fourth Phase will take place on Zevil Island, pointing to it in the distance. The other examiner then reveals a small box, and Lippo explains that they will all draw lots. With the examinees left wondering what it will decide, Lippo smiles and reveals that it will determine who they will hurt and who will hunt them.

Chapter 220 Reunion: Part 1 (①, "Saikai (Ichi)") is the 220th chapter of the Hunter × Hunter manga, written and illustrated by Yoshihiro Togashi. Synopsis. Killua returns to the lake where Gon and Palm were having their date, but finds that the two are gone and have left their stuff behind. This worries Killua, who wonders if another Ant has found them. He quickly returns to town and the room they share to find Gon on the ground writing a hundred calligraphy apology notes, while an angry Palm with a knife in her hand watches him do so. She turns to look at Killua who asks her what she is doing, and she explains that she is punishing him for hurting her feelings. Relieved that the two are safe, he replies that she is making unreasonable demands. She tells him to stay out of it since it has nothing to do with him, but Killua responds by telling her the same and demanding she leaves. She asks him about his cuts, and after he tells her that he got them while training, she suddenly attacks him and says that she will give him more. For a split second, it looks like she stabbed Killua in the head, but he casually dodges her, saying that he could even dodge her knife in his sleep. This pushes her over the edge, and she goes ballistic and charges at him with the intent to kill. Killua then picks up Gon and starts running away while daring her to try and catch them. While running, Killua argues with Gon about Palm, telling him they never need to see her again and that they can just meet up with Knuckle, adding that he needs to take her seriously since he doesn't have his Nen right now. But Gon defends Palm by saying that she will just get angrier with them later and he should get back to her. Killua worries about Palm backstabbing Gon, but Gon laughs it off and says Palm wouldn't do it, leaving Killua flabbergasted considering what she just tried to do to him. Crazed and back in her room, Palm reveals that they can't get away from her, proudly saying that she can find them anywhere. She then pulls out a strange object. She sets it down upon a desk, revealing it to be an orbuculum (crystal ball) held up by a creepy, dried-up merman corpse. Palm scratches open her wrist and forearm with her own nails until she is bleeding from multiple spots and then feeds her own blood to the dead merman while asking it to show her were Killua is. The merman shudders as it ingests her blood and a picture then starts to appear in the orbuculum, showing that Killua and Gon are in front of the hotel by the train station. After seeing this, Palm starts blaming Killua for everything that went wrong while she pulls out over 40 knives and ties them together with ropes which she hangs all around her neck and torso. Palm then steps outside ready to go after them, but is suddenly confronted by Knov, who calmly asks her where they went. She tells him and he relays the information that Gon and Killua are at the Tri-Orb Hotel to Morel, who tells Knov that the boys just called him. Knov tells Palm that he will observe them and find out if they can handle seeing Kite as he is now. He states that she used her ability without his permission and berates her for not following his orders and not being prepared for the unexpected. He then tells Palm to understand that her blood is a limited resource and she should only use it for him. She agrees to this while thinking that Knov is the only one for her. Knov then asks about her getup, but she laughs it away and says it's nothing. In the hotel, Killua tells Gon that he should tell Palm to wait until they save Kite, but Gon responds that he already tried that. It's stated that Gon has been dumped without any warning and that the 12-year-old Gon with blood type B was briefly forced to date the 22-year-old Palm with blood type A. Elsewhere, Cheetu is running along on a deserted highway when Knuckle tries to punch him but misses. Smoke then starts billowing up all around them as a large pipe is swung right at Cheetu's head. Cheetu, however, quickly dodges and, seeing Morel as the one connected to it, releases a flurry of rapid strikes upon him and Knuckle. Cheetu says that the two of them are only a little better than the guys he fought yesterday. Back at the hotel, it's shown that Shoot is the one observing Gon and Killua.

Chapter 221 Reunion: Part 2 (②, "Saikai (Ni)") is the 221st chapter of the Hunter × Hunter manga, written and illustrated by Yoshihiro Togashi. Synopsis. Cheetu is facing Morel and Knuckle on a deserted highway. He tells them that he knows they were waiting for him and that he will beat them at their own game, without giving them the chance to strike back. Knuckle smiles at him and replies saying that his punches are weak since they do not weight them, adding that he couldn't kill him and Morel even with 10,000 of them. Cheetu ignores Knuckle's insult and assumes that he is too proud to admit defeat. The Chimera Ant then starts running all around the Hunters, punching them while they are unable to hit him back. Cheetu laughs about them swinging after the strike and tells them that he isn't even putting effort into his speed and power yet. Knuckle then almost hits him accurately in the face, and this surprises Cheetu since Knuckle can't even follow him with his eyes. Morel then nearly hits him with his pipe and Cheetu, again surprised, realizes that even though they have only been fighting for a minute, both of them have already adjusted to his speed. The Ant, finding it fun that they can do this and thinking it's worth playing with his food, tells them that they can't react fast enough and, as inferior beings, wonders if they'll try to match his speed with guns or by recruiting more Hunters. Knuckle smiles again and tells Cheetu that they will make up the difference with wits and experience. Morel then blows out more smoke, making Cheetu wonder if it could be poison or sleeping gas, but after seeing that they are breathing it too, he rejects these notions and wonders if this is Morel's ability. Morel taunts him by asking if he is scared and giving him the chance to run away. Cheetu laughs and asks if it means that he won't, then deducing that it's a smokescreen that they'll use as cover to attack. He tells them to show him what they got as Knuckle is about to punch him. Cheetu sees it from the corner of his eye and dodges, only to become surrounded on all sides by numerous Knuckles. Surprised by this, he doesn't notice one of them hitting him hard in his side and pushing him away. The smoke clones of Knuckle created by Morel then disappear, and Knuckle tells Cheetu that people freeze when they are startled and this wouldn't work a second time, but one time is enough for him. Cheetu asks Knuckle why he thinks this, for he was caught by surprise but it didn't hurt him. Knuckle's A.P.R. then shows up floating beside Cheetu's shoulder, making him wonder what it is and why it calls out that he has accrued interest. Knuckle taunts him, and Cheetu continues to demand the answer, but Knuckle disappears into the smoke, and as Cheetu moves toward him, Morel sticks his leg out from the smoke and trips the Ant. With a grin, Morel tells him that now that he's blinded by rage, making him stumble is easy. Cheetu completely loses his cool and screams at them in anger, but as the smoke disappears, so have Morel and Knuckle and all he can do is ask them where they went. A.P.R. then tells him it is time and that he has accrued interest while showing him the number 375. Angered, Cheetu decides to leave A.P.R. in his dust regardless of what it is, running away as quickly as he can. Morel and Knuckle then come out of the bushes beside the road, and Morel remarks that Cheetu can't cope with Zetsu, which they used to hide their presence. Knuckle responds that Cheetu is a newbie, and Morel tells him to keep his guard up and not underestimate him. Knuckle explains that A.P.R. will give him Cheetu's general location and that they can chase him down, close in, and kill him. Surprised, Morel states that he thought A.P.R. loses its effect once it gets too far away. Knuckle explains that it stops accruing interest, but it won't disappear and will start counting down again when he gets close to his target, adding that he doesn't need it to make it change to I.R.S. Morel quickly rebukes him, saying that even if they know his pitches, it isn't a guarantee against striking out and that someone else will be better suited to fight him. Knuckle agrees with his master and wonders how Gon is doing. Coming to a stop in a forest, Cheetu realizes that being fast isn't good enough to get rid of A.P.R. since it involves Nen, knowing that he has to use something besides speed. Meanwhile, in the Tri-Orb Hotel, Killua says that Gon got a rare prize, while Shoot is seen watching the two from behind a corner.

Chapter 222 Reunion: Part 3 (③, "Saikai (San)") is the 222nd chapter of the Hunter × Hunter manga, written and illustrated by Yoshihiro Togashi. Synopsis. Inside a storeroom of a big castle, Killua and Gon have met up with Knov, Knuckle, and Shoot. They get told that Kite is in the floating cage next to Shoot and that he isn't the same anymore. Gon replies it is okay and that they will put him right. The cage is lowered to the ground and the gate on it is opened as a tiny Kite slowly walks out of it. Shoot explains that this cage is his ability, Hotel Rafflesia, which allows him to trap either individual parts or a person's whole body after he has dealt it a certain amount of damage. He states that a person will return to their normal size once released. Killua immediately understands what happened to his eye earlier. Shoot warns them to be careful, for even though Kite can't use Nen, he is still is an adversary. Kite returns to his normal size and his arms, hands, and torso are covered in scars. A strange aura comes from him which surprises Gon and Killua. Kite grinds his teeth while looking at them from beneath his long hair. His face is also scarred up and one of his eyes is slacked over while the other is bulging out. This shocks and saddens Gon, who sees Kite in full looking like a rag doll, and Knuckle explains that they assume he was being used as a training tool for the soldier Ants because he automatically attacks anything that approaches. Killua gives Kite a sad look, while Gon tells Kite that he is safe now as he walks over to him. As he gets close, Kite hits him straight in the face, which slightly shocks both Knuckle and Killua. With a sad look on his face and as the wound begins to bleed, Gon remembers that Kite hasn't hit him since that day they met on Whale Island. He then allows himself to be hit some more, while Knuckle and Shoot look on disgruntled. Morel questions the group and asks if they really want to let this go on since Gon can't use Nen. Killua replies that Gon will quickly figure out Kite's attack pattern if he hasn't already and starts to imply that Gon is letting himself get hit intentionally. Knov follows his train of thought and states that Gon is taking the punches intentionally while suppressing his reflexes to dodge and parry. Knuckle wonders if it is really possible for Gon to have figured out his pattern within a couple of minutes. Killua responds that Gon doesn't know what else to do now that he is faced with the reality they helped create. Switching over to Gon's perspective, he is indeed anticipating Kite's moves and understands that he is moving like a machine. He then gets angry about how weak this version of Kite is. He then dodges one of his punches which he considers way too weak and then hugs Kite around his waist to the shock of Knuckle and Shoot. Gon then apologizes to Kite for what has happened to him, stating it is his and Killua's fault. With a sad expression on his face, Gon further tells him that he can rest now and to leave the rest to them. Killua is then taken aback as Neferpitou's Nen puppet technique appears above Kite's body, which Gon can't see due to Knuckle's I.R.S. Knuckle explains that this is Level 2, which gets activated when someone touches Kite. He goes on to explain that you need advanced fighting skills to beat him now and that even though his technique has sealed Kite's Nen, the puppeteer is the Nen of the person controlling Kite. He then warns Gon to watch out, stating that he will attack again when he is touched. Gon starts to ask what he should do, but then asks him how they stopped him. Shoot looking slightly contrite tells him they had to wound him severely and apologizes to Gon for doing this. He goes on to reiterate that if you keep away from him, Kite won't attack. Gon clenches his fists and walks away from Kite, promising that they will put him right. Then looking at Killua with a fierce gaze that startles Knuckle, he swears to them and himself that he will take on Pitou personally. Knuckle then asks Killua what they did to change so much in a short time. Killua responds that they did nothing, saying that the Ants were the ones who changed them.

Chapter 223 10: Part 1 (10—①, "Jū (Ichi)") is the 223rd chapter of the Hunter × Hunter manga, written and illustrated by Yoshihiro Togashi. Synopsis. A train is going along a mountain track. On it, Morel asks Knov if it was alright that they brought Gon and Killua along, for it breaks their promise to Netero. Knov replies by stating that the selection was to see who would go to NGL, and since they are now going to East Gorteau, they aren't technically breaking the promise. Morel responds that he is splitting hairs, and Knov questions if they should turn them back. Morel remarks that there is a tiger in Gon now and that he will straighten out his own messes. Meanwhile, Gon and Killua are talking about something in the background. Shoot responds that he is sure about Killua but not about Gon, for he seems deflated even though the fire in his eyes was impressive, adding that he loses focus and there is no consistency in his power. Morel replies that there is a method in Gon's madness, saying that he'll be at his best when the chips are down, for his motivation is like a coiled spring. Knuckle wonders what he means by this, and Morel explains that Gon is saving everything up to unleash it all upon his enemy. And they will soon see where he stands since he gets his Nen back the following day. Morel then looks out of the window of the train heading towards a city in the distance. In a bar in a rough part of the city, everyone is seen listening to a news broadcast. The female news broadcaster talks about what is going on in East Gorteau. She reports that Ming Jol-ik has made another speech in which he has called upon the entire population to come to the capital within ten days to celebrate the founding of the nation. She and another broadcaster discuss if there is a precedent for this, and she explains that there have been other rallies, but those lasted only a day, and hospital workers and public servants were exempt from attending these and this led to them having about 70% attendance. This new one, however, will last three days and everyone is required to attend, including infants and the weak. Ming Jol-ik is shown giving a speech while surrounded by clapping generals as he is being controlled by Neferpitou's puppeteer Nen ability. The other newscaster goes on to state that the waving of transportation fares is also unusual and that the rally is most likely for another purpose than all previous rallies. He goes on to speculate when asked by his colleague that Ming Jol-ik might be announcing a successor and/or ceding political power or that it might be a diversion to distract people from something else, for Ming stepping down is impossible. The female broadcaster states that the world will be watching what happens in ten days before moving on to the next item. Morel tells the group that Colt thinks they will be sorting the entire population. Knov goes on to state that they already know how to awaken Nen by force and that even though they don't know what they are going to use the population for, they are sure 99% of the population will die in the process and this must be prevented at all costs. Killua then asks him what Netero is doing, and Knov answers that he has infiltrated East Gorteau already, but there hasn't been any word from him since then. Killua wonders if Netero is already dead, and Knov explains that they were told to assume the worst if they don't hear from him today. Knov's phone then rings and it is the Chairman, making Morel wonder if he has satellite dishes for ears. Knov tells them Netero knew that Gon and Killua were brought along as well as Morel's comment. The message Knov received reads: ""Split up in three teams of two and lure the Royal Guards away from the King. Commence at midnight sharp, the night before the rally. From: the old man with satellite ears."" Morel replies to this by stating that Netero is supernatural for sure. At night the next day, Gon sees I.R.S. for the first time and it tells him that he hates to say goodbye, but that the 30 days are up so he has to split. disappearing in a puff of smoke. Knuckle tells him that he can use his Nen again, and Gon activates it. Morel looks at it and tells him he isn't up to the challenge, wanting to see his resolve. He then undoes his tie and tells Gon to pretend that he is the enemy who tortured Kite, saying that if his punch isn't good enough, he is going to call in a replacement Hunter. Knuckle knows Morel is playing the bad cop for he has approved of Gon long ago, he then tells Gon to show him his Jajanken without holding back. Morel throws away his shirt while telling Gon he fails if he holds back or hesitates. Then, as Gon walks towards him, Morel hulks out revealing an extreme amount of muscle. Gon closes his eyes and remembers Pitou attacking Kite and the state he currently is in. He looks at Morel with extreme hatred as Killua, Knuckle, Shoot, Knov, and Palm (who was in the background for everything that happened previously) look on. Gon gathers his Nen in his right hand and begins to summon Rock to attack Morel, who is terrified by Gon's power. Killua, however, reaches out towards Gon, placing his hand on Gon's shoulder while telling him it is enough. Then looking at a sweaty Morel, he asks if he agrees; stunned by the power gathered by Gon, Morel agrees. Gon snaps out of it and thanks Killua, apologizing to Morel for almost killing him. Morel grinds his teeth, then smiles and starts laughing, saying that Gon wins and that he has just the right touch of lunacy. He puts his shirt back on while telling them that they will split up for now and to fulfill their mission however they like. Gon and Killua will take on Neferpitou as they requested, while Knuckle and Shoot will take on Menthuthuyoupi. He wishes them good luck as the matchups are laid out: Killua and Gon versus Neferpitou; Knuckle and Shoot versus Menthuthuyoupi; Knov, Palm, and Morel versus Shaiapouf; and finally, Netero versus Meruem.

Chapter 224 10: Part 2 (10—②, "Jū (Ni)") is the 224th chapter of the Hunter × Hunter manga, written and illustrated by Yoshihiro Togashi. Synopsis. A female reporter is broadcasting a news story on the alleged mysterious animals sightings. These sightings are set apart from others of their kind due to the increasing number of victims and the shocking footage, giving the world tangible proof of their existence. The broadcast switches to an on-the-scene reporter interviewing several witnesses, most of whom are police officers. One of the officers interviewed is a man named Tsukuma who lost both his legs and an eye to a lobster-like cryptid. Recorded footage shows Bloster walking amidst the dead bodies and cut limbs of many police officers. The studio reporter says there are many similar incidents of these creatures, whose standard features are their savagery and capacity for human speech. The most famous example is the lion-man of Nebaska, who sat down for an interview and talked at length about his underdeveloped theory of an imperial rule while the freelance reporter patiently listened. When she inquired whether he was honest, he bit off her upper body in one bite, proving that the Ants were not humans in a costume. The studio reporter tells the people they shared this report to warn them and state that the monsters are real. The sighting of these creatures has been limited to the Yorbian Continent, but they will likely spread to the other continents, and so far, no method of stopping them has been found. It warns the viewers not to approach these creatures and to retreat to safety immediately. Phantom Troupe members Shalnark, Phinks, Feitan, Bonolenov, Shizuku, and Kalluto arrive in Meteor City and hear about the news regarding the Chimera Ants from a television store in front of which a man is smoking a pipe. They discuss the Ants and the fact that they probably have human DNA mixed in. Shizuku states that they most likely came from the Balsa Islands. Phinks wonders why they would leave their nest and wander, and Shizuku replies they might somehow be attracted to the scent of garbage in Meteor City, but Phinks thinks there is no coincidence. Shizuku responds that both NGL and East Gorteau have isolationist policies just like Meteor City, making the conditions the same. They walk through a giant waste dump, which Shalnark notes has not changed whatsoever. Three people wearing hazmat suits approach them and inform them that there are over 300 deaths, including suicide bombers, but nothing works against the creatures. They also tell them that the assembly is divided over the definition of death. The Troupe members are led to a church that houses some of the dead, revealing that some have become Chimera Ant-human monstrosities. Phinks asks what the problem is since they are clearly dead. The man reveals that some do not stay dead and go over to their side. The assembly wants to mark them as dead if there is no way to turn them back. Phinks, partially annoyed and happy, remarks that the assembly hasn't changed as they debate things like that instead of retaliating. He tells them they'll do things their own way, namely mowing down everyone who interferes and getting rid of the so-called "Queen" by the end of the day. The queen's enormous palace made of webs is shown in the distance. She declares herself queen, stating that those who defy her will be put to death, while the chosen will be given permanent residence in paradise. The queen is then shown and revealed to be Zazan. She states that her mother's greatest failure was to lay eggs and build her army that way, which she considers ineffective and says that her only success was creating her. Zazan's servants bring another captured human, who pleads with her to kill him. She calls him lively and full of promise, and then with her Queen Shot Nen ability, injects Chimera Ant DNA into his neck, and he is easily changed into a hybrid, now loyal to her. Her handmaidens welcome him to paradise and bid him to swear loyalty to the queen. He does this by kissing Zazan's feet. Zazan smiles, being content in her role as the true queen. She then thinks that with her Queen Shot ability, she will rule the world. The Troupe members reach the front of the palace, and Shalnark asks whether they should just walk in through the front door, which Phinks agrees sounds good.

Chapter 225 10: Part 3 (10—③, "Jū (San)") is the 225th chapter of the Hunter × Hunter manga, written and illustrated by Yoshihiro Togashi. Synopsis. The Phantom Troupe members enter the Chimera Ant palace and discover that there are no guards at the entrance. They begin to choose different routes, which briefly confuses Kalluto. Phinks explains that splitting up is more efficient for both them and Kalluto to hide their Nen abilities from each other. It will be a race to find the Queen, and whoever kills her first will be the acting leader of the Troupe. The Troupe members scatter. Pike has sensed them from the get-go and immediately reports back to Zazan. She questions if they are strong, and Pike tells her they are and she orders him to go after them. He insists on staying by her side to protect her, but Zazan claims she is confident that Pike will defeat them. Feeling praised, Pike sets off to hunt the Spiders. Zazan gets up from her throne, and one of her handmaids asks if she is going to join the fray, and she tells her that it was her mother's misfortune to never enjoy the fun of combat. Bonolenov encounters a spiky Chimera Ant along the way. The Chimera Ant instantly attacks him, removing his bandages in the process. Bonolenov is then shown to have several holes across his body, as he begins to dance gracefully and emit music from the holes. He is revealed to be descended from the Gyudondond Tribe, a small tribe chased out of their lands, whose members use needles to poke a hole through their children's bodies from age three. Bonolenov uses his Battle Cantabile: The Prologue Nen ability against his opponent. His melody is transformed into strength, and he pierces his opponent with a strange weapon and states that his tribe is the most graceful in battle. The Ant is unharmed, but insults Bonolenov's tribe, saying that their soul is mediocre. Bonolenov drops his boxing gloves, revealing all the holes in his hands and fingers. He angrily tells him that he can't take that back and that the ramblings of a beast mean nothing to him. Elsewhere, the other Troupe members have found their opponents. Phinks confronts a gorilla-like Chimera Ant with several weapons, and the Ant asks what he is going to use to attack. Phinks answers a punch, which surprises the Ant, and as he rears up for a punch, then states that it should take about 15, confusing the Ant. Pike finds Shizuku and is locked in a battle with her. His web is caught up in Shizuku's conjured vacuum cleaner, Blinky. She wonders about his thread while he wonders where the vacuum cleaner came from. Shalnark plans to stick his antenna into a large beetle-like Chimera Ant, but wonders how he will accomplish piercing its shell. Finally, Feitan has found Zazan. He asks about the Queen, and Zazan proudly claims that he is looking at her. Feitan then states that it is not a funny joke, a remark which enrages her. Kalluto is spying on the other members of the Troupe, using his paper dolls and the pieces of paper attached to each Spider and allowing him to hear all their conversations. When he discovers that Feitan has reached the Queen, he plans to move out. However, a humanoid beetle-like Chimera Ant with a steel rope confronts him. The Ant is surprised to find a little girl and tells him that he must take her by force. Left with no choice, Kalluto prepares for battle, stating he is in a hurry.

Chapter 226 10: Part 4 (10—④, "Jū (Yon)") is the 226th chapter of the Hunter × Hunter manga, written and illustrated by Yoshihiro Togashi. Synopsis. Kalluto brings out his paper fan and confetti, and uses the wind to manipulate the paper towards his enemy. As the confetti sticks onto his body, the Small Beetle mocks Kalluto for his weak attack. Kalluto continues whirling his fan, surrounding his opponent with more confetti. Agitated, the Ant uses his steel rope to attack, yet Kalluto uses his fan to cut it apart easily. Kalluto uses his Dance of the Serpent's Bite ability to dismember his opponent, while also warning the Ant that he will remove his right arm next. Elsewhere, Shalnark struggles to stick his antenna into the large beetle-like Chimera Ant. Once he realizes that the Ant's claws are sharp, he deduces that he has a 20% chance to escape without injury. He takes some damage, but successfully stabs the Ant with his antenna. He pulls out his cell phone to begin controlling it, but suddenly gets trapped between the claws of his opponent, leaving him confused since the Ant should have been under his command. Another Chimera Ant named Boki arrives, who controls Pell using a remote controller, guessing that Shalnark is also a Manipulator and that sticking an antenna into an opponent is one of his conditions. Shalnark realizes that his ability didn't activate because Pell is already being controlled by Boki, who confirms this and says that he will now take him to the queen. Shalnark is unable to escape Pell's clutches and says that he has no choice, even though he doesn't feel like using it. With a free punch, Phinks begins winding his arm while counting. At fifteen, he punches the gorilla-like Chimera Ant and kills him in the process. As he looks down on his kill, Phinks admonishes himself that half of his Ripper Cyclotron would have been enough to defeat his enemy. Later, he flips a coin to choose the next path he will take. Finally, Feitan and Zazan encounter each other and proceed to fight. Feitan uses his incredible speed and sword umbrella to attack the self-proclaimed queen. As Zazan's shirt is ripped apart by his attack, she comments on his hidden sword and says that Feitan likes to conceal things under his clothing. Feitan says that the two of them think alike since it's only common to assume so when someone wears baggy clothing.

Chapter 227 10: Part 5 (10—⑤, "Jū (Go)") is the 227th chapter of the Hunter × Hunter manga, written and illustrated by Yoshihiro Togashi. Synopsis. The Gun-toting Ant and Bonolenov continue their battle as the Chimera Ant attempts to hit Bonolenov but never manages to make contact. Suddenly the Ant stops and Bonolenov asks why since it was aiming to stop his performance. Making a dash for the exit, the Ant leaves the room, intending to find Pike and have him tie Bonolenov up in silk to stop him from creating any more sounds. Bonolenov goes on the offensive and uses Battle Cantabile: Jupiter to summon a giant boulder with an appearance similar to the planet Jupiter and squashes the Ant underneath it. The impact creates a large shockwave that rumbles the colony and leaves a massive crater where it landed. Bonolenov stands over the Ant's corpse and says it was a fitting end for a bug. Elsewhere, Kalluto has also defeated his adversary but chides himself for taking too long, saying he had a bad habit of toying with his prey which he has to stop. Meanwhile, Shalnark is still in Pell's clutches and asks Boki what will become of him. Boki responds that he will become a slave who will work for the queen until he dies, and then snidely remarks that it will not be much different from how he is right now. Shalnark responds that while that may be true, there is one crucial difference and that is who he is working for. Saying that he would rather die than become a yes-man for someone he doesn't even like, Shalnark rebuffs Boki's remark. Boki says that he is quite bold for someone who can only move his lips, and Shalnark bluntly retorts that he can move his fingers and left leg as well, annoying Boki even further. Losing patience, Boki attempts to take control of Shalnark. Still, before he can do so, the Spider stabs himself with an extra antenna he always carries around for emergencies. Pulling out his cell phone, Shalnark turns autopilot on for the antenna and enters a new form, bursting with aura and leaving Boki stunned. Eliminating both Pell and Boki in one swoop, Shalnark returns to normal. As soon as he switches back, the transformation immediately begins to take its toll on Shalnark, who says he will be too sore to move for a couple of days. He says this was why he hates using that mode despite its power, since the backlash is so strong. He also notes that he never remembers what he does while in that state, so he never feels a sense of accomplishment. Elsewhere, Shizuku continues her battle with Pike as she tries to find an opening against her opponent. She summons her vacuum to help evade another of Pike's attacks, much to his frustration as he says he is having difficulty catching her in his threads. Determined to catch Shizuku, Pike jumps up to the ceiling and uses his special move Love Shower to create a net of silk that surrounds Shizuku on all sides. The net closes in, and Pike finally captures Shizuku. As she struggles against the binding, he gloats to her and says that not even Bihorn with his super strength, could cut through his threads. Dragging her along, he tells her that he will now offer her to his queen Zazan, hoping she will be happy. Suddenly he notices that his burden has gotten much lighter and turns around to receive a flurry of attacks. Shizuku jumps back, and he sees that she has taken off her clothes and escaped, surmising that she used them and the vacuum to keep the silk off her skin and then squeezed through the gaps in the thread while rematerializing Blinky once she was out. Pike points out that she will not be able to use the same trick to escape again, to which Shizuku responds that he will not be able to catch her again either as she now knows the range and speed of his silk and how he twitches twice before shooting out his special move. Shizuku then declares that she and Blinky have won. Meanwhile, Feitan continues his battle against Zazan, blocking a flurry of blows from her stinger. Yelling out that he is no match for her, Zazan tells Feitan to return when he gets his act together. To her surprise, Feitan agrees, saying that he has gotten out of shape, but then Zazan's mood quickly sours as he says that she is good practice and prepares to continue fighting her.

Chapter 228 10: Part 6 (10—⑥, "Jū (Roku)") is the 228th chapter of the Hunter × Hunter manga, written and illustrated by Yoshihiro Togashi. Synopsis. Pike begins to laugh and says Shizuku is even dumber than he is. Asking her how she expects to win when she said she would run, Pike scoffs at her. Shizuku replies that she said she would only be keeping her distance and not running. With Pike confused and merely giving her a dumbfounded stare, she tells him that she will show him the difference and orders Blinky to suck up all his blood. Blinky begins to suck up all of Pike's blood through the wounds Shizuku had given him right after escaping, much to his shock. He spews some silk at her to stop her but she evades, as his blood continues to be drained. Pike begins to feel dizzy and then has the idea to use all his limbs to cover up the wounds. However, as he does so he finds that he has more wounds than he can cover-up. Shizuku tells him that she wounded him in twenty-nine carefully chosen spots so that he would be unable to plug them up even with his extra limbs. Blinky finishes sucking up all of his blood and Pike shrivels up, falling unconscious. Shizuku begins to run away, but is suddenly struck with a revelation and runs back to Pike. She tells him that if he had covered himself up with his own silk, then it would have stopped the bleeding. This leads her to call the both of them stupid. Meanwhile, Feitan continues his battle with Zazan, managing to parry and evade the flurry of attacks the queen makes with her stinger. Kalluto looks on in awe at the speed of their exchanges, barely able to keep up with their movements. The other Spiders look on at the battle and note that Feitan's movements have improved, but are still nowhere near his peak capabilities. Kalluto is shocked that they had all arrived so much earlier than him that they had even gotten comfortable on the sidelines. Staring at the battle, Kalluto accepts with a smirk that he's nowhere near their level. Shizuku then arrives wearing her torn clothes, and the others are surprised to see her in a battered condition, asking her what happened. She responds that she had trouble with Pike, and Phinks asks her if she lost, to which she snappily retorts that she didn't. Turning their attention back to Feitan, the Spiders continue analyzing the fight and Shizuku notes that Zazan is quite powerful and must be the queen. She then reiterates that Feitan is moving poorly, with Kalluto thinking irritably that he has heard that before and being self-conscious that he was barely able to keep up with even this inferior movement and has far to go. Feitan then sheathes his blade back into his umbrella and closes it. He creates a large number of afterimages and attacks Zazan from behind. She catches it with her stinger and exasperatedly notes that he is getting quicker and that the rest of the Spiders are beginning to flock over, meaning her men have all been defeated. Feitan then presses a button at the bottom of his umbrella handle, and the tip of the umbrella shoots forward, wounding Zazan's face right next to her left eye. Enraged at this scarring of her face, Zazan rips off her stinger and transforms into a more lizard-like form, growing a new tail and gaining a considerable amount of muscle. Feitan takes advantage of Zazan taking her eyes off him by swooping behind her and attacking with Ko right at the back of her neck. However, his blade snaps on contact with her, and she fires off a weak blast of aura at him, tearing the front of his shirt. Phinks notes that Feitan's Ko attack backfired as that left him defenseless and even the weak emission from Zazan dealt severe damage. Zazan laughs and says her body is indestructible, while Kalluto asks if they should help Feitan, but Phinks says that it is a race and the next person could give it a try if Feitan failed. As the Spiders argue over who will get to fight Zazan in case Feitan loses, Kalluto asks himself what is wrong with them and calls them a bunch of freaks.

Chapter 229 10: Part 7 (10—⑦, "Jū (Nana)") is the 229th chapter of the Hunter × Hunter manga, written and illustrated by Yoshihiro Togashi. Synopsis. The other Spiders continue to watch the fight between Feitan and Zazan, and with a coin toss, it's decided that Bonolenov will fight her next if Feitan loses. Kalluto realizes how much he underestimated the Phantom Troupe, but stays resolved in working his way up through their ranks. He adds that he wants to get his brother back, no matter long it takes, and a family photo is shown with all the Zoldyck sons and their mother, along with an unknown sibling facing the other way in the background. In the midst of the fight, Feitan's left arm is suddenly broken, and Phinks playfully asks if he wants to switch with Bonolenov. Aura begins swelling around Feitan, and he angrily uses an unknown language as he spits out blood. The other Spiders realize how serious he is, and head for cover as they tell a confused Kalluto to do the same. Shizuku says they tried to watch once and were almost killed. Phinks says his ability is activated by rage, and that this one would completely destroy them if they stayed close by. Kalluto is intrigued by the fact that his ability could have different forms and hesitates to follow the others. Feitan is then shown in an elaborate outfit covering his whole body, with only his eyes and nose visible. Zazan is confused about the change, but focuses on the fact that his strength has greatly increased. As Feitan says he will pay back the pain and turn it into heat, a large ball taking the form of a sun begins to rise up into the air above Zazan. The Rising Sun variant of his Pain Packer ability slowly burns Zazan to a crisp as Feitan mocks her and laughs maniacally. The ability ends, and Feitan tells her that she could have had a quicker death if she had hurt him more. The Troupe members begin to make their way out of Zazan's palace, walking past the numerous Chimera Ants she created. Phinks believes they're no longer under her control, and one of the Ants approaches and begs them to kill him. The other Ants do the same, and Phinks gleefully refuses and tells them that they are still natives of Meteor City, ordering them to show that they still have some spirit left. After the Spiders ready their weapons, Phinks and one of the Ants rush toward one another. Back in Meteor City, Phinks is upset that the elders are now arguing about whether they should go after the real Queen. He plans to stay put and kill any more Ants that come near the city, saying that killing "survivors" leaves an awful aftertaste. Shalnark's phone suddenly rings, with Phinks desperate to know if it's Chrollo, but Shalnark says it's Nobunaga and that he wants them to help him with something. Phinks gets even more upset at having to wait and Shalnark and Feitan give him a hard time about acting like a girl with a crush, which causes Phinks to throw pieces of rubble at the two as they run away from him. In East Gorteau, Meruem sits in the throne room of the palace, with nine days left until the sorting.

Chapter 23 Two Enemies (の, "Futari no Teki") is the 23rd chapter of the Hunter × Hunter manga, written and illustrated by Yoshihiro Togashi. Synopsis. Lippo tells the examinees that they will draw lots to determine the hunter and the hunted. He explains that the box has 24 cards with their badge numbers and that they will draw one each. He tells them that they will draw lots in the order in which they passed the Third Phase, and Hisoka is the first to pull a card out of the box. After the remaining 23 examinees each draw a card, Lippo assures them that the tabulator has recorded the badge numbers and that they can dispose of the card if they wish. As Lippo reveals that the examinee whose badge number is on their card is their target, Gon slowly flips his card to find the number 44. Lippo then tells them that their objective is to collect the badges of other examinees, explaining that the badge of their specified target is worth three points and that their own badge is worth three points if they are able to keep it. He adds that all other badges are worth one point and that they need at least six points to reach the final phase of the exam. Lippo finishes his explanation and tells the examinees to enjoy their time on Zevil Island. With the examinees now on board a boat, a female official from the Hunter Association congratulates their passing of the Third Phase and tells them that it will take around two hours to reach the island. She also joyfully reveals that they have all received an unconditional invitation to the next exam if they don't pass the current one, but the examinees are so focused on the current task that they barely react to the news. With many of them wondering who has their badge number, it's stated that most of them had already removed their badges and hidden them, waiting in silence and avoiding eye contact. The official tells them to relax and enjoy the voyage before awkwardly moving to another part of the boat. As Gon sits alone on the boat, Killua approaches him and sits down beside him, eventually asking what badge number he has. Gon replies that it's a secret and asks Killua the same question. The two sit in awkward silence before putting on smiles and feeling relieved. Killua assures Gon that he didn't draw his number, and Gon says the same to Killua. The two then reveal their targets on the count of three, with Gon showing #44 and Killua #199. Killua can't believe how bad Gon's luck is, and Gon wonders who has the #199 badge. Killua replies that he doesn't know either and that no one bothered to memorize the numbers, adding that most had already hidden their badges when he scanned the crowd. Killua suddenly notices Gon's expression and tightly gripped hands, wondering if he's scared or excited. Gon replies that it may be both, knowing that he would easily lose in a normal duel against Hisoka but that it's possible to "win" if he only has to steal his badge. However, even given his skill level, he is left unsure about his chances and says that he can only try, again clenching his hands together. Killua then stands up and wishes good luck to both of them before riding away on his skateboard, with Gon giving him a parting thumbs-up. As the boat reaches Zevil Island, the female official explains that they will disembark in the order in which they completed the Third Phase, with two-minute intervals between each examinee. She adds that they will be left on the island for one week, accumulate the necessary six points, and then return to the landing site. As Hisoka makes his way into the island's forests, both Kurapika and Leorio realize the advantage that he has since he can hide and watch where everyone else goes, especially his target. Agon is the seventh to disembark, Imori the fifteenth, and Killua the twenty-first. Gon then disembarks two minutes after Killua and says that he needs to prioritize finding Hisoka. However, he suddenly senses something behind him, but sees nothing when he turns around, telling himself that he must be imagining things. Hiding behind a nearby tree, Geretta realizes how close it was and praises Gon's perception, telling himself to take it slow.

Chapter 230 9: Part 1 (9—①, "Kyū (Ichi)") is the 230th chapter of the Hunter × Hunter manga, written and illustrated by Yoshihiro Togashi. Synopsis. Sneaking through a river, Gon and Killua successfully make their way into East Gorteau. The two re-dress and then worry about getting seen by any civilians. Killua elaborates the system of whistleblowing that the country employs, whereby citizens are put into teams and receive points for catching spies/defectors and informing the authorities of any uprisings. In addition, families are separated to prevent groups from conspiring to defect, with any family members left behind being either imprisoned or executed. Killua continues by talking about the enormous wealth gap in the country, with most of the citizens in poverty and starving. He continues to explain things, but Gon's brain becomes overloaded with all the information. Killua tells him he learned it from Illumi, who probably heard it from Zeno (who once infiltrated the country for a mission). All the information was also available on the Hunter Website. The two come across a little village filled with several huts, and Killua takes the lead, telling Gon to wait while he checks things out. He finds everything abandoned and gives Gon the all-clear. Gon wonders if everyone left for the capital, but Killua realizes that someone poorly tried to cover up an attack. He discovers a mass grave unearthed by wild dogs and believes that the entire village is buried there, surmising that the true purpose of the national rally is to make it look like thousands of citizens have left their homes to attend. He guesses that the selection process has already started, and given the large population of 5 million, that the Chimera Ants are going through the villages and towns one by one. And with no one allowed to use cell phones, it will much easier for them to raid the villages eastward toward Peijin, with the citizens unable to warn their neighbors of the coming attack. The two wonder how the selection process works, and Gon believes the enemy doesn't have enough Ants to sort for possible soldiers. But Killua says that the sorters wouldn't even need to know Nen if they're being manipulated. Gon immediately thinks of Kite and the state he's in. Killua explains that that's Pitou's ability and that they can probably have it on autopilot for many people at the same time, likening it to what Genthru did. All Pitou would have to do is force some aura into the puppet's fist, use them to hit the target, and they could make 50,000 soldiers, leaving behind 4,950,000 dead. Killua is confident that the two of them could easily take out numerous puppets, inciting riots and getting the surviving citizens to check the neighboring villages, but he knows that that would immediately compromise their plan of invading the palace. He decides it's best if they lay low, but Gon says they can't just ignore it if it's already started. Killua gives in, but says he will do it alone and that Gon has to stay hidden. Gon is confused at first, but Killua quickly reminds him that their one job is to take down Pitou, telling him not to think about anything else. Killua says the job will be easier if he does it alone, and Gon says he understands, but Killua questions if he really does. He pleads Gon to promise to stay hidden, regardless of how many people he sees being killed.

Chapter 231 9: Part 2 (9—②, "Kyū (Ni)") is the 231st chapter of the Hunter × Hunter manga, written and illustrated by Yoshihiro Togashi. Synopsis. Killua tells Gon that he will text him later, apologizing for being on edge. As the two continue walking through the forest, a hidden figure observes them from a distance. They can tell that the boys aren't citizens, considering them young to be spies, but recognizing their strength and wondering if they could be here to assassinate the King. They worry about making a move against both of them, especially Killua, who they consider to have the potential of a Squadron Leader. Suddenly, Killua looks back at the hidden figure, but seems to think it's nothing, and he and Gon go their separate ways. The figure is astounded that Killua could still feel his presence even though he had removed all traces, gleefully adding that they're fine with it. In a large city, Marcos asks Morel and Knov if they're sure they can give him and his family asylum. Knov assures him that everything is arranged, as long as he signs the paperwork and gives them the necessary military information. In turn, Marcos assures them he will uphold his end of the agreement and tell them all about Ming Jol-ik's crimes. While Morel thanks him aloud, he thinks to himself that Marcos isn't innocent in all this, since he's only living in such a nice place and drinking such expensive wine because he followed orders. Knov gives him a stern look to let him know how important the information is. Morel understands, telling Marcos to continue his normal routine and that he and his family will be on a beach in two weeks. Sitting together high up in a tree, Knuckle and Shoot argue about what to do regarding the selection process. Knuckle says he can't just look away while millions of people are killed, with already 495,000 dead. Shoot, however, reminds him that if they don't stick to the plan, billions will die. If the Royal Guards discover what they're doing, they will be unable to separate them from the King, and Netero will be unable to defeat him. Shoot tells him to repress his emotions for the sake of humanity and to blame him if that's what it takes. Knuckle seems to give in, and Shoot says they have to risk their own lives to succeed. Gon sits alone at the base of a tree, eating a fruit and hoping Killua is okay. He notes how weird he was acting and thinks they should have stayed together, but knows he would get angry if he tried to follow him. Gon seems to notice something as a single leaf slowly falls from the tree, and suddenly an enormous Chimera Ant Snake appears behind him, wrapping up the tree with its body and causing it to crash to the ground. Gon quickly dodges out of the way and Snake compliments his skill, but quickly uses his tail as a spring and begins leaping through the trees, eventually wrapping up and immobilizing Gon. Snake is confident that he can crush him, but Gon easily escapes and punches him unconscious, wrapping him around a tree with his own tail. Believing that Snake has the genes of a python, Gon says that he can live without food for over a week. He thinks he may need to hide better since they found him so fast, but then remembers that some snakes are able to see the heat their prey gives off, even in darkness, using it to detect the target's size and the distance to them. Gon then wonders why they have soldier Ants stationed in an area where the sorting is already finished and considers that they're acting as guards close to the border. He suddenly hears something and is sent reeling from an unknown attack. Looking up into the darkness, he sees an Owl and a Bat. The hidden figure from before continues to observe, curiously asking what Gon will do in a fight against two.

Chapter 232 9: Part 3 (9—③, "Kyū (San)") is the 232nd chapter of the Hunter × Hunter manga, written and illustrated by Yoshihiro Togashi. Synopsis. Gon tries to get his bearings after being ambushed by Hollow and Bat, worrying that both are nocturnal hunters. He suddenly hears a flapping sound to his left, waiting for the attack, and three feathers strike the back of his neck as Bat flies in and attacks. She gleefully laughs, and as he pulls out the feathers, Gon realizes that she's using the sound of her wings to cover Hollow's movement. Detailed information is given about Hollow's, regarding both the quietness of their wings and their ability to hunt by using sound with the position of their ears. Hollow is confident in his extraordinary hearing, able to sense Gon stepping on leaves and his clothes moving. Gon feels something to his right, and three feathers strike him in his right upper leg, with Bat again flying in with an attack. An angry Gon recognizes their strategy and realizes something, suddenly using Ren. Bat is impressed but not worried, and the two Chimera Ants initiate their attack once again. This time, however, Gon focuses on Bat's wings alone and as soon as Hollow's feathers strike his back, he is able to tell where she's attacking from. He throws a punch right toward her, but she quickly dodges, and Gon realizes she must also be using echolocation (which is explained in detail). Gon tries his strategy again, but the same result happens. Bat is impressed by his sense of hearing, and Hollow says to himself that his feathers aren't doing much damage. Gon knows he has to change things up, suddenly calming his breathing and readying Rock. Hollow worries about the increase in aura, but Bat is confident they can use it their advantage if they're able to overcome what is probably his signature attack. Bat declines help from Hollow, confident in her echolocation as she flies high up into the sky. Gon notices her getting farther away and eventually can't hear her at all. She suddenly uses her Dive Bomb, but Gon knows what she's trying and that it won't work since her wings aren't like Hollow's. Bat remains confident, especially when Gon doesn't move a muscle, and continues flying straight toward him. Gon moves at the last possible moment, with Bat's attack only cutting the top of his jacket as she realizes she's fallen into his trap. However, she is sure that she can dodge his punch since he's in an awkward stance after dodging her attack. But instead of throwing a punch, Gon screams as loud as he can right toward her, disrupting her echolocation and causing her to flee. Gon is also confident in his hearing and uses Paper to send a ball of aura right at her. But right before it makes contact, Hollow deflects it with a thrown rock, and Gon sees his new form: Gorilla Mode. He hurtles toward Gon and breaks a tree with his punch, which is followed by a loud sound that makes Gon cover his ears. Hollow seizes his chance and sends Gon back with a hard right. Gon wonders if ultrasounds caused the loud noise as he sees Bat flying up above. She yells at him for screaming in her face and says she's the best when it comes to sonic attacks. Gon realizes that their real combination attack is Bat stunning the target with sound and then Hollow beating them with his strength. The hidden figure is still observing from a distance, again curious to know how Gon will deal with the situation.

Chapter 233 9: Part 4 (9—④, "Kyū (Yon)") is the 233rd chapter of the Hunter × Hunter manga, written and illustrated by Yoshihiro Togashi. Synopsis. Both Bat and Hollow are confident that they can win with their combination attack. Gon is caught in a dilemma, wanting to cover his ears to avoid Bat's attack, but need to hear in order to react. He thinks to use Gyo, and Hollow realizes that he's using aura to enhance his sight. Bat launches another Secret Noise attack, causing Gon to cover his ears in pain and allowing Hollow to land another strike. Hollow throws a second punch, but hits a tree as Gon quickly dodges out of the way. Gon knows he has to do something about the noise, cleverly ripping off two small pieces of his jacket, wetting them with saliva, and plugging up his ears as Hollow lands another punch. Bat takes note of Gon's cleverness, still launching another sonic attack, but Gon is able to bear through the pain this time, simultaneously tracking Hollow's aura in the darkness. The aura trail draws closer, but it's actually one of Hollow's feathers, with the Chimera Ant suddenly appearing behind him. Gon does his best to block the flurry of blows and realizes that the two are making use of Zetsu, which would come naturally to them since they were once wild animals. Gon starts to get worn down by their attacks and worries about keeping up his use of Gyo. The hidden figure notes that Gon possesses more latent aura than the two Ants and that he's unhurt even after all their attacks. However, he says that potential doesn't mean much without tactics. Gon knows he has to break up their teamwork, suddenly charging forward toward Hollow. Bat sends out another of her attacks, and Gon is confident he can easily defeat Hollow with Rock, but worries that Bat would get away and bring backup. Hollow is able to see and keep track of Gon as long as stars are in the night sky, closing his ears and allowing Bat to use her attacks as much as she wants. He unleashes a flurry of punches at Gon, who blocks the brunt of the attack with a shield of aura around himself. The hidden figure takes note of this, saying the fight could last forever and thinking Gon may not be a good choice. Understanding that he has to undermine their teamwork, Gon picks up one of the fallen trees and swings it at Hollow. And since Hollow is directly in front of him, Gon knows that Bat will be right behind him, swinging the tree in her direction. The gust of wind drives her into a rock face behind her, knocking her unconscious and leaving Hollow stunned at Gon's plan. Gon is confident he can take out Hollow by himself, and the hidden figure is only slightly impressed, saying that it makes him just above average. Hollow quickly turns and flees, with not enough time to switch back to his owl mode. All of a sudden, Gon begins readying Rock as he sprints right up behind a terrified Hollow, punching him hard with the attack and sending him flying back to NGL. The hidden figure is very impressed, and after seeing Gon's signature move, thinks he may be of use after all, but isn't sure how. Elsewhere, Killua is seen helping villages and towns, dealing with the attackers himself. He urgently tells the residents that Jol-ik is no longer in power and that they need to warn the other villages before the brainwashed soldiers kill their friends and family. Pitou senses this and curiously wonders who is hindering their plans.

Chapter 234 9: Part 5 (9—⑤, "Kyū (Go)") is the 234th chapter of the Hunter × Hunter manga, written and illustrated by Yoshihiro Togashi. Synopsis. Pitou continues to sense the intruder taking out the puppets to the southeast of the palace. They're unsure if the person is an assassin or a decoy, finding them annoying and wanting to kill them. While playing his violin, Pouf assures them that it's simply a diversion they shouldn't go after. The two go back and forth about the situation, with Pouf wondering if he's overanalyzing things. He reminds Pitou that their sole duty is protecting the King, and as he says others should handle it, Leol, Flutter, and Hina appear before the Royal Guards. Leol thanks them for taking them back after they escaped the Hunters, and for helping them with their abilities. He wants to repay them, and Pitou asks him to take out the person causing problems with the puppets. They give him a cell phone and say they will update him on the intruder's location. The group leaves, and Youpi wonders if they can trust the three. Pitou quickly answers they can't, but knows they will be extremely willing to follow orders since they seek to gain their trust. But Pitou knows the group is waiting for their chance to turn on them, and telling Youpi they will deal with them when that time comes. Elsewhere, Killua is seen saving another village, then using his phone's GPS to find the next one he should help. He begins to head off into the forest, but suddenly feels an ominous aura from that direction, getting bad vibes from it and running another way. Knuckle and Shoot continue to sit up in a tree, and the former says that Cheetu is quickly heading their way. He thinks that the Hunter assigned to detain him must have failed, and Shoot asks if he's coming toward them, with Knuckle saying he will pass to the south of them. Knuckle stands up in anger, resolved to catch the Chimera Ant. He says that the Hunter Association has captured 319 outside the NGL so far, but reminds Shoot that Colt said no Squadron Leaders were among the captured. Eight of them are still roaming free, with Hunters having confronted four of these, but unable to capture them. Knuckle knows that Cheetu is coming their way to meet up with the King and to get stronger by working under him, and he worries that he won't be able to defeat Cheetu if he attains a more powerful ability. Knuckle continues to harangue Shoot about the risks, but Shoot calmly manifests the cell phone out of his hand and tells Knuckle to call Morel since he may need to get replacements for them. In a hotel room with Knov, Morel is upset that the Association didn't use Likke for the job like they recommended. Knov wonders what's wrong, and Morel confirms that Cheetu got away since the Association most likely chose a Temp Hunter for the job. Detailed information is given about Temp Hunters: the Association accepts jobs from governments and private groups and offers these to Hunters who are guaranteed a set fee, whether they succeed or fail. Some Hunters deride those who make a career out of taking such jobs, referring to them with the aforementioned title. If the Association is inundated with applications for a job, a review board is in charge of matching someone based on their skill and fit. Morel is angry at himself, saying that he should have asked Likke personally. However, Knov reminds him that Netero would have been blamed if they had tried to go over the board, especially since Netero had trouble convincing them to allow even the few members of the Extermination Team. Morel continues to complain about the board's mentality, wondering how Knov can be so calm when the dangerous Squadron Leaders are still free. Knov recognizes their strength and the danger they pose, and Morel worries that the board is dragging their feet so much because they want them to fail. Knov asks him if he's talking about the rumors that the supporters of the Vice-Chairman are bribing the board to only give jobs to the Hunters who have said they will vote for the Vice-Chairman in the next election. Knov tells him he has no proof, but Morel says that's the point and that it's too convenient that the Squadron Leaders keep getting away, with Netero taking the blame if they fail and the Vice-Chairman's supporters surely calling for Netero's resignation afterward. Morel continues to agonize over the situation, saying that even if they kill the King, the mission will be a failure if five million people die. Knov tells them that they and Netero knew this going in and that the deaths are unfortunately inevitable in order to take out the King. Morel's phone suddenly rings with a call from Marcos, who urgently says that rumors of a coup are spreading throughout the country. Terrified, he also says that people are reporting mass graves and genocide, angrily asking if they're the ones responsible. Morel assures him it's not them and that he will explain later, telling him to stay calm so he's not discovered. As Morel realizes that the public at large has learned what's going on. Knov directs his attention to the television, where it's announced that Ming Jol-ik will be giving an emergency broadcast. The announcer tells everyone to increase the volume of the official speakers so everyone can hear his message, adding that everyone should turn on their radios and televisions. The manipulated dictator appears on screen wearing dark sunglasses and announces that East Gorteau is now under martial law. He informs the citizens that traitors have been exposed and need to be caught, ordering all residents to stay locked indoors and to not be swayed by any false propaganda from the enemy. Lastly, he says that soldiers will be going by their houses one by one and checking for terrorists, ordering them not to answer the door for anyone else. Morel gleefully realizes that Gon and Killua must be involved, and Knov worries about how well-prepared the Ants are, guessing that they had this secondary plan in case the sorting was discovered. He's also concerned that they're now able to use all the military force they want to seal off the entire country. Elsewhere, Killua feels extremely confident about taking on the enemy, promising to take down even their tanks and fighter jets.

Chapter 235 8: Part 1 (8—①, "Hachi (Ichi)") is the 235th chapter of the Hunter × Hunter manga, written and illustrated by Yoshihiro Togashi. Synopsis. Knuckle tells Shoot that Cheetu is close and will pass by them in ten minutes. He's sure that Cheetu will sense him right before he passes by, and says that interest will start accruing once Cheetu gets within 100 meters of him, confident that they can get him before the next announcement. It's explained that an announcement of interest happens every ten seconds, and if the target gets more than 100 meters away and then moves back within that radius, the ten-second countdown will restart from where it left off. Knuckle guesses how fast Cheetu is running and believes that as long as there are more than three seconds left, they can take him out before he notices. With the two of them ready for the ambush, Knuckle says Cheetu is close, but then says he suddenly changed course to the forest below them. Knuckle attempts to run after him, but Shoot quickly stops him, saying he can't catch something that has the speed of a cheetah. Knuckle was confident in his use of Zetsu and wonders how Cheetu sensed them. He tests the direction of the wind, confident that Cheetu couldn't have used that to sniff them out since they're downwind. Shoot notices something high above and the two of them spot Flutter eyeing them. Flutter communicates with Leol telepathically, asking him what he should do. Leol says to ignore them since the two aren't their target. Flutter informs him of Cheetu passing through, and that he warned him before he ran into their ambush.
