Leol realizes that he was the one that got cornered, afraid for his life and beginning to swallow water. As his eyes start to roll back in his head, he suddenly spots Morel at the bottom of the chapel using his pipe to form numerous smoke hoses. Leol wonders what poison was used, and Morel says to himself that it's a common gas in the air: carbon dioxide. It's explained that CO2 can become toxic in large quantities very quickly, with 5% causing headaches and heart difficulties and 20% leading to death within seconds. It's revealed that Morel had been consuming the oxygen in the sealed chapel and was converting it to carbon dioxide as quickly as he could. Saying that he had started his attack before Leol had and hoping that Grachan's ability has been returned to him, Morel begins to swim his way out of the underground chapel. In Area D beneath the palace, Bizeff is seen snoring on a large bed as Palm gets dressed and says she can now move freely for the next couple of hours. Removing her contacts and resolved to see the Ants with her own eyes, she uses Bizeff's laptop and says that she had observed Bizeff's actions to see how to escape upstairs. She knows that he won't be able to tell anyone about her escape since he kept the prostitutes a secret from the Royal Guards. She enters the elevator and nervously knows that her targets are upstairs. The elevator reaches the palace's main floor, and Palm begins her reconnaissance mission.

Chapter 255 5: Part 1 to 2: Part 1 (5—①~2—①, "Go (Ichi) - Ni (Ichi)") is the 255th chapter of the Hunter × Hunter manga, written and illustrated by Yoshihiro Togashi. Synopsis. Killua suddenly wakes up in a clinic with Ikalgo sitting beside his bed and asking him how he feels. With his head and arms bandaged, a panicked Killua addresses him as an octopus and asks how long he was out. Ikalgo sternly reminds him not to call him that, telling him that he slept for two days and explaining that the clinic is kept secret and used by activists and Mafia members. Killua wobbles out of bed, but Ikalgo worries about his wounds reopening. Killua is determined to follow through with the mission, and as Ikalgo tells him to rest more, a nurse enters the room and explains that if he dies here, all his body parts will be sold off. Killua says that he gets to be discharged since he's fine, but the nurse reveals that the total costs of all his procedures adds up to 1.8 million jenny and that one of his body parts will be taken if he's unable to pay. Killua assures her that he will wire the money later, but the nurse doesn't budge, forcing him to stay until the bill is paid. Killua adamantly asks for a phone, and the nurse goes over the exorbitant prices for a phone call, leaving Killua even more annoyed. Killua uses the phone to call Gon, who immediately asks where he is and if he's okay. Killua tells him that he's recovering in a hospital and that he will be back soon. Gon is happy to hear it and tells Killua that they made a new friend who is getting along well with Knuckle, as the two are shown laughing together. He reveals to Killua that they may have a plan to defeat the King, hoping to talk it over once he gets back. Killua asks him to wire money to an account and says that he can be there within the day. Ikalgo isn't sure about the state of Killua's body, but once Killua disrobes, Ikalgo is stunned to see that almost all his wounds have already healed. Killua stretches out his arms and says that he's ready to go, with the nurse coming by to confirm that she received his payment. Killua runs off, with Ikalgo unsure what to do, and he tells the Chimera Ant that he will introduce him to his friends. Ikalgo still seems unsure as he struggles to reply, and Killua turns away, indifferently saying that he doesn't have to come along, but thanking him for his help. As Ikalgo asks if it's okay to go, Killua asks him what his problem is and wonders if he was the only one who thought the two were already friends. Ikalgo is visibly shaken by Killua's comment, again asking if it's okay for him to come along. Killua becomes irritated, but Ikalgo assures him he will go. Killua tells him that if something serious happens again, he won't thank him for it and says that Ikalgo shouldn't thank him either if his life ends up being saved. He says the reason for this is because it's obvious that friends will save each other, so it's nothing special and goes without saying. Ever so slowly, Ikalgo's eyes begin to tear up and he says that this is the world he had always wanted to live in, but he never thought that someone like him could achieve it. He begins to sob and tells Killua that he could die happy now. Killua is taken aback by the waterworks, but quickly becomes serious, warning Ikalgo that the human world is much harsher than that of the Ants. He confidently says that risking one's life and throwing it away are two very different things, asking Ikalgo if he still wants to come along. Ikalgo gives no hesitation to leave his old life behind now that he has gotten a taste of paradise, running after Killua and confident that he has finally found a place where he can belong. Gon tells Knuckle and Meleoron that he still can't contact Palm. He guesses that she's still inside the palace, worrying that she may have been detected by Pitou's En. Shoot says that she could be in the underground hangar, which is outside of Pitou's range, but says she couldn't get out from there since the exit is up in the palace. Gon calls Morel and asks about Knov, who is shown sitting with his hands in his arms and still shaken by the earlier encounter. Morel says that he won't be able to continue the mission, but that he did his job in setting the exits, so the plan will still commence in three days. Thousands of East Gorteau citizens are shown making their way toward the palace. The King and the blind girl are still playing Gungi as Pouf sits nearby reading a book. She wins once again, but seems fatigued now, and Pouf realizes she has reached her limit, confident that the King can win in the next couple of games. A stern look comes over the King's face, and he suddenly rises and tells the girl that they will start again in 12 hours. She begins to protest, but he calmly says that he wouldn't enjoy a victory over her when she's weak, telling her to rest up. Pouf is stunned that the King went back on his word of not taking any more breaks, realizing that the girl is a bigger liability than he thought.

Chapter 256 2: Part 2 (2—②, "Ni (Ni)") is the 256th chapter of the Hunter × Hunter manga, written and illustrated by Yoshihiro Togashi. Synopsis. After the King offers the blind girl a break from their games of Gungi, the spectating Pouf worries that the girl will become a liability to the King. As she excuses herself and walks past him reading his book, Pouf begins to raise his right hand slowly, but he swiftly grabs his wrist with his other hand to control himself. His book falls to the floor, and the girl excuses herself before leaving. Pouf thinks that he must not act hastily, since killing her now would mean that the King would only ever know defeat in Gungi as he hasn't yet beaten her while she's at her peak. Pouf begins to cry, with a single tear quickly turning into a stream as he starts to wail, thinking to himself about how foolish he was for almost letting a reckless impulse leave an irreversible scar on the King. He begins to play his violin as he bawls, telling himself that the only way he'll be able to make up for this will be with his own life, laid down after he's assured that the King will reign over the world. Youpi passes by and looks toward the wailing Pouf in confusion. Elsewhere in an abandoned building, the Extermination Team discuss their infiltration strategy, and it's decided that the six of them and Morel will invade the palace from Knov's Nen mansion. Knuckle says that Netero will be coming from outside Pitou's En and will be a few seconds later, and that that time can be used to separate the Royal Guards from the King. He asks the group what the three guards will do if they show up in the middle of their camp, and Gon replies that they'll protect the King with their own lives by surrounding him in a triangle formation. Killua says that it'll be difficult to knock them back, and Meleoron explains that that's where he comes in, with Killua realizing that they will have two surprises to exploit. A strategy is formed and drawn out, with Killua then asking the group if they have any questions. Gon inquires about Palm's well-being, to which Killua replies that logically she must either be dead or hiding out. He adds that if she had escaped, she would have called them, and she was prepared to take her own life if she was discovered. Shoot agrees with Killua's assessment and says that if they attempted to find her, it would be an insult to her resolve. As a despondent look comes over Gon's face, Knuckle rebukes both of them for being too harsh and says that Gon is just worried about her. Killua says that a rookie worries like that, angering Knuckle, but adds that if Palm was captured, the Chimera Ants would know all about their plan. Shoot agrees, and Killua says the only thing they can do is trust Palm. Meleoron tries to clarify Gon's point, saying that there's still time to change the plan if Palm has been captured. Killua chides him for being too soft with Gon, saying that Gon would make rescuing Palm their top priority if he could (and ask them how to do it). Both Gon and Knuckle realize that he's right, and Killua recognizes Gon's concern for Palm, but sternly tells him to forget about her until the mission is done. Meleoron understands that any distractions could lead to their downfall, and Killua says that Palm could still call them in the remaining two days. The King and blind girl resume playing Gungi, discussing various strategies as the girl tells him that he can't always play aggressively. Pouf gets the King's attention, but doesn't want to discuss the matter in front of the girl. The King says that it's fine, and Pouf rambles on about the national rally in two days. The King tells him to get to the point, and Pouf brings up "unification" after the rally's completion. The King loses patience and wonders why Pouf is bothering him with such minutiae, leaving the matter up to him and ordering him to stay out until called. Pouf moves outside the room and sits near Youpi, who chuckles at the fact that the King made him leave too. He's confident that things will go back to normal once the King wins, and asks Pouf if it should still only be a couple more games. Pouf, however, says that this is not the case anymore, explaining that while the King may be improving, the girl is doing so as well. He says that he can no longer predict the outcome, but Youpi stays confident that it's only a matter of time. Pitou keeps watch atop the palace and gazes toward Peijin in the distance, certain that the person who killed Leol is working alone. They say that Welfin reported that the soldiers running through the city were just puppets made of smoke, with their complex behavior throwing Pitou off. They say that Morel can't use as many puppets as they can, but again mentions the greater complexity. Pitou gets the sudden urge to fight him, but knows they can't leave their post, wishing Morel would come to them and meowing loudly toward the sky as Youpi looks on in confusion. The Extermination Team split up, with Knuckle and Shoot planning to sneak into Peijin to throw off the Ants' theory that only one person is behind things there. Knuckle says that once the East Gorteau citizens begin their march toward the palace, the three of them will vanish. He hopes the Ants will assume that they're hiding within the crowd in an attempt to assassinate the King, diverting their attention to outside the palace when the group will suddenly appear inside via Knov's portal. Using a makeshift layout of the palace, Knuckle guesses that the King will be in the throne room on the third floor in order to watch the sorting process. Killua thinks back on Knuckle's analysis, but wonders if the King will really be there, saying that something isn't right. One day remains until the Hunters' infiltration of the palace.

Chapter 257 1: Part 1 (1—①, "Ichi (Ichi)") is the 257th chapter of the Hunter × Hunter manga, written and illustrated by Yoshihiro Togashi. Synopsis. The night sky hangs over the palace as the King and blind girl continue their Gungi match. The King notes the girl's offensive strategy and thinks that her perception is increasing. However, he says that he's actually enjoying things and that her control of the board is proof that she is still much more skilled, wondering how much stronger she can become. The girl suddenly says that she feels weird, with small bubbles coming from her hand as she places a Gungi piece. The King realizes that it's Nen, and as aura surrounds her body, the girl says incredible moves keep flowing into her mind, confident that she can play even better. The King realizes this and resigns the match soon after. The girl asks if she can take a short break, and the King asks her if anything is wrong, noting that it's the first time she's asked for one. She says that she would just like to record all the moves that are coming to her, and the King wonders how she'll be able to with her blindness. She tells him that she just has to lay out the pieces and then she never forgets a sequence once she has physically moved them. The King wonders if that's the case for all the moves she's ever played, but realizes it's a stupid question, allowing her to take a break. But he quickly gets her attention and asks for her name, with the girl saying that it's Komugi. In return, the girl politely asks what the King's name, but he suddenly realizes that he doesn't know what his name actually is. The King summons his Royal Guards, and all three kneel before him. He first addresses Pouf and says that he is Pouf, leaving the three of them confused. He then asks them what his name is, and Pouf is the first to reply, saying that he is the one and only King and assuring him that they will get rid of all imposters using the title. The King, however, quickly corrects him by saying that "King" is indeed a title, not a name. He moves on to Youpi, who admits that he is not knowledgeable enough to give an answer. Pitou answers that his feelings are most important, saying that he should choose a name he thinks fits him the best. The King seems to shrug it off, but Pouf assures him that he will have time to choose a name after the sorting, which they must ensure runs smoothly the next day. The King remains silent, and Pouf tries to comfort him, saying that he should tell the three of them if anything is bothering him. The King finally says that Komugi's body was covered in light. Pouf isn't sure who he's talking about, and the King says it's the blind girl. Internally, Pouf is stunned that he would learn her name, and the King goes on to say that she awakened to Nen, which will make her even better at playing Gungi. He asks Pitou if the girl would have survived if she had been put through the sorting process, and Pitou says that she would have died since it only keeps those with a mind and body strong enough to be a soldier. Pouf realizes where the King is going with this and begs him in his mind to stop. But the King reveals that after competing against Komugi, he learned that strength can manifest in different ways. Pouf continues his internal protest as the King brings up the fact that he killed a child before reaching the palace, saying that there's the possibility that she could have surpassed him in some field one day. Pouf kneels in agony, thinking that it's not appropriate for a king to waver and repent like he is. The King says he robbed the girl of that potential, but before he continues, a menacing smile suddenly comes over his face and the Royal Guards look on in apprehension.

Chapter 258 1: Part 2 (1—②, "Ichi (Ni)") is the 258th chapter of the Hunter × Hunter manga, written and illustrated by Yoshihiro Togashi. Synopsis. The King clenches his fists and begins to laugh, proudly saying that he extinguished a life for no reason and that it's a sign of his power. He continues to revel in his power to crush the fragile "strengths" of others, proclaiming that violence is the ultimate force in the world. He leaves the Royal Guards, and a crying Pouf says that he has failed in his duty. Pitou asks him what he means, and he says that he wrongly assumed that the King was repenting and he almost insulted him for it. Youpi playfully says that Pouf thinks too much, and Pitou brings up the fact that the King has changed since meeting the girl. Youpi simply tells Pouf to kill her if she's becoming a problem for the King, and with tears still running down his face, Pouf can't believe that he was thinking the same thing as Youpi. Walking alone through the palace, the King continues to assure himself that his power is the greatest in the world and that all others pale in comparison. Komugi suddenly comes to mind, and he declares that she's the same as the others, and only strong at a simple game. He stresses how easily he could kill her and wonders what's stopping him, remembering that he was only playing games to keep him occupied until the sorting tomorrow. Approaching Komugi's room, he realizes that he has had his fun and has no need for her anymore. As he bursts open the doors, Komugi is seen huddled up as she's viciously attacked by an eagle. The King instantly kills it with a swipe of his tail, and Komugi thanks him. Distraught, he asks her why she didn't call out for help, kneeling down beside her and holding her hand. He examines the numerous wounds and realizes how fragile she is. Komugi answers that she didn't want to bother anyone since it was so early in the morning. He assures her that she's not a nuisance but an important guest, suddenly remembering that he came here to kill her. Komugi begins to sob and apologize, crying out that no one has ever been so nice to her. The King doesn't understand the reason for her tears and asks himself why he didn't kill her, unsure of what kind of creature she is, and of what he wants to do with her. Inside an abandoned cabin in the woods, Gon, Ikalgo, and Killua go over their plan one last time. Killua checks his phone and says there are 19 hours left until midnight, explaining that he and Gon will take the central staircase up to the throne room, while Ikalgo will take the elevator down to the basement to look for Palm. He tells Ikalgo to escape without them if he finds her. As Killua brings up the possibility of the King and the Royal Guards not being in the throne room, both Gon and Ikalgo wonder why keeps mentioning it. Killua says that it's very unlikely to be the case, but that exceptions do happen, with Ikalgo left confused by what he means. Killua uses the example of tailing a target and observing his daily routine, but says that on a specific day, things can completely change from that usual pattern. But unlike those jobs, Killua explains, they can't abort this mission and all their lives are on the line, stressing that they have to consider every possible scenario. Killua mentions Pitou's En and says that if they feel the sinister aura, they can be sure that the Chimera Ants are at least inside the palace. But he considers the possibility that they don't feel the aura when they enter, or that Pitou isn't using En even when inside the palace. Ikalgo quickly interjects and wonders why Pitou wouldn't be using En to protect the King. Gon reminds him that it happened on the day Knov infiltrated, and Killua is still intrigued as to why saying that Colt told them that Knov must have seen Pouf's aura. He guesses that Pitou ceasing their use of En must have something to do with their ability. Gon says they should call Colt, and Killua agrees. As a small child plays with toys in the background, Colt answers the phone and says that Pitou was probably giving medical care to someone, reminding them that Pitou was the one who "repaired" Kite. He thinks that Pitou wasn't using En then either, and guesses that when they're using that ability, they can't use En or their puppets. Killua now thinks he knows what happened, guessing that the King or one of the Royal Guards was injured, which forced Pitou to cease using En and their puppets to heal them. As Ikalgo wonders who would even be capable of hurting them, Gon posits that the King could have attacked one of them, but Ikalgo is very confident that Pitou would never expose the King to danger by healing someone else. Gon and Killua both realize that the King himself must have been hurt in that case. Gon calls Morel in Peijin to tell him about their theory, but Morel is left unsure about who could have hurt him, saying that it wouldn't have been any of the Royal Guards. Gon says they concluded that the King must have hurt himself, leaving Morel stunned at first, but he realizes that their theory may just be right. Morel gazes toward the palace far off in the distance and says that something must be amiss there, now worrying that something will go wrong during the infiltration.

Chapter 259 1: Part 3 (1—③, "Ichi (San)") is the 259th chapter of the Hunter × Hunter manga, written and illustrated by Yoshihiro Togashi. Synopsis. Sirens begin to blare across Peijin, and it's announced that everyone should assemble for their march toward the palace. Knuckle, Shoot, and Morel look on as thousands of citizens exit their homes and prepare to leave. Shoot checks his phone and says ten hours are left until they infiltrate. Back in the palace, the three Royal Guards discuss the rally, and it's stated that the area in front of the palace will be filled with five million people in 25 hours. Pitou is asked about the situation in the capital, and they say that there are now multiple enemies. Youpi guesses that they will use the rally as a way to sneak in, and Pouf worries that they will try to take down the King, who has said he wants to participate in the sorting. He also worries that one of the enemies could have a teleportation ability and use it to move the King somewhere far away from them. He says that one of them will have to stay by the King's side at all times during the sorting, and Pouf realizes that he's really the only choice given Youpi's size and Pitou's personality. Pitou suddenly notices something and says that the auras of the enemy have disappeared completely, guessing that they're using Zetsu to hide among the crowd. Puppet soldiers are shown standing on rooftops as thousands of citizens make their way through the city. Knuckle and Shoot enter Knov's Nen mansion and join up with Meleoron, eating snacks and discussing the situation. Meleoron is confident that the rally will not be postponed since the Royal Guards would never allow the King to accept defeat. Pitou says that their puppets will no longer be able to tell the people in the crowd apart since it's moving now, asking Pouf if they should recall the puppets. He tells Pitou to maintain them and stresses that the enemy can't be allowed to roam free, adding that Pitou should keep the puppet soldiers with the crowd to act as a deterrent. In a back alley, Morel watches the passing crowd and then enters one of Knov's portal to join the others. He drinks a bottle of water and tells them that, as expected, the puppets are going with the crowd. Using a makeshift map, he points out the six entrances that Knov set up around the palace. He says that they should avoid the three in front and wait at one of the three behind the palace. Shoot stresses that once they enter those rooms, the only exit will be through the palace. Knuckle asks if he's afraid, but Shoot says that he just wants to be prepared, worried about waiting around outside the palace, but also concerned about having to stay confined in the room until midnight. Knuckle understands his point, saying that they won't be able to gather new information and can't use their cell phones since the Ants' antennae will pick up the signal. Shoot worries about having to wait in the room for several hours, but both Knuckle and Meleoron remind him how dangerous it is to wait outside. With his face gaunt and his hair white, Knov suddenly appears and says that he will watch for any changes at the palace while the group waits inside. Morel asks him if he's sure, and Knov says it should be fine since he will be outside of Pitou's En. Morel reminds him that their En isn't circular, saying it could change its shape to reach him, just like it did with Kite. Knuckle says that Kite purposely took the risk to see how strong the enemy was, with Knov remarking that Kite underestimated them. Morel warns him that a piece of Pitou's En could extend up to 2 kilometers, but Knov assures him that he won't take any risks, saying that he fears the Royal Guards more than any of them do. A military official announces to the citizens in orderly ranks that they will begin their march toward the palace, warning that if anyone moves out of line, they will be immediately shot. Back at the palace, the King confronts Pitou about whether they knew that Komugi was being attacked earlier. Kneeling before him, Pitou confirms his suspicion, but says that they didn't think the threat would bring any harm to him, so they did not inform him. The King orders Pitou to use their En to monitor Komugi as well and to act accordingly if anything happens. Pitou agrees to follow his order, and the King walks back down the hallway. The millions of East Gorteau citizens make their way toward the palace, escorted by soldiers and a number of tanks to keep them in line. Knov watches things from a hill in the distance and compares the blocks of people to ants or rodents on a mass suicide. He notes that it's almost night, saying he should call Morel soon, but suddenly spots something far off, using a telescope to get a better view. Taken off guard, he sees Pouf hovering with his wings fully spread and scattering dust or butterfly scales.

Chapter 26 The Night Before the Showdown (, "Kessen Zen'ya") is the 26th chapter of the Hunter × Hunter manga, written and illustrated by Yoshihiro Togashi. Synopsis. On Zevil Island, Tonpa is seen barely conscious and tied up on top of a large rock, with a sign behind him telling people not to feed him. Elsewhere, with their weapons drawn, Kurapika and Leorio catch up to Sommy and his monkey, tying them up and recovering Leorio's #403 badge from inside a nearby tree stump. Leorio praises his idea of working together, and Kurapika notes that they not only recovered Leorio's badge, but also now have Tonpa and Sommy's badges. Leorio deduces that Tonpa was Kurapika's target and thanks him for stopping the Rookie Crusher. Kurapika replies that he doesn't deserve any thanks since he didn't say anything before Sommy was about to attack him. With Leorio realizing it, Kurapika tells him that he hoped he would be able to handle it, especially if he wanted to be his partner. Kurapika tells him that he just barely passed, but before Leorio becomes too angry, he realizes that everything worked out in the end, just glad that the two are allies. He then tells Kurapika that he already has six points with Tonpa's badge and his own. Kurapika points out that he now has to hold on to them, adding that Sommy's badge is only worth one point. The two then decide to look for Leorio's target, Ponzu, by watching for stalkers. Elsewhere on the island, as Killua walks alone in a forest, he knows that someone is following him and wonders if they realize how obvious they are. Turning around, he tells the person to come out and says that they can play. With Gon still waiting for Hisoka to make a move, the latter suddenly tells someone to show themselves. As Gon's heartbeat quickens, Hisoka guesses that they aren't ready and says that he will come to them, standing up and walking right in Gon's direction. Although Gon worries that he's been spotted and considers making a move, Goz suddenly stands up from the bushes nearby, swinging his spear and just barely missing Gon's head. The examinee tells Hisoka that he desires to fight him, but Hisoka replies that he seeks death, with Gon telling himself that it's his chance to steal Hisoka's badge. After readying his spear, Goz swings the weapon and cuts right through a tree, with Hisoka swiftly jumping over the strike. Goz then thrusts the spear toward Hisoka, who dodges out of the way before Goz fells another tree, with Hisoka ducking below the strike. Although Gon prepares to make his move when Hisoka counterattacks, Hisoka continues to stay on the defensive, only dodging Goz's attacks and leaving Gon confused. Now exhausted, Goz wonders why Hisoka won't fight back, and Hisoka replies that he is already dying, pointing out the swarm of Hemotropic Butterflies now hovering around the wound on his lower back. Hisoka guesses that someone already inflicted the injury, adding that he understands why Goz wants to end his life as a warrior. Goz then desperately wonders why Hisoka still refuses to fight him, and Hisoka coldly replies that the dead don't interest him, stating that he prefers to look into living rather than lifeless eyes. After Hisoka calmly sits down on one of the stumps, Goz angrily charges forward with his spear as Gon prepares to make his move. However, several needles suddenly fly toward Goz and pierce his face, killing him as he falls to the ground. With Gon left stunned, Gittarackur appears and apologizes for letting his victim run away. Hisoka calls him a liar and says that he let Goz escape knowing that he would find him and want a final duel. Gittarackur points out that Goz was dying anyway and adds that Hisoka also does the same when he doesn't immediately kill someone. Hisoka replies that he only does that for those who are worthy since it would be a shame to end their lives so quickly. He asks about Goz's badge, and Gittarackur holds up the #371 badge, saying that he now has six points. He then reveals the #80 badge and offers to give it to Hisoka, who asks whose it is. Gittarackur replies that it belonged to one of the snipers, whom he killed because his use of a gun aggravated him. Gittarackur suddenly removes the needles from his face, causing it to change its appearance. Hisoka comments that it's always fun to watch, and Gittarackur tells him that while he doesn't particularly enjoy it, it feels good when it stops. With Gittarackur's true appearance revealed, he quickly digs a hole in the ground and jumps inside, wishing Hisoka good luck and saying that he will wait there until the deadline. After Gittarackur covers up the hole and night eventually falls, Hisoka holds the #80 badge in his hand and prepares to hunt for more targets, noting that he needs two more points. Gon continues to follow Hisoka from the bushes and hopes that he will be able to make his move. Hisoka makes his way to a small cliff and puts his hand around his right eye to get a clearer view, chuckling as he spots Kurapika and Leorio in the forest below.

Chapter 260 1: Part 4 (1—④, "Ichi (Yon)") is the 260th chapter of the Hunter × Hunter manga, written and illustrated by Yoshihiro Togashi. Synopsis. As Pouf continues to spread scales from his wings, Knov realizes that a faint breeze is carrying them toward the crowd. He checks his telescope and sees that the citizens' faces are blank, and their bodies have gone limp, guessing that the dust has a hypnotic effect. One of the soldiers orders the crowd not to fall out of line and to remain in their block. Knov realizes that the repeated commands and sounds to the exhausted crowd is the perfect primer for hypnosis, saying that they will stay right where they are even when their fellow citizens begin to be slaughtered in front of them. Knov returns to the mansion and tells the others about the hypnosis. Morel believes it will benefit them since there will be less panic among the crowd when the battle starts, leading to fewer stampedes once they escape. Knuckle says that half the citizens will be assembled by midnight and is relieved since they feared that panic alone would cause tens of thousands of casualties. And since their biggest fear is no longer an issue, he says that they can go all out now. Six hours remain until their infiltration. Gon, Killua, and Ikalgo enter the mansion, with Gon immediately asking about Palm. Morel says they haven't heard from her, but that they plan to wait until 11:30 to see if she contacts them. Shoot watches Gon and Killua and notes how calm the two boys are, especially Killua, saying that he seems much more confident and strong than when he fought him. He then wonders why Killua seems so sad at times, but quickly reminds himself that he can't worry about the others when he's the most nervous of the group. As Shoot mutters to himself that the future of humanity rests in his hands, Knuckle thinks about Colt as well as Meleoron and Ikalgo, saying that even though they're Chimera Ants, the three of them are good at heart. He believes that everyone has a heart, wishing he could just subdue the King, but knows that it's kill or be killed in this situation. As Knuckle mumbles that mantra to himself, Gon thinks about Kite and swears to restore him to how he once was. Pitou's face suddenly enters his mind, and he angrily declares that he will take them down. Killua notices Gon's intensity and says to himself that he won't let anyone interfere in their fight, saying that he will use his new move, Godspeed, to make sure of it. Morel reflects on his exhaustion from having fought so many battles in a row, saying that he's only at 35% of his peak condition. But he knows that he can't back out at this point, especially with Knov out of the fight, and says that now he can just resign himself to his fate, telling himself to focus on keeping his target away from the King. Knov silently apologizes to Morel and the others, knowing that he can't face the Royal Guards again, and tells them aloud that he is going to check on the palace. As Knov leaves through the door, Meleoron works on holding his breath, saying that his limit is two minutes, but knowing only half that is more likely given how nervous he will be. As Meleoron is partially confident that one minute should be enough, Ikalgo thinks about his new life starting tomorrow, tearfully looking at Killua and thanking him for helping him achieve his dream. He promises to accomplish his mission for Killua's sake and to celebrate his rebirth. At the palace, Pitou keeps watch from a tower, Pouf continues spreading his scales toward the crowd, Komugi sits alone in front of a Gungi board, and Youpi does his best to keep an eye on the King without him noticing. The King stands alone and tells himself that he is the king, but wonders who he really is, what his purpose is, why he was born. The Extermination Team knows that their time is up, and they each exit through the open door. The last to leave is Gon, who thinks about Palm before he walks through the door and joins the others. As their heartbeats quicken, they kneel together behind some bushes and look toward the palace in the distance. Ten minutes remain until their infiltration.

Chapter 261 Charge: Part 1 (①, "Totsunyū (Ichi)") is the 261st chapter of the Hunter × Hunter manga, written and illustrated by Yoshihiro Togashi. Synopsis. As the Extermination Team ready themselves outside the palace, and decides to charge all at once through the exit by the central staircase, Leol's Squad Captain, Hina, complains about her Exorcism ability making her lose her figure, especially if she has to exorcise a powerful ability. Shidore, a peon in Leol's Squad, listens on in silence as Hina asks her to talk for once. While on the phone, Bizeff nervously walks down a corridor and tells the person on the other end to shoot the escaped woman on sight (referring to Palm). As he continues to panic, Welfin appears and reminds him not to use his cell phone up there since the frequencies give them headaches, though they are able to listen in on any conversations. He threatens to rip Bizeff's arm off if he does it again, but Bizeff pleads that it's important. Welfin wonders how important a runaway woman is, but then offers to help him find her, only needing a piece of clothing to pick up a trail. Bizeff is grateful and goes off to get it. Welfin plans to be in charge behind the scenes and understands that he needs to take down Bizeff to do so. A peon informs Welfin of an emergency, and he's led to Knov's shoes by a puddle of Taragetter's blood. Given the shoes' condition, Welfin knows that they're from an intruder and wonders why they would have come just to kill Taragetter. He considers asking Pouf for advice, but decides to catch them on his own. Sniffing one of the shoes, he picks up the trail leading further into the palace, and prioritizes it over helping Bizeff, enlisting two of his soldiers to help him, Inzagi and Maenole. Elsewhere in the palace, Bloster and Cheetu meet up, with the latter saying he's finally mastered his new ability. Bloster wishes him luck and leaves Cheetu disappointed that he didn't want to know more. Komugi sits alone at a Gungi board with all the pieces arranged, saddened that the King wouldn't give her his name as she longs to play him again. Also alone, the King looks out at the mindless crowd of humans and thinks about his identity and purpose, lamenting the fact that he has no name and his castle isn't his own. He begins laughing maniacally, saying he only fears how bored he will become if this is his destiny. Youpi follows him as he walks down a corridor, and the King orders him to stop, striking him in the face with his tail as he begins to give an excuse. Pitou watches on, and Youpi informs them that the King has said that their En is annoying him. Pitou asks the King if they could make a hole in their aura around him so that their En would no longer be a distraction. The King quickly rejects this, saying that it would force him to stay in one spot since Pitou would have to watch his every move otherwise. He orders Pitou to only use En outside of the palace, but Pitou considers the possibility of intruders, especially those being manipulated and entering the palace from underground. The King becomes annoyed and allows them to maintain their En only up to the first floor and to not let anyone come up to the second, including the Royal Guards themselves. The three meet at the palace's outer wall, and Pouf tells Youpi to stay at the central staircase, in case any intruders come from below. Youpi recognizes that the King's losses to Komugi are causing him frustration, and Pouf knows that he could use Spiritual Message on him to determine the exact cause, but recognizes that it would be the greatest insult. He begins to feel incredibly anxious and afraid of what could be happening to the King.

Chapter 262 Charge: Part 2 (②, "Totsunyū (Ni)") is the 262nd chapter of the Hunter × Hunter manga, written and illustrated by Yoshihiro Togashi. Synopsis. The Extermination Team returns to Knov's Nen space, and Morel tells them there are seven minutes left, and that they're free to do what they need to until the one-minute countdown. Knuckle goes over the plan again with Meleoron, who knows to tap his shoulder ten seconds before he needs to breathe, and then to tap again right as he holds his breath. Knuckle wonders if he's having any withdrawal from not smoking, but even though Knuckle tells him that Morel's smokescreen would mask any smoke from him, Meleoron wants to eliminate any risks and prevent any regrets. Knov enters from a portal and informs them of the Royal Guards' movement: Pitou stayed at the top of the main gate, Youpi went back into the palace, and Pouf began flying again. He quickly heads back out in order to let them know if they move again before the invasion starts. Killua and Ikalgo argue over how close the Royal Guards will stay to the King, and Morel theorizes that a woman could be involved if one of his goals is reproduction. Knuckle considers that Bizeff may have procured the women for the King, and he and Morel suddenly realize that Palm may be forced to reproduce with him. Even with that consideration, there are no changes to the plan, and Killua stresses to Ikalgo how important it is to overanalyze. He then tells Gon not to worry about Palm, and to focus only on Pitou. And because Pitou had turned off their En for a period of time, Killua wonders why the King would have hurt himself to need to be healed by Pitou. Knuckle reminds him that that's only his theory, and Shoot wonders if they should be thinking this much with only three minutes left. But Morel continues the discussion, asking them in what scenario someone would hurt themselves. In Gon's mind, an image of the broken Kite appears, and he says when someone can't forgive themselves. Welfin continues to follow the trail outside, but the rain has washed away the rest. He maps out the intruder's route and wonders if he fulfilled his mission or used an ability. Youpi appears at the central staircase and tells him that the King will kill anyone who goes upstairs. Upon seeing Youpi's wings, Welfin then worries to himself about the intruder being able to fly and possibly still being inside the palace. But he realizes that if Pitou is using En, they would already be aware of the intruder, and so he asks Youpi if Pitou ever turned off their En, possibly on the day that it had rained. Youpi informs him of what happened with the King, and that Pouf was in charge of En while Pitou healed the King. Now knowing all the facts, Welfin considers telling Youpi about the intruder, but knows he wouldn't get the credit he deserves, deciding instead to find out more information and report it to either Pitou or Pouf. He suddenly gets a buzzing in his ear from Bizeff using his cell phone and seizes the opportunity to lie to him about what's going on, pretending that the intruder and the runaway woman are working together to blow up the palace. Bizeff begins to panic, but Welfin tells him he will find the bomb while Bizeff readies the bomb squad. Bizeff promises him a great reward, and Welfin is gleeful that this will increase his status. Morel continues to theorize about the King's personality and says combat will be the only option given how prideful he and his Royal Guards might be. As Killua worries about the King harming himself and a possible third party in the palace, Morel informs them that there's less than one minute left. They gather near the door, and it's stated that two minutes before Morel's command to charge, two men jumped off a large creature flying high above East Gorteau.

Chapter 263 Charge: Part 3 (③, "Totsunyū (San)") is the 263rd chapter of the Hunter × Hunter manga, written and illustrated by Yoshihiro Togashi. Synopsis. Maintaining their En and monitoring the crowd, Pitou sits alone at the main gate and senses something high up in the sky, simply because they had a vague feeling to look up. They jump to a higher vantage point to better assess the threat, then readying themself for the battle ahead, moves their En upwards in response to the power of the descending aura. Youpi feels Pitou's En disappear from within the palace, and flying nearby, Pouf realizes something must be coming from above. While the Extermination Team is gathered near the door, and Morel counts down the remaining ten seconds, Killua is the only one to notice the serious change in Gon as an icy shadow falls over his eyes. In the meantime, an enormous dragon descends from the heavens, and both Pitou and Pouf notice it, but should have paid more attention to the two men riding on it: Zeno Zoldyck and Netero. As the dragon comes into contact with Pitou's En, Pitou and Zeno immediately understand the other's capability. Pitou then turns off their En to utilize all their aura for battle, but suddenly the dragon breaks apart into dozens of smaller dragons that rain down upon the palace, leaving Pitou in shock. And at that moment, Morel gives the command to charge as the clock strikes midnight.

Chapter 264 Charge: Part 4 (④, "Totsunyū (Yon)") is the 264th chapter of the Hunter × Hunter manga, written and illustrated by Yoshihiro Togashi. Synopsis. As Zeno's Dragon Dive rains down, Pouf immediately flies toward the throne room in defiance of the King's orders. Pitou's decision to turn off their En had backfired, and they fearfully look for the two men in Zetsu among the dragons. But Pitou quickly focuses, detecting Netero in the sky, and leaps up toward him. Pitou activates Terpsichora, which takes 0.1 second from activation to attack, but it's stated that Pitou swore that in that tenth of a second, they heard Netero speak, saying that he had anticipated several options and Pitou has made a bad move. The scene shifts to Zeno talking to someone about time slowing down when one is near death, or when two powerful warriors clash. He's asked about the secret to Netero's power and first says that his Nen is so quiet that no one is able to follow the flow of his aura to determine his next move. He then reveals that Netero was an old man even when he was a baby, being the only person to fight his *grandfather and live. He adds that the two have a yin and yang relationship, but clarifies that Netero has always been stronger than him, telling the other person to watch out for his ability in combat: 100-Type Guanyin Bodhisattva. Back to the present, it's stated that Pitou had thought they had seen Netero's movements as fluid, but all of it took place within that timeframe of 0.1 second. Netero readies his hands into a praying motion, and Pitou was only able to witness his movements by infinitely compressing their awareness, by stopping their own sense of time. However, Netero moves his left hand down, and a portal seems to open, unleashing an attack so swift that it's unable to be avoided. In disbelief over how the attack came from where it did, Pitou is sent flying back, with Netero saying he would appreciate it if they just disappeared into the distance. And at that moment, less than one second past midnight, the Extermination Team exits the portal into the palace as Youpi stands on the staircase.

Chapter 265 Charge: Part 5 (⑤, "Totsunyū (Go)") is the 265th chapter of the Hunter × Hunter manga, written and illustrated by Yoshihiro Togashi. Synopsis. A 46-year-old Netero is seen in the middle of a field in winter. It's stated that he had become frustrated upon reaching his limit in martial arts and physical training. He reflected and realized how indebted he was to his training and the martial arts that had made him who he was, deciding to show his gratitude by performing 10,000 straight punches daily. He would focus his energy, bring his hands together, pray, move into position, and punch. On the first day, it took him 5-6 seconds to complete this sequence, and 18 hours to finish the 10,000 punches. He would collapse upon afterward, and wake up the next to do it all over again. After two years of this, he noticed that the sun was still up after completing them. Two more years later, at the age of 50, he could perform these 10,000 punches in less than one hour, which left him more time for prayer and meditation. Coming down from the mountains, and entering a "dojo", Netero displays his abilities before everyone present. He quickly punches, vanishing for a second and destroying the floor beneath him. His fists are said to be faster than sound. They are all unable to comprehend what happened, and the teacher says it was, tears streaming down his face. Netero asks him whether he wants to fight for his "dojo", but the teacher quickly bows before him and asks to be his student. It's stated that this took place over 60 years ago. Back in the present, Pitou continues to fly back from Netero's attack, yelling to Pouf for help, who is unable to hear them because of his focus on the King. Pitou summons Doctor Blythe, and it's stated that the ability cannot move from its initial position, and since Pitou is connected to it by their tail, they have to stay within 20 meters of the construct. This restriction kept Pitou in the fight, and they slowly descend as they helplessly see the shower of dragons striking the palace. Youpi catches sight of the Extermination Team, with the exception of Knuckle and Meleoron. Ikalgo (wearing Flutter's corpse) heads in the opposite direction, and Morel readies his pipe as the others head toward the stairs. And within an instant, with Youpi ready for battle and Knuckle and Meloreon climbing the stairs, Zeno's Dragon Dive pierces through the ceiling and crashes all around them.

Chapter 266 "In the Unlikely Event Of..." (『が』, "Man ga Ichi") is the 266th chapter of the Hunter × Hunter manga, written and illustrated by Yoshihiro Togashi. Synopsis. Even with Pitou's En missing, and Youpi unexpectedly standing on the first floor, Killua can remain calm through his experience. Also caught off-guard, Youpi immediately ceases all thought and grows four more monstrous arms, declaring that he's a shield that will protect the King. It's revealed that, of the Royal Guards, he's the only non-human hybrid, having only magical beast genes. His lack of individuality and ego gave him more strength. With Youpi standing in wait on the stairs, Shoot stops at the bottom because he knew if he moved any further, Youpi could lash out and hit Knuckle and Meleoron. As Shoot begins to move his flying hands to draw away Youpi's attention, Zeno's Dragon Dive comes crashing through the ceiling. Although Killua recognizes it as his grandfather's technique, he is startled along with everyone else, with the exception of Gon and Youpi, who keep their minds focused on the enemy in front of them. The rest are stunned at Gon's action since Youpi wasn't his target, but they eventually realize that if Knuckle and Meleoron were to be hit by one of the arrows and killed, no one could be sure if God's Accomplice would deactivate, or if the ability would remain, leaving the two to decay without ever being found. And so as Gon charges forward, Shoot feels shame at not having realized this, but Morel doesn't blame him and says to himself that if Gon and Killua are taking on Youpi, Shoot's target is now Pitou. However, it's said that Shoot didn't feel shame, but had admiration for Gon, wanting to tell the world about this boy to whom he owes everything. Shoot reflects on his past fears, feeling stuck in a cage as his friends try to break him out, and Gon eventually being the one to do so. He swears that he'll survive in order to thank Gon, advancing along with him toward Youpi. But suddenly something seems to hit Youpi, moving him to the side as Gon and Killua run past him, and the others are relieved to know that Knuckle and Meleoron are still alive. Through the shower of dragons and the hail of rubble, Pouf flies desperately toward the throne room. When he reaches his destination and sees that the room is empty, he quietly smiles.

Chapter 267 Activation (, "Hatsudō") is the 267th chapter of the Hunter × Hunter manga, written and illustrated by Yoshihiro Togashi. Synopsis. Youpi is left confused by the attack, with Gon and Killua running by him and Shoot drawing near. Under God's Accomplice, Knuckle activates Hakoware and A.P.R. manifests behind Youpi. It's stated that he and Meleoron had made sure that the two abilities would work together, leaving Youpi unaware of A.P.R. at his side. As a result, since Youpi felt no damage or change, he returns his focus to the enemy, transforming his head and adding multiple eyes to it and his upper body. Even though Knuckle had landed a hit, the transformation left him frozen, unable to see any limit to Youpi's aura. Given his experience in battle, he was usually able to tell how much aura his opponent had, but Youpi's leaves him unsure, guessing it could be around 700,000 as he worries about how long it will take for him to go bankrupt. But right at that moment, Pitou's aura suddenly surrounds them, causing them to hesitate, which Youpi quickly takes advantage of, dramatically increasing the size of his right arm and destroying the central staircase to send them all flying. Pitou continues to fall, watching the aerial attack come down. They quickly use their En to envelop the palace, which wouldn't have happened if Pitou had had wings, since their first concern would have been to head for the King, just as Pouf had done. Pitou is now able to spot the King and Komugi in the guest suite. However, they also catch sight of Zeno and Netero (who are also using En) making their way toward the King. Pitou realizes just how dire the situation is, and curls up to pounce, swelling up their legs to twice the size they were before the attack on Kite. Upon reaching the ground, Pitou rockets toward the King in order to reach him before the intruders can. But as Pitou nears the tower, they regret their hasty decision, feeling the full brunt of the King's aura and leaving it very clear what his state of mind is. Blood falls to the floor, the Gungi board lies broken in two, and as Pitou looks in, they find the immovable King holding a wounded Komugi, with the central staircase being destroyed at the same moment.

Chapter 268 The King (。, "Ō。") is the 268th chapter of the Hunter × Hunter manga, written and illustrated by Yoshihiro Togashi. Synopsis. Zeno, Netero, and Pitou all look upon the scene in disbelief. The King's face is still blackened out, but changes slightly once he looks away, while the others still remain frozen. As the King gently sets Komugi down, Zeno and Netero have a standstill because of the creature's show of kindness toward a wounded human. His expression returns to normal, and he asks Pitou to heal Komugi, entrusting her to their care. Pitou happily leaps down and tears up, though not understanding these emotions. Netero holds up his hand for Zeno to wait, since if they intervened in this moment of love for a human life, their own justification and humanity would be lost. Zeno says this wasn't what he was given to expect, and Netero feels the same. The King says they should go somewhere else, and that this would benefit them. It's stated that Netero had paid Zeno a fortune to help him separate the King from the Royal Guards, and while he doesn't object, he feels he's lost the advantage. As Pitou summons Doctor Blythe to begin healing Komugi, the two men are distracted by this and believe the King will seize his chance to kill them. However, he merely strolls between the two, leaving both of them in shock. Youpi's destruction of the staircase has separated the Hunters from one another, and with multiple arms whipping through the smoke, he stands in wait to prevent any of them from ascending. Knuckle and Meleoron barely made it to the second floor, and Shoot and Morel are among the rubble below, the former's right leg badly broken. Morel says the rest is up to Shoot, using Deep Purple to surround Youpi with smoke and sending numerous "Smoke Troopers" toward him. While Youpi easily dispatches them, Morel waits for an opening, swinging his pipe at Youpi's side, but Youpi realizes the tactic and manifests another arm to block the attack. He swipes at Morel, but it's revealed to be only smoke which was wielding the pipe, as the real Morel runs away to slip by. Now enraged, Youpi turns all his attention on the escaping Morel, but knowing exactly what to do, Knuckle appears and punches Youpi hard in the side.

Chapter 269 Adversity Is a Good Thing (, "Gyakkyō Maru") is the 269th chapter of the Hunter × Hunter manga, written and illustrated by Yoshihiro Togashi. Synopsis. The punch from Knuckle was supposed to send Youpi flying, but it only moved him a couple of feet to the side. The interest of A.P.R. is only at 590, and Knuckle comments that it's taking forever for ten seconds to pass. Unaware of the attack, and having lost Morel amid the smoke, Youpi becomes even more enraged, but returns to his senses as he sees a figure flying up above. With his right leg broken, Shoot stands with his other leg on one of his flying hands--something he had never tried before, but which he knew would be his signature move. He also covers his right eye with a piece of his clothing, only because he enjoys how dire the situation was. He takes flight and moves all around Youpi with another of his flying hands, putting him on the defensive to retrieve Morel's pipe. Morel thinks to himself about getting drunk with the two once the mission is completed, and, using the dust from the destruction of the staircase to spread his smoke throughout the palace, he takes his leave to find Pouf, who is stated to be in the throne room. Gon and Killua had dodged Youpi's attack and head for the third floor of the central tower, planning to jump from the second floor of the right tower. The two-pass Ikalgo on his way to the elevator leading to the basement, and it's stated that his ability, Living Dead Dolls, allows him to control a corpse host and that Flutter's compound eyes were the reason why he safely avoided Zeno's Dragon Dive. An overview of the palace is shown, focusing on the locations of several characters five seconds into the invasion. As Gon and Killua make for the stairs, the latter notices two soldier Ants out of the corner of his eye, both standing in front of the elevator. Worrying about Ikalgo, Killua sprints toward them, but questions his decision, especially since he was the one who was so adamant to the others about focusing on their own tasks. Ikalgo wonders why he's running that way, and even with his mind panicked, Killua's body acts rationally, using the speed and accuracy of his yo-yos to quickly destroy the Ants' heads. To finish the job, he handily tears off their arms and puts holes in both their chests. Ikalgo witnesses the massacre, but Welfin also catches sight of the attack from a side hallway, unseen by Killua and Ikalgo. In the meantime, six and a half seconds into the invasion, Gon reaches the top of the right tower and immediately recognizes the smoke surrounding the throne room.

Chapter 27 A Volatile Situation (, "Isshoku-sokuhatsu") is the 27th chapter of the Hunter × Hunter manga, written and illustrated by Yoshihiro Togashi. Synopsis. After spotting Kurapika and Leorio in the forest below him, a chuckling Hisoka decides to make them his next targets and quickly leaps down toward them. Still hiding in the bushes nearby, Gon desperately wonders what he should do and decides to steal Hisoka's badge the moment he attacks. However, he quickly changes his mind and tells himself that helping his friends is more important than points. Both Kurapika and Leorio are shocked to see Hisoka, who tells them that he needs two more badges to pass and asks for theirs. As Leorio angrily asks Hisoka if he thinks that they will simply hand over their badges, Kurapika interrupts him and focuses on Hisoka's mention of two more badges, deducing that neither of them is his specified target. Hisoka replies that it isn't the issue and again asks if they will hand over their badges. With Gon nervously watching from the bushes nearby, Kurapika reveals that they have four badges in total: his own, that of his target, one worth one point, and Leorio's. He adds that only his badge and the one-pointer could be Hisoka's specified target, explaining that Leorio (#403) was Tonpa's target and that Tonpa (#16) was his own. Although he understands Kurapika's explanation, Hisoka wonders what his point is. Kurapika clarifies that while they have no issue handing over the one-pointer, they will not surrender the other three, with Kurapika quickly drawing his and Leorio opening his switchblade. Hisoka remains silent at first and then puts his hand in front of his face as he begins to chuckle. He asks for Kurapika's badge number, and Kurapika tells him that it's #404. Hisoka confirms that he isn't his target and agrees to take the one-pointer, hoping that he gets lucky with the number. Kurapika pulls out the badge and puts it inside the opening of a nearby tree. Hisoka assures them that he won't move, and the two examinees slowly back away before disappearing into the bushes behind them. Although impressed by their progress over just a few days, Hisoka notes that the two still have a long way to go. He then comments on the strange appeal of "unripe fruit" before approaching the tree and removing the #118 badge, disappointed that it isn't his specified target. As Hisoka prepares to look for another target, Gon tries to calm himself as sweat pours down his face, deciding to make his move once Hisoka finds someone else. However, he suddenly realizes that Hisoka may find someone who hands over their badge without a fight, guessing that it's more likely than not. He then senses something and becomes frightened, with Hisoka's expression revealed to have changed drastically. The forest's creatures run away from Hisoka, and Gon is left terrified by the bloodlust, trembling and sweating once again. Hisoka licks his lips and tries to control his urges, waiting out the night by standing in the same spot. Once the sun rises, with dark circles now around his eyes, Hisoka slowly makes his way through the forest. Gon follows after him and notes that he still looks terrifying even though the intense bloodlust has passed. He guesses that Hisoka will attack the next examinee he finds, whether they surrender or not, and decides to find them first so that he can lie in wait for a clear shot. Gon quickly climbs to the top of a tall tree and uses his extraordinary perception to spot Agon in the forest below, climbing down and guessing that Hisoka is only a minute behind him. He races down toward Agon and lies in wait behind a nearby bush. Once Hisoka spots Agon, he puts on a large grin and chuckles, suddenly dashing forward to attack the examinee.

Chapter 270 Indebted To (し, "Kashi") is the 270th chapter of the Hunter × Hunter manga, written and illustrated by Yoshihiro Togashi. Synopsis. Alone in the throne room, Pouf belittles himself and criticizes his inability to protect the King, or even to know his location. He dances around happily, hurling insults at himself and trying to remain convinced that the King would never go help Komugi in her chambers. But he knows it to be true, tears streaming down his face, and continues to disparage himself for not immediately going there instead. As he repeats that he lives for the King, finally realizing he must go to his side, he finds himself surrounded by smoke with Morel standing in front of him. Pouf immediately flies to escape, but the wall of smoke stops him. He asks Morel if there's anything he can do to be let out, but Morel refuses, causing Pouf to activate Spiritual Message. After killing Inzagi and Maenole, Killua worries over his decision as Ikalgo draws near. When they pass by each other, Ikalgo says Killua owes him one, causing a mix of emotions within Killua and refocusing his attention on the task at hand. Ikalgo reaches the elevator, but as he does so, the doors to two rooms occupied by soldier Ants open almost simultaneously. Looking up at the throne room, Gon recognizes Morel's Smoky Jail and realizes the King and Pitou must be elsewhere if he has Pouf trapped inside. He continues searching, and spots the King walking on a roof in the distance, accompanied by Netero and Zeno. The former spots Gon and points back toward Pitou's location, changing Gon's expression to one of enraged resolve.

Chapter 271 Separation (, "Bundan") is the 271st chapter of the Hunter × Hunter manga, written and illustrated by Yoshihiro Togashi. Synopsis. The King deduces the two men's plan to separate him from the Royal Guards and says they can take him wherever they choose to resolve the situation. The two men glance at each other, and ensuring his Nen has no ill-will within it, Zeno uses Dragon Head to transport Netero and the King away from the palace. Gon and Killua watch on, with the latter saying that Pitou is in the left tower and then leaping toward it. He had said "let's go" before jumping, and Killua wonders how he meant it, but fears that if he asks Gon directly, his answer would forever change things. And so Killua follows after him, not saying a word. Ten seconds before Netero and the King left the palace, Shoot and Youpi continue their fight, and it's stated that Shoot's reckless strategy of not fearing death was actually the reason he was still alive. He uses Hotel Rafflesia to take one of Youpi's eyes, and even though the damage inflicted was effectively nothing, it causes Youpi to waver and become hesitant. But both remain resolved to keep the other away from the King. As Youpi's attacks gradually weaken Shoot, Knuckle watches on helplessly, unable to do anything since it would confirm to Youpi that there's another enemy around. Seeing his friend covered in blood and continuing to fight, Knuckle begins to sob and begs that he hangs on. From the two sets of doors near the elevator, Cheetu and Bloster walk down the hallway toward Ikalgo (disguised as Flutter). Welfin continues to stay hidden, surmising that Flutter and the person who killed Inzagi and Maenole must be working together. Cheetu and Bloster confront "Flutter," and the latter asks him what happened to his wings. He says he was attacked, and Cheetu asks if he's going down the elevator. Ikalgo says he's acting on Hagya's orders, and the other two wonder what they should do, since they weren't told to defend the palace. As Cheetu says he wants to try out his new ability, Zeno's Dragon Head shakes the palace, and Cheetu and Bloster go their separate ways, leaving Ikalgo alone. However, both Bloster and Welfin linger on the fact that Ikalgo used the name Hagya.

Chapter 272 Error (, "Gosan") is the 272nd chapter of the Hunter × Hunter manga, written and illustrated by Yoshihiro Togashi. Synopsis. A.P.R. adds interest, increasing the total to 649. Knuckle is in disbelief that only ten seconds have passed, feeling as if he's suffocating as he watches Shoot suffer Youpi's barrage of attacks. Unable to hold back, he charges in, but feels Meleoron tap his shoulder, stopping him in his tracks. Meleoron had tapped not to stop Knuckle, but because he couldn't hold his breath any longer. With Knuckle distracted by this, one of Youpi's tentacles swipes him across the face, lowering the lent aura to 322 and offsetting Knuckle's first punch plus interest. Because of God's Accomplice, Youpi hadn't heard A.P.R.'s announcement or felt his strike against Knuckle. Realizing how careless he's being while Shoot is sacrificing his life, Knuckle runs back so Meleoron can catch his breath, frustrated with himself and the situation. Once Meleoron deactivates God's Accomplice, Youpi notices A.P.R., panicking at first, but realizes it must be connected to what he felt back on the central staircase. He wonders about the conditions to activate it, and what the number on its forehead means. Believing Shoot to be the source, he turns around and curls up, firing hundreds of needles from his back. Shoot thinks he won't be able to escape the attack, but ingeniously uses his two remaining flying hands to propel himself out of the way. This reaction from Shoot lets Youpi know that he can win the fight at any moment, but the mistake in Youpi's thinking was not realizing that Shoot didn't care if the fight meant losing his life. And at that moment, even though he says he can still fly, Shoot reaches his limit and begins to slowly fall to the floor. But Knuckle releases a deafening scream and reveals himself to Youpi, hoping to draw away his attention to save Shoot's life. Youpi realizes A.P.R. must be his ability, and it's stated that Knuckle's decision was correct, but that there was one mistake in his thinking.

Chapter 273 We Meet Again (, "Saikai") is the 273rd chapter of the Hunter × Hunter manga, written and illustrated by Yoshihiro Togashi. Synopsis. Pouf and Morel stand opposite each other in the latter's Smoky Jail. Morel remembers that Knov said the butterfly dust has a hypnotic effect, and so he makes sure not to breathe any of it in. Pouf commends him for not talking, and begins analyzing him with his ability, Spiritual Message, identifying vigilance, resolve, and confidence in a 2:3:5 ratio. He introduces himself and continues his analysis internally. It's stated that Spiritual Message allows Pouf to diffuse his butterfly scales to analyze one's aura flow and consequently one's emotional patterns to infer their thoughts. As Morel's vigilance increases, Pouf is disappointed that he won't even give his name in return, assuring him that he's not being tricked into breathing in the scales. And right then, Pouf envelops himself within a dark cocoon and asks Morel to wait a moment while he's reborn. Unfazed, Morel is content with Pouf taking as much time as he wants. The elevator to the basement is explained in detail, allowing anyone to descend but requiring a code to go back up. A different eight-digit code is given to each person to track usage, and if the wrong code is entered, it triggers a siren and the door is locked. Multiple errors alert the security guards and fill the elevator with sleeping gas, resulting in the intruder's arrest and then death by torture. The records are closely monitored by Bizeff on his computer. Ikalgo makes his way to the basement, using the code that Marcos had given to Morel. He uses Flutter's Satellite Dragonflies to desperately search for Palm. Even though he has never met her, he considers her a friend and respects the risk she took in infiltrating the palace, resolved not to leave until he finds her. As Welfin approaches the elevator, it's stated that it also includes a security camera and scale, and goes back up on its own once it's confirmed to be empty at the bottom. To return upstairs, the elevator allows only once occupant since the weight must match the data corresponding to an individual's unique code. If the weight deviates considerably, the alarm goes off and traps the person in the elevator. The only two exempt from this restriction are Bizeff and Marcos, who often bring in various objects including people, and so using the freight entrance would be tedious for them. Welfin smells a terrible odor coming from the elevator, and wonders if Flutter has been living in a morgue. He is also able to detect Bloster, who went down before him, but can't identify another faint scent, with his sense of smell affected by that from Flutter's corpse. He wonders whether Bloster also noticed Flutter's use of "Hagya", but then worries that Bloster was watching him while he was watching them. He panics and considers the possibility that Bloster went down the elevator first in order to set up an ambush to kill him. He had hoped to set up Flutter as the one who planted the bomb, so Bizeff would see the value he has. But right as he thinks of Bizeff, he worries that he could have died during the attack on the palace, and makes it his first priority to find him. Gon and Killua land on the opposite rooftop and Zeno greets them, saying that he's completed his mission and knows nothing beyond it. He only tells them that it's their call to make inside, holding back the rest of what he wanted to say as he leaves. Gon and Killua slowly enter the tower, and witness Doctor Blythe in the process of healing Komugi, with Pitou crouched beside her. With a look of angry determination, Gon asks them if they remember him, telling them his name and declaring he's here to restore Kite.

Chapter 274 Solution (, "Kaidō") is the 274th chapter of the Hunter × Hunter manga, written and illustrated by Yoshihiro Togashi. Synopsis. As Gon continues to yell at Pitou, it's stated that the Chimera Ant was oblivious to any of his words because they were focusing entirely on finding a solution and carrying out the King's orders. Pitou tells themself that they need to protect Komugi at any cost, and Killua asks himself why Pitou isn't preparing to fight, noticing that they are leaving themself defenseless by not using any aura. As Killua assures himself that Pitou couldn't defeat them without aura, he also notices that Gon's aura has completely changed and that Pitou wouldn't stand a chance against him. After considering the distance between the two, Killua compares Pitou to a mother protecting its young and is left confused by Pitou's behavior. He then remembers Zeno's words before they entered and wonders why his grandfather was so cryptic. It's then stated that as Gon looked at Komugi, he actually saw Kite being dismantled. As aura billows around him, Gon clenches his fist and walks toward Pitou, telling them to move away from the girl. After repeating his order and telling them to remove the monster, he orders Pitou to fight him so that he can make Kite whole. However, Pitou suddenly holds out both hands and bows their head, with Killua quickly recognizing the gesture's meaning. Pitou politely asks him to wait, but Gon is left stunned and angrily tells Pitou to get up. It's stated that while Gon didn't know where to direct his anger, Killua was beginning to understand the situation, realizing that Zeno accidentally injured the girl with his Dragon Dive. Killua also realizes that the girl is probably the reason why the King hurt himself, guessing that she's special to him and that Pitou is healing her on his orders. As Killua realizes that Pitou's healing ability not only keeps them from using En but requires all of their aura to use, it's stated that Killua also understood that the entire situation would have a negative effect on Gon. As Killua wonders what he should do, Gon begins walking forward. Killua says Gon's name, but Pitou quickly interrupts him and assures Gon that they will do anything he asks, begging him to wait so that the girl's life can be saved. Gon is again left stunned and wonders what Pitou means. When Killua tries to question Pitou as well, Gon sternly says that he is the one asking the questions, again asking what Pitou meant by "save". It's stated that Komugi's life depended on Pitou's answer and that while Pitou was unsure of what to say, they replied with the truth, answering that she is important to someone who is important to them. Pitou adds that the King became who he is because of her and that he wouldn't be himself anymore if she died. After Pitou assures him that they will do anything he wants after healing her, Gon is first left confused by Pitou's action and then becomes enraged once again, claiming that it isn't fair as he struggles within himself.

Chapter 275 Promise (, "Yakusoku") is the 275th chapter of the Hunter × Hunter manga, written and illustrated by Yoshihiro Togashi. Synopsis. Gon continues to struggle with what to do, but questions, why he should do what Pitou, wants, slowly moving toward them with his fists clenched. Killua quickly tells him to wait, pointing out that the girl probably got hurt because of Zeno's Dragon Dive, and that Pitou is likely healing her. He wants him to wait until she's completely healed, but Gon wonders why Killua is basing things on chance, especially since Pitou may not even do what they want after they wait. He continues to yell at Killua, asking him how he can believe what Pitou says and declaring that they can't trust any of them. But all of a sudden, Pitou violently breaks their own left arm, leaving the two stunned. Pitou says they can break their right arm as well, and even both their legs. They can also mangle their body if they don't think the promise will be kept after Komugi's healing, as long as it doesn't disrupt their use of Doctor Blythe. Pitou again begs Gon and asks him to let them save her. In utter distress, Gon slams both his fists into the floor and screams at Pitou about how unfair it is—how they're able to heal this girl even after what they did to Kite. Killua tries to calm him down, but Gon's rage boils over, disturbing both Killua and Pitou. He asks them why he should go along with this, his face filled with anger and tears running down his face, and begins to summon a Jajanken attack. Killua quickly yells his name and tells him that if he kills Pitou, Kite will never be as he was. Gon reluctantly stops the attack, and says Killua can only stay this calm because he has nothing to do with what's going on. A look of sadness comes over Killua's face, but he tells Gon that he's just trying to keep him together. He reminds him of his goal to restore Kite and yells at him to get ahold of himself. A look of emptiness comes over Gon's face as he says he's fine now, but Killua's returns to one of sadness again. Gon asks Pitou how long they'll have to wait, and they say three to four hours for her to be fully healed. Gon immediately rejects this, and Pitou asks for at least one hour to be able to stabilize her, begging him yet again. Gon asks them if they promise to go to Peijin with him and fix Kite afterward. Pitou agrees, and Gon slowly sits down in front of them, resting his right arm upon his knee and saying he will wait there for the entire hour.

Chapter 276 Missileman (, "Misairuman") is the 276th chapter of the Hunter × Hunter manga, written and illustrated by Yoshihiro Togashi. Synopsis. Knuckle goes against the plan and shows up before Menthuthuyoupi, in order to lead him away from Shoot. Just then ten seconds pass and A.P.R. adds interest. This frustrates Youpi and he tries to hit A.P.R., but to no avail. He then leaves A.P.R. and tries to attack Knuckle, ordering him to tell him why his attacks didn't work on it. Knuckle expertly dodges the attacks and confidently shouts that he won't. He leads the Royal Guard away from Shoot into another room. Before Youpi follows him, he blows up the staircase that led to the room. Meanwhile, Meleoron, who was observing silently, curses Knuckle for trying to fight Youpi alone. He decides to follow the two, walking slowly, but efficiently, so as not to lose breath. Even Shoot tries to follow Knuckle, but his injuries do not allow him to do so and he falls to the ground. Realizing that he couldn't move anymore, he switches his focus to stay conscious, as Hotel Rafflesia would deactivate if he were to fall unconscious. Meleoron passes Shoot on the way and hesitates at seeing the Hunter's condition. But he sets his priorities and decides to follow Knuckle instead of saving Shoot, and prays that Shoot stays alive. Upon reaching the room, Meleoron looks around to confirm that no one is there. He then releases Perfect Plan to catch his breath, only to activate it again. While leaving the room, Meleoron spots Morel's Smoky Jail, indicating that Morel and Shaiapouf's battle is still ongoing. He decides to go find Gon and Killua in order to help them. As he was about to turn a corner, he encounters Welfin and stops indecisively. Knowing that he can't hold his breath any longer, he runs around a corner, and quickly deactivates and reactivates Perfect Plan. Even in that second, Welfin senses Meleoron's presence and immediately puts his guard up, activating Missileman, a power that enables him to find and get information from a person efficiently. But the attack fails as Meleoron was using Perfect Plan, leading Welfin to believe that there is one more terrorist amongst the enemy. Realizing the danger he could be in, Welfin begins to question whether or not finding Bizeff should be his top priority. Meleoron then surprises Killua by touching him on the shoulder, and it's stated that Gon's cry had led him there.
