Chapter 277 Insult (, "Bujoku") is the 277th chapter of the Hunter × Hunter manga, written and illustrated by Yoshihiro Togashi. Synopsis. After meeting up with Killua, Meleoron uses God's Accomplice on him so the two can find a safe place to talk, and deactivates it afterward. He tells Killua about Shoot being unable to fight as well as Knuckle trying to take on Youpi alone and running away from him to buy time. Killua asks him how many seconds he can use his ability, and Meleoron says around a minute now that he's calmed down. Killua thinks it will be enough time, asking Meleoron to give him one chance. Three minutes and five seconds before their conversation, Youpi blasts a hole in one of the towers, forcing Knuckle to jump out as he flees Youpi's tentacles. It's stated that Knuckle considered his ability to make a quick escape his best asset, having eluded the police for 24 hours and never getting caught on the day of his elementary school graduation. His speed is likened to that of a gazelle, and he had hoped to keep Youpi distracted in order to save Shoot's life, but at that moment, Youpi stops his pursuit and disappears back into the tower. Knuckle immediately worries about Shoot, but his assessment of Youpi's priority was misplaced, for Youpi's central mission was to protect the King. Youpi had assumed the King was still in the throne room, and that Pitou and Pouf were there protecting him. Knuckle comes across Shoot, barely alive and slowly crawling forward. To get to the throne room, Youpi would have seen Shoot lying there, and yet he left him alive. The fact that Youpi didn't feel it necessary to finish off either Knuckle or Shoot enrages the former considerably, who proclaims that he should go bankrupt in around ten minutes. As Knuckle puts Shoot's arm around his shoulder, he hears Youpi yelling around the throne room and realizes that Morel has it sealed with Smoky Jail, meaning that he has Pouf trapped within and the King is elsewhere. He happily plans to move Shoot somewhere safe, but suddenly realizes the severity of Youpi's disrespect. He knows that Shoot and Youpi must have looked at each other in the face, yet Youpi still ignored him and treated him as something not worth finishing off, even when Shoot had given everything he had in their fight. Knuckle wonders if he can just walk away after such an insult, questioning if he can just shake Shoot's hand and the two of them celebrate afterward. He makes his decision, absentmindedly dropping Shoot to the floor and quickly apologizing for doing so. He promises to punch Youpi right in the face, once for himself and once for Shoot. Although Shoot knows he should be trying to stop Knuckle at this moment, tears streaming down his face, he angrily begs him to fight Youpi after he treated him like dirt. Knuckle pounds his chest and assures him he will, apologizing to Morel for the decision they've both made, but saying that there are things more important than the world. As Youpi pointlessly tries to break into Smoky Jail and yells for Pitou and Pouf, Morel hears his cries and wonders if Youpi has killed Knuckle and Shoot, also worrying about Netero. Pouf hasn't made any movements since entering his cocoon, and this begins to worry Morel, but he quickly refocuses and maintains his composure. Inside the cocoon, Pouf notes the swirling of negative emotions as well as consistent conviction from Morel, which he determines will end up affecting Morel's judgment. Unable to sense Pitou's En, Youpi worries that the other Royal Guards have abandoned him. A.P.R.'s announcement of interest continues to annoy him, as does the effect of Shoot's Hotel Rafflesia on his shoulder. He realizes he should have killed Shoot to get rid of the black fuzz, but knows he has to find the King first. Already annoyed, he then comes across Knuckle waiting for him. Youpi violently leaps down opposite him and screams out in frustration.

Chapter 278 Destruction (, "Hakai") is the 278th chapter of the Hunter × Hunter manga, written and illustrated by Yoshihiro Togashi. Synopsis. As Youpi screams out in frustration, he shifts his form into one of pure destruction, causing Knuckle to immediately turn and run. Youpi pounds the floor and shakes the tower's entire foundation. Welfin sees it from a distance, and Knuckle quickly escapes the incoming rubble and carries Shoot out of harm's way. He asks Knuckle if he punched Youpi for him, but Knuckle says he has to get him to safety first. But right then, Knuckle hears an ominous sound and looks behind him, seeing an enormous dark mass billowing toward him. Youpi's stress causes him to explode, completely destroying the bottom of the central tower. His body and En swelled from his rage, and the resulting destruction gave him pleasure, but as he returned to his normal size, he felt extreme loss standing in the middle of the rubble. Making use of his experience, Knuckle realizes that he can take advantage of Youpi's rage and cause him to explode again, hopefully giving him a window to land a hit as well as making Youpi go bankrupt faster from the increased aura use. But even wavering between pleasure and despair, Youpi begins to figure out how to best utilize his selfish ability for the King, understanding that he has to control his rage while not being consumed by it. Zeno is seen talking to Cheetu, the former saying he's not in the mood for a fight right now. Cheetu asks if he can try out his new Nen ability on him, to which Zeno simply replies with a sigh. Cheetu admits he would rather fight someone else, possibly Morel, and Zeno tells him to go find him. Cheetu says he tried, but the wall of smoke wouldn't let him in, and as he was climbing up to get a better view, he spotted him. Zeno continues to shrug him off, feeling guilt at having possibly killed an innocent for the first time since being in charge of the Zoldyck Family. But Cheetu only continues to brag about his ability, with Zeno realizing he won't be able to make him go away. He warns Cheetu to watch his back, which Cheetu playfully dismisses. He begins to cite the advice of Morel of not taking one's eyes off the enemy, but he's interrupted when an enormous explosion lands right on top of him. Silva is seen on top of Cheetu's corpse, his right fist having crushed his head in. Silva asks his father if he should have spared him, and Zeno says he didn't particularly mind. Aboard their dragon, Silva asks him about Killua, and Zeno says he's grown up and believes he's removed Illumi's needle. He tells him about his experience with time feeling condensed, and Silva remembers that his father is prone to embellish his stories.

Chapter 279 Escape (, "Dasshutsu") is the 279th chapter of the Hunter × Hunter manga, written and illustrated by Yoshihiro Togashi. Synopsis. The throne room was kept safe from Youpi's explosion by Morel's Smoky Jail, just barely staying balanced and intact off to the side. Youpi stands in the rubble's midst and begins his plan to feign rage in order to lure Knuckle toward him. Within the throne room, Morel feels the commotion outside, but stays resolved to maintain Smoky Jail. Still inside his cocoon, Pouf begins releasing an innumerable amount of microscopic bugs, slowly trickling out through the smoke at a rate imperceptible to Morel. From these bugs, the outline of a figure forms outside of the throne room. A layout of the warehouses in the basement north of the palace is given, with a focus on the one in which Bizeff set aside to keep his women. Ikalgo makes his way there by truck, and using Flutter's "Satellite Dragonflies," he sees that the door to the warehouse is already open, surmising that Palm escaped from Bizeff and he quickly went after her, most likely forgetting to lock it. Another dragonfly catches sight of Bloster at the basement beneath the palace, and Ikalgo knows he may have made a mistake during their conversation earlier and that he'll have to talk his way out of things when he returns there, still expecting to be attacked. Upon reaching the girls' quarters, he yells out that he was sent by Bizeff and asks for Palm using her alias. The other girls refuse to talk with him, guessing that this is a test by Bizeff to see if they are loyal or not. Using Gyo to search the rooms, Ikalgo spots writing on the wall which says that Palm went to the palace and that if they don't receive word from her before the attack, they should assume she's dead. Ikalgo feels despair at the news, but he remembers Morel's orders to use the "Satellite Dragonflies" and telepathy to work with the other Ants, pretending to be updating his superior but actually informing Meleoron. And if he created a mix of truth and lies, it would confuse the enemy and benefit the mission. Still not giving up on rescuing Palm, Ikalgo resolves to eliminate Bloster no matter the cost, driving back to the other end of the basement to meet him. Bloster asks him if he finished the job for Hagya, but brings up the fact that he gets mad when they use that name now. As Ikalgo hesitates, Bloster fires a barrage of shots from his claws into the truck, tearing apart Flutter's corpse. Thinking he's taken out the impostor, he finds the back of the truck empty and plans to ask Hagya about it later. Ikalgo hides on the truck's underside and worries how he should proceed once he goes back upstairs. Bloster enters the elevator, unsure exactly how it works, and Ikalgo realizes he may have come down without knowing about the different codes, and that he has two choices in what he describes as a perfect opportunity.

Chapter 28 A Huge Favor (きなり, "Ōkina Kari") is the 28th chapter of the Hunter × Hunter manga, written and illustrated by Yoshihiro Togashi. Synopsis. Hearing a noise behind him, Agon turns around and suddenly sees Hisoka charging toward him with a playing card in his hand. As Agon draws his sword to defend himself, Gon continues to watch the encounter and seizes his chance to steal Hisoka's badge, taking aim and swinging his fishing rod. Hisoka closes in on Agon, and the moment before the two clash, Gon snags Hisoka's badge with the hook and pulls it back toward himself. After the two examinees pass each other, a wound suddenly opens up on Agon's shoulder as blood pours out. Gon catches the #44 badge, and Hisoka stares blankly at him before realizing that his badge was taken and appearing impressed by the accomplishment. As soon as Hisoka takes one step toward him, Gon quickly runs in the opposite direction and can't believe that he was able to take Hisoka's badge. However, a strange feeling suddenly floods his body, and he staggers before falling to the ground. With Gon unable to move, Geretta appears behind him and picks up Hisoka's badge, saying that 7,000 represents the number of chances he had to attack Gon before then as well as the casts that Gon practiced to improve his accuracy. He then removes a small blow dart from the back of Gon's neck and says that while he left himself open during his practice, his efforts deserve respect, especially his cast that stole Hisoka's badge. Geretta steals Gon's #405 badge and tells him that skill and caution are two different things, wishing him better luck next time before he quickly takes his leave. Gon lies upset and motionless on the ground before Hisoka eventually appears holding Geretta's severed head with several Hemotropic Butterflies around him. Hisoka smiles and praises Gon's achievement, asking if he was waiting until he attacked someone else. He also wonders if Gon learned his stalking technique on his own and calls it a work of art, praising his timing and the concealment of his bloodlust. He then drops his #44 badge on the ground in front of Gon and is confident that while Geretta's blow darts have a muscle relaxant that lasts for ten days, he should easily be able to move before then. Gon wonders why he's leaving without his badge, and Hisoka reveals that he doesn't need it since Geretta turned out to be his specified target, pointing to the #384 badge on his chest. Gon tells him to take it anyway, but Hisoka allows him to keep it, explaining that he didn't recover it from him and adding that Gon now owes him one. However, when Hisoka turns to leave, Gon suddenly stands up and holds up Hisoka's badge, adamantly stating that he doesn't want to owe him anything and again telling him to take it. Surprised at first, Hisoka puts on a sinister smile and chuckles before refusing to do so. Tossing away Geretta's head and walking toward him, Hisoka tells Gon that he won't kill him until he becomes a worthy opponent, suddenly punching him hard in the face and sending him flying back. He assures Gon that he will take his badge back if he can punch him like that, telling him not to lose it and chuckling as he walks away. As night falls on Zevil Island, a sulking and determined Gon is seen sitting inside a hollowed-out tree.

Chapter 280 Direct Hit (, "Chokugeki") is the 280th chapter of the Hunter × Hunter manga, written and illustrated by Yoshihiro Togashi. Synopsis. Knuckle spies on Youpi from a distance, with Shoot leaning up against a pillar, barely remaining conscious. Knuckle says it's been five minutes since Hakoware was activated, so Youpi's debt should reach 7,000 aura soon. However, he worries about taking a direct hit and it doing enough damage to terminate A.P.R. and hurting him. He says it will take ten minutes for Youpi to go bankrupt, but is unsure if Shoot can survive that long. Running to the crater's entrance, Knuckle draws his attention, and Youpi is gleeful that his fake rage has worked. He continues to complain about A.P.R. while carefully going through his plan in his head. Knuckle mocks him before suddenly charging in at A.P.R.'s next announcement, right as Youpi begins to swell with rage. Knuckle reassures himself that his plan will work, and remembers to punch Youpi twice in the face, making his escape right before the explosion. He reflects on his relationship with Shoot, having considered him annoying at first, but now thinking of him as a best friend. He believes it was inevitable given the life-and-death situation the two are in, but also because of how badly Youpi disrespected Shoot, when he had given everything in their fight. Thoughts continue to flood Knuckle's mind, enraging him even more, and he decides to throw three punches now, two for Shoot and one for himself. But he realizes how quickly his mind is moving and remembers the saying that time feels like it slows down before one's death. Right as he says this and closes in, Youpi shrinks back to his normal size, leaving Knuckle in disbelief and expecting the worst. He realizes the damage from Youpi's punch will easily offset all the lent aura, apologizing to the team and leaving the rest up to them. But all of a sudden, Killua unleashes Thunderbolt from high up in the air, with Meleoron holding onto him. Youpi is stunned mid-punch, and Knuckle seizes his chance, landing a hard left directly to his face.

Chapter 281 Godspeed (, "Kanmuru") is the 281st chapter of the Hunter × Hunter manga, written and illustrated by Yoshihiro Togashi. Synopsis. Knuckle thinks it may have been lightning that completely paralyzed Youpi, but doesn't waste any time in unleashing a fury of punches, finishing it off with a hard kick to his face. He quickly escapes, realizing how close he was to dying, and celebrates the eight strikes he made as he runs to take Shoot to a hospital. Youpi remains frozen, still in disbelief about what happened and how he could not notice that much electricity from possibly overhead, but remembers the initial incident with A.P.R. and how that affected him without realizing it. At the top of the crater, Killua stands looking at him with a menacing glare, and Youpi recognizes him from earlier at the staircase. Killua says he plans to take his anger out on Youpi, summoning lightning as his hair begins to stand on end and become shaped like lightning. He vanishes in front of Youpi's eyes, reappearing and delivering a strike before Youpi can react. Youpi attempts to counterattack, but Killua vanishes again and appears elsewhere to deliver a kick to his face. Killua's new ability, Godspeed, electrifies his whole body and allows him to be faster than his physical limits will permit. It has two core functions: Speed of Lightning, which allows him to move his body at speeds beyond his limits, and Whirlwind, which takes control of his body and has it respond to the actions of his opponent. He used the latter when stopping the fish dart from piercing his skull, programmed to respond to malevolent intent in an enemy's aura as well as bypassing the slower functions of his brain. Youpi continues to be completely outmatched by Killua's speed, unable to react or understand what's happening, though the power of Killua's attacks are less than a tenth of Youpi's strength. He understands how complex aura can be and says it's the first time he has enjoyed a fight. It's stated that this new outlook would soon cause Youpi to make a surprising choice. Suddenly Killua's hair returns to normal, and he realizes he used up all his charge already, quickly escaping from the crater as Youpi chases after him. But once Youpi reaches the top, he feels no trace of Killua (who's shown under Meleoron's God's Accomplice as the two slowly walk away), and surmises that one of them must have the ability to appear and disappear at will. Elsewhere, Knuckle finds Shoot missing from the pillar he had been leaning up against, asking where he could have gone as he stares at the blood from his friend's wounds. Morel continues to stand opposite Pouf's cocoon, worried that Pouf didn't answer Youpi's calls because he was unable to, since he may be just a defenseless mass while transforming. He thinks he should attack, but questions whether Pouf would make such a critical mistake at this point. Still wavering, he worries if attacking the cocoon will trigger a trap or if Pouf's goal is to get him to wait indecisively. Pouf speaks to himself, saying Morel is hesitating because he's a great soldier. Morel's indecisiveness continues still.

Chapter 282 Sealed Area (, "Misshitsu") is the 282nd chapter of the Hunter × Hunter manga, written and illustrated by Yoshihiro Togashi. Synopsis. As Bloster continues to struggle inside the elevator, unaware of the code needed, Ikalgo carefully thinks through his two choices once the elevator locks and fills with sleeping gas: (1) leave Bloster and head back up through the freight entrance, leaving him trapped even after he wakes up, but taking the risk of someone finding him there; or (2) move the unconscious Bloster to the warehouse left open, trapping him there since a key code is required once the door is shut. He hesitates for a moment, but realizes that his only option is to kill Bloster while he's knocked out, planning to manipulate his corpse afterward. As he forms his Fleadom, it's stated that even though Living Dead Dolls allows him to control corpses, Ikalgo has never taken a life before. He realizes that the surveillance monitor room has a feed from the camera in the elevator as well as various controls, and quickly heads there while Bloster is warned he has 30 seconds left to enter the correct code. As Ikalgo inputs the code to enter the surveillance room, Bloster blasts through the elevator door and looks for another exit, startling Ikalgo as he goes inside the room and begins watching the monitors. He tries to consider other options, but again realizes that letting Bloster return upstairs will only limit his own movement, especially if he disguises himself as Flutter again. He quickly shuts the bulkhead behind the truck, startling Bloster as he fires two shots at it, but to no avail. The elevator begins to emit sleeping gas, spilling out into the corridor. Bloster starts to walk down another corridor to avoid the gas, and Ikalgo takes his chance to seal him in, but Bloster anticipates the trap, using two shots to propel himself back out before the bulkhead closes. With Bloster now aware that someone is watching him, Ikalgo panics upon realizing that there's still a way for him to escape the gas, devising a plan before Bloster himself realizes it. Using the supplies available to him in the surveillance room, Ikalgo works on constructing something as Bloster keeps trying to shoot his way through the bulkhead, but again to no avail. Bloster realizes that the controls for the bulkhead are in the surveillance room, and begins to head there. He remembers that he still has to destroy one of them to make it back upstairs, but seems to figure out a way to escape without needing to do so. But right then, the bulkhead behind him begins to open, and a large tank moves forward, the bulkhead closing behind it. Bloster can't fathom that the person in the tank would block their own route of escape, so he assumes there are three people involved, one still watching from the surveillance room. As Bloster threatens to take the one in the tank and tear him to shreds, Ikalgo steels himself for the coming showdown.

Chapter 283 Determination (, "Kesshin") is the 283rd chapter of the Hunter × Hunter manga, written and illustrated by Yoshihiro Togashi. Synopsis. Protected inside the tank, Ikalgo accelerates toward Bloster, who fires multiple shots, all of which do only minimal damage. But Bloster quickly dodges out of the way, shooting out the tank's treads as it slams into the wall, stopping in front of the elevator. Bloster immediately understands his mistake, realizing he could have blasted a hole in the elevator's ceiling and used the cable to climb up. Ikalgo says he's cleared the first hurdle, subsequently pouring alcohol all over the tank's interior and using a lighter to ignite it. Bloster approaches and sees the smoke and flames inside, thinking that the driver may have killed himself. Only a tiny gap remains between the tank and the elevator, and Bloster fires multiple shots at it out of frustration. He yells toward the surveillance room that the person in the tank is burning alive, as Ikalgo is shown in the elevator conserving air with a length of tubing. He patiently waits for Bloster to fall asleep from the gas, squeezing out of the elevator and slowly approaching him. He readies his Fleadom and loads one round, holding the gun between the plates of Bloster's shell near his head. He repeatedly tries to convince himself that killing him is the best option as tears form in his eyes. However, Ikalgo then seemingly runs out of air, putting two of his tentacles in his mouth. He approaches the bulkhead, having not closed it all the way but kept it sealed with a long stretch of tape, and squeezes his way through. He reaches the surveillance room and fully closes the bulkhead, vomiting, and sobbing as he shuts off the sleeping gas. He continues to weep, declaring himself a coward. Within his Smoky Jail, Morel readies his pipe as Pouf wonders if he will deviate from his original plan of waiting. And Morel does, swinging his pipe toward the cocoon and breaking it apart, with Pouf in shock outside of the smoke. Morel deactivates Smoky Jail, surmising that it had to be a trap since the cocoon appeared after Pouf knew his plans. In addition, he sensed no reaction, not even Pouf pretending to react, as he prepared to attack with his pipe. At this conclusion, Pouf begins to laugh slightly, saying "fifteen minutes" with a smile on his face.

Chapter 284 Fifteen Minutes (15, "Jū Go Fun") is the 284th chapter of the Hunter × Hunter manga, written and illustrated by Yoshihiro Togashi. Synopsis. Pouf tells Morel that fifteen minutes was the amount of time he thought he would waste before deactivating his smoke. He planned to slip through, and kill off Morel's comrades in the meantime. Morel is surprised that Pouf would think that lowly of him, but Pouf says he gave him too much credit, suddenly leaping high into the air and dividing into hundreds of small clones. As they all chuckle, Pouf says slipping through the smoke was a last resort, and Morel deactivating his smoke is what really allowed him to escape. Morel doesn't believe him, but Pouf continues to assert that Morel made a mistake, with all the clones thanking him. Morel uses Deep Purple to summon his "Smoke Troopers" to attack the clones, who all run away as they laugh hysterically. The "Smoke Troopers" try to destroy them, but they reform from the divided pieces, leaving Morel in disbelief and wondering if they are invincible. They disappear into the distance, and Morel assures himself that destroying the cocoon was the best move. As he tries to consider Pouf's next move and runs ahead with his "Smoke Troopers," Pouf suddenly appears behind him, taking hold of his pipe and kicking him hard to the ground. He laughs maniacally and flies away with the pipe, leaving Morel unable to use Deep Purple and left with his remaining "Smoke Troopers." But right then, out of the corner of his eye, Morel notices Youpi slowly approaching him. As he asks Morel if he's the one who can teleport, Knuckle suddenly appears as well, demanding to know what he did with Shoot. Morel says the maximum number of "Smoke Troopers" he can currently maintain is 89, quickly turning them all into Knuckles to surround Youpi. He realizes their plan and manifests more arms, intending to take Knuckle's life once he lets him land a single punch.

Chapter 285 Doubles (, "Bunshin") is the 285th chapter of the Hunter × Hunter manga, written and illustrated by Yoshihiro Togashi. Synopsis. Hina and Shidore sneak through the palace, planning to escape while they can. Hina assumes that Leol is dead since she can't contact him, and Cheetu as well since her stomach deflated. She says she hasn't heard anything from Flutter either and intends to be a queen somewhere and to make Shidore her deputy. They come across Bizeff trapped under a large piece of rubble, and he pleads them to get him out. Hina says it's too risky to help and begins to walk away, but Bizeff promises to reward her with all the treasure located in the basement. Once Hina gets more details about the treasure, she easily lifts the large stone off Bizeff's legs and throws it down the hallway, telling him to keep his promise, or she'll kill him. As Shidore carries Bizeff on her back, he wonders if the destruction was caused by an air raid and worries about being captured, saying he'll either be put in prison for life or executed if they force a false confession from him. And so he resolves to escape and avoid getting caught. Elsewhere, the "Smoke Troopers" resembling Knuckle have Youpi surrounded and begin their assault on him. Youpi knows the real one is hiding among the doubles and plans to land a counterattack once Knuckle makes his move. He quickly dispatches five of them, leaving Morel with 84, and can feel that the clones are like smoke, confident that he can confirm when the real Knuckle punches him. The number of "Smoke Troopers" continues to fall, now at 70, and Youpi remains confident that he won't be taken off-guard like he was by the lightning strike. Thinking he may be moving too fast, he subtly tries to give the real Knuckle an opening in order to enact his plan. Right on cue, one of the Knuckles moves in close and lands a hard right to Youpi's side. But as Youpi quickly dispatches him, he realizes it's just smoke and becomes enraged. Morel asks him if he finally realizes that the real Knuckle was never among them, causing Youpi to swell with rage as he billows toward Morel. But the real Knuckle suddenly appears and punches the giant mass just before it explodes, with the horde of citizens shown still in front of the palace.

Chapter 286 Core (, "Hontai") is the 286th chapter of the Hunter × Hunter manga, written and illustrated by Yoshihiro Togashi. Synopsis. Still flying away with Morel's pipe, Pouf drops it in a nearby river and uses his ability, Beelzebub, to divide himself again. He plans to explore the palace and find the King, though knowing that he would just be a bother to him anyway. It's stated that the smallest of his clones can be nanosize, and the smaller they are, the more he can create. However, Pouf's core is forced to stay the size of a bee. Pouf reflects on his confrontation with Morel, saying that the core couldn't have escaped if Morel had just maintained his smoke, which would have limited his ability in combat by half. He declares himself invincible now, and continues to analyze Morel's mistake, saying he should have wondered if the empty cocoon really meant that he had escaped, and then questioned if the voice he heard outside the smoke was the real thing. He describes the plan he had to kill off Morel's comrades as a suicide mission since Morel could have quickly figured things out, captured the bee-size Pouf, and squished him like a bug. He says that Morel may have lost a few of his friends, but he would have defeated him, and Pouf was about 10% willing to accept that outcome. Pouf's clones survey the palace, finding Pitou healing Komugi in the west tower, with Gon sitting near them. They then spy Hina, Shidore, and Bizeff making their way to the shelter underground, with Welfin closely tracking them. Pouf surmises that one of the dragon arrows probably struck Komugi, but wonders if the boy sitting there knows Komugi since he isn't attacking Pitou. In the east tower, the clones catch sight of a human that was captured days ago, a female silhouette sitting up in a cocoon, and Pouf says it should be hatching soon. Next, the clones spot Youpi's fight with Morel and Knuckle, and Pouf is surprised by the 50 or so enemies, but relieved that Youpi is dispatching them fairly quickly. He wonders if A.P.R. is Youpi's new ability, and guesses that all the Knuckles are made of smoke and that Morel is limited to those alone since he no longer has his pipe. He thinks Youpi will only need one minute to find the real one among the doubles, and summons his clones back, still wondering where the King is. It's stated that even though Morel had let his fatigue and nervousness get the better of him in his showdown with Pouf, it was actually very fortunate that he released Smoky Jail when he did since it made sure that Knuckle didn't have to face Youpi by himself. In addition, this timing wasn't entirely coincidental, but the result of Morel's experience in battle, as he realized that the other team members may have needed his help against the overwhelming power of the enemy. Pouf flies back toward the palace, with Killua and Meleoron hiding and left unseen by his clones. As Pouf draws near, he sees the explosion of aura and wonders if it was Youpi, confused since he seemed to be the one easily winning. He's concerned about him, but finding the King remains his top priority. Knuckle is seen barely escaping the blast, thanking Morel and saying he would have charged in without his constant reminding him. A flashback to the two of them before the invasion, where Morel tells him that the only time he will make doubles of him with an angry look on their faces is when Knuckle has lost his cool, unable to think clearly. He instructs him to hide among them, calm down, and then remember the task at hand. Back in the present, Knuckle runs off and realizes that Youpi wasn't the one who moved Shoot, still wondering who could have done so, but quickly refocusing. Shoot is seen lying on a table surrounded by three doctors, his body covered in bandages, and an oxygen mask on his face. He wonders where he is at first, but recognizes a silhouette leaving Knov's Nen space. A tower collapses near Hina, Shidore, and Bizeff, causing them to quicken their pace before their route gets blocked. Welfin continues tracking them, hoping to take Bizeff and wishing he knew what Hina's ability was. Elsewhere, Killua recharges his electricity using a wall socket and says he plans to return to Gon once he's done, telling Meleoron to check on Knuckle. Since Pouf is out, he guesses that Morel is probably in trouble, and tells him to see how things are going, and then decide to either stay out of it or help Knuckle in the fight. Meleoron asks him about the situation with Gon, and Killua knows he won't budge, himself prepared to go down with him if he has to. But he quickly says he was joking, and tells him that he can just mention Kite and everything will be fine. He tries to assure Meleoron, but the latter wonders why he looked so sad earlier. But since he either can't or won't tell him, Meleoron decides not to ask, and the two go their separate ways. Pitou continues using Doctor Blythe to heal Komugi, with Gon sitting in the same position in front of them. Pitou suddenly looks worried and tells Pouf not to come any closer as he stands in the doorway. He asks why and says he could have killed Gon if they had stayed quiet. He wonders why Pitou seems so afraid, and Pitou tells him that Gon would have noticed his bloodlust and then attacked Komugi, something they couldn't risk happening. Pouf is again confused, thinking that Gon is waiting because he wants Komugi to be saved, whereas Pitou seems to be implying that Gon would harm her. In the middle of his questioning, Gon coldly interrupts him, telling him to shut up and leaving Pouf with a serious look on his face.

Chapter 287 Present State (, "Genjō") is the 287th chapter of the Hunter × Hunter manga, written and illustrated by Yoshihiro Togashi. Synopsis. Pouf remains serious at first, mentioning that he's downwind from Gon and Pitou, but seems to acquiesce, saying that Pitou is in charge as he begins to leave. But Gon tells him to stop and reveals that he can manipulate people with his scales. Pitou begs him to do what he says, and Pouf is surprised, wondering why they care so much about Komugi. Pitou stresses that it's for the King's sake, and Pouf again tries to work out what changed while he was imprisoned. He promises to stay exactly where he is, but asks Pitou to tell him everything that's happened so far, understanding that if he were to ask about the King directly, Gon might silence him again. He hopes Pitou provides a subtle hint, making it sound natural, and is confident that things will become violent if they cannot do so. A.P.R. announces another accruing of interest beside Youpi, recovering after the recent explosion. He stands in the middle of the crater and thinks he can control his ability with one more attempt, quickly becoming enraged again before he forgets the sensation. As his body begins to transform, he calmly unleashes his anger, both creating and destroying, even though he still didn't fully understand why conflicting emotions could coexist. He emerges in his new form, that of a, his right arm a sharpened blade and his left shoulder taken over by a large face, his left arm coming out of its mouth. Youpi realizes that rage has to be controlled and directed, laughing maniacally as he threatens to destroy his enemy. He spots Morel amidst the doubles of Knuckle, quickly charging him and cutting him in half, only to realize that it's just another smoke clone. He laughs it off, asking them to make him even angrier. As he continues to destroy the doubles, with the face on his left shoulder storing the rage, it's stated that Youpi's multiple explosions and transformations had begun to consume his aura at an alarming rate. And so, even if he reduced his consumption down to the minimal amount, he would go bankrupt from A.P.R. in three minutes and 50 seconds, leaving him unable to use Nen. Elsewhere, Netero and the King fly on Zeno's Dragon Head to a remote location. The dragon begins to disappear, and the two drop down toward the earth. Netero tells him this is where military weapons are tested, and so they can have an all-out battle. However, the King asks him why they have to fight since Netero has no chance of winning. Netero is slightly offended, telling him not to judge him by his appearance. But the King clarifies that he recognizes how skilled Netero is, but stresses that he alone was born to rule the world. At first, he considered humans only livestock, but after meeting those like Netero and Komugi, he believes there are a few who deserve to live. He considers sparing Netero if he backs down, but since it would only be his life that was spared, Netero says he cannot accept that proposal as he prepares to attack.

Chapter 288 Accolade (, "Shōsan") is the 288th chapter of the Hunter × Hunter manga, written and illustrated by Yoshihiro Togashi. Synopsis. Pitou recounts to Pouf what happened since the start of the invasion, mentioning things unknown to Gon in order to draw his attention. They leave out the moment when the King held Komugi in his arms, unsure how to articulate the event. In response, Gon doesn't move at all, but Pitou notices a slight change in his eyes and ends their account by saying that the King freely left with the enemy, pointing toward Pouf's direction. As Pitou stresses that there's no need to go after them, Pouf discerns that they headed to the south, silently thanking Pitou. He feigns compliance, saying they will all wait until the King returns, but begins to secretly release the core from his body, leaving the shell (1/7) of himself behind while the rest (6/7) slowly trickles out in order to make for the King. Netero stands ready to fight, but the King still wonders why if he knows he will lose. He asks him if he fights for humanity's sake, and says Netero should side with him if that's the case, denouncing the concept of borders and the inevitable inequality they bring. He promises to do away with the former and to create a world that may not be perfectly equal, but one that is at least without unjust poverty. Netero seems unsure, and the King admits that he will use power and fear at first, but only to maintain the necessary order. He assures him he now understands that the purpose of power is to protect the weak who deserve to live and not to subjugate the conquered. As the King refuses to fight and offers to talk, sitting down and resting his right arm on his knee, Netero worries that he's wavering between Ants and humans, claiming that he has to choose between the two. A flashback to Netero on the phone with various government officials. They only desire that the creatures are killed as quickly as possible. Netero asks them if there are any restrictions, but they defer to the Hunters since they are the experts, with Netero realizing that the Hunter Association will take the fallout if any problems arise. Back in the present, Netero realizes he must act before he begins to be swayed by the King's words. He slowly walks forward, and moves his hands into a praying motion, with a look of disbelief on the King's face as Netero's 100-Type Guanyin Bodhisattva unleashes its First Hand directly on him. Youpi continues to dispatch the Knuckle clones with ease, with only ten left as Morel realizes Youpi is leaving him for last. Completely exhausted and unable to even stand, Morel can no longer move the doubles very far, hoping to delay Youpi until A.P.R. causes him to go bankrupt, but Youpi quickly destroys the rest first. Youpi slowly approaches him and says he already spotted him much earlier, but wanted to save him for last. Youpi's mind is now clear since he can store his rage elsewhere, and as he calls Morel a half-dead fly, he says their perseverance is what makes humans amazing. These words of admiration are not what Morel expected, but he knows them to reflect how Youpi truly feels. Youpi goes on to say that he feels he has to give him a respectable death, planning to end his suffering with one strike from his blade. Morel realizes it's the end of the line for him and doesn't mind being killed by Youpi as the blade closes in, with a small spray of blood seen soon after.

Chapter 289 Terms (, "Jōken") is the 289th chapter of the Hunter × Hunter manga, written and illustrated by Yoshihiro Togashi. Synopsis. Right as Youpi finishes his strike, Morel completely disappears, though with some of his blood on Youpi's blade. Youpi is confused at first, but remembers that one of them may have the ability to teleport. However, he saw no one else around, and if Morel himself had teleported away, he wouldn't have been able to draw any blood. He guesses that he turned invisible somehow, surmising that one of his comrades has the ability to make others invisible as well. He looks at the blood on his blade, and knows that the wound he inflicted is deep. And then suddenly, he notices a trail of blood leading away, as Meleoron is shown using God's Accomplice on the wounded Morel, working as hard as he can to get him to safety. Meleoron realizes Youpi can see the blood, and knows he will have to leave Morel behind if Youpi strikes again. But Youpi sees something out of the corner of his eye, and Meleoron turns to look as well: Knuckle appears and decides to face Youpi alone, sweat pouring down his face, if Youpi will let them escape. Meleoron is in disbelief that he didn't stick to the plan of staying hidden to let A.P.R. bankrupt Youpi. It's revealed that Knuckle risked using words because he had been so affected by Youpi's own to Morel. Youpi laughs and rejects the proposed deal, but agrees to consider it if Knuckle gets rid of A.P.R. for him. Morel yells for Knuckle not to take the deal, though his cry is unheard because of God's Accomplice. However, it causes Meleoron to realize what he should do next, and he proceeds to let go of Morel, leaving Knuckle in shock. Morel begs Knuckle to leave him there, as Youpi slowly approaches with his blade drawn. By letting go of Morel, Meleoron had hoped that Knuckle would be affected by Morel's words and not waste everything he had risked to get to that point. But as he runs toward Knuckle, Meleoron's hopes are dashed as A.P.R. suddenly breaks apart in the air, with Hakoware deactivated by Knuckle. Meleoron and Morel are left speechless, both aware that they now have no way to defeat Youpi. With tears streaming down Knuckle's face, it's stated that he decided to give in to Youpi's deal because seeing Morel covered in blood had reminded him of Shoot, causing his will to instantly fall apart. He orders Youpi to leave Morel and screams at him to kill him, but Youpi quickly leaps above him and lands on the other side, refusing to do so. The three are in disbelief, especially Knuckle, and Youpi says he's going to the King, jokingly asking Knuckle if he wants to join him. He says if Meleoron's ability isn't teleportation, then they better get Morel to a hospital before the deal they made ends up being pointless. He shrugs off Knuckle's look of shock and says they can come after him anytime they want, prepared to stomp them down and wanting to fight them as equals. He charges off in anger, and it's stated that Youpi should have killed them all where they stood since his top priority was protecting the King. And the fact that he didn't bother Youpi in a way, unlike his previous rage. It's further stated that Youpi had learned how incredible Nen was from the enemy, and once his individuality awakened and he discovered how to store his rage elsewhere, he could no longer see things in such simple terms. Youpi scolds himself, saying he sounds like Pouf, and wonders what to do with his compartmentalized rage since he doesn't feel like using it on the three he spared. As Youpi is left unsure whether the change in him is a sign of maturity, Knuckle stands dumbfounded, feeling completely defeated.

Chapter 29 Killua's Case (キルアの, "Kirua no Baai") is the 29th chapter of the Hunter × Hunter manga, written and illustrated by Yoshihiro Togashi. Synopsis. In a forest on Zevil Island, Killua tells his stalker that they're only wasting time and that they won't be able to sneak up on him even if they follow him forever. Hiding in the bushes in the distance, Imori chuckles and says to himself that even though Killua knows that he's there, he should still be very afraid. He adds that he plans to wait until he succumbs to exhaustion before making his move, again repeating that Killua should be afraid of him as he inches his way closer. However, when Killua announces that he's walking toward him, Imori becomes extremely nervous when he sees him getting closer. Killua then tells him how annoying he is and guesses that his badge is only worth one point to him. Conflicting thoughts run through Imori's head as he wonders whether he should fight Killua, first saying that he will lose and then pointing out that he's only a kid. Although he considers running away and rethinking his plan, he remembers how his brothers will react and adds that they will be just as upset if he doesn't take Killua's badge before they come back from their own hunt. Amori and Umori then appear behind their brother and wonder how his hunt is going, apologizing for taking so long and guessing that he's already done. However, when the two see Killua standing right in front of him, they kick and punch their brother to the ground as they wonder why he hasn't taken his badge yet. Imori replies that the thrill is in the chase, but when Umori threatens to punch him again, Imori finally works up the courage to approach Killua, promising not to hurt him if he hands over his badge. After Killua calls him an idiot in reply, Imori suddenly kicks him in the midsection and sends him flying back. Killua lies on the ground for a second with his hands still in his pockets, but quickly stands up, with Amori guessing that his kick whiffed and Umori wondering if he's toying with him. Killua then reveals that he stole Imori's #198 badge, and the three brothers are left stunned. Killua tells them that while it's close, his specified target is #199, asking the other two if that's their number. Amori tells Umori that it's time for them to take positions, and the three brothers stand in a triangle shape in front of Killua. However, Killua smiles and suddenly leaps off a nearby tree high into the air, landing right behind Amori and kicking the back of his legs to force him to kneel. He then holds his right hand at Amori's throat and tells him to stay still, explaining that his nails are razor sharp as he draws a drop of blood from his skin. With Umori and Imori left terrified, Killua is disappointed that Amori is #197 and finally guesses that Umori is #199. Umori confirms it and begrudgingly tosses over his badge. After thanking him, Killua throws the other two badges far into the distance, telling the brothers that they have five days left to recover them. He then wishes them good luck and quickly dashes away, leaving Amori exasperated at their defeat. An examinee tracks one of the thrown badges in the forest below and then leaps up to grab it. It's revealed to be Hanzo, who says that his target (#197) always stayed with #199 and that he tracked him until Killua ended up stealing his badge for him. He flips the badge in the air and happily says that he only had to chase after it once it was thrown. However, when he flips the badge around to check the number, he discovers that it's #198, quickly falling to his hands and knees.

Chapter 290 Name (, "Namae") is the 290th chapter of the Hunter × Hunter manga, written and illustrated by Yoshihiro Togashi. Synopsis. Morel, despite his mortal injury, refuses to accept help from Knuckle and exhorts him to resume the extermination mission against Youpi and the King. Knuckle admits that he cannot continue as is, because he has begun to see the Ants as fellow people who have acknowledged and respected him, insisting that he has no reason to defeat them now. However, Knov arrives suddenly, and looking worse than ever, asserts that the soldier Ants' humanity doesn't matter when the King can order them howsoever he pleases. Knov then also reveals that Netero has succeeded in sequestering the King; no matter what the Royal Guards do, they will be too late. He takes away a still-resentful Morel and mentions that Shoot is safe as well, and asks in passing about Palm. Before he leaves for the final time, he also asks Knuckle whether he wants to go with him or stay and fight. Knuckle, refusing to acknowledge that he is redundant, declares that Youpi is not the only Royal Guard he can pursue. Meanwhile, Youpi and Pouf run into one another and catch up with the events that have happened since the invasion began—each guard noting the development that has occurred in the other. Pouf tests Youpi's new mindset, and obliquely they both agree that despite Youpi's new maturity and Pouf's deepening madness, what matters most is the King's well-being. On their chosen battlefield, the King has just taken a direct hit from Netero. He nevertheless continues to insist on the debate over the battle. Netero muses that he cannot back down, and strikes with his Third Hand, only to be brushed off by the King's power. The King tells Netero that the only thing that he can hope to exchange with him is words. Netero believes that if such a small thing were enough, he wouldn't be forced to do this, and curses the King's naivete. However, he suddenly realizes a word that might gain the upper hand. Netero asks the King if he would like to know his own name. The question unsettles the King, and Netero grins malevolently as he sees his bait is taken. He explains the circumstances of the Queen's death and insinuates that he may be the only one left who knows the King's name. Netero challenges the King to force him to admit defeat and the King's name with it—impossible if he is dead, of course. The King compares this challenge to playing with a handicap in a game of chess and declares his intent to checkmate Netero.

Chapter 291 Soliloquy (, "Jimon") is the 291st chapter of the Hunter × Hunter manga, written and illustrated by Yoshihiro Togashi. Synopsis. Right as the King accepts Netero's challenge, the latter leaps into the air and positions himself like a lotus flower, reminiscing back to his younger days in a "dojo" and asking himself when he started waiting for his opponents to attack first. Manifesting his 100-Type Guanyin Bodhisattva, he unleashes its Ninety-Ninth Hand upon the King, repeatedly smashing him into the ground with incredible force. Netero continues to reflect on his younger self, saying that it became customary for his defeated opponents to hold out their hands in gratitude to him, and for him to accept them without a second thought. But his current self rebukes this habit, reflecting on his long-held desire to reach perfection, and he admits that he has always dreamed of fighting with everything he has against an unrelenting adversary. The force of Netero's attack continues to push the King further and further down, eventually breaking through and reaching an underground chamber filled with numerous pillars. The two reach the bottom, and as the King recovers from the onslaught, Netero informs that that this location will be his grave. He quickly brings his hands together to pray, and a hand blindsides the King, sending him flying into one of the pillars. Netero considers himself lucky, saying he is thankful for everything that has allowed him to get here, that has allowed him to face the King, as he moves his hands from a praying position and makes them form a heart shape in front of his chest.

Chapter 292 Hidden Agenda (, "Omowaku") is the 292nd chapter of the Hunter × Hunter manga, written and illustrated by Yoshihiro Togashi. Synopsis. The two continue their fight, and as the King breaks free from the grasp of the 100-Type Guanyin Bodhisattva, Netero uses another hand to slam him into the ground and into another pillar. As Netero approaches to unleash another attack, the King sits in disbelief, barely following Netero's afterimage and feeling complete admiration for both Netero and Zeno. Netero smashes him into the ground, but the King quickly recovers, appearing out of the rubble and coming within inches of Netero before he does his praying motion to beat him back with another hand. The King astutely recognizes that the movement of bringing his hands together is the only thing that surpasses his own speed. He wonders how Netero mastered such a risky technique and believes he must have been near insanity with the amount of time he spent mastering it. Once again, Netero sends the King flying into the ground, but he easily recovers, acknowledging Netero's dedication to improving himself. Netero is not surprised to see the King unharmed by all of his attacks, and the King cites him as an exceptional human who has transcended his limits through effort alone. He commends him with a stern look, but Netero feels ridiculed by the insect and sends him flying yet again. However, the King quickens his speed by bouncing off the pillars, startling Netero as he races to deflect his incoming attacks. It's stated that the King's strategy was simply to keep attacking, and since the 100-Type Guanyin Bodhisattva did next to no damage to him, he could remain unperturbed by the repeated strikes. He likens Netero to a puppet with strings and envisioning a Gungi match, plans to force him to reveal a new move by attacking from an angle that cannot be parried with a move he has already seen. Although Netero's combination of hands may be close to infinite, the King is confident that by predicting and disrupting his rhythm—something everyone possesses—he will be able to land a hit eventually. He assures himself of his victory, laughing maniacally as he launches toward Netero, and hopes that he can win his game before the old man completely collapses. Netero notes his laughter and says he's enjoying the fight as well. He begins to analyze the King's movement, understanding how vital it is not to make even one mistake since a single strike could tear him apart instantly. He recognizes the importance of focus and endurance, and that when he runs out of moves to use, it could result in his death. But that's exactly what he wants the King to think, hoping he tries his best to checkmate him, as he plans to reveal his Zero Hand.

Chapter 293 Metamorphosis (, "Henbō") is the 293rd chapter of the Hunter × Hunter manga, written and illustrated by Yoshihiro Togashi. Synopsis. The horde of hypnotized citizens is shown still standing in front of the palace, and in the east tower, the captured human mentioned by Pouf finally emerges from its cocoon. Killua finishes his electrical recharge, but as he starts to move down the hallway, he gets the feeling that someone is watching him, and quickly darts for cover. He slowly rolls his one of his yo-yos into the hallway to check the reflection, at first seeing no one, but suddenly glimpsing a figure slowly approaching—the figure of Palm transformed into a Chimera Ant. Seeing her with scales on her arms and legs, and a large orb on her forehead, Killua is shocked and realizes she must have been captured by the Royal Guards. He immediately thinks about how Gon will react, and worries that he could completely lose it, especially if Palm's mind has been altered as well. Killua reveals himself to Palm, hoping there's a chance she retained some of her sense of self. He's confident that she saw him first, but remembers back to her ability and how it probably has something to do with clairvoyance. Since Palm was unable to see him directly from her location, Killua believes she somehow sensed him and thinks that she would have kept her distance if she didn't remember him. But he gets confirmation that she does remember him when Palm utters his name, then asking where Gon is. Killua shows relief on his face, slowly walking toward her as she comments on her appearance and wonders if Gon will like her anymore. The two go back and forth about Gon, but she continues to ask where he is, prompting Killua to say he's with Pitou. But Killua suddenly hesitates, wondering how she saw him but not Gon. Palm asks him what's wrong, and he wonders if she approached him by chance. She replies that he's the one who came around the corner, and Killua catches her in a lie, with Palm calling him a pest and asking again about Gon's location. Killua realizes that she must have seen him coming her way, backtracked, and then acted like she was approaching him. With an angry look on her face, Palm again asks where Gon is, but Killua readies his yo-yo and says he won't answer an enemy. Palm's hair suddenly grows in length and covers her entire body, and she tells him she's realized that it's better to yield to her rage than to keep it locked up. Killua becomes extremely worried, and with her new ability, Black Widow, Palm charges at Killua and shatters his thrown yo-yo, sending him flying back and following up with a quick series of punches. She asks him whether he wants to stay silent, surrender and talk, or die, with Killua feeling the full effect of her new power. Elsewhere, having disregarded Meleoron's protests, Knuckle approaches Pouf, still waiting in the doorway near Gon and Pitou, and tells him to step outside.

Chapter 294 Breakdown (, "Kekkai") is the 294th chapter of the Hunter × Hunter manga, written and illustrated by Yoshihiro Togashi. Synopsis. Palm's Black Widow is explained in detail, extending her hair in length and covering her entire body. The final shape is determined by her emotions, with Palm currently sporting a dress, heels, and a large sun hat. The ability is completely defensive in nature, but this allows Palm to direct all her focus on attacking. She strikes Killua with another heavy punch, sending him far back as he blocks it with his right arm. He remembers that she was an Enhancer, and comments on her incredible power with this new ability, concerned that he won't last if her barrage continues. However, he knows he has to keep Palm away from the already-distressed Gon at all costs, even if she still has some of her former self. He quickly asks her why she wants to see Gon, hoping for a good reason, but she says she just wants to see him and knows he's close, sending Killua back with another punch and quickly pursuing him. Killua dodges in time and suddenly apologizes for calling her an enemy, confident that she's still Palm. She appears surprised, and Killua goes on to explain the situation with Gon and how Palm's new appearance could upset him even more, telling her to promise to use his name first and to let him know she's okay when she meets him. He continues to tell her how much Gon was thinking of her before the invasion, and it's revealed that Killua was just saying this to buy time, by no means planning to let her see Gon. But as he continues to speak about Gon and his fragile state of mind, tears begin to roll down his face and he slams his fists into the floor, screaming out in frustration and sadness at being unable to help Gon anymore. A small Pouf suddenly appears from behind Palm's hat and tells her that the plan has changed, calling her "Number 1" and ordering her to kill the defenseless Killua. A flashback to when Palm infiltrated the palace. She had approached the central staircase, and was enveloped by Pitou's fresh En, suffering a mental breakdown just as Knov had from Pouf's. As the two Royal Guards drew near, her mental state deteriorated even further, imagining herself as a victim of Bizeff, and attempted to commit suicide on the spot. But Doctor Blythe prevented this, and the two were so fascinated by the power of her aura that, with the King's approval, they decided to make her the first test subject. It's explained that those with enough willpower, especially those with Nen, are more likely to retain past memories that could cloud the emotions of their new self. Pitou and Pouf were aware of this, and the former used Doctor Blythe to break the synapses between Palm's memories and her emotions. They had previously experimented on both Cheetu and Leol, learning that those retaining their memories emerged from their cocoons more quickly. This plan of allowing puppets to keep their memories made Palm the ideal first test subject. As Killua sits still in despair on his hands and knees, Pouf gleefully gives the order again, commanding her to kill him. But Palm coldly silences him, leaving both Pouf and Killua in shock, and yells that her name is Palm Siberia as she smashes the tiny Pouf. Deactivating Black Widow, she assures herself that she will never be a tool for the Ants, and thanks Killua for removing the wall in her mind that was separating her from her emotions. She tells him to never believe he's powerless, offering to help Gon however she can, but reminding him that Gon needs him the most. It's mentioned that in those trying to recover, especially from brain injuries, the love from family and friends can hasten recovery and defy medical expectations. Pouf continues to fly toward the King with Youpi, who wonders what's wrong after Pouf seems disappointed. He says it failed, leaving Youpi confused, and continues to fly on, thinking to himself that they will need soldiers with both memories and emotions anyway. Consequently, Pouf believes he will no longer need Pitou's ability and is confident he can make soldiers on his own. As he accepts Knuckle's offer to fight, he happily envisions a kingdom made for only himself and the King.

Chapter 295 Determination (, "Ketsui") is the 295th chapter of the Hunter × Hunter manga, written and illustrated by Yoshihiro Togashi. Synopsis. Pouf immediately informs Knuckle that the body he sees is just a shell, and that his core is making its way to the King. It's explained that Pouf assumed that Knuckle had learned about his ability from Morel, and Knuckle confirms this for Gon's sake, but asks Pouf why he mentioned it. Pouf's mind lingers on Youpi, and the fact that Knuckle is alive confirms that Youpi allowed him to live and didn't tell Pouf. He decides he has to settle things peacefully here to question Youpi about what happened. And so he tells Knuckle that he revealed the information about his shell and core to gain Gon's permission to let him leave. Pouf agrees to face Knuckle, but stresses he won't use any of his abilities, only wanting to talk and knowing that Knuckle will fall for such a straightforward approach. Gon, on the other hand, immediately calls out his hypocrisy, since Pouf had just recently tried to take him by surprise and kill him. He tells Knuckle not to fall for his tricks, asking how they can be sure that he's actually telling the truth about his shell and core. Pouf realizes how much trouble Gon could cause, considering him to have the most unrelenting determination of all their enemies. He believes himself lucky that he is so focused on Pitou, and tells him that he can't verify his earlier statement without giving himself a big disadvantage, playfully saying that they can decide how things play out now. Pitou seems extremely concerned and tells Pouf to stop, but he suddenly bursts apart into his tiny clones, informing Knuckle that he will wait for ten minutes at the front gate if he still wants to duel. Pitou desperately tries to appease Gon, apologizing for Pouf's action, but Gon also says ten minutes, clarifying that they now have ten fewer minutes to heal Komugi. Pitou begins to tremble, first at Pouf's reckless decision, but even more so at Gon ignoring it and then reducing the amount of time. It's revealed that Pitou's initial request of three to four hours was solely to protect Komugi as much as possible and that the one-hour decision was the actual time that it would take to heal her. But even with ten fewer minutes, Doctor Blythe could completely heal Komugi with the remaining time since it had begun to improve through Pitou's repeated use of it. Even though they are fairly certain that Gon only chose ten minutes because it's the amount of time that Pouf gave, Pitou can't help but think that Gon's awareness and focus were so heightened that he could predict something like Doctor Blythe's subtle improvement. Because of this, Pitou understands the risk that Gon could pose to the King and how important it is to stop him. Gon tells Knuckle that he can deal with things here, and believes that Pouf was telling the truth about his core, knowing that he went south toward the King. Gon knew which direction the King went because he had seen him and Netero leave, but Pitou was unaware of this fact and panics, thinking that Gon had realized Pouf's plan. Understanding just how dangerous Gon is, Pitou resolves to kill him for the King's sake, no matter the cost. But they quickly think about Komugi, unable to risk her life and wondering to whom they should entrust her, especially when both Pouf and Youpi wouldn't agree to it. Before Knuckle leaves, he begins to reveal what happened with Youpi, but quickly restrains himself, realizing the danger Gon could be in if the information made him hesitate or affected his mental state any further. In the basement, Ikalgo continues to weep, but quickly refocuses on finding Palm, suddenly noticing on the monitors that multiple doors have been opened when he wasn't looking. Crouching on the table behind him, Welfin appears with his Missileman ready and threatens to shoot if he tries anything during his questioning. Ikalgo realizes that Welfin will torture him if necessary to reveal any information about his friends and their abilities. However, hoping that he's a Manipulator, he suddenly expands the size of his head, with Welfin desperately threatening to kill him. Ikalgo calmly tells him to do so, preferring to die rather than betray his friends, as he quickly forms his Fleadom and fires a round at the panicked Welfin.

Chapter 296 Admission (, "Kokuhaku") is the 296th chapter of the Hunter × Hunter manga, written and illustrated by Yoshihiro Togashi. Synopsis. As Welfin screams out in pain from the shot, Ikalgo faces retaliation from Missileman as two missiles suddenly fly toward him and explode. Ikalgo is surprised that he's not only alive, but hasn't taken any damage from the attack. Welfin continues to ache from being shot, also shocked that Ikalgo discovered his weakness, with Missileman requiring an exchange of words. He rejoices that his own wound isn't deep and that Ikalgo will suffer a slow death, manifesting his "Black Centipedes" in Ikalgo's head. Welfin explains that the centipedes feed on his defiance, and if he disobeys his orders or tries to harm him, he will face unimaginable pain and eventual death. Ikalgo disregards the threat, prioritizing his friends' safety over his own well being, and, struggling through the centipedes as they dig further out of his head, fires another shot at Welfin. He assures him that he's only trying to incapacitate him, firing yet another shot as Welfin yells out and the centipedes continue to grow in Ikalgo's head. Ikalgo gives a sly smile, finding it incredibly easy to be so reckless when his life alone is on the line. Ikalgo's persistence forces Welfin to surrender, and Ikalgo feels less pain as the centipedes themselves seem to suffer, and he wonders if it's because Welfin said he surrendered. He asks him to remove the centipedes, but Welfin keeps to himself that he cannot disable Missileman after firing it, knowing it could cause Ikalgo to kill him. And so to buy time, he awkwardly pretends to pass out, but Ikalgo immediately aims his Fleadom and forces Welfin to admit the aforementioned information about his ability. Once again, Ikalgo feels the centipedes writhing in pain, this time after Welfin's confession. After Welfin points out that Nen abilities reflect one's personality, Ikalgo asks if he remembers anything from his human life. After being pressed at gunpoint, Welfin reluctantly reveals the memories of his death by the Chimera Ants and his subsequent rebirth. As an Ant, the first thing he remembered was the one thing he wanted to forget: his own father strangling him, with a woman watching on, but his stepbrother eventually saved him. He remembers that his stepbrother was very similar to Gyro, a name that gets Ikalgo's attention as Welfin reminds him that he is their king. As he reminisces about the time he and Gyro spent together, wondering where he is, he desperately wishes to see him again. Following Welfin's sincerity and confession, the centipedes begin to disappear and Ikalgo questions him about the doors he left open. Welfin tells him he left them open for people who were after treasure in the basement (i.e., Bizeff, Hina, and Shidore). He had been watching the monitors and assumed that Ikalgo would be an easy opponent after he spared Bloster. Before leaving, Ikalgo asks him if he's seen a woman in the palace, and Welfin reveals that a human was caught and put into a cocoon, deemed "Number 1." He gives Ikalgo the cocoon's exact location and laughs upon realizing how easy it is, to tell the truth. After thousands of strikes from Netero, the King begins to feel a slight ache inside his body. But suddenly, Netero's right lower leg is instantly severed, as the King commands him to stop the bleeding and tell him his name, commending him on how long he lasted for a human.

Chapter 297 The Last (, "Saigo") is the 297th chapter of the Hunter × Hunter manga, written and illustrated by Yoshihiro Togashi. Synopsis. The King tells Netero that he will surely die of blood loss from the wound, but Netero quickly dismisses him and suddenly brings his hand to his leg, using Nen to affect the blood vessels and muscles and sealing up the wound. He confidently stands on his one leg and tells the King not to be so sure of himself after a lucky strike, declaring that their fight has just begun. Although impressed by his perseverance and determination, the King comments on the inevitability of receiving the wound because of Netero's imperfect defense strategy. It's stated that his Gungi matches with Komugi had allowed the King to anticipate at near-supernatural levels, and he tells Netero that it was as easy as determining his rhythm, calmly threatening to take his left arm next as he leaps high into the air. As Netero readies his hands and realizes the finality of the moment, it's stated that their exchange lasted less than a minute and resulted in over a thousand blows from the increased adrenaline and Netero's understanding of the situation. The King continued to take the full-brunt of Netero's attacks and to detect the subtle bias within them, eventually reaching his target and severing Netero's left arm at the shoulder. With the arm still flying through the air, the King calmly sits down and asks Netero again for his name. Now missing two limbs, Netero simply smiles and addresses him as the King of Ants, asking him if he thought two arms were necessary for prayer. He states that prayer is an action of the heart, suddenly summoning the Zero Hand of his 100-Type Guanyin Bodhisattva directly behind the King. Two of the hands gently envelop the King with a firm grasp, and it's revealed that the thing Killua had been wary of earlier in the forest was Netero focusing the entirety of his aura for this attack. Netero's eyes go white, and as he raises his middle finger, an enormous blast fires from the goddess' mouth straight down upon the trapped King. Once the smoke and rubble begins to clear, a severely weakened Netero barely has the strength to hold himself up, his body much thinner than before. Walking out through the smoke, the King commends Netero and compliments the power of his attack, with only superficial damage done to his body from Netero's Zero Hand. Netero sits in disbelief, but the King reminds him that he was born to rule the world and that generations of evolution have been building up to his arrival. He continues with the idea that Netero is just one individual of his species, whereas he has complete responsibility for the future of his species. As Netero sits in despair, the King informs that because the individuality of humans disrupts the Ants' ordered system to such a degree, he will no longer use them for reproduction, promising to put aside a settlement where humans can live and reconsider the amount he will take to use as food. He assures him that his fight wasn't pointless, but demands that he finally tell him his name. Netero simply laughs and says he's not alone, instructing him not to underestimate humanity and at last uttering his name: Meruem.

Chapter 298 Rose (, "Bara") is the 298th chapter of the Hunter × Hunter manga, written and illustrated by Yoshihiro Togashi. Synopsis. On the verge of dying, Netero responds to the King's earlier question that his name is "Meruem" and releases a tremendous amount of aura. As the King wonders what is happening, Netero declares to him that he knows nothing of the ""bottomless malice within the human heart"." This strikes the King with fear for the first time as Netero sits triumphant despite his current state. He immediately thrusts two fingers in his heart, thus activating his final attempt at retaliation. A flashback shows a doctor explaining to Netero that once his heart stops beating, the bomb itself will trigger. Netero tells the King that if Hell exists, he'll see him there. Realizing that he planned all of this from the very beginning, Meruem attempts to run away. However, the Poor Man's Rose activates, destroying the tomb and plain they were fighting in. The bomb is stated to be a low budget weapon, but simultaneously destructive and lethal. Consuming millions of lives, an international treaty was signed banning the bomb's production. But over 80% of the countries rejected the proposal, leaving hundreds of thousands of "seeds" waiting to "bloom" in many countries. Witnessing the explosion from afar, Pouf and Youpi rush toward it and already know what the rumbling signifies. Meanwhile, Knuckle encounters one of Pouf's clones, who shows its true appearance and flies off to follow its main body; Knuckle remembers Knov's words about the Ants becoming mindless drones to the King, and wonders if Netero managed to kill him, his own spirits crushed after seeing an overwhelming obstacle on Pouf's face. Upon seeing the ground zero of the Poor Man's Rose, Pouf is shaken with horror. However, Youpi snaps him back to reality and orders him to surround the area in case the explosion sent the King flying, while he himself will enter the flaming abyss to search for him. Admitting that he was wrong about the humans, Youpi tells him that once they find the King, they'll kill them all. The two of them begin to search around the area, with Youpi entering the chasm while Pouf breaks into hundreds of clones and searches everywhere. But as Youpi looks around the burning earth, he notices something that causes him to let out a blood-curdling scream.

Chapter 299 Regeneration (, "Saisei") is the 299th chapter of the Hunter × Hunter manga, written and illustrated by Yoshihiro Togashi. Synopsis. Youpi flies from the burning gorge of the Poor Man's Rose, howling in grief as he cradles something in his arms. Pouf flies towards him, tears already flowing as his fears were becoming true even before he knew it. In unison, the two scream as they look at the King himself, who is completely unrecognizable after the explosion. With limbs blown away and skin now blackened, he is horribly mutilated beyond a doubt. Despite this, the King slowly opens his eyes, shocking his Royal Guards. However, Youpi knows he won't last long and that it's already too late to reach Pitou. Suddenly, Pouf has an idea. He claims he can save the King by offering his cells to him. As he does so, the King begins to glow and breathe rapidly. Pouf asks him if feels all right, and the King can only describe it as ""an exquisite delicacy beyond description." His compliments fill Pouf with euphoric ecstasy. Youpi provides the King with more food as he liquefies his cells for him to drink. Like Pouf's, the King praises it as "veritable dewdrops of the angels"", imagining that it had to have come from the heavens and causing Youpi to rejoice with ecstasy as well. Declaring both their offerings as supreme, the King wants more of it. Overwhelmed with euphoria, Pouf and Youpi gladly accept this as they offer more of their bodies to the King. At the same time, the two can't help but wonder why they feel this happy. But at that moment, their questions are answered when the King tells them that from now on, they can call him "Meruem," the name that was given by his mother. Reaching an epiphany, Pouf and Youpi come to realize that this feeling is actually unconditional love, the love of a mother for her child. Now that the two had revived the King, they had become equals to the mother of their species, and both cry with overwhelming joy.

Chapter 3 The Ultimate Choice (の, "Kyūkyoku no Sentaku") is the 3rd chapter of the Hunter × Hunter manga, written and illustrated by Yoshihiro Togashi. Synopsis. It's stated that the only information provided to every Hunter applicant are the date and time of the Hunter Exam and a general location of the exam site, acting as yet another step to becoming a Hunter. At Dolle Harbor, the three applicants walk among a busy crowd, with Leorio saying that they now need to get a ride to Zaban City. Kurapika examines the crowd's people and guesses they are heading for the same location. Gon approaches the captain and thanks him for everything. After shaking Gon's hand and wishing him good luck, the captain points to a lone pine tree on a nearby hill and tells him it's a good place to start looking for the exam site. Once Gon happily thanks him and takes his leave, the captain tells Ging not to worry since his son has what it takes. Behind a nearby building, an unknown figure is seen eavesdropping on the conversation. Standing in front of a large map, Leorio points out Zaban City and asks Gon why he wants to head toward the pine tree in the opposite direction. He suggests taking the express bus and says climbing the hill would be a waste of their time, with Kurapika asking Gon if he heard the captain correctly. Gon remains confident and plans to make his way there, with Leorio telling him not to trust others so much and again suggesting that they take the bus. As Gon continues walking toward the pine tree and waves goodbye, Kurapika begins to follow him and Leorio wonders why. Kurapika smiles slightly and says he's intrigued by what Gon may do. Leorio stubbornly makes his way to the bus stop and sits down to wait, eventually hearing two men discussing that the buses never reached Zaban City and that it was a trap exposing any rookies. Sitting motionless for a moment, Leorio jumps up and runs toward the pine tree, yelling after Gon and Kurapika. On their way to the pine tree, the three eventually find themselves in a deserted alley, but Gon and Kurapika can sense that there are people around. Leorio is left confused and asks how they can tell, with Kurapika saying that he can hear them breathing and Gon saying that their clothes are rustling. After Leorio is still unable to hear anything, several people suddenly appear in front of them, including an old woman holding a cane. She speaks softly at first, but then yells out that it's time for a two-choice quiz, leaving the three applicants confused as her masked attendants clap in response. The woman explains that the town is the only safe way to reach the pine tree, revealing that the other trails are mazes filled with magical beasts. She then tells them that she will ask a question and give them five seconds to answer, adding that they will fail and be unable to take part in that year's Hunter Exam if they answer incorrectly. After the woman adds that they must answer with either #1 or #2, Leorio realizes that they only get one question between the three of them, but Gon points out that they can work together to answer.
