The applicant, who was eavesdropping on Gon and the captain back at Dolle Harbor, suddenly appears, asking if he can take the test and revealing to Gon that he listened in on his conversation. Leorio realizes that they can see what the woman's questions are like if they let the other applicant go first. After thanking them out loud, the man calls them stupid internally and plans to set up traps on the path ahead. The woman then tells the applicant that criminals have taken his mother and true love captive, asking which of the two he would save. Kurapika is left confused since the question is purely subjective, wondering if they have to guess which answer she prefers. The applicant chooses the first option, but tells himself that he only chose it because it's the answer the woman most likely prefers. She then asks for his reason, and he explains that while another true love can be found, a person's mother cannot be replaced. The woman talks with her attendants and tells the applicant that he may go, with the man smugly walking past them. Leorio becomes furious at the woman and her quiz, pointing out that the question has no right answer and declaring that he will find another route to the exam site. However, the woman reminds him that it's the only way and that he won't be able to enter the exam if he leaves. Kurapika suddenly realizes something, and as Leorio wonders if he plans to go along with the quiz, the woman stops them from speaking and tells herself that Kurapika has heard. She then warns them that if they speak without answering the question, they all fail, asking whether they will take the quiz or not. Kurapika quickly chooses the first option, internally telling Leorio to think since it's a simple trick. He also guesses that Gon has realized it, pointing out that the quiz isn't about the questions, but what they hear and don't hear. The woman then tells them that their son and daughter have been kidnapped, asking which of the two they will get back. As she begins counting down from five, Leorio can't believe that she asked a question similar to the first, walking over to a stack of wooden poles. He grabs one and breaks off a piece to make it shorter, telling her that the seconds left are how much longer she has to live. Once the woman reaches the end of the countdown, Leorio suddenly leaps toward her and swings the makeshift weapon. Still, Kurapika jumps in the way and uses his to block the strike. Kurapika tries to calm him down, but Leorio continues to express his anger toward the woman and the entire Hunter Exam process. However, Kurapika suddenly reveals that they have passed the test, again telling Leorio to control his temper. He explains that the correct response is no response at all, pointing out that while the woman told them they could only say #1 or #2, she didn't tell them that they had to say anything. Leorio then angrily points out that the earlier applicant was allowed to pass. Still, Kurapika reminds him that she didn't say he was correct, revealing that he heard his scream and guessing that he had encountered a magical beast. After Kurapika surmises that the path he took isn't right, the woman confirms it and has her attendants reveal a hidden passage to the real path, a plain trail that will take them to the pine tree in two hours. Leorio is left embarrassed and apologizes, but the woman tells him that he makes the job interesting and wishes the three applicants good luck. However, Gon finally speaks up and happily says he can't come up with an answer. Both Kurapika and Leorio chuckle, pointing out that they already passed, but Gon wonders what they will do if they have to make a similar choice one day. He adds that it won't be about right or wrong, but about what's in their heart when things are rough. With Kurapika and Leorio saying nothing in response, the woman says to herself that Gon has realized the point of the test and that they must be ready for such events in their lives. The three then wave goodbye and walk toward the pine tree through the door.

Chapter 30 The Slithering Trap (く, "Ugomeku Wana") is the 30th chapter of the Hunter × Hunter manga, written and illustrated by Yoshihiro Togashi. Synopsis. On Zevil Island, Kurapika and Leorio continue to look for other examinees but are unable to find any. Leorio notes that the Fourth Phase has lasted almost six days and only has one day left. When Kurapika points out that their last encounter was with Hisoka three days earlier, Leorio proposes returning to the landing site to see whether anyone has already passed. However, Kurapika replies that no one has since collecting badges worth six points in total is only one part of the challenge, reminding Leorio that the other is to hold on to them and that the deadline isn't until the following day. Leorio still thinks that it may be worth checking, and Kurapika agrees since those who already have six points will start making their way back toward the landing site. Although the two spot the boat in the water, they don't see any examinees. Kurapika then proposes that they continue hunting and set a time and place for their rendezvous. Someone suddenly asks if they can help, and the two look up to find Gon watching them in a nearby tree. With the two surprised to see him, Gon jumps down and reveals that he spotted several examinees around the landing site. Leorio wonders why they didn't think of using an elevated position, and Kurapika points out that Gon was only able to see them because of his extraordinary perception. Kurapika then asks if he has his badges, and Gon confirms that he does, with Leorio realizing that he's the only one left and asking Gon if he has seen his target (#246), a woman named Ponzu. Gon replies that he hasn't and leaves Leorio disappointed, but Kurapika rationally considers the four possibilities: 1) Ponzu is alive and still has her badge; 2) she is alive and no longer has her badge; 3) she is dead and still has her badge; 4) she is dead and no longer has her badge. Leorio wonders how the third option could be possible, and Kurapika explains that Ponzu may have had an accident or been attacked after she had already hidden her badge elsewhere, adding that the badge may never be found if she was killed after hiding it. Although Leorio continues to lose hope, Gon wonders if Ponzu has any specific traits like Leorio's use of cologne, and Kurapika realizes that Gon may be able to track her scent. Leorio wonders how they can know if she uses a fragrance, and Kurapika reminds him that Ponzu uses chemical weapons, guessing that some of them have particular odors. Gon agrees to give it a shot and stresses that he came to help. The other two then follow Gon as he sniffs the grass and air. He eventually picks up a scent and tells them that they're close, leading them to a nearby cave. Leorio decides to investigate it by himself and tells the other two to wait, first checking the opening and making sure that there are no traps. He then tells Gon and Kurapika that he will go inside alone and that they should wait until he gives the all-clear. Kurapika says that if they don't hear from him after 30 minutes, they will go inside no matter what. Although Leorio adamantly disagrees and tells them to forget about him so the two of them can return to the landing site, Kurapika points out that they can't leave anyone behind in an alliance. Speechless at first, Leorio tells them that the alliance is over and thanks them for their help, saying that it's up to him now. However, Gon and Kurapika are adamant about staying behind to help him, and Leorio eventually relents, preparing to enter the cave with a lighter and tossing back his briefcase for them to keep safe. After Leorio enters the cave and night eventually falls, he yells out for them to stay back and warns that there are snakes inside. Gon and Kurapika quickly dash toward the cave entrance and yell Leorio's name, only hearing the slithering of snakes inside. The two then make their way down into the cave and find Leorio lying hurt on the ground with several snakes cut in half around him, as Ponzu and Bourbon sit up against the cave's walls. Leorio struggles to speak and reminds them that he told them to leave, but Kurapika sees that he's covered in snake bites, worrying that they belong to vipers. Gon picks up one of the dead snakes and confirms that they are vipers, pointing out that while they aren't too venomous, Leorio has been struck enough to receive a fatal dose. Gon then starts to suck out the venom and spit it out, but Kurapika worries about the bleeding and gets Gon to help him move Leorio so they can get him to a doctor. However, Ponzu suddenly speaks up and reveals that they are trapped inside the cave, explaining that the snakes will attack them all at once if they try to leave. As she adds that the trap was set up by Bourbon, dozens of snakes begin to slither inside the cave. Ponzu explains that like Leorio, they will be paralyzed by the bites and then slowly succumb to death. Kurapika addresses Bourbon and offers to give him their badges in exchange for letting them leave, but Ponzu reveals that Bourbon is dead.

Chapter 300 Insurance (, "Hoken") is the 300th chapter of the Hunter × Hunter manga, written and illustrated by Yoshihiro Togashi. Synopsis. Ikalgo is shown leaving the basement, and he's shocked to see that so much of the palace has been destroyed in only half an hour. One of the fallen towers begins crumbling, forcing him to escape the rubble. Someone suddenly calls his name, and he spots Killua accompanied by Palm. The three sit and talk, with Ikalgo thrilled that Palm is alive, saying that he can drive her to Peijin as they planned. But Killua tells him that she wants to stay, and adds that she's probably stronger now than he is. Palm longs to see Gon, but says she wants to respect his wishes, confusing Ikalgo. Killua clarifies that Gon plans to fight Pitou on his own, and Ikalgo realizes that they're staying behind because Gon has no chance against the Royal Guard, and neither do they, so they plan to stay and die together. Killua mentions that they're looking for Knuckle, and Ikalgo agrees to help. Some time passes, and the three meet up with Knuckle and Meleoron, who tell them that they separated the Royal Guards and Netero has taken out the King. Since they've done what they were supposed to, Knuckle asks them if they should leave or stay, personally saying that they should fight until the very end. The rest silently agree, and they all begin walking toward the palace. Gon rises to his feet and tells Pitou their time is up, leaving them in shock at how he knew that the surgery was finished when they had tried to hide it so well. As Pitou continues to worry about Gon's heightened awareness, he tells them to stand up and that they will make it to Peijin more quickly if they run. With Doctor Blythe deactivated, Pitou anxiously rises as Komugi awakens and asks what happened to her. Pitou begins to say something to Gon, but his expression suddenly darkens as he threatens to kill Komugi if Pitou talks out of turn again. With Komugi scared, Pitou agrees to follow him, and it's stated that Pitou could have taken off Gon's head at that moment, but restrained themselves, understanding how sharp his perception was. They know their chance will come, and that they have to somehow transfer Komugi to the King during their journey to Peijin. But Killua and Knuckle suddenly appear, with the latter asking Gon if he wants him to use Hakoware to be able to keep track of Pitou if they escape (with A.P.R. also acting as a shield for him if they attack). Gon calmly refuses the offer, saying that he trusts Pitou, and tells him to take care of Komugi until he and Pitou reach Kite. Both Knuckle and Pitou immediately realize that he's using her as a hostage, and Gon promises to release her once Kite is healed. He then sternly asks if Pitou will trust him as well, sweat dripping down their face, and the two sprint off toward Peijin. The rest of the group stands around Komugi, and Ikalgo asks Killua if he's sure he didn't want to go with them. Killua says it's fine, and that he was glad when he heard the hostage plan since if Pitou were to capture him, he would become one himself and a hostage exchange could ruin things. Knuckle shudders at Killua's cold composure, wondering how much he's been through to think this way. Palm assures them that she can see what happens since she saw Gon with her eye, and Killua reminds them that Pitou won't abandon Komugi, who trembles with fear and confusion at the whole ordeal.

Chapter 301 Memory (, "Kioku") is the 301st chapter of the Hunter × Hunter manga, written and illustrated by Yoshihiro Togashi. Synopsis. Meruem emerges more powerful than ever after absorbing Pouf and Youpi's cells, with both overjoyed at this. However, they sense that Meruem is disturbed about something, and remind him of the food that awaits him at the palace. Meruem speaks of a voice he heard call his name, though he doesn't know whether it was real or a dream. From this, they learn that he's suffering from memory loss, unable to remember why he is there. Meruem orders them to explain what happened, confused why they look different. Pouf says they sent out their segments to eliminate any enemies they find, but Meruem moves his tail toward Pouf's face, recognizing the lie and asking them if he ate them. Both Royal Guards assure him that it was their own decision, and Meruem tells them to explain things further. Pouf asks him if he can remember their original forms and the first day they served him. Meruem is unsure, only recognizing them but retaining no memory of events. Pouf theorizes that his memories are temporarily lost because of the explosion, explaining Meruem's duel against Netero, and the suicidal bomb he used to try to finish him off. The word "duel" triggers Meruem's memories of playing a board game, but not fully. As Pouf continues to explain the events leading up to the present and tells him they had no choice but to sacrifice part of themselves to revive him, his clone secretly rushes back toward the palace, excited with the chance it's been given. If he can eliminate Komugi, Meruem will have no way to remember her. He has a 20-minute window in which to do it before Meruem runs back to the palace. But much to Pouf's surprise, Meruem suddenly sprouts wings and asks where the palace is, stating that the answer he desires lies there. Pouf and Youpi hang on tight as Meruem quickly flies off, with the former realizing it will take Meruem only five minutes to reach the palace at his current speed. However, by seeing all the humans lined up, he hopes that Meruem will remember that his only purpose is to rule all life, with Pouf hellbent on killing Komugi and upholding his duty as a Royal Guard to carry out the Queen's wishes. As he enters the tower and finds it completely empty, Knuckle suddenly lands a hard right to his side, hidden again under Meleoron's God's Accomplice and activating Hakoware. Palm appears from around the corner and says she can observe Pouf from anywhere since she saw him with her eye before he put her in the cocoon. Pouf senses his clone being hit, but does not know who it was since Knuckle was hidden. Meruem notices A.P.R. on Pouf, who explains that someone attacked his clone. Meruem quickens his pace as a result, and the members of the Extermination Team become aware of the fact that the King is still alive.

Chapter 302 Target (, "Hyōteki") is the 302nd chapter of the Hunter × Hunter manga, written and illustrated by Yoshihiro Togashi. Synopsis. Palm continues to observe the movement of Pouf's core, telling the others that he's with the King and they're quickly making for the palace. Knuckle worries how they can possibly win if even Netero lost, and Komugi still waits in confusion as to what's happening. Flying quickly to the palace, Meruem becomes more annoyed by the sight of A.P.R., and Youpi informs them that it belongs to one of the enemies, guessing that it won't go away until they hurt him. Meruem wants to test the theory, and suddenly manifests Youpi's rage on his left arm, with an opening appearing on his left hand and firing a giant beam at A.P.R. An enormous mass of stone is destroyed as A.P.R. appears out of the rubble, and Youpi is amazed, realizing that his ability was never meant for himself, but to be given to Meruem. But Meruem seems confused, asking Youpi how he knows about the ability. Youpi confesses that it was previously used on him, and Meruem wonders why he left the enemy alive and, consequently, how he deactivated the ability. Youpi admits that he struck a deal with them, sparing all their lives, but Meruem remains confused as to why he didn't kill them afterward, with Youpi unsure, though he says that not keeping his promise, even to an enemy, would have felt like a defeat. Pouf quickly rebukes him for not seizing his chance, and as Youpi prepares to receive punishment, to their surprise Meruem moves on and makes it clear that he only asked him for the truth. He notes the complexity they all possess now and tells them that they are connected in mind and body now, informing them that no secrets can exist between them. As Youpi begins to tear up and Pouf worries that Meruem is sensing his guilt at going behind his back, his clones finally reach the palace, desperately looking for Komugi even if his decision results in his own death. Knuckle suddenly appears before them and taunts their weakness, but they simply ignore him as he yells that they can only get rid of A.P.R. by fighting him. Pouf tells Youpi about the situation, asking if he also has the ability to teleport, but Youpi says it's the chameleon, clarifying that he can make himself and others invisible and that he's a traitorous Chimera Ant. Pouf is in disbelief that he spared a traitor as well, but Meruem assures them that the emotions they're feeling are simply to be overcome on their way to further evolution. He recognizes that they have the remains of the human ego within them, but tells them to consider it to be just a transition before they reach their final stage. It's stated that Meruem's beliefs are completely different from how they were before the Rose's explosion, and it's asked whether this is due to the blast, but quickly answered that he possesses both mindsets. Pouf's clones plan to shrink down even further, hoping to be able to find Meleoron by touch. Knuckle wonders why he came back if not for him, worrying that Meleoron is his target and stating that they have no way to defeat the King without God's Accomplice. Palm is shown running toward the underground entrance, stating that besides the core, she can only see Pouf's clones when they're full size. As Pouf realizes that the enemy thinks he's after Meleoron, the latter is seen using God's Accomplice as he rides piggyback on Killua, with Komugi sitting on his tail and holding onto his back. Pouf continues to theorize about how the enemy is thinking, considering that they will leave Komugi behind to protect Meleoron if they think that is the one he's after. And since Pitou was so focused on healing Komugi, he surmises that they will never think that he's after Komugi, hoping he may even be able to set up an exchange for her. He sees Palm opening up the underground entrance, and realizes that they're trying to separate his clones even more. And suddenly spotting Killua standing on one of the walls, with Komugi on his back, Pouf realizes that they're forcing his hand so they can learn whether Meleoron or Komugi is his target. He considers all his options, but determines that he has no time to play games and quickly flies toward Killua and Komugi.

Chapter 303 Pain (み, "Itami") is the 303rd chapter of the Hunter × Hunter manga, written and illustrated by Yoshihiro Togashi. Synopsis. As Pouf flies in with extreme confidence to kill Komugi, Killua uses Godspeed to easily dodge the attack and Pouf realizes his speed will be nearly impossible, to match. As he panics over Meruem's impending arrival, he says he has a perfect magic trick and uses Beelzebub to send out his clones. Killua believes that he's using these smaller clones to avoid damaging Komugi, and he easily outruns them, saying he wouldn't even need to use Godspeed to do so. But Pouf laughs, saying that Killua's plan has been thwarted, and tells him the King will forgive him if he surrenders. Komugi perks up at the word "King," and Pouf relishes that Killua is running further away, hoping that Meruem won't see him when he finally reaches the palace. Killua understands how important it is to hold onto Komugi, who recognizes Pouf's voice, surmising that the King must be "dear leader," as she calls him, and wonders who it is that's carrying her. Pouf's clones continue to yell at Killua to surrender, claiming he will put Komugi under a spell with his words. With Killua still confused at Pouf's plan, Komugi begins pulling at Killua's hair, wondering why it feels like static, and tries to escape off his back. He tries to assure that he's rescuing her, asking her if she trusts bugs more than him, but she has no clue what he means, with Killua quickly figuring out that she's blind. During the confusion, Pouf suddenly swoops down and Killua barely moves out of the way in time. Pouf claims his "poison" has worked and wonders how well he can run with Komugi struggling against him. Killua works out that not only is Pouf going for Komugi, but he's trying to kill her. Pouf laughs maniacally and knows they won't kill her since she has value as a hostage. Killua calmly sets her down on the ground, saying that she's unconscious and that Pouf is really annoying him. With Komugi lying at his feet, he surrounds himself in a circle of electricity and threatens to kill Pouf if he crosses it. Pouf immediately flies in with no hesitation, and Killua easily destroys his right eye, telling him how easy it is to burn cells with electricity. Pouf realizes how dangerous the situation is, with Meruem sensing his frustration and offering to help, but Pouf calmly declines and says recovering his memory is their priority. At that moment, they hold the palace in their sights, and Pouf proudly showcases the waves of hypnotized humans below him, stressing that Meruem's destiny is to have the world flourish beneath his light. But a pain stirs in Meruem as he stops in midair and notes that there was something else, asking why the palace is so destroyed. Youpi tells him that it was caused by their fight with the enemy, and Meruem asks to see the remains of his living quarters. Pouf suddenly realizes that if he sees the Gungi board and its pieces, it could trigger his memory of Komugi. His clones fly away from Killua in order to find all of them as quickly as possible. Elsewhere, Gon and Pitou reach Peijin, looking toward a large mansion in the mountains where Kite is being kept.

Chapter 304 Magic (, "Mahō") is the 304th chapter of the Hunter × Hunter series, written and illustrated by Yoshihiro Togashi. Synopsis. Meruem touches down inside the palace grounds, and the others immediately feel his presence. Pouf's segments begin to carry off the Gungi board and pieces, looking for Welfin as well, and Ikalgo looks for another corpse to take over, but the ones he finds are too mangled to use. Knuckle and Meleoron walk through the crowd of hypnotized citizens, with the former saying that A.P.R. won't increase its interest from where they are, also worrying about when Pouf and the King separate, unsure if he should deactivate the A.P.R. on Pouf and then try to use it on the King. Pouf informs Meruem of the cocoons he walks by, telling him that they contain humans who will be skilled for combat once they hatch. Palm meets up with Killua, who is still carrying the unconscious Komugi. She tells him the King's location and thinks they should hide among the crowd. Killua asks her about Gon and Pitou, and she replies that they just reached Peijin and Kite's location. She explains more about her observation ability, Wink Blue, which allows her to keep track of someone if she's seen them with just her right eye. She can then monitor them with just her left eye. Like different channels on a television, she is currently watching Gon/Pitou, herself/Killua, and Pouf/Youpi/the King. She can have up to three people registered at once (so currently, Pouf, Gon, and Killua). If she has three people registered and looks at someone else with her right eye, the oldest is replaced (Pouf, in this case). Killua thinks they don't need to observe Pouf anyway since Palm can only see his core, but she believes that may be the key to defeating him because destroying the core would result in Pouf's death. Observing them from the bushes, one of Pouf's segments worries that they have figured him out, but gleefully wants them to see what Gon and Pitou are up to. Killua awkwardly thanks her for helping out and considers her a friend. He asks her how Gon is doing, but as she goes to check, she sees something that leaves her in disbelief and makes Killua worried. Gon and Pitou enter the mansion, and the former directs them to Kite's location. Given the silence and Pitou's extraordinary hearing, they were able to hear a voice from a cell phone in their pocket. Welfin speaks, saying that he and Bloster recovered Komugi, putting her on the phone. She says she's safe, and this leaves Pitou with a serious look on their face. Welfin is shown hanging up the phone and asks for a doctor to treat his wounds, as Pouf is shown with Komugi's head, revealing that he can reconfigure his cells to affect even the vocal cords. Pouf declares that Pitou is now under his spell too, hoping it will finally release them from Komugi's curse. Gon and Pitou reach Kite, who rests on his knees facing the other way. Gon orders them to heal Kite and agrees to let Komugi go afterward. Pitou asks for his name again, and once he gives it, they tell him that they feel the need, to be honest with him since he let them heal Komugi, suddenly revealing that Kite is already dead. They say he died when the two first fought, and Kite's body slumps face down onto the floor. As Gon begins to cry, Pitou says their ability is unable to revive the dead, only able to preserve and manipulate bodies since the soul is gone. They apologize to Gon as he drops to his knees and remembers Kite scolding him when he was younger. He says to himself that he's the one who killed Kite, and continues to blame himself as he remembers when Kite entrusted him with Ging's Hunter License, now looking upon his body lying motionless on the floor.

Chapter 305 Sorry (, "Zannen") is the 305th chapter of the Hunter × Hunter manga, written and illustrated by Yoshihiro Togashi. Synopsis. Gon remembers Kite's words about animals liking good Hunters, as he continues to say that he killed Kite. Words begin to flood his mind: he regrets what he could have done, wonders if Kite is really dead, realizes Pitou is to blame, not himself, desperately begs for help and repeats that Kite is dead, saying no again and again and again as tears stream down his face. Pitou suddenly manifests Doctor Blythe, and Gon thinks Pitou must have been lying before and that they really can revive Kite. But Pitou begins to heal their own broken arm, confusing Gon and making him wonder why they're not healing Kite first. Killua nervously asks Palm what's happening, and she says she isn't entirely sure since she can only see them, not hear what's going on, but she sees that Pitou isn't healing Kite and spots Gon crouched on the floor. Killua assures himself that as long as they have Komugi, Pitou won't be able to disobey them. Pouf suddenly appears before them, saying that Pitou thinks Komugi is safe away from them and that they can freely kill Gon now. He promises to stop Pitou if they hand over Komugi, but Killua quickly snatches up the segment and destroys it. Palm catches Komugi and assures Killua she will take care of her, with Killua using Speed of Lightning to reach Gon and desperately hoping that he can hang on until he gets there. Pitou finishes healing their arm, quickly testing it out, and apologizes to Gon, saying that he has to be killed for the King's sake. Still crying, Gon is even more confused and wonders why they won't even try after all he went through. He calls them a liar, slowly rising to his feet as an ominous gust begins to fill the mansion and startles Pitou with confusion. With his face emotionless, Gon says he's had enough and just wants things to end, his hair suddenly billowing up and his entire figure transforming. He coldly states he doesn't care what happens to himself, asking for all the power he will ever have. Pitou quickly uses Terpsichora, understanding that they were right about the threat Gon could pose to the King and knowing they have to kill the unrecognizable figure standing opposite.

Chapter 306 Relief (, "Ando") is the 306th chapter of the Hunter × Hunter manga, written and illustrated by Yoshihiro Togashi. Synopsis. As Gon's transformation nears completion, Pitou activates Terpsichora to go beyond their limits. Realizing that his power could potentially rival the King's, they charge towards Gon with the intent to kill, only for him to disappear instantly. Shocked, Pitou looks around the room for where he could have gone and sees the door behind them now open. Believing that Gon could be going after the King, they run down the hall. But blocking their path is a tall, dark figure who challenges them to fight outside the mansion, not wanting to destroy it. It is then revealed that the figure itself is really Gon, transformed into an adult with long hair flowing endlessly. His aura flows calmly, yet ominously at the same time. As the two-step outside the mansion, Pitou has no idea what has happened, but concludes that Gon somehow forced his body to mature to the point where he could defeat them. In another desperate attempt, Pitou tries to kill him again. However, Gon effortlessly dodges it and sends Pitou flying into the air with a kick to the stomach. He then shifts into his Jajanken stance, summoning tremendous power as Pitou plummets back down. At point-blank range, Gon strikes them in the face with a Rock, sending the Ant straight into a dense forest As they fade into unconsciousness, Pitou is relieved, now realizing that the reason Gon became so powerful was that he was willing to give up all the Nen and potential he has to defeat them—unable to use Nen ever again after this. They rejoice at the fact that they're the one, to suffer all his rage, as Gon slowly approaches their mutilated body.

Chapter 307 Loss (, "Sonshitsu") is the 307th chapter of the Hunter × Hunter manga, written and illustrated by Yoshihiro Togashi. Synopsis. As Killua finally reaches Peijin, he sees a flash of aura coming from the forest, its sound being described as "a saw being drawn across steel strings." He immediately notices it and heads toward its location, only to see what he wasn't expecting. He encounters Gon, now an adult, who kneels beside Pitou, pummeling their head continuously. With a powerful Jajanken, Gon finally shatters their skull. He stands up and addresses to Kite that he's finished the job, just like he told him to. Stunned, Killua calls out to Gon and asks if it's really him. Gon acknowledges his presence as he turns around, revealing his tears. Seeing Gon's new form, Killua is immediately reminded of Biscuit. However, he deduces that while Biscuit could change her physical appearance at will, Gon must have done something drastic to get this much aura. With no warning, Pitou's Terpsichora activates and manipulates their headless corpse to attack Gon. Killua reacts to the movement and tries to save him, only for the corpse to move faster and cut off Gon's right arm. Due to the Royal Guard's loyalty to the King, their Terpsichora has become stronger with Nen amplified after death—its sole intention to kill Gon. While there was no time to blink as Pitou's body leaps toward them, Gon reassures Killua that he's all right. He feels content as he can now be like Kite in the end. Punching Pitou's body back, he grabs his severed arm and impales the corpse into the ground with it. Gon prepares to unleash one last Jajanken, much stronger than the last, to destroy Pitou once and for all. Killua screams out to Gon, knowing what will happen to him if he uses too much aura. At that moment, Gon snaps out of his rage and looks at him tearfully. An explosion comes shortly after, destroying the whole forest.

Chapter 308 Flash (, "Senkō") is the 308th chapter of the Hunter × Hunter manga, written and illustrated by Yoshihiro Togashi. Synopsis. Meruem continues his search of the palace, finding the west tower empty as Pouf desperately hopes to buy enough time for him not to remember Komugi. Meruem still feels like something is missing, and Youpi assures Pouf that he won't tell Meruem about Komugi, desiring things to stay as they are. Meruem believes his sense of longing could just be due to the memory loss, and his two Royal Guards are confident that he will make a full recovery soon. He asks them about the selection process happening at noon, and they tell him they can move things up since the rest of the citizens will be in place by 9:00 a.m. But Pouf remembers that he hasn't hypnotized the newly arriving citizens, and plans to use his scales to do so. Meruem asks Youpi what he plans to do, and he says he will look for Pitou since he isn't very useful in his current form. The mention of Pitou brings back Meruem's memory of them, and Pouf is now worried that names can be a trigger, hoping he can convince Pitou to side with them. Another pain runs through Meruem, and he remembers entrusting something to Pitou's care and giving them an order. He orders Youpi to summon Pitou, planning to look for them himself as well as to track down the remaining enemies at the palace, both to get information from them and for his own fun. Pouf questions his decision to go off on his own, and an enraged Meruem asks him if he believes any of the enemies could defeat him, his aura immediately silencing both guards and making them realize that quantity of aura alone could win a battle. Trembling with fear, Pouf quickly backs down and says that Meruem is without equal in strength. The King's terrifying aura reaches the others around the palace and fills them with terror, causing Knuckle to immediately realize the hopelessness of the situation and to tell Meleoron they need to make their way through the crowd back to Peijin. Meleoron worries about the others, but Knuckle knows they will reach the same conclusion after feeling the King's aura. Meleoron tries to convince him that their combination attack will work, but again Knuckle stresses how dire the situation is: even if they're able to land an attack, the two would have to stay within 50 meters of the King for A.P.R. to add interest, and unless Meleoron has the lung capacity of Morel, it would be pretty much impossible. In addition, Knuckle worries that they already know their abilities and can easily counter them, worrying that he should have already contacted the Association to tell them about Netero's death so they can begin a backup plan. With Knuckle driven by duty, and Meleoron by revenge, the two-step forward at different rates. But at that moment, Meruem's En illuminates the entire palace, and he suddenly appears right beside Knuckle, applying pressure to his neck and knocking him unconscious. Meleoron is unable to even think about using Perfect Plan before Meruem quickly strikes the back of his neck, putting him to sleep as well. A.P.R. vanishes from Pouf, and Meruem reappears before the Royal Guards, holding both Knuckle and Meleoron and saying he plans to question them later. He had sensed two others with his En, as Ikalgo and Palm carrying Komugi on her back are seen desperately running away, with Pouf fearing that one of them has Komugi.

Chapter 309 Game (, "Shōbu") is the 309th chapter of the Hunter × Hunter manga, written and illustrated by Yoshihiro Togashi. Synopsis. Shaiapouf suggests the King entertain himself more, and at the latter's request for an explanation, the Royal Guard replies that they should have a competition: as he and Menthuthuyoupi search for Neferpitou, the King will try to catch the two remaining intruders, who are both Nen users. Whoever finds their target first wins. Youpi asks him if he plans to use his scales to hypnotize the rest of the citizens. Pouf replies that he will, so he'll need the King to wait for a while since the difference between his own power and that of the intruders is so great that it would end in a second without being amusing at all; and since they don't know Pitou's location, it may take a while before they find them. So he sets one more condition: the King will use his En only once more. Meruem accepts, promising to grant them one wish each if they win. The two Royal Guards agree with this. Youpi inquires about the nature of the King's wish, and he and Pouf are appalled to discover that Meruem expects them to reveal what they are hiding from him. Due to their bodies being linked, he can sense their negative emotions; however, because of that, he can also feel their strong loyalty, so he has let them live. If he loses the competition, he will also allow them to keep their secret. Pouf returns to his normal form, swearing he will do his best to spread his scales as fast as possible, without trying to buy time. Meruem repeats the rules for the last time and states that if Pitou returns on his own, he will tell him to hide. He also informs the guards that the remaining Nen users that he perceived through his En before were an octopus and a human carrying something. Pouf reflects that he has to win at all costs, knowing that Pitou and the girl will be a problem. He instructs Youpi not to look for Pitou, but to keep him away from the King. Youpi does not understand the meaning of the handicap he set, considering he cannot split and spread his scales simultaneously, but Pouf tells him to trust him and flies off. In the meantime, Palm continues to flee after feeling the King's En, still shocked by his aura. She realizes that Meleoron and Knuckle were captured and not killed, so she gazes at Killua with her power. She sees him carrying an unconscious person who, due to the crystal only showing two people, has to be Gon despite his long hair. She wonders what happened while she was not watching and where Pitou is, and silently begs them not to come to the palace. She then spies on Pouf, whom she finds scattering his scales, although she does not understand for what use and why he is far from the King. However, since he is going in the opposite direction, she does not worry about him. Remembering the King's frightening display of power in catching Meleoron and Knuckle, she guesses that she and Ikalgo will be next, and he could very well appear behind her right there and then. She wonders if it would be better to hide underground, where the King's En might not reach, at the cost of risking remaining trapped, or if she should run away from the palace. She is startled to feel a presence near her, but it is only Ikalgo, who, like her, has thought of hiding there and urges her inside. Palm seems on the verge of objecting, but ultimately agrees to go with him. As they run, she tells Ikalgo that Killua is with Gon and that she does not know what happened to Pitou. Ikalgo drives the truck he has previously stolen and asks Palm why, in her opinion, Meleoron and Knuckle are still alive. Palm says she isn't even sure they are, just hoping so. However, Ikalgo states that he believes they are alive for a hostage exchange. He is determined to set a trap, starting with hiding Komugi in Bizeff's room. Once they arrive, he tells Palm to gather the four girls that worked under the secretary and suggests she tie their hands and blindfold them to avoid panic. She agrees and inquires as to why he has taken Welfin and an unconscious Bloster along. The reason is revealed shortly afterward when Ikalgo asks Welfin to be his messenger: he will tell the King or the Royal Guards that they are in the underground vault and they have the girl. To avoid casting suspicion on himself, Welfin makes clear that he will have to inform them that it is a trap, to which Ikalgo agrees. Still, Welfin considers not going along with it in his hand, thinking about the danger he risks in relaying such a message to the King. But he tells Ikalgo he'll do it, and takes the truck. Palm, due to his key role in their strategy, wants to watch him with her power even if it means being unable to observe Pouf any longer, but Ikalgo stops her. He then tells Welfin that he will be free after he delivers the message, and suggests he go and see Gyro. Welfin gets mad at him, but Ikalgo calls him by his true name, Zaiqahal, which Welfin had never disclosed to anyone. Ikalgo reveals that, although he does not remember his own name, in his former life, he was his comrade. He then asks Welfin if he considers the Chimera Ants the enemy of their NGL. The wolf curses himself for giving in as he drives the truck out of the hangar, while Meruem is bothered by something, with the word "game" lingering in his mind.

Chapter 31 By the Skin of Their Teeth... (に⋯, "Kyūshi ni...") is the 31st chapter of the Hunter × Hunter manga, written and illustrated by Yoshihiro Togashi. Synopsis. As dozens of snakes slither inside the cave from the entrance and the crevices above, Kurapika wonders how Bourbon set the trap if he's dead. While Ponzu reveals that she killed him, she refuses to elaborate further. After Kurapika tells Gon to take the paralyzed Leorio and approaches Bourbon's body, numerous snakes suddenly appear on and around the corpse when he reaches to touch it. Ponzu notes that it's impossible to examine Bourbon's body, explaining that the snakes will attack anyone who tries to leave the cave or touch his body. Kurapika notices Bourbon's swollen hand and comments that it's a sign of serious anaphylactic shock, deducing that Ponzu attacked him with a neurotoxic bee. It's then stated that anaphylactic shock can occur when a person is stung by a bee, and antibodies are created against the toxin. If the person is stung by the same type of bee, they will have an allergic reaction; severe cases are known as anaphylactic shock, which can be fatal. Ponzu quickly confirms Kurapika's deduction and reveals that Bourbon was her specified target. She explains that she stalked him to the cave and then used sleeping gas after he entered, going inside once it took effect and finding Bourbon asleep. However, she reveals that he had already set his trap and when she reached for his badge, the snakes fell down on his body, guessing that the gas was unable to reach them in the cave's crevices. She adds that even though she jumped back before touching him, her own defenses were activated. Shen then taps the side of her hat and causes several bees to fly out, surprising both Gon and Kurapika. Ponzu explains that if she is startled or moved about, the bees come out and prepare to attack. She stresses that while she didn't mean to kill him, she couldn't have known that he was allergic and was unable to help him because of the snakes. Telling her bees that they can go back inside her hat, Ponzu continues by saying that Bourbon's death didn't deactivate his trap, guessing that his snakes protect him as long as they're alive. She admits that she has failed and resigns herself to being saved by the Hunter Association, pointing out that all the badges have transmitters that allow them to be tracked and saved if they are unable to pass a phase. She adds that they are lucky since there's only one day left for the Fourth Phase and that they only need to wait for help to arrive. Kurapika quickly reminds her that Leorio needs immediate medical attention to survive, but Ponzu notes that the committee only arrives once a phase ends, reminding the two that it's the same committee that allows the examinees to murder one another. Ponzu then stresses that Leorio ignored her warning and approached the exit to warn them about the snakes, causing several to strike him at once. She tells them that their only hope is that Leorio can hold out until help arrives. Kurapika realizes that while they have another option, it could result in another victim if they are wrong. Gon suddenly turns to Kurapika and tells him to take Leorio, walking toward Bourbon's body and leaving Ponzu in disbelief. As soon as Gon reaches out and grabs Bourbon's collar, several snakes leap toward him and sink their teeth all over his body. Even though more snakes bite down and cover his entire body, Gon holds firm and continues to examine the corpse, eventually finding an antidote with two needles and tossing them to Kurapika. As Gon falls paralyzed to the ground, Kurapika is left worried about his condition, but Gon tells him to give the antidote to Leorio first. Kurapika administers it to Leorio, and Ponzu is left stunned that Gon was looking for an antidote, pointing out that he couldn't have known that Bourbon had one. Kurapika tells her that it was more likely than not since it's necessary when poison is used as a negotiating tactic. As Kurapika administers the antidote to Gon, he says to himself that it was still incredibly courageous of Gon to take the risk. Gon quickly recovers from the venom and asks Ponzu if she has any sleeping gas left. She confirms that she does, but then wonders why he wants it. Gon reveals that he was also able to grab Bourbon's #103 badge, holding it up and offering to exchange it. While Ponzu agrees that releasing the gas inside the cave would be more effective and put all the snakes to sleep, she stresses that it will take five minutes to take effect and wonders who can hold their breath for that long. Gon stretches his arms and reveals that his personal best is nine minutes and 44 seconds, promising to get them all out safely. With the others left speechless, he tells Ponzu to release it on his signal, taking a big breath of air and then giving a thumbs-up. After Ponzu activates the gas, every creature inside the cave eventually falls asleep as Gon counts the seconds to five minutes. He then carries the three examinees on his back outside the cave and lets out an enormous exhale. He sets the sleeping Ponzu against a tree and gives her Bourbon's #103 badge so that the committee will find her. He rummages through her things and eventually finds her #246 badge, taking it as his rescue fee and playfully apologizing.

Chapter 310 Action (, "Shidō") is the 310th chapter of the Hunter × Hunter manga, written and illustrated by Yoshihiro Togashi. Synopsis. Not yet hypnotized, citizens at the back of the crowd talk amongst themselves and wonder what's going on, hearing rumors about the soldiers falling like broken puppets. They talk about the loud sounds they've heard coming from the palace, and think a coup could be happening. As they continue to speculate, a dust cloud suddenly falls upon them, hypnotizing them as Pouf flies high above. He worries that he won't be able to scatter his scales as well as before, since he gave 6/7 of his body to revive Meruem. He notices that Pitou's puppets have vanished, and wonders what kind of battle they're fighting if they need that much aura. Finally, Pouf is concerned that he's unable to use Beelzebub while scattering his scales, but knows that it will be his last chance to find and kill Komugi. Youpi searches the palace grounds, unable to find Pitou even after ten minutes. Welfin lets Bizeff's women go, telling them to untie their bonds and to escape in one of the trucks. He sees Bloster still unconscious in the back of the truck and remembers Ikalgo saying he was one of them and to take him along. He drives off, and thinks back to his conversation with Ikalgo, asking him how he knows Gyro is alive. Ikalgo can't be completely sure, but knows Gyro would not have died like that. Back in the present, Welfin proudly thinks that Ikalgo is right, declaring that the Ants are their enemy, and in exchange for getting him to see the truth, finally decides to go along with Ikalgo's plan. He drives the truck back outside, and Youpi immediately intercepts him. Welfin plays his role as the messenger, telling the Royal Guard that the enemy has Komugi in a warehouse underground and want to trade her for their friends. Youpi tells him he will relay the message to the King, but secretly keeps his promise to Pouf, planning to keep the information between themselves and continuing to wonder what Pitou is doing. As Youpi flies away, Welfin angrily reminds himself that the Ants are their enemy, as well as Gyro's. He gets Youpi's attention and asks him if he remembers anything from before he became an Ant. Youpi sternly says he doesn't, declaring that there's no before and after and telling him to not ask stupid questions. But Welfin gets his attention again, angering Youpi as he suddenly sees Welfin ready to attack. Welfin tells him that he has some more questions, telling him to answer in five seconds. Youpi threatens him with a menacing glare, but blood begins to run from his nose. Back in the west tower, with Knuckle and Meleoron still unconscious, Meruem continues to look for clues and suddenly spots a broken Gungi piece. He instantly remembers that he was playing a game with someone, unable to remember who, but knowing that he hasn't beaten them one time yet. As these memories flood his mind, the throbbing pain resurfaces, and his nose begins to bleed as well. Pouf finishes his hypnotizing of the crowd and flies back hopeful that Pitou has returned, but suddenly spots Youpi motionless on the ground. He approaches his body, dry blood near his nose and mouth, and yells out to Meruem once he realizes he's dead. He returns to the west tower and urgently informs him of Youpi's death, but Meruem just asks about Pitou's location. Pouf is still unsure, and Meruem says he can finally act now, with Pouf stressing how dangerous things are. But Meruem says he has won their game, ordering him to tell him everything as he reveals a game board he's made on the room's floor. Pouf is in disbelief and follows Meruem as he exits the tower, desperately wondering where Pitou is. Underground, Palm tells Ikalgo that everything is fine now, leaving him confused as to what she means.

Chapter 311 Deadline (, "Kigen") is the 311th chapter of the Hunter × Hunter manga, written and illustrated by Yoshihiro Togashi. Synopsis. In Area D underground, Palm tells Ikalgo that Killua believes Komugi is important to the King somehow, but that the Royal Guards possibly don't agree with one another, citing Pitou's protection of the girl and Pouf's attempt to kill her. Ikalgo is adamantly against the theory, wondering how the guards' opinions could differ, but Palm reminds him that both of them sided with humans over the Ants. She points out that they all still feel loyalty to the King, but some think they're helping him by protecting Komugi and others by killing her. Ikalgo gives in to her logic, but goes back to his question of how she knows they're safe. She mentions that they haven't been caught or killed, even though the King first used his En 20 minutes ago. If he had seen her carrying someone on her back, he would have come for her first. But Palm guesses that her hair prevented him from seeing that she was carrying Komugi. Ikalgo doesn't understand her point, but she clarifies that if they cover her with something, it means the King's En can't find her. Ikalgo panics, and wonders, if she's planning on leaving Knuckle and Meleoron, to die. Palm says she does plan to negotiate, but also wants to buy time, stressing how important it is to keep Komugi hidden. Ikalgo asks her for how long, and she says until the King is dead, shocking Ikalgo as he wonders how they can know when that will be. Palm confidently says it won't take long, saying he will be dead in only a couple of hours. The two hide Komugi in a storage crate in a large warehouse, and Palm tells Ikalgo they can now negotiate, using their leverage but not pushing the King too much. It's stated that humans are no different from the Ants, having the ability to be far worse as scenes of war, poverty, and other cruelties are shown. The divide between the rich and poor is stressed, with people protesting on the streets put in stark contrast to those lavish hosting gatherings. A Poor Man's Rose is seen exploding in the middle of a city, and it's revealed that the Rose contains poison, concentrated in the survivors' bodies, slowly decomposing them. In addition, those contaminated can infect others, creating more hosts to spread the poison further and causing a domino effect of death: a weapon devised to be the ultimate evil. As Pouf is seen flying behind Meruem, the former stops and coughs up blood in his hand, looking both shocked and terrified.

Chapter 312 Resolve (, "Kakugo") is the 312th chapter of the Hunter × Hunter manga, written and illustrated by Yoshihiro Togashi. Synopsis. Pouf remains in disbelief over the blood on his hand, and Meruem notices his hesitation, but Pouf asks him if anything is wrong, wondering if he is willing to evacuate from the palace now. Meruem thinks that Pouf will never reveal his fate, even if he's aware of it, telling Pouf that he plans to capture the remaining intruders and make sure he won't return on his promise to reveal his secret if he loses. Right as Pouf confidently agrees, Meruem once again uses his En to illuminate the entire palace, spotting a new set of footprints, Youpi's corpse, as well as a truck left behind and a door leading underground left open. A new person reacts to his En, and he immediately leaps toward them, appearing before Welfin amidst the crowd and leaving him petrified. Meruem asks him if he killed Youpi, and Welfin quickly denies it, saying the two were just talking when he started expelling blood. However, he keeps to himself that he shot him with Missile Man, but that he died before his questions could be answered and the centipedes could hatch. As he assures the King that he is looking for Youpi's killer in the crowd, Pouf spots the two and lands behind Meruem, with Welfin worried that Pouf will see through him and Pouf worried that Welfin will reveal his secret. Pouf plans to deem him a traitor and have him killed, or at least send him away, but as he goes to address Meruem, the latter already knew what he was going to say, revealing he can feel the emotions of those he's touched with his En and that Welfin is displaying incredible hostility toward him. Pouf realizes that Meruem has acquired not only Youpi's ability and wings, but Spiritual Message as well, improving them beyond what the Royal Guards were capable of. He begins to rejoice at the King's invincibility, while at the same feeling overcome with anxiety as blood begins to run down his nose, with roses depicted all over his body. Meruem questions Welfin about the anger he feels toward him, ordering him to speak the truth. But Pouf suddenly bows behind him, apologizing and revealing that Welfin is involved in his secret but unaware of it. Welfin nervously waits in confusion, and Pouf concocts a plan to entangle the facts with the truth, reminding the King of their game and that he shouldn't want to collect his reward before the match ends. Welfin remains utterly confused about what secret he knows and fears the King's unbelievable strength. He realizes how dumb he was to think he could defeat him, deluded by ideas of grandeur and blinded with a longing to avenge Gyro, even though he's probably still alive. He blames Ikalgo for making him a messenger, as thoughts continue to flood his mind about how to survive the situation. He tries to remember Pouf's secret and knows that one word could be the thing that saves his life. With a menacing glare, Meruem asks Pouf if his secret has something to do with Welfin's hostility, quickly surmising Pouf's plan to confuse him. It's stated that Meruem's use of Spiritual Message allows him to analyze Pouf even without an answer, sensing his complete devotion. However, Meruem's aura grows ominous, and no matter the truth of Pouf's answer, if it does not please him, Meruem will have to take his life. Pouf is dedicated to dying, calling himself a martyr for his devotion, and answers Meruem by saying he has no words since their match is still ongoing. Pouf's insane commitment stalls Meruem's killing intent for a moment, but he suddenly says he's hungry. Without warning, he looks back with an intense glare toward Welfin, who instantly realizes his fate.

Chapter 313 One Word (, "Hitokoto") is the 313th chapter of the Hunter × Hunter manga, written and illustrated by Yoshihiro Togashi. Synopsis. Welfin imagines his face being eaten by the King, as Shaiapouf watches on still bowing. Welfin is so full of terror and dread at dying by the King's hands, he begins to lose his fur and rapidly ages as if 100 years passed. His life begins to flash before his eyes as his human life flashes by and combines with the present. All this happens while he desperately tries to think of a single word to keep himself alive. Ikalgo's message, Pouf's secret, memories, fears, death, and survival: all enter his thoughts at once, scrambling his brain as he stands speechless in front of the King. Finally, knowing he has one second to live, he whimpers out, "Komugi...?" Pouf and the King are stunned, especially the King, whose memories of playing Gungi with her return. Pouf instantly realizes how much he cares for her, blood still dripping from his mouth and nose, and tears streaming down his face, realizing that all hope is lost. He's shocked Komugi could have such an incredible impact on the King, even after his amnesia. The King asks if this was the secret Pouf was keeping, and he says yes, and awaits punishment. The King says he knows his answer without his expressing it, since the two are of one mind now. He doesn't blame him, asking him to look for Neferpitou and to release Knuckle and Meleoron after the two are questioned. Pouf accepts his loss and tearfully nods in assent. At the same time, Meruem realizes Ikalgo and Palm must have been the ones moving Komugi underground. The King turns to Welfin, asking if his hatred toward him has to do with the octopus. All the King wants to know is if Komugi is there. He says he will gladly let Welfin go free for helping him remember Komugi. Welfin tells him they're in Bizeff's quarters. As the King walks away, Welfin screams out how Gyro is his one and only king. Meruem hopes Welfin can see Gyro one day, and that he can possibly live a human life. Pouf screams out in anguish as the King slowly walks away.

Chapter 314 Persuasion (, "Settoku") is the 314th chapter of the Hunter × Hunter manga, written and illustrated by Yoshihiro Togashi. Synopsis. Meruem stands in Bizeff's secret hangar underground, not seeing the two he's looking for, but knowing they're just trying to delay him. It's stated that his En can transform aura into innumerable photons, something he had learned from his two previous uses. The photons hang in the air as they emit aura and attach to objects around him, allowing Meruem to determine their properties, as well as the emotions of people. Meruem's analysis of the target becomes more accurate if more photons attach themselves, and his proficiency was quickly increasing. He sends out a host of photons, and by looking for someone covered with them from his first use of En, he can easily spot Palm hiding in one of the rooms. He slowly makes his way upstairs and asks for her demands as she hides in the bedroom's closet. After coming into contact with her Nen, he only feels a sense of duty and resolve, and assures her that the battle between humans and Chimera Ants is over, that their side has won. His only desire is to see Komugi, and he knows that Palm has felt his Nen as well and knows his current state. He repeats that he only desires to spend his remaining time with Komugi, and Palm anxiously reveals herself. She worries he may be toying with her, both saying aloud how he can expect her to trust him and thinking to herself that the King would never lie to a low creature like her, in disbelief that he admitted defeat and professed feelings of love. Tears streaming down her face, she continues to yell that she won't bring Komugi to him, but knows he speaks the truth. Meruem ponders how things arrived at this point and wonders what he could do with the world, even knowing he's not a god, but realizes it's only now that he can consider things so carefully. He reminds her that she knows how little time he has left, and says he wanted to ask her permission instead of looking for Komugi himself. She yells at him to torture the information out of her, simultaneously begging in her mind for him to stop. He knows that she wouldn't give in to any torturing, and describes her resolve as the most powerful and beautiful he's ever witnessed. He begins to bow before her, causing Palm to scream out with tears still flowing. She tells him that since she is part Ant, she knows how much he means to the species, but recognizes how much he loves Komugi, finally deciding to let him see her as long as she can watch the two with Wink Blue. Meruem agrees to her condition, and Palm tearfully apologizes to Killua for breaking her promise. Among the crowd of hypnotized citizens, Pouf lies dead with a trail of blood behind him, with tears and blood all around his face. Back underground, Meruem slowly opens the storage crate Komugi is sleeping in. She says Gungi moves aloud as she dreams, and Meruem gives a slight smile and chuckles, waking her up with her name and saying it's time for them to play.

Chapter 315 Home (, "Kikyō") is the 315th chapter of the Hunter × Hunter manga, written and illustrated by Yoshihiro Togashi. Synopsis. Bloster and Welfin have a final chat before they go their separate ways. Bloster has decided to stay in NGL, feeling like it's his home and unable to remember Gyro. Welfin respects his choice, and the two agree that it's probably safer than most other places, especially given how Bloster looks. Welfin asks about Shidore, and Bloster is sure she remembers her previous life, just as Welfin and Hina do, and adds that he can just tell which ones remember. He guesses that she doesn't speak much because she's most likely a small child. Hina ruins the moment by calling out to Welfin, wanting to leave in a big caravan with Bizeff driving. As Bloster says his goodbye and thinks the two won't see each other again, Welfin tells him one of Gyro's sayings: "Don't die until you're dead." With Bloster still unable to remember Gyro, the two Ants go their separate ways. Bloster then turns to Shidore and asks if she's ready to go. In the caravan, Welfin and Hina are in good spirits and ready to find Gyro. Welfin asks Bizeff if they can make it out safely, and the latter believed so, but now that he's banished, says Meteor City will be the only place they can go. Welfin tries to cheer him up, guessing that Gyro probably went the same way and hoping that he's already rebuilding to start his own country. Welfin attributes his positivity to having survived insurmountable odds twice, and proudly adds that he stopped the King, saying he fears nothing anymore. Bizeff's mood improves and he decides to enjoy life while he can, with Welfin chiming in with a variant of Gyro's aforementioned saying. Bloster and Shidore make it to the village the latter was looking for, and immediately the villagers run for cover after seeing the two Ants. Bloster convinces them they won't hurt them, and one of the villagers cautiously approaches, still wary of the two. Bloster recognizes their concern and asks them to listen to their story. In one of the village huts, a gaunt woman sits in mourning by a shrine. Shidore trembles by the doorway, cowering to the side as the woman sees her. The woman's eyes light up and she calls out, "Reina?!" Her mother races out and tearfully embraced her. Shidore begins to cry as well, wondering how she could tell it was her, and Haruna knew that she was her baby, rejoicing that she's back home. Still in tears, Shidore recounts Kurt bravely trying to protect her, and how scared she was then. Her mother reassures her that they both tried hard, and apologizes for not being able to protect her and Kurt. The other villagers happily approach and know the two must be hungry. An old woman asks Bloster to join them all for bringing Reina back, but he politely declines. He walks off in frustration, revealing that he only did this because Ikalgo spared his life. Shidore suddenly appears behind him, holding one of his claws and insisting he stay and eat with them. He begins to cry and becomes confused by the emotion. Airships from the Hunter Association begin to descend from the sky over the palace. News reports have finally come out that hundreds of thousands of people have died due to a genocidal campaign, blamed on Ming Jol-ik, whose body was found in the rubble. They speculate that he planned to use a Rose in a murder-suicide plot. The reporter also comments on Bizeff, whose whereabouts are unknown, and mentions possible sources that a military takeover was involved. With mass graves also mentioned, she ends the report by saying that further investigation into NGL and the surrounding countries is all but inevitable given the governments' lack of response. On an unknown farm, the real Ming Jol-ik sits reading a book, reciting an excerpt from a book titled, "This Creature Called Man." It's stated that he has been living a simple life for 30 years. A video from Netero is released the same day, announcing that he is resigning as the Association's Chairman and including how his successor will be chosen. However, because it was overshadowed by more eye-catching news, only a few realized that the message signified Netero's death.

Chapter 316 Real Name (, "Honmyō") is the 316th chapter of the Hunter × Hunter manga, written and illustrated by Yoshihiro Togashi. Synopsis. Morel talks to Beans on the phone informing him that Netero did his job, but they have not confirmed it yet. They are waiting for Palm's word, who is seen with Ikalgo. Beans questions the authenticity of confirming Meruem's death with just one person. Morel argues that Beans' men can write up the perfect report, and people on the field trust each other when someone says that they can handle the situation. After the phone call, Beans opens a hidden safe and retrieves a disc. He quietly thanks Netero for his service and hopes he can rest in peace. Morel then receives a phone call from Colt. He reassures Colt the politicians are treating the situation as a diplomatic issue: the Chimera Ants will be classified as a new species and there will be no problems regarding their existence. However, there is something else on Colt's mind, and Morel asks him what it is. Meleoron sits by Shoot's bed. Knov and Knuckle are waiting outside, as a senior doctor comes out from Gon's room. Knuckle approaches him and inquires about Gon's condition. The doctor replies that Gon is still in extremely critical condition, saying that he has to stay on life support and should not be moved. He is in disbelief over Gon's appearance, wondering how a 12-year-old could have transformed into that in a single day. Knov says that he will bring specialists to Gon since he is a hero and deserves it. He swears he will not let Gon die, even if it means rebuilding half the hospital. Killua is watching over Gon through a window. He reflects over what happened when they encountered Neferpitou. He understands that it was Gon's fight and how much Kite meant to him, but still he wishes that Gon would have asked for his help in fighting Pitou. He thinks about what Gon meant when he said "let's go", wondering if he meant for the sake of the mission or as friends. Then Killua says to himself that it is the same thing every time: Gon runs ahead and Killua cleans up his mess. He continues, saying that he will do it again, and will make sure that Gon makes it up to him and apologizes this time. Knov comes in and says to Killua that he will organize a medical team for Gon. He invites Killua to come with him, but Killua refuses and says that he is going to save Gon. He then says that Gon will need the doctors until he gets back, leaving Knov stunned. As Killua leaves, he takes out his phone and repeats that he will be the one to bring Gon back. Meanwhile, Colt continues his conversation with Morel and tells him about the girl he's been taking care of, and that she keeps saying her name isn't Reina. Amidst a collection of girls, as she plays with a toy sword, the little girl adamantly says that her name is Kite. Dumbfounded by the news, Morel runs through the hospital lobby, yelling out for Gon and Killua. Elsewhere, Palm slowly approaches Ikalgo and, with tears streaming down her face, tells him that it's over.

Chapter 317 Answer (, "Hentō") is the 317th chapter of the Hunter × Hunter manga, written and illustrated by Yoshihiro Togashi. Synopsis. Komugi is seen arranging Gungi pieces to prepare for her match with the King. She is so glad that they can finally play again, remarking that playing in one's dreams isn't the same as in real life. She recounts when she was kidnapped, guessing that he was the one who saved her, but the King says it was his subordinates. He remembers his Royal Guards, feeling he didn't deserve their loyalty, and Komugi says she should thank them. The King tells her he will let them know, adding that he will join them soon. Before they start their match, he recalls the time when Komugi first asked for his name, leaving him confused since he himself didn't know it at the time. But he finally reveals that his name is Meruem, at which point Komugi shows her gratefulness by bowing and calling him "Meruem-"sama."" She gives her own name, and he says he already knows it, but reflects that his former self knew nothing of what is actually important. She calls him Meruem-"sama" again, and he tells her there's no need for the honorific, insisting that she not make him repeat himself. He makes a bet with her: if he wins their match, Komugi must address him without the honorific. Komugi agrees and asks if he can wait and let her die until afterward. Meruem tells her he won't kill her now, since he is no longer the way he used to be, and playfully says she should ready herself for many losses. He asks her what she wants if she wins, and she quickly says another chance to play—an answer he knew was coming. They start to play once again, playing various moves before Meruem notices that Komugi used "Kokoriko." He sternly asks her if she's mocking him, but she quickly says no and assures him she never messes around with Gungi. He crushes a piece in front of her and changes his mind, saying she can die after she loses. He thinks he can easily counter her move, but Komugi's response leaves him impressed. She begins to explain that she came up with the move the night before, but Meruem quickly silences her so he can think. He carefully considers his next move and plays something to counter her new tactic. But as he looks over to her side, Komugi is shown sobbing, leaving Meruem confused. She asks him if she deserves to be this happy, adamant that she doesn't deserve so many wonderful things in her life since she's only good at one thing. Lowering his face, Meruem confesses to her that he's going to die soon because of poison. He states that during his last moments, he wanted to spend his remaining time playing Gungi with her. He adds that the poison is contagious, and if she stays with him for too long, she might be poisoned as well. But Komugi simply ignores this and continues playing, using another new move to counter the one that he had used to counter her own. She tells him she is beyond happy and asks him to let her accompany him in death. As he looks upon her smiling, tearful face, Meruem realizes he was meant to be here right now, that this was the moment for which he was born.

Chapter 318 Final Will (, "Yuigon") is the 318th chapter of the Hunter × Hunter manga, written and illustrated by Yoshihiro Togashi. Synopsis. Shrouded in darkness, Meruem and Komugi continue playing Gungi as the former asks her if she's still there. She assures him she is, and then declares checkmate. He asks her again, and she reassures him, telling him they need to start another game and that the loser goes first. Meruem says he was never able to beat her even once, but she consoles him by saying that they still have many matches to play. As the two keep exchanging moves, Meruem keeps ensuring Komugi is still present, eventually telling her he feels a little tired. He says he will take a short nap and asks her to keep holding his hand. She assures him that she's still there, and he tells her he will wake up shortly, asking if she will stay by his side until then. She promises the two of them will always be together, with Meruem thanking her and asking if she will utter his name for a final time. She says good night, addressing him without the honorific, as the two are finally shown together, Meruem lying down with Komugi still holding his hand and using her other arm to support his head on her lap. With blood all around them, and blood now on Komugi's face, she assures him that he won't be alone, that she will join him shortly. It's stated that 478,594 citizens died as a result of the selection. 12,905 soldiers were dead, and 46,613 people became ill after coming out of Pouf's hypnosis and then died within 24 hours. Both the Republic of East Gorteau and NGL were punished by the International Security Agency, and the two were completely broken up. The now five million refugees were accepted by the other three countries within the Mitene Union, with the stipulation that East Gorteau's resources and territory be divided equally among them. Finally, it was decided that the lands of NGL would become a nature reserve and that the Hunter Association would have control of them. The video message from Netero is shown, with him announcing his resignation as Chairman and declaring that an election will decide his successor. The only condition he gives is that all Hunters must vote, and if there isn't a 95% turnout, the results are to be ignored and a revote called. Lastly, he says the details will be handled by the Zodiacs, estimating the mission's difficulty level to be "D" and waving goodbye. Eleven individuals are then shown standing outside the Association's headquarters.

Chapter 319 Lottery (, "Chūsen") is the 319th chapter of the Hunter × Hunter manga, written and illustrated by Yoshihiro Togashi. Synopsis. It's stated that the Zodiacs are twelve top Hunters selected personally by the Chairman. They are tasked with managing the Hunter Association during emergencies and act as sparring partners for the Chairman. Each is assigned a name from the, and most legally change their names and alter their appearances out of loyalty, but exceptions exist. Eleven of the Zodiacs sit around a large table within the Association's headquarters: The last member shows up late for the meeting, Pariston (Rat and Vice Chairman of the Association), the other exception in addition to Ging. Smiling and laughing, he mentions East Gorteau as his reason for being late and sits at the head of the table. He attempts to lead the meeting, but the others quickly object. Pariston asserts that he outranks them all, but asks Botobai (the most senior member) and Cheadle (best leadership skills) if they want to lead the meeting. They both pass, and he asks the others if they oppose him being the moderator. Four members raise their hands, and so he continues to lead the meeting, first nominating himself as Chairman and saying they can just skip the election. This enrages everyone (except Ging), and Pariston brings up how much time and money the election will waste since the results are obvious. Gel says none of them would vote for him, but Pariston stresses that they are only eleven votes. Unlike Netero, he can understand and empathize with the plight of the weaker Hunters. Piyon says the weaker Hunters are like slaves to his temp agency, and that Pariston has been receiving kickbacks. Mizaistom mentions "eighteen", which signifies the number of Hunters who have gone missing in the three years since Pariston became Vice-Chairman. Before then, the annual average was 0.6 (including Ging every couple of years). Pariston replies that this pains him, but assures him that it will go down once he becomes Chairman. Ging suddenly says that he nominates himself, and will follow Netero's wishes, shocking the other members who wouldn't want to vote for him either. Pariston asks Ging about the situation with Gon, and if he would like to visit him. Ging tells him to go nonchalantly, and Pariston says he could be dead when he gets there. Ging again tells him to go, confidently saying that Gon won't die. Pariston moves back to the election, saying they should reconsider the idea of self-nomination, which angers the others since he brought it up in the first place. He says he was trying to save time and money, but if they have to follow procedures, then they should decide how to proceed. The others worry about Pariston running things, but Cheadle then suggests that they draw lots to decide the voting method, keeping in mind Netero's requirement of "everyone is a voter" and a 95% quorum. She then adds that a third party will draw a slip at random, and the others think Beans will work. Pariston agrees, saying he won't lose and that they should write their names on the slips. They summon Beans and inform him of what they're doing. He nervously looks toward Ging and then draws Ging's slip. He's amazed that these are the top Hunters and reads Ging's first rule: all Hunters are nominated and eligible to vote.

Chapter 32 And the Final Test...? (は⋯？, "Saishū Shiken wa...?") is the 32nd chapter of the Hunter × Hunter manga, written and illustrated by Yoshihiro Togashi. Synopsis. The boat off the coast of Zevil Island starts its engine, and an announcement is made that the Fourth Phase of the exam has ended, telling all examinees to make their way to the landing site. As Pokkle and Killua move about in the bushes, it's added that they will fail if they don't arrive in the next hour and that anyone who attempts to trade badges at the landing site will be immediately disqualified. Nine examinees wait near the edge of the water and spot the Hunter Association airship in the distance: Hisoka, Gon, Kurapika, Pokkle, Leorio, Gittarackur, Killua, Bodoro, and Hanzo. With the examinees now aboard the airship, Chairman Netero and several of the examiners sit together while eating and discussing the situation. Netero is impressed that six of the nine remaining examinees are rookies, and Buhara wonders if it's ever happened before. Netero confirms that it has and that it usually follows a pattern of a decade of no impressive rookies and then one year with multiple, revealing that it's happened four times since he became Chairman. Menchi wonders how old Netero is, and the small official tells her that he's been saying around 100 for the past 20 years. As Satotz asks what they will do for the final phase, Buhara wonders what could surpass the previous one and Menchi is confident that the increased difficulty could still cause trouble for the rookies.
