Netero reveals that he wants to try something new and plans to interview each of the examinees, with Menchi left confused and Beans telling her that they have to brace themselves. Kurapika finds Gon by himself as he looks out one of the airship's windows, telling him that the final phase is soon and thanking him for his help. After Gon is humble in reply, Kurapika asks him if he's okay and wonders if something happened, noting that he has seemed distracted since they met up on Zevil Island. Gon reveals that he drew Hisoka's number and that while he successfully stole his badge, someone else struck him with a blow dart and took it. He adds that Hisoka then killed that examinee and returned his badge as a favor, punching him in the face after he refused to keep it and agreeing to take it back only if Gon could punch him as well. Admitting that he felt extremely frustrated, Gon grits his teeth as tears stream down his face. With Kurapika speechless, Gon wipes away the tears and says that he didn't want to be alone after the encounter, revealing that he felt inadequate by himself and wanted support to make himself feel useful. Kurapika tells Gon that he and Leorio only made it to the final phase because of him, assuring him that he is nowhere close to inadequate. As Gon thanks Kurapika for his kind words, an announcement is made that the Chairman is conducting interviews and that all examinees should make their way to the reception room on deck two when their number is called. Hisoka's number is called first, and Netero tells him to sit across from him, with Hisoka wondering if the interview is the final test. Netero replies that he just wants to ask a few questions before it starts, first asking why he wants to become a Hunter. Hisoka replies that he is only interested in the benefits of a Hunter License, explaining that it allows a person to kill and usually avoid any consequences. Netero then asks which of the examinees interests him the most, and Hisoka answers #99, noting that while #405 also caught his attention, he would like to challenge #99 eventually. Netero reaches his final question and asks whom he would least like to fight. Hisoka's answer is #405, but he adds that he feels the same for #99, adding that it isn't the right time to fight #405 yet. He then gleefully reveals that he would like to fight Netero, who is left unfazed by the comment and ends the interview. After leaving the room, Hisoka calls Netero cunning and realizes that his own malevolence couldn't equal his indifference. Netero then interviews Pokkle, who is most interested in #404 and would prefer to avoid #44 since he wouldn't have a chance against him. Killua is most interested in Gon (#405) since they are the same age and says that #53 wouldn't be worth the time or effort. Bodoro is most interested in #44 and would prefer to avoid #405 and #99 since he doesn't fight children. Gittarackur tersely answers #99 for the former and #44 for the latter. Gon answers that #44 is the one on his mind the most and that he would hate to fight #99, #403, or #404. Hanzo is most interested in #44 since he is the most challenging and would prefer to avoid #44 since he is the most dangerous. Kurapika is most interested in #405 in a positive way and #44 in a negative way, adding that he only fights if there is a reason to do so and that someone's personality is not a factor. Leorio is most interested in #405, calling him amazing and adding that he owes him. He then reveals that those are the same reasons why he wouldn't want to fight #405. Netero uses a brush with ink to finish drawing something on a canvas, eventually summoning the examiners and the small official to show them the matchups. The five seem surprised or intrigued, and Buhara wonders if Netero is serious with his decision. Netero assures him that he is and chuckles, with the small official realizing that it's the truth. Netero then makes an announcement across the airship and thanks the examinees for their patience, telling them that they can relax until they reach the site of the final phase. He wishes them success in becoming Hunters as the airship approaches a large building.

Chapter 320 Voting (, "Tōhyō") is 320th chapter of the Hunter × Hunter manga, written and illustrated by Yoshihiro Togashi. Synopsis. The Zodiacs decided to determine the rules of the election via a lottery in which each member submitted a paper with their proposed set of rules. Ging is the lottery winner as his paper is drawn. He has a set of five rules: However, Ging immediately concedes the last rule to get the Zodiac to accept the rest of his rules (the fourth rule, in particular, had been controversial). It is then revealed through a flashback that Ging had foreseen that the election rules would be put up to a lottery and had rigged it by entrusting his paper to Beans in advance. However, he also stated that he had no desire to influence the election's outcome and was taking action purely for the thrill of the hunt. The election takes place on October 8th, on the first-floor lobby of the Hunter Association headquarters. Other voting sites are valid if at least three Zodiac members attend. Hisoka arrives to vote, but it turns out that he has an empty ballot and is only there to rate the power of various Hunters. He rates the overall strength of Kanzai as 85 points, Ginta as 90 points, Pyon as 77 points, and Illumi, disguised as Gittarackur, as 95 points out of 100. Illumi tells Hisoka about the Chimera incident, Gon's current situation, and that Killua is now planning on negotiating directly with his father. However, Illumi believes that if Killua keeps to his current course of action, both he and Gon will die. When Hisoka tells him to explain, Illumi says that he has a "younger brother" that he wishes to eliminate. It becomes apparent in later chapters that he was referring to Alluka Zoldyck; notably, although Illumi refers to Alluka as his "brother," various other characters refer to Alluka as female (see her wiki page for a more in-depth discussion of this topic). The votes are tallied; Pariston comes in first place at 37.6%, with Cheadle coming in a distant second. However, as the participation rate in the vote was only 87.7%, it must be re-held.

Chapter 321 Monster (, "Kemono") is the 321st chapter of the Hunter × Hunter manga, written and illustrated by Yoshihiro Togashi. Synopsis. As the previous two votes have failed to reach the necessary 95% participation rate, Pariston makes two propositions: first, have Beans approve each vote before submission to avoid intentionally invalid votes; second, confiscate the Hunter License from those who are absent or vote invalidly. Saiyu agrees with the first proposal, but not the second. He mentions that even without invalid votes, they needed at least a 95% turn-up. Pariston argues that a considerable number of people would want to violate the former chairman's will by not attending if their invalid votes were not counted. This angers Kanzai, but Mizaistom convinces him to stand down. Pariston asks Kanzai if he would consider no-shows or invalid voting being a betrayal to the former chairman. Kanzai states that those people simply don't want Pariston to become chairman. Pariston then offers to have someone else to do it, though most would disagree, and asks if Kanzai could even understand that. The results of the second poll are shown, where Pariston is in 1st, whereas Kanzai is in 16th. Kanzai lashes out and is stopped by his fellow Zodiacs. Mizaistom issues him a "warning". Cheadle suggests that the candidates' message should be transmitted, and notes that invalid voting and abstaining can't be called violations. Pariston agrees with the first half, but not the second, and dubs it suspicious that one of the forefronts of the former chairman's faction would say such a thing. He reminds her that the difficulty of this assignment was D, and this should be no problem with star-possessing Hunters. The other Zodiacs point out that it the end, it did not mean the absence of invalid voting were violations. Pariston clarifies that by a violation, he meant anything that might show disrespect to the former chairman. Mizaistom, fed up with the arguing, agrees to both proposals. Before it is passed, Cheadle mentions that Pariston might be thinking of having pro Hunters lose their "pro" status if their license were confiscated. Pariston immediately denies it. Mizaistom asks him if pros who lost their License can still vote. Pariston says yes since otherwise, it would be possible to manipulate the vote by taking Hunters' Licenses. Meanwhile, Cheadle thinks that they have to manipulate the voting, but in a way that doesn't cause too much harm. Cheadle wonders how Netero could have chosen a man like Pariston as his vice-chairman. A flashback reveals Netero telling Beans that he wanted the type of person he was most incompatible with by his side. However, Beans admits that even at the current moment he things Netero was wrong. At the Zoldyck estate, Zebro informs Seaquant that Killua has returned. Zebro is concerned for him due to his facial expression and asks Seaquant to tell him if any of Killua's friends appear, as he wants to ask them to help Killua. Seaquant informs Zebro that friends are actually the cause of Killua's expression and explains Gon's situation. Killua sees Silva, and demands to let him have Alluka, as he needed Alluka's power. Silva tries to dissuade him, stating that Alluka is not a person, but a creature from a dark place. However, Killua is adamant, both that Alluka is actually family, that she is the only one who can save Gon, and that he can control her. He tells Silva that it's for Gon's sake, referencing the pledge that he had made to Silva to never betray his friends, so Silva leads him to Alluka's room.

Episode 7 (1999) Trauma × Limit × Sweet Trap (トラウマ×限界×甘いワナ, "Torauma × Genkai × Amai wana") is the 7th episode of the original Hunter × Hunter anime. It first aired on November 27th, 1999. Overview. "Tonpa has placed Leorio and another examinee named Nicholas near a hallucinogenic sap. In a dream state, Leorio explains that he wants to be a Hunter for money to become a doctor who doesn't charge his patients. Meanwhile, Gon and Killua bond. At the end of the first stage, a man appears to accuse the examiner of being a fake." Synopsis. As the exam continues Gon and Kurapika find Tonpa lying on the ground. They ask what happened, and Tonpa replies that there is a trap inside the tunnel where Leorio is. But actually, Tonpa is tricking them to fall into the trap as well. Inside the tunnel, Nicholas and Leorio start to see hallucinations. Nicholas passes out for a brief moment, while Leorio follows an illusionary shadow he calls Pietro, an old friend of his who died because of illness. In the illusion, he enters a room where he sees Pietro in his deathbed. However, he could still hear Pietro's voice talking to him, asking him to cure him. Meanwhile, as Gon and Kurapika continue searching for Leorio, Kurapika gets affected by the sweet scent surrounding the tunnel, which causes the illusions. Gon then carries Kurapika on his shoulders since he was unable to move. Tonpa, on the other hand, is running to catch up with the other examinees when he sees Killua, who threatens to kill him. Killua then follows after Gon. When he arrives, Killua kicks the blonde to make him snap out of the illusion. Killua then explains that the sweet scent surrounding the tunnel is from the sap of the Illusion Tree. Meanwhile, Leorio is still stuck in an illusion. It turns out that Pietro died because there is not enough money for his operation. Leorio wants to become a Hunter so that he could pay for the expenses involved to be a doctor and then cure sick people like his friend. But Pietro discourages him and asks Leorio to just come with him. Leorio apologizes, telling Pietro that he does not want to die without trying anything. In the end, Pietro encourages him to become a fine doctor. Just then, an explosion snaps Leorio out of his hallucination for Gon, Kurapika, and Killua have destroyed the sap-covered walls. The four of them then use the same technique to catch up with the rest of the examinees. They soon reach the exit and stand before the Milsy Wetlands, also known as "Swindler's Swamp". Satotz warns them about the various creatures inhabiting it. Just then, a man appears carrying a creature in a cloth. He claims to be the real examiner, which causes confusion among the examinees.

Episode 7 (2011) Showdown × On The × Airship (ヒコウセン×ノ×ケッセン, "Hikōsen × No × Kessen") is the 7th episode of the Hunter × Hunter 2011 series. It first aired on November 13th, 2011. Overview. "During the free time in the airship bound for the third exam location, Kurapika and Leorio take a rest while Gon and Killua wander around the airship. Chairman Netero sees and challenges them to a game that involves getting a ball from him, telling them that they will automatically become Hunters if they succeed." Summary. The examinees and examiners board the airship and Chairman Netero is formally introduced to the examinees. Beans, the Chairman's secretary, announces that the airship will arrive at the site of the Third Phase the next morning at 8 AM. The applicants are thus free to dine and rest. Gon and Killua decide to explore the airship and invite Kurapika and Leorio. The two refuse, saying that they would rather rest. Kurapika ponders how many phases remain. Tonpa approaches and says that on average there are about five or six. He also warns them that the rest time might just be another test for the applicants and that they must still remain vigilant. He wants to prevent them from getting enough rest to impair their performance for the next exam. Kurapika and Leorio sit with the other applicants, and Leorio falls asleep fast. Kurapika believes that it is unlikely that any surprise will come, and chooses to rest also. Meanwhile, the examiners talk about the applicants over dinner. They agree that the batch is impressive. Menchi cites Hanzo is a dangerous applicant, Buhara mentions it was Hisoka who was on the verge of attacking someone when Menchi initially failed all applicants. Menchi corrects him, saying that Hisoka is already dangerous even before the Second Phase, and it is also the reason why she was edgy from the very beginning. Satotz comments that Hunters seek worthy rivals, but Hisoka is someone who hits the floor running when others would have slowed down already. Gon and Killua eventually settle in to talk about their families. Gon wonders about Killua's parents and their occupation, to which Killua nonchalantly replies that they are probably alive and they are assassins. Gon is surprised and asks if both of them are assassins. Killua laughs for he finds Gon's reaction amusing and he is the one who has taken Killua's answer seriously. Killua shares that he comes from a family of assassins and he's pressured to perform as the future heir of the family's business. He had to attack his mother and brother in order to leave their home and find his own future. He even says dreamily that he will capture his own family for a bounty when he becomes a Hunter. Chairman Netero sees them, and plays a trick by making them feel someone else is watching them from the other side of the corridor, and then appearing from the opposite direction. Killua knows that he is the culprit and praises his speed. The Chairman then challenges them to a game that involves getting a ball from him, telling them that they will automatically become Hunters if they succeed. Killua even uses an assassination attack, Rhythm Echo to confuse him with afterimages. Killua also hits the old man's leg, but it is he who feels the pain. Gon also tries to catch the ball, and even teams up with Killua. Meanwhile, Tonpa discovers that he is not successful in sabotaging Kurapika and Leorio, who are already asleep. Gon and Killua are not able to get the ball from the Chairman. Killua says that he is so skilled he does not need to use all his limbs. Killua is secretly pissed off and decides to quit. Gon is adamant and vows to make the old man use his right arm. Killua bids goodbye, saying that he will get some sleep when he sees Gon is determined to get the ball. Killua then bumps into two of the examinees along the corridor and they confront him for not apologizing. Killua kills them in an instant and mumbles that he might have killed the Chairman in order to get the ball had he not left sooner. Meanwhile, Gon is able to make the Chairman use his other arm, to Netero's amusement. Gon lies on the floor in exhaustion and is fast asleep within minutes.

Episode 80 (1999) Without Nen × New Year × Hunter Exam (除念×新年×ハンター試験, "Jonen × Shinnen × Hantā Shiken") is the 80th episode of the original Hunter × Hunter anime and the 2nd episode of the Greed Island final OVA series. It was released on DVD on February 18th, 2004. Overview. "Abengane seeks Biscuit and Gon's help. Killua exits the game to retake the Hunter Exam and passes. Gon continues training with Biscuit while the Bomber trio kills Nickes' Alliance." Synopsis. All of the members of Nickes' Alliance are immediately engaged after Genthru outs himself as the Bomber. Jispa tries to attack Genthru from behind, but Genthru can strike him first using his ability, Little Flower, and Jispa explodes. Genthru explains his ability, Countdown, to the group and how to deactivate it to activate his bombs, which suddenly appear on everyone in the hideout. He informs the group of where they must meet him if they wish to trade their cards for their lives, the grasslands by the Shiso Tree, and then uses his book to teleport out of the hideout. In the badlands, Gon continues to develop his Nen ability, working on Paper and hoping to be able to move on Scissors soon. Killua then shows off the amount of electricity he can generate between his two hands, promising it is even greater when he is well-rested. Gon is very impressed by Killua, but Biscuit thinks about how unfortunate Killua's upbringing must have been for him to be capable of such a thing. Biscuit allows the boys some time off since she says New Year's is soon. Gon freaks out about hearing how much time has passed since it means Killua may not meet the Hunter Exam deadline that year. Killua asks Biscuit about how he could get out of the game in time, and the three go to obtain the card Transport Ticket, which, although typically difficult to get according to Biscuit, proves easy for the boys. Before Killua leaves, Gon tells him to let the family of Kiriko near Dolle Harbor know that he is Gon's friend, as they will bring him straight to where the exam hall and Biscuit gives Killua some training instructions for the duration of his absence. Biscuit and Gon plan to return to Masadora to continue Gon's training. On the way, Biscuit gets Gon to train his Transmutation skills by having him practice quickly forming his aura into different numbers as she does during her tests. In the middle of this, Abengane teleports to them and introduces himself. Biscuit asks about the contraption on his shoulder, feigning her typical cutesy attitude while doing so, and Abengane tells them about Genthru. Although Abengane believes Genthru may be lying about parts of his deal, he believes they have no real way of fighting back against him right now. He asks Biscuit and Gon to avenge him and the rest of Nickes' Alliance, as they seem like the most reliable people he's met in the game. Abengane then left to try and spread the word about the Bomber to more people. Nickes, Puhat, Nomdieu, and Assam go to meet the Bomber trio at the Shiso Tree to exchange the cards for the alliance's lives. Abengane teleports to Bunzen and reveals that he had not told Biscuit and Gon about Genthru because they seemed reliable, but actually because they were the only other people he could reach in the game. He then lights a fire to perform an exorcism on himself using his Nen ability. The wooden doll he throws into the fire becomes a large beast who crawls towards him and sucks the bomb off of his shoulder. The beast then wraps itself around Abengane, seeming to have no intention of letting go, so Abengane puts on a large cloak and head covering to conceal himself and the beast, intending to hide for a while until he gets the chance to attack the Bomber. Gon and Biscuit plan their next moves, deciding to focus on training to prepare to fight the Bomber eventually. After completing the trade with the Bomber trio, Nickes demands that Genthru keep up his end of the bargain by removing his bombs from the alliance members. Genthru complies and gets Sub and Bara to perform a "release" with him. An explosion is heard, and Genthru sinisterly says that they have been "released", and explains that "release" was the detonation word for all the bombs. He chides the dead members of the alliance for ever trusting him, and the trio walks away. Killua goes to meet with the Kiriko Gon told him about, who sniffs him and agrees he smells like Gon. They offer to take him to the location of the Hunter Exam as he wants, and Killua regales them with the stories of his and Gon's adventures following the last Hunter Exam. In Masadora, Biscuit takes Gon to buy spell cards, believing that if the BombBomberlly did kill all the people in the alliance, there would finally be spell cards in stock at the shop. Just as she suspected, the NPC at the card shop informs them that a bunch of spell cards just became available, and they purchase sixty between the two of them. They plan to head out to train next, and Hisoka's shoes can be seen around the corner as he listens in on their conversation. Killua makes his way to the 288th Hunter Exam and notices how many more people are there than the previous year. The Examiner arrives to give instructions to the group on the first phase. He claims that because so many people came this year, they need to get the number of participants down to just three hundred. He tells them all to fight each other and that they must take down five people and collect their badges before meeting him outside. The moment the door closes behind the Examiner, everyone begins to fight. Killua quickly knocks out every other exam participant and brings all their badges to the Examiner, who is utterly shocked to see this. Netero arrives to inform Killua that he does not need to do the next phase at all, and the Examiner announces that Killua has passed the exam. Gon struggles a little bit with his training, but still manages to impress Biscuit with how fast he progresses.

Episode 80 (2011) Evil × And × Terrible (ゴクアク×ト×サイアク, "Gokuaku × To × Saiaku") is the 80th episode of the Hunter × Hunter 2011 series. It first aired on May 19th, 2013. Overview. "Gyro's past is revealed. Pokkle and his crew are attacked by Zazan's squad. Kite's crew receives a message sent by Ponzu." Summary. Gyro, in his childhood, experienced many abuses from his drunk father. Getting beaten, learning to sleep without any emotions or movement in fear of making a sound in bed that might wake his father, even learning to control his bladder at night. Even so, he still saw his father as a God from the lesson, "Don't make trouble for others" and Gyro took by that advice. No matter how cruel his father would be, he continued to idolize him for two reasons: when Gyro was five, he got a fever that almost killed him, but his father stayed all night taking care of him and his father never asked or ordered him to leave from their home. However, Gyro's feelings towards his father changed when a guy from his work revealed that the only reason his father let him stay was because he brought money and his neighbor was the one who actually took care of him when he was sick. His father did nothing. Gyro snapped after hearing the truth and attacked the guy, but was badly beaten. Bloody on the ground, his father glanced at him while walking by and never helped him. He now knew his father never cared for him and the lessons he taught were for his own benefits. He realized that the world never gave him a single thing. He stood up, grabbed a hammer and killed his father. Nine years later, Gyro founded and ruled NGL, to ruin life by distributing Drug D². In the present, Yunju's team has killed Gyro's soldiers and took over the hidden drug factory. The situation in NGL is getting worse as the Chimera Ants continue to kill humans on their own accord, while Pokkle's team watches on helplessly. After learning about soldier Ants killed by guns from Cheetu, Colt collects information from Peggy by examining the corpse. It is revealed to him that some humans possess special abilities that the Chimera Ants don't, but he believes they can easily learn what humans can. Peggy explains the human strength of learning, and knows if they find out the Queen makes them vulnerable, humans will do everything to kill her. Colt gets furious and warns Peggy that they will do everything to protect their Queen. He tells Peggy that they will protect Reina, but can't remember who that is. Meanwhile, Pokkle and his group can't send any messages to other Hunters about the situation, so they decide to leave NGL, but a group of Chimera Ants attack them. After one of his colleagues is killed, Pokkle manages to kill a Chimera Ant by using his Nen, but a spider-like Chimera Ant comes for him. Pokkle fires another arrow, but it is easily caught by his opponent who knows about Nen techniques. He attacks Pokkle, who manages to dodge, but Balda gets caught in the spider web, is pulled and instantly killed when Pike bites off his head. This angers Pokkle who attacks the Ant by punching him multiple times. When he is about to do a finishing blow, Pokkle suddenly faints from getting stung by Zazan's tail. Zazan orders Pokkle's body to the Queen, believing he has the nutrients of a thousand humans. Ponzu, who was in Pokkle's team, manages to escape and uses her bees to send a message to any nearby Hunters for help. Ponzu keeps running for her life, but is suddenly shot down by a Gun-toting Ant who shoots her multiple times and eats her body. Kite, Gon and Killua receive the message from Ponzu and Kite asks if Gon and Killua will join him even if it is dangerous. Before going any further, Kite asks Stick and Podungo to leave NGL and contact the Hunter Association about the situation in NGL. Kite, Gon, and Killua race to their destination. They arrive only to find Ponzu's blood and clothes on the ground. They discover a bullet made by NGL, but Kite and the others know that the massacre was done by the Chimera Ants. Kite fears that the Ants and NGL is the worst combination imaginable.

Episode 81 (1999) An encounter × Chrollo × The Gold Dust Girl (遭遇×クロロ×金粉少女, "Sōgū × Kuroro × Kinpun Shōjo") is the 81st episode of the original Hunter × Hunter anime and the 3rd episode of the Greed Island final OVA series. It was released on DVD on March 3rd, 2004. Overview. "Killua contacts Kurapika while Hisoka meets up with the Phantom Troupe. Biscuit brings Gon and Killua to different locations to obtain the cards they need to complete the Greed Island." Synopsis. Killua returns to Greed Island and he and Gon happily reunite. Biscuit shows him all of their newly acquired spell cards, but admits that they haven't tried using any of them aside from Blackout Curtain. Killua suggests that they start learning how to use them and pulls out Contact for them to test first. Gon activates the card, and a list of players they've previously met in-game appears in the book for them to choose from. Killua's eyes widen when he sees Chrollo's name on the list and asks Gon when he crossed paths with Chrollo in the game. Gon says he never did, and the two get confused as they had thought Chrollo was restricted by Kurapika's Nen ability. Biscuit lashes out at Gon and Killua after they continuously talk over her when she tries to ask questions, but her anger doesn't last long, and she tells them how another person's Nen can be removed from someone via Exorcism. They decide to inform Kurapika of Chrollo's supposed Exorcism, and Killua again exits the game to go tell him. At the same time, Shalnark also notices Chrollo's name on his list of players and informs the other Spiders with him. Because of the prophecy Chrollo received, Shalnark believes Chrollo came to Greed Island by accident while looking for the Exorcist he sought and was thrown out. He then asked someone else to enter Greed Island under his name to send a message to the other Troupe members. The Spiders change their current course of action and decide to look for the Exorcist Chrollo had been seeking on Greed Island. However, they get interrupted by Hisoka, who comes out of the forest during their planning. Hisoka corrects Shalnark's explanation by informing them it was actually his own idea to use Chrollo's name, but the Spiders are unimpressed. Hisoka tells them to keep in contact with him if they receive any news of the Exorcist and then leave. Killua calls Kurapika to tell him the news, but Kurapika says it's impossible for Chrollo to have already removed his Nen since Kurapika would have felt it happen. He thanks Killua for informing him nonetheless and hangs up. Melody comes to retrieve Kurapika and bring him to Light. Neon sits alone in her room, which is a complete mess, and struggles to understand why she can no longer use her Nen ability. Light's room is equally messy, and when Kurapika stands before him, he shakily asks Kurapika what he is supposed to do now. Kurapika tries to tell him he has everything under control, but Light lashes out at him in a panic. Killua meets back up with Gon and Biscuit, and Biscuit has Gon show Killua how his Nen ability has developed. Killua questions why Gon has to announce his ability before using it since it makes it easier for enemies to anticipate what he will do. However, Gon refuses to drop that part since he loves announcing his ability. However, Biscuit is less worried about it and congratulates them both for getting so far. She decides it is time for them to move on to actually working to clear the game. They travel to a giant tree where an NPC informs them of the quest to capture King White Stag Beetles that live inside the tree. He tells them to hit the circular mark on the tree as hard as possible and offers them his hammer. Gon declines, however, deciding to use his bare hands. He uses his Rock ability to strike the tree so hard that the entire area around them shakes. Tons of bugs fall from the trees around them, and they can collect three King White Stag Beetles. They move on to their next task, which involves rescuing a girl from a mansion. The guard outside the estate claims that no such girl exists, but also says only a few people may enter the mansion and that they may trigger traps if they try to sneak in to get to her room. While Gon gets confused while listening to the contradicting instructions, Killua shouts that he has already found her and brings the young girl outside with him. He receives the Gold Dust Girl card as his reward. The trio then heads to Dorias, where Biscuit says three cards are given out as prizes for an event. On their way, Gon and Killua want to stop by Antokiba to participate in the tournament. They win as a team and receive a Paladin's Necklace as their reward. Not knowing what it is for, they revisit the Antokiba Trade Shop NPC, who explains its usage, and Gon puts the necklace on around his neck. In Dorias, they win a Witch's Love Potion card, a Memory Helmet card, and a Risky Dice card. Biscuit also informs them of cards they can get from getting three 7's on the slot machines in the city, but the odds are very low, and it would likely end up costing them a lot of money. Killua rolls the Risky Dice they obtained and manages to get three 7's on the slot machine on his first try. He wins a Rainbow Diamond card. Biscuit warns him about getting bad luck when using the dice, and while Killua is trying to convince her that the bad luck the odds are really low. At that moment, an explosion occurs at the casino that injures a player. A patron had said it resulted from the player using some strange dice. Killua still wants to gamble using his Risky Dice; however, he manages to win Fledgling Gambler. When he refuses to stop gambling even after that, Biscuit knocks him out, and Gon carries him as they head to the next city.

Episode 81 (2011) The × Fight × Begins (タタカイ×ノ×カイシ, "Tatakai × No × Kaishi") is the 81st episode of the Hunter × Hunter 2011 series. It first aired on May 26th, 2013. Overview. "Gon and Killua have their first Chimera Ant fight against Rammot, who they manage to defeat, but not kill, due to Colt saving him at the last minute. Back at the nest, Rammot develops a grudge against these two and promises revenge as word spreads about humans with special abilities." Summary. As the Chimera Ants continue their ravage throughout NGL, Gon, Killua, and Kite rush to the location of the nest, hoping to reach it before the King is born. Meanwhile, the Chimera Ant Queen demands over a hundred humans per day to assure the King's growth. Even though he is initially surprised, Colt does not hesitate to comply with the Queen's orders, although he rejects Turtle's idea to immediately increase their ranks. At that moment, Zazan appears to tell everyone about the capture of a rare human. After a short bicker between Zazan and Pike and later Bihorn and Pike, the Chimera Ants continue talking about rare humans and realize that the officers can see their Nen and disable them. Gon, Killua, and Kite arrive to a village to find it abandoned. However, Gon picks up something that smells and upon reaching the location of the smell, they come across corpses of horses that were feasted on by Rammot. Suddenly, they are approached by Rammot himself while, unbeknownst to them, being watched by Colt from the forest. Rammot angrily claims the horses are for himself and charges towards the Hunters. The boys are overwhelmed by his attack, but Kite effortlessly evades it and unleashes his Nen. He backs away and tells Gon and Killua to deal with the Chimera Ant soldier on their own in order to prove that they're able to face them. Gon and Killua step forward, unleashing their Nen. While Rammot notices a sudden difference in the boys' power, Gon and Killua tell Kite not to treat them like kids and attack Rammot. Even though the Chimera Ant seems to be overpowering them at first, Killua uses his lightning skill and casts a Thunderbolt to immobilize Rammot, while Gon uses his own technique to blast the Chimera Ant away. Much to their surprise, Rammot is suddenly snatched away by Colt and the two escape as Rammot yells at the boys, wanting to eat them. Gon and Killua realize that their attacks didn't have much effect, however, Kite praises them and asks whether they want to come with him, receiving a positive answer from the boys. Meanwhile, at the nest, Rammot's anger is at its finest, wanting more than just simply killing Gon and Killua. He reveals to Colt that other squads have been killing humans and leaving their corpses there. Colt questions other Squadron Leaders about that and Hagya simply states that it's fun. However, he promises to bring the rare ones to the Queen. This turns out to be a lie as Leol states that they will find a rare one and eat it. Meanwhile, Gon and the others find more corpses that were brutalized by the Chimera Ants. They reach a drug factory overtaken by the Chimera Ants and decide to look inside.

Episode 82 (1999) Contact × Razor × A United Front (接触×レイザー×共同戦線, "Sesshōku × Reizā × Kyōdōsensen") is the 82nd episode of the original Hunter × Hunter anime and the 4th episode of the Greed Island final OVA series. It was released on DVD on March 3rd, 2004. Overview. "Gon, Killua, and Biscuit continue collecting cards. A united front rises to prevent the Bomber team from winning the game by monopolizing a card they still need." Synopsis. Genthru, Sub, and Bara force Motaricke to keep rolling the Risky Dice for them while Motaricke begs for his life. They claim that they'll let him go if he manages to secure them a Wild Luck Alexandrite using Lottery. Although Motaricke doesn't roll poorly, he only receives a Roaming Ruby card from the Lottery. Motaricke is forced to continue rolling, while Sub and Bara sadistically cheer him on. After some time of still not getting their desired card, Motaricke cowers on the ground, shaking, and Sub and Bara happily offer to roll the die themselves despite the high risk to their lives. Instead, Genthru takes the die from Motaricke and rolls it himself, saying they should all face the challenge together. Biscuit, Gon, and Killua look over their card collection, which now consists of fifty-one unique cards. Killua points out that they will soon need to start engaging with other players in order to progress, but Biscuit encourages them to finish collecting all the ones they can on their own first, and the group makes its way to the next city. Tsezguerra's team, consisting of himself, Kess, Barry, and Rodriot meet up with Genthru to make a trade. Genthru agrees to give them Night Jade in exchange for Miniature Dragon, Spirited Away Hollow, and Patch of Forest. Tsezguerra and Genthru hand off their cards to each other, but Sub and Bara emerge from hiding underground and each roll a Risky Dice before using Thief cards. The Bomber trio then teleports away to Masadora, having stolen back the card they were meant to trade, as well as taking a Witch's Rejuvenation Potion and a Levitation Stone from Tsezguerra, a Fledgling Novelist and a King White Stag Beetle from Barry, a Pre-Order Vouchers and a Hypothetical T.V. from Rodriot, and a Sacrifice Armor from Kess. Rodriot suggests they follow Genthru using Accompany, but Tsezguerra informs his team that Genthru is the Bomber and what happened to everyone originally aligned with him. While his team worries that Genthru may now have all the cards necessary to complete Greed Island, Tsezguerra checks the list of cards and sees that no player has yet to obtain Plot of Beach, and they head out to go start searching for it themselves. In Masadora, the Bomber trio looks over their collection, which now consists of ninety-two out of the hundred required cards. They plan to obtain Mad Scientist's Plastic Surgery, X-Ray Goggles, and Tree of Plenty before going to look for Plot of Beach. Gon makes a trade with another player, Michiro, for the card Favor Cushion, which causes Gon's Paladin's Necklace to activate. Killua calls out Michiro for giving them a fake card, and Michiro sheepishly gives them the real card before running away. Gon wonders if he could use his Paladin's Necklace to help the Sick Villagers they encountered long ago. Biscuit claims it won't work because the villagers aren't cards, but Killua confidently tells them they should try anyway. After returning to the village, Gon asks the villagers to trust him, and they comply since Gon had been so nice to them before. The villagers turn into cards, and Gon can use his Paladin's Necklace to dispel the curse on them, and their Sick Villagers cards turn into Healthy Villagers cards. The villagers return to their human forms and thank Gon, giving him the Wild Luck Alexandrite card as a reward. The trio leaves, and his book informs Gon that another player has used Contact on him. When they see it's a player named Kazsule, the boys have no recollection of him, and Kazsule introduces himself as the guy who stole their Sword of Truth in Antokiba. Kazsule says that he wants to meet up with the boys, now that they've amassed a lot of cards, along with some other groups he has invited, to discuss the Bomber, who is getting close to winning the game. Gon, Killua, and Biscuit attend the meeting with the other groups and Kazsule talks about potentially forming a united front against the Bomber trio to stop them from winning. He claims the only cards the Bomber doesn't currently possess are Ruler's Blessing, Plot of Beach, Tree of Plenty, and Wild Luck Alexandrite, and urges everyone to work as a team to collect at least one of the three latter cards. Asta agrees with the overall plan, but voices her disbelief that some groups there, particularly Gon's group, could help them. Gon and Killua inform them that they actually know what Genthru's abilities are and that they already possess one of the cards Genthru still needs. Amana asks about Genthru's abilities, but Killua insists that they have to prove that they'll be useful to them as well before they give up any information. Asta offers to trade a Rank A card for the information, but Killua refuses since they can easily obtain Rank A cards on their own. Killua tells them to give two rank S cards or information equal to theirs. Asta is upset at first, but begrudgingly hands over Shield of Faith and Pregnancy Stones. Gon explains Genthru's Nen abilities to the groups, and everyone else at the meeting is shocked to realize they have likely already had a bomb planted on them by Genthru since they have all been in contact with him. The groups decide to go after Plot of Beach, and Amana uses Guidepost to figure out where they can get the card. The groups immediately travel to Soufrabi. Kazsule has the groups split up to gather information, but the townspeople prove unhelpful, with some warning them not to go looking for Plot of Beach at all, since it'll cost them too many lives. Eventually, they find an NPC willing to give them info and tell them of fifteen pirates who came to the island seeking underwater treasure years ago. She says anyone who knew about Plot of Beach, including her father and brother, were killed. In private, Kazsule finds it strange that they were suddenly able to get the information they were looking for when everybody in town hardly spoke to them when they came before. Amana suspects it may have something to do with the number of players they came with this time, since they now have fifteen players altogether, which is equal to the number of pirates in the NPC's story. The groups go together to the local tavern and confront the group drinking there, led by Bopobo, asking them to leave town. Bopobo's group laughs at Kazsule, before Bopobo pours liquor in a circle around himself, lighting it on fire. He says he'll let them see his boss if they are able to remove him from the ring of fire without stepping out themselves. Zeho steps forward to challenge Bopobo and jump into the ring of fire, slamming into Bopobo, but Bopobo is easily able to pick him up and tries to crush him to death while holding him over the fire. Zeho forfeits and begs for his life, but Bopobo continues to crush him until Gon kicks Bopobo in the face, releasing Zeho from his grasp. Gon is angry with Bopobo for not letting Zeho go, but Bopobo says Gon has already lost since Gon came into the ring to strike Bopobo and then stepped back out again. Gon eagerly wants another chance to take him on, and almost gets it before Killua steps in to whisper to Gon not to. He knows Gon is probably planning to use his Nen ability, and Killua tells him to keep it a secret from people until he really needs it. Instead, Killua steps up to challenge Bopobo. Before entering the ring, Killua gets a bottle of alcohol from the bar and jumps into the ring, pouring the bottle on Bopobo's head. Killua generates electricity between his fingers and uses it to set the alcohol, and therefore Bopobo's head, on fire. Bopobo rolls out of the ring, trying to put the fire out. Bopobo becomes incredibly enraged at Killua for beating him and goes to strike Killua, but one of the other pirates enters the ring and kicks Bopobo so hard that he goes flying into a wall. The pirate chastises him for being a sore loser and then offers to take the fifteen challengers to meet his boss. He leads them to a lighthouse that acts as their fortress, where the group encounters Razor and his teammates in a training room.

Episode 82 (2011) Kite × And × Slots (カイト×ノ×スロット, "Kaito × No × Surotto") is the 82nd episode of the Hunter × Hunter 2011 series. It first aired on June 2nd, 2013. Overview. "Kite and company arrive at NGL's drug factory and run into Yunju's team, where a fight begins. Meanwhile, Rammot is introduced to Nen." Summary. After defeating Rammot, Gon, Killua, and Kite further advance into the territory of NGL and come across a cliff. When Gon speculates this to be the Chimera Ants' nest, Kite corrects him that the Ants do not make nests in holes. Kite leads the group within the cliff, to which Killua later identifies as a drug factory. He assumes that only the leaders of NGL know about its existence and that the Chimera Ants have discovered the facility and wiped out all the workers. As Gon begins to ask questions, Kite immediately hushes him, sensing the presence of few Chimera Ants. Killua asks him about En, to which Kite replies that he could stretch his En up to forty-five-meter radius. From the middle tunnel, a centaur-like Chimera Ant named Yunju arrives, accompanied by two naked men crawling on the ground. He accuses Kite and his group for trespassing his territory. One of the men, identified as Spot, begins to call out for help. Yunju punishes his "dog" and kills him. He claims that he has become bored with his dogs. Rover immediately pants and howls like a dog, but Yunju admits that begging only motivates to kill him. Gon is about to rush towards them when Kite stops him. From the other tunnels, two members from Yunju's squad appear: Mosquito and Centipede. As Yunju proceeds to kill Rover, Gon turns away. Kite admonishes him for doing so, saying that turning away could lead to another attack. Then, Yunju declares that he would make the three Hunters his new dogs. Kite gives out the order: he would take Yunju, while Gon and Killua would fight against Centipede and Mosquito. Centipede follows Gon and attacks him relentlessly with punches, which Gon effectively blocks. Gon delivers a powerful blow on his opponent's left side, but Centipede only praises the power of his punch. Realizing that Chimera Ants are tougher, Gon proceeds to use his Janken. On the other side of the field, Mosquito flies overhead, taunting her opponent. Killua goes into "assassin mode" and uses "The Snake Awakens", an assassination technique, to dismember Mosquito. Enraged, Mosquito attacks with her stinger, which Killua easily dodges, but it was her poisonous tail that has struck Killua on the back. She proudly announces that the poison in her tail is very effective. Killua falls on the ground, seemingly unconscious. As Mosquito searches for Centipede, her neck is snapped by Killua. Sensing her confusion, Killua explains that his body is immune to poisons. He kills her after Mosquito admits her weakness. In the Chimera Ants' nest, Rammot is seen crawling on the ground. He curls his fist, where aura emanates. Back in the drug factory, both Gon and Centipede hesitate to attack. Yunju mocks his soldier for hesitating. Centipede begins to devise many plans to defeat his opponent. He decides to sacrifice his eight legs, to give him a chance to poison Gon. While the other two were occupied, Yunju challenges Kite into battle. Kite inquires about the leader of NGL, but Yunju only answers that he might already be inside the Queen's belly. He rushes forward to attack, but Kite simply evades all of his attacks. Kite then summons his Nen ability, Crazy Slots, which complained about being summoned only when Kite is in danger. The slots proceed to roll and lands on number four, a rifle. As Yunju bolts toward him, Kite shoots him through the head, killing him. Finally, Centipede attacks Gon but is left dumbfounded when Gon uses his Scissors to bifurcate him. As he lies on the ground, he waits for Gon to come close enough for another attack. However, as Centipede jumps, Kite interrupts and shoots him through the head. Kite reprimands Gon that Chimera Ants could survive a day, even with a head and body only. One must crush the heads to ensure death. When Crazy Slots also gives out some advice, Gon and Killua remember when Kite first used it to shoot a Chimera Ant nest. The clown face explains that his slots go from one to nine, and each number sends different weapons. Kite dismisses his Nen ability and complains that he could not use another weapon until the one summoned by his Crazy Slots was used first. He calls the ability aggravating, leaving Gon and Killua wonder why Kite even came up with the concept in the first place. Elsewhere, Flutter announces that Yunju's squad could not be reached any longer. Hina claims that the three newcomers look "tastier" than the others. Knowing that the rare humans are still close to the drug factory, Hagya, Hina, and Flutter make their move. Kite praises both Gon and Killua's abilities. He deduces that Gon has incorporated Enhancement, Transmutation, and Emission in his Janken, whilst Killua is a Transmuter due to his lightning. When Killua admits that he easily loses power, Kite ensures that he has time to improve. He leads the group outside the drug factory, in search of the nest. Back in the Chimera Ants' nest, the pores on Rammot's body burst open, and a large amount of aura is released, which leads him to learn Nen, much to the surprise of both Colt and Peggy.

Episode 83 (1999) Meeting Again × Hisoka × Sporting Event (再会×ヒソカ×スポーツ勝負, "Saikai × Hisoka × Supōtsu Shōbu") is the 83rd episode of the original Hunter × Hunter anime and the 5th episode of the Greed Island final OVA series. It was released on DVD on March 7th, 2004. Overview. "Kazsule's Alliance loses to the pirates, and the Alliance groups part ways. Gon, Killua, Biscuit, and Goreinu organize a stronger team, which includes Hisoka and Tsezguerra." Synopsis. Bopobo tells Razor that Kazsule's Alliance has come to challenge their team to try and kick them off the island. Razor accepts and explains that each member of his team will challenge one of the opposing teams in a sport that his teammate is good at. The first team to eight wins will be victorious; no player can compete in more than one challenge. Bopobo tries to challenge Killua in sumo to get revenge on him, but Killua says he'll only accept once a team reaches seven wins. One of the pirates begins with boxing and jumps into the boxing ring. Montreux accepts the challenge and enters the ring with him. Razor tells them that they must abide by a special rule, which states that anything created by Nen can be used as a weapon. Montreux still agrees to challenge the boxer pirate, and the match begins. Montreux launches a projectile punch at the pirate boxer, surprising him, and the pirate boxer barely manages to dodge it. Montreux manages to knock the pirate boxer to the ground using a flurry of punches. Souheil and Yabibi assume that Montreux has managed to win, but Gon and Killua know better and say that the blows were equally exchanged. Montreux also falls to the floor, and Razor begins to countdown. The pirate boxer can get back up before Razor gets to ten, but Montreux stays down, and the pirates win the round. Everyone on Kazsule's Alliance outside of Gon's group is stunned by the results, and Kazsule asks Killua what happened. Killua explains that the pirate boxer could very quickly teleport his fist and land a critical uppercut on Montreux. The next pirate steps up, spinning a football on his finger. Goreinu overhears Killua speaking with Gon and Biscuit before the trio agrees on something together, and Biscuit cheerfully offers to go next. The pirate footballer explains that the two must compete to see who can juggle a football for longer, but they are allowed to attack each other with Nen while doing this, as long as they don't touch the football with their hands. Biscuit immediately drops her ball, putting on her usually cutesy façade, and loses. Gon goes next and performs very poorly in his challenge, losing as well. Killua eventually faces off against Bopobo and steps out of the ring when Bopobo charges at him, making himself lose. Bopobo calls him out for losing on purpose. Razor immediately realizes that Gon, Killua, and Biscuit are just data mining the challenges for when they return with a better group, as they believe they can't win with their current party. After being defeated, Kazsule's Alliance part ways, and only Gon, Killua, Biscuit, and Goreinu remain outside the lighthouse. Killua asks Goreinu what he'll do next, and Goreinu offers to join forces with them. The four of them go to sit at a restaurant and look over the list of players in Gon's book to find strong players. Gon says that Chrollo would be the strongest person for them to ask, but Killua points out that Kurapika was certain that Chrollo was an imposter. Gon says he still wants to meet up with this person to see why they would use Chrollo's name, but won't team up with them if they end up being someone from the Phantom Troupe. Killua dislikes Gon's idea of meeting up with this person. Still, Gon goes through with it anyway, using Accompany to transport the quartet to the location of the Chrollo imposter. The group gets teleported to Hisoka, who is bathing naked in a lake. Hisoka is impressed to see how much Gon and Killua have grown and figures they must have had a good master to teach them. He realizes the teacher must be Biscuit, who can't stop staring at Hisoka's naked body. Gon asks Hisoka why he is playing Greed Island, and Hisoka decides to lie since Gon and Killua will likely try to stop his plans if he tells them the truth. He says he's there searching for Chrollo to tell him about a potential exorcist who can restore his Nen so that Hisoka can finally fight him. He entered the game using Chrollo's name so that it might draw the attention of the Spiders, who he knew had an interest in Greed Island. Biscuit asks Hisoka to join their party of strong players in an adorable manner, and Hisoka immediately agrees, claiming he has nothing else to do. Goreinu opposes Hisoka's joining them, however, claiming that he seems too dangerous. Biscuit turns to face her group, telling them aloud that Hisoka seems friendly while she writes in the air using Nen to tell them that she believes he's lying to them. Hisoka joins their party, and the group walks off together. While Hisoka walks beside Goreinu, Killua asks how she knows Hisoka is lying, and she says it's just her intuition, but she can tell he's hiding something about Chrollo. Killua deduces that Hisoka has likely already found the Spiders and isn't currently searching for them like he said, based on the fact that Hisoka told them he had nothing better to do than join their group; he's certain that both Hisoka and the Spiders are in the game trying to find this supposed exorcist. Killua doesn't tell Gon any of this information, knowing Gon probably won't be able to keep it a secret and doesn't want to risk Hisoka leaving them while they still need strong players. Gon suggests they try and recruit Tsezguerra since they know he's strong, and Gon feels like they might be able to negotiate with him. Killua gets the idea to check Hisoka's book to see if any of the Spiders' names appear in it. At that moment, Gon runs up to Hisoka and asks to see his book to see if he has met Tsezguerra before in the game since that will make getting to him much easier. Hisoka checks his book and sees that he has met Tsezguerra before. Killua is shocked when Hisoka willingly shows the group his book and is even more shocked when Killua sees none of the Spiders' names listed in it. Killua questions if he and Biscuit were wrong about Hisoka all along. Gon hands Hisoka an Accompany card to take to Tsezguerra, and when the group's eyes are off his book, Hisoka removes the Texture Surprise he had used to conceal the Spiders' names. The group negotiates with Tsezguerra's group, and Tsezguerra likes their plan to thwart the Bomber, but points out that even with their two groups combined, they only have nine people on their team. Goreinu says they can recruit players who need help leaving the game to fill out the rest of their team, as long as their group of nine can win eight total matches against the pirates. Killua tells Tsezguerra's team to demonstrate their Ren to prove their capabilities, and Tsezguerra happily agrees, demonstrating his vertical jump that has been enhanced with Nen, which launches Tsezguerra into the air. Gon and Killua get excited upon seeing this and want to try it for themselves. When they do, they completely blow past Tsezguerra in the sky, and Tsezguerra is shocked to see how far they have improved quickly. Killua tells Tsezguerra that he has passed, and Tsezguerra asks Goreinu about what sports the pirates will challenge them to. Goreinu shows a list of the eight sports they know of for the pirate challenges, and the group decides what sports each member will do if they come up with the challenges. During their discussion, Barry tells the group that Genthru has reached ninety-seven cards.

Episode 83 (2011) Inspiration × To × Evolve (カンカ×シテ×シンカ, "Kanka × Shite × Shinka") is the 83rd episode of the Hunter × Hunter 2011 series. It first aired on June 9th, 2013. Overview. "Netero receives an order from the leaders of the world and prepares to eliminate the Ants. Colt and his fellow Ants are eager to learn more about Nen. Gon, Killua, and Kite battle a group of Ants in a one on one battle." Summary. The Hunter Association finally learn about the Chimera Ants through a source of information. Netero receives an order from the world leaders to quickly eliminate the Ants and he agrees though knows the leaders will put all the blame on the Hunter Association. Kite's team gets some information about the Chimera Ants rank, from the Queen, Royal Guards, Squadron Leaders, and Captains. When the King is born the hierarchy is shifted and the King will take the place of the Queen and find a new one. Rammot rejoices about his newfound power and Colt comes to a conclusion on how Rammot learned to use Nen: by getting hit by Gon's attack. He's sure the Ants can learn Nen now and asks Rammot to punch him. Rammot happily agrees and hits him hard. Hagya, wandering in the woods in NGL, informs his squadron to find their targets who are nearby. Kite, Gon, and Killua are suddenly surrounded by a large number of Ants. The leader of the group, Frog, immediately confronts the three and gives them three choices: 1, decide the order in which they'll fight; 2, attempt to escape; and 3, by surrendering. The three choose the first one for one on one battles and Kite says that one on one fighting is perfect and the Ants have lost their characteristics of Ants and are becoming more human. Gon fights first versus Baro, an armadillo Ant. Before the fight, Gon asks his opponent the conditions to win. Baro says the fight is to the death and Gon asks if they can fight until one of them gives up. Baro becomes impatient and attacks Gon, he evades, but Baro strikes by shifting his course and is able to hit Gon that sends him crashing into a large tree, though Gon quickly recovers. Baro explains why they're killing humans, not by eating them or feeding on them to the Queen, but because it's fun. This angers Gon, so when Baro starts to attacks, Gon releases a large amount of energy and stops Baro with his bare hands, crushing him and leading to Baro's death. Killua now is up against a huge Ant with horns named Rhino, who calls Baro trash. After analyzing Gon and Killua's abilities, Kite believes they can reach the Queen's nest before she gives birth to the King, though he feels something bad in the air. Peggy wants to do research on Nen to understand it better and learn how to be able to synchronize it with their abilities. Colt, still hurt after Rammot's hit, remembers Zazan telling them about the rare human they caught. Killua is in control in his fight, but no attacks have any effect on Rhino who is covered by hardened skin. Killua uses his electricity ability, cracking Rhino's chest and instantly kills him, using his hand. Kite is impressed by the two and wonders if he was worried about nothing. The Frog immediately volunteers to fight, Kite uses his Nen ability Crazy Slots and a scythe appears in his hand. He advises Gon and Killua at the count of 3 to jump. The place is covered with fog and the Ants become scared of Kite's aura. In a flash, Kite spins, using his scythe and kills every Ant surrounding him. As the group advances, Kite warns the two to be more cautious, that it will be worse from here and advises them to show no sympathy to their enemies. Gon replies that he will show no sympathy for the Ants who call each other trash. Kite sees Gon's point of view as dangerous for he won't know what Gon will do if he ever sees an Ant that cares for his comrades.

Episode 84 (1999) Lighthouse × 8 People × Game Master (灯台×8人×ゲームマスター, "Tōdai × Hachinin × Gēmu Masutā") is the 84th episode of the original Hunter × Hunter anime and the 6th episode of the Greed Island final OVA series. It was released on DVD on March 7th, 2004. Overview. "After the team is gathered, they easily pass the initial sports contests, but still must defeat Razor in an 8 vs 8 game of deadly Nen-charged dodgeball." Synopsis. After spending a week filling out the rest of their party and practicing, Gon's group returns to the lighthouse on Soufrabi with a full fifteen players on their team. There, they challenge Razor and the pirates once again. Barry faces off against the pirate boxer. Once the match begins, Barry immediately gets up close to the pirate boxer and starts punching. The pirate boxer is able to block the hits, but is thrown off by the close combat and Barry's speed. Barry manages to land some hits on the boxer and is able to knock him down. The boxer stays down for the count, winning Gon's team the match. The pirate footballer then challenges them to a bowling match, which Rodriot accepts. The bowling game uses human-sized pins, which Rodriot is easily able to clear, and Kess wins the basketball challenge. Razor is impressed with the new team Gon, Killua, and Biscuit have brought, and tells his teammates they can lose their matches and leave the rest to him. Bopobo, upset at this news and wanting to get his revenge on Killua, quits working for Razor on the spot and tells Killua to fight him outside. Razor tells Bopobo that this violates his contract with Razor, but Bopobo doesn't back down, and instead turns to the other pirates looking for them to join him in taking down Razor. While Bopobo is trying to convince the other pirates, Razor creates a ball of aura and throws it at Bopobo, hitting him in the head. This sends Bopobo flying across the room and kills him. The weaker members of Gon's group panic upon seeing this, and tell Goreinu they don't want to participate anymore, but Tsezguerra assures them they won't have to fight anyone on Razor's team. Killua asks who will be considered the winner of the sumo match, since Bopobo is now dead, and Razor lets Killua have the win without question or consideration. However, since Killua had yet to actually accept the sumo challenge, Killua argues that they should be able to give the win to anyone on their team. Razor allows it, and Killua assigns it to one of the weaker members. Razor is next to challenge Gon's group, and uses his ability 14 Devils to create seven Nen players to fill out his dodgeball team. Goreinu questions how an individual winner will be decided, if eight people have to play on each team, and Razor says that the winner will be awarded eight points, making the previous challenges completely meaningless. The weaker members of Gon's team immediately try to back out, not wanting to risk their lives. Gon asks if they can compete in the dodgeball match using only six players on their team, but Razor insists that they need eight. Gon gets mad, since Razor is technically fighting alone on his team. He asks Razor what Bopobo did to deserve being killed, and Razor outlines Bopobo's various heinous crimes, and Gon backs off. Tsezguerra tells Gon that Razor is a Game Master, and therefore not an NPC, with the pirates being real-life convicts sentenced to death, making Bopobo's sudden execution after breaking his contract much more reasonable. Hisoka steps forward to confirm that Greed Island is real, which is news to everyone else on the team. Razor also recognizes Gon as Ging's son when Gon mentions Ging's name. At the presence of Razor's overwhelming aura, the weaker members of Gon's team run out, leaving them with not enough members to play. Goreinu insits that he can play as three people, and uses his abilities White Goreinu and Black Goreinu to create two gorillas. With two teams of eight finally made, Razor outlines the basic rules of the challenge and the game commences. When the teams tip-off, Razor purposefully lets Killua take the ball first, which Goreinu views as an act of being overly confident and gets annoying. He harshly throws the ball into Number 4 as a response, knocking them out. Goreinu then easily takes out Number 5 in the same way. Razor, still confident even after losing two players, claims he is line to defeat the other team now. Goreinu attempts to slam the ball into Razor but Razor is easily able to catch it with just one hand. Goreinu is certain he won't be able to dodge or catch the ball, so he has White Goreinu switch places with him and take the hit instead. White Goreinu gets destroyed on impact, and Goreinu is left exhausted and put in the outfield. The ball goes back to Razor's side, where the teammates all pass the ball between their members as lightning speeds, making it incredibly difficult for the other team to tell where the ball is and who is going to try and throw to hit them. Number 4 throws the ball at Tsezguerra, striking him in the back and knocking him out. Razor asks the other pirates to treat Tsezguerra's injuries when he goes to sit out, as he claims even after protecting himself with Nen, Tsezguerra likely has broken bones, but Tsezguerra refuses their help. Gon prompts Hisoka to take the ball, so that Hisoka will be able to use his Bungee Gum to make the ball return to him after he knocks someone out. Hisoka throws the ball, and he and his team are shocked when Number 6 and Number 7 combine to become Number 13, who is easily able to catch Hisoka's throw. The ball gets handed to Razor, who is shocked to see Gon and Killua using Ken, clearly preparing to try and catch whatever throw will come their way in an attempt to get the ball back to their team. Razor remarks that Ken will probably save the two from dying to one of his throws, depending on where the ball hits them. Razor throws the ball at Gon full force, and at the last minute Gon switches to Ko and focuses all of his aura into his hands where the ball is about to hit.

Episode 84 (2011) A × Fated × Awakening (サダメ×ノ×メザメ, "Sadame × No × Mezame") is the 84th episode of the Hunter × Hunter 2011 series. It first aired on June 16th, 2013. Overview. "Gon, Killua, and Kite cause Hagya's squad to retreat back to the nest. Neferpitou awakens and turns out to be a Specialist. It manipulates Pokkle to learn about Nen. Meanwhile, Colt's own Nen power awakens." Summary. On their way to the Queen's nest, Kite senses somebody following them from the skies and quickly warns Gon and Killua. Flutter, an officer under Hagya, commands his fellow dragonfly-like Ants to distract the three while attacking them from a distance. The three start to run when the flying Ants are visible. Gon and Killua attempt to attack, but can't hit them due to the trees where the Ants are hiding. Kite realizes that the flying Ants are luring them into a trap, as Hagya and Hina lie in wait a short distance away to attack. Meanwhile, Peggy and Rammot head to the butcher's place to ask whether he has seen the rare human whom Zazan brought in; unfortunately they couldn't determine if he had been eaten by the Queen or if he was still there. Pokkle is seen alive and hiding in a pile of bones. While Peggy continues to bug the butcher, Rammot plans on mastering his new-found ability in order to become king. Suddenly, they feel a dark aura due to the awakening of one of the Queen's Royal Guards. Flutter, Hagya, and Hina witness the power of Kite making Flutter suggest to Hagya and Hina that they retreat. While Kite's team approaches, Hagya quickly understands the situation and realizes that they can't win against Kite and the boys; he realizes that no matter how powerful he is now, there are others who are much stronger. Hagya knows they have no chance of defeating Kite and the others, but have learned more about "rare humans", and one day they'll win. Kite, Gon, and Killua decide to follow them, knowing the trio of Chimera Ants, shall return back to the Queen's nest. Feeling the power of the Royal Guard member's aura, Rammot is struck with intense fear. He realizes that he is nowhere near this person's level, that his dream of becoming king is pointless, and that he should use his power to serve the real King. As they walk away, the Royal Guard senses and captures Pokkle, who was still hiding under a pile of bones. The Royal Guard learns about the human brain, and comes up with an idea to extract information on Nen from Pokkle. The Royal Guard operates on Pokkle's brain using a pair of antennae, forcing Pokkle to tell them all about Nen. Meanwhile, Colt's Nen powers are finally activated. After learning about Nen from Pokkle, the Royal Guard asks Rammot to try the Water Divination. Rammot falls under the Enhancer category, and shortly after, the Royal Guard decides to take its turn. The leaf wilts, marking it as a Specialist. Peggy is shocked by the fact that the member of the Royal Guard had Nen without first having fought a rare human. Finally, the Royal Guard reveals its name: Neferpitou.

Episode 85 (1999) Jan × Ken × Rock (ジャン×ケン×グー, "Jan × Ken × Gū") is the 85th episode of the original Hunter × Hunter anime and the 7th episode of the Greed Island final OVA series. It was released on DVD on April 28th, 2004. Overview. "Gon uses his new abilities in the dodgeball game. Killua's hands are heavily injured. Only Razor remains on his team, facing Gon, Killua, and Hisoka."

Episode 85 (2011) Light × And × Darkness (ヒカリ×ト×カゲ, "Hikari × To × Kage") is the 85th episode of the Hunter × Hunter 2011 series. It first aired on June 23rd, 2013. Overview. "As they head toward the Chimera Ants' nest, Kite, Gon, and Killua are attacked by Neferpitou as it attempts to gauge its own power. After successfully escaping with Gon thanks to Kite's sacrifice, Killua meets up with Chairman Netero along with two other pro-Hunters sent to exterminate the Chimera Ants." Summary. All the Chimera Ant Squadron Leaders and Captains have been called to assemble in the Ants' nest for an important announcement by Neferpitou. Peggy explains that those who can endure considerable pain will be rewarded with incredible power. Kite continues to use En to follow Hagya, Flutter, and Hina, who are currently heading towards the nest. Killua explains how difficult it is to maintain En for long periods of time with great range. Killua thinks Kite is probably stronger than a Nen master because of his skills and that he is the first proper "Pro Hunter" they have met, not including Bisky and Wing who were their Nen mentors and Tsezguerra who they considered being just another player in Greed Island. Gon and Killua reflect on how they always seem to meet the right people at the right time in order to help them get stronger, and how Ging deliberately sent them to Kite after they beat Greed Island. Kite tells Gon and Killua he can't train them and that if their resolve isn't strong enough, the Ants will eat them. He explains that to be a successful Hunter, you need to have a strong resolve, and understand your enemy and yourself. Kite then remembers to give Gon a Double-Star Hunter License. To Gon's surprise, it was Ging's. Ging gave his license to Kite, telling him to return it once he found him. Naturally, Kite forgot all about the license and had it this whole time, entrusting Gon to return it to his father once he finds him. Meanwhile, Rammot is punching the Squadron Leaders with Nen in order to awaken their own. Suddenly, Pitou's ears perk up as they sense something. Without hesitation, they leave Peggy in charge and disappear, saying only that they want to find out how strong they truly are. Kite quickly notices a dark aura approaching. He crouches down and tells Gon and Killua to run. Pitou's leg muscles contract, tripling in size. Without warning, they leap directly from the Ants' nest toward their current location. Gon and Killua hesitate; Kite jumps up and demands that they get away from him immediately. The next thing they see is Kite's right arm flying through the air. Gon takes one look at Kite's arm on the ground and unleashes all his Nen in a frenzy. Killua quickly knocks Gon out, knowing that if they tried to fight, they would only get in Kite's way, or worse. Kite commends Killua for his choice of judgment and tells him to run as far away as he can. He activates his Crazy Slots Nen ability, rolls a three, and readies himself for battle. Killua carries Gon through the forest, demoralized at how overconfident and much weaker than Kite they are not to be able to help. Killua crosses the NGL Border Stop and uses his phone to contact Kite's colleagues who couldn't accompany them. Monta explains that they have reinforcements and can come to meet them. The truck parks, and Killua look up to find Netero, and two other Pro Hunters emerge: Morel and Knov. After some unfriendly remarks from the Pro Hunters, Netero asks whether the enemy was strong. Still, in shock and anger, Killua replies one of them could use Nen, and that it felt worse than both Hisoka's and Illumi's. He further speculates that not even the three Pro Hunters could defeat it. After patronizing Killua some more, Morel explains that you can't judge a fight by who has the stronger Nen because you are unaware of the other's abilities. Any moment of carelessness can turn the entire battle around. He then goes on to say Killua was disqualified from being a Hunter the moment he fled from the battle. Changing topics, Netero asks whether Gon is asleep, and Killua explains how he used force to stop him. Netero says that they have sent two assassins to the nearby village. If Gon and Killua want to continue fighting and remain, Hunters, then they must first defeat the assassins. Netero makes it clear that he only requires the strong. Heading to the village center, Killua checks the notice board to find a message awaiting them, asking whether or not they will fight. Later, in the hotel room, Killua reflects on what Morel said. Soon after, Gon wakes up and thanks Killua for stopping him. Killua, convinced he let Kite die, is interrupted by Gon saying he definitely is still alive and they should hurry and go back to save him. Agreeing with him, they go back to the village center and leave a reply saying they were ready at any time. Colt tells the nest they need a freezer to store over a hundred humans. Neferpitou explains that it's to ensure their collection will not rot. They then say aloud, "Hmm... I think I am pretty strong," with Kite's severed head on their lap.

Episode 86 (1999) Unite × Impact × Bungee Gum (合体×衝撃×バンジーガム, "Gōtai × Shōgeki × Banjī Gamu") is the 86th episode of the original Hunter × Hunter anime and the 8th episode of the Greed Island final OVA series. It was released on DVD on April 28th, 2004. Overview. "Gon's team wins and they get the Plot of Beach card. The game master Razor tells Gon about Ging. Hisoka goes his own way."

Episode 86 (2011) Promise × And × Reunion (チカイ×ト×サイカイ, "Chikai × To × Saikai") is the 86th episode of the Hunter × Hunter 2011 series. It first aired on June 30th, 2013. Overview. "Gon and Killua meet Knov's student, Palm. They also reunite with Biscuit and begin training for their battle with Morel's students, Knuckle and Shoot." Summary. Gon is convinced that Kite is still alive and would never let a Chimera Ant beat him. He tells Killua they should hurry back once they are stronger in order to save Kite. As they walk around the place, Killua holds two tokens. Netero had hired two assassins and they need to take the same wooden tokens from them. They arrive at the station and an eccentric young woman approaches them. Her displeasing aura prompts Gon and Killua to take defensive stances. The woman introduces herself as Palm Siberia and invites Gon and Killua to have tea outside. She tells them she is Knov's student and Gon questions Killua who Knov is. Killua suggests that Knov is probably one of the men accompanying Netero. Palm confirms this and starts to compliment and praise him. While she rambles, Palm absentmindedly adds too much sugar in her tea. She begins talking about love and tells them that Knov doesn't know about her feelings for him. She then drinks her cup of tea which greatly disgusts Gon and Killua. Killua interrupts her babbling, wondering if she is the one they should fight. Palm apologizes and says Netero and Knov insisted she shouldn't come, but Palm wants them to acknowledge her determination. She begins talking on her own again, mentioning how Knov is such a gentle person. Killua interrupts her again and asks the condition Netero told her. The ones to defeat are Knuckle Bine and Shoot McMahon. She tightens her grip on her tea cup and releases a small amount of Hatsu, causing the tea to overflow while she calls Knuckle and Shoot "unmannerly brats." Gon wipes off the tea from the table warily and realizes that Palm is an Enhancer like him. Palm continues, saying that she can't fight Knuckle and Shoot, but Gon and Killua must. She explains Knuckle and Shoot are Morel's students and they received a condition too. Only one group will enter NGL, either the team of Knuckle and Shoot, or Gon, Killua and Palm. The deadline is one month. Elsewhere, Shoot worries about his own wooden tokens. He dissolves the token in his right palm and asks Knuckle what they should do. Knuckle is determined to find and kill them. He parades around town using a megaphone, loudly challenging the other token holders. Killua passes as Knuckle continues ranting. Killua confusingly states that even if Knuckle said a location to fight, he wouldn't go. Later, Killua tells Gon that Knuckle is only a decoy for Shoot who is expected to observe from the shadows if anyone reacts suspiciously. Moreover, Palm told them before that neither Knuckle nor Shoot knows their names. Gon asks Killua whether Knuckle is strong, and he replies Knuckle is indeed strong and he has no idea how to defeat him. He suggests that they work on their fundamentals and learn more about their opponent's abilities. Gon disagrees, saying that their goal isn't to defeat Knuckle and Shoot, but to become stronger and save Kite. In other words, they should be strong enough to defeat enemies they know nothing about. They return to their place, and upon opening the door, Gon is punched. Biscuit emerges, with Palm standing behind her. She asked Biscuit to come with her. Gon and Killua ask Palm how she knows Biscuit, and she replies she used her ability. They begin training and Biscuit punches Gon again. She tells them that Netero is famous for his nasty nature. Whenever Netero gives someone a one month task, it usually takes an entire year so defeating Knuckle and Shoot in a week is impossible. Gon insists they be quick and save Kite.
