With that squared away, Killua pays his clinic fees and leaves the underground clinic with Ikalgo by his side.

Underground Clinic Nurse The Underground Clinic Nurse is the head nurse of the Underground Clinic in the Republic of East Gorteau. Appearance. The Underground Clinic Nurse is a short, black haired, narrow eyed, and stout looking lady, dressed in standard nurse clothing with a stethoscope hung around her neck. Personality. The nurse is shown to be extremely greedy since she is willing to charge medical fees at cutthroat prices for every patient in the clinic. She is also very forceful to the point of sadism in which she refuses to let any patient leave the clinic unless they pay their ridiculously huge medical fees or else she will take their body parts as payment. Her greediness also extends to other services like phone bills since she charges Killua 10,000 per minute. Plot. Chimera Ant arc. The Underground Clinic Nurse approaches Killua and Ikalgo as soon as Killua awakens from his two day coma. She informs them that if Killua happened to die, he wouldn't need a grave as his body would have been harvested and sold. When Killua says he's ready to leave the clinic, the Nurse tells him that he can't leave unless he pays for his medical fees that added up to 1,800,000 and if he can't pay, the clinic can accept a body part instead. Killua bluffs that he left his wallet at home and asks if he can leave to go get it, but the Nurse refuses saying that he'll have to stay until he finds a way to pay for his fees. Killua, irritated by the nurse's unwillingness to cooperate with him, then asks to use the phone. The Nurse informs him it's 10,000 per minute and because Pail is the currency used at the clinic, she can exchange 500,000 for one Pail. Livid by the Nurse's greed, Killua tells the Nurse to buzz off and uses the phone to contact Gon, while the Nurse pesters him for money. Finished with his phone call, Killua gives the Nurse his account number to his bank and after it clears, she allows him to leave.

Underground Lake The Underground Lake (, "Chitei-ko") is a lake located in the Republic of East Gorteau. Overview. The lake is the place where Killua Zoldyck faced off briefly against, Ikalgo and a swarm of Chimera Ants, and finally against the Ortho Siblings. Inhabitants. The lake is underground, and trees grow underwater. Ikalgo, Remora, and the Ortho Siblings (including their squads), who all carry the genes of water animals, can be found in this lake. Plot. Chimera Ant arc. Trying to lose Flutter, Killua falls into this lake while fighting Ikalgo, who is almost eaten by his own grunts, but is saved by Killua. Later on, Remora sneaks up behind Killua and attaches a badge that activates the Ortho Siblings' ability, Dart De Darts, and engage in a battle. After Killua is severely wounded and near death, Ikalgo takes him along a path that leads to a secret hospital.

Underground Ruins Underground Ruins (地下遺跡, "Chika Iseki") are ruins located in the country of Midonite that only appears in the "" game. Overview. The Underground Ruins are ruins in Midonite that were recently discovered by the Midonite Government Environment Protection Bureau. At the entrance, tortoises and other creatures can be found. While the path leading there is typical cave infrastructure, the ruins themselves are built with cobblestone and filled with Flying Lizards. Furthermore, various marble statues of flying creatures can be found throughout. Plot. "Altar of Dragon Vein". Hoping to find a hint on proceeding onward into the Forest Ruins, Killua and Leorio head over there. As the group travels below, they soon find a flying masked marionette. It summons various skeleton monsters to fight the duo. Once it's defeated, they proceed onward. Deeper in the ruins, they find a room with a golden ring. Leorio speculates that no one has reached this room since it was there. As the group considers showing Romaria the ring, Kurapika suddenly appears. He demands that they give him the ring instead. He then resorts to force, taking the ring and handing it to Amane. It is promptly revealed that Amane is mind-controlling him with his Nen ability. Amane then realizes the two boys to be from the Hunter Association. He thanks them for doing the work for him. As Killua and Leorio pursue them, he forces Kurapika to fight them. To properly end the fight, the duo must instead attack Amane. Once defeated, Kurapika is left lying on the floor as Amane leaves with the ring. Killua and Leorio bring Kurapika to the airship for Ponzu to heal him. It is later revealed the ring before was the key to the Forest Ruins door. There are two required.

Unicorn Tribe The Unicorn Tribe (, "Ikkaku-zoku") is a tribe whose members have a single horn protruding from their forehead. Overview. Their skulls are items sought by flesh collectors such as Neon Nostrade. Plot. Yorknew City arc. Baise retrieves a Unicorn Tribesman Skull in order to qualify for the Nostrade Family bodyguard position.

Unicorn Tribesman Skull Unicorn Tribesman Skull (, "Ikkaku-zoku no Zugaikotsu") is a skull from the Unicorn Tribe. Background. It is one of the requested items for the Nostrade bodyguard applicants to obtain. Plot. Yorknew City arc. The Unicorn Tribesman Skull is retrieved and delivered by Baise, which allows her to be hired as a bodyguard.

Union Arena Union Arena (ユニオンアリーナ, "Yunion Arīna") is a trading card game launched by Bandai. Bandai has collaborated with "Hunter × Hunter", as well as many other titles. Overview. "Hunter × Hunter" was one of the earliest titles to get a Union Arena release, launching during the first wave in March 2023 along with four other titles. In the English launch, "Hunter × Hunter" will be one of the first three titles to get a release announced. The Japanese "Hunter × Hunter" Union Arena series currently has one extensive card collection containing two volumes, while the English version is set to release the first volume of the collection in October, 2024. Premium Card Set. The Union Arena Premium Card Set (ユニオンアリーナ プレミアムカードセット), part of the UA03PB series, was the first available card set for Union Arena's "Hunter × Hunter" line, available for reservation during the period of February 19th 2023 to February 28th 2023 in Japan. The set contained 4 cards in total (1 Character card and 3 Action Point cards), all of which are exclusive to the set. The cards came packaged in a folder and were originally sold for 1,000 yen. Hunting Enemies With Comrades × Courage × Wisdom. Hunting Enemies With Comrades × Courage × Wisdom (仲間× 勇気×知恵で相手を狩れ!), was released March 24th, 2023 in Japan. It included booster packs (UA03BT) (individual or box of 20), as well as a starter deck (UA03ST). The North American booster packs (UE02BT) and starter deck (UE02ST) are scheduled to be released in October 2024. The collection uses 5 rarity types for its cards: Common (C), Uncommon (U & U★), Rare (R & R★), Super Rare (SR & SR★ & SR★★ & SR★★★), and Action Point (AP). All of the ★ rarities are technically considered Parallel Rare, as they all have a Parallel foil on them. The title Hunting Enemies With Comrades × Courage × Wisdom only appears on the Union Arena official page for the collection, and does not seem to appear on any of the packaging itself. Many of the cards in the collection utilize art from the 2011 anime adaptation; however, some of the cards use art exclusive to the Union Arena collection. Booster Pack Vol. 1. The individual Japanese Booster Packs (UA03BT) contain 8 cards per pack, and can also be purchased as a Booster Box containing 20 Booster Packs (160 cards total). The North American versions (UE02BT) are planned to be released with 12 cards in each pack. In addition, the English release announced that Booster Packs have the chance to come with an autographed version of the Gon SR★★ foil card, signed by Gon's Japanese voice actor, . Starter Deck. The Japanese Starter Deck (UA03ST), designed for beginners, includes a 50-card deck, 3 Action Point cards, and a playsheet. It also contains some exclusive cards not available in the Booster Packs. The English Starter Deck (UE02ST) will contain the same number and types of items as the Japanese deck and will be released in October 2024. Booster Pack Vol. 2. The Booster Pack Vol. 2 (EX01BT) is the second release under the collection Hunting Enemies With Comrades × Courage × Wisdom. The Booster Pack was first released in Japan on October 27th, 2023. This pack does not currently have a set date for an English release. The volume as a whole contains 8 SR cards, 12 R cards, 25 U cards, 29 C cards, and 4 AP cards. Individual Booster Packs contain 8 cards in total. Like Vol. 1, some of the cards in this release contain illustrations exclusive to this pack. The pack had originally been titled UNION ARENA Extra Booster Pack HUNTER×HUNTER (UNION ARENA エクストラブースターパック HUNTER×HUNTER), before later being changed to UNION ARENA Booster Pack HUNTER×HUNTER Vol.2 (UNION ARENA ブースターパック HUNTER×HUNTER Vol.2), which is why the product number for the pack (EX01BT) and the printing on the cards contain the "EX" (for "extra"). Demo Deck. The English release of Union Arena launched an early Trial Event prior to the actual official release of any Union Arena cards in English. The event took place at Bandai Card Games Fest 23 -24 in Los Angeles, from January 27th, 2024 to January 28th, 2024. In order to participate in the event, players could choose from and receive one of three Demo Decks available (corresponding to each of the three titles releasing their Union Arena collabs first, including "Hunter × Hunter"). The Demo Decks were also given to players who participated in the Union Arena local store events in mid-March of 2024. The majority of the cards in the small "Hunter × Hunter" Demo Deck have the same card art as cards that have already been released in various Union Arena sets in the Japanese version of the game (and likely in the future English releases of the game as well). However, the Demo Deck also includes three cards with unique card art not yet present in any of the main Union Arena Japanese sets (UA03BT, UA03ST, or EX01BT). It is not yet known if these three cards will be available in future official English releases of the game. Bandai Card Games Fest 23-24 Special Set. The Hunter × Hunter Bandai Card Games Fest 23-24 Special Set (BANDAI CARD GAMES Fest 23-24スペシャルセット) first released in Japan on March 2nd, 2024 for the Bandai Card Game Fest 23-24. The set includes a rubber playmat, a set of sixty card sleeves, three Action Point cards, and a storage box. Promotional Cards. Jump Festa 2023 Promotion Pack Ver.0. The Promotion Pack Ver. 0 (プロモーションパック Ver.0) was available on December 17th, 2022 and December 18th, 2022 to those who visited the Bandai booth at Jump Festa 2023. The folder contained three Union Arena UAPR cards, one of which features Gon. The Gon card on its own has been distributed at other Union Arena events besides Jump Festa 2023. For the specific events it has been available at, see its listing in the individual promotional cards table. Action Point Vol. 1. The Action Point Card Pack Vol. 1 (アクションポイントカードパック VOL.1), part of the UAPR series, first became available April 29th, 2023. The volume contains 5 exclusive Action Point cards, one from each of the titles in the collection, with each pack containing 1 card. The titles included in the collection are "Code Geass", "Jujutsu Kaisen", "Hunter × Hunter", "THE iDOLM@STER ShinyColors ", and "Demon Slayer". The "Hunter × Hunter" AP card features Chrollo, Kurapika, Killua, Gon, and Leorio. The pack has and continues to be distributed as part of prize pools for many different Union Arena events. Action Point Vol. 3. The Action Point Card Pack Vol. 3 (アクションポイントカードパック VOL.3), part of the UAPR series, first became available August 26th, 2023. The volume contains 6 exclusive Action Point cards, one from each of the titles in the collection, with each pack containing 1 card. The "Hunter × Hunter" AP card features the Phantom Troupe. The pack has and continues to be distributed as part of prize pools for many different Union Arena events. Super Pre-Release Starter Deck & Event. The North American release is set to release an exclusive pre-launch Starter Deck (UE02ST PRE) from August 23, 2024, to September 8, 2024, titled the Super Pre-Release Starter Deck. The Pre-Release deck will contain the same number and types of items as the regular Starter Deck, however the cards from the Super Pre-Release Starter Deck will have a special gold stamp on them. The Super Pre-Release Starter Deck will launch alongside an event, called the Super Pre-Release Event. Miscellaneous Promotional Cards. Some promotional cards distributed as prizes for participating in Union Arena events do not belong to specific volumes or sets, but are single UAPR or URPR cards. The following is a list of the single UAPR and URPR cards and the events at which they were distributed: Union Arena Month - DECKS STADIUM. From March 15th, 2023 to May 25th, 2023, the Bandai Namco official card game shop "DECKS STADIUM"' held Union Arena Month. During this period, the shop was themed around the prominent Union Arena titles of the time, including "Hunter × Hunter". Union Arena Tutorial App. The Union Arena Tutorial App first launched in Japanese on October 25th, 2023, and was designed to help players learn the basics of the game. It launched with both an Android and IOS version of the app and a version that could be played on a browser. The Japanese version launched alongside an event that ran from October 25th, 2023, until November 14th, where players could play online in a campaign. A lottery prize of a set of three of the Union Arena Starter Decks, including the "Hunter × Hunter" Starter Deck (UA03ST), was available for this event. The English version of the browser app launched on December 28th, 2023, alongside the official English release of Union Arena.

United States of Saherta The United States of Saherta (, "Saheruta Gasshūkoku") is a country in the middle of the Yorbian Continent, and one of the countries of the V6. Background. It was originally part of the V5 before the Kakin Empire joined them and they became the V6. In the past, the United States of Saherta sent its special forces into an expedition to the Dark Continent. The forces went through the north of Lake Mobius and ended up in a sea of trees. After reaching 400km, they found the ruins of an ancient labyrinthine city where in grows an herb that can cure all kind of diseases. However the protector of this empty city, the botanical weapon Brion, decimated their forces, leaving only two survivors. Locations. Saherta is located on the Yorbian Continent. Notable places in this country are:

Universal Survey (G.I card) Universal Survey (なんでもアンケート) is a card found in the Greed Island game. It is one of the game's 100 designated slot cards and is required for a player to complete the game. Give this survey to somebody and they will answer all the questions truthfully. Summary. Universal Survey なんでもアンケート - This card grants the user the ability to find out what people truly think about you. Write a set of questions about yourself, and whoever you give it to, will answer all of the questions honestly. (This is reusable)

Unma Hui Guo Rou Unma Hui Guo Rou (ウンマ＝ホイコーロ, "Unma Hoikōro") is the First Queen of the Kakin Empire and first wife of Nasubi Hui Guo Rou. She gave him two sons: Benjamin and Tserriednich Hui Guo Rou. Plot. Succession Contest arc. Queen Unma is briefly mentioned as one of King Nasubi's 8 wives. After the meeting Kurapika, 8th Queen Oito, and 14th Prince Woble have a meeting with 3rd Prince Zhang Lei, Queen Unma contacts and orders Coventoba to inform Slakka to become Prince Woble's bodyguard along with Hashito and Sakata. A picture of Queen Unma is shown as being the mother to both Benjamin and Tserriednich. Unma's Royal Guards. "Active/Alive" • "Deceased" • "Former/Arrested" Abilities & Powers. As the first queen, Unma has the authority to send her own soldiers to spy on the lesser princes.

Unmanned Rock The Unmanned Rock (, "Mujinseki"—lit. "Inexhaustible Stone [or Transistor]") is a mineral ore found in the Dark Continent. Overview. It has the capacity, once submerged in water, to generate electricity. A small bead can put out about 20 megawatts of power for a day. It is found in the mountain ranges of the northeastern shore of Lake Mobius. However, this is also the territory of one of the Five Threats, Pap. In the past, the Begerossé Union attempted to retrieve the stone, but of the 1,000 people sent, only 7 survived Pap's attack and returned. Plot. Dark Continent Expedition arc. Ging Freecss narrates the five trips undertaken towards the Dark Continent, and mentions the Unmmaned Rock to three members of Beyond Netero's Expedition Team, including Curly and Mascher.

Unnamed Bunny The Unnamed Bunny is an anime-only animal in the 1999 anime adaptation. Appearance. The Zevil island bunny has two pointy large ears, a fluffy tail, red eyes, and a beige fur. Plot. Hunter Exam arc. After Gon and Hisoka's encounter during the fourth phase of the 287th Hunter Exam. The Unnamed Bunny befriended and helped Gon, who was struggling from Geretta's toxins and Hisoka's punch.

Unnamed One-eyed Monster The Unnamed One-eyed Monster is a type of Greed Island monster. Overview. It is a strange floating box-shaped creature with one eye which is able to move quite fast. Plot. Greed Island arc. Gon and Killua encounter this monster while roaming Greed Island, and can do nothing about it, as Biscuit never taught the boys how to defeat it. Card. "Unknown"

Unnamed Slime Monster The Unnamed Slime Monster is a type of Greed Island creature. Overview. It is a type of slime creature that has eyes and a mouth that stays stationary and doesn't do much, but is still hard to defeat due to its durable body. Plot. Greed Island arc. Gon and Killua encounter this monster while roaming Greed Island, but are unable to do anything, because Biscuit has yet to teach them how to defeat it. Card. "Unknown"

Unnamed Worm Monster The Unnamed Worm Monster is a type of Greed Island creature. Overview. It is a large purple worm-shaped creature with no eyes and a wide toothed mouth; it is able to run quickly in the underground tunnels also thanks to several pairs of tiny legs placed in the lower part of the body. Plot. Greed Island arc. Gon and Killua encounter this monster while roaming Greed Island, but are unable to do anything, because Biscuit has yet to teach them how to defeat it. Card. "Unknown"

Usamen Usamen (ウサメーン, "Usamēn") is a Temp Hunter and one of the Dark Continent Expedition Team members affiliated with Beyond Netero. Appearance. Usamen has a prominent underbite, irregular eyes, cleft chin, and a Japanese "sushi" chef headband. His cleft chin was replaced with a more squared jaw in later chapters. Usamen also wears a piece of fabric or apron, hanging from his hip, that features the "kanji" 鮮 (which generally means "fresh"). Plot. Dark Continent Expedition arc. Usamen debuts as one of the the ten people affiliated with Beyond Netero to join him on the adventure to the Dark Continent. When Ging talks with Pariston, Usamen quickly moves to accost him, but is effortlessly lifted by Ging and subjected to several punches. Though all of those were feints, Usamen thought he had actually been hit by those punches until he realized otherwise. Being confronted by Mascher and Marione, Ging then offers to pay double of what Beyond has offered them all in order to become the 2nd in command. Usamen accepts Ging as 2nd in command, but will refuse to follow any of his commands and refuses to accept any of his money. The Dark Continent Expedition Team has divided into 2 groups, one that will accept Ging's money and the others that won't, which Usamen was a part of. Ging, however, baffles them all with his deduction that they're all specialists in various fields with skills necessary for them to get to and survive within the Dark Continent. Later, Ging demonstrates his abilities in the game of Pip-Play. Usamen, a self-proclaimed master of Pip-Play, looked as though he was about to faint from being unable to measure up. Ging admits that the game has no practical use, but Usamen lividly states that's what makes Pip-Play so amazing. After Muherr and his men return from the Hunter Exam and try and pick a fight with Ging, Usamen surprisingly defends Ging, by trying to reason with Muherr and his men. Abilities & Powers. Usamen's specific Nen abilities are not revealed, though Ging deduces that he is a specialist in some field; his abilities, or at least one of them, must have been scouted to be able to deal with the dangers of the Dark Continent. Nen. Usamen is a self-proclaimed master in the game of Pip-Play, in which a player moves around his aura to do tricks, though that game has nothing to do with one's actual abilities, being no different than spinning a pen on one's fingers. However, he was still no match for Ging's abilities. Since creating shapes with one's aura is considered a Transmutation ability, Usamen might be skilled in this field.

Uvogin Uvogin (ウボォーギン, "Ubōgin") was member #11 of the Phantom Troupe and physically the strongest in the group. Appearance. Uvogin was the tallest and most muscular member of the Phantom Troupe. He had an unruly mane of grizzled hair, sideburns, long, thick eyebrows, and coarse hair on his shoulders, arms, and chest. He had naturally tanned skin and dressed in a wild manner, donning bearskin clothing and boots, whilst also being naturally hairy and rarely wearing a shirt. In his youth, Uvogin had an . His spider tattoo was located on his back, with the number 11 on the spider's abdomen. Personality. Uvogin was a typical Enhancer: determined, headstrong, simple, and sometimes disrespectful. He was barbaric in manner, viewing even pain as merely a nuisance. Like all members of the Phantom Troupe, Uvogin never hesitated to kill and was remorseless in doing so. He was only interested in physical training and fighting. He particularly enjoyed fights against skilled opponents, but he would typically rush into battle without a plan. However, despite often rushing into battle and fighting in a barbaric manner, he was extremely resourceful, able to defeat three skilled Nen users (Porcupine, Rabid Dog, and Leech) using only his head, after being paralyzed from the neck down. Although he prefered to fight alone, Uvogin became stronger when fighting with a partner, because he fought better when he had someone to protect. Uvogin was best friends with Nobunaga, and the two brought out the best in each other during combat. The inhabitants of Meteor City are also stated to share remarkable bonds that have been described as "thinner than water, and yet thicker than blood". This was also proven by the fact that the Phantom Troupe is a major asset in the defense of the city. Like the other members of the Troupe, Uvogin was absolutely loyal to Chrollo and the Spiders' ideals. He disliked carrying money and claimed that he had no use for it, firmly believing that one should steal whatever they desire. He would only remember people he killed if they made a lasting impression. He was also very punctual and often argued with Nobunaga and Franklin about their tardiness. Uvogin was also cold-blooded, ruthless, and not above inhumane mass murder, most notably when he brutally massacred the Kurta Clan alongside his teammates. He also enjoyed killing people who wanted revenge. The gruesome murder of their dear friend Sarasa and thirst for revenge against the perpetrators have desensitized him to such atrocities. It is worth mentioning that he is the most emotional of the Troupe members throughout the ordeal, indicating how deeply he cares for them. Background. Uvogin was among the founding members of the Troupe, all of whom originated from Meteor City, a junkyard city inhabited by outcasts who refuse to be part of society. People who live there do not exist in any official records, and the existence of the city itself is known to very few people. During his youth, about fifteen years prior to his series debut, Machi alerted Uvogin that Chrollo, Shalnark, and Franklin were digging in one of his garbage piles, and he engaged in battle with Franklin to take back a Mighty Sweepin' Power Cleaners VHS tape. Franklin tossed it to Chrollo before he could get it back. He later attended Chrollos dubbing of the power cleaners and grew a newfound respect for him and took part in later rehearsals along with Sarasa, Shelia, Feitan, Phinks, Nobunaga, and Pakunoda. One day when Sarasa was late for one of the rehearsals, he and the rest of the troupe went to look for her. Arriving at the Uga Forest only to discover she was killed and dismembered by child traffickers, much to his and the other's horror. After he and the troupe attend Sarasa's funeral, he talks to Chrollo about their plans for the future. Chrollo asks him to wait three years, during which he will be able to get the necessary funds to carry out his plan, which consists in creating a website that brings together criminals. During the conversation, they are joined by the other members of the Troupe, except for Sheila, who decides to leave the group. He and the other members choose Chrollo as the leader of the group, which will be formed in three years. As a founding member of the troupe, he took part in the massacre of the Kurta Clan. Plot. Yorknew City arc. Uvogin first appears with the rest of the Phantom Troupe during their meeting in Yorknew City on August 31st, where Chrollo announces to the group that they will steal every item from the Underground Auction. Uvogin asks if Chrollo is serious since it would cause the entire Mafia to chase after them. Chrollo then asks if he's scared, but Uvogin tells him that he's ecstatic, asking him to give the order as blood drips from his mouth. Once Chrollo gives them permission to kill anyone in their way, Uvogin lets out a loud roar as the Troupe prepares for the mission. Uvogin, Machi, Feitan, Shalnark, Nobunaga, Shizuku, and Franklin head to the auction while the rest stay behind at the hideout. The members arrive at the auction, and after Franklin, Feitan, and Shizuku kill all the guests and dispose of the evidence, they all discover that the auction items have already been taken from the vault. The members are forced to leave empty-handed, and Uvogin contacts Chrollo by phone to give him an update on the situation. As the Troupe members make their escape in a hot-air balloon, Uvogin speculates that there might be a among them, but Chrollo convinces him that there isn't and adds that the Mafia's security would have been tighter if they knew about their plan. He guesses that they only received a vague tip and that the higher-ups trusted the source enough to act on it. Uvogin then tells Chrollo about the Ten Dons and the Shadow Beasts, adding that before they killed the auctioneer, he told them that a Shadow Beast named Owl showed up and somehow left empty-handed after emptying the entire vault. Chrollo guesses that he has a Nen ability similar to Shizuku's and that the Mafia knows that Nen is involved after 500 guests suddenly vanished. Uvogin asks for permission to fight them, and Chrollo tells him to cause enough of a disturbance to draw out the Shadow Beasts. After their balloon is shot down in the Gordeau Desert and dozens of Mafia members order them to come down from the high ledge, Uvogin assures his comrades that he will take care of them, sliding down the cliffside and confronting them. A Mafia member points a gun in Uvogin's face and asks if they kidnapped the guests, which Uvogin confirms. Uvogin simply smiles when the man asks about their leader, and when he fires at point-blank range, Uvogin catches the bullet with his teeth and breaks the man's neck with a single swipe. He then begins to massacre the other Mafia members, surviving both a shot from a sniper rifle and an anti-tank missile.Kurapika and the other Nostrade bodyguards watch the carnage from afar when four Shadow Beasts arrive to deal with the Troupe. Worm, Leech, Rabid Dog, and Porcupine all confront Uvogin. Worm is the first to be incapacitated by Uvogin's Big Bang Impact. After Uvogin is distracted by Porcupine and immobilized by Rabid Dog, Leech begins to insert his leeches into the wound on Uvogin's shoulder. However, Uvogin kills him by biting off a portion of his head and then spits out a fragment of his skull like a bullet to kill Rabid Dog. With Porcupine still attached to his arm and unable to use physical attacks against him, Uvogin lets out a loud scream right toward him that results in his death. As Shalnark explains how to remove the leeches from his system, Kurapika takes advantage of Uvogin's paralysis and captures him with Chain Jail, quickly driving away from the canyon with the other bodyguards. Uvogin is taken to an undisclosed location and interrogated by Dalzollene and the other bodyguards. However, Uvogin isn't frightened by Dalzollene's threats and offers to spare their lives if they let him go. Dalzollene refuses Uvogin's offer and leaves him to die at the hands of the Mafia, but when the supposed members arrive, it's revealed that they are the Troupe members in disguise. After Phinks kills Dalzollene and Shizuku removes the neurotoxin from Uvogin's system, Uvogin vows to get revenge on the chain user. With help from Shalnark, he eventually tracks Kurapika to the hotel where Neon and the rest of her bodyguards are staying. Uvogin allows him to choose where he wants to die, and Kurapika suggests somewhere remote since he is confident that Uvogin's death will be loud. The two travel to the Gordeau Desert, and after Uvogin gets the last of the leech eggs out of his system, he asks Kurapika who he is, adding that he feels an incredible amount of determination in his Nen. Kurapika first asks him if he remembers the people he has killed, and Uvogin realizes that Kurapika is trying to avenge someone. Kurapika mentions the Kurta Clan by name and reminds him that he attacked them for their Scarlet Eyes five years earlier. Although Uvogin confirms that he was in the Troupe then, he says he doesn't remember the incident. They begin their fight, and Kurapika is seemingly able to endure all of Uvogin's attacks. Kurapika eventually captures Uvogin with Chain Jail and reveals his Emperor Time ability, questioning him about the location and abilities of the other Troupe members. Uvogin refuses to answer any of his questions and repeatedly tells Kurapika to kill him. Finally, Kurapika pierces Uvogin's chest with his Judgment Chain, setting the condition that Uvogin must answer all questions honestly and promising to allow him to live a little longer if he complies. Kurapika once again asks Uvogin for the location of the other Troupe members, but Uvogin only smiles and tells him to get lost. Kurapika's Judgment Chain then activates and crushes Uvogin's heart, killing him instantly. Uvogin is buried in an unmarked grave at the site of their battle. His death rattles the rest of the Troupe, especially Nobunaga, so much that they massacre the Mafia to avenge their fallen comrade. In Pakunoda's flashback remembering the formation of the Troupe in Meteor City, Uvogin can be seen among the founding members listening to Chrollo's speech about the importance of the Spider. Equipment. Clubs: In the past, when fighting alongside Nobunaga, Uvogin was shown wielding two large clubs made out of wood. Abilities & Powers. Due to Uvogin being born in Meteor City, his existence is not recorded in any database, which makes obtaining information on him nearly impossible. Uvogin boasted the strongest body in the Phantom Troupe and was best suited for close-range combat, including against armed crowds. In addition to his strength and aura, his unflinching spirit allowed him to utilize his aura efficiently regardless of the dire situation. Despite his penchant for fighting by himself, he was at his strongest when fighting alongside a partner, particularly against multiple enemies, as it gave him the chance to protect someone. According to Chrollo, Uvogin could overpower just about anyone but was at a disadvantage against the complex abilities used by Manipulators and Conjurers. He did not appear to rely on any kind of martial art, having resorted to simple, wide swings that made full use of his brawn and build. Uvogin could tell the time by gauging how long it had been since his last meal. Immense Strength: Uvogin was an extremely strong human being, ranking first in arm wrestling even in the Phantom Troupe, whose members are all endowed with superhuman brawn. He could destroy rocks, tear apart normal humans with a swing of his arm, and bend reinforced metal with ease. It took just one hit for him to kill an average person or weaker Nen users. He could throw rocks more than one mile, giving them the strength of sniper bullets. Moreover, he could stop a bullet fired at point-blank range with just his teeth. He could also bite through the skulls of competent Nen users, and by hitting the ground, he could raise effective smokescreens, create deep holes, or send boulders flying toward his enemy. Enhanced Speed and Reflexes: Uvogin showcased superhuman speed when confronting the Mafia members, mowing down a countless number of them in mere minutes. His reflexes were superb, as he was able to catch a bullet with just his teeth and to avoid Kurapika's Chain Jail, which could bind its target in 0.5 seconds. Advanced Agility: Uvogin was able to jump from one building to another with ease. Enhanced Durability: Even without aura, Uvogin's body was sturdier than average, which he demonstrated by surviving a beating from Kurapika while he was forced into Zetsu and the latter was using Ryu or Ko and had his physical strength enhanced by his Scarlet Eyes and Emperor Time. However, it should be noted that Kurapika did not intend to kill him immediately. Uvogin was so confident in his durability that even being likened to a tank made him feel insulted. Enhanced Stamina: Uvogin was capable of massacring dozens of Mafia members and dealing with four Shadow Beasts minutes later. Later that same night, he also fought Kurapika without his abilities seemingly being affected. Enhanced Endurance: Uvogin was very resistant to pain, as he didn't react when Kurapika punched him in the face, possibly breaking his nose. He could bear the latter torturing him without selling out his comrades or passing out. He did not even flinch when Rabid Dog ripped off two chunks of his flesh, Porcupine impaled him with his hair, or Leech inserted his leeches into the wound. Advanced Toxin Resistance: Dalzollene claimed that he had to use a triple dose of muscle relaxant gas to hold him down. However, Uvogin was fully awake and capable of speaking normally when the Phantom Troupe came to rescue him. Nonetheless, he was affected by Rabid Dog's neurotoxin and needed Shizuku to remove it from his body. He was also able to function normally despite the large amount of beer he had consumed. Amateur Strategist: Despite preferring to fight head-on, Uvogin was able to come up with crafty diversions. He was able to determine the trajectory of two sniper bullets, and his knowledge of Nen allowed him to deduce that something was off about Kurapika's abilities. Nonetheless, he was easily outsmarted by the latter. Hand-to-Hand Combatant: Uvogin held some skills in hand-to-hand combat, although he mainly relied on sheer strength to overpower and crush his opponents. His blows usually had his full weight behind them, having aimed to maximize their power even if it meant leaving an opening for his opponent. He always bested his partner Nobunaga in unarmed combat. Due to his powerful aura, it was difficult to seriously wound him, but he was eventually captured and killed by Kurapika. Master Thrower: Uvogin demonstrated a high degree of accuracy, killing two snipers atop a rocky formation in the distance by hurling stones no larger than the palm of his hand at each of them. Nen. Uvogin was an Enhancer, having used his aura to strengthen his natural abilities and talents. He used his great aptitude for Enhancement skills to increase his monstrous brawn and raise his durability to vastly superhuman levels. His aura output was enormous, as acknowledged by Kurapika. When he engulfed himself in Ken, Uvogin's body became impervious to the bluntest trauma, and even sniper bullets had no effect on him. He was highly resilient to heat and explosions as well, having even rendered an anti-tank missile ineffective. However, two members of the Shadow Beasts were able to injure him, and Kurapika could only do so after forcing him into Zetsu with Chain Jail. Later when Uvogin was using only half of his power, not even Kurapika's attacks during Emperor Time were able to injure him, despite hurting him. By merely focusing his aura into his hand and swinging it, he could break the ground in front of himself and hurl rocks at his target. Even when he expelled an object from his mouth, it acquired tremendous piercing power if powered with Shu, suggesting that he also had some proficiency in Emission. Uvogin could enhance his voice to release a shout strong enough to kill an unsuspecting person at close range. His mastery of Enhancement also granted him a powerful healing factor, which allowed the wounds caused by Rabid Dog to stop bleeding in minutes, possibly seconds. He could also use Gyo, In, and Ko proficiently, the latter of which implies a working command of Ten, Ren, Gyo, Zetsu, and Hatsu.

V6 The V6 (, "Bui Shikkusu"), formerly the V5 (, "Bui Faibu"), is a group formed by the main leaders of the world. Overview. The group is composed of two female and four male leaders from different countries: United States of Saherta, Federation of Ochima, Mimbo Republic, Kukan'yu Kingdom, Begerossé Union, and Kakin Empire. Plot. Chimera Ant arc. Although they are not formally named, they use Knov and Morel Mackernasey as delegates to negotiate a diplomatic deal with Marcos offering him and his family asylum in exchange for his extensive military knowledge on the Republic of East Gorteau. Marcos agrees to these terms. In a flashback involving Netero, a member of the V5 orders the extermination of the Chimera Ants and while it's insinuated by any means necessary, they simply want them eradicated. This implies that the Hunter Association will suffer the fallout, when this is all over. However, the fallout for the Chimera Ant crisis never occurs as it's turned into a diplomatic issue by the V5. Thus the Chimera Ants are exonerated from any or all blame and they will now be classified as a new kind of Magical Beast. Dark Continent Expedition arc. Sometime after his big announcement that he's leading an expedition to the Dark Continent, Beyond Netero is informed by one of his Expedition Team members named Curly that the V5 has personally contacted their benefactor King Nasubi Hui Guo Rou of the Kakin Empire to withdraw their announcement and sign the treaty that would bind them to follow their policies. Beyond tells his subordinate to have the King reject it and inquire what the rules are exactly. Curly thoroughly elaborates the rules, however, Beyond tells him to shut up as he's annoyed by the long-winded detail, much to Curly's dismay. Beyond goes onto say that the V5 would have him wait years to put his plans into motion and add insult to injury have him be a part of a chaperoned tour, which doesn't suit him. After learning that the late Chairman Netero had left two DVDs for all of the Zodiacs to watch, the Dog Cheadle Yorkshire tells the other members that the V5 has given them an order to hunt Beyond Netero. Prerecorded footage of the late Chairman Netero's DVD reveals that for political reasons the V5 avoided approaching the Hunter Association and surreptitiously sent in their own teams and his son Beyond was in charge of expedition decision making. The video ends with the Zodiacs believing that Netero has given them an order to go to the Dark Continent and bring back "hope". The Zodiacs then discuss how to approach this situation and the Ox Mizaistom Nana questions whether they should contact the V5 about this. Furthermore, he states that the V5 can't decide on something like going to the Dark Continent for the better of the world since that's just a pretense to culminate land and resources. The meeting abruptly ends with a phone call directly from Beyond himself. They meet the wanted man at an undisclosed location, who requests the Zodiacs get in contact with the V5 and inform them they caught him, calling it a "quid pro quo". Before reporting Beyond's capture to the V5, Cheadle catechizes the incarcerated Beyond in his cell and also records it. Beyond first elaborates on the true meaning of the V5's official policy and starts with that he suggested an unlimited door policy that would clarify the choice. However, this idea would be shot down by the V5, so Beyond went behind their backs and made a deal with the Kakin Empire that could circumvent any conditions placed by the V5 to enter the Dark Continent all while making the empire a pioneering hero. This, on the other hand, would make the V5 loose face and so they made the Zodiacs hunt Beyond, and act as his chaperone in the Dark Continent. The incarcerated Beyond then challenges the new Chairman Cheadle if she and the association she represents is up to the challenge, whereas, she answers yes and has Mizaistom contact the V5. She also states that their plans have changed and that they will be going to the Dark Continent with Beyond as a top-secret mission for the V5. The International Permit Agency (IPA)'s Assistant Director Steiner leads a meeting with the V5 in regards to the Dark Continent and the expeditions made to it. Many of the facts stated are redundant and for the circuitousness of the start of the meeting, Steiner jumps to the main point: in order to peacefully quell the situation the V5 should invite the Kakin Empire into the group thereby reestablishing as the V6. This way they can unofficially support the Kakin Empire in their endeavor all while allowing Kakin to go down in history for a pioneer of the Dark Continent and, in exchange, they equally distribute its culminated resources with the other five nations. It's also noted that the Hunter Association has been commissioned to hunt Beyond Netero, and they manage to catch, convince him to agree with the terms, and will act as his chaperones in the Dark Continent. If perchance he were to escape while in their custody then they'll resolve the matter directly with the Kakin Empire and resolve it with the V6 offer. Though the V5 is initially skeptical about the Hunter Association's credibility for carrying out this mission and the fact that their budget would inflate an estimated 25 times, the matter is approved. After the meeting, Steiner talks with his superior the IPA Director about the meeting he had with the V5. While his superior praises him for a job well done, Steiner questions whether or not what he promoted and done in the meeting was right, though his superior claims there was no right or wrong in what he promoted, they played their part and the rest of the matters is in their hands. The V5 is briefly mentioned in a confrontation involving Pariston and Ging. The two argue over the fact on whether Netero would officially allow the Hunter Association to go to the Dark Continent without the consent of the V5, Ging believes he would, but Pariston disapproves of that notion. He claims that he'd risk losing the V5 as a client and refuse to accompany Beyond. Afterward with the matters settled between Pariston and Ging, Ging usurps Pariston's number two position, he holds a discussion with three of Beyond's Expedition Team members and elaborates on the V5 expeditions they did and the Five Threats they brought back. The IPA Director has Cheadle draft a contract to be signed by Beyond to fulfill one of the newly established V6's conditions to enter the Dark Continent. The incarcerated individual doesn't object with what he reads and signs it. The V6 and their expeditions are once again brought up in a Zodiacs meeting lead by Cheadle. Mizaistom informs the incarcerated Beyond about the Black Whale voyage to the Dark Continent and that the Kakin Empire has petitioned the V6 to allow him to attend the ceremony they're holding.

Vantine Vantine (ヴァンタイン, "Vantain") is the private military commander for Prince Tserriednich. Appearance. Vantine is an older man with slicked-back hair that goes past his ears. He also has a mustache and soul patch. He wears the usual black suit and tie of a bodyguard. Personality. Vantine is very formal and professional. He reports to Tserriednich often and informs him of important matters. The Prince trusts Vantine so much that he was personally sent to invite Melody to Tserriednich's quarters. Plot. Succession Contest arc. After Kurapika's emergency announcement, and Benjamin sends his private soldiers to spy on each Prince, Vantine asks Tserriednich what he would like them to do, reminding him that since he is the son of the First Queen, he is not obligated to comply. Tserriednich replies that Vantine should tell Benjamin, "You idiot," adding that he is focusing on his Nen. During Tserriednich's Nen training with Theta, Vantine is seen with at least three other bodyguards outside the room. After the gunshot and Theta faints, Vantine tells Tserriednich about missing time and that after they rushed in once they heard the sound, they saw a beautiful landscape in front of them. He adds that they were unable to move and guesses that it was due to the music broadcast. Tserriednich asks if it was supposed to be Salé-salé's rap, and Vantine confirms it, telling him that the performance was by a Hunter named Melody. Tserriednich tells him to call her over and make it sound like an invitation. Vantine worries that they might refuse if it's not a summons, but Tserriednich stresses that it's a feeler, explaining that they can make inferences based on their response. At the Justice Bureau on Tier 2, Vantine introduces himself to Melody as the private military commander for Prince Tserriednich. He uses the word "negotiations", which puts Melody on her guard. He then explains that the Prince would like to invite her to his quarters, asking if she would accept. Melody politely replies that she cannot make a decision on her own, and Vantine wonders if the reason is because she was hired to guard Prince Kacho. Melody quickly says that she cannot comment on her contract, and Vantine rephrases his question, asking if she is unwilling to perform again. Melody replies that she would be happy to play anywhere given the right circumstances, and Vantine tells her that the Prince will be pleased. Melody then tries to put emphasis on "negotiations", but Vantine is left confused, saying that they can work out the details after she is released. Melody senses confusion and doubt in his heartbeat, reaching the conclusion that the Fourth Prince isn't behind what's happening to Fugetsu.

Varvard Varvard [University] (, "Bābādo-dai") is an educational institution in which Curly, a Dark Continent Expedition Team member, is a professor. Plot. Dark Continent Expedition arc. Sequentially after Ging bests Curly in a ancient language contest on Kappe, Pekotero tells Ging that Curly is a professor at Varvard.

Vehicles There are various types of vehicles in the Hunter × Hunter world. Transportation Vehicles. Aircraft. Airships are a type of aircraft widely used for long-distance travel. They are spacious enough to include bars, lounges, and bedrooms. The first airship seen in the series is used by Chairman Netero when he visits the participants of the 287th Hunter Exam during the Second Phase. Lingon Airport near Yorknew City seems to have only airships, as does the Hunter Association. This suggests that blimps are the prevalent means of aerial transportation, whereas airplanes do not seem to exist at all. The only sighting of a helicopter is during Cheetu's confrontation with the police in the Republic of Rokario. At the World Tree, a one-person seater helicopter with a rescue basket is also used to help climbers who are in trouble. Another type of aircraft is the hot-air balloon. The Phantom Troupe uses a hot-air balloon to escape to the Gordeau Desert after raiding the Underground Auction. Milluki uses a small hot-air balloon to leave Kukuroo Mountain to go to Yorknew. Watercraft. In the preliminary phase of the 287th Hunter Exam, Gon, Kurapika, and Leorio travel to Zaban City on a ship. For the Fourth Phase, the candidates travel by boat to reach Zevil Island. The Phantom Troupe also uses a boat to reach Greed Island. Road vehicles. Cars are the most used type of transportation. Leorio drives a car to help Kurapika go after the Phantom Troupe. During their trip to Yorknew, Neon's bodyguards are shown to have several cars of their own. Aside from private cars, vehicles for hire, such as taxicabs and buses, are also popular. In the Republic of Padokea, Gon, Kurapika, and Leorio take a tour bus to reach Kukuroo Mountain. During Killua's journey to save Gon, he and his butlers are seen using a limo as a means of transportation. The police have both cars and motorcycles at their disposal. Bizeff, Hina, and Welfin are seen using an to travel to Meteor City to find Gyro. Transportation vehicles such as trucks are used in the Republic of East Gorteau to transport items to the basement of the Royal Palace. Rail vehicles. Rail vehicles are a common type of transportation. The first train seen is the one that Gon, Kurapika, and Leorio use to travel to a town near Kukuroo Mountain. In the 1999 anime adaptation, Kurapika meets Melody in a train station. The Phantom Troupe rides a train when chasing after Kurapika. Morel and his comrades take a train to arrive in the Republic of East Gorteau during their extermination mission. Only the names of a few stations are known (Castor, Lipa, and Tarsetol). Gon and Killua ride a train to meet Kurapika at the beginning of the movie. Drone. Drones are known to be used to deliver goods. In Tier 1 of the Black Whale, rich people, high-class general stores as well as stores that sell luxury goods can order goods to be delivered through large long-ranged delivery drone from any country in the Known World to the Black Whale. Military Vehicles. Armored Vehicles. An armored vehicle is a type of vehicle used in warfare. It can range from artillery tanks to armored transportation vehicles. Military Aircraft. Fighter aircraft are known to exist, although they have yet to make an appearance. Bombers are similar in appearance to heavily armed airships.

Vending Check-Up (G.I card) Vending Check-Up (コインドック) is a card found in the Greed Island game. It is one of the game's 100 designated slot cards and is required for a player to complete the game. Summary. Vending Check-Up (コインドック): This card allows the caster to scan themselves for any inconsistencies the body may be suffering from. Unfortunately, it can only give you two responses. "All Clear" and "Anomaly Detected". It costs 500 to use this device.

Vergei Vergei (ウェルゲー, "Werugē") is the Captain of Queen Sevanti's Royal Guard as well as the Captain of the Guards of Prince Marayam. Appearance. Vergei has well-groomed short, dark hair, a tall forehead and an angular face with very prominent cheekbones that give him a somewhat gaunt appearance. As a bodyguard, he wears a black suit and a tie. Personality. Kurapika described Vergei as a stubborn man who trusts no one but himself. He was irritated by Kurapika's manner of speaking due to him working for a lower-ranked queen and answered back rudely, although not in a vulgar way. He snapped at the Hunter and even pretended to trust him for a while, before revealing he believes the Hunter Association to intend to destroy Kakin from within. Vergei later seemed to have mellowed out and showed a soft and more trusting side after being captivated by Biscuit. Plot. Succession Contest arc. At the request of Queen Sevanti, Vergei along with the other Hunters and servants are ordered to protect their client's younger brother, Prince Marayam. Vergei asks the Queen whether she is certain they don't need to escort Prince Momoze to which she replies that protecting Marayam is more important. When Queen Oito's Little Eye infiltrates into Prince Marayam's room through the air ducts, Vergei is seen overseeing Queen Sevanti and Prince Marayam. Rather than Vergei, Queen Sevanti decides to send Barrigen to attend Kurapika's two-week teaching of Nen, which pleases Barrigen. That night, Vergei contacts Kurapika in order to have him investigate the identity of Momoze's murderer, offering to assign the Hunter who worked for her to Woble in return. Kurapika attempts to convince Vergei the room he is in has been isolated due to a Nen ability, but the bodyguard ignores him and requests that he investigate about the identity of Momoze's killer. When Kurapika reveals he already knows who the culprit is, Vergei initially pretends to be accommodating, accepting to open the door to a Hunter Association member in exchange for the information, but then asserts that he is not convinced by the rumors spreading about Nen, which seems too convenient for the Hunters. Still hoping to form an alliance, Kurapika tells him that the killer was Tuffdy and how he carried out the murder. Vergei states that Kurapika's explanation has only strengthened his belief that the Hunter Association intends to weaken Kakin from the inside and hangs up. The next morning, Vergei announces to Biscuit and Hanzo that there is no longer a need to send Belerainte for Kurapika's Nen lessons, as he finds it a risk after Barrigen died under strange circumstances. Instead, Biscuit proposes to teach everyone Nen through her own way, though Vergei keeps insisting that Nen is only a magic trick. Biscuit reverts back to her real form, which shocks Vergei; not because of Biscuit's manly form, but because of her beauty. He admires Biscuit's muscles while she explains that she can enhance everyone's physical capabilities within a month. When she asks whom to teach, Vergei enthusiastically volunteers. He also agrees to resend Belerainte over to 1014, though he staunchly denies that it has something to do with Nen. At the entrance doors, Vergei and the other bodyguards watch Belerainte leave the room. They confirm that they can see Belerainte outside the room, though the former could not see anyone from the inside. And when he tries to return inside, his body parts disappear. Biscuit concludes that this is the work of Prince Marayam's Guardian Spirit Beast. After seeing this, Vergei insists that everyone should start learning Nen. On Sunday, he lets some of Marayam's servants attend the performance as scheduled, even though they will be unable to return to the room. He explains to a Hunter that, unlike the royal family, a servant backing out would arouse suspicion and might result in Queen Sevanti and Prince Marayam being forced to leave the room for questioning. He states that he wishes the prince would be able to stay in the room until they reach their destination. Biscuit agrees with him but convinces him to also send the Hunters in the teleported room to the empty one. Vergei asks her what she will do, to which she replies that she will stay in the teleported room because they need a woman around. Her words leave Vergei even more infatuated.Hunter × Hunter - Volume 37, Chapter 383</ref>

Vic Vic (ビク, "Biku") was an underling of the Cha-R Family working under Tsudonke. Appearance. Vic had a large nose and distinctive eyebrows. With a receding hairline, his hair came to a noticeable point. Personality. Little was known about Vic's personality, but he was quick to show initiative, planning to answer the door to the Cha-R's office when he heard someone knocking on it. Plot. Succession Contest arc. In the Cha-R's office on Tier 5, Ken'i introduces Nobunaga, Phinks, and Feitan to Tsudonke and three of his underlings, including Vic. He explains that the three of them will be in the rotation from now on, asking the Cha-R members to teach them the ropes. Later, Nobunaga and Phinks are seen sitting across from each other while Feitan reads a magazine in a nearby bunk bed. As a Cha-R member watches surveillance footage, Nobunaga suggests getting Franklin and splitting into teams of two to search outside in shifts. Phinks guesses that he would turn them down since he hates cramped places, but Nobunaga replies that he will team up with Franklin while the two of them stay there. Feitan says that even though the enemy will be reluctant to attack the three of them together, they shouldn't lose their patience. In the front room, several Cha-R members hear a knock on the door and wonder if the search team is back, but the member watching the surveillance footage tells Vic not to open it as he quickly asks the Troupe members to come to look at the monitors. An arm is seen coming through an opening as the person knocks on the door. Phinks notes that he's toying with them when he could have taken them by surprise. The member points to another monitor and sees that the search team is returning. However, when they open the door to the front room, they find no one there, with Phinks guessing that they must have been taken. Nobunaga notes that it doesn't matter how many grunts are around if they can't use Nen. The member nervously wonders where his comrades are, but Nobunaga quickly orders him to stay in the other room and bolt the door, telling him to look for the search team on the monitors and let them know if anything happens. When Tsudonke and three other underlings return to the office, he asks where the underlings are. Nobunaga reveals that they were all killed by the hitman who killed the guards in the warehouse, showing his decapitated and bisected corpse.

Vice Vice (バイス, "Baisu") is a player of the Greed Island game. Appearance. Vice has fair curly hair. He wears a jacket, pants, and shoes. Plot. Greed Island arc. After Gon and Killua obtain their first specified slot card "Sword of Truth" in the city of Antokiba, Vice appears with some other experienced players such as Asta and Kazsule with the intention of stealing it. Later, he is shown to be still alive in the game as there is a bright dot next to his name in Gon's contact list. Abilities & Powers. Nen. Due to being able to access Greed Island, Vice is capable of utilizing Nen.

Vict Vict (ビクト, "Bikuto") is a high-ranking soldier in the Royal Army of the Kakin Empire, and one of the personal soldiers of Prince Benjamin. He was among Prince Momoze's bodyguards under direct orders from Prince Benjamin, until her death. He has since been released from captivity and has been reassigned to Prince Halkenburg. Appearance. Vict has thick eyebrows, a thick mustache, and extra-long sideburns, nearly forming a muttonchops-style mustache. He wears the standard Kakin military attire of a zipper jacket, pants, and dark combat boots. He wears an earpiece in his left ear. Background. As one of the First Prince's soldiers, Vict graduated from Kakin's Royal Military Academy and became a part of his army. Plot. Succession Contest arc. Vict, among the other thirteen soldiers working under Prince Benjamin, is present during Balsamilco's explanation before the journey's start. Later, Prince Benjamin orders his private soldiers, to both act as bodyguards and spies to all the other princes, and to report any information regarding the Princes' Guardian Spirit Beasts and the Hunters' abilities. As Prince Momoze rests in her bedroom, Vict, Nipaper, Bladge, and Laroc stand guard outside her room, while Tuffdy patiently waits to assassinate the Prince. After Prince Momoze's murder, Vict, along with the other bodyguards are taken into custody by the Kakin Army to be interrogated about the murder. Vict is subsequently freed and eventually assigned to Room 1009. He uses his Nen ability to attack Prince Halkenburg, to no effect. He manages to warn Benjamin about the latter's bow before being defeated. When Steiner along with his associate Peuckert and the Kakin Justice Bureau arrives at Prince Halkenburg's room, Vict is nowhere to be found. Abilities & Powers. Vict has received military training. Nen. Vict is a Nen user skilled enough to have developed a Nen ability. However his superior Balsamilco believes him to be less knowledgeable than Hunters in that regard.

Village of the Bandits from the Mountains The Village of the Bandits from the Mountains is a place in Greed Island where the sick bandits reside. Overview. The village is the home for the Sick Villagers and the location where to acquire the "Wild Luck Alexandrite" card. Plot. Greed Island arc. Gon and Killua are confronted by the Sick Villagers who beseech them for their help. The two with Biscuit Krueger learn that the villagers suffer from an unknown illness and a child in their village has it the worst. So the two donate their Jenny and most of their worn clothes to the villagers in hopes to get an item or information, however, they receive nothing in return. After winning the Paladin's Necklace from Antokiba's monthly tournament Gon and the group return to the village and due to the villagers trusting them to allow Gon to use his newly acquired Paladin's Necklace to dispel the curse laid upon them. With the villagers in a healthy state, they reward Gon the "Wild Luck Alexandrite" card.

Vincent Vincent (ビンセント, "Binsento") was a high-ranking soldier in the Royal Army of the Kakin Empire, and one of the personal soldiers of Prince Benjamin. He briefly acted as Prince Woble's bodyguard under direct orders from Prince Benjamin. Appearance. Vincent sported a shaven head and wore the standard Kakin military attire of zipper jacket, pants, and dark combat boots. He wore an earpiece in his left ear. Personality. Vincent presented himself as poised and liked to say "yessir" at the end of nearly all of his sentences. He has sociopathic tendencies, as he shows no remorse after killing one of Queen Oito's attendants in an alleged self-defense. Immediately after Vincent commits suicide by poisoning himself, Balsamilco praises him for his courageous action to die so he could avoid confessing his crime of attempting to assassinate Prince Woble. Background. As one of the First Prince's soldiers, Vincent graduated from Kakin's Royal Military Academy and became a part of his army. Plot. Succession Contest arc. Right before the Black Whale sets off, Vincent and the other thirteen soldiers working under Prince Benjamin listen to Balsamilco's explanation on what to do and how to proceed on the ship. Later, Benjamin orders his fourteen soldiers to not only act as bodyguards, but also spy on the other Princes; he wants them to report back any information on the Princes' Guardian Spirit Beasts and the Hunters' abilities. In case they come under attack or suspect any animosity coming from anyone, they have the right to defend themselves and have full permission to kill their opponent. Later, Vincent visits Prince Woble's quarters, and upon entering the room, he kills Sandra, claiming she tried to attack him with a knife and had a small vial of poison on her person. In his defense, Vincent claims he was merely exercising his right to defend himself. Kurapika tries to retaliate against the solider though he resists after hearing Vincent would use his right to defend himself. Denying his accusation of being the greatest danger to Woble's safety, Vincent asks the two other bodyguards for "cooperation", by which he means murdering the queen, prince, and remaining maid. Immediately, Kurapika stabs Oito with one of his chains, baffling the soldier and leaving him perplexed about whether Kurapika has gone turncoat by accepting his request. Though with an open opportunity, Bill charges at Vincent, who shoots his gun in self-defense; however, Bill is impervious to the bullets thanks to his aura. Left with no other options, Vincent prepares to activate his Nen ability. However, his aura is drained by Kurapika's chain. Unable to retaliate, the two Hunters restrain Vincent to the floor. Vincent claims his innocence, but Oito promises that she'll testify against him. Kurapika also assures Oito that he'll use his ability to force a confession when he's on the stand. At a dead-end, Vincent uses a suicide pill hidden in one of his molars. Thanks to his earpiece, which was later found and destroyed when Kurapika and Bill move Vincent's corpse, Balsamilco, and Benjamin become aware of most of what transpired and make conjectures about what occurred and Kurapika's abilities. Balsamilco also compliments the late Vincent for taking his own life, claiming he had balls of steel and was prepared to die at any minute. With Vincent out of the picture, it was decided that Babimyna would replace Vincent as bodyguard for Prince Woble. After receiving calls from three different Princes (including Benjamin), Kurapika realizes that the First Prince knows Vincent is dead because of them, worrying that they could be in a state of war already. Later, Shimano explains that negotiations have broken down over Vincent's death and that Benjamin's camp is only interested in letting their enemies choose how they die. After Musse's death, Benjamin inherits his ability and mentions Vincent's name as well, asking that they live on through him. It's then explained that Benjamin's ability, Benjamin Baton, allows him to inherit the ability of Nen users who swore loyalty to him when they die. Equipment. Knife: Vincent used a knife to kill Sandra and frame her as an assailant. Poison: Vincent showed Bill and Kurapika a vial of poison to frame Sandra as an assailant. He also has a suicide pill in his molar. Handgun: Vincent wields a handgun of unknown brand and caliber. Abilities & Powers. Vincent has received military training and was able to kill an attendant in a matter of instants and in cold blood. The fact he framed her shows he can plan ahead. Nen. Vincent is a Nen user. Although his superior Balsamilco believes him to be less knowledgeable than Hunters in that regard, Benjamin is confident Vincent would never lose in a matter of moments, not even in a 2 versus 1 situation against Hunters, if he could use his Nen ability.

Virtual Restaurant (G.I card) Virtual Restaurant バーチャルレストラン - is a card found in the Greed Island game. It is one of the game's 100 designated slot cards and as such is required for a player to complete the game. Summary. Virtual Restaurant バーチャルレストラン - This card allows the caster to dine in a virtual restaurant. You are able to order and eat anything you want to. You will feel as though you have eaten all of that food but it's only an illusion. As such, you are only fooling your brain and your body will probably suffer from malnourishment. To prevent this from happening, you are given a multivitamin tablet on your way out.

Visca Forest Preserve The Visca Forest Preserve (, "Bisuka Shinrin Kōen"—lit. "Visca Forest-park"), or Visca Forest (, "Bisuka no Mori"), was the first site of the Second Phase in the 287th Hunter Exam. Overview. A forest spreading past the Milsy Wetlands, the reserve is home to the Great Stamp, the world's most ferocious pig, and to the Spider Eagles that live in the Split Mountain. It also contains numerous streams and lakes, home to a variety of freshwater fish. Plot. Hunter Exam arc. The examiner for the First Phase of the 287th Hunter Exam, Satotz, leads the remaining one hundred fifty examinees to the Visca Forest Preserve as part of the end of his phase of the Hunter Exam. Soon afterward, they're greeted by the Second Phase examiners Menchi and Buhara. For the first part of their test, Buhara requests "Roast Pork" and has the examinees look for it nearby in the forest. Unbeknownst to the examinees, the only pig available in the forest is the world's most ferocious pig, the Great Stamp. Only seventy examinees manage to complete this task. For the second part of the test, Menchi requests "sushi"; however, all but one of the examinees are ignorant of this dish. Examinee #404 Kurapika figures out the dish's main ingredient. However, examinee #403 Leorio yells it out loud, so they and several others rush to a nearby river and go fishing. Now with their fish, they prepare "sushi" dishes, but all of them fail. The only non-ignorant person about the "sushi" dish, examinee #294 Hanzo, serves Menchi as a perfect dish, although he also fails the exam. This causes Hanzo and Menchi to have outbursts with one another, and, in the process, Hanzo reveals the secret to making "sushi". The remaining examinees then try to make their own "sushi", and of course, they all fail, making none of the examinees pass the Second Phase of the exam. Menchi reports this to the Hunter Association secretary Beans, who in turn informs the Chairman Netero, who decides to intervene. At the Hunter Exam site, examinee #255 Todo starts a scene and is ultimately KO'ed by Buhara since if he didn't intervene, Menchi would have killed him. Menchi then gives a speech about how being a Gourmet Hunter is a strenuous job. The Chairman then arrives in his airship and lands on the ground, approximately sixty-foot drop. The two talk with one another, and it's decided a retest will be held at Split Mountain, where the examinees are tasked with getting a Spider Eagle egg. In this new phase of the exam forty-two people pass.
Vocal Song Collection The songs in this collection are collected from the Musical Hunter × Hunter.

Voconte Voconte (ボコンテ, "Bokonte") is a member of the Heil-Ly Family. Appearance. Voconte has a long face and bags under his eyes. He has black hair that's parted in the middle and falls just above his ears. He is seen wearing a shirt, jacket, and pants. Personality. Voconte seems practical, advising his fellow Heil-Ly members to trap their would-be victims using his ability. Like his fellow members, he has sadistic tendencies and no qualms about killing many people. Plot. Succession Contest arc. Voconte is seen with the other Heil-Ly members as Morena uses her Contagion on them one at a time and explains how her Nen ability works. In the Heil-Ly's hideout, several members look at the bottom half of Luini's corpse up against a nearby wall. A construction worker named Daemon (level 20) points out how much Luini's loss will affect them since he allowed them to hunt for prey from the hideout. Gelato (a professional gamer and level 19) adds how dangerous it will be now since the military is on high alert. An investigator's assistant named Perigord (level 18) suggests that someone should recreate Luini's ability. An arcade employee named Bille (level 20) says that he has already decided on his ability. Perigord reminds them that Morena said everyone has an innate type, confident that Luini was an Emitter. Bille replies that an Emitter needs to do the job, but Gelato points out that they need to figure out how to raise their levels so they can reach level 21. Voconte, an Emitter and mercenary transporter (level 26), speaks up and suggests using his "door" ability to catch prey that wander into the trap, adding that they could also invite them. After Bille kills Tassi, Terebellum takes Tassi's corpse to the disposal area in the group's hideout and tells Chiffon Toto and Montblanc Toto that Voconte connected the room to processing. When Hinrigh and Nobunaga infiltrate the Heil-Ly's hideout, Voconte can be seen sitting on a sofa and casually reading something. Abilities & Powers. Nen. Voconte is an Emitter. Having reached level 26 with Morena's Nen ability, Voconte's aura amount and output have been increased. He also obtained a teleportation Nen ability that he refers to as "Door". The ability is used to teleport unsuspecting victims from Room 3101 (with Gateaume acting as the lookout) to the Heil-Ly's hideout where the members can easily kill them to gain levels. The trap is analyzed in detail by Nobunaga, Phinks, and Feitan, with Nobunaga describing it as a land mine type, where the activation switch is set up in specific locations and is more coercive than a barrier type.

Volume 0 Kurapika's Memories (クラピカ, "Kurapika Tsuioku-hen") is a prequel one-shot and "volume zero" of the Hunter × Hunter manga series. It was given out to the first one million viewers of the 2013 feature film, . A digital edition was released by on July 4th, 2023. The with Togashi and information about the film were not included. Summary. In the village of the Kurta Clan, a young Kurapika continues to argue with the Elder about not being allowed to go to the outside world. He talks about it with his friend Pairo, who tells him about the rule and how people of the outside world discriminate against their kind. Kurapika then thinks back to a year ago when they met an injured girl named Sheila, who taught them about the outside world and gave them a book called "Dino Hunter", which made Kurapika and Pairo want to go on their own adventure. Kurapika eventually convinces the Elder to allow him to take the exit exam. Kurapika concentrates on studying and easily passes the first two tests. The Elder explains that the final test involves a shopping trip to a neighboring town in the outside world. He then reveals special eyedrops that will cause a Kurta's eyes to stay scarlet if they turn red within 24 hours of administering them. He stresses that Kurapika will fail if his eyes turn scarlet within those 24 hours. After Kurapika chooses Pairo to accompany him, the two take three Piko with them to Nancha City. Kurapika then thinks back on how Pairo saving him from falling off a cliff caused the injuries to his eyes and legs. He vows to find a doctor for him and hopes that they can explore the outside world together with no time limit. After they reach the town and begin shopping at the department store, three local thugs cause an incident with Pairo. Several bystanders eventually take the side of the two boys, who finish their shopping with their help. However, the three thugs wait for them on the outskirts of town and order them to pay a toll before they can leave. Bystanders again cause the thugs to back down, but after the main thug trips Pairo and calls him a gimp, Kurapika becomes enraged and easily subdues all three, his eyes becoming scarlet as he refuses their apologies. As Pairo calms him down, the main thug reveals that an old man (the Elder) was the one who hired them to confront them, eventually explaining all the details. Pairo tells him to call the old man and explain that they weren't able to get them angry, which the thug quickly does before continuing to apologize for taking things too far. As the two prepare to return to the village, a crowd of townspeople gathers behind them, and the old woman from the department store throws small rocks at Kurapika, calling them the devil's messengers and ordering them to leave. Her granddaughter begs her to stop and worries that they will kill them all if they get any angrier. On the return trip, the two discuss what happened, and when Kurapika points out that he failed since his eyes turned scarlet, Pairo reveals that he switched the eyedrops and used his medicine instead. After they return to the village, the Elder tells Kurapika that he has passed and allows him to leave for an indefinite amount of time, also giving him an envelope with the details about Pairo's condition so that he can look for a doctor. Kurapika prepares to leave and assures Pairo that he will find a doctor for him. However, Pairo reminds him about Dino Hunter and how they wanted to have an adventure, asking him to promise that he will have a trip where he has fun. Kurapika says goodbye to Pairo and his clan, and it's stated that the Kurta Clan massacre was reported to the world six weeks later, an account of which is given in extensive and brutal detail. Lastly, it's mentioned that the following message was found near the 128 bodies: "We'll accept anything you leave, but don't ever take anything away from us."

Volume 1 The Day of Departure (の, "Shuppatsu no Hi") is the 1st volume of the Hunter × Hunter manga series. It was released by on June 4th, 1998 in Japan and by on April 5th, 2005 in English. Summary. Gon Freecss has almost reached the age of twelve, the earliest age at which one is allowed to register for the Hunter Exam. Despite the objections of his aunt Mito (also his adoptive mother), Gon sets off to follow in the footsteps of his father, the legendary Hunter Ging Freecss. However, registering for the Hunter Exam does not mean one can take it. Gon must journey from his native Whale Island to the location on the mainland where the exam is held. On the way, he must contend with fierce storms and screeners who weed out unpromising examinees. It is during this time that he meets and befriends his fellow examinees and future companions: the cold and determined Kurapika, and the seemingly brash and avaricious Leorio. The trio reaches the hidden exam site shortly before registration is finalized. Gon quickly makes friends with a boy named Killua, the only other examinee as young as he is. The First Phase involves a marathon of unknown length through an underground tunnel and a deadly swamp to an unknown destination, led by the examiner Satotz. The situation becomes even more dangerous in the swamp when another examinee, the deadly Hisoka, believes that the first test is too boring and decides to "help" in the examination process.

Volume 10 Fakes, Swindles, and the Old Switcheroo (93, "Kugatsu Mikka"—lit. "September 3rd") is the 10th volume of the Hunter × Hunter manga series. It was released by on November 2nd, 2000 in Japan and by on September 5th, 2006 in English. Summary. After healing his broken arm and explaining that his Chain Jail ability enforces Zetsu on the captured target, Kurapika begins his torture of Uvogin, asking him about the location and abilities of the other Phantom Troupe members. With Uvogin refusing to answer, Kurapika eventually uses his Judgment Chain on him and orders him to answer truthfully. However, when Uvogin again doesn't answer Kurapika's question about the Spiders' location, the chain crushes his heart and kills him instantly, with Kurapika burying his body in the Gordeau Desert before heading back to the city. Gon, Killua, and Leorio reach nothing but dead ends looking for information on the Spiders by themselves, so they decide to take an interest-free loan of 100 million for Gon's Hunter License, allowing them to pay out rewards for information. While Leorio sifts through the offered information, Gon and Killua discover that they can use Gyo to find valuable items at a street auction, and the two start to use this method to make money. They meet an antiques expert named Zepile who prevents them from getting swindled when they try to sell the items they found, and the two boys wind up making him their auction agent, for a cut of the final proceeds. By this time, the Troupe realizes that Uvogin must have been killed by the chain user since he hasn't returned. After Nobunaga and Machi are sent out to find any traces of Kurapika, Gon and Killua follow them based on a tip from an informant. This, however, results in the boys being captured and brought back to the Troupe's hideout on the outskirts of the city, where they are interrogated about the chain user.
