Not knowing Kurapika's abilities or actions, they pass the questioning, but Nobunaga is intrigued by the pair and holds them captive, intending to have Chrollo interview them and let them join the Spiders. However, Gon and Killua utilize the doctoring methods they learned from Zepile and begin their escape from Nobunaga.

Volume 11 Next Stop: Meteor City—The Junkyard of the World (94, "Kugatsu Yokka"—lit. "September 4th") is the 11th volume of the Hunter × Hunter manga series. It was released by on March 2nd, 2001 in Japan and by on November 7th, 2006 in English. Summary. Gon and Killua manage to escape from Nobunaga by busting through walls and creating exits for themselves. By this time, Killua has realized from the Phantom Troupe's questions that the chain user is none other than Kurapika, and he suggests to Gon that they ask Kurapika how he became strong enough to kill a Spider so quickly. Meanwhile, the Mafia has hired several professional assassins to deal with the threat of the Troupe so the Underground Auction can be held. Among them are Killua's grandfather and father, Zeno and Silva Zoldyck. At the same time, Neon Nostrade escapes from her bodyguards, intent on participating in the auction herself, regardless of the danger. She is picked up by Chrollo, who has disguised himself in civilian clothing. He gets close to her, requests a fortune for himself, then steals her ability with his own ability, as he had planned all along. Chrollo knocks her out, has an ambulance take her away from the building so she is safe, then orders the Troupe to descend on the Cemetery Building, killing all the Mafia members in their way. He also kills all of the hired assassins aside from Zeno and Silva, who tracks him to the building's basement using En. A battle ensues, but at the last moment, they receive a call from Illumi, stating that he has fulfilled Chrollo's contract hit on the Ten Dons. With no paying clients, Zeno and Silva leave the scene, with Chrollo injured but alive. In the aftermath, the Troupe provides fake corpses, created with Kortopi's ability, and a faked message from the Ten Dons stating that the Spiders have been killed. They auction off copies of the real auction items, taking the Mafia's money in the process. The Mafia eventually learns that the Troupe is connected to Meteor City and considers calling off their hunt for the Spiders. Gon, Killua, Kurapika, and Leorio reunite at a hotel in the city, with Kurapika revealing the details of his ability and expressing his desire to move on from hunting the Spiders. However, Killua stresses that the remaining members will continue to look for him, adamantly suggesting that they stop them and secretly hoping for the reward money as well. At the Troupe's hideout, as Nobunaga questions his order to leave the city after the auction and prefers to find the chain user, Chrollo conjures his book and tells Nobunaga to answer his questions.

Volume 12 September 4th: Part 2 (94 その2, "Kugatsu Yokka Sono Ni") is the 12th volume of the Hunter × Hunter manga series. It was released by on July 4th, 2001 in Japan and by on January 2nd, 2007 in English. Summary. Using the fortune-telling ability stolen from Neon, Chrollo creates fortunes for most of the Phantom Troupe's members. It reveals that if they act normally, half of them will die in the coming weeks. Faced with this information, Chrollo decides to order the Spiders to leave the city. Thinking quickly, Hisoka alters his fortune to instead indicate that the deaths of the Spiders will be a direct result of returning home, forcing the group to stay so that Hisoka might find an opportunity to fight Chrollo. He also reveals the ruse of the dead bodies to Kurapika with a text message. The Mafia cancels any reward on the members they believed to still be alive, after they discover that the members are connected to Meteor City. Gon, Killua, and Leorio all offer to help Kurapika track down the Spiders again. They also enlist Melody to help them. Using her supernatural hearing, she is able to follow the Spiders as they leave their hideout. The group tracks the Spiders, but Gon and Killua are captured once again. Kurapika quickly formulates a plan in which he communicates with Gon and Killua via Leorio pretending to yell through his phone. A blackout is orchestrated at the Hotel Beitacle, and Kurapika captures Chrollo while Gon and Killua provide a distraction in the darkness. A ransom note is left for the Phantom Troupe, demanding that Pakunoda keep secret the memories she has extracted from Gon and Killua or Chrollo's life will be forfeit, and a hostage exchange is set up over the phone. As Pakunoda heads to Lingon Airport for the exchange and the other members prepare to return to the hideout, Hisoka asks for help from Illumi so that he can have the chance to fight Chrollo.

Volume 13 September 10th (910, "Kugatsu Tōka") is the 13th volume of the Hunter × Hunter manga series. It was released by on November 2nd, 2001 in Japan and by on March 6th, 2007 in English. Summary. A hostage exchange is arranged over the phone, and Kurapika allows Pakunoda to meet with him first to confirm that Chrollo is still alive. At the meeting, she also agrees to allow Kurapika to use his Judgment Chain ability to plant chains around both her and Chrollo's hearts. Pakunoda's chain is set to kill her if she reveals Kurapika's abilities to another Phantom Troupe member, while Chrollo's chain will kill him if he uses his Nen or communicates with another member of the Troupe. Back at the Troupe's hideout, the Spiders continue to disagree about the hostage exchange but eventually decide that it's for the best. Hisoka secretly follows Pakunoda to the exchange, arranging a fight with Chrollo after revealing that his Spider tattoo was fake. However, he immediately becomes uninterested once he discovers that Chrollo can no longer use Nen. After the exchange, Pakunoda returns to the Troupe's hideout without Chrollo. To answer the questions of the other members, she uses her Memory Bomb ability to transmit her memories and knowledge of Kurapika to the founding members, knowing that she will instantly be killed by the Judgment Chain and hoping that her sacrifice will save the lives of the remaining members. With Gon and Killua free, they are able to attend the Southernpiece Auction. They lack the ability to buy a copy of Greed Island, so they plan to apply for one of the Hunter positions that the multibillionaire Battera is filling to clear the game. At the auction, they unexpectedly run into Phinks and Feitan, who tell them that the Troupe is no longer seeking to kill Kurapika, as doing so would only strengthen the Judgment Chain around Chrollo's heart, and probably kill him. However, they keep secret the fact that Chrollo is most likely looking for an exorcist to remove Kurapika's chain. After the auction, Gon and Killua gain a preliminary interview with Tsezguerra, a fellow Hunter and Battera's chosen interviewer. He tells them that they are too weak in their current condition to play. Though frustrated, Gon and Killua do not give up. They spend the next four days before the official interview developing their respective abilities and pass with flying colors, shocking Tsezguerra with the speed of their progress. At the same time, the Spiders have also kept busy, having stolen one of Battera's copies of Greed Island. After traveling to Battera's Castle and entering the game, Gon listens to a message from his father telling him to enjoy the game he made with his friends. He then learns about the game's mechanics and anxiously waits for Killua to enter after the other new recruits.

Volume 14 The Secret of Greed Island (の, "Gēmu no Himitsu") is the 14th volume of the Hunter × Hunter manga series. It was released by on April 4th, 2002 in Japan and by on May 1st, 2007 in English. Summary. Gon and Killua have finally managed to enter Greed Island, as contracted players of the multibillionaire Battera. After encountering another player, they head toward a nearby town and learn more about Greed Island's card system of support "spells" and items, finding even the game's money to be in card form, much to their dismay. Just as they start to have fun in this Nen-based game, they are shocked by the sudden death of a player who had entered the game along with them (with the man's death caused by an unknown Nen ability). The true nature of Greed Island becomes apparent to Gon and Killua: in order to claim Battera's 50 billion reward for being the first to clear the game, some players have resorted to stealing cards and killing off the competition. The foremost among them is the anonymous Bomber, a powerful Nen user who can use Nen bombs to kill his victims. Gon, Killua, and the other new players hired by Battera are approached by an alliance that proposes an alternative, non-violent way of winning the game. They plan to monopolize items so only their group can transform them into the 100 specified slot cards needed to clear the game, agreeing to split the reward money. Angered by how the players have turned Ging's game into one of robbery and murder, Gon refuses to join and simply decides to enjoy the game as Ging encouraged him to do. The two boys then decide to head to Masadora, the City of Magic, but they also pick up a follower in the form of the young girl named Biscuit Krueger, another player recruited along with them. They try to outrun her, but she easily keeps up with them as they journey toward Masadora. Along the way, they face creatures inside the game for the first time, a pack of giant Cyclops, but the two are able to defeat them with minimal effort. Their spirits are raised, but they quickly encounter more creatures that they cannot figure out how to defeat. Quietly judging them all the while, Biscuit watches the two and quickly becomes frustrated with their wasted potential, eventually revealing her true identity to them—that of a 57-year-old Hunter. Biscuit forcibly takes Gon and Killua under her expert tutelage, just in time to use an attack by another player, a serial killer named Binolt, as a teaching tool. The two improve greatly during the ten days of training and eventually force Binolt to surrender before he agrees to leave the island and turn himself in.

Volume 15 Progress (, "Yakushin") is the 15th volume of the Hunter × Hunter manga series. It was released by on October 4th, 2002 in Japan and by on July 3rd, 2007 in English. Summary. After making their way to Masadora and buying spell cards, Gon, Killua, and Biscuit return to the badlands to continue their Nen training. The two boys eventually discover the technique Shu as they dig their way back to Masadora. They continue to improve gradually to the point where each is able to catch a Hyper Puffball and Bubble Horse. Biscuit then teaches them other advanced techniques such as Ko, Ken, and Ryu, with the two constantly sparring to practice. After training Gon and Killua for two weeks in the badlands, Biscuit moves on to training by Nen type and stresses a balanced, all-around approach. In the meantime, several members of the Phantom Troupe uses a boat to reach the island outside of the game, but a Game Master named Razor tells them that they will have to enter the correct way, using an "Eliminate" card to teleport them away and destroying their boat. Back in the badlands, Biscuit begins with Enhancement training and then explains that rock-paper-scissors is based on real martial arts. Gon uses this concept and decides that he wants to create an ability based on the game, with rock using Enhancement, paper Emission, and scissors Transmutation. After Killua reveals his lightning ability and impresses the two, Gon reminds him that the next Hunter Exam is approaching. The three defeat a pack of wolves on their way to the harbor where Killua exits the game and then makes his way to the Lone Pine Tree. During Killua's absence, Abengane approaches Gon and Biscuit to tell them about the situation with the Bomber, asking them to spread the word and keep him from clearing the game. He then uses his exorcism ability to remove the bomb, putting on a disguise to cover the Nen#Nen beast and planning to satisfy the conditions to dispel Genthru's Nen. At the hideout for Nickes' Alliance, as the group continues to amass specified slot cards and prepares to take on Tsezguerra's group, Genthru suddenly reveals that he is the Bomber, killing Jispa when he tries to subdue him. He then reveals that he has planted bombs on every member of the alliance and, as a condition of his Countdown ability, explains how to deactivate them. He warns them that his Little Flower will keep them from getting close and offers to spare their lives for 90 specified slot cards, escaping from the hideout before anyone can stop him. Although the members eventually agree to the deal and hand over the cards, the Bombers pretend to deactivate the bombs but actually detonate them all at once, killing nearly every member of the alliance. As Killua talks with the Kiriko before heading to the exam site, Gon and Biscuit learn that the Bomber has attacked the alliance when a new shipment of cards arrives in Masadora. While Gon continues to train with Biscuit, Killua arrives at the exam site and knocks every other examinee unconscious, collecting their badges and becoming the only one to pass as he leaves the examiner stunned. He quickly returns to the game and is surprised to see how many spell cards Gon and Biscuit have collected. As the two suddenly notice Chrollo's name in Gon's book, the Troupe members have returned to the island using the correct way and realize that the exorcist Chrollo is looking for must be on Greed Island. Hisoka then reveals himself and explains that he is looking for the exorcist for Chrollo, with the others realizing that Chrollo hired him for the job and intends to reward him with a fight afterwards. Killua calls Kurapika to confirm that his Judgment Chain still hasn't been removed, and at the Nostrade's Mansion, Light has a mental breakdown as he struggles with the loss of Neon's ability. After Gon reveals his ability to Killua, the trio begin to collect specified slot cards by completing various challenges around the island, eventually reaching 57 and celebrating.

Volume 16 Face-Off (, "Taiketsu") is the 16th volume of the Hunter × Hunter manga series. It was released by on February 4th, 2003 in Japan and by on September 4th, 2007 in English. Summary. Gon, Killua, and Biscuit, in their quest to collect all 99 specified slot cards to clear Greed Island, begin contacting other players in order to trade information regarding the remaining cards. However, the Bombers are nearing completion of the game after a successful encounter against Tsezguerra's team. Several teams combine strength into a single alliance to stop them, with Gon's team being invited as well. During their meeting, they reach the conclusion that they need to obtain a monopoly on the only card in the game that no one has yet acquired—"Plot of Beach". The players then travel to Soufrabi where they learn that the town has been taken over by fifteen pirates, among whom is their leader named Razor—an ex-convict and acquaintance of Ging. The alliance has to defeat the pirates in competitive sports and win eight games to force them out of Soufrabi, but the majority of the players are useless. While the rest of the alliance gives up on acquiring the card after discovering that the Bombers will be unable to obtain it, Gon's team continues to try and comes back with a group of stronger competitors to complete Razor's challenge. During the search for companions, Gon's team encounter Hisoka and convince him to help them. Killua comes to realize that his true motive for being in Greed Island is to find an exorcist who can remove Kurapika's chain from Chrollo, and the group also learns that Greed Island is taking place within the real world. In addition to Hisoka, the group enlists Tsezguerra's team and a Hunter named Goreinu so that they can defeat Razor in a deadly game of dodgeball and acquire the rare card.

Volume 17 Three-Way Struggle (つの, "Mitsu Domoe no Kōbō") is the 17th volume of the Hunter × Hunter manga series. It was released by on June 4th, 2003 in Japan and by on November 6th, 2007 in English. Summary. The game of dodgeball continues, and both sides are quickly whittled down to a few members. Gon unleashes his new ability against Razor to take the offensive, surprising competitors on both sides with the tremendous amount of aura he can produce. With the help of both Killua and Hisoka, Gon manages to defeat Razor and his 14 Devils. Before Gon leaves, Razor tells him about his relationship with Ging, revealing that while his father isn't on Greed Island and he doesn't know where he is, he hopes that Gon is able to find him. Gon and his team eventually obtain the rare "Plot of Beach" card and the potential to make copies. Aware of the situation, Genthru threatens the lives of Tsezguerra and Gon's team unless they concede. Tsezguerra decides to stave off the Bombers for three weeks to give Gon and Killua time to recover. Under Biscuit's tutelage, the two further train their Nen in order to fight Genthru and his comrades. Meanwhile, Hisoka regroups with the Phantom Troupe after Abengane is spotted. Kalluto, Killua's younger brother, is revealed to have joined the Troupe. As Tsezguerra is pursued by the Bombers, his team ends up leaving the game, and in Battera's mansion, they are told that the reward for completing Greed Island has been canceled; this, therefore, ends all the contracts of the Greed Island players. Now that Gon and his friends are the final contenders in Greed Island, Genthru, Sub, and Bara begin their attack on his team.

Volume 18 Chance Encounter (, "Kaikō") is the 18th volume of the Hunter × Hunter manga series. It was released by on October 3rd, 2003 in Japan and by on January 1st, 2008 in English. Summary. Gon, Killua, and Biscuit each confront one of the Bomber members and fight them one on one. Biscuit reveals her true appearance to defeat Bara, Killua makes use of his lightning ability and yo-yos to defeat Sub, and although he takes a beating from him and decides to improvise, Gon follows through with the plan and defeats Genthru, with the group using "Angel's Breath" cards to heal Gon, Bara, Genthru, and Killua. With the help of Goreinu, they succeed in collecting 99 specified slot cards, and a 100-question quiz is then won by Gon to obtain the last card to complete Greed Island. In the meantime, Abengane dispels Genthru's Nen from himself and meets up with Hisoka, planning to leave the game to make a fortune from the exorcism for Chrollo. After Gon meets the Game Masters List and Dwun, he is rewarded by being allowed to take three cards outside the game. Bidding their farewell to Biscuit, who leaves with one of the cards, Gon and Killua use the other two in an attempt to travel to Ging, but they are taken to Kite instead. Kite invites the boys to join him and his team to assist with their research for the Kakin Empire. The group learns from Wong that a piece of an unidentified creature has been found and is currently at the Southernpiece Auction House in Yorknew City. The creature, revealed to be a Chimera Ant Queen that's the size of a person, starts preying on humans in the nearby Balsa Islands to build her own colony.

Volume 19 NGL (, "Enu Jī Eru") is the 19th volume of the Hunter × Hunter manga series. It was released by on February 4th, 2004 in Japan and by on March 4th, 2008 in English. Summary. As Chimera Ants capture dozens of humans and take them back to their nest, Kite and his group research the species and discover that the Ant they're looking for may have washed up on the shores of NGL in the Mitene Union. The Queen assembles the Squadron Leaders and orders them to bring her 50 humans a day so she can focus on giving birth to the King. Kite, Gon, Killua, and Kite's companions arrive at NGL's border stop and prepare to enter the country. The NGL ambassadors explain that no modern technology is allowed, and after being screened, the remaining members of Kite's group begin their search for the species. Inside the country, all the Hunters who ventured there are either killed or captured as food for the Queen. After encountering one of the Ants, Gon, Killua, and Kite discover the dark side of NGL, a narcotics factory producing a drug known as D², and each defeats a Chimera Ant once inside. Rammot awakens to Nen after his fight with Gon and Killua and begins awakening the power in his fellow Ants. Elsewhere, the three Hunters are ambushed and surrounded, forced to fight in order to survive. Each is victorious, and they continue making their way toward the nest. The Royal Guard named Neferpitou awakens and discovers Pokkle hiding under a pile of bones, torturing him for information on Nen. As the three Hunters get closer to the nest, Pitou senses their presence, attacking Kite and severing his arm. Killua knocks Gon unconscious to keep him from attacking, and the two boys flee as Kite prepares to fight Pitou. After Killua carries Gon back to NGL's border stop, Netero and two other Hunters (named Morel and Knov) arrive as reinforcements to eliminate the Chimera Ant threat. Netero stresses that Gon and Killua can only join them if they defeat the other two candidates for the team. When Gon wakes up, he assures Killua that Kite is still alive and that they have to get stronger so they can rescue him. In a forest in NGL, Pitou is seen holding the decapitated head of Kite.

Volume 2 A Struggle in the Mist (のの, "Kiri no Naka no Kōbō") is the 2nd volume of the Hunter × Hunter manga series. It was released by on September 2nd, 1998 in Japan and by on May 4th, 2005 in English. Summary. Bored by the first phase, Hisoka has decided that he will "help out" in the selection process by using his playing cards to kill the examinees he deems unworthy. Many nearby join up to attack him, but Hisoka's superior skills leave them all dead in seconds. Fortunately, he decides Leorio, Kurapika, and Gon all pass his test, and they arrive relatively unharmed at the site of the Second Phase. The next examiners, the Gourmet Hunters Menchi and Buhara, reveal themselves shortly and explain that the focus of the Second Phase is cooking. The first part of the phase is to hunt and roast Great Stamps found in the surrounding woods to satisfy Buhara's massive appetite. The more demanding Menchi, however, challenges the examinees to create a dish almost no one there has heard of: sushi. But when one examinee accidentally reveals the details of the dish, Menchi becomes even more critical of the examinees' dishes. Everyone unsurprisingly fails, and Chairman Netero is called in to resolve the situation. A replacement test is given, which requires the examinees to dive into Split Mountain to retrieve and boil the egg of a Spider Eagle. Gon, Kurapika, Leorio, and Killua all pass easily, and the remaining examinees are transported via Netero's airship to the next exam site. Forty examinees remain at the start of the Third Phase: Trick Tower managed by the Blacklist Hunter Lippo and two other examiners. They have 72 hours to reach the bottom alive or they are disqualified. Gon, Leorio, Kurapika, and Killua stumble upon "The Path of Majority Rules" method of descent, but are joined by a fifth examinee, the "Rookie Crusher" Tonpa, who takes the Hunter Exam every year solely to sabotage the efforts of others. The five eventually reach an arena where they must win a best of five matches against prisoners whose sentences will be reduced by one year for every hour that they delay an examinee. After Tonpa quickly surrenders to Bendot, Gon evens the score by using his speed to beat Sedokan in his challenge involving candles.

Volume 20 Weakness (, "Jakuten") is the 20th volume of the Hunter × Hunter manga series. It was released by on June 4th, 2004 in Japan and by on May 6th, 2008 in English. Summary. Gon and Killua meet Palm, one of Knov's students, who tells the boys that they have one month to defeat Morel's two students (Knuckle and Shoot) if they want to join the Extermination Team and return to NGL. Back in the Chimera Ant nest, Neferpitou watches over Kite frozen in a block of ice. The Royal Guard wishes that they could fight him again, suddenly deciding to create an ability with which to fix him. Knuckle tries to lure out Gon and Killua, loudly challenging the two to a duel, but the boys head back to their hotel and find Biscuit waiting for them. She works on their Ren training so the two will be prepared to face Knuckle. Netero, Morel, and Knov monitor the nest at a distance, and Morel uses his pipe to create smoke rabbits in order to get a count of the enemy's forces. Another Royal Guard, Shaiapouf, awakens and discusses the situation with Pitou, telling them that they will simply destroy the targets if they get close to the nest. After underestimating Gon's strength, Knuckle agrees to fight the two boys as many times as they want, but tells them that they won't be able to beat him in the remaining time. In the same city, the former kingpin of NGL named Gyro walks the streets, reborn as an Ant but rejecting the Queen's commands and retaining all his human memories. His backstory is given in detail, and it's explained that he plans to spread evil throughout the world. Making use of Morel's smoke and Knov's portals, Netero is able to eliminate dozens of soldier Ants. As the last Royal Guard (Menthuthuyoupi) awakens, Gon confronts Knuckle and improves during the course of the fight, but eventually falls unconscious when he runs out of aura. As Killua spars with Biscuit back at the hotel, she lectures him about giving up and running away, stressing the danger it could cause Gon if Killua eventually leaves him to die during a fight. She then gives him an ultimatum: if he can't defeat Shoot, he has to stay out of Gon's life. Gon and Knuckle begin their rematch, and the latter explains his A.P.R. ability in detail, confident that he can make Gon go bankrupt. Nearby, Killua and Shoot are prepared to begin their fight, with the latter also revealing his ability.

Volume 21 Reunion (, "Saikai") is the 21st volume of the Hunter × Hunter manga series. It was released by on February 4th, 2005 in Japan and by on July 1st, 2008 in English. Summary. As Killua fights against Illumi's influence and struggles in his duel with Shoot, the King is suddenly born in the nest, mortally wounding his mother and killing two Squadron Leaders. The three Royal Guards arrive and escort him outside, with the King killing a family of three in his search for rare humans. While many of the other Squadron Leaders abandon the dying Queen, Colt surrenders himself to Morel and Knov, pleading the two Hunters to save the Queen's life. Knuckle and Shoot make their way into NGL as Gon and Killua stay behind, with Gon now under the effects of Knuckle's I.R.S. and unable to use Nen for 30 days. After Netero departs to see an old friend, the other Hunters and a medical team head to the nest and attempt to save the Queen's life. Her wounds are too severe, but before she dies, she tells them that her son's name is Meruem. Colt finds a tiny baby still alive in her womb, swearing to protect it and reminiscing on his human sister and mother. With the other Squadron Leaders spreading out to become kings, the King and Royal Guards arrive at the royal palace in East Gorteau. Massacring the soldiers and eating them to become stronger, the King then kills the country's dictator and plans to turn the palace into a processing plant for humans. To appease Palm after not defeating Knuckle and Shoot, Gon promises to go on a date with her. He also gets word from Knuckle that they found Kite and are bringing him back from the nest. As Killua keeps an eye on Gon during his date, he encounters Rammot and overcomes Illumi's spell by removing a needle that was secretly implanted in his forehead. With his mind now clear, Killua easily decapitates and kills the Chimera Ant. Morel and Knuckle have a short fight with Cheetu, during which time Knuckle attaches A.P.R. to the Ant. Gon reunites with Kite, but is overcome with emotion as he sees the torture he endured as a training tool for the Ants. Gon promises to fix him and swears to fight Neferpitou on his own. The Hunters receive a message from Netero to invade the palace at midnight the night before the rally. With the 30 days that have passed, Gon is able to use Nen again, and Morel orders Gon to attack him to see if he's ready for the mission. Killua stops Gon before he can unleash his powerful Jajanken, and Morel is left frightened and satisfied. The matchups for the invasion are arranged: Gon and Killua versus Neferpitou, Knuckle and Shoot versus Menthuthuyoupi, Morel and Knov versus Shaiapouf, and Netero versus Meruem.

Volume 22 8: Part 1 (8—①, "Hachi (Ichi)") is the 22nd volume of the Hunter × Hunter manga series. It was released by on July 4th, 2005 in Japan and by on September 2nd, 2008 in English. Summary. After learning that Chimera Ants have attacked Meteor City, several Phantom Troupe members journey there to eradicate the threat. In her giant nest nearby, Zazan uses her stinger to mutate and control dozens of the city's residents. The Troupe members decide that it's a race to kill the Queen, and each finds an opponent: Bonolenov defeats the Gun-toting Ant, Phinks defeats Gorilla, Shizuku defeats Pike, Shalnark defeats Pell and Boki, Kalluto defeats Small Beetle, and after struggling at first, Feitan uses his Pain Packer ability to defeat the transformed Zazan. Elsewhere, Gon and Killua successfully sneak into East Gorteau and realize that the selection process has already started, discovering empty villages and mass graves. After the two go their separate ways, Gon is ambushed by Snake (whom he easily incapacitates) and then by Hollow and Bat, whose teamwork gives him trouble at first, but he eventually overcomes the two Ants. Neferpitou senses Killua saving villages and warning them about the genocide, and orders Leol's squad to take care of the problem. While Pitou uses the manipulated Ming Jol-ik to order Peijin's citizens to stay in their homes, Flutter uses his surveillance ability to warn Cheetu about an ambush set by Knuckle and Shoot, also tracking Killua through the dense forests and ordering soldier Ants to attack him.

Volume 23 6: Part 1 (6—①, "Roku (Ichi)") is the 23rd volume of the Hunter × Hunter manga series. It was released by on March 3rd, 2006 in Japan and by on November 4th, 2008 in English. Summary. After defeating several soldier Ants from Leol's squad, Killua is struck by multiple bullets from an unknown sniper that turns out to be an Ant named Ikalgo. Killua is led to an underground lake where the Ortho Siblings use their Needlefish De Darts ability to wound Killua and nearly kill him, but he utilizes his own ability and his knowledge of darts to survive the final strike, decapitating the brother and sister. Killua begins to bleed out from the numerous wounds, but Ikalgo returns and carries him to a secret clinic as quickly as he can. Elsewhere in a desert, the invisible figure following Gon finally reveals himself and says that his name is Meleoron. He reveals his abilities and tells Gon that he plans to take down the King since he killed Peggy (who was his foster father when they were human), asking Gon if he wants to team up. Meanwhile, in the palace, the King spends his time learning board games like and, forcing the national champions to play against him. After learning the rules of a game called Gungi, he has trouble beating the champion, but is confident that he can disrupt her rhythm eventually. In Peijin, Morel uses his Deep Purple's "Smoke Troopers" to take out the soldiers manipulated by Neferpitou, but he is interrupted by a confident Cheetu, who uses his ability to transport Morel to a Nen space where he has to tag the Ant in a certain amount of time in order to escape. As Knov uses his Hide and Seek ability to escape Pitou's puppets, he spots Flutter providing reconnaissance for the Ants and plans to take him out. While the King is still unable to defeat the Gungi champion, Morel's patience against Cheetu pays off and he has the Ant cornered, but Cheetu suddenly develops a new ability.

Volume 24 1: Part 4 (1—④, "Ichi (Yon)") is the 24th volume of the Hunter × Hunter manga series. It was released by on October 4th, 2007 in Japan and by on January 6th, 2009 in English. Summary. After Cheetu's new ability ultimately proves ineffective, Morel escapes from the Nen space and meets up with Knov, who has incapacitated and captured Flutter. As Leol and his squad look for the two Hunters in Peijin, the King underestimates the champion's commitment to Gungi and rips off his own arm as an apology. Shaiapouf pleads with him to receive medical attention and the champion refuses to play until his arm is healed, causing the King to finally give in and receive assistance from Neferpitou. Pitou's Doctor Blythe begins healing the King, but the ability uses a considerable amount of aura, not allowing them to control the puppet soldiers or their En during that time. Knov knows that this may be his only chance to place an exit near the palace, and he successfully sets three but is unable to go any further once he encounters Pouf's En. He escapes and is overcome with fear, having a mental breakdown, and declaring that he can't return to the palace. Taking advantage of Director Bizeff's lust, Palm infiltrates the palace and plans to get a glimpse of the King and Royal Guards so she can provide reconnaissance with her ability. In an underground chapel, Leol uses the ability of Morel's friend against him, but Morel's Deep Purple and lung capacity prove victorious and lead to the Chimera Ant's death. Ikalgo and a recovered Killua meet up with the other members of the Extermination Team and plan their infiltration of the palace. Still unable to defeat the champion and seeing that she is unconsciously using Nen, the King learns that her name is Komugi, but realizes that he doesn't know his own. He asks each of the Royal Guards about his name, displeased with or ambivalent toward their responses. He speaks fondly of Komugi and understands that strength can manifest in different ways, initially regretting that he killed a young child on the way to the palace, but his mood quickly changes and he declares that his strength is to destroy those weaker than his. As the King enters Komugi's room planning to kill her, he finds an eagle attacking the girl and kills it to protect her, confused by how conflicted his emotions are. The citizens of East Gorteau begin their forced march toward the palace, hypnotized by Pouf's scales once close enough, and the Extermination Team (excluding Knov) ready themselves for the infiltration.

Volume 25 Charge (, "Totsunyū") is the 25th volume of the Hunter × Hunter manga series. It was released by on March 4th, 2008 in Japan and by on March 3rd, 2009 in English. Summary. As the Extermination Team prepares to infiltrate the palace, the King remains conflicted and orders his Royal Guards to leave him alone on the second floor. Welfin plots to get in the King's good graces, and as Neferpitou and Shaiapouf suddenly notice an enormous dragon (ridden by Netero and Zeno) descending upon the palace, which splits apart into hundreds of smaller ones, the clock strikes midnight and the Extermination Team begins their infiltration. Pouf flies toward the King's location, and Pitou goes after Netero floating the sky, but is sent back by his 100-Type Guanyin Bodhisattva. Netero's development of the ability is explained: he would throw ten thousand punches of gratitude every single day, eventually allowing him to punch faster than sound. The Extermination Team confronts Menthuthuyoupi on the central staircase, causing him to transform in order to better protect the King. Zeno's Dragon Dive pierces the palace, causing many of the Hunters to hesitate, but while making use of Meleoron's God's Accomplice, Knuckle activates A.P.R. on the Royal Guard. As Youpi transforms even further, Pitou's En envelops the palace and causes the Hunters to stiffen with fear, which Youpi takes advantage of when he destroys the central staircase and separates the group. Pitou spots Netero and Zeno heading toward the King and Komugi, and shoots toward the King once they hit the ground. But once the Royal Guard reaches the tower, they find the King holding a wounded Komugi in his arms as Netero and Zeno look on in fear. The King asks Pitou to heal Komugi and tells the two old men that he will fight them somewhere else. With Youpi guarding the entrance to the second floor, Morel distracts him and allows Knuckle to land another punch. Though wounded, Shoot distracts Youpi so that Morel can leave with his pipe to fight Pouf. As Gon and Killua look for Pitou, the latter notices two soldier Ants that Ikalgo (disguised as Flutter) will have to pass by, quickly using his yo-yos to kill them, but Welfin catches sight of the attack from the shadows. In the empty throne room, Pouf laughs and cries about his failure as a Royal Guard, but suddenly finds himself surrounded by smoke with Morel standing opposite him. After killing the two Ants, Killua passes by Ikalgo, who simply tells Killua that he owes him one now—words that refocus Killua's mind on the mission at hand. Gon spots Morel's Smoky Jail surrounding the throne room and then sees the King accompanied by Zeno and Netero, the latter of whom gestures back toward Pitou's location, causing Gon's anger to flare up.

Volume 26 We Meet Again (, "Saikai") is the 26th volume of the Hunter × Hunter manga series. It was released by on October 3rd, 2008 in Japan and by on January 5th, 2010 in English. Summary. As Zeno uses Dragon Head to transport Netero and the King away from the palace, Shoot fearlessly fights Menthuthuyoupi, with each trying to keep the other away from the King. Making use of God's Accomplice, Knuckle feels powerless as he watches Shoot endure Youpi's strikes. Welfin and Bloster confront Ikalgo (disguised as Flutter), and after he accidentally uses Leol's old name, the two Chimera Ants realize something is wrong. Shoot begins to reach his limit against Youpi, but Knuckle suddenly reveals himself and challenges the Royal Guard. In the throne room, Shaiapouf introduces himself to Morel and uses Spiritual Message to analyze the Hunter, eventually wrapping himself up in a cocoon. As Ikalgo heads to the basement to look for Palm, Gon and Killua find Neferpitou using Doctor Blythe to heal Komugi, but while Killua understands that Pitou is protecting the girl, Gon can only see her being hurt and envisions the torture that was inflicted upon Kite. Pitou begs Gon to let them heal Komugi, causing him to fly into a rage as he nearly decides to kill the Royal Guard. However, Killua quickly reminds him that they need Pitou in order to heal Kite. Gon finally agrees to wait one hour for Pitou to heal Komugi, ordering them to follow him to Peijin and heal Kite once the hour has passed. Elsewhere, Knuckle taunts Youpi and gets the Royal Guard to chase after him as Meleoron meets up with Killua. After Youpi gives up chasing Knuckle and passes by the wounded Shoot, Knuckle is unable to take Shoot to take safety, declaring that he has to get revenge for Youpi's insult, which Shoot tearfully urges him to do. With Morel left unsure by Pouf's plot, an enraged Youpi attacks Knuckle and destroys the base of the central tower in the process, revealing to Knuckle that too much anger causes the Royal Guard to unleash an explosion. Outside the palace, Cheetu confronts Zeno but is quickly killed by Silva, with the two Zoldycks riding off on a dragon. As Pouf slowly escapes Morel's Smoky Jail, Ikalgo continues his search for Palm and as he worries that she may be dead, he is attacked by Bloster and Flutter's corpse is destroyed. Youpi uses his fake rage against Knuckle, drawing the Hunter in and leaving him defenseless as he prepares to kill him with a single punch. But high above in the sky, making use of God's Accomplice, Killua unleashes Thunderbolt on Youpi, immobilizing the Royal Guard as Knuckle punches him hard in the face.

Volume 27 Name (, "Namae") is the 27th volume of the Hunter × Hunter manga series. It was released by on December 25th, 2009 in Japan and by on March 1st, 2011 in English. Summary. After Knuckle finishes attacking Menthuthuyoupi and makes his getaway, Killua uses his Godspeed to overwhelm the Royal Guard, but runs out of electricity and escapes with Meleoron's God's Accomplice. In the throne room, Morel further questions if he should keep waiting or attack Shaiapouf's cocoon. In the palace's basement, Ikalgo struggles to kill Bloster, eventually knocking him unconscious with sleeping gas but unable to pull the trigger. Morel finally destroys Pouf's cocoon and deactivates Smoky Jail, and Pouf splits into hundreds of clones, thanking the Hunter for setting him free. Unable to defeat the clones, Morel and his "Smoke Troopers" ignore the Royal Guard, but Pouf suddenly steals his pipe and flies away. Knuckle and Youpi suddenly appear before him, and the two Hunters use their smoke clone strategy to fight Youpi. As Hina and Shidore rescue Bizeff from the fallen rubble, Morel and Knuckle trick Youpi twice, allowing Knuckle to land a punch on the Royal Guard just before he explodes. Pouf throws Morel's pipe in a nearby river and uses his clones to survey the palace, suddenly seeing the explosion as he returns. With Shoot saved by Knov, Killua recharges and tells Meleoron to assess the situation with Morel and Knuckle, adding that he will go back to Gon. As Neferpitou continues to heal Komugi and Gon sits in silence, Pouf appears and attempts to find out the King's location. Youpi harnesses his rage and transforms into a centaur-like creature, destroying Morel's smoke clones as the interest from A.P.R. continues to increase. Arriving at their destination, the King attempts to dissuade Netero from fighting, but the Chairman understands the mission's importance and uses his 100-Type Guanyin Bodhisattva to strike the King. After learning the King's location, Pouf plays along with Gon's orders and secretly sends most of himself to assist the King. Morel reaches his limit, but is saved by Meleoron when Youpi tries to kill him. Knuckle reveals himself and deactivates A.P.R. in exchange for Youpi letting Morel and Meleoron live. After a bald Knov arrives and takes Morel to safety, Knuckle and Meleoron team up to take on the other Royal Guards. Youpi and Pouf find one another and make their way toward the King, who still refuses to fight back. Netero offers to reveal the King's name to him if he can make Netero admit defeat, and the King agrees.

Volume 28 Regeneration (, "Saisei") is the 28th volume of the Hunter × Hunter manga series. It was released by on July 4th, 2011 in Japan and by on September 4th, 2012 in English. Summary. Using his Ninety-Ninth Hand, Netero forces the King down into an underground chamber and is grateful for the opportunity to fight him. Having admiration for Netero's ability, the King's confidence doesn't waiver and he uses the pillars to increase his speed, relentlessly attacking Netero until he makes a mistake. Netero understands the King's strategy and plans to unleash his Zero Hand at the right moment. Having been turned into a Chimera Ant, Palm confronts Killua and asks about Gon, but Killua refuses to answer. The two begin to fight, but Killua eventually breaks down sobbing and tells Palm that only she can help Gon now. Palm ignores Shaiapouf's commands and assures Killua that he is the one Gon needs. Elsewhere, Knuckle confronts Pouf and asks him to fight, and the Royal Guard disobeys Gon and flies away after bursting into hundreds of clones. Neferpitou panics and Gon tells them that they have ten fewer minutes to heal Komugi. Pitou realizes how dangerous Gon is and resolves to kill him to protect the King. In the palace's basement, Welfin confronts and attacks Ikalgo, who fights against the centipedes from Welfin's Missileman and eventually learns that Palm may still be alive. After enduring thousands of strikes, the King severs Netero's right leg and asks for his name, but Netero quickly seals up the wound before the two exchange a thousand more blows. As he promised, the King then severs Netero's left arm and again asks for his name, but Netero summons his Zero Hand and unleashes an enormous blast directly upon the King. With Netero left gaunt from the attack, the King comes out only superficially harmed, and after Netero reveals the King's name, he pierces his own heart with his hand and detonates a Poor Man's Rose. Youpi and Pouf arrive at the site of the explosion and find the King barely still alive. The two Royal Guards feed themselves to him and rejoice as he is brought back to life. Ikalgo, Killua, Palm, Knuckle, and Meleoron meet up and decide to fight until the end. Pitou finishes healing Komugi, and after Gon threatens to kill the girl, he and Pitou make their way to Peijin to heal Kite, with Komugi left behind as a hostage.

Volume 29 Memory (, "Kioku") is the 29th volume of the Hunter × Hunter manga series. It was released by on August 4th, 2011 in Japan and by on January 1st, 2013 in English. Summary. Meruem emerges fully healed after Shaiapouf and Menthuthuyoupi offered him part of themselves, but he is unable to remember anything besides his name. He eventually remembers fighting someone, and as the three prepare to head back to the palace to hopefully awaken his memory, Pouf seizes his chance and has his shell fly back to kill Komugi before Meruem can reunite with her. After Knuckle activates his A.P.R. and Palm uses her Wink Blue, the others learn that the King is still alive. As Pouf uses his clones to look for Komugi, Killua holds her on his shoulders and eventually realizes that the Royal Guard is trying to kill her. After Killua fights him back, Pouf leaves to hide the Gungi board and pieces so they don't trigger Meruem's memory. Gon and Neferpitou arrive at Kite's location in Peijin, with the Royal Guard believing that Komugi is no longer a hostage. Gon orders them to heal Kite, but Pitou reveals that he died when the two fought and that their ability is only able to preserve and manipulate. After handing over Komugi to Palm, Killua uses Speed of Lightning to race toward Gon, who begins to break down and finally becomes distraught at Pitou's deceit, summoning an incredible amount of power. After their Terpsichora proves ineffective, Pitou sees that Gon has forced himself to grow to the point where he can beat them. The Royal Guard tries to strike him from behind, but Gon easily dodges and kicks them high into the air, punching their face with a powerful Jajanken. Killua finds Gon repeatedly punching Pitou until their death, but with post-mortem Nen and their Terpsichora, the headless Royal Guard servers Gon's right arm, which Gon then uses to stab Pitou's chest, pinning them to the ground as he unleashes an even more powerful Jajanken. Still trying to regain his memory, Meruem unleashes his En to search the palace and then incapacitates both Knuckle and Meleoron. While Palm and Ikalgo hide Komugi in the basement, Welfin acts as a messenger and confronts Youpi. As his nose begins to bleed, Meruem spots a lone Gungi piece and remembers his game with someone. Pouf finds Youpi lying dead and informs Meruem, who orders Pouf to tell him everything.

Volume 3 Resolution (, "Ketchaku") is the 3rd volume of the Hunter × Hunter manga series. It was released by on November 4th, 1998 in Japan and by on July 6th, 2005 in English. Summary. After Gon defeats Sedokan, the prisoner Majtani enrages Kurapika by pretending to be a member of the Phantom Troupe. Kurapika then displays his strength and rage by defeating Majtani with a single punch. However, it's revealed that Majtani is possibly still unconscious and the match is unable to end since the two agreed to fight to the death. After Kurapika refuses to kill him, the examinees are forced to wait and see if the prisoner wakes up. Elsewhere in Trick Tower, Hisoka kills the examiner Togari and becomes the first to pass the Third Phase of the exam. Back inside the arena, the prisoner named Leroute proposes to Leorio that they wager their time to make a series of bets. It's eventually discovered that Majtani was faking his unconsciousness to buy time for his team (giving Kurapika the win), but after Leorio loses the final two bets against Leroute, he loses the match and leaves the score even at two each. With the group left with 50 fewer hours to descend the tower, Killua quickly dispatches Johness the Dissector, and Kurapika and Leorio learn from Gon that he is from an elite family of assassins. Using a simple solution from Gon, the five examinees eventually reach the bottom of Trick Tower just before their time runs out. The examiner Lippo then reveals that the Fourth Phase will take place on Zevil Island for one week, where they will collect the badges of other examinees to reach six points (with the badge of their specificed target giving them the most points). After receiving Hisoka's badge number, Gon thinks about how to confront him and practices with his fishing rod, deciding that he will go for Hisoka's badge when he is distracted by other prey. Gon eventually finds Hisoka and waits for him to make the first move. Elsewhere on the island, Tonpa and Sommy work together to trick Leorio and take his badge, but Kurapika helps him to capture the two examinees, revealing that his target was Tonpa. As the two work together to find Leorio's target (Ponzu), and Killua is followed by someone, Gon continues to watch Hisoka. The magician is eventually confronted by Goz, but Gon is unable to take advantage of the situation when Gittarackur suddenly appears and finishes off the wounded examinee. It's then revealed that Gittarackur can alter his appearance, and he digs a hole in the ground to wait inside until the deadline. Needing two more points, Hisoka continues to look for targets during the night and eventually spots Kurapika and Leorio making their way through a nearby forest.

Volume 30 Answer (, "Hentō") is the 30th volume of the Hunter × Hunter manga series. It was released by on April 4th, 2012 in Japan and by on May 7th, 2013 in English. Summary. As Palm and Ikalgo hide Komugi in order to buy time, she tells him that Meruem will be dead in a few hours. It's explained that the Poor Man's Rose is poisonous, infecting victims and causing them to be contagious to others to create a chain of deaths. Shaiapouf begins coughing up blood, and Meruem decides to continue their game, once again using his En and then confronting Welfin among the hypnotized crowd. As Meruem's bloodlust grows, Welfin desperately searches his mind for the answer and finally says Komugi's name aloud, causing the King to remember playing Gungi with her. Meruem spares Pouf and asks Welfin where the other intruders are. Even after Welfin yells out that Gyro is his king and the Chimera Ants are his enemy, Meruem simply walks away and hopes that Welfin can see Gyro again and live as a human. In Bizeff's private hangar, Meruem uses his refined En to locate Palm, assuring her that their side has won and that all he desires is to spend his remaining time with Komugi. After Palm agrees to tell him under the condition that she can watch the two with her ability, Meruem locates the sleeping girl and wakes her up so the two can play again. Outside, Pouf is seen lying dead among the hypnotized crowd. Welfin and Bloster go their separate ways, the latter staying behind in NGL and the former journeying to Meteor City with Hina and Bizeff to find Gyro. Bloster escorts Shidore to a nearby village, and it's revealed that Shidore is Reina. She and her mother have a tearful reunion, and Bloster stays behind as well. Hunter Association airships surround the palace, and as news reports discuss the situation in East Gorteau, the real Ming Jol-ik enjoys a simple life elsewhere. A doctor tells Knuckle and Knov that Gon is in critical condition, and Knov is prepared to do whatever it takes to keep him alive. Killua waits outside his room and wishes that Gon had asked for help even once. He resolves to save Gon, but swears that he will make him apologize. Morel talks with Colt about the child he has been watching. The girl exclaims that her name is Kite, leaving Morel in disbelief. Meruem and Komugi spend their time playing Gungi, and the King reveals that he has been poisoned. Even after being told that it's contagious, Komugi is happy to stay by his side. The two continue playing until their deaths, with Meruem never winning against her. It's explained that East Gorteau and NGL are dismantled after what took place, with the latter being designated as a reserve and put under the Hunter Association's jurisdiction. In a video made public, Netero announces his resignation as Chairman and says that an election (with a required 95% turnout) will be held to decide his successor, adding that the other details will be left up to the Zodiacs. At the Association's headquarters, the twelve Zodiacs have Beans see who will get to decide the rules for the election, and he pulls out Ging's slip (a plan formulated by Ging before the other Zodiacs arrived). Cluck uses her ability to send ballots to the other Hunters, and the voting commences. Illumi informs Hisoka that both Gon and Killua are likely to die, leaving Hisoka concerned and confused. Illumi explains that they have another brother in the Zoldyck Family, and he wants to kill him. Pariston leads the first round of voting, but since the turnout requirement isn't met, a revote is called.

Volume 31 Joining the Fray (, "Sansen") is the 31st volume of the Hunter × Hunter manga series. It was released by on December 4th, 2012 in Japan and by on December 3rd, 2013 in English. Summary. The second round of voting again fails to meet the turnout requirement, and the Zodiacs discuss the situation in detail. Killua returns home and asks his father to let him see Alluka, but Silva stresses that they aren't family and that they came from another place. Killua brings up the situation with Gon and eventually convinces Silva to take him to Alluka, who is able to grant wishes in exchange for fulfilling three of her demands. It's further explained that if one refuses four of her demands in a row, multiple causalities can occur depending on the size of the wish. Illumi and Hisoka discuss the situation, with the former worrying that tens of thousands will die as a result of Killua's wish and asking Hisoka to kill Alluka if they can't get Killua to cooperate with them. Killua is able to take Alluka away from the estate since she has to touch the target to heal it, but he is accompanied by Gotoh, Canary, and Amane, with Tsubone keeping her distance after Alluka makes a demand. As the group journeys to the hospital, the Hunter Association's exorcist says that she is unable to heal Gon. The Zodiacs speak in front of the other Hunters to stress the need for them to vote, and during the session, Leorio asks Ging why he hasn't visited Gon. Ging's answer infuriates Leorio, who uses his ability to punch Ging. The election reaches a 95% turnout, and the next round of voting is narrowed down to the top 16 candidates. Still on their way to the hospital, Killua and the others are forced off the road by Illumi's puppets. Killua seizes his chance and uses Speed of Lightning to head for the hospital, but Tsubone continues to track him. In the forest, Hisoka confronts Gotoh and eventually decapitates the butler. Tsubone transforms into a motorcycle, with Amane and Canary using her to pursue Killua, who makes his way by airship to the hospital. As Illumi uses his needles on innocent civilians, Teradein, Loupe, and Bushidora team up with other Hunters to confront Illumi and those he's manipulating. As the voting is narrowed down to the top 8 candidates, Hisoka and Illumi take out the forces of the new Pure Paladin Squad, with only Loupe and Teradein left alive. Killua is confronted by Illumi and several of his needle people, and even though he is sure that Killua is still leaving out details, Illumi learns that Killua may be able to heal Gon without harming their family. Hisoka kills Teradein as he reports what happened to the Pure Paladin Squad. The voting is narrowed down to the top 4 candidates: Pariston, Leorio, Cheadle, and Mizaistom.

Volume 32 Total Defeat (, "Kanpai") is the 32nd volume of the Hunter × Hunter manga series. It was released by on December 28th, 2012 in Japan and by on April 1st, 2014 in English. Summary. After Ging and Cheadle argue back and forth about the election and Pariston, the remaining four candidates prepare to speak to the crowd. Killua arrives at the makeshift hospital built for Gon and waits for Alluka to wake up. As the candidates give their speeches, Alluka wakes up and Killua has Nanika heal Gon, the effects of which are felt by everyone nearby. The voting is narrowed down to Leorio and Pariston, but a crying Morel suddenly enters the auditorium and lets Leorio know that Gon is okay. Gon enters shortly after, and the two embrace as the crowd applauds Gon's return. As Cheadle confronts Pariston, Gon spots Ging and runs to meet him, blaming himself for what happened to Kite. Ging assures him that it wasn't his fault and tells him to go see Kite and apologize. Gon votes for Pariston since Leorio is studying to be a doctor, and after winning the election, Pariston makes Cheadle his Vice Chairman and immediately resigns. Finally realizing that Killua was able to bypass Alluka's rules because he was giving an order, Illumi confronts his brother and desires to control both him and Alluka. But Killua quickly summons Nanika and sends Illumi back to Kukuroo Mountain. Now alone, Killua orders Nanika to never come out again, but Alluka yells at her brother for making Nanika cry, causing Killua to apologize and summon Nanika again as the two embrace. Koala discusses rebirth with Kite, who orders him to stay by their side as punishment for the rest of his life. Gon then enters and apologizes to Kite, who thanks him and tells him to go be with Ging. Gon learns that his father is waiting for him atop the World Tree, and after apologizing to and parting ways with Killua, he ascends the tree and talks with Ging, who reveals that their world is only a small part of a much bigger one. Although he hopes to journey there, he says that he just wants to enjoy the journey and tells Gon to enjoy the detours. After the two happily talk and part ways, Gon returns to Kite and watches the flight of small-billed swans with him, Kite's companions, and Koala as many of his friends see the spectacle from their computers and phones. At a meeting of the Zodiacs, Beans bursts into the room and shows them a video in which the King of Kakin announces that he plans to expand their empire to the Dark Continent, adding that they have hired Netero's son, Beyond, to lead their expedition. Beyond gives an impassioned speech urging people to make the journey with him. In a city somewhere, Beyond refuses to cooperate with the V5 and tells his team (including Pariston) that he is prepared to destroy anyone that hinders his journey. Before the Zodiacs can watch another video left by Netero, Cheadle announces that Pariston and Ging have requested to leave the Zodiacs (and she approved both). Lastly, she says that they have been contacted by the V5 to hunt down Beyond.

Volume 33 Threats (, "Yakusai") is the 33rd volume of the Hunter × Hunter manga series. It was released by on June 3rd, 2016 in Japan and by on March 7th, 2017 in English. Summary. The IPA director and Steiner discuss the situation with Kakin and the Dark Continent, with the former giving him a book titled "Journey to the New World" which details the Five Threats. From the video message left behind by Netero, the Zodiacs learn that Beyond's previous journey brought back new threats. He had forbidden his son from going there again until after his death, and he then orders the Zodiacs to explore the continent before his son does, telling them to return with hope. Beyond meets with the Zodiacs and allows himself to be put in their custody, confident that they will accompany him to the Dark Continent. Steiner discusses the situation with V5 officials and suggests allowing Kakin to join the organization (to become the V6) and having the Hunter Association supervise Beyond during the journey. Both sides agree to the deal, and the enormous Black Whale ship is made ready to transport up to 200,000 people. Meanwhile, Ging meets up with Beyond's team and asks Pariston to let him join. After Cheadle invites Leorio to join the Zodiacs, Mizaistom meets Kurapika and asks him to come with them to the Dark Continent (at Leorio's request). Initially hostile, Kurapika is convinced when Mizaistom tells him that the owner of a collection of Scarlet Eyes will be aboard the ship: Kakin's Fourth Prince, Tserriednich Hui Guo Rou. Ging ingratiates himself with the members of Beyond's team and tells them that the author of the east edition of "Journey to the New World" is still writing it: a man named Don Freecss. After Gon contacts his father about not being able to use Nen, he returns to Whale Island and Mito overloads him with homework and assignments. Ging continues to work his way into Beyond's team, and Beyond signs the contract that puts him in the custody of the Association during the journey. Leorio and Kurapika join the Zodiacs, and at their first meeting, Kurapika believes that Beyond has allies inside the Association and even a spy among the Zodiacs. Pariston and the others attempt to get Ging to reveal his ability, but their plan fails. As numerous applicants are interviewed during the 289th Hunter Exam, Kurapika uses his Dowsing Chain while in Emperor Time to spot several spies trying to become Provisional Hunters. First Prince Benjamin contacts his brother Tserriednich and tells him that their father has decided that whoever survives the voyage will become the next king. During a meeting of the Zodiacs, Kurapika uses the same method to determine that Saiyu is the informant, eventually learning that he is working with Pariston to break Beyond out of custody. Before boarding the Black Whale, all fourteen Princes take part in the Seed Urn Ceremony and receive a Guardian Spirit Beast that feeds off their aura. After learning that the Princes are hiring bodyguards, Kurapika enlists the help of Biscuit, Basho, Hanzo, Izunavi, and Melody to infiltrate their teams and try to obtain information on Tserriednich. Kurapika thinks that he will be meeting with Halkenburg, but Queen Oito enlists his help to protect Woble, revealing to him that the voyage will be a killing spree until one Prince is left.

Volume 34 Battle to the Death (, "Shitō") is the 34th volume of the Hunter × Hunter manga series. It was released by on June 26th, 2017 in Japan and by on March 6th, 2018 in English. Summary. At Heavens Arena, Hisoka and Chrollo begin a battle to the death, with the latter using multiple abilities to elude and overwhelm his opponent. Chrollo makes copies of the crowd and turns them into suicide bombers, and although Hisoka does his best to fight them off, he is eventually killed. During the aftermath, Machi, Shalnark, and Kortopi arrive to confirm his death. As Machi is left alone with the body, Hisoka suddenly comes back to life using post-mortem Nen and covers up his wounds with Texture Surprise. He immobilizes Machi with Bungee Gum and tells her that he plans to kill every member of the Phantom Troupe. Chrollo calls Shalnark and tells him that they will be making the journey to the New Continent, but soon after Hisoka easily kills both Shalnark and Kortopi. Thousands of passengers board the Black Whale, and Kurapika assesses the situation in detail and gathers more information. As the ship sets sail, some Zodiacs discuss their upcoming plan while others keep watch over Beyond sitting in a cell. Kurapika and the other bodyguards discover Woody drained of his blood, and Kurapika learns that the others may not know about the battle for succession among the Princes. After the Royal Family leaves the inaugural banquet, Kurapika and the others discover four more bodyguards drained of their blood. He uses his Dowsing Chain to question them, learning that most are working for higher-ranking Queens and that the battle for succession will be fought among the Princes themselves. As they begin to discuss the Seed Urn Ceremony and parasitic Nen, several Nen beasts suddenly invade the room and Kurapika issues an emergency call. One of the bodyguards, Sayird, is manipulated by a Nen beast and forced to kill two bodyguards with a knife. He begins charging toward Kurapika, who prepares to subdue the threat. Extras. Chrollo vs. Hisoka: A Commentary

Volume 35 Ship of Fools (, "Nenjū"—lit. "Nen Beast") is the 35th volume of the Hunter × Hunter manga series. It was released by on February 2nd, 2018 in Japan and by on March 5th, 2019 in English. Summary. After Kurapika easily disarms Sayird and uses Steal Chain to borrow his ability, the Royal Army arrives to clean up the scene, leaving Oito and Woble with only two bodyguards. Before leaving the banquet, Halkenburg tells his father that he wishes to withdraw from the succession battle. The King sees the Guardian Spirit Beasts of his children, explaining that they neither kill one another nor attack those who have them. After hearing Kurapika's emergency call, many of the Princes are interested in the concept of Nen and Nen beasts. Benjamin argues with Camilla in front of his father, and initially decides to begin killing his siblings, but Balsamilco calms him down and convinces him to use his soldiers to observe the other Princes, who are told to use lethal force if they have to defend themselves. One of these soldiers, Vincent, kills Sandra and confronts Kurapika and Bill, who subdue him before he can harm anyone else. After Vincent commits suicide, Benjamin sends Babimyna as his replacement. Kurapika transfers Sayird's ability to Oito and plans to have her use it in order to gather information on the other Princes. It's revealed that every second Kurapika has Emperor Time activated, he loses one hour of his life. Shortly afterwards, Zhang Lei invites Kurapika and Oito to a meeting so that he can learn more about Nen. Four hours into the voyage, the actions of all the Princes are shown, and in the bottom tier of the Black Whale, a distraught Chrollo is seen among the crowd of people. While teaching Zhang Lei's guards about Nen, Kurapika has Oito use Sayird's ability on a roach, planning to use the insect to spy on the other Princes. But when Oito checks on Momoze, she finds the Prince being strangled by an unknown guard. Kurapika falls unconscious from the strain of using Emperor Time, and Hanzo resolves to avenge Momoze's death. Theta continues teaching Nen to Tserriednich, although the Prince begins to question how truthful she is being. Kurapika wakes up after nine hours and realizes that he has had Emperor Time activated for 12 hours (meaning that roughly five years have been taken off his lifespan). He convinces Oito to continue using Sayird's ability, but when she goes to observe Tserriednich's quarters, his Guardian Spirit Beast appears in the air duct and eats the bug. Several Princes send their bodyguards and servants to learn Nen from Kurapika in the promised two-week time frame. During the lesson, someone uses an ability called Silent Majority and has four snakes attack Barrigen to drain him of his blood (the same attack that killed Woody and the others), shifting Kurapika's focus to finding the assassin among the group.

Volume 36 Balance (, "Baransu") is the 36th volume of the Hunter × Hunter manga series. It was released by on October 4th, 2018 in Japan and by on August 6th, 2019 in English. Summary. After Loberry is arrested as a suspect for Barrigen's murder and an investigator is sent to monitor Kacho's quarters, Kurapika convinces the remaining students to stay and continues with the Nen training. On Tier 5, several Phantom Troupe members confront the Buor Family and learn about the other Mafia families, hoping to find a way up to the higher tiers as they continue their search for Hisoka. In a large room filled with fourteen coffins surrounding a chamber in the middle, Nasubi stands beside the deceased Momoze and declares that she will become the foundation for the tree of Kakin. Using his Hanzo Skill 4 to create a doppelganger, Hanzo tracks down and kills the bodyguard that killed Momoze. After the first lesson, Kurapika talks with Zhang Lei's and Halkenburg's bodyguards, trying his best to form an alliance with them. Camilla confronts Musse, one of Benjamin's soldiers, and causes him to shoot her. Her ability, however, takes Musse's life and uses it to revive the Prince. Camilla then confronts Benjamin, but she is quickly restrained and put into a cell, with Benjamin using his Benjamin Baton to continue using Musse's Secret Window to spy on Camilla. Unable to find his body or anyone in Room 1013, Hanzo goes to Kurapika for help, and after a heated conversation with Vergei, Kurapika learns that the ability of Marayam's Guardian Spirit Beast is most likely the cause of the hidden Nen space. The abilities of the other Princes' Guardian Spirit Beasts are revealed, with one of Benjamin's soldiers witnessing the power of Halkenburg's, who plans to appeal to his father in order to end the succession battle. In Room 1013, Vergei continues to be skeptical about Nen, but Biscuit reveals her true form and leaves him in disbelief at her beauty, and she agrees to teach Nen to everyone there. As Benjamin and Camilla are put under surveillance until Musse's body is found, Silent Majority strikes again at Kurapika's Nen class, killing Myuhan. Kacho, Fugetsu, and Melody begin working together to find a way to escape, planning to make their move at the Sunday banquet. Theta allows Tserriednich to take the Water Divination test, discovering that he's a Specialist. All current members of the Phantom Troupe gather together, and the newest member, Illumi Zoldyck, reveals that he joined on Hisoka's commission and that Hisoka hired Illumi to kill him. The Spiders go their separate ways to look for Hisoka, with Bonolenov and Shizuku teaming up with Chrollo. While the Xi-Yu and Cha-R Families decide to find Hisoka before the Spiders do, the boss of the Heil-Ly Family, Morena Prudo, uses her ability on her subordinates, encouraging them to kill civilians, Nen users, and Princes. After recovering their weapons from a storage room, Phinks, Nobunaga, and Feitan begin working with the Cha-R Family to eliminate the hitman who has been killing their men. Mizaistom briefs the Royal Army on the killings in the lower tiers and advises moving more troops there, but worries that he's only delaying the inevitable. During their search for the murderer, Mizaistom finds Illumi and Kalluto on Tier 3, learning that all the Spiders are on board and wondering if he should tell Kurapika. He suddenly receives an urgent message and discovers that Fugetsu is on Tier 3.

Osu! Training Osu! Training (押忍！修行っす, "Osu! Shugyōssu") is a character song from the 2011 Hunter × Hunter anime adaptation, performed by as Zushi and featuring as Wing. The song was released on 08/22/2012 on the album .

Otocin Otocin (オトシン, "Otoshin") is a private second class in the Royal Army of the Kakin Empire. Appearance. Otocin has dark eyes, light-colored hair parted to his left, and prominent eyebrows. He wears the standard attire of a Kakin soldier. Personality. Otocin is talkative, playful, and observant. He is quick to ask questions, especially when he has a plan in mind. He has the closest relationship with Tserriednich, shortening his name to "Tserried" and "Tserri" and even referring to him as a "punk". According to Momolly, he is the only person who can talk back to the Prince without getting shot. Plot. Succession Contest arc. After breaking into the Heil-Ly's office with the other soldiers, Gipper emphasizes the importance of capturing Morena Prudo before the situation reaches that point, adding that they should hand her over to Tserriednich before he has to trouble himself with it. He tells his subordinates that while they can sweep Tier 3 with the help of the Xi-Yu and Cha-R, they don’t want to draw attention from the Royal Army and police, ordering them to carry only handguns during the search. Otocin speaks up and asks about creating a counterstrategy if the Heil-Ly have any Nen users among them. Gipper is left confused by the term, and Otocin explains that it's a dangerous power spreading quickly on Tier 1, guessing that it's the reason why "Tserried" hasn't handled the situation on Tier 3. Gipper wonders who reported the information to a private second class, and Otocin reveals that they learned about it from Borksen, a provisional Hunter on security detail at the royal living quarters. Gipper recognizes them as a private first class and says that he will request for her to be transferred to Tier 3 as an advisor. Gipper then threatens to rip out Otocin's eyes if he ever abbreviates Tserriednich's name again. He warns him that he will put him on the front line against Nen users, and Otocin quickly addresses him as sir. Momolly can't believe that Otocin would involve Bork in the situation, but Otocin replies that her information will be crucial, explaining that Morena wouldn't pick a fight with "Tserri" if she didn't have a plan. Momolly points out that Otocin did just that against Gipper, but Otocin replies that it was calculated since he was able to get Bork transferred. Gipper then threatens to shoot Otocin if he doesn't be quiet, and Otocin quickly addresses him as sir again. After further discussion, Otocin wonders why Gipper isn't yelling at the other soldiers for constantly talking. Gipper replies that they are actually smart and that he agrees with their opinion, again saying that they need to find Morena as soon as possible. Momolly, however, says that Otocin has a point. Otocin is shocked and asks if he can kiss her, but after telling him to die, Momolly points out that Tserriednich has remained silent despite Morena's rebellion, confident that he would only delay exacting revenge against a traitor if he has found a new toy. Gipper guesses that she's referring to the story about Tserriednich's firearm disassembly and reassembly drill in seventh grade, saying that he heard the Prince broke the academy's record after practicing without eating or sleeping. Otocin clarifies that Tserriednich said he was "playing", not practicing, also calling him a punk. Otocin eventually criticizes Tserriednich's short temper and recounts the other classmate's words to Tserriednich about accomplishing something first. Momolly replies that logic doesn't work on the Prince and tells Otocin that he is probably the only one who can talk back to him without getting shot. Later, as the soldiers think about Tserriednich, Otocin says to himself that their friendship seems to take a back seat the closer they get to him, adding that he prefers to stay at the bottom and loudly ask Tserriednich if it's really what he wants. A flashback is then shown with Tserriednich holding a gun after having shot his classmate in the leg. After meeting up with the five soldiers, Borksen explains that Tserriednich is learning Nen from Theta, his personal bodyguard, warning that they will be instantly demoted if they leak the top-secret information. Otocin wonders about Nen, but Borksen herself is unaware of it since it's classified, adding that she was planning to investigate it before being transferred. Otocin asks if she's upset, and Borksen confirms it with a smile on her face, chastising him for revealing the information to Corporal Gipper. Otocin replies that they needed to know the details and adds that they were able to propose the transfer request early warning system. Borksen calls him naive and says that Gipper wouldn't agree to switch now that he's moved up, guessing that he's using her as a pretext to restrict communications with soldiers in the lower tiers in order to prevent information leaks. Later, Borksen explains that while she doesn't know the details, she could tell from Theta and Salkov's reactions that Nen is comparable to a top-secret weapon. Otocin quickly reminds them that he said it was more dangerous than a gun, but Momolly replies that Borksen's words carry more weight. Otocin is present with the other soldiers at the meeting with the Xi-Yu and Cha-R.

Overture Holding Hands~Listen, My Companions Overture Holding Hands~Listen, My Companions (オーヴァーチュア;手をつないで~聞け、同胞よ, "Ouverture; te wo tsunaide ~ kike, harakarayo") is the first song from the Musical Hunter × Hunter sung by Madam Isabel's actress, Yuu Daiki.

Owl Owl (, "Fukurō"—lit. "") is one of the most valuable members of the Mafia Community and a member of the Shadow Beasts, the elite guard of the Ten Dons. Appearance. Like almost all members of the Shadow Beasts, Owl resembles the animal that inspired his codename. He has large, piercing eyes which often remain hidden behind a large pair of sunglasses (even at night). Together with a large shirt and sandals, Owl appears very laid back. He also has dark hair framing his face and a short beard on his chin. Personality. Owl never seems to worry too much about what's happening around him, but in more serious situations he makes sure to stay on his guard. Plot. Yorknew City arc. After the massacre inside the Cemetery Building and as the Phantom Troupe members make their escape, Uvogin calls Chrollo and tells him that the vault was already empty. He adds that the auctioneer told them that the items were relocated a few hours ago by one of the Shadow Beasts named Owl, who used no tools, left holding nothing, and somehow emptied the 25 m2 vault. Chrollo guesses that Owl has a similar Nen ability to Shizuku's, and Uvogin agrees with him. After Uvogin is captured by Kurapika and the other Nostrade bodyguards in the Gordeau Desert, the members of the Phantom Troupe pursue them. Out of nowhere, Owl suddenly jumps on the hood of their car and uses his Fun Fun Cloth ability to envelop it. Four of the Troupe members are able to escape being caught, but Nobunaga is trapped by the ability and shrunk down inside the cloth as he wonders what's going on and orders Owl to let him out. As Owl holds the tiny cloth in his hand, he looks at the four Troupe members and realizes that he can't underestimate them since they were able to reach quickly enough to escape his trap, telling himself that he needs to stay cautious. Feitan points out that Nobunaga had a bad position inside the car, and Machi describes Owl's ability as the ultimate accessory for stealing. Shalnark guesses that he was able to carry all the auction items in his pocket and that he can return them to their original size. After the five remaining Shadow Beasts, Feitan readies his aura and says that they need to ask them if the chain user is part of their group. Although the other Shadow Beasts are all killed, Owl is kept alive and brought back to the Troupe's hideout where he is seen sitting in a chair with his hands restrained and a sack over his head (with some blood on the sack and his shirt). His torturer Feitan sits calmly nearby reading a book.
