After the accident, Killua had to tell his parents about Alluka's secret because Mitsuba had already reported it to them. It turned out that when Alluka had three requests fulfilled, her eyes and mouth would turn pitch-black, and they would change back to normal only when she heard and granted a wish. To test the ability, her mother Kikyo ordered Mitsuba to decline any request from her, no matter how small it was. Due to that, Mitsuba and her lover Hassam, who was not around Alluka then, were simultaneously mysteriously crushed into minced meat. Killua explained that this resulted from saying 'No' to Alluka's requests four times. Some time afterward, Yasuha, another female servant of the Zoldyck Family, gave Alluka a piggyback ride at her request, thus activating her wish-granting mode. Giving in to her greed at the time, Yasuha wished that Alluka would make her a billionaire. Nanika agreed, and suddenly, many banknotes started to rain down from a blimp in the sky. It was later reported that a currency transport vessel had suddenly gone missing, and by the time it had been found, all the money had disappeared, and the captain and crew kept giving nonsensical answers. Illumi became interested in Alluka's power and asked for Silva's permission to deal with Kasuga, the next servant, to take care of Alluka in his way. He told her to listen to Alluka's requests in exchange for his tolerance of her romantic relationship with an outsider to the Zoldyck Family. When Kasuga was with Alluka, Alluka suddenly asked her for her liver, which Kasuga declined. She followed up with three continuous requests for her duodenum, spine, and brain, respectively, which were also declined. As a result of Kasuga's refusal to fulfill those four requests, 67 people, including herself, were killed simultaneously by Alluka's strange power. This occurrence revealed that her ability had a cumulative effect; the greater the last wish was (in terms of fulfillment difficulty), the greater the consequences of refusing her next set of requests. From this, they also learned the requests became much more difficult to fulfill after Nanika granted a large wish. Following the blimp incident, Nanika's power caused the death of six couples, for a total of twelve more people: two were necessary for Kikyo to be convinced, two more to test the rules, and two when Milluki sacrificed tourists in exchange for cheap toys. At some point, another big incident also resulted in the death of 13 people, caused again by Milluki, who asked Nanika to kill his target for him. Milluki had a tourist named Muna pay the price by telling him to ignore Alluka's requests. More recently, Milluki used Nanika to get the latest—at the time—computer. Plot. 13th Hunter Chairman Election arc. Killua returns home on Kukuroo Mountain to see his younger sister and asks for his father's permission. Still, Silva disagrees, thinking that it's too dangerous because no one can keep Alluka in check as "it" is a non-human entity, something from another place, that came out of the "darkness"; meanwhile, Alluka sits unemotionally on the floor of a room full of dolls. After a long talk, his father takes him to Alluka's room, hidden behind a series of five big safety vaults, each of which can only be opened after entering a 10-digit password. Alluka excitedly greets Killua when he enters the room, calling him "Big brother". She first wished for Killua to "die" for her. Next, she wanted to play and, lastly, have Killua pat her on the head. Silva, Kikyo, and Milluki watch the whole scene through a surveillance camera. Kikyo is delighted with Killua's actions, while Milluki regrets wishing for a PC which made Alluka's wishes for Killua so easy. This earns him a glare from his father. Silva then asks about the rules regarding Alluka's power. When Killua takes Alluka with him, Silva disapproves and insists that the wish be made inside the room. Killua wishes to tell Alluka that their mother will be killed if they cannot leave the mountain together within 30 minutes. If they are, then she will kiss Killua on the cheek. Silva lets them leave, but orders a few butlers to accompany them, including Gotoh, Canary, Tsubone, and Amane. As they make their way to the hospital where Gon is, a truck whose drivers were being manipulated by Illumi crashes their car. Killua protects Alluka; according to the restriction rules that their father laid down, they will be taken home instantly if Killua stays at least one meter away from Alluka. As Illumi and Hisoka watch from afar, the assassin asks the latter to eliminate the butlers or, if possible, take Alluka away from Killua. Using his Godspeed ability, Killua escapes their butlers with ease, but Tsubone follows them. Killua and Alluka continue to escape and are still followed by Tsubone. Killua tries to escape faster, but Tsubone uses her ability to catch up to Speed of Lightning's velocity. The two Zoldycks reach the airport and ride in an airship to escape Illumi further. Alluka is seen sleeping inside while Killua drives the airship himself. He explains to Morel about Alluka's wish-granting ability, which Morel thinks is a vaguely terrifying ability. When the airship they were riding on finally landed, Killua made arrangements to continue their escape by car, only to find themselves surrounded by Illumi and his Needle People. There, Illumi asks for Alluka to be handed over to him while Killua straightly refuses. In the middle, Tsubone appears and reveals that it is her fault that they are tailed through a hidden camera being fed to their Kikyo and Milluki, where the latter, in turn, is sending the information to Illumi's phone. After seeing Tsubone, Alluka's request mode commences again when she asks for the nails from Tsubone's middle and ring finger, completing the three requests and entering her wish-granting state. Instead of using the wish to get out of their predicament, Killua uses the wish to heal Tsubone's hand to demonstrate and reveal to Illumi some rules that he only knows. Finally, Alluka walks into Gon's hospital room. Killua asks his sibling to turn into Nanika, but Alluka refuses, wanting to stay with Killua. When Killua begs her, she eventually gives in and changes into Nanika. Killua asks Nanika to heal Gon, and Nanika complies and touches Gon's hand. As Nanika is healing Gon, an enormous amount of aura is released, which is so powerful that Hunters in the Hunter Association building feel it. Alluka successfully heals Gon and falls asleep. Illumi tells Killua that if he can control Alluka as Killua does, he will guarantee minimum freedom for Alluka. However, Killua wakes Nanika and orders her to send Illumi home, which Nanika does, and Illumi finds himself instantly teleported back to the Zoldyck mansion. Due to Killua's request, Amane and Tsubone leave the room to give the siblings privacy. Killua tells Nanika that she can't come out anymore. Nanika disagrees and is upset by Killua saying how much she likes Killua. After a brief argument that leads Killua to yell at her, she becomes upset but complies, returning inside. Alluka wakes up and is angered by what Killua said to Nanika. She yells at Killua, saying that he needs to protect both Alluka and Nanika and that Alluka would hate any brother who was mean to Nanika. Killua realizes his mistake and asks Alluka to bring Nanika out so he can apologize. Nanika reappears teary and upset from the previous confrontation. Not long after, Alluka and Killua accompany Gon on his trip to the World Tree. There, they say their goodbyes and part ways with Gon. Gender And Pronoun Context. Throughout the series, different characters refer to Alluka with different pronouns, giving conflicting information about her gender. Alluka is primarily referred to and exclusively uses feminine terms and pronouns throughout the series, though. For instance, Killua introduces Alluka to Gon as his sister, Killua stated that Alluka being a girl was the reason they needed female butlers to attend to her on their mission to save Gon, and Killua refers to Alluka as his sister multiple times, including when they were children. Additionally, "Alluka" (アルカ or あるか, Aruka) is a traditionally female given name. In accordance with Alluka’s gender identity and expression, this article uses feminine pronouns in reference to her, and this page is placed in the female characters category. Abilities & Powers. Unlike her brothers, Alluka has no combat abilities at all. She is like a normal kid regarding fighting and physical endurance. However, due to being Nanika's host, her own relatives fear her ability to wipe out the family instantly. Alluka shares an empathic link with Nanika, which allows her to perceive its emotions. Nen. "See also: Nanika's Ability" Alluka is a Specialist, but she has no Nen skills or Nen abilities of her own and only acts as a medium so Nanika can use its wish-granting powers. It is unclear whether these powers are aura-based, and thus presumably Nen-related, or if they are a separate type of ability.

Altar of Dragon Vein (Location) Altar of Dragon Vein (龍脈の祭壇, "Ryūmyaku no Saidan") is a location in the country of Midonite that only appears in the game. Overview. An altar made by ancient civilizations to hold the Earth's aura, or a Dragon Vein. They act as aura amplifiers. In order to take the aura power within, a Nen user must be sacrificed in close proximity to the vein itself. There, they will then take the Earth's aura for themselves. If the respective Dragon Vein is destroyed, the altar will collapse. According to Zegin, there are multiple Dragon Veins in the world. This could imply multiple altars exist. For the altar in the game's story, it is a square room surrounded by waterfalls. The walls and center platform appear to be made of concrete. At the center is the Dragon Vein atop a small pedestal. Plot. "Altar of Dragon Vein". After unlocking the entrance at the Forest Ruins, Zegin heads for the altar itself. He then awaits for Sabaki and Amane to appear. However, only Sabaki appears. The duo proceeds to talk about their current circumstances. However, when Sabaki lies about Amane's whereabouts, Zegin calls him out for this, knowing he betrayed them both. At this, Sabaki reveals his true intentions to Zegin. He then attempts to kill him. However, he survives. This is because the nearby Dragon Vein replenishes him with the Earth's aura. Zegin then proceeds to knock Sabaki unconscious. Once the Hunter group arrives, Zegin preaches to them regarding his motives. A fight then breaks out. However, as Zegin heals himself with Dragon Vein, Sabaki briefly awakens. Sabaki proceeds to destroy the Dragon Vein permanently before being knocked out. This allows for the Hunter group to put an end to Zegin once and for all properly. As his body lands on the ground, the altar begins to collapse. Thus, the group escapes whilst carrying Sabaki.

Amami Herb The Amami Herb (アマミ草, "Amami Kusa")‎‎ is a type of medicinal herb. Overview. The Amami Herb is one of the four herbs that Ponzu requests for, in her sidequest. Item Description. It is called by this name because its large leaves face the heavens. Plot. Altar of Dragon Vein. Ponzu asks the Hunter group for four different kinds of herbs and when they manage to retrieve them, she thanks them and joins their group.

Amana Amana (アマナ, "Amana") was a player of the game Greed Island. She was also a member of Team Asta and a member of Kazsule's Alliance. Appearance. Amana wore a long sleeveless dress and had her long hair parted over her left eye. Personality. Amana was quiet as well as observant, and quick at deducing conditions to acquire certain cards within the game. Background. Amana and her other teammates were fairly advanced in the game, as they collected 71 specified slot cards by the time they decided to cooperate with Gon and Killua. Plot. Greed Island arc. Amana, a member of Team Asta, attends a meeting of fifteen players arranged by Kazsule in order to stop the Bombers from clearing the game. As the meeting escalates, Asta gets into a heated argument with a member of Gon's team, Killua. Amana and her team member Manheim stop the argument by offering two S-rank cards in exchange for information on the Bomber's abilities. When it's decided that the newly-formed alliance will look for "Plot of Beach", Amana uses a "Guidepost" card to learn that it's in Soufrabi. The group then uses an "Accompany" card to travel there. Arriving at Soufrabi, Kazsule instructs them on how to acquire an SS-rank card, and the alliance members split up into small teams to go around the town to acquire information on the "Plot of Beach" card. A female NPC informs them that Razor and his fourteen devils, a group of pirates, rule over the city. She promises to tell them where the card is if they drive the pirates out of the town. Amana deduces that the NPC is only giving this information now because of certain conditions that were met (fifteen players traveling to the town with an "Accompany" card). The alliance members then make their way to the pirates' base in the town and are challenged by the pirate Bopobo to a sumo match. Killua manages to beat him, and the group is led to the pirates' lighthouse base, where they are challenged to a series of sports trials, but they fail them all. Seeing that there's no possible way for the Bombers to collect the "Plot of Beach" card, Asta convinces most of the others to leave the alliance. Amana's name is mentioned in Gon's binder. After Gon and his group successfully defeat Razor and collect the rare card, they are contacted by Genthru, who mentions that Amana and the rest of the alliance members are dead. Abilities & Powers. Gon's team estimated her to be too weak to defeat Razor's convicts, as turned out to be the case. Amana was also unable to see the pirate boxer's teleporting uppercut. Nen. Due to being able to access Greed Island, Amana was capable of utilizing Nen.

Amane Amane (アマネ, "Amane") is a female servant of the Zoldyck Family. She, along with her grandmother Tsubone, are ordered by Silva Zoldyck to accompany Killua Zoldyck and Alluka Zoldyck on their trip to save Gon Freecss. Appearance. Like the other servants of the Zoldyck Family, Amane wears a male black formal suit and tie. She has a flat nose and long black hair that is combed backward, leaving two hair strands hanging down over her forehead. Personality. Amane is loyal to Silva and will not hesitate to execute his orders. She is not as good at concealing her emotions as her grandmother, as shown when Gotoh mentions Illumi's name. Her professional, impassible demeanor is occasionally interspersed with moments of haughtiness. Nonetheless, Canary succeeded in making her snap and behave frantically, noting that she was cuter when she loosened up, her sincerity leaving Amane baffled and embarrassed. Plot. 13th Hunter Chairman Election arc. Silva tasks Amane and her grandmother Tsubone with accompanying and monitoring Killua in his endeavor to save his friend Gon with Nanika's powers. She is ordered to seize Alluka immediately if Killua moves more than one meter away from her. She introduces herself to Canary with an air of disdain. After Tsubone goes into hiding right after granting Alluka's first request, Amane rides in a limousine with Killua, Alluka, and Gotoh. She fails to hide her anxiety when Gotoh greets Illumi over the phone, allowing Killua to determine that his brother's agenda clashes with his father and grandfather's, and that he wants to kill Alluka. As soon as Killua challenges him, Illumi has three vehicles driven by manipulated individuals crash into his car and knock it off the mountain road into a forest. The occupants survive unscathed and become aware of Illumi's position thanks to Hisoka triggering his bloodlust. Amane recommends changing their course and the group begins to run through the woods. Killua declares himself suspicious of her, so she responds that she and her grandmother are not his enemies, neither are Silva and Zeno, as they instructed them to protect him. Killua stops abruptly, and, after declaring that they will be his enemies as long as Alluka's protection is not one of their concerns, activates Speed of Lightning and disappears into the woods with Alluka. The three butlers begin to give chase, but soon run into Hisoka. Amane prepares to intercept his attack, but Gotoh deflects it and tells her and Canary to keep following Killua while he deals with the magician. After being updated on Killua's direction by her grandmother, Amane and Canary quickly catch up to him by riding Tsubone's motorcycle form, but they lose him when he jumps back into the woods. Tsubone questions the two on what his next move might be. Amane first suggests a disguise, but, with her grandmother's hints, realizes his destination is likely Parasta's airport. The three butlers head him off there, with Tsubone going back into hiding. Amane books an airship, but Killua protests that they will need at least five or six others to shake Illumi off. While Amane books six more airships and Canary feigns incompetence to distract her, Killua slips away with Alluka, causing Amane to become angry with Canary, who merely replies she looks cute when she loosens up and that Killua would like her better like that. They then split up and while Canary boards one of the decoy airships, Amane follows Killua's from the ground with her grandmother, who turns into a glider and instructs her to shoot down any suspicious flying objects. After landing, Killua immediately finds himself surrounded by Illumi and his Needle People. Tsubone and Amane come out into the open and the former offers to pay the consequences for Killua's wish together with her granddaughter, who becomes anxious. Everyone is shocked when Killua asks Nanika to heal Tsubone's hand, explaining that there needs to be physical contact for Nanika to fix something, and claiming that healing wishes have no backlash. Illumi withdraws and Amane drives Killua to the hospital where Gon is. When she gets there, she and her grandmother watch over Killua as he waits for Alluka to wake up so he can restore his friend. The tremendous power unleashed by Nanika while healing Gon causes Amane to lose her composure. When, after Gon and his friends leave, Illumi arrives at the hospital, Amane is visibly upset by his proposition to manipulate both Killua and Alluka. At Killua's request, she and her grandmother leave him alone while he talks to Nanika. She is later seen paying respects to the recently deceased Gotoh and is surprised when she sees Gotoh walk up behind her. Amane questions how this is possible, and Canary explains that a Kiriko was hired to impersonate the butler to keep Killua from realizing he had been killed trying to protect him. Abilities & Powers. As a butler of the Zoldyck family and one of Silva's two most trusted employees, the other being her grandmother, Amane is an expert fighter and a resourceful servant. She has a superhuman degree of durability, surviving a car crash engineered by Illumi. In the anime, she displayed enhanced strength, speed, and combat proficiency. Her peculiar fighting stance may suggest that she is a practitioner of some form of unarmed combat if it is not related to her Nen abilities. Enhanced Strength: Amane was strong enough to bend iron bars with a kick at high speed casually. As a butler of the Zoldycks, she is also able to open the Testing Gates, although the number of doors she can open is unknown. Enhanced Speed and Reflexes: Amane is fast enough to keep up with Killua, Canary, and Gotoh, though she is slower than Tsubone. She can nonetheless steer her in her motorcycle form on a winding road despite the tremendous speed reached, which easily dwarfs Killua's Speed of Lightning. Enhanced Agility: Amane can quickly leap to the top of a tree. Skilled Driver: Amane is capable of driving cars as well as motorcycles, gliders, whose weapons she also knows how to operate, and presumably all other vehicles Tsubone can transform into. Nen. Although Amane has not shown any Nen abilities of her own, she knows about the existence of aura, which she fueled Tsubone with (in her motorcycle form). She has enough of it to fly Tsubone's glider form for several minutes, if not hours. Since her arrival seems to have surprised Killua, it is possible that Amane is a skilled Zetsu user.

Amane (Video game) Amane (アマネ, "Amane") was an associate of Zegin Highline who sought to gain entry into a locked ruin to acquire the Dragon Vein from within. He only appears in the video game . Appearance. Amane is a tall, slim man with a prominent chin and round head shape. He has thin hazel eyes, violet hair, and very sharp eyebrows. He sports what appears to be a red-pink tuxedo over a white long-sleeved dress shirt that is cuffed at the wrists. Personality. Amane appears to be quite sadistic and selfish, showing no hesitation to manipulate Kurapika as he sees fit. He also seems to be very undisciplined and not very hard working, showcasing this when he steals the ring from Killua and Leorio after they put effort into locating and attempting to retrieve it. Background. Amane was an Amateur Hunter who had done various business transactions within the Black Market. He purchased a fake Scarlet Eye pendant from there. He would eventually become allies with Zegin. Prior to the game events, Kurapika began seeking out Amane for his Scarlet Eye necklace. The two would then engage in battle. From this, Kurapika would accidentally let his guard down and be put under hypnosis. Plot. "Altar of Dragon Vein". Amane, along with a mind-controlled Kurapika, arrives at the ruins where Killua and Leorio are, who are attempting to retrieve the ring and bring it to Romaria as it might hold some clues or other forms of value. Amane has other plans, though, and commands Kurapika to retrieve the ring before Killua and Leorio can do so themselves. Kurapika successfully grabs the ring and hands it over to Amane. The two attempt to leave the ruins shortly after, but Killua and Leorio chase after them and persist that they hand the ring over. Amane proposes a dual, so he controls Kurapika to square off against the two. After the battle, he leaves with the ring in tow. Amane is seen once again at Zegin's Mansion. Here, he accompanies both Zegin and Sabaki. The trio then drive off to find the second ring. During the second visit to the Crystal Caves, Amane awaits the Hunter group. To distract them from Zegin's attack on the airship, he uses his ability to control one of the group members. He then forces them to fight him once again, but Amane is soon wounded. Sabaki then appears. He proceeds to knock Amane unconscious from him being a liability. Sometime before Zegin's demise, Amane awakens. He then finds his body in the altar's rubble and turns him into his puppet. While the Hunter group searches inside Zegin's mansion once again, they find the duo. Amane reveals he has the remaining Goddess Advent Card to them, and had been searching for them prior to the Dragon Vein's destruction. Furthermore, he plans on adding Zegin to his private collection of mind-controlled soldiers. He then manipulates Zegin to attack. After the long battle, Amane is finally defeated. He laughs to himself on wanting the Hunter group for his collection. With his last breath, he controls Zegin to use his remaining aura to kill everyone in the room, only for Sabaki to kill Zegin. Abilities & Powers. Nen. Amane was a Manipulator. The only Nen technique he showed was Hatsu. Amane's Nen ability, Trembling Melody, was a coercive type of mind control achieved through the sound of a bell he carried.

Amateur Hunters The Amateur Hunters are a group of aspiring Hunters led and mentored by Kite. The group is hired by the Kakin Empire on the Azian Continent to conduct a biological survey. Background. Little is known about when Kite met each member of the group, but one said that they have been with the group for three years. Unsurprisingly, Kite has spent more time with them than Gon. Kite also seems to have the closest connection with Spin and Stick, since he financed the purchase of their home so that they could protect the Small-billed Swan. It can also be deduced that other members of the group were with Spin and Stick since the former mentioned that Kite was the first adult who listened to a "bunch of kids" with nothing to their names. Although Kite called the group's members excellent "hunters", it’s unlikely that any of them have passed the Hunter Exam and possess a Hunter License. Gon also asked Spin why she wants to be a Hunter. None of the group's members are Nen users. Plot. Chimera Ant arc. After meeting Gon and Killua in a forest in the Kakin Empire, Kite explains to them that he was hired by the country to conduct ecological research of new species. He reveals that he has six others with him, calling them amateurs but excellent hunters. The six individuals arrive right on cue and wonder who the two kids are. Kite explains that they are his friends who stopped by during their travels. One member of the group introduces herself as Spinner Clow, telling them that they can call her Spin. When Gon introduces himself using his full name, Spin is taken aback by his last name, and Kite confirms that he is Ging's son, surprising the others as well. Killua then introduces himself, and two members pick up on his last name, asking if he belongs to the family of famous assassins. Killua confirms this but adds that he quit the business. Kite reveals that both boys are professional Hunters and that they can learn a lot from them, leaving Kite's group stunned. The group of nine then sits around a table of food, and the remaining members of Kite's group introduce themselves. A man named Monta Yuras tells them to call him Mon. A boy named Lin Koshi is glad to meet them. A man named Stick Dinner explains that he is in charge of cooking, playfully pointing out the connection to his name. A girl named Banana Kavaro is also glad to meet them. And finally, a girl named Podungo Lapoy introduces herself. Kite asks them about the Camp Tigers, and they reply that they were able to capture amazing footage, wondering what they should do now since they finished earlier than planned. Kite replies that they have another month until their contract ends, and Mon suggests that they keep working and focus on small creatures. Stick quickly agrees, and Lin points out that discovering seven more species will double the quota on the contract, with Spin agreeing that it would be a good place to stop. As Gon and Killua look eager to help, Kite asks the two if they want to work with them, and they excitedly ask if they can. Kite explains that they simply need to use the camera to take a digital picture of anything unusual and that it will automatically compare it to the database so that they can know if it's a new species. He reveals that Lin has discovered the most with more than 1,000 in three years, and Lin points out that the exact number is 1,019. Another member playfully adds that Kite is last with only 68. Kite explains that he works with large mammals and isn't good at finding small bugs. Banana adds that the Camp Tiger was the biggest discovery of their trip, and Killua wonders what the creature is. Spin reveals that they make use of fire, and Banana adds that it's the first discovery of a non-magical beast that prefers cooked meat to raw. They then show Gon and Killua footage of the tigers roasting prey that they caught with their large horns, with Podungo pointing out that their horns are retractable. Later that night, Spin and Stick are impressed by how many new and rare species Gon and Killua are finding, with Stick praising their intuition, luck, and observational skills. Kite tells himself that while his group relies on experience and knowledge, Gon and Killua use their five senses to notice things that most people would pass over, calling it a method only possible for professionals who know how to use aura. The group delivers their findings to Mr. Wong, who excitedly says that it's worth 200 years of their own research. He apologizes for not being able to pay them a bonus, but promises to recommend them to the ministries of other countries. He then tells them about a segment of a strange creature that was acquired by the Southernpiece Auction House, adding that they can't list it since it could be unregistered and cause legal issues. He then reveals that they would prefer to sell it to a licensed Hunter than have it taken by a bureaucrat. The group travels to Yorknew City and makes their way to the auction house, eventually reaching the segment mentioned by Wong. Kite asks Lin what he thinks, and he replies that it's clearly from a previously unregistered species and that while it looks like an insect leg, there has never been any insect with a leg so large. Spin points out that the claws are also different from other insects, and Banana adds that they usually have two while this one has six. After the group discusses the specimen further, Podungo suggests taking a sample back to find out more, and Kite asks the auction official if they can have a small piece. The man replies that he cannot refuse someone recommended by Mr. Wong and gives them two samples after asking them to let the auction house know if they ever find an Albino Ponytail Cat. While Podungo and Mon plan to examine the samples and call them when they get the results, Kite and the others leave to interview the man who found the leg. Killua asks Kite where it was found, and he replies that it was south of Yorknew, suggesting that they go by land since the weather has been unstable lately. The group travels by truck and eventually finds the man, who tells them that it was on a nearby beach just floating near the water's edge. As the group searches the shoreline, Killua notes the thick forest behind them, and Banana adds that it will be difficult to find the creature if it hid inside. Spin isn't sure if the creature is still alive, and Stick adds that they don't even know if it washed up on the same island. Banana then reveals a small dog in her backpack and lets it smell the sample, with Gon eagerly wanting to smell it as well. Killua wonders if the sample is rotten, but Banana explains that the dog would refuse it if it were. However, the dog is unable to pick up any sort of trail, and Kite guesses that the creature washed up elsewhere, asking how the currents flow. The man who found the leg tells them that they change direction day and night and that it depends on the season and day as well. Spin says that it will be impossible to specify a location, but Gon suggests that they split up. Kite wonders if he can find it, and Killua explains that Gon's nose works just like a dog's. However, they find that the scent is gone and guess that the rain washed it away. Kite's phone suddenly rings, and Podungo reveals that the creature is most likely a Chimera Ant queen, with Kite and the others taken aback by the news. Killua wonders what a Chimera Ant is, and Spin explains that it's an insect designated quarantine level one. Killua asks if it's dangerous, and Spin adds that it has a ravenous appetite and uses a strategy known as phagogenesis to reproduce. She finally reveals that the creature can eat many times its own weight in a single day and that it's called the "gourmet ant" for that very reason. Killua asks how large it can get, and Spin replies that queens are around 10 cm. Killua guesses that the one they are looking for is probably two meters tall and that it could eat people. After the group goes silent, they eventually decide to keep looking for the creature. Spin explains that a Chimera Ant queen keeps moving until she finds a place she likes and that she will continue to produce soldier Ants until then. She will also produce numerous construction Ants to build a nest and will then remain there until her death. Spin adds that the soldier Ants will catch enough food to satiate her appetite and that a two-meter-tall queen can develop a taste for human flesh, which can cause entire villages and towns to go missing. However, as Spin does a search on her laptop, she is unable to find any mass disappearances in the past six months. Gon asks about individual disappearances, but Spin says that it wouldn't help them since hundreds of thousands of people go missing around the world every year. Killua asks about areas with higher rates of missing reports, but Spin replies that she can't do that either since the data is two years old. Others suggest looking up sightings instead since a two-meter-tall insect would make the news, but Spin says that she isn't getting news or even any rumors. Banana wonders if they are worrying for nothing, and Spin guesses that the creature may already be fish food. Kite asks her to show him the data on ocean currents for the day the insect's leg was found. Spin brings up a map of the location, and Kite asks her to show him where the leg could have been ten days ago based on those currents, speculating that the leg may have been severed after the creature washed up elsewhere. Spin tells him that the entire Balsa Islands are a possibility, and Kite replies that the Mitene Union is also possible in that case. Stick wonders what it is, and Banana suddenly realizes that it's where NGL is. Kite points out that it's also the location of East Gorteau, and Killua wonders what NGL is. Kite replies that it stands for "Neo-Green Life" and that the country forbids all modern technology and lives among nature. Spin brings up a map of the Mitene Union and clicks on NGL, saying that all their communication is done by mail and all their transportation by horseback. She confirms that it's illegal to bring in modern technology and cites a case in 1987 when three members of a TV crew were caught trying to film a documentary, one of whom was executed and the other two left imprisoned. She adds that it has a population of 2.17 million, one percent of which are volunteers while the rest are "members". Kite wonders what they would do if the Chimera Ant washed up there, and Spin replies that they would likely do nothing, citing the example of an epidemic when they declined international aid because they wanted to let nature take its course. Kite points out that it would be too late anyway even if any information got out, guessing that the Chimera Ant is already building its nest. Kite and the others then make their way to the NGL Border Stop, and the driver explains that it acts as both the country's checkpoint and embassy. He wonders why the place is so interesting, revealing that he has already transported ten other groups there. Kite realizes that others must have had the same idea, telling the group to prepare themselves since NGL isn't the eco-friendly group they claim to be. Gon is left confused, and Banana whispers to him that there are many troubling rumors about them. The two ambassadors ask about the nature of their visit, and Kite explains that a biohazard-class insect may have wandered into their country. The group is led inside and surprised by the multiple computers. The ambassadors explain that they aren't inside the country yet and that the computers are used for diplomacy and information exchange. They stress that all metals, glass, and petroleum products will have to be removed before they are allowed to enter. Lin wonders if that includes his glasses, and the man confirms it, adding that they also need to remove any clothing that has any plastic or metal parts, or that's made from synthetic fibers. Spin worries about having to strip naked, but the ambassador assures them that they will provide clothing with natural fibers. The other ambassador adds that anyone with irremovable implants (e.g., surgical bolts, metal dental fillings, silicone prosthetics) will be refused entry. Only Kite, Stick, Podungo, Gon, and Killua continue the entry process. Kite tells the others to wait in town and that they will contact them in two weeks. A woman leads them to the inspection area and explains that they will have to go through a metal detector, x-ray, and ultrasound since people have tried to smuggle gun parts, cameras, or cell phones in their bodies before. The five are eventually granted entry and rent three horses for 12,000 a day. They decide to check out the communities along the coastline first and realize that the translator guides are keeping a close eye on them. Kite tells Gon and Killua that he doesn't expect any help from the people, adding that his instincts are telling him the creature is somewhere inside the country. After receiving a bloody note with directions from one of Ponzu's bees, Kite tells Gon and Killua that it will be dangerous and asks if they want to come. The two show no hesitation in agreeing, and Kite tells the translator that the horses will be too slow for them. He then tells Stick and Podungo to go back with the others and inform the Hunter Association that it's a top-level threat. After their confrontation with Neferpitou, Killua safely carries Gon back to the NGL Border Stop. He then calls Spin and tells her that they had to leave Kite behind, enraging her as she orders them to explain themselves. Mon takes the phone from her and tells Killua to wait there since they are on their way with reinforcements. In the back of the truck, Mon hangs up as Banana and Podungo are seen with Netero, Morel, and Knov. After leaving Knuckle and Shoot at the NGL Border Stop and begging the former to save Kite, Gon rides back in the truck with Killua and Spin, who is seen reading a book. Gon eventually stops sulking and says that he needs to get stronger so that Kite won't be disappointed after Knuckle rescues him. Spin tells Gon that while he may have met Kite before they did, they have spent more time with him. She adds that she would have kicked him off the truck if he kept sulking since Kite wouldn't want to see him like that. She is also confident that Kite is still alive, telling Gon that he wants to see wits and determination from him, not regret or remorse. She then tells him to train harder if he's weak and that he can do squats or pushups right there in the truck. Gon begins doing handstand push-ups and eventually asks Spin why she wants to be a Hunter. Spin replies that she needs money to pay off an immense debt, asking if they have ever heard of the Small-billed Swan. Gon replies that he hasn't, and Spin explains that while they don't know why yet, it only lives near a certain mine. She continues by saying that they bought what was left of the entire mountain and that Kite financed it for them, adding that he was the first adult who would listen to a group of kids with nothing to their names. She then reveals that the mountain is home for her and Stick, who were both born there. She adds that their most lasting memory is seeing thousands of swans take flight as the sun rose behind them, realizing how much the place meant to them once they heard that it was being considered an industrial waste site. She reveals that Kite said he envied them since he doesn't know where he was born and doesn't have a place to call home. With Gon and Killua still listening intently, Spin tells them that she will take them there once the mission is over, calling the place priceless. 13th Hunter Chairman Election arc. During Kite's discussion with Koala, Spin enters the room and tells him that he has a guest. Kite tells her to let him in, and Gon appears in the doorway. After his talk with Kite, Gon waves goodbye to him and the Amateur Hunters. After meeting Ging at the top of the World Tree, Gon happily joins Kite and the Amateur Hunters to watch thousands of Small-billed Swans take flight as the sun rises behind them. He then sends a video to all his friends so that they can see the spectacle. Kakin Exploration Team. Spinner Clow. A young woman who is always seen chewing gum. She came to survey the country with Kite. She aspires to be a Hunter so that she can pay back her debt to Kite, who financed her purchase of an entire mountain in her hometown—a mining townhome to the Small-billed Swan. Monta Yuras. A large man with a koala-like face also surveys Kakin for new species. He seems to be in charge of the luggage. Lin Koshi. He came to survey Kakin with Kite. He already discovered over a thousand new species even before meeting Gon and Killua. He's a short young man with round glasses and usually appears nervous and stuttering. Stick Dinner. He came to survey Kakin with Kite. He came from the same town as Spin. He likes saying puns and has an afro. He also said that he handles the cooking because his surname is Dinner. Banana Kavaro. She came to survey Kakin with Kite. Banana tells Gon about the Camp Tigers, has short hair, and wears baggy clothing. Podungo Lapoy. She came to survey Kakin with Kite. Podungo has dark skin with hair tied up in a topknot. She is the smallest member of the group.

Amoeba Amoeba (アメイバ, "Ameiba") is one of the Heavens Arena's Floor Masters. He only appears in . Appearance. Amoeba is spindly with long limbs. He has a skeletal face, topped by a shock of unkempt, greenish hair. He has a small chin and thick purple lips. The most striking feature on his face is his eyes: his right eye's sclera, iris, and pupil are completely yellow. A visor covers the other. In the Heavens Arena, he wears golden bracelets, a matching golden collar, a white and azure striped shirt that leaves his belly bare, a white belt with a round golden buckle, dark blue jeans, possibly with bell bottoms, and brown shoes. The right sleeve of his shirt is longer and baggier to hide a small cannon. On his chest, the stripes form the motif of a vortex. Personality. Not much is known about Amoeba's personality due to the limited number of scenes he appears in during, but he is often seen as eccentric and strange, even by the other Floor Masters, particularly Gama who is weirded out by Amoeba's strange movements during training. Amoeba also appears to be impatient, sometimes speaking with a whiny tone, particularly before the Battle Olympia begins when voicing his complaints to Gama. Plot. The Last Mission. As a Floor Master, Amoeba takes part in the Battle Olympia at Heavens Arena along with twenty other fighters. He is first seen walking into the arena with the other fighters during Cocco's introduction to the event. Before the tournament's first match, Amoeba is seen in a room with the other fighters doing some warm-ups. While the other fighters are doing standard warm-ups, like jumping rope or punching, Amoeba waggles his body back and forth, which weirds out Gama. Jed enters the training room wearing a cloak and quickly defeats all of the Floor Masters. Amoeba is seen lying on the ground with puncture wounds on his neck and an empty vial of Jed's blood beside him. After being trapped in a room with Amoeba and eight of the other Floor Masters, Gon and Killua get attacked by Kanjiru and get sent flying back. Gon lands against Amoeba, who grumbles at Gon. Later, while Gon tries to dodge Dani's attacks, Amoeba ambushes Gon from behind using his Amoeba Attack. Even after the Floor Masters in the room are knocked out, they get back up, walking in a zombified manner after Gon and Killua. The two boys manage to escape from the room using the elevator, leaving the Floor Masters behind. Abilities & Powers. Not much is known about Amoeba's abilities, but the fact that he was a Floor Master is proof enough of his power and proficiency in Nen. Still, he was defeated single-handedly by Jed. When fighting Gon and Killua, he is shown to fire an unknown liquid from his right sleeve at high pressure. Whether this is, a form of Nen or a hidden weapon is unknown. In the magazine held by Killua, he is seen dodging an attack by leaping backward over his opponent, demonstrating a good deal of agility.

Amori Amori (アモリ, "Amori") is one of the Amori Brothers. He was examinee #197 in the 287th Hunter Exam and #127 in the 288th Hunter Exam. Appearance. Amori sports a vertical striped skull hat, a long-sleeved turtleneck shirt, plain pants, and shoes. He has almond-shaped eyes and sharp markings below both of them. Personality. Amori is confident and arrogant, often chastising Imori when he doesn't take action quickly enough. However, he is the most reflective and introspective of the brothers, willing to acknowledge when an opponent completely outclasses him. Background. According to Tonpa, Amori and his brothers have attempted the Hunter Exam multiple times and improved their teamwork each year. During the First Phase, Satotz's marathon, he and his brothers help Tonpa to cause some of the weaker contestants to drop out (such as Nicholas), showing that they have known Tonpa for some time and likely worked with him before. Plot. Hunter Exam arc. First Phase. When pointing out some of the regulars of the Hunter Exam, Tonpa mentions that Amori and his brothers specialize in teamwork and keep improving every year. During the First Phase, as an exhausted Nicholas struggles to keep up during Satotz's marathon, the Amori Brothers surround and mock him, saying that he has won the year's pathetic award and wondering how he made it so far. After Nicholas falls to his knees and drops out, the three brothers catch up to the rest of the pack, and Tonpa pays them for their help. Amori says that Nicholas did okay for a rookie and praises Tonpa's ability to exploit an examinee's weakness. In the Milsy Wetlands, as various creatures kill dozens of the examinees, Amori notes that no one is behind them anymore, and Imori adds that there were more than 100 only a second earlier. Second Phase. After Menchi tells the examinees that they will have to make sushi next, they are all left confused by the term. Amori asks Umori if he has any idea what it is, but his brother replies that he doesn't. Third Phase. When one of the examinees reaches the bottom of Trick Tower and collapses soon afterward, the three brothers surround his body and pronounce him dead. Fourth Phase. On Zevil Island, as Imori stalks Killua to take his badge, Amori and Umori pursue Shishito and Kenmi. Amori is followed by Hanzo, but the ninja does not act because Umori is always with Amori. The two eventually succeed in getting the badges of their targets before meeting back up with Imori, thinking he has done the same. When they learn that he hasn't, Amori kicks him, and Umori punches him, with the former calling him a wuss and wondering how he hasn't beaten a little kid yet. When Killua quickly recovers from Imori's kick, Amori guesses that the attack must have whiffed, and Umori asks if he's toying with him. After Killua steals Imori's badge and asks the other two if they have #199, Amori becomes serious and tells Umori to take positions. The three brothers form a triangle in front of Killua, who suddenly leaps off a nearby tree high into the air and appears right behind Amori, kicking the back of his legs and forcing him to his knees. Killua then holds his sharp nails to his neck and draws a drop of blood, telling him to keep still and left disappointed by his #197 badge. After receiving Umori's #199 badge, he throws Imori and Amori's badges far into the distance. He tells them they have five days left to recover them, quickly disappearing into the forest. Amori is seen lying down with his hands behind his head, but he quickly sits up and pounds the ground in frustration. Hanzo, having been deceived into taking Imori's badge by Killua, eventually returns for their two remaining badges. Greed Island arc. Amori and his brothers participate in the 288th Hunter Exam, but all three are easily defeated along with the rest of the examinees by Killua during the First Phase. Amori reflects on their training and says they were confident and practiced until they coughed up blood, perfecting their combination moves. However, he realizes that they failed because they ignored the existence of prodigies they couldn't imagine, describing Killua as someone born to be a first-rate Hunter. He wonders what their effort was for, especially since Killua will see them as having accomplished nothing. As his consciousness begins to fade, Amori says that it will be their last year taking the exam, guessing that others will make the same decision.

Amori Brothers The Amori Brothers (, "Amori San Kyōdai") are a trio of siblings that are recurring veterans of the Hunter Exams, whose specialty focuses on teamwork above all else. During 287th Hunter Exam, Amori was #197, Imori was #198, and Umori was #199. Background. According to Tonpa, the brothers have attempted the Hunter Exams multiple times before the 287th session, improving their teamwork each time. Plot. Hunter Exam arc. In an introduction given by Tonpa, the Amori Brothers are a trio that specializes in teamwork and are constantly improving on it. Amid the first part of the First Phase of the Hunter Exam, the trio chastise and disparage examinee #187 Nicholas, and are paid by Tonpa for their "good work". During the second part of the First Phase of the exam in the Milsy Wetlands, brothers Amori and Imori notice that a hundred examinees behind them simply vanished and it was due to the local flora and fauna. The brothers, though exhausted and profusely sweating, manage to make it to the Second Phase of the Hunter Exam. The trio passes the first part of the Second Phase of the exam, however, like nearly all of the other examinees, are confused about what exactly "sushi" is. At the bottom of the Trick Tower where the Third Phase of the Hunter Exam was held, they witness an examinee immediately die the moment he reached the end. Umori insults the deceased examinee, claiming he should have simply failed and tried again next year. At the end of the Third Phase, the brothers are among the twenty-five (including one deceased) to pass the exam. Outside the tower, the examinees are briefed by the Third Phase examiner Lippo about the Fourth Phase on Zevil Island. The examinees draw lots and the point system in the Fourth Phase is disclosed by Lippo. On the boat ride to Zevil Island, the examinees are given a brief speech by Khara and upon landing on the island Imori is the first brother to step foot on ground. While Amori and Umori pursue Shishito and Kenmi, Imori stalks Killua to claim his own badge. Killua, aware of Imori's presence, calls out for them to play, but Imori does not respond. After some time passes, Imori still hasn't revealed himself to Killua. Annoyed, Killua begins making his towards way Imori, prompting him to panic before his brothers return from their successful hunts. The two berate Imori and pressure him into attacking his target, but Killua easily takes Imori's badge. Killua then overpowers and holds Amori hostage to force Umori to surrender his badge, which is the one he needs. After that, he throws the two badges he doesn't need into the forest. Hanzo, who was stalking Amori but waiting on account of Umori accompanying him at all times, is tricked by Killua into catching the wrong badge. Hanzo eventually managed to pass the phase regardless by taking the Amori Brother's remaining two badges while the trio subsequently failed the exam. Greed Island arc. The Amori Brothers confront Killua again while partaking in the 288th Hunter Exam, only to be easily defeated in the First Phase by him. Seeing the tremendous gap in ability between Killua and themselves, despite the boy being much younger than them, the brothers unanimously decide they will never take the Hunter Exam again.

Analysis (G.I card) Analysis (, rom. "Anarishisu") is a spell card found in the Greed Island game. It allows the caster to read the text of a numbered card of their choice, except for #000. Summary. This spell allows the caster to read the text of a numbered item card (so a specified slot card between #1 and #99) of their choice, and thus to figure out its effects. This implies that the target card's number must be known to cast this spell.

Ancient Kappe Ancient Kappe (, "Kodai Kappē") is an ancient language. Plot. Dark Continent Expedition arc. Curly, a member of Beyond Netero's Dark Continent Expedition Team, challenges Ging to another ancient language contest. He chooses the Ancient Kappe language as the subject, starting with 'N'. The two square off; however, Curly becomes easily burnt out. This is because of Ging's superior knowledge of his linguistic knowledge on Kappe, and he concedes defeat.

Angel's Breath (G.I card) Angel's Breath (, "Daitenshi no Ibuki"—lit. "Breath of Archangel") is a card found in the Greed Island game. It is one of the game's 100 designated slot cards and so is required for a player to complete the game. This angel's breath will cure any illness a person may currently be suffering from. Summary. This card summons forth an angel whose breath can cure any injuries sustained upon a player. She only appears once and afterward, the card is destroyed. You can trade all 40 spell cards in at Masadora for this card. If the maximum card limit has already been reached, then you will be given a Voucher instead. This voucher will then transform into an "Angel's Breath" at the next available chance.

Animal Control A few characters in Hunter × Hunter are shown to use animals as a form of weaponry. This could be due to the fact that they are Manipulators or simply because they have tamed the animals. Some of these animals are:

Animate Cafe The Hunter × Hunter Animate Cafe, shortened to Hunter × Animate Cafe (ハンター×アニメイトカフェ, "Hantā × Animeito Kafe"), is a collaboration between Animate Cafe and the Hunter × Hunter series. Information. The Animate Cafe collaborates with popular anime and game franchises. For each collaboration, the interior is specially decorated and offers unique menu items and limited edition merchandise. DECOTTO by Animate Cafe is a take-out shop by Animate Cafe that also does collaborations and sells original donuts. There are several Animate Cafe locations and a specific collaboration may only be available at one or more of those locations. Cafe reservations can be made online or you can walk-in to purchase the limited edition merchandise. Point cards are also distributed after purchases and the customer can receive a special collaboration card as a gift per every two stamps collected.

Anita Anita (アニタ, "Anita") is an anime-only character in Nippon Animation's version of Hunter × Hunter; she aspires to become a Blacklist Hunter. Appearance. Anita has black hair in twin ponytails and green eyes. She wears a maroon tunic over a navy top and matching color pants, white earrings, a brown bag worn around her right side, black bracers, and boots. She also wears her examinee badge #111 on the top left side of her chest. Personality. Anita is mostly serious and highly determined to avenge her father, like Kurapika. She could sometimes be snappish or rude like when she tells Gon he can't win against Chairman Netero. Anita is also observant, noticing that he hasn't used his right arm or left leg against Gon and Killua yet. Background. She is the daughter of a wealthy spice merchant who was assassinated by one of the Zoldycks. Anita takes the 287th Hunter Exam because she knows that Killua was taking the Hunter Exam, and she wants to kill him to avenge her father. Plot. Hunter Exam arc. Anita, examinee #111, fails the Second Phase in the 287th Hunter Exam, but stowaways on Chairman Netero's airship, carrying the examinees to the Third Phase. There she meets Killua and attempts to attack him with a knife. But Netero intervenes, knowing that she failed the exam, and keeps her under watch until they arrive at the next Phase. Anita breaks free and goes after Killua again; this time, Killua enters his assassin mode. He changes his nails into claws and slices the blade off her knife. He then pins her to the ground and holds his claws to her neck, ready to slit her throat. He snaps out of his assassin mode just before he is about to do this and knocks her out cold instead. When the airship reaches the Third Phase, Anita is sent back, and Killua hands her her earring while telling her that her father was, in reality, a drug merchant. The spice from his mine was a highly addictive substance; her father made a profit off the suffering of others, and that was why he was assassinated. Anita takes this very hard as she always thought of her father as a kind and loving man and began to cry.

Antokiba Antokiba (アントキバ, "Antokiba"), also known as "The Town of Prizes", is a city on Greed Island and the closest to the center of the island. Overview. Antokiba is the first town many new players find since it's so close to the Starting Point. It offers a variety of shops and numerous rewards, which it advertises through posters. On the 15th of every month, a major contest is held in which the winner is rewarded with a specified slot card. The only known contests are rock-paper-scissors and two-person tug of war. Plot. Greed Island arc. Upon reaching Antokiba, Gon and Killua are surprised to see so many reward posters, with Killua unable to tell if the "Cursed Statue of Lady Luck" for finding a lost dog is a good item. Gon then spots the monthly contest list and notes that September is rock-paper-scissors, with Killua pointing out that it may not even be September in the game. Gon asks a nearby man, who says that it's September 11. After the two learn that the dates are the same, Killua sees that there's a contest on the 15th of every month and that September's prize is the "Sword of Truth". As they wonder if it's an item they need, they spot several of the players hired by Battera and guess that the competition will be tough, but decide to enter several contests and gather information until then. The two then spot a nearby restaurant that also offers information and prizes. The cat waiter brings them two large plates of spaghetti and tells them that if they can eat it all in half an hour, they get the meal for free and also win a "Gargaida" card. The waiter is left confused by some of their questions, and when he leaves to get their prize, Killua tells Gon that he's a game NPC, explaining that they will have to ask people one by one to learn everything. The waiter returns with their cards and explains the information, with Gon and Killua realizing how bad the card is. The two prepare to leave, but the waiter points out that they still owe 1,020 for the three drinks they had, threatening to call the police if they don't pay. The two are forced to wash dishes since even the money is in cards. After paying off their debt, the two go outside and suddenly hear screaming around the corner. They see a large crowd gathered together and find Jeet lying dead on the ground, with blood covering his midsection. The two recognize him as one of the players hired by Battera and had seen him earlier at the monthly contest list, learning from one of the onlookers that he suddenly exploded from the inside. As Gon is left stunned and says that it doesn't seem at all like a game, the corpse vanishes and returns to the real world, with Gon now worrying about the spell cast on Killua. Nickes overhears their conversation and assures them that the player wasn't killed by a spell, but by the Nen of another player. He then asks if they want to join his alliance and promises that his group has a perfect strategy to clear the game. The two eventually agree to listen to Nickes' offer and follow him to Antokiba's plaza where they find other members of the alliance (including three other new players who were also invited to join). They learn about the deadly Bomber, and the alliance's plan to monopolize spell cards. The alliance assures the new players that they intend to put an end to the killing from the Bomber by clearing the game, with Nickes again asking them if they will join. After Puhat and Abengane agree to join, Gon declines the offer and says that he wants to play on his own, with Killua following his lead and the two leaving Antokiba's plaza. Gon tells Killua that he wants to just enjoy the game as Ging told him. As the two continue to talk about the game and their journey together, Biscuit listens in on their conversation and understands why the two didn't join the alliance, saying that little boys are innocent and gleefully adding that it's fun to ruin their friendships. Gon and Killua then practice rock-paper-scissors for the upcoming tournament, with the latter becoming more and more frustrated at losing. Gon tells Killua that there's a trick to it that a fisherman who came to Whale Island taught him. After the explanation, Killua becomes angry at Gon for cheating during all their bouts, but Gon doesn't want the others to overhear. He tells Killua that it seems simple, but takes a lot of talent and practice, adding that Leorio couldn't do it. Killua still calls it cheating, but isn't against it in order to win the Sword of Truth. They eventually face each other in the finals of the rock-paper-scissors tournament, and Killua clinches the win by using rock with his left hand. The judge presents him with the Sword of Truth, which immediately transforms into the card once Killua touches it. He sees that it's a specified slot card, and the two rejoice that it's their first one. Although Gon and Killua are able to keep multiple players from taking the card, a group of at least eight players suddenly ambushes them and says that they can't run away. They play rock-paper-scissors among themselves to decide the order to cast spells, and Kazsule says that only idiots enter the contests. After the card is taken from them, Gon sulks at the loss, but Killua tells him to forget it and be glad that the players didn't use violence. The two agree that it's time to head to Masadora for spell cards. Before they leave, they visit a trade shop and sell four "Gargaida" cards and earn 120,000. Gon suggests buying food and water so they can head to Masadora as soon as possible, but Killua tells him that they still need a map. The two return to the shop and decide whether they should buy the detailed or empty map. Gon opts for the latter since it will be more fun to find locations on their own. They pay 30,000 to the shopkeeper for information on Masadora, and he gives them specific directions, but warns them about bandits and monsters. This excites the two as they make their way toward the city. While collecting specified slot cards, Gon and Killua suddenly remember that the monthly tournament in Antokiba is tomorrow and make their way there, with both of them eventually winning and receiving the "Paladin's Necklace." They aren't exactly sure what it does, so they head to |a trade shop where the shopkeeper explains that the necklace casts "Reflect" on someone as long as it's being worn and allows them to revert cards cursed by "Clone" or "Fake" by touching them. Killua is ecstatic that they won't have to worry about having their cards stolen, but Gon says that they won't be able to have it as a card then. Biscuit points out that it's the prize for January and so they only have one chance to get it a year. Killua has them both take a closer look at the card, pointing out that the card is D-rank, which means they can cast "Recycle" on it. Gon wonders why it's D-rank if they can only get it once a year, but Killua checks his notes on spell cards and says that it's also possible to get it using "Compromise" and "Corruption." Gon turns the card into the necklace and puts it on, with all three rejoicing as they make their way to Dorias. When Kazsule contacts Gon to offer a trade, he says that he was that took the "Sword of Truth" from him at Antokiba. When Goreinu tells Gon and Killua that the light next to a player's name goes off when they leave or die, he asks if they know Jeet and reminds him that he was the one killed in Antokiba.

Antokiba Trade Shop NPC The Antokiba Trade Shop NPC is a non-player character shopkeeper in Antokiba's Trade Shop, Greed Island. Appearance. The Trade Shop NPC is a burly gorilla-esque male with spiky hair, shaven sides, thick eyebrows, a fleshy nose, dead fish-like eyes, and a short beard. He wears a sleeveless T-shirt with text that translates to "Gori", plain shorts, and two bracelets around both of his wrists. Personality. The Trade Shop NPC divulges information in a monotone voice and only shows a smirk when talking about how his store also acts as a bank. Asta reveals that if you shop at the Trade Shop more than fifty times, you'll become their "Best Customer" and be able to purchase all B-Ranked cards from their store. Background. His function is buying items from players (only in card form) in exchange for the island's currency which is Jenny in card form. He also sells information to players, such as card functions and directions to the island's locations, and also functions as a bank, where he takes players' Jenny cards for safekeeping. Plot. Greed Island arc. The Trade Shop NPC greets Gon and Killua to his shop, and they sell to him four "Galgaida" cards for 120,000. The shopkeeper also mentions that they can store their money there, but Killua instantly declines. Later the boys purchase a map from another shop and return to the Trade Shop NPC for information on the location of Masadora. The shopkeeper agrees to disclose the information for 3,000, much to Killua's annoyance, who wants a discount, though the shopkeeper remains obstinate. They pay the fee, and the shopkeeper divulges how to get to Masadora, though he warns them of bandits and monsters on the way. Rather than be fearful, this excites the boys, to which the shopkeeper looks dejected. Months after completing their Nen training with Biscuit Krueger in the badlands, the boys, now accompanied by Biscuit, return to the trade shop and are divulged a more elaborate description on the Paladin's Necklace after winning the card in the monthly tournament held in Antokiba.

Anzel Anzel (エンゼール, "Enzēru") is one of five personal guards for Prince Tyson. Appearance. Anzel has pupil-less eyes, a wide nose, and light and dark hair covering his face's right side. He wears the usual black suit and tie of a bodyguard. Personality. In his roleplaying as Tyson’s little brother, Anzel has a cheerful and sincere demeanor. Plot. Succession Contest arc. In Tyson’s quarters, Anzel introduces himself as the Prince’s little brother, adding that the two of them are the only ones who know about it. After the rest of Tyson’s bodyguards introduce themselves, Giuliano realizes that they are acting out the characters Tyson likes.

Arka Arka (アーカ, "Āka") is a player of the game Greed Island. Appearance. Arka is a skinny man of average height. He has a long face with high cheekbones and sharp buck teeth. He is seen wearing a light green shirt with a white loose collar. Personality. Arka is an opportunist, waiting for Gon and Killua to be caught off guard after one of their first encounters. However, he appears to be a coward, as he quickly retreats once his plan backfires and is forced into a confrontation. Plot. Greed Island arc. Intent on stealing Gon and Killua's newly-acquired "Sword of Truth" card, he appears right after Motaricke fails to steal the card. Arka uses two "Pickpocket" cards to randomly steal cards the boys have gathered. However, due to the boy's precautionary actions to protect their cards, Arka only manages to steal a single "Rock" card. Running out of tricks and realizing that the boys are too smart for him to trick, he gives up and flees. Arka's name is mentioned in Gon's binder when the latter checks to see who is still (alive) inside the game. Abilities & Powers. Nen. Due to being able to access Greed Island, Arka is capable of utilizing Nen.

Aromatherapy Girl (G.I card) Aromatherapy Girl 発香少女 - is a card found in the Greed Island game. It is one of the game's 100 designated slot cards and is thus required for a player to complete the game. Summary. Aromatherapy Girl 発香少女 - This is the Aromatherapy Girl NPC in card form. When gained, this girl emits the most comfortable and pleasant aroma for the caster. When she is by the player's side, they will be completely free of any stress. This also allows for a calm mind, enabling the player to think more clearly.

Aruto Aruto (アルト, "Aruto"), a video game-only character protagonist of, is a boy from a village that had the Aura Stone robbed by the Phantom Troupe. He chases the Spider with the only remaining Aura Stone's pieces/fragments. Abilities & Powers. Nen. Aruto is a very rare/unusual person whose Specialist Nen ability power is immeasurable.

Assam Assam (アッサム, "Assamu") was a Greed Island player, hired by Battera, and a founding member of an alliance formed to clear the game. Appearance. Assam was a man of average height and build. He had a defined jaw, a slightly upturned nose, squinty eyes, and short eyebrows. His hair was a dark blond color and in a mound towards the top. He was seen wearing a lavender shirt in the 2011 anime adaptation and an ash-gray shirt in the 1999 anime adaptation. Personality. Like his fellow alliance members, he had an informative personality with extensive knowledge of the game. Plot. Greed Island arc. Assam is amongst the players trying to recruit new players into their alliance. He discloses that there are three ways to obtain cards in the game and allows the new players to name them. He elaborates on the sudden increase of people using the most unscrupulous method of obtaining cards because of the card conversion limit and how it's responsible for the spike in player hunters and deaths within the game. The alliance, however, has managed to obtain 67 of the 100 specified slot cards. In the five years since the alliance started, all seemed hopeless initially, but in recent months it doubled the number of members and cards. So, to stop the needless bloodshed over the years, the alliance members ask the new players to join their group. In the end, only two of the possible five join (whose names are Abengane and Puhat). Afterward, the alliance members meet up with Jispa, who uses a "Leave" card on each of the two new members and reports that Contarch has recruited eight new members. This causes the alliance members Genthru and Nickes to get into an argument over the reward money, but Assam stops them by telling them that Nomdieu and Isaac may overhear their conversation. After Nickes announces that the alliance has nearly completed its goal, Genthru gets the group's attention and reveals that he is the Bomber and has placed bombs on all of the alliance members. Hearing this revelation, Jispa tries to incapacitate him but gets his face blown off first. Genthru then explains his two Nen abilities to the alliance and escapes. Assam curses the fact that Genthru will be getting away with 50 billion while he was supposed to split 20 billion with the other founders. He gets into an abrasive argument with a junior member whose payout is paltry compared to his. Nickes stops the argument and beseeches that the group hand over their cards to save Jispa's life. A man by the name of Bara, who later reveals that he is also a Bomber member, delivers Puhat's severed head as an example to the group to give in to their demands. He also discloses an alternate way for them to disarm the bombs. The alliance members eventually surrender their cards, but instead of disarming the bombs, the Bombers detonate them and kill nearly all of the alliance members. Assam's name is mentioned in Gon's binder. Abilities & Powers. Since most of the alliance members joined because they lacked combat abilities, it can be assumed that Assam also had none. Nen. Due to being able to access Greed Island, Assam was capable of utilizing Nen.

Assassin A Assassin A was one of the assassins hired by the Ten Dons to eliminate the Phantom Troupe. Appearance. Assassin A was a tall man with a medium build. He had distinct facial features with a prominent nose, heavy bags under his eyes, downward angled eyebrows, and lazy but piercing, light-colored eyes. He kept medium-length hair that reached his shoulders, outstanding sideburns, and likely possessed substantial body hair as noted by his hairy arms. His clothes consisted of generally military-like attire with a combat army shirt, a military-style beret, and a pair of combat boots into which he tucked the legs of the trousers. Personality. Assassin A was a confident and individualistic man who was also quite bloodthirsty. With a solitary personality, he was not interested in working with the other assassins and proposed that they should work by themselves in their mission to eliminate the Phantom Troupe. He also confidently ridiculed the idea of using color codes as brought up by the other assassins, claiming that no one would use them. Assassin A was also shown to be a perceptive man, able to catch a glimpse of Chrollo's extremely swift strike to Neon's neck on surveillance footage, claiming that anyone else would have missed it. He was also quite assertive and directed the discussion to use a majority rule vote, most likely to validate his personal stance and to sway the conversation to his side. Assassin A was shown to be a bloodthirsty man fully indulged in the thrill of the hunt, especially when the target had demonstrated to be a worthy enough prey. To complement this, he had a sturdy composure and was able to hide this side of him extremely well, containing all of his thoughts internally even as he was growing excited at the prospect of facing his opponent. His composure allowed him to think cautiously and tactically despite his turbulent inner thrill, and he took the necessary precautions and considered things carefully as he hunted his target. However, his confidence and composure would later diminish when facing the things truly unknown to him, entering a state of panic. Plot. Yorknew City arc. When the assassins first meet up with the Mafia in Yorknew City to learn about their mission in detail, Assassin A's confident attitude makes Kurapika think that he and Assassin B are the only ones who are not intimidated by Silva and Zeno Zoldyck and can hold their own. During the meeting, Assassin A chiefly opposes the idea of using code names and working as a team, proposing that they all work by themselves. Once Kurapika sides with those who want to work by themselves and a majority is formed, Assassin A leaves to find the targets on his own. Before the start of the rescheduled Underground Auction, Assassin A is seen standing in the control room of the Cemetery Building and observing the surveillance footage to catch any irregularities. He eventually spots something and asks a Mafia member to rewind the footage, allowing him to see Chrollo knocked Neon unconscious with an incredibly fast strike to her neck. He tells himself that anyone else would have missed it and becomes excited at the prospect of hunting a worthy prey, chuckling as he leaves the room to kill his target. During his search, Assassin A smells blood and realizes that the target has deliberately left a trail of blood and then wiped it up to leave just enough of a scent. He breathes in the smell and says that only those as skilled as himself can detect it, adding that he and his target are both predators addicted to killing. He makes his way to a room with Assassin F tied to a chair and stabbed with several pens in his legs. After Assassin A quickly throws a knife at his chest to confirm that he's dead, Chrollo peers out from behind him and assures him that any won't use any boring traps. Chrollo pulls a pen from Assassin F's head and asks that they fight one on one. Readying his aura and holding a large knife in his hand, Assassin A happily agrees to the duel. Breathing heavily and sweating profusely, Assassin A laughs and asks Chrollo why he's still alive as his body is shown pinned in pieces up against a wall. Chrollo explains that the Nen creatures who have eaten parts of him are called Indoor Fish and can only exist in a closed room. He adds that they are carnivores and enjoy human flesh, explaining to Assassin A that he can't feel pain or bleed while they are feeding on him. As Chrollo opens a large window and explains that he can't die until the creatures disappear, Assassin A's mangled corpse falls bloody to the floor. Equipment. Combat Knives: Assassin A used combat knives as his primary weapon of choice. In the manga, he carried at least two of them so that he could throw them to scout and attack at a distance. While in the 2011 anime adaptation, he seemed to carry only one. Abilities & Powers. Assassin A was considered a powerful warrior who specialized in murder. He gave proof of his quick reflexes when he noticed how Chrollo had knocked Neon unconscious with an incredibly fast strike to her neck. He was also a skilled tracker with a superhuman sense of smell, as seen when following a faint trail of blood left by Chrollo. He appeared to be very proficient in knife handling, using a military combat knife as his main weapon, as well as a very accurate thrower. Nen. Assassin A was able to use Ren at the very least. He was one of two assassins hired by the Ten Dons who Kurapika said was not intimidated by the two Zoldycks and could hold his own.

Assassin B Assassin B was one of the assassins hired by the Ten Dons to eliminate the Phantom Troupe. Appearance. Assassin B had crimson hair, which he had shaved on the left side to display a bird-like tattoo, while keeping the hair on the right side long and tied at the front to cover the right side of his face entirely. He had additional tattoos around his left eye and cheek, though it is unclear if he had similar tattoos around his other eye. He wore traditional clothes which was in stark contrast to his trendy hairstyle. Personality. A man of few words, very little is known about Assassin B. According to Kurapika, he and Assassin A were the only two not intimidated by Silva and Zeno Zoldyck. He also agreed with Assassin A that they should all work by themselves, saying that they each have different styles and they can't force everyone to work together. In the 2011 anime adaptation, he also showed a side of confidence during his short clash with Chrollo. Plot. Yorknew City arc. When the assassins first meet up with the Mafia in Yorknew City to learn about their mission in detail, Kurapika recognizes that both Assassins B and A are the only ones who are not intimidated by the two Zoldycks and can hold their own. During the meeting, Assassin B agrees with Assassin A that they should work alone since they all have different styles. He is never seen again after the meeting, presumably killed some time after setting out to hunt his target, with Zeno telling the Mafia members that some of the assassins have already been killed. Assassin B's fate is only depicted in the 2011 anime adaptation. In the middle of the chaos at the Cemetery Building, he finds Chrollo and challenges him. The two clash for an instant, with Assassin B emerging with a smirk on his face and believing that he has struck down the infamous thief. However, he collapses immediately after and reveals a fatal wound from a pen stabbed into the back of his head. Unscathed, Chrollo leaves the assassin's body behind. Equipment. In the 2011 anime adaptation, Assassin B seemed to prefer the use of traditional weaponry and wielded a pole-axe. Since he brought it with him to hunt the Troupe members, it is likely that he was proficient with it. Abilities & Powers. Assassin B was considered a powerful warrior who specialized in murder.
