While Majtani pretends to be dead to further prolong the examinees from advancing, Leroute bets against Leorio Paradinight whether Majtani is alive or dead, using their time as credits. She proposes to use their remaining 50-hours each and continue until one party has no more time credits to bet. As a consequence, if Leorio loses, his team has lesser hours to escape the tower, but if Leroute loses, the time will be added to her sentence. Leorio agrees to the match and bets ten hours that Majtani is alive. He and Leroute check the prisoner, and confirm that he's not dead yet. For the next topic, Leorio proses if Majtani is actually unconscious or only faking it. Leroute bets 20 hours that her colleague is unconscious, but asks Leorio how to confirm it. He takes Majtani and dangles him off the ledge. Leroute protests that it will kill the prisoner, but Leorio assures her that if Majtani screams, Kurapika will lose the match. She agrees on the terms, but changes her initial bet of 20 hours to 40 hours, claiming that the prisoner will wake up. As Leorio is about to let go, Majtani stops his pretense and runs back to the other prisoners. Leroute observes that Leorio knew all along, and he explains that he is a medical student. For the next bet, Leroute finally removes her hood and bets whether she is a woman or not. She explains that Leorio can check her body until he is satisfied, to confirm his answer. Thus, Leorio bets 10 hours that she is a man, but Leroute says otherwise. Just to confirm, she lets Leorio touch her, putting their scores at 90-10, the favor being with the prisoners. With only 10 hours to lose, Leorio bets on a rock-paper-scissors game. She agrees and starts analyzing the game and Leorio. For the first try, it ends with a draw. She guesses that uncertainty would affect her opponent's psychological stability and uses paper against Leorio's rock. Leroute wins the match, successfully reducing 50 hours from the examinees' allotted time to escape Trick Tower. Her sentence is also reduced by 50 years. She is shocked, when she witnesses Killua kill Johness by tearing out and destroying his heart. Abilities & Powers. Leroute is not a fighter, but in the 1999 anime adaptation she is very dangerous nonetheless. She is extremely analytical and knowledgeable in psychology, to the point she can nearly read the mind of a person and effectively guess what memories haunt them the most, to use them to inflict pain or even force her victim to commit suicide. She figured out Leorio's thought pattern the moment she set her eyes on him. Additionally, she is very attractive, which contributes to the influence she has on her targets. In the manga and the 2011 anime adaptation, she is shown to be a good gambler with knowledge in statistics and who is able to anticipate the moves of her opponent.
Let's Go Let's Go (さぁ行こう, "Saa Ikou") is a song from, sung by the whole cast.

Levitation Stone (G.I card) Levitation Stone (浮遊石) is a card found in the Greed Island game. It is one of the game's 100 designated slot cards and so is required for a player to complete the game. Summary. Levitation Stone 浮遊石 - This card allows the caster to summon forth a stone of levitation. This stone has the ability to levitate on its own. Anyone who holds it will also begin to levitate. This ability only works with a single person at a time, and the effects wear off once the user lets go of it. It receives energy from sunlight.

Levy (G.I card) Levy (, rom. "Rebi") is a spell card found in the Greed Island game. It allows a player to steal a random card from every player within a 20 meter radius. Summary. This card allows the user to randomly steal a card from every player within a 20 meter radius. It can steal from both designated card slots and free slots. Because it is random, the caster may obtain some good cards or some bad cards. Rolling a Risky Dice can increase the odds of stealing good cards.
Life Life ("Inochi") is a song from the Musical Hunter × Hunter, sung by Yuu Daiki as Madam Isabel and as Mitsuko.

Light Nostrade Light Nostrade (ライト゠ノストラード, "Raito Nosutorādo") is the former head of the Nostrade Family, a Mafia group under the leadership of the Ritz Family, as well as Kurapika's employer. After Neon lost her ability to Chrollo and Kurapika took over the leadership of the Nostrade Family, his current role is unknown. Appearance. He is a middle-aged man who has his hair combed back and a thick mustache. He usually wears a suit. Personality. Light usually has a calm personality, but gets put on edge when the safety of his daughter Neon is jeopardized. He is very indulging of his daughter's whims. While it's unclear how much of his affection for her is sincere, a large part of his behavior is due to the value he places on her fortunetelling ability. It has been revealed that exploiting this ability was how he got ahead in the Mafia and is how he plans to rise to the top, declaring that he can rule the world with his daughter's ability. Background. Light was originally just the leader of a small gang, but by shrewdly exploiting Neon's ability, he gained prestige and rose up the ranks of the Mafia. Plot. Yorknew City arc. En route to Yorknew City, Neon calls her father and threatens to stop writing fortunes after being flooded with more requests than she can handle. Light negotiates with her and promises her more gifts, which delights Neon. On the night of September 1st, Dalzollene, the leader of the bodyguards, contacts Light from the Hotel Beitacle to tell him about something troubling among Neon's fortunes. He explains that four clients received the same fortune which involved death and that all four plan to attend the Underground Auction. Understanding the danger, Light tells Dalzollene not to let Neon attend and to bring her home immediately. Dalzollene warns that trying to talk her out of it will backfire, and Light says that while Neon cannot attend the auction, they should spend whatever they have to in order to win the items she wants. As Dalzollene expected, Neon throws an enormous tantrum after learning that her father forbade her from attending the auction. Dalzollene calls Light and asks if he can hear the noise, saying that they don't know what to do. Light cancels all his plans and plans to head to the city, ordering Dalzollene to acquire the mummy so that Neon will be in a good mood. On the night of September 2nd, Neon contacts Light to inform him that all of the auction items were stolen by thieves and that Dalzollene may have been killed. Light talks to Kurapika and is shocked to hear that Dalzollene is dead since he was a capable Nen user. After hearing Kurapika's thoughts, Light instantly promotes him to the head bodyguard position and says that his first order is to watch his daughter until he arrives. During the afternoon of September 3rd, Light meets with the bodyguards and learns everything that has happened. He asks Neon if she is okay with being sent home, and Neon replies that it would be pointless to stay since everything was stolen and the auction is canceled. Light assures her that the stolen items will be retrieved and she can attend next year's auction. He then orders Melody and Basho to take Neon back to the mansion and that they should put on disguises even though their pictures aren't on the Hunter Website. After Neon leaves the room to pack her things, Light reveals to the bodyguards that the auction will actually resume that very night, that all the Shadow Beasts aside from Owl are dead, and that the Ten Dons have hired a number of professional assassins to eliminate the Phantom Troupe and retrieve the stolen items. Not wanting the assassins to take all the credit, Light asks Kurapika to join them. Later, Light and Kurapika attend a meeting where the freelance assassins, Silva and Zeno Zoldyck, and a Mafia member named Zenji accompanied by bodyguards all discuss how to deal with the Phantom Troupe. After the meeting, Zenji confronts Light and, after a hostile exchange of words, punches him in the face repeatedly. Kurapika threatens Zenji with a knife, but Light tells Kurapika to stop as Zenji's bodyguards pull their leader away. Light admits to Kurapika that he has made a lot of jealous enemies with his success and will make even more as he continues to rise up the ranks. He expects great things from Kurapika and promises to award him generously for his efforts. Soon after, Melody contacts Kurapika and tells him that Neon has run away. Panic-stricken, Light is assured by Kurapika that his daughter must have discovered his lie and is making her way to the Cemetery Building to attend the auction. After Light contacts the police to have them be on the lookout for his daughter, one of them informs him that a young girl with different hair and clothes didn't know she needed a pass and mentioned her father before having her taxi turn around. Light urgently calls someone else and tells them to put out an A.P.B. for his daughter and print out her picture, pleading them to search for her. Keeping calm about the situation, Kurapika uses his Dowsing Chain and a map to discover that Neon is already inside the Cemetery Building. Upon their arrival, Light immediately rushes to Neon's room and finds her unconscious. He becomes furious when he finds out that Neon's picture is actually available on the Hunter Website, and Kurapika quickly calms him down, reminding him that their top priority is Neon's safety. He also explains that the other bodyguards are on their way and predicts that the auction might be canceled again due to the upcoming battle. A medical team arrives later to transport Neon to a local hospital, with Light staying by her side the entire time. Light learns from Kurapika that the Phantom Troupe members are dead and that he will attend the auction as ordered. He insists that Kurapika should win the Scarlet Eyes regardless of the cost. Ultimately, the Scarlet Eyes are purchased for a total price of 2.9 billion because of a bidding war against Zenji. Although upset by the price paid for the eyes, Light reminds himself that the money is going back to the community and that his prestige will only be greater, adding that he can easily make the money back and continue to amass more power with Neon's fortunes. After regaining consciousness, Neon thanks her father for the eyes and forgives him. Outside Neon's hospital room, Light congratulates the bodyguards for a job well done and informs them that they just need to win the used tissue at the auction tomorrow. He lastly says that he will be leaving the city the day after tomorrow and that Neon can stay behind to go shopping. Greed Island arc. Sometime after the auction, Light is seen having a serious mental breakdown after the loss of Neon's fortunetelling ability. He summons Kurapika to his unkempt room and begs him for advice. Although Kurapika tells him to leave everything to him, Light angrily replies that he has no idea what will happen, ordering him to return Neon to normal before he puts his hands over his face and wonders why it happened. Dark Continent Expedition arc. The Nostrade Family survived the loss of Neon's ability and is now led by Kurapika. The organization is exclusively involved in legal activities such as personal security details and gambling.

Likke Likke (リァッケ, "Riakke") is a Hunter and an acquaintance of Morel Mackernasey. Background. During the course of their life, Likke became a Hunter and befriended Morel. At some point, Likke also learned Nen. Plot. Chimera Ant arc. After Knuckle and Morel fail to capture Cheetu, Morel contacts the Hunter Association requesting they deploy Likke to deal with the Chimera Ant. However, the review board refuses, sending someone else, probably a Temp Hunter, who fails in the task, much to Morel’s anger and whom blames the Vice Chairman for the incident. Abilities & Powers. Likke has all the benefits granted by their status as a Hunter. Likke is likely very strong, since Cheetu, their intended target, managed to put up a good fight against Knuckle and Morel. It is heavily implied that Likke specializes in fighting extremely fast opponents.

Limeiro Limeiro (リーメイロ, "Rīmeiro") is the capital of Greed Island. Not only the castle, even the streets of the city are full of energy. The last event of the game is held in this city. Overview. The big castle where, according to rumors, Game Masters live is the city's symbol. The players who clear the game, arrive in this city and receive an impressive welcome as the game's ending. Plot. Greed Island arc. Right after Gon receives an invitation from an owl and a confrontation with Gashta and Zetsk Bellam, Killua uses a "Drift" spell card until he reaches Limeiro. He then reconvenes with Gon and Biscuit, and they all use an "Accompany" to reach Limeiro. Gon enters the castle, where he is greeted by List, who welcomes him. List leads Gon to a garbage-filled slipshod room where a sloven man named Dwun, who is playing a video game greets Gon. List and Dwun get acquainted with Gon and later a parade followed by a party is held in Gon's honor for beating the game.

Lin Koshi Lin Koshi (リン゠コウシ, "Rin Kōshi") is an Amateur Hunter and member of the former Wildlife Exploration Team who come to survey the Kakin Empire with Kite. Kite has stated that Lin and his fellow Amateur Hunters in the team have excellent potential to be Pro-Hunters. Appearance. Lin is a short man with fair hair neatly combed to the right side, rabbit-like front teeth, squinty eyes, and no visible nose. Lin wears a plain two-button dress shirt that is tucked into his dress pants, and dress shoes. Personality. Lin is a brainy individual who speaks candidly and tends to stutter the first word in every sentence that he says. Plot. Chimera Ant arc. Lin and his fellow Amateur Hunters arrive back at the campsite in the Kakin Empire where they are introduced to Kite's "kid friends" Gon and Killua and are left astounded after learning about their parental backgrounds and that they're both Pro-Hunters. During the introductions, Lin pleasantly introduces himself and it is later revealed that within the three year period in the Kakin Empire, he has managed to find exactly 1019 new species. A month goes by and the group delivers their results to their benefactor Wong. He elaborates that a piece of an unknown species has been found and procured by the Southernpiece Auction and so the group now with Gon and Killua visit the place to investigate the piece. In Lin's opinion on the piece, he says it looks like an insect leg, however, there is no known insect that is so large. The group split into two and the group Lin is a part of investigating the location of where the insect piece was found. Their search bears no results, however, a call from Podungo confirms that the insect piece is that of a Chimera Ant Queen. With this new information the group narrows down the plausible location of where the Chimera Ant Queen could be at is the NGL. The group visits the NGL Border Stop and divides into two groups, Lin being a part of the group that cannot enter the NGL due to its strict screening processing and return to the town they stayed at before. Sometime afterward at an undisclosed location, Lin and Banana elaborate the Chimera Ants' hierarchy system and behavior personalities to Stick and Spinner. 13th Hunter Chairman Election arc. The Amateur Hunters, Kite, and Koala wave goodbye to Gon, after he visits Kite. Later, in Spinner's hometown along with the rest of the Amateur Hunters, Gon, Koala, and Kite, Lin watch flocks of Small-billed Swans fly into the sky.

Lingon Airport Lingon Airport (, "Ringōn Kūkō") is an airport in the Yorknew City suburbs, roughly 90 minutes by car from the Hotel Beitacle, through a road in a desert area. Overview. Lingon Airport is a major airport close to Yorknew City. Plot. Yorknew City arc. In a briefing with the new Nostrade Family bodyguards, the head bodyguard Dalzollene mentions the airport as the location where their airship will land the following day to transport their boss, Neon Nostrade, to the Hotel Beitacle in the city. On August 31st, the airship safely lands on one of the airport's runways. Neon exits and is escorted by her bodyguards to a limo that transports her to the hotel. On the afternoon of September 3rd, the day of the rescheduled Underground Auction, Neon is accompanied by her two maids and her bodyguards Melody and Basho as she goes on a shopping spree at the airport. During their break, Neon slips away by pretending to go to the bathroom and sneaks by them in a disguise among a group of gossiping women. She is eager to go the auction by herself after her father lied about it being cancelled, and it's revealed that an unknown man is following her as he holds her picture in his hand. Melody then contacts Kurapika to update him on the situation involving Neon's escape. On September 4th, the airport is used as the location for negotiations between Kurapika with Chrollo and Pakunoda with Gon and Killua (both of whom are back at the Troupe's hideout). Pakunoda arrives at the airport and enters one of the airships where the negotiation is successful. After Kurapika details his conditions for the exchange, Pakunoda returns to the airport with her hostages. However, they are greeted by Hisoka, who arrives to fight Chrollo after the exchange. The fight between Chrollo and Hisoka doesn't take place because of the former's inability to use Nen. Back at the airport, Hisoka parts ways with Pakunoda after revealing his true fortune. After witnessing her maid Eliza have an emotional breakdown over the loss of Squala, Neon chooses to leave Yorknew from the airport on September 5th. On September 7th, Leorio says goodbye to Kurapika and Melody at the airport as they return to the Nostrade's Mansion.

Linn Linn (リン, "Rin") is a player of the Greed Island game. Appearance. Linn wears a hat, overalls with a short-sleeved shirt underneath, and wears a bracelet around his left wrist. Plot. Greed Island arc. After Gon and Killua win their first specified slot card "Sword of Truth" in the city of Antokiba, Linn and a number of long-time players including Kazsule and Asta show up with the intention of stealing it. Later he's shown to be still alive in the game as a bright dot can be seen next to his name in Gon's binder, which indicates if a player is dead or alive. Abilities & Powers. Nen. Due to being able to access Greed Island, Linn is capable of utilizing Nen.

Linne Horsdoeuvre Linne Horsdoeuvre (リンネ＝オードブル, "Rin'ne Ōdoburu") is a Double-Star Gourmet Hunter and is currently the oldest member of the Hunter Association. She is also an unofficial survivor of the Dark Continent. Appearance. Linne is an old woman of short stature. She has a round face covered in wrinkles. She has short blond hair parted in the middle and light-colored eyes, possibly due to some age-related sickness, since they were dark in her youth. When she was younger, her hair was more flyaway and slightly longer, a bit ruffled at the top and worn in a cowlick. Personality. Linne appears to be a silent person. During the election, the only time she spoke she showed to be uninterested in the ballot and wished for Netero to come back to life. She still seems to be deeply attached to him. In her youth, she demonstrated her zeal and courage by accompanying him to the extremely dangerous Dark Continent. Background. When she was young, Linne was a Hunter and a friend of Isaac Netero. At some point in her life, she joined Netero in his expedition to the Dark Continent, along with Zigg Zoldyck. Plot. 13th Hunter Chairman Election arc. Linne makes 16th place in the first round of the 13th Hunter Chairman Election. The following election second round she places in 13th place, sharing the spot with Biscuit Krueger, and again shares 12th place with Biscuit and also Cutie Beauty in the third round. At the close of the forth round, Linne finishes in 11th place and becomes one of the 16 candidates in the fifth round. It's said in her election bio that it's been 5 years since the last time her voice was heard. Linne is eliminated in the fifth round, for not making the top 8, by placing in 11th place. Giving her losing candidacy speech, she claims that she wants Netero to come back to life and be chairman again. Dark Continent Expedition arc. Ging mentions Linne along with Netero, and Zigg during his explanation about how the trio explored the Dark Continent and were astonished by the massiveness of the creatures that inhabit the continent. Abilities & Powers. Linne has all the benefits granted by her status as a Double-Star Gourmet Hunter, which also denotes exceptional competence in the culinary arts. Having traveled to the Dark Continent with Isaac Netero and lived to tell the tale, she likely possessed a great deal of strength and survival skills in her youth. Nen. As a Hunter, Linne knows how to use Nen.

Linssen Linssen (リンセン, "Rinsen") is a Hunter and currently the most senior bodyguard for the Nostrade Family. Appearance. Linssen has medium-length hair, beady eyes, and a very slender physique. He usually dressed in traditional Chinese clothing, but later wears a jacket and collared shirt. Personality. Linssen is very fearful and cautious, which is shown when he is strongly against Kurapika's decision to capture Uvogin. When subtly criticized by Mizaistom for being a Hunter working for a Mafia family, Linssen shows some pride and justifies himself. He argues that all the family's income comes from gambling and personal security details (both legal) and that they pay their taxes. Background. At some point during his life, Linssen took and passed the Hunter Exam to obtain a Hunter License. He was also hired as a bodyguard for the Nostrade Family. Plot. Yorknew City arc. On a private runway at Lingon Airport, Linssen, Ivlenkov, Tocino, Dalzollene, and Squala accompany Neon as she exits an airship and enters into a car that heads toward Yorknew City. On the night of the Underground Auction, Dalzollene instructs the bodyguards at the Hotel Beitacle what each of them needs to do during the auction. Linssen is assigned to guard the rear entrance of the auction house with Basho. Dalzollene coordinates with Linssen and the others after he learns about the massacre during the auction. Sometime later, Linssen and the other bodyguards follow the Phantom Troupe members to the Gordeau Desert. They subsequently witness Uvogin as he massacres dozens of Mafia members. The Shadow Beasts then appear before the Nostrade bodyguards and challenge Uvogin. During the confrontation, Linssen claims that he has never seen Nen like Uvogin's. Along with the other bodyguards, Linssen is shocked by Kurapika's decision to try and capture Uvogin. To avoid any conflict between them, Melody uses her Nen ability to calm everyone down. Nevertheless, Kurapika still insists on capturing Uvogin and manages to do so. As they drive back toward the city, Linssen spots a car tailing them. Linssen guesses that they lost them, but Basho points out that it looked like someone landed on top of the car, with Dalzollene confident that it was the other Shadow Beasts. Back in the city, the Nostrade bodyguards try to interrogate the restrained Uvogin to learn what happened to the missing attendees and auction items. After Dalzollene is killed and Uvogin is rescued by the other Troupe members, Linssen, and the other bodyguards all agree that Kurapika should become the new head bodyguard so he can contact and inform Light Nostrade of the current situation. When Light arrives in Yorknew and is brought up to speed, he thanks the bodyguards for their work, and after he plans to send Neon home, he divulges important information to the group about the Underground Auction, the Shadow Beasts, and how the Ten Dons plan to deal with the Phantom Troupe. When Kurapika checks the Hunter Website, he sees pictures and descriptions of Neon, Linssen, and the other bodyguards (besides himself and Melody). 13th Hunter Chairman Election arc. After the death of Chairman Netero, Linssen is seen at the Hunter Association's headquarters to vote in the first round of the 13th Hunter Chairman Election. Dark Continent Expedition arc. At an undisclosed location owned by the Nostrade Family, Linssen is visited by Mizaistom, who wishes to see Kurapika. Linssen informs him that Kurapika is away now and asks him to leave. However, as Mizaistom insists on staying to wait for him, three lackeys prepare to make him leave, but Mizaistom restrains them with his Cross Game ability. Linssen begrudgingly tells Mizaistom that Kurapika is downstairs, warning that he shouldn't provoke him since he's in a bad mood. Mizaistom then wonders why he's working for the Nostrade Family if he's a Hunter. Still, Linssen retorts that the family isn't a crime syndicate since they get all their income through personal security details and gambling (both of which are legal) and that they pay their taxes. He calmly tells Mizaistom that he has no right to say anything. After Kurapika arrives, Mizaistom proposes a quid pro quo and asks him to join the Zodiacs and accompany them to the Dark Continent, eventually revealing that he has information on the remaining Scarlet Eyes he seeks. Linssen internally remarks that Kurapika is looking for the eyes' owner and that they haven't found any clues so far. Succession Contest arc. Days after Kurapika joins the Zodiacs, Linssen informs him that the Kakin Princes are hiring bodyguards for the voyage. Kurapika urgently asks if he can tell who is hiring, but Linssen replies that only the salary is shown (which keeps increasing as the Princes try to outdo one another). He finally tells Kurapika that there are six offers. Abilities & Powers. Linssen has all the benefits granted by his status as a Hunter. He has considerable prowess, as proven by the fact that he successfully retrieved an item as part of a test required to be hired as a Nostrade bodyguard. Nen. Linssen's Nen type is unknown. He is at least capable of using Gyo.

Lipa Station Lipa Station (, "Ripa-eki") is a train station in Yorknew City. Overview. Lipa Station is located in the city's downtown area. Plot. Yorknew City arc. Half of the Phantom Troupe members take the Castor Line to Lipa Station while they are unknowingly tailed by Killua (in the last car) and Melody (in the same car). Melody continues to follow them while pretending to read a book and eventually tells Killua that the Troupe members got off. Killua calls Kurapika and tells them their location, adding that the Troupe members are heading for the Saloma Mall exit. Kurapika then realizes that it's in the direction of the Hotel Beitacle.

Lippo Lippo (リッポー, "Rippō") is a Blacklist Hunter who acted as the examiner for the Third and Fourth Phases of the 287th Hunter Exam. Appearance. Lippo is a petite man with a distinguishable violet mohawk, red eyes, and large eyeglasses (tainted orange in the 1999 series). Personality. Lippo likes to watch fights and has a sweet tooth. He is proud of his accomplishments as a Blacklist Hunter, and although he has no sympathy for criminals, he views them as his champions in the Third Phase of the Hunter Exam, relishing in their victories against the examinees, even the most brutal ones. He seems to have been close to the late Chairman Netero, as he's shown tearing up during the first round of the election. Background. Lippo is a Blacklist Hunter with a repertoire that includes the capture of Johness the Dissector, the most notorious mass murderer in Zaban City's history. To coerce prisoners to fight examinees inside Trick Tower, he offers to shorten their sentence by one year for every hour they stall the examinees. Plot. Hunter Exam arc. On top of Trick Tower, Beans explains to the examinees that they have 72 hours to reach the bottom of the tower alive. Inside the tower, a smiling Lippo tells Togari and another examiner that it's showtime. As the examinees begin to enter the tower, the three examiners are shown sitting on the floor and eating various snacks. Lippo whistles and several hooded figures appear with restraints around their wrists. He then tells them to move and take their positions, with the prisoners obeying his orders. After Gon, Killua, Kurapika, and Leorio enter the tower and wait for one more applicant so they can start the path of majority rules, Lippo talks over the nearby intercom and tells the examinees that each route down the tower has different requirements. He stresses that a single person cannot complete their path and that they will have to work together to reach the bottom of the tower alive, wishing them good luck. After Gon and his team enter the arena inside the tower, the shrouded Bendot turns to the nearby surveillance camera and points out that the examinees have arrived asking that his handcuffs be unlocked. Lippo quickly unlocks them, and the restraints around Bendot's wrists fall to the floor. Bendot then removes the shroud from his head and tells the examinees that the committee has chosen them as their taskmasters. On the other side of the arena inside the tower, the prisoners chuckle at the examinees quarreling and hope they continue to waste time, revealing that it will shorten their prison terms. Lippo eats a snack and sits in front of several monitors, eagerly watching all the examinees throughout the tower. It's revealed that each of the five prisoners is serving consecutive sentences of over 100 years. He has promised to shorten their sentences by one year for every hour that they can delay an examinee. After Bendot's win against Tonpa, Sedokan offers to go next and looks up at the surveillance camera, politely asking Lippo to unlock his restraints. After Gon defeats Sedokan in his game of candles, Lippo smiles and praises Gon's ability. After defeating Leorio, Leroute asks how much time the examinees had left, and Lippo's reply is 59 hours and 45 minutes. Bendot says that the examinees now have less than ten hours, with the last prisoner adding that time won't matter since his opponent will die. After the examinees defeat the prisoners, they wait in a nearby room, with Lippo telling them that the door will open in 50 hours so they can continue to descend the tower. Outside Trick Tower, Lippo congratulates the 24 examinees who completed the phase and reveals that the exam only has two more phases to complete. He explains that the Fourth Phase will take place on Zevil Island, with the location seen behind him. He then snaps his fingers, and the other examiner appears with a box on a cart. Lippo explains that they will draw lots to decide who they will hunt and who will hunt them. He adds that the box contains 24 numbered cards that correspond to the remaining examinees, telling them to draw in the order in which they reached the bottom of the tower. After they each draw a card, Lippo assures them that the tabulator has recorded the badge numbers and can dispose of the card if they wish. He then reveals that the examinee whose badge number is on their card is their target and that their objective is to collect the badges of other examinees. He explains that the badge of their specified target is worth three points and that their badge is worth three points if they can keep it. He adds that all other badges are worth one point and that they need at least six points to reach the final phase of the exam. Lippo finishes his explanation and tells the examinees to enjoy their time on Zevil Island. Lippo is seen among the other examiners as they discuss the remaining examinees and the final phase of the exam. When Netero reveals the matchups, Lippo appears just as surprised as the other examiners. 13th Hunter Chairman Election arc. After Netero's death, Lippo participates in the first round of the 13th Hunter Chairman Election. He also appears visibly distraught and begins to tear up. Abilities & Powers. Lippo has all the benefits granted by his status as a Hunter. Nen. As a professional Hunter, he is capable of utilizing Nen. Given his status as a Blacklist Hunter and his role as an examiner of the 287th Hunter Exam, he is very likely proficient in Nen. However, his abilities were never mentioned or shown.

Liquor Spring (G.I card) Liquor Spring (酒生みの泉) is a card found in the Greed Island game. It is one of the game's 100 designated slot cards and is required for a player to complete the game. It can turn water into alcohol. Summary. Liquor Spring (酒生みの泉): This card transforms any water taken out of the spring, to turn into a random alcoholic drink. The result will always taste both exquisite and extraordinary. The water will only transform if it has been taken out the spring for an hour. Returning the transformed alcohol back to the spring will return it back to its water state.

Lisamsetta Lisamsetta (リサムセッタ, "Risamusetta") is the Private Guard of the Second Prince Camilla in charge of killing the Seventh Prince Luzurus through a Nen curse. Appearance. Lisamsetta is a young man with fair hair and chiseled features. They wear the standard uniform of Camilla's private guards. Plot. Succession Contest arc. After Camilla is confined to a room in the VVIP area, Lisamsetta and most of her other bodyguards attend a meeting called by Sarahell about Shikaku's suicide. Abilities & Powers. As a Provisional Hunter, Lisamsetta has all the benefits granted by their status as a Hunter. However, these are all temporary, and their Hunter status and license will expire after the voyage to the New Continent. Nen. Lisamsetta is a Nen user and can cast the same curse as the other Have-Nots in Prince Camilla's employ.

Lisores Lisores (リゾル, "Rizoru") is a priest who resided in Meteor City. He worked at the city's church. Appearance. At the time of his appearance, Lisores was an elderly man. He had thick, bushy eyebrows and an even bushier mustache. He had thick, curly hair. He wore a hat and ornate outfit reminiscent of a Catholic priest's attire. Personality. Lisores was shown to be a kind priest and expressed particular interest in Chrollo, believing that his creative ideas might be worth mentioning to the city’s elders. The inhabitants of Meteor City are also stated to share remarkable bonds that have been described as "thinner than water, and yet thicker than blood". Plot. Succession Contest arc. In a flashback at Meteor City, after recovering a videotape from the junk piles, Chrollo eventually reaches a large church and makes his way inside. Lisores welcomes him back and asks if he is studying videos again. Chrollo says he is and points out that more small graves are outside. Lisores says that they even enter the internal residential zones now to abduct more and more kids who never return, warning Chrollo not to visit the outskirts alone. Chrollo says that he's going to the video room, and Lisores tells him to take his time, adding that the previous visitor is still there. In the church's basement, Lisores addresses an older individual and tells them that Chrollo has great promise based on his curiosity and intelligence, wondering if his ideas could be of use to the elders. The individual replies that it would be wonderful if Chrollo could help fix the problems plaguing the city. After Chrollo and some of his friends decide to dub one of the videotapes, Lisores announces that there will be a special screening at the church and welcomes many of the children with snacks. Phinks is left confused when Sarasa holds a bowl of snacks near his face, and she asks him to help hand them out. He angrily wonders why he has to help, but when Lisores looks in his direction, and Sarasa continues to hold up the bowl, Phinks quickly takes it and tells the rejoicing children to get their snacks if they haven't taken any. While he sets up the projector inside the church, Lisores tells the children to take their seats and wait until the screening starts. Backstage, Chrollo asks Lisores what the problem is, and he explains that the sound tape is tangled up, saying that while they could cut it to fix the problem, it would take a while. After Chrollo asks Lisores for the microphone, Uvogin yells from the back of the auditorium and wonders if Chrollo has nothing else to play, with Machi kicking him and telling him to be quiet. After the performance, as the audience cheers and applauds, several children are seen mimicking the Power Cleaners' moves, with Lisores shaking Chrollo's hand and giving him a pat on the head. After Sarasa's death, Chrollo and his friends gather around her body lying in a casket at the church, calling her beautiful and saying that it's like she's still alive. Lisores tells them that it's called embalming, explaining that it's a technique used to restore and keep a person's body as close as possible to how it was when they were alive. He adds that it's a miracle that her body was able to be restored so well given the condition it was in, asking them to thank the embalmer, Ms. Renko. Trivia. In real life, is a commune in the Calvados department in the Normandy region in northwestern France.

List List (リスト, "Risuto") is one of the Game Masters and creators of Greed Island. He lives in the castle of Greed Island along with Dwun, in the game's capital city, Limeiro. Appearance. List is a youthful-looking, short man with messy blond hair and thin freckles over his nose. He wears a purple dress shirt with a small blue tie. He also has black dress shoes with black pants and overall straps. Personality. List has accommodating, cordial manners and is often seen wearing a polite smile on his face. He did, however, lose his composure when Ging seemed unwilling to talk to Gon again. Background. List and the other Game Masters created Greed Island together and released it in 1987. Plot. Greed Island arc. List cordially welcomes Gon to Limeiro when he enters the castle. He then leads Gon to his associate Dwun's room, where he introduces Dwun to him. Dwun presents Gon with the "Ruler's Blessing" card and informs him that he won't be able to find any clues about Ging or his location (which isn't on Greed Island). List suggests that they move on to the next event, and Dwun then presents Gon with a case that he can use to take three cards outside the game. Dwun asks him whether he wants the generic ending or the one specifically for him, but List reveals that Dwun is just messing around and that the latter doesn't exist. With the game business out of the way, List finally introduces himself and Dwun as friends of Ging. List also reveals that the initials of the G.I. Game Masters' first names make up the game's title. Ging is the G, Razor the R, Eta and Elena the two Es, while List is the L and Dwun one of the Ds. List also mentions that a parade will be held to celebrate Gon's achievement, adding that he will get to choose his three cards at the harbor and reach the ending of the game. Dwun tells Gon the story about how his name was changed from Wdwune to simply Dwun by Ging since he needed the initial for the game's title. List says that Ging had Dwun's name changed in less than a minute, simply using a computer and phone, and with his name change, Dwun's luck apparently changed for the better as well. 13th Hunter Chairman Election arc. In the first round of the 13th Hunter Chairman Election, List appears to vote for the new Chairman. He is seen again later with Dwun and others visiting Gon in the hospital. He is seen as Ickshonpe Katocha gives his speech before the election's eighth round. He and Dwun both sit next to Ging in the front row. Before the top 4 candidates start their debate, List is seen using his phone. During the ninth round, when Gon appears after making a full recovery, Dwun waves at Gon, while List points at Ging, much to Ging's dismay. After Gon spots his father, List smirks with Dwun at Ging, who seemingly loathes the two for pointing him out. When Ging seems reticent to talk to Gon again, List joins the chorus of Hunters rebuking Ging. Abilities & Powers. List has all the benefits granted by his status as a Hunter. Nen. As a Hunter and a Game Master of Greed Island, he is able to use Nen. It was, however, never shown.

List (G.I card) List (, rom. "Risuto") is a spell card found in the Greed Island game. It allows the caster to view the number of other players currently in possession of a target card and the number of copies in use. Summary. This spell allows the user to view how many people are currently in possession of any one target card, as well as the total number of copies of that card in circulation, so as to verify whether the card has reached its maximum conversion limit and work out one's priorities. It requires the number of the target card to be stated out loud.

List of Volumes and Chapters The chapters of the Hunter × Hunter manga series are written and illustrated by Yoshihiro Togashi and first published by in the Japanese magazine . The first chapter was published on March 2, 1998, with subsequent chapters released with intermittent breaks ranging from one to seven weeks. However, starting in February 2006, the breaks increased dramatically in length, after which time a set of at least 10 chapters would be released. For more information, see the production section on the main article. An anime adaptation of the series was produced by and aired on for 62 episodes from October 16, 1999 to March 31, 2001. The TV series is based only on the first 11 volumes of the manga, as frequent delays in the publication of the manga and an unwillingness to produce low quality "filler" episodes resulted in a lack of content. Three DVD series were produced by Nippon Animation, adapting subsequent chapters of the manga up to Chapter 185. A new Hunter × Hunter anime adaptation was announced in July 2011. Instead of continuing the story from the OVA series, it restarted the story from the beginning of the manga in an attempt to adapt it more accurately. The series was produced by and aired on for 148 episodes from October 2, 2011 to September 24, 2014. The current manga chapters have been compiled into 36 "tankōbon" volumes in Japan by Shueisha. The first "tankōbon" was released on June 4, 1998, the most recent on October 4, 2018. In English, Hunter × Hunter is licensed for publication by as a part of their line of graphic novels aimed at older teenagers (age 16+). However, this imprint has since been dropped, and all reprinted volumes no longer have the "Shonen Jump Advanced" logo. The first English volume was released on April 5, 2005, the most recent on August 6, 2019. Chapters not yet in volume format. These chapters have yet to be published in a "tankōbon" volume. They were originally serialized in "Weekly Shōnen Jump".

Living is... Living is... (生きてくってことは..., "Ikite Kutte Koto Wa...") is a song from the Musical Hunter × Hunter, sung by Gon's voice actress, ; Killua's voice actress, ; Kurapika's voice actress, ; Leorio's voice actor, and Madam Isabel's actress, Yuu Daiki.

Loberry Loberry (ロベリー, "Roberī") is one of Prince Kacho's maids during her voyage in the Black Whale to the Dark Continent. Appearance. Loberry dresses in a standard maid's robe. Personality. As Prince Kacho's maid, she resents Kacho for her personality and deems herself lucky for getting away from the room for a while. She showed to be a little high strung during the encounter with Silent Majority. Plot. Succession Contest arc. She and her fellow maids and bodyguards witness Kacho's outburst on the meal prepared for her. Disgruntled, she whispers to her colleague Yuri if only they are assigned to Prince Fugetsu. In reply, a bodyguard wonders why both princes are so different given that they are twins. Prince Kacho sends Yuri and Loberry to attend Kurapika's two-week teaching of Nen. The maids express their delight about being able to get away from Prince Kacho for the time being. Amidst waiting for the teaching to begin, the two maids talk with Prince Fugetsu's maids Ladiolus and Illardia. A mysterious figure, notes that the ability user and Loberry who's being possessed by the doll can see the said doll. The moment Kurapika inquires if any of them can already use Nen and two people raise their hands. Loberry asks why would they attend the teaching if they already can to which Yuri has no clue as to why and then she immediately spots the doll. Prince Benjamin's soldier Furykov notices that Loberry has seen something. Anxious by what she has seen, she tries to point out a mysterious woman wearing a mask, but Yuri, Ladiolus, and Illardia cannot see her. In an outburst Loberry points out the "Mysterious Woman", but nobody sees it. While everyone is distracted, Silent Majority kills one of Prince Marayam's bodyguards Barrigen. In the aftermath Yuri asks where the "Mysterious Woman" has gone and bewildered Loberry claims it disappeared. Immediately Hashito restrains her, while Sakata contacts Cleapatro to report and request that Loberry be arrested for the murder of Barrigen. The request is denied due to circumstantial evidence, but Queen Seiko would be monitored for the next 72 hours. Furykov indirectly mentions that Loberry was taken into custody by the army. Abilities & Powers. Nen. Furykov identified Loberry as someone who has awakened her Nen abilities, which he speculated was due to her having been the host of Silent Majority. However, since she never mentioned seeing other people's aura (or her own), it appears highly likely she only "half awakened", a state common among victims of Manipulation and targets of parasitic-type Nen abilities.

Lone Pine Tree The Lone Pine Tree (, "Ipponsugi"—lit. "One Cedar") is a huge tree located in an arboreous area near Dolle Harbor with a quartet of Kiriko that live in a cabin under the tree. Overview. Another pre-exam trial that tests the examinees in many facets is held at this location. Plot. Hunter Exam arc. Following the tip given by the Captain and the Quizzing Lady; the Hunter examinees Gon, Kurapika, and Leorio follow a path into a forest that leads them to a log cabin where the Lone Pine Tree stands. In that cabin, a husband is attacked and wounded while his wife is taken hostage by a Kiriko. This turn of events is eventually solved and it's revealed that the husband and wife were the son and daughter to the one Kiriko they encountered in the log cabin and the other one that tried to attack Gon in the forest was the father and mother respectively. They pass the trio and take them to the Hunter Exam site. Greed Island arc. After registering for the 288th Hunter Exam, Killua plans to head to the Lone Pine Tree as Gon suggested, however, he would first take a shower. That night he manages to reach his destination and the Kiriko recognize Gon's scent on Killua, although, he took a shower beforehand. So to kill time, Killua tells the Kiriko about his adventures with Gon up to that point.

Lonely Sapphire (G.I card) Lonely Sapphire (孤独なサファイヤ) is a card found in the Greed Island game. It is one of the game's 100 designated slot cards and is required for a player to complete the game. Summary. Lonely Sapphire 孤独なサファイヤ - This card allows the user to summon forth a Lonely Sapphire. The owner of this rare jewel will acquire a vast amount of wealth. As a result, however, the owner must live with the curse of being alone for the rest of their life. They will be forsaken by all their friends, family, and anyone else who holds some significant value in their life.

Long Lost Delivery (G.I card) Long Lost Delivery (失し物宅配便) is a card found in the Greed Island game. It is one of the game's 100 designated slot cards and is required for a player to complete the game. Summary. Long Lost Delivery (失し物宅配便): This card allows the caster to gain back an item that was lost or never delivered. To use this card, call the number provided and describe the item you lost. The next day, the item will be delivered to you. This only works for items that have been lost or undelivered for more than one month.

Longhi Longhi (ロンギ, "Rongi") is a Royal Bodyguard for Prince Tubeppa. Appearance. Longhi has fair hair tied back in a long ponytail behind their back, and gaunt cheeks. As a Royal Bodyguard, they wear a black suit and a tie. Personality. Longhi seems to be a careful person, as they agree with their superior Maor that the best way of communicating with Kurapika discreetly is by letter, since signaling in code risks interception. He also appears to be less vocal than Maor. This is shown as he didn't intervene to support or contradict him when he accused Kurapika of being the mysterious killer. Plot. Succession Contest arc. Prince Tubeppa sends Maor and Longhi to attend Kurapika's two-week teaching of Nen. The two remember Tubeppa's order to persuade Kurapika within the two weeks they're there for, in order to be her ally even if it means involving Prince Woble. Maor believes that a written letter offering an alliance with Kurapika would be best and Longhi concurs as trying to communicate any other way would pose a high risk of getting intercepted. After Loberry's outburst, Longhi witnesses Barrigen be killed by a small pack of snakes. Following the murder, Kurapika tells his students to decide whether to stay or leave. They all remain and he teaches them his first exercise. The following day, Longhi returns to Room 1014 for Kurapika's lecture. Longhi does not intervene when Maor and Satobi accuse Kurapika of being behind the attacks after Myuhan's death. On the 7th day of the voyage, Longhi continues taking part in Kurapika's Nen training. Like everyone else, they begin to have doubts about the training, since they always repeat the same exercise. The following day, Longhi observes Kurapika's Water Divination. With Kurapika and Bill behind closed doors, they summon Ladiolus to perform Water Divination in private. Satobi confirms once again with Maor if the latter is fine with allowing them to proceed as they please, to which Tubeppa's bodyguard replies that they have no choice on the matter, as their goal is to learn Nen. Longhi remarks that if Woble's camp really intends to exploit their vulnerability, they are playing right into their hands. Right after Maor returns from the main bedroom, he confirms to his associate Longhi that everything Kurapika said is true. The two remain in the hall until the other students complete their Water Divination. Once the two reconvene with their Prince, Tubeppa assigns them the task of choosing new students among her staff, if Kurapika should announce a second training course. On the 10th day of the voyage, Tenftory reports to Prince Zhang Lei that all of the students who have taken Kurapika's Nen training are able to utilize Nen. In Room 1014, as aura swirls around them, Longhi tells Kurapika that Water Divination isn't needed since they can already use Nen, asking him if he will agree to the contract after hearing what they had to say. With Bill by his side, Kurapika agrees to the deal and says that he will collaborate with Prince Tubeppa.

Lottery (G.I card) Lottery (, rom. "Rotorī") is a spell card found in the Greed Island game. When cast, it transforms into a random item card. Summary. When used, this card turns into a random non-spell card that has not exceeded its conversion limit, making it an easy way to obtain high-ranked or unknown cards. Although the odds of getting the desired card are quite slim, they can be improved by rolling a Risky Dice before casting the spell. However, this strategy can generate only cards up to Rank A, thus preventing the caster from acquiring S-Rank cards.

Loupe Highland Loupe Highland (ルーペ゠ハイランド, "Rūpe Hairando") is a Lost Hunter and a candidate in the 13th Hunter Chairman Election. He specializes in seeking those from whom contact has been lost and has engaged in the problem related to lost members of the Hunter Association. He is also a member of the new Pure Paladin Squad. Appearance. Loupe is a slim, dark-skinned man of average height. He wears glasses and has a strong jaw line. He's seen wearing a black turtleneck sweater and jeans. Personality. Loupe is a reflective man, a manipulator, and a good tactician. When he has a goal, he pursues it while also ignoring any moral complications—in contrast with Teradein who is a convinced moralist. It is very self-evident that Loupe is a calm and calculated man. Plot. 13th Hunter Chairman Election arc. Loupe Highland and Knov places in 19th in the first round of the 13th Hunter Chairman Election, in the second round, he places in 12th. In the third round he places in 11th, while in the fourth round he is one of the sixteen candidates qualifying for the fifth round and ties 13th place with Bushidora Ambitious. In a video presentation for the 16 candidates for chairman, presented by Beans, it's states Loupe's a Lost Hunter—a specialist of finding contacts to missing persons. When Killua warns Morel his older brother is going to attack he and Alluka with brain-washed minions Needle People once they reach the hospital where Gon is hospitalized. Morel contacts Teradein, alongside Loupe and Bushidora, for their assistance. The 3 hold a meeting together within the Hunter Association, with a large group of Hunters and plan out a strategy to try and stop Illumi's Needle People. Soon after agreeing to help with the Needle People crisis, Teradein along with Bushidora and Loupe hold a special joint broadcast announcement. In the announcement Teradein praises the late chairman and intends to carry on his ideals and reform the Pure Paladin Squad that Isaac Netero once belonged to. Bushidora details Teradein shall act as the Leader, Loupe as the deputy, and he himself shall be captain of the acting forces and as a show of unity he and Loupe will vote for Teradein and implores all who agree with their purposes to vote for Teradein. Loupe then informs the viewers of a related matter in which criminal activity occurring by a certain member of the association. When the results of the election's fifth round for the 13th Hunter Chairman results come in after the broadcast, both Bushidora and Loupe place in 15th and are eliminated for not making the top 8 candidates. Sometime after the fifth round of the election, Teradein, Loupe, and Bushidora try to get in contact with the groups of more than 20 Hunters they were in contact with, including the Hunters Latoon and Kenzaki. Bushidora boasts his capable abilities as Captain. When inquired about the votes from Loupe, Bushidora states anyone who's free to vote go and vote as long as Teradein makes the top 4. Although Teradein voices his concern about the prediction of where the votes will go and doesn't want to sway the election through absentees. Loupe suggests they hire a group of Temp Hunters in order to reduce the number of votes for Pariston Hill. Bushidora and Teradein both agree with the plan, unbeknownst to them that was really a clever ploy to kill off the Temp Hunters by the enemy making them absent in the next election. Loupe also contemplates that Teradein is too honest, while Bushidora is too careless. However after Bushidora and company confront the group they're massacred and Loupe reports this to Teradein. After Hisoka killed Teradein, Loupe's current status is unknown.

Lubo Lubo (ルボ, "Rubo"), probably a country, is where the Lubo Civil War (, "Rubo no Naisen") took place. Overview. A civil war took place in Lubo and the mercenary group known as Stone Wall became famous for being the only group that was able to survive the entire war without a single casualty. Plot. Dark Continent Expedition arc. Muherr mentions the Civil War that took place in Lubo, when he divulges the backstory of Golem's mercenary group the Stone Wall to Ging.

Luciart Luciart (ルチアート, "Ruchiāto") is a Greed Island player. Appearance. Luciart has short hair and wears a shirt. Plot. Greed Island arc. After Gon and Killua obtain their first specified slot card, "Sword of Truth", in the city of Antokiba, Luciart appears together with a number of long-time players with the intention of stealing it. As there are several people wishing to take a single card, they have to use rock-paper-scissors to decide who is going to steal it. Later, a white dot is seen next to his name in Gon's book, indicating he's still alive. Abilities & Power. Nen. Due to being able to access Greed Island, Luciart is capable of utilizing Nen.

Luck Bankbook (G.I card) Luck Bankbook (幸運通帳) is a card found in the Greed Island game. It is one of the game's 100 designated slot cards and is required for a player to complete the game. This book allows you to turn luck into money. Summary. Luck Bankbook 幸運通帳 - This card allows its user to convert their use of good luck into money. To be more precise, it converts the user's ability to not act upon their good luck. In order to make any money from this card, you need to choose not to be lucky. (This does not make you unlucky!! It simply doesn't make you especially lucky.)

Luini Luini (ルイニー, "Ruinī") was a member of the Heil-Ly Family. Appearance. Luini was described as a man of slim build in his twenties, between 185 and 190 cm tall, and with a large crescent-shaped scar on his left cheek. He has prominent teeth, a high brow, and fair, combed-back hair. During his killing spree on the Black Whale, Luini disguised himself as a Kakin soldier. Afterwards, he switched into a tracksuit similar to what Phinks usually wears. Personality. Like his fellow Heil-Ly members, Luini had sadistic tendencies and no qualms about killing many people. He murdered 20 passengers in a short span of time and later killed a Mafia member as a "prank" for three members of the Phantom Troupe, whom he respected and described as his idols. Like his leader, Morena Prudo, he wanted to destroy the world. Luini also had a loathing towards the upper class, hoping that he could work with the Troupe to wipe them out. Plot. Succession Contest arc. Luini is seen with the other Heil-Ly members as Morena uses her Contagion on them one at a time and explains how her Nen ability works. In a warehouse on Tier 5, Nobunaga, Phinks, and Feitan follow a Cha-R member as they prepare to retrieve their weapons. However, as the member turns the corner, Nobunaga stops the other two and says that the man just disappeared from his En, with Phinks confirming it. After they turn the corner, they see no one at the dead end. They hear a sound behind them and quickly turn around, walking back around the corner and finding the man dead on the floor with his throat slit and several wounds in his chest. The three are left confused, but Phinks and Feitan prioritize their mission, with Nobunaga in disbelief that he is the only one worrying about how the man died. At the same time, Luini begins to open a portal in the ceiling above them. In the general passenger area on Tier 3, several soldiers cordon off the area as a large crowd begins to gather. An official tells them to stay back and that the area will be off-limits until forensics is done with the scene. Mizaistom asks someone how many victims there are, and the person says twenty, adding that the perpetrator entered the room disguised as Royal Army and killed quickly. Mizaistom wonders if Nen was involved, but the person replies that they only know a blade was used, with no sign of a Nen ability. Mizaistom describes it as a random attack and asks if there are any witnesses. The person says that there is a witness who described the perpetrator as in his twenties, slender, 6' to 6'2", with a crescent scar on his left cheek. They add that canvassing the area didn't return any eyewitness accounts of someone who fits that description, guessing that their testimony may be flawed because of confusion from shock. Mizaistom then sternly asks to speak to the witness. Back in the warehouse, Luini slowly opens the portal and excitedly looks at the three Troupe members. He chuckles and says it's only fitting that the Commando Team for the Spiders ignored his prank. Continuing to watch them from inside the portal, he says that they are his idols and hopes that they can work together to destroy the world. Mizaistom eventually goes to the scene of the crime, and Cashew begins to recount what happened. She first says that she heard a knock, and the victim went to the door. Once she opened it, Cashew then heard someone collapse, calling out but getting no answer. As Cashew opened the bathroom, she saw Luini dressed as a soldier and standing there before he quickly ordered her to move and threatened to kill her if she made a noise. After seeing the victim's body on the floor, Cashew emphasizes how afraid she was and says that she made sure to focus on following his orders so that he would spare her life. As she was desperately hoping that he wouldn't kill her, Luini says that he planned to stop at 20 and that it was the whole point of going for single rooms. He then begins to count and realizes that levels and number of people are offset by one, adding that it bothers him and angrily wondering which number he should count by. Cashew suddenly heard a scream outside the room and the sounds of people running, pounding on doors, and more screams. She tells Mizaistom that the man locked the bathroom door from the inside, and Mizaistom is left confused. She explains that she sat there until the Royal Army pried the door open, revealing that he had somehow escaped. Mizaistom points out that the pipes aren't even big enough for a rat, and Cashew is certain that he didn't come out, adding that the soldiers confirmed the door was locked. She then pleads with Mizaistom to catch the man and ask him. Mizaistom begins to analyze the situation with himself, wondering why he would have left a witness alive and emphasizing that the various words the man used are clues to the mystery. Mizaistom asks how she knew the victim, and Cashew replies that they hit it off right away after they happened to sit next to each other to eat. She then begins to cry, saying that the woman wanted advice about her personal life and she didn't get to give it to her. Mizaistom kneels down beside her and tells her to go rest in her cabin, adding that they will talk to her again. After Mizaistom escorts her away from the scene, Cashew's expression instantly changes, and it's revealed that she is a level 1 member of the Heil-Ly Family. In a flashback, Cashew explains her plan to Luini, saying that she will mix the truth with lies and make sure that it hints at why she wasn't killed. Luini praises her idea and tells her to describe his scar accurately. Cashew asks if he's sure, and Luini replies that he wants to know their investigative ability, clarifying that he wants to know how long it takes between being identified and getting found. Cashew again asks if he's sure, pointing out that he will be put to death if he is caught. Luini assures her that he won't get caught and adds that even if he does, he will escape. He then remembers Morena's line about their ability providing for them if they wish hard enough. With aura swelling around him, he finally says that he has been bestowed with a gift and the power will take him where he wants to go. Back in the present, Cashew says that Luini disappeared from the bathroom after that, guessing it's a transportation Nen ability and saying that she doesn't care for it. She asks herself if it's fun to get it over with so quickly, adding that she will level up slowly and ask for the gift. Lastly, she says that she has succeeded in contacting the investigators and will now get to know them better, licking her lips in delight. Now wearing a tracksuit, Luini explains that one door and a room of impenetrable walls are the activation conditions of his ability. As he opens a portal in a wall, he says that he can go somewhere else from the wall or floor. He adds that although he can return to the original room at any time and from any location, if the original door opens and the room is no longer sealed, the Nen ability will reset and he can never use it in that room again. He says that he is also limited to places he has been to before, guessing that while he can most likely go outside the ship, he can't test it at the moment since he can't risk the danger of getting reset. After stashing two dead Cha-R members in an empty storeroom, Luini says that he will first enjoy his collaboration with the Spiders. At the warehouse entrance, the three Troupe members find the guards missing and spot a trail of blood as they begin to analyze the motives of the killer. Nobunaga eventually realizes that the first corpse was meant to mess with them, and Feitan notes that the wound was made by something bigger than a card (ruling out Hisoka's involvement), describing it as shoddy. Phinks then realizes that the perpetrator wants to pick a fight with the Cha-R, not with the Troupe. After the three members follow the blood trail to a locked door, they are confronted by Ken'i Wang, the Cha-R underboss, who asks them if they have attacked the warehouse guards. Ken'i eventually realizes that the two have a common enemy, guessing that he was a hitman from another family that desires conflict. Phinks points out that the hitman's goal may have been to get inside the hideout since those with teleportation abilities usually need to "mark" locations. Ken'i then proposes working together with the Troupe while telling himself that they are a risk factor that has to be eliminated. In a meeting with several military officials, Mizaistom describes the killings on Tier 3 and eventually connects the incidents to the Seed Urn Ceremony, surmising that the perpetrator killed in order to gain supernatural powers for himself. Back at the Cha-R's hideout on Tier 5, Ken'i shows the Troupe members the surveillance footage of the perpetrator, who made sure that the cameras never got his face. Nobunaga eventually eyes a locked door, and Ken'i asks if he wants to see what's inside. Nobunaga replies that he won't ask for free, offering to kill the hitman in exchange for the answer. At 10 a.m. on the fourth day of the voyage, Luini is shown to be at the Heil-Ly's office on Tier 3. It's then announced that a stowaway with a deadly weapon is on the loose, with the passengers asked to stay in their cabins and to keep their doors closed until instructed. Soldiers then begin to search every cabin and look for anyone without an I.D. ticket. At 8 p.m. on the fifth day of the voyage, it's announced that the alarm has been canceled since the stowaway has been arrested. It adds that the lockdown order has been lifted, and the passengers are free to move about the ship. On the seventh day of the voyage, the three Troupe members discuss the situation with Ken'i and Tajao. Ken'i explains to him that eight of their men have gone missing so far, and the same is happening to the Xi-Yu Family. The total number of missing workers is over 300, and Ken'i believes that the hitman who murdered civilians on Tier 3 has come down with accomplices to the lowest tier to keep killing. Tajao agrees that quick action is needed, but wonders how this involves the Troupe. Phinks explains that they were looking for someone named Hisoka, but that he wasn't in Tier 5. He says if Tajao can get them permission from the Xi-Yu to let them search Tier 4, they will kill the hitman. Phinks goes on to describe the hitman's Nen ability, and that the hitman is interested in the door that Tajao and Ken'i came through, guessing that it's connected to a higher tier. Tajao says that the Heil-Ly have their own door through Tserriednich, but Phinks guesses that maybe the hitman is planning to take out the Cha-R Boss, Brocco Li. Ken'i adds that Tserriednich may also be wary of Morena since she recently took over as the boss. After explaining the Mafia code of conduct, Tajao tells the Troupe members that if the Spiders kill the hitman, they will personally be at war with the Heil-Ly, and Nobunaga is fine with that. Ken'i and Tajao point out that that means the Troupe won't be able to get information or help from the low-level thugs anymore. Nobunaga comes up with a quick solution and offers to take out the Heil-Ly boss personally. It will solve the issue of Morena causing problems, and they may even get thanks from Tserriednich. Phinks asks them to verify Morena's location, telling them that they will gather the other Spiders and hunt down the hitman first. Ken'i and Tajao give each other a look, both understanding how dangerous the Troupe can be. On the tenth day of the voyage, as a Cha-R member watches surveillance footage, Nobunaga suggests getting Franklin and splitting into teams of two to search outside in shifts. Phinks guesses that he would turn them down since he hates cramped places, but Nobunaga replies that he will team up with Franklin while the two of them stay there. Feitan says that even though the enemy will be reluctant to attack the three of them together, they shouldn't lose their patience. In the front room, several Cha-R members hear a knock on the door and wonder if the search team is back, but the member watching the surveillance footage tells Vic not to open it as he quickly asks the Troupe members to come to look at the monitors. An arm is seen coming through an opening as the person knocks on the door. Phinks notes that he's toying with them when he could have taken them by surprise. The member points to another monitor and sees that the search team is returning. However, when they open the door to the front room, they find no one there, with Phinks guessing that they must have been taken. Nobunaga notes that it doesn't matter how many grunts are around if they can't use Nen. The member nervously wonders where his comrades are, but Nobunaga quickly orders him to stay in the other room and bolt the door, telling him to look for the search team on the monitors and let them know if anything happens. An opening suddenly appears on the front door, and Luini slowly reveals his face, telling the Troupe that they are acting so out of character since they should be betraying the Cha-R and using their door to the upper tiers so that they can kill all the rich scum. As Luini continues to voice his disappointment, both Phinks and Feitan react with utter disgust at his maniacal rambling, with the latter asking the extent of the Heil-Ly hitman's knowledge of their organization. Luini wonders if he should edit their wikipedia page since it currently says that they are diabolical thieves. Nobunaga quickly draws his "katana" and tells him to also add the line that they show "no" mercy to idiots that annoy them. After assuring the three Troupe members that he doesn't want to fight them, Luini proposes working together so that they can eliminate the Cha-R Family, the Xi-Yu Family, and Kakin's royal family before taking control of the Black Whale and returning to the old world to destroy it. However, Nobunaga suddenly lunges forward with his "katana" and stabs Luini in the head, saying that he isn't making sense and criticizing his pointless antics at the warehouse. He removes his "katana" and says that he will destroy him if he wants to destroy the world, striking Luini with his "katana" once again. Tsudonke and his men return to the office, with Nobunaga opening the door for them. Hiding his excitement at Nobuanga's gesture, Tsudonke asks what happened to the other Cha-R members. Nobunaga reveals that they were all killed, leading them to Luini's decapitated and bisected corpse. With Tsudonke unable to believe the carnage, Nobunaga explains that they found the hitman who killed the guards at the warehouse, holding up his head and adding that they have decided to destroy the Heil-Ly Family. Elsewhere on the ship, several Heil-Ly members look at the bottom half of Luini's corpse up against a nearby wall. A construction worker named Daemon (level 20) points out how much Luini's loss will affect them since he allowed them to hunt for prey from the hideout. A professional gamer named Gelato (level 19) adds how dangerous it will be now since the military is on high alert. An investigator's assistant named Perigord (level 18) suggests that someone should recreate Luini's ability. An arcade employee named Bille (level 20) says that he has already decided on his ability. Perigord reminds them that Morena said everyone has an innate type, confident that Luini was an Emitter. Bille replies that an Emitter needs to do the job, but Gelato points out that they need to figure out how to raise their levels so they can reach level 21. An Emitter and human trafficker named Voconte (level 26) suggests using his "door" Nen ability to catch prey that wander into the trap, adding that they have ways to reel them in. After one of the Cha-R's members falls into the Heil-Ly's trap, Hinrigh says that it's probably the same person who was abducting their members, but Ken'i points out that Nobunaga killed the hitman. With Hinrigh left surprised, Ken'i adds that even though the Troupe members left their office, the hitman's head and torso remain there, revealing the Troupe's declaration to eliminate the Heil-Ly. Equipment. Knife: Luini's weapon of choice was a knife with a thin blade more than twice the length of the handle. Abilities & Powers. Luini quickly killed 20 people with a long knife, which suggests a certain amount of skill. However, according to Feitan, his killing of several Mafia members was shoddy. Luini was also one of the 22 survivors after Morena had her underlings kill each other. He seemed to be quite fast, having snatched the Troupe's guide inside the warehouse in a split second. He also seemed to have some planning and infiltration aptitude, as he successfully disguised himself at least twice, having managed to sneak into the Cha-R Family's hideout on the latter occasion. Nen. Luini was an Emitter. Having reached (and surpassed) level 21 with Morena's Nen ability, Luini's aura amount and output were increased. He also obtained a Nen ability.

Luis Luis (ルイス, "Ruisu") is an anime-only character in the 1999 anime adaptation, and a pro-Hunter who was one of the judges of the 287th Hunter Exam. Appearance. Luis has neatly combed brown hair, long thin eyebrows, and a defined jaw. He wears a black suit and black sunglasses. Personality. Luis kept a calm and professional demeanor for the most part, but an attack by Illumi made him notably distressed. Background. At one point in his life, he took the Hunter Exam. He passed and eventually became an examiner for the exam itself. Plot. Hunter Exam arc. Luis acts as one of the examiners for the Final Phase of the 287th Hunter Exam, more specifically, the referee in Hisoka vs. Kurapika's match, Hisoka vs. Bodoro's match, and Killua vs. Gittarackur's match. During the last fight mentioned, when Gittarackur (who had already revealed himself to be Illumi) learns that Killua would like to be friends with Gon and starts exiting the room to kill him, Luis tries to stop Illumi from leaving the unfinished match. Illumi throws his needles at Luis' head; as a consequence. He begins to feel great pain, and his face begins to deform, causing him to reveal where Gon is. Illumi coldly informs Luis that he will not die, his face will change form a little, but if he does not remove the pins in time, it might never return to normal; finally, Luis falls to the ground. Abilities & Powers. Luis has all the benefits granted by his status as a Hunter. Nen. As a Hunter, Luis can utilize Nen. Due to having been an examiner for the Hunter Exam, he is likely proficient in using Nen, although he never displays this.

Lukso Province The Lukso Province (, "Rukuso-chihō") is the former residence of the Kurta Clan, prior to their massacre by the Phantom Troupe. This province is not easily found, which is the reason why Kurta Clan members were able to hide themselves. Kurapika lived in the area during his early childhood. Flora. The Lukso Province has an abundance of trees and plants with varying swirl patterns. Fauna. Pikos were one way that Kurta Clan members traveled and transported items. Kurapika and Pairo used these birds to ride back and forth from the village to the province and to carry the groceries obtained for the third test. When journeying to the outside world, Kurapika also used one. Another type of large bird, with green plumage and a curved beak, was native to the province.

Luonton City Luonton City (, "Ruonton-shi") is a city located in the Republic of East Gorteau. Overview. Luonton City is the only place Killua went to that did not adhere to his warning. Plot. Chimera Ant arc. Neferpitou contacts Leol to have him set up an ambush north of Luonton City to deal with the "Target", which is all based on a hunch they had. Meanwhile, Killua's warning to the people in Luonton City is not adhered to, so he decides to quit warning people about the genocide and shifts his focus to taking out militants and puppets he encounters. Killua's movement is tracked by Flutter as he reports his discovery to Leol that he's heading northward into the forest by the highway northeast of Luonton City.

Lurka Ruins The Lurka Ruins (, "Ruruka Iseki") or Lurka Civilization Ruins (, "Ruruka Bunmei Iseki") are ruins that were discovered by Ging Freecss and excavated and restored primarily by him. Background. The Lurka Ruins were once excavated and restored by Ging Freecss, who used his own money to pay for the restoration and public viewing facilities that emphasized the need for preservation. These methods have since been adopted as the veritable textbook on archaeology. Plot. Hunter Exam arc. In a flashback involving Kite and a younger Gon, Kite informs the boy that Ging discovered the Lurka Civilization Ruins and achieved numerous other things in his tenure as a Hunter. Satotz mentions to Gon how he learned humility from a Hunter's work at the Lurka Ruins. The Hunter paid for all of the restoration and public facilities that emphasized the need for preservation of the ruins. Finishing his story, Satotz recommends that Gon visit the place someday, which he agrees to do. Seeking information on the Hunter License that he received from Kite, Gon asks Satotz. After checking its number, he reveals that it belongs to Ging Freecss, the unnamed protagonist of his Lurka Ruins story.

Luzurus Hui Guo Rou Luzurus Hui Guo Rou (ルズールス゠ホイコーロ, "Ruzūrusu Hoikōro") is the Seventh Prince of the Kakin Empire and the son of his father's second wife, Duazul. He is also in league with the Cha-R Family, one of the three great Mafia families of the Kakin Empire. Appearance. Luzurus is a thin man with a long nose and a pointy chin. He also has some stubble. Unlike his full-siblings, who all have hair in sharp, curving strands, Luzurus' hair seems to curl in two puffs at the side. It is fair in color. He appears clean-shaven when he presents for the banquet held in the Black Whale dining hall. Personality. Not much is known about Luzurus' personality, but his elder brother Tserriednich thinks of him as a moron. An example of that is when Luzurus sent his soldiers to take the Hunter Exam with assassination on their minds, without taking the time to think that there could be the possibility of lie detectors being used during the Hunter Exam. However, given Tserriednich's own pride on his own intellect and his low opinion on those he considers inferior to his, this is somewhat questionable. He is level-headed and thoughtful as he doesn't at all alarmed on learning the existence of his own Guardian Spirit Beast and Nen. He seems to have a caring side as well as he plans to use the healthy drug, Clean Leaf to rehabilitate drug addicts. Plot. Dark Continent Expedition arc.
